blackness: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 漆黑；黑暗； blackness Blackness is the state of being very dark.
blackout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 战时灯火管制期； blackout A blackout is a period of time during a war in which towns and buildings are made dark so that they cannot be seen by enemy planes.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 新闻等的禁播，封锁，禁止出版； blackout If a blackout is imposed on a particular piece of news, journalists are prevented from broadcasting or publishing it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 停电；断电； If there is a power blackout , the electricity supply to a place is temporarily cut off.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 晕厥；暂时昏迷； If you have a blackout , you temporarily lose consciousness.
black out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 晕厥；暂时昏迷； black out If you black out , you lose consciousness for a short time.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 对…实行灯火管制；使一片漆黑； If a place is blacked out , it is in darkness, usually because it has no electricity supply.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 禁播[电影等]; 禁止发行，禁止出版文章、图书等； If a film or a piece of writing is blacked out , it is prevented from being broadcast or published, usually because it contains information which is secret or offensive.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 涂黑，盖住，涂掉文字等； If you black out a piece of writing, you colour over it in black so that it cannot be seen.
black pepper: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 黑胡椒； Black pepper is pepper which is dark in colour and has been made from the dried berries of the pepper plant, including their black outer cases.
black pudding: [N-VAR 可变名词] 血肠，黑香肠用肥肉和猪血制成的黑衣香肠； Black pudding is a thick sausage which has a black skin and is made from pork fat and pig's blood.
black sheep: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 害群之马；败家子；败类； If you describe someone as the black sheep of their family or of a group that they are a member of, you mean that they are considered bad or worthless by other people in that family or group.
blacksmith: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 铁匠； A blacksmith is a person whose job is making things by hand out of metal that has been heated to a high temperature.
black spot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 危机焦点；隐患；雷区； black spot If you describe a place, time, or part of a situation as a black spot , you mean that it is particularly bad or likely to cause problems.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 交通事故多发地段； black spot A black spot is a place on a road where accidents often happen.
black tie: [ADJ 形容词] 社交场合穿晚礼服的，正式的； A black tie event is a formal social event such as a party at which people wear formal clothes called evening dress.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 男式晚礼服； black tie If a man is dressed in black tie , he is wearing formal evening dress, which includes a dinner jacket or tuxedo and a bow tie.
blacktop: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 铺路面用的柏油碎石； blacktop Blacktop is a hard black substance which is used as a surface for roads.
bladder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 膀胱； See also: gall bladder ; Your bladder is the part of your body where urine is stored until it leaves your body.
blade: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 刃；锋； blade The blade of a knife, axe, or saw is the edge, which is used for cutting.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 螺旋桨的叶片； The blades of a propeller are the long, flat parts that turn round.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 桨叶； The blade of an oar is the thin flat part that you put into the water.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 草的叶片； A blade of grass is a single piece of grass.
blag: [VERB 动词] 通过花言巧语获得；巧妙地免费得到； To blag something such as a concert ticket means to persuade someone to give it to you free.
blah: [CONVENTION 惯用语] 表示无趣或不重要…啊之类的；等等；诸如此类的； blah You use blah, blah, blah to refer to something that is said or written without giving the actual words, because you think that they are boring or unimportant.
blame: [VERB 动词] 责怪；怪罪；归咎于； blame If you blame a person or thing for something bad, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 对坏事应负的责任； blame The blame for something bad that has happened is the responsibility for causing it or letting it happen.  /  [VERB 动词] 怨；怪；责备； blame If you say that you do not blame someone for doing something, you mean that you consider it was a reasonable thing to do in the circumstances.  /  [PHRASE 短语] …难辞其咎；应对…负责； blame If someone is to blame for something bad that has happened, they are responsible for causing it.
blameless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无可责备的；没有过错的；清白的； blameless Someone who is blameless has not done anything wrong.
blanch: [VERB 动词] 突然变得煞白； blanch If you blanch , you suddenly become very pale.  /  [VERB 动词] 退缩；回避； blanch If you say that someone blanches at something, you mean that they find it unpleasant and do not want to be involved with it.  /  [VERB 动词] 焯； blanch If you blanch vegetables, fruit, or nuts, you put them into boiling water for a short time, usually in order to remove their skins, or to prepare them for freezing.
blancmange: [N-VAR 可变名词] 牛奶冻； Blancmange is a cold dessert that is made from milk, sugar, cornflour or corn starch, and flavouring and looks rather like jelly.
bland: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 枯燥乏味的；无聊的；无趣的； bland blandness If you describe someone or something as bland , you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 食物淡而无味的； bland Food that is bland has very little flavour.
blandishments: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 奉承话；花言巧语；甜言蜜语； blandishments Blandishments are pleasant things that someone says to another person in order to persuade them to do something.
blandly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 平淡地；平静地； blandly If you do something blandly , you do it in a calm and quiet way.
blank: [ADJ 形容词] 空白的；空的； blank Something that is blank has nothing on it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 空白处；空格； blank A blank is a space which is left in a piece of writing or on a printed form for you to fill in particular information.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 茫然的；漠然的；毫无表情的； blank blankly blankness If you look blank , your face shows no feeling, understanding, or interest.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 头脑或记忆一片空白； blank If your mind or memory is a blank , you cannot think of anything or remember anything.
blank cheque: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 空白支票； blank cheque If someone is given a blank cheque , they are given the authority to spend as much money as they need or want.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 自行处理权；全权； blank cheque If someone is given a blank cheque , they are given the authority to do what they think is best in a particular situation.
blanket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 毯子；毛毯； A blanket is a large square or rectangular piece of thick cloth, especially one which you put on a bed to keep you warm.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 覆盖层； blanket A blanket of something such as snow is a continuous layer of it which hides what is below or beyond it.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 不好的情感、性质等的弥漫，充斥； blanket You can refer to something such as an unpleasant emotion or an undesirable quality that seems to affect every aspect of a particular situation as a blanket of that emotion or quality.  /  [VERB 动词] 覆盖；遮盖；盖住； blanket If something such as snow blankets an area, it covers it.
blank out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 不再去想；刻意忘却； blank out If you blank out a particular feeling or thought, you do not allow yourself to experience that feeling or to have that thought.
blank verse: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无韵诗，素体诗英语无韵诗中通常每行有五个重读音节； Blank verse is poetry that does not rhyme.
blare: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 高声鸣响；使发出刺耳的声音； blare blare out 同 blare If something such as a siren or radio blares or if you blare it, it makes a loud, unpleasant noise.
blarney: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 奉承话；恭维话； Blarney is things someone says that are flattering and amusing but probably untrue, and which you think they are only saying in order to please you or to persuade you to do something.
blaspheme: [VERB 动词] 亵渎； blaspheme blasphemer If someone blasphemes , they say rude or disrespectful things about God or religion, or they use God's name as a swear word.
blasphemous: [ADJ 形容词] 亵渎神明或宗教的； blasphemous You can describe someone who shows disrespect for God or a religion as blasphemous .
blasphemy: [N-VAR 可变名词] 亵渎上帝或宗教的言行； blasphemy You can describe something that shows disrespect for God or a religion as blasphemy .
blast: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 爆炸； blast A blast is a big explosion, especially one caused by a bomb.  /  [VERB 动词] 爆炸；炸毁；炸出；炸开； blast If something is blasted into a particular place or state, an explosion causes it to be in that place or state.  /  [VERB 动词] 炸[石]; 爆破； blast blasting If workers are blasting rock, they are using explosives to make holes in it or destroy it, for example so that a road or tunnel can be built.  /  [VERB 动词] 枪击；开枪射击； blast To blast someone means to shoot them with a gun.
blast away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 连续射击；连续开枪； If a gun, or a person firing a gun, blasts away , the gun is fired continuously for a period of time.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 收音机等发出巨响；流行乐队带来喧闹的乐声； blast away If something such as a radio or a pop group is blasting away , it is producing a loud noise.
blasted: [ADJ 形容词] 讨厌的；该死的； blasted Some people use blasted to express anger or annoyance at something or someone.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 荒凉的； blasted A blasted landscape has very few plants or trees, and makes you feel sad or depressed when you look at it.
blast furnace: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 炼铁的鼓风炉，高炉； A blast furnace is a large structure in which iron ore is heated under pressure so that it melts and the pure iron metal separates out and can be collected.
blast off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 火箭点火起飞，离地升空； See also: blast-off ; When a space rocket blasts off , it leaves the ground at the start of its journey.
blast-off: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 火箭的发射，点火起飞； blast-off Blast-off is the moment when a rocket leaves the ground and rises into the air to begin a journey into space.
blast out: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 音乐或噪音震天响，轰响； If music or noise is blasting out , loud music or noise is being produced.
blatant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 公然的；露骨的；明目张胆的； blatant blatantly You use blatant to describe something bad that is done in an open or very obvious way.
blatantly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 强调糟糕非常，极为，完全； blatantly Blatantly is used to add emphasis when you are describing states or situations which you think are bad.
blather: [VERB 动词] 喋喋不休；废话连篇；絮絮叨叨； blather If someone is blathering on about something, they are talking for a long time about something that you consider boring or unimportant.
blaze: [VERB 动词] 熊熊燃烧； blaze When a fire blazes , it burns strongly and brightly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大火；烈火； blaze A blaze is a large fire which is difficult to control and which destroys a lot of things.  /  [VERB 动词] 照耀；发出[强光]; 绽放光彩； blaze If something blazes with light or colour, it is extremely bright.  /  [VERB 动词] 眼睛闪耀，闪烁，充满[感情]; 情感在眼中燃烧； blaze If someone's eyes are blazing with an emotion, or if an emotion is blazing in their eyes, their eyes look very bright because they are feeling that emotion so strongly.
blazer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指学童和运动队成员穿的运动夹克，运动上衣； A blazer is a kind of jacket which is often worn by members of a particular group, especially schoolchildren and members of a sports team.
blazing: [ADJ 形容词] 炽热的；炎热的； blazing Blazing sun or blazing hot weather is very hot.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 争吵激烈的； blazing When people have a blazing row, they quarrel in a very noisy and excited way.
bldg: 尤用于建筑物名称； Bldg is a written abbreviation for (书面缩略=) building , and is used especially in the names of buildings.
bleach: [VERB 动词] 漂白；使变白； bleach If you bleach something, you use a chemical to make it white or pale in colour.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 晒白；使褪色；使变白； bleach If the sun bleaches something, or something bleaches , its colour gets paler until it is almost white.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 漂白剂； Bleach is a chemical that is used to make cloth white, or to clean things thoroughly and kill germs.
bleachers: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 体育场的露天看台； The bleachers are a part of an outdoor sports stadium, or the seats in that area, which are usually uncovered and are the least expensive place where people can sit.
bleak: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 情形没有希望的，前景暗淡的； bleak bleakness If a situation is bleak , it is bad, and seems unlikely to improve.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 地方凄清的，荒凉的，萧瑟的； bleak If you describe a place as bleak , you mean that it looks cold, empty, and unattractive.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 天气阴冷的，寒冷的； bleak When the weather is bleak , it is cold, dull, and unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人无精打采的，沮丧的，阴郁的； bleak bleakly “什么也没有留下，”她沮丧地说。； If someone looks or sounds bleak , they look or sound depressed, as if they have no hope or energy.
bleary: [ADJ 形容词] 眼睛模糊的，蒙眬的，惺忪的； bleary If your eyes are bleary , they look dull or tired, as if you have not had enough sleep or have drunk too much alcohol.
bleat: [VERB 动词] 羊咩咩叫； bleat When a sheep or goat bleats , it makes the sound that sheep and goats typically make.  /  [VERB 动词] 微弱地尖声诉说；羊叫般地说； bleat If someone bleats , they speak in a weak, high voice.  /  [VERB 动词] 抱怨；低声诉苦； bleat If you say that someone bleats about something, you mean that they complain about it in a way which makes them sound weak and irritating.  /  相关词组： bleat on about �
bleat on about: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 喋喋不休；唠唠叨叨； If you say that someone is bleating on about something, you mean that they are talking about it a great deal in a way which makes them sound weak and irritating.
bled: + + + Bled is the past tense and past participle of bleed .
bleed: [VERB 动词] 出血；流血； bleed bleeding When you bleed , you lose blood from your body as a result of injury or illness.  /  [VERB 动词] 颜色渗开，弥散； bleed If the colour of one substance bleeds into the colour of another substance that it is touching, it goes into the other thing so that its colour changes in an undesirable way.  /  [VERB 动词] 逐渐榨取…的钱财； bleed If someone is being bled , money or other resources are gradually being taken away from them.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 榨干…的钱财或资源； If someone is being bled dry or is being bled white , all of their money or other resources are gradually being taken away from them.
bleeding: [ADJ 形容词] 该死的；讨厌的； Bleeding is used by some people to emphasize what they are saying, especially when they feel strongly about something or dislike something.
bleeding edge: [N-SING 单数名词] 某一活动领域的最前沿，最令人兴奋的发展阶段； bleeding edge If you are at the bleeding edge of a particular field of activity, you are involved in its most advanced or most exciting developments.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 设备、技术最先进的，尖端的； Bleeding-edge equipment or technology is the most advanced that there is in a particular field.
bleeding heart: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 假装同情者；滥发善心的人； bleeding heart If you describe someone as a bleeding heart , you are criticizing them for being sympathetic towards people who are poor and suffering, without doing anything practical to help.
bleep: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电子仪器发出的哔哔声，嘟嘟声，短促尖锐的声音； A bleep is a short, high-pitched sound, usually one of a series, that is made by an electrical device.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出哔哔声；发出嘟嘟声；发出短促尖锐的声音； bleep If something electronic bleeps , it makes a short, high-pitched sound.  /  相关词组： bleep out �
bleeper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同beeper； A bleeper is the same as a beeper .
bleep out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 电视或广播节目中用哔哔声盖过粗话； In a television or radio programme, when someone bleeps out an offensive word, they use an electronic device to make the sound of a bleep so that people cannot hear the word.
blemish: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 污点；瑕疵；疤痕； blemish A blemish is a small mark on something that spoils its appearance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 缺点；缺陷；不足； blemish A blemish on something is a small fault in it.  /  [VERB 动词] 玷污；损害； blemish If something blemishes someone's character or reputation, it spoils it or makes it seem less good than it was in the past.
blemished: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有污点的；有瑕疵的；有疤痕的； blemished You use blemished to describe something such as someone's skin or a piece of fruit when its appearance is spoiled by small marks.
blend: [V-RECIP-ERG ] 使混合；调和；掺和； blend If you blend substances together or if they blend , you mix them together so that they become one substance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有用或令人愉快的事物的融合，混合，组合； blend A blend of things is a mixture or combination of them that is useful or pleasant.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 颜色、声音或风格融合，交融，协调； blend When colours, sounds, or styles blend , they come together or are combined in a pleasing way.  /  [VERB 动词] 结合，融合，综合想法、政策和风格； blend If you blend ideas, policies, or styles, you use them together in order to achieve something.
blender: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 食物搅拌器； A blender is an electrical kitchen appliance used for mixing liquids and soft foods together or turning fruit or vegetables into liquid.
blend in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 融入；与…融为一体；与…协调； blend in If something blends into the background, it is so similar to the background that it is difficult to see or hear it separately.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 与…打成一片；成为…的一员；融入； blend in If someone blends into a particular group or situation, they seem to belong there, because their appearance or behaviour is similar to that of the other people involved.
bless: [VERB 动词] 为…祈求上帝保佑；为…祈神赐福； bless When someone such as a priest blesses people or things, he asks for God's favour and protection for them.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 用于表达爱意、感谢或祝愿愿上帝保佑； bless Bless is used in expressions such as ' God bless ' or ' bless you ' to express affection, thanks, or good wishes.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 对刚打喷嚏的人说长命百岁； You can say ' bless you ' to someone who has just sneezed.  /  See also: blessed ; blessing ; �
blessed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 拥有…的；享有…的； blessed If someone is blessed with a particular good quality or skill, they have that good quality or skill.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 令人快乐的；可喜的；美好的； blessed blessedly You use blessed to describe something that you think is wonderful, and that you are grateful for or relieved about.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 强调生气该死的，倒霉的，讨厌的； blessed Some people use blessed to emphasize that they are annoyed about something.  /  See also: bless ; �
blessing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 幸事；福气；好事；福祉； blessing A blessing is something good that you are grateful for.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 支持；赞同；准许； blessing If something is done with someone's blessing , it is done with their approval and support.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 祈福；祷告；祈祷； A blessing is a prayer asking God to look kindly upon the people who are present or the event that is taking place.  /  See also: bless ;
blew: + + + Blew is the past tense of blow .
blight: [N-VAR 可变名词] 破坏因素；祸根；阴影； blight You can refer to something as a blight when it causes great difficulties, and damages or spoils other things.  /  [VERB 动词] 破坏[生活]; 使希望破灭；摧毁；损毁； blight If something blights your life or your hopes, it damages and spoils them.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 植物的枯萎病； Blight is a disease which makes plants dry up and die.
blighter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 可恶的家伙；讨厌鬼； blighter You can refer to someone you do not like as a blighter .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 家伙； blighter You can use blighter as an informal way of referring to someone.
Blighty: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 英国老家； Blighty Blighty is a way of referring to England.
blimey: [EXCLAM 感叹语] 表示惊奇或强烈的感情啊呀，天哪； You say blimey when you are surprised by something or feel strongly about it.
blimp: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同airship； A blimp is the same as an airship .
blind: [ADJ 形容词] 盲的；瞎的；失明的； blind 盲人；瞎子；失明的人 blindness Someone who is blind is unable to see because their eyes are damaged.  /  [VERB 动词] 使…看不见；使…失明； blind If something blinds you, it makes you unable to see, either for a short time or permanently.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 暂时看不见的；双眼模糊的；目眩的； blind blindly If you are blind with something such as tears or a bright light, you are unable to see for a short time because of the tears or light.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 看不到的；视而不见的；没有意识到的； blind blindness If you say that someone is blind to a fact or a situation, you mean that they ignore it or are unaware of it, although you think that they should take notice of it or be aware of it.
blind alley: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死胡同；绝路；困境； blind alley If you describe a situation as a blind alley , you mean that progress is not possible or that the situation can have no useful results.
blind date: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 盲目约会；由第三方安排的男女初次约会； A blind date is an arrangement made for you to spend a romantic evening with someone you have never met before.
blinder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 运动员或音乐家等的精彩的表现，出色的表演； If you say that someone such as a sports player or musician has played a blinder , you are emphasizing that they have played something very well.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 同blinkers； Blinders are the same as blinkers .
blindfold: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 眼罩；障眼物；蒙眼布； A blindfold is a strip of cloth that is tied over someone's eyes so that they cannot see.  /  [VERB 动词] 蒙住…的眼睛；遮住…的视线； blindfold If you blindfold someone, you tie a blindfold over their eyes.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 蒙住眼睛的； blindfold If someone does something blindfold , they do it while wearing a blindfold.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 能轻而易举；蒙着眼睛都可以； blindfold If you say that you can do something blindfold , you are emphasizing that you can do it easily, for example because you have done it many times before.
blinding: [ADJ 形容词] 光线刺目的，炫目的，耀眼的； blinding A blinding light is extremely bright.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 显而易见的；非常明显的； blinding blindingly You use blinding to emphasize that something is very obvious.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 痛苦强烈的，巨大的； blinding Blinding pain is very strong pain.
blindly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 盲目地；未经思考地； blindly See also: blind ; If you say that someone does something blindly , you mean that they do it without having enough information, or without thinking about it.
blind spot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无视；一无所知； blind spot If you say that someone has a blind spot about something, you mean that they seem to be unable to understand it or to see how important it is.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 视线内的盲点，看不到的地方，死角； A blind spot is an area in your range of vision that you cannot see properly but which you really should be able to see.
blind trust: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指议会成员等为防止被指责滥用职权而对自己的投资进行的保密委托，全权信托； blind trust A blind trust is a financial arrangement in which someone's investments are managed without the person knowing where the money is invested.
bling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 昂贵的珠宝；高档首饰； bling Some people refer to expensive or fancy jewellery as bling or bling-bling .
blink: [VERB 动词] 眨眼； blink When you blink or when you blink your eyes, you shut your eyes and very quickly open them again.  /  [VERB 动词] 灯光闪烁，闪动，忽明忽灭； blink When a light blinks , it flashes on and off.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 一眨眼的工夫；转眼之间；瞬间； blink If you say that something happens in the blink of an eye , you mean that it happens very quickly.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 机器不能正常工作，出故障，出毛病； blink If a machine goes on the blink , it stops working properly.
blinkered: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 看法、态度、方法狭隘的，有偏见的；人心胸狭窄的； blinkered A blinkered view, attitude, or approach is narrow and does not take into account other people's opinions.
blinkers: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 有色眼镜，眼罩比喻观点狭隘，不考虑他人的想法； blinkers If you describe someone as wearing blinkers , you think that they have a narrow point of view and are not taking other people's opinions into account.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 系于马眼旁使其只能直视的马眼罩； Blinkers are two pieces of leather which are placed at the side of a horse's eyes so that it can only see straight ahead.
blip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雷达等仪器屏幕上的伴有短促尖声的光点，信号； A blip is a small spot of light, sometimes occurring with a short, high-pitched sound, which flashes on and off regularly on a piece of equipment such as a radar screen.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 直线上的转折点，跳点； A blip in a straight line, such as the line on a graph, is a point at which the line suddenly makes a sharp change of direction before returning to its original direction.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 暂时的突变；突然的中断； blip A blip in a situation is a sudden but temporary change or interruption in it.
bliss: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 巨大的幸福；极乐； bliss Bliss is a state of complete happiness.
blissful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极为高兴的；极乐的； blissful blissfully A blissful situation or period of time is one in which you are extremely happy.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 对不好或严重的事情丝毫没有察觉的，毫不知情的； blissful blissfully If someone is in blissful ignorance of something unpleasant or serious, they are totally unaware of it.
blister: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 皮肤上因烫伤或反复摩擦而起的水疱； A blister is a painful swelling on the surface of your skin.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使皮肤长水疱； blister When your skin blisters or when something blisters it, blisters appear on it.
blistering: [ADJ 形容词] 酷热的；炎热的； blistering Blistering heat is very great heat.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 评论严厉的，愤怒的，尖刻的； blistering A blistering remark expresses great anger or dislike.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 体育动作飞快的，强劲的，有力量的； blistering Blistering is used to describe actions in sport to emphasize that they are done with great speed or force.
blithe: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻率的；欠考虑的；漫不经心的； blithe blithely You use blithe to indicate that something is done casually, without serious or careful thought.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无忧无虑的；快乐无忧的； blithe Someone who is blithe is cheerful and has no serious problems.
blitz: [VERB 动词] 以闪电战空袭；以闪电战攻击； blitz If a city or building is blitzed during a war, it is attacked by bombs dropped by enemy aircraft.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] 德军对英国城市的空袭，伦敦大轰炸1940年至1941年间； The heavy bombing of British cities by German aircraft in 1940 and 1941 is referred to as the Blitz .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 努力；下工夫； blitz If you have a blitz on something, you make a big effort to deal with it or to improve it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 为吸引注意力的大规模活动； blitz An advertising or publicity blitz is a major effort to make the public aware of something.
blitzkrieg: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 闪电战；奇袭战； A blitzkrieg is a fast and intense military attack that takes the enemy by surprise and is intended to achieve a very quick victory.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 体育运动中的猛攻；政治、广告宣传等中声势迅猛的活动，铺天盖地的行动； blitzkrieg Journalists sometimes refer to a rapid and powerful attack or campaign in, for example, sport, politics, or advertising as a blitzkrieg .
blizzard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大风雪；暴风雪； A blizzard is a very bad snowstorm with strong winds.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 指令人反感或恼火的事情大量，铺天盖地； blizzard You can refer to a large number of things that you do not like or which annoy you as a blizzard of those things.
bloated: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 身体或身体某部位肿胀的，膨胀的，发胀的； bloated If someone's body or a part of their body is bloated , it is much larger than normal, usually because it has a lot of liquid or gas inside it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 吃撑了的；肚子胀的； bloated If you feel bloated after eating a large meal, you feel very full and uncomfortable.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 机构臃肿的，人浮于事的； bloated If you describe an organization as bloated , you mean that it is larger and less efficient than it should be.
bloating: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 身体的肿胀，膨胀； bloating Bloating is the swelling of a body or part of a body, usually because it has a lot of gas or liquid in it.
blob: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 黏稠液体的一滴，一团； blob A blob of thick or sticky liquid is a small, often round, amount of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 模糊不清的一团，一点； blob You can use blob to refer to something that you cannot see very clearly, for example because it is in the distance.
bloc: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 国家集团；阵营；共同体； bloc See also: en bloc ; A bloc is a group of countries which have similar political aims and interests and that act together over some issues.
block: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大楼；大厦； block A block of flats or offices is a large building containing them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 街区； block A block in a town is an area of land with streets on all its sides.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 长方形块，大块； block A block of a substance is a large rectangular piece of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 阻塞，堵塞道路、管道等； block To block a road, channel, or pipe means to put an object across it or in it so that nothing can pass through it or along it.
blockade: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 封锁；阻塞； blockade A blockade of a place is an action that is taken to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving it.  /  [VERB 动词] 阻塞；封锁； blockade If a group of people blockade a place, they stop goods or people from reaching that place.
blockage: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 堵塞物；障碍物；堵塞； blockage A blockage in a pipe, tube, or tunnel is an object which blocks it, or the state of being blocked.
blockbuster: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轰动一时的电影；一度热卖的畅销书； A blockbuster is a film or book that is very popular and successful, usually because it is very exciting.
blockbusting: [ADJ 形容词] 电影轰动一时的；书畅销一时的； blockbusting A blockbusting film or book is one that is very successful, usually because it is very exciting.
block capitals: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 正体大写字母；无衬线字体大写字母； Block capitals are simple capital letters that are not decorated in any way.
block in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…的车堵住；使…的车无法开出； If you are blocked in , someone has parked their car in such a way that you cannot drive yours away.
block letters: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 同block capitals； Block letters are the same as block capitals .
block off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 封闭，封住门、窗或通道； When you block off a door, window, or passage, you put something across it so that nothing can pass through it.
block out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 不去想；设法忘记； If someone blocks out a thought, they try not to think about it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 挡住，遮挡光线； Something that blocks out light prevents it from reaching a place.
block up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使封闭；使堵住；使封死； block up If you block something up or if it blocks up , it is blocked completely so that nothing can get through it.
block vote: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 由一人代表大量选民投的集团投票； A block vote is a large number of votes that are all cast in the same way by one person on behalf of a group of people.
blog: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 博客；部落格；网络日志； blog blogger blogging A blog is a website containing a diary or journal on a particular subject.
blogosphere: 博客世界；博客圈； blogosphere In computer technology, the blogosphere or the blogsphere is all the weblogs on the Internet, considered collectively.
bloke: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人；家伙； bloke A bloke is a man.
blonde: [COLOUR 颜色词] 头发金色，浅棕色，浅黄色； blonde A woman who has blonde hair has pale-coloured hair.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 金发的；浅色头发的； blonde Someone who is blonde has blonde hair.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 金发女郎； A blonde is a woman who has blonde hair.
blonde bombshell: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 金发美女； Journalists sometimes use blonde bombshell to refer to a woman with blonde hair who is very attractive.
blood: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 血；血液； Blood is the red liquid that flows inside your body, which you can see if you cut yourself.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 血统；出身；门第；家世； blood You can use blood to refer to the race or social class of someone's parents or ancestors.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 仇恨；憎恶感；厌恶感； blood If you say that there is bad blood between people, you mean that they have argued about something and dislike each other.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 要求惩罚；要求严惩； blood If you say that people are baying for blood , you mean that they are demanding that someone should be hurt or punished.
blood and thunder: [ADJ 形容词] 表演紧张激烈的，震耳欲聋的；表演者充满感情的； A blood and thunder performer or performance is very loud and emotional.
blood bank: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 血库； A blood bank is a place where blood which has been taken from blood donors is stored until it is needed for people in hospital.
bloodbath: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大屠杀；血洗； bloodbath If you describe an event as a bloodbath , you are emphasizing that a lot of people were killed very violently.
blood brother: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 结拜兄弟；歃血为盟的兄弟； A man's blood brother is a man he has sworn to treat as a brother, often in a ceremony which involves mixing a small amount of their blood.
blood count: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 血球计数；血细胞计数；血球计数检查； blood count Your blood count is the number of red and white cells in your blood.
bloodcurdling: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人毛骨悚然的；让人深感恐惧的； bloodcurdling A blood-curdling sound or story is very frightening and horrible.
blood-curdling: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人毛骨悚然的；让人深感恐惧的； blood-curdling A blood-curdling sound or story is very frightening and horrible.
blood donor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 献血者；捐血人； A blood donor is someone who gives some of their blood so that it can be used in operations.
blood feud: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 世仇；宿仇；血海深仇； A blood feud is a long-lasting, bitter disagreement between two or more groups of people, particularly family groups.
blood group: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 血型； Someone's blood group is the type of blood that they have in their body.
blood heat: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人体血温；人体正常温度； Blood heat is a temperature of 37˚C, which is about the same as the normal temperature of the human body.

blood-letting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤指敌军之间的武力冲突，流血事件，杀戮； blood-letting Blood-letting is violence or killing between groups of people, especially between rival armies.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 新闻用语内讧，同室操戈； Journalists sometimes refer to a bitter quarrel between two groups of people from within the same organization as blood-letting .
bloodline: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 血统；世系；遗传； A person's bloodline is their ancestors over many generations, and the characteristics they are believed to have inherited from these ancestors.
blood lust: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 嗜血；杀戮欲； If you say that someone is driven by a blood lust , you mean that they are acting in an extremely violent way because their emotions have been aroused by the events around them.

blood poisoning: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 败血症；血中毒； Blood poisoning is a serious illness resulting from an infection in your blood.
blood pressure: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 血压； blood pressure Your blood pressure is the amount of force with which your blood flows around your body.
blood pudding: [N-VAR 可变名词] 同black pudding； Blood pudding is another word for black pudding .
blood-red: [COLOUR 颜色词] 血红色；鲜红色； blood-red Something that is blood-red is bright red in colour.

bloodstock: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 为赛马培育的纯种马； Horses that are bred for racing are referred to as bloodstock .
bloodstream: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 血流；血液； bloodstream Your bloodstream is the blood that flows around your body.
bloodsucker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吸血动物；吸血虫； A bloodsucker is any creature that sucks blood from a wound that it has made in an animal or person.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吸血鬼；剥削者； bloodsucker If you call someone a bloodsucker , you disapprove of them because you think they do not do anything worthwhile but live off the efforts of other people.
blood test: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 验血； A blood test is a medical examination of a small amount of your blood.

blood transfusion: [N-VAR 可变名词] 输血； A blood transfusion is a process in which blood is injected into the body of a person who is badly injured or ill.
blood type: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同blood group； Someone's blood type is the same as their blood group .
blood vessel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 血管； Blood vessels are the narrow tubes through which your blood flows.
bloody: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 尤用于生气时加强语气该死的，讨厌的； Bloody is used by some people to emphasize what they are saying, especially when they are angry.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 血腥的；暴力的； bloody bloodily If you describe a situation or event as bloody , you mean that it is very violent and a lot of people are killed.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 血淋淋的；血迹斑斑的； bloody bloodily You can describe someone or something as bloody if they are covered in a lot of blood.  /  [VERB 动词] 使流血；使出血； If you have bloodied part of your body, there is blood on it, usually because you have had an accident or you have been attacked.

boat train: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 往返于港口间接送旅客的港口联运火车，水陆联运列车； A boat train is a train that takes you to or from a port.
boatyard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 造船厂；船坞；修船厂； boatyard A boatyard is a place where boats are built and repaired or kept.
bob: [VERB 动词] 像物体在水中飘浮似的上下移动，起伏； bob If something bobs , it moves up and down, like something does when it is floating on water.  /  [VERB 动词] 快速移动；突然消失或出现； bob If you bob somewhere, you move there quickly so that you disappear from view or come into view.  /  [VERB 动词] 快速点头如打招呼等； bob When you bob your head, you move it quickly up and down once, for example when you greet someone.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 英国旧时货币单位先令； bob In Britain, people used to refer to a shilling as a bob .
bobbed: [ADJ 形容词] 女子头发齐短式的，蘑菇头的； If a woman's hair is bobbed , it is cut in a bob.
bobbin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 缝纫机等的线轴，绕线筒； A bobbin is a small round object on which thread or wool is wound to hold it, for example on a sewing machine.
bobble: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 用来装饰衣物的小绒球，小羊毛球； bobble A bobble is a small ball of material, usually made of wool, which is used for decorating clothes.  /  [VERB 动词] 球不规则移动，乱动； bobble If a ball bobbles , it moves in an irregular and uncontrolled way.  /  [VERB 动词] 失掉[球]; 漏接球； bobble If a player bobbles a ball, they drop it or fail to control it.
bobble hat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 顶部有绒球的羊毛帽，毛绒帽； A bobble hat is a woollen hat with a bobble on it.
bobby: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 英国级别最低的警员，警察； bobby A bobby is a British policeman, usually of the lowest rank.
bobby pin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小发夹； A bobby pin is a small piece of metal or plastic bent back on itself, which someone uses to hold their hair in position.
bobcat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 短尾猫，红猫，山猫一种北美野猫； A bobcat is an animal in the cat family which has reddish-brown fur with dark spots or stripes and a short tail.
bobsled: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 bobsleigh； A bobsled is the same as a bobsleigh .
bobsleigh: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑雪比赛用的雪橇； A bobsleigh is a vehicle with long thin strips of metal fixed to the bottom, which is used for racing downhill on ice.
bod: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人；家伙； bod A bod is a person.
bode: [VERB 动词] 预示[好事或坏事]; 是…的兆头； bode If something bodes ill, it makes you think that something bad will happen in the future.
bodge: [VERB 动词] 粗制滥造；拙劣地修补； bodge If you bodge something, you make it or mend it in a way that is not as good as it should be.
bodice: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连衣裙上身； bodice The bodice of a dress is the part above the waist.
bodice ripper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 以旧时生活为背景的情色电影，艳情小说； You can refer to a film or novel which is set in the past and which includes a lot of sex scenes as a bodice ripper , especially if you do not think it is very good and is just intended to entertain people.
bodice-ripping: [ADJ 形容词] 以旧时生活为背景的电影或小说色情暴露的，充斥性爱内容的； bodice-ripping A bodice-ripping film or novel is one which is set in the past and which includes a lot of sex scenes.
bodily: [ADJ 形容词] 身体的；肉体的； bodily See also: grievous bodily harm ; Your bodily needs and functions are the needs and functions of your body.  /  [ADV 副词] 整个身体地；全身地； bodily You use bodily to indicate that an action involves the whole of someone's body.
bodily function: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人体生理功能；尤指人体排泄功能； bodily function A person's bodily functions are the normal physical processes that regularly occur in their body, particularly the ability to urinate and defecate.
body: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 身体；人体； body Your body is all your physical parts, including your head, arms, and legs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 躯干[不包括头和四肢]; 躯体； body You can also refer to the main part of your body, except for your arms, head, and legs, as your body .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人的尸体； body You can refer to a person's dead body as a body .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 团体；机构；组织； body A body is an organized group of people who deal with something officially.
body armour: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 军人、警察等穿的防弹衣，防护服； Body armour is special protective clothing which people such as soldiers and police officers sometimes wear when they are in danger of being attacked with guns or other weapons.
body bag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 运尸袋； body bag A body bag is a specially designed large plastic bag which is used to carry a dead body away, for example when someone has been killed in a battle or an accident.
body blow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沉重的打击；重大挫折； body blow A body blow is something that causes great disappointment and difficulty to someone who is trying to achieve something.
bodybuilder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 健美运动员；健身爱好者； A bodybuilder is a person who does special exercises regularly in order to make his or her muscles grow bigger.
bodybuilding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 健美运动；健身； Bodybuilding is the activity of doing special exercises regularly in order to make your muscles grow bigger.
body clock: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人体生物钟，生理时钟； body clock Your body clock is the internal biological mechanism which causes your body to automatically behave in particular ways at particular times of the day.
bodyguard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保镖；警卫队； bodyguard A bodyguard is a person or a group of people employed to protect someone.
body language: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 身体语言；肢体语言； Your body language is the way in which you show your feelings or thoughts to other people by means of the position or movements of your body, rather than with words.
body mass index: [N-SING 单数名词] 体重指数； body mass index A person's body mass index is a measurement that represents the relationship between their weight and their height.
body odour: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 汗臭；体臭； Body odour is an unpleasant smell caused by sweat on a person's body.
body politic: [N-SING 单数名词] 视为政治整体的全体国民，人民； body politic The body politic is all the people of a nation when they are considered as a complete political group.
body search: [VERB 动词] 对…搜身；对…进行搜身检查； body search If a person is body searched , someone such as a police officer searches them while they remain clothed.
body stocking: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 舞蹈演员经常穿的紧身内衣，连体紧身衣； A body stocking is a piece of clothing that covers the whole of someone's body and fits tightly.
bodysuit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女式紧身衣； A bodysuit is a piece of women's clothing that fits tightly over the top part of the body and fastens between the legs.
bodywork: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 机动车的车身，外壳； bodywork The bodywork of a motor vehicle is the outside part of it.
Boer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 布尔人南非荷兰移民的后裔； The Boers are the descendants of the Dutch people who went to live in South Africa.
boffin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指从事研究工作的科学家，科技工作者； boffin A boffin is a scientist, especially one who is doing research.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 奇才；天才； boffin Very clever people are sometimes called boffins .
bog: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沼泽；湿地；泥塘； A bog is an area of land which is very wet and muddy.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 厕所；茅厕； The bog is another name for the toilet.  /  相关词组： bog down �
bog down: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使拖延；使停滞不前； See also: bogged down ; If a plan or process bogs down or if something bogs it down , it is delayed and no progress is made.
bogey: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 令人谈之色变的事物；让人担心的人； bogey A bogey is something or someone that people are worried about, perhaps without much cause or reason.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 干鼻屎； A bogey is a piece of dried mucus that comes from inside your nose.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 高尔夫球比标准杆数多一杆的进球； In golf, when a player scores a bogey at a hole, he or she takes one more shot than the standard that has been fixed for that hole.
bogeyman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 怪人；怪物；坏蛋； bogeyman A bogeyman is someone whose ideas or actions are disapproved of by some people, and who is described by them as evil or unpleasant in order to make other people afraid.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 父母用来吓唬小孩的鬼怪，妖怪； A bogeyman is an imaginary evil spirit.
bogged down: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 深陷泥沼的；停滞不前的； bogged down If you get bogged down in something, it prevents you from making progress or getting something done.
boggle: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 思想困惑；使无法想象；使难以理解； boggle See also: mind-boggling ; If you say that the mind boggles at something or that something boggles the mind, you mean that it is so strange or amazing that it is difficult to imagine or understand.
boggy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 地面泥泞的，沼泽般的； Boggy land is very wet and muddy land.
bog-standard: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无新意的；无特色的；普通的； bog-standard If you describe something as bog-standard you mean that is an ordinary example of its kind, with no exciting or interesting features.
bogus: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 假的；冒牌的；伪造的； bogus If you describe something as bogus , you mean that it is not genuine.
Bohemian: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 艺术家波希米亚风格的，不拘于传统的，放荡不羁的； bohemian 生活放荡不羁的人 You can use bohemian to describe artistic people who live in an unconventional way.
boil: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使达到沸点；使沸腾；使烧开； boil When a hot liquid boils or when you boil it, bubbles appear in it and it starts to change into steam or vapour.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使水壶或锅里的水烧开； boil When you boil a kettle or pan, or put it on to boil , you heat the water inside it until it boils.  /  [VERB 动词] 水壶或平底锅里的水烧开，沸腾； boil When a kettle or pan is boiling , the water inside it has reached boiling point.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 用开水煮；在开水中煮；  boil When you boil food, or when it boils , it is cooked in boiling water.
boil away: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使煮干； boil away When you boil away a liquid, or when it boils away , it is boiled until all of it changes into steam or vapour.
boil down: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 液体或食物煮稠；把…熬稠； boil down When you boil down a liquid or food, or when it boils down , it is boiled until there is less of it because some of the water in it has changed into steam or vapour.
boil down to: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 重点是；将…归结为； If you say that a situation or problem boils down to a particular thing or can be boiled down to a particular thing, you mean that this is the most important or the most basic aspect of it.
boiled sweet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 高温熬制的硬糖； Boiled sweets are hard sweets that are made from boiled sugar.
boiler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指为建筑物提供集中供暖的汽锅，锅炉； A boiler is a device which burns gas, oil, electricity, or coal in order to provide hot water, especially for the central heating in a building.
boiler suit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连体工作服； A boiler suit consists of a single piece of clothing that combines trousers and a jacket.
boiling: [ADJ 形容词] 炎热的；酷热的； boiling Something that is boiling or boiling hot is very hot.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 感觉极热的；热得难受的；  boiling If you say that you are boiling or boiling hot , you mean that you feel very hot, usually unpleasantly hot.
boiling point: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 沸点； boiling point The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which it starts to change into steam or vapour.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 局势的爆发点； boiling point If a situation reaches boiling point , the people involved have become so angry that they can no longer remain calm and in control of themselves.
boil over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 沸溢；潽出； boil over When a liquid that is being heated boils over , it rises and flows over the edge of the container.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 感情爆发；失去理智；大怒； boil over When someone's feelings boil over , they lose their temper or become violent.
boil up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…煮沸； boil up If you boil up a liquid, you heat it until it boils.
boisterous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 喧闹的；活泼的；精力充沛的； boisterous boisterously Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.
bold: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 大胆的；勇敢的；无畏的； bold boldly boldness Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 在众人面前大胆的，放肆的，莽撞的； bold boldly Someone who is bold is not shy or embarrassed in the company of other people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 色彩或图案明亮的，醒目的； bold boldly A bold colour or pattern is very bright and noticeable.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (线条) 粗重的；图案清晰的； bold Bold lines or designs are drawn in a clear, strong way.
bolero: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女士无袖短外套，短上衣； A bolero is a very short jacket, sometimes without sleeves.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 波莱罗舞一种西班牙传统舞蹈； bolero The bolero is a traditional Spanish dance.
Bolivian: [ADJ 形容词] 玻利维亚的；玻利维亚人的； 玻利维亚人 Bolivian means belonging or relating to Bolivia or its people.
bollard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 防止汽车驶入私人领地或进入某段公路的水泥隔离柱，短柱，护柱； Bollards are short thick concrete posts that are used to prevent cars from going on to someone's land or on to part of a road.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 河岸或港口的系船柱，系缆桩； Bollards are strong wooden or metal posts on the side of a river or harbour.
bollocks: [EXCLAM; N-UNCOUNT 感叹词；不可数名词] 玩儿蛋去，见鬼去用于表达反对、讨厌或恼火； Bollocks is used by some people to express disagreement, dislike, or annoyance.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 睾丸； A man's bollocks are his testicles.
Bolshevik: [ADJ 形容词] 布尔什维克的；布尔什维克主义的； Bolshevik Bolshevik is used to describe the political system and ideas that Lenin and his supporters introduced in Russia after the Russian Revolution of 1917.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 布尔什维克；布尔什维克主义者； A Bolshevik was a person who supported Lenin and his political ideas.
Bolshevism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 布尔什维克主义； Bolshevism is the political system and ideas that Lenin and his supporters introduced in Russia after the Russian Revolution of 1917.
bolshy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易怒的；不合作的； bolshy If you say that someone is bolshy , you mean that they easily get angry and often do not do what other people want them to do.
bolster: [VERB 动词] 增强[信心]; 鼓舞士气； bolster If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it.  /  [VERB 动词] 巩固[地位]; 加强； bolster bolster up同bolster If someone tries to bolster their position in a situation, they try to strengthen it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 垫在普通枕头下的长枕，垫枕； A bolster is a firm pillow shaped like a long tube which is sometimes put across a bed under the ordinary pillows.  /  相关词组： bolster up �
bolt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 螺栓； A bolt is a long metal object which screws into a nut and is used to fasten things together.  /  [VERB 动词] 用螺栓固定；闩上； bolt When you bolt one thing to another, you fasten them firmly together, using a bolt.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 门、窗的金属插销，闩； bolt A bolt on a door or window is a metal bar that you can slide across in order to fasten the door or window.  /  [VERB 动词] 闩上门、窗； bolt When you bolt a door or window, you slide the bolt across to fasten it.
bolthole: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 躲避处；藏身地； If you say that someone has a bolt-hole to go to, you mean that there is somewhere that they can go when they want to get away from people that they know.
bolt-hole: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 躲避处；藏身地； bolt-hole If you say that someone has a bolt-hole to go to, you mean that there is somewhere that they can go when they want to get away from people that they know.
bolt-on: [ADJ 形容词] 采购追加的，附加的； bolt-on Bolt-on buys are purchases of other companies that a company makes in order to add them to its existing business.
bomb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 炸弹；爆炸装置； bomb A bomb is a device which explodes and damages or destroys a large area.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 核武器；核弹； bomb Nuclear weapons are sometimes referred to as the bomb .  /  [VERB 动词] 轰炸；向…投炸弹； bomb bombing When people bomb a place, they attack it with bombs.  /  See also: petrol bomb ; pipe bomb ;
bombard: [VERB 动词] 连珠炮似的质问[或批评]; 使大量面对； bombard If you bombard someone with something, you make them face a great deal of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 用炮火或炸弹猛烈轰击或攻击； bombard When soldiers bombard a place, they attack it with continuous heavy gunfire or bombs.
bombardment: [N-VAR 可变名词] 猛烈而持久的炮击，轰炸； bombardment A bombardment is a strong and continuous attack of gunfire or bombing.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 一连串想法、要求、质问或批评； bombardment A bombardment of ideas, demands, questions, or criticisms is an aggressive and exhausting stream of them.
bombast: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 夸夸其谈；大放厥词； bombast Bombast is trying to impress people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.
bombastic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 夸夸其谈的；大话连篇的；词藻华丽空洞的； bombastic If you describe someone as bombastic , you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.
bomb disposal: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 未爆炸弹处理； bomb disposal Bomb disposal is the job of dealing with bombs which have not exploded, by taking out the fuse or by blowing them up in a controlled explosion.
bombed-out: [ADJ 形容词] 被炸弹炸毁的； bombed-out A bombed-out building has been damaged or destroyed by a bomb.
bomber: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轰炸机； bomber A bomber is a military aircraft which drops bombs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 在公共场所引爆炸弹的人； bomber Bombers are people who cause bombs to explode in public places.
bomber jacket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 紧腰短夹克； bomber jacket A bomber jacket is a short jacket which is gathered into a band at the waist or hips.
bomb out: [PHR-V-PASSIVE 被动动词短语] 建筑物、地区、家园被炸毁；被炸得无家可归； See also: bombed-out ; If a building or area is bombed out , it is destroyed by bombs.
bombshell: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 意外的坏消息；出乎意料的消息； bombshell 投下一枚重磅炸弹；带来令人意外的坏消息 See also: blonde bombshell ; A bombshell is a sudden piece of bad or unexpected news.
bomb site: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 炸弹爆炸后的废墟； 轰炸后的废墟； bomb site A bomb site is an empty area where a bomb has destroyed all the buildings.
bona fide: [ADJ 形容词] 真实的；真正的；名副其实的； bona fide If something or someone is bona fide , they are genuine or real.
bona fides: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 善意；诚意；真诚； bona fides Someone's bona fides are their good or sincere intentions.
bonanza: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 财运；鸿运；好运； bonanza You can refer to a sudden great increase in wealth, success, or luck as a bonanza .

border on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 接近；近似； See also: border ; If you talk about a characteristic or situation bordering on something, usually something that you consider bad, you mean that it is almost that thing.

born: [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 出生；诞生；为…所生； born When a baby is born , it comes out of its mother's body at the beginning of its life.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 生下来[有某种疾病或问题]; 天生具有某种性格； born If someone is born with a particular disease, problem, or characteristic, they have it from the time they are born.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 用于姓名前出生取名…的； born You can use be born in front of a particular name to show that a person was given this name at birth, although they may be better known by another name.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 天生的； born You use born to describe someone who has a natural ability to do a particular activity or job.

borstal: [N-VAR 可变名词] 英国旧时的少年管教所，少年犯感化院； In Britain in the past, a borstal was a kind of prison for young criminals, who were not old enough to be sent to ordinary prisons.
bosom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女子的乳房； bosom A woman's breasts are sometimes referred to as her bosom or her bosoms .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 怀抱；关怀； bosom If you are in the bosom of your family or of a community, you are among people who love, accept, and protect you.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 朋友知心的，亲密的； bosom A bosom friend is a friend who you know very well and like very much indeed.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 接纳；关怀；关爱； bosom If you take someone or something to your bosom , you accept them and treat or regard them with great affection.
boss: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 老板；上司； boss Your boss is the person in charge of the organization or department where you work.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 领导；头儿；发号施令者； boss If you are the boss in a group or relationship, you are the person who makes all the decisions.  /  [VERB 动词] 对…颐指气使；对…指手画脚； boss boss around,boss about英国英语同boss If you say that someone bosses you, you mean that they keep telling you what to do in a way that is irritating.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 为自己打工；自己拿主意； boss If you are your own boss , you work for yourself or make your own decisions and do not have anyone telling you what to do.

botany: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 植物学； Botany is the scientific study of plants.

bother: [VERB 动词] 操心；费力；麻烦； bother If you do not bother to do something or if you do not bother with it, you do not do it, consider it, or use it because you think it is unnecessary or because you are too lazy.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麻烦；不便；麻烦事； bother Bother means trouble or difficulty.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麻烦用于淡化问题的严重性； bother You use bother to refer to serious trouble, usually when you want to make it sound less serious than it really is.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使烦恼；使担忧；使不安； bother bothered If something bothers you, or if you bother about it, it worries, annoys, or upsets you.

bottle-green: [COLOUR 颜色词] 深绿色的； Something that is bottle-green is dark green in colour.
bottleneck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 瓶颈路段；狭窄路段；交通拥堵地段； A bottleneck is a place where a road becomes narrow or where it meets another road so that the traffic slows down or stops, often causing traffic jams.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 阻碍进展的瓶颈，障碍； bottleneck A bottleneck is a situation that stops a process or activity from progressing.

bottler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 装瓶工人；装瓶公司； A bottler is a person or company that puts drinks into bottles.

bottle up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 压抑，抑制强烈的感情； bottle up If you bottle up strong feelings, you do not express them or show them, especially when this makes you tense or angry.
bottom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 底；底部； bottom The bottom of something is the lowest or deepest part of it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 最下方的；底部的；底层的； bottom The bottom thing or layer in a series of things or layers is the lowest one.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 底面；内底面；外底面； bottom The bottom of an object is the flat surface at its lowest point.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] [某市场或产业的)最差状况，低谷； bottom If you say that the bottom has dropped or fallen out of a market or industry, you mean that people have stopped buying the products it sells.
-bottomed: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] 用于形容词或名词后构成形容词表示“有…底的”； -bottomed -bottomed can be added to adjectives or nouns to form adjectives that indicate what kind of bottom an object or person has.

bout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 疾病或不愉快情绪的发作； bout If you have a bout of an illness or of an unpleasant feeling, you have it for a short period.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不愉快之事大量发生的一阵，一小段时间； bout A bout of something that is unpleasant is a short time during which it occurs a great deal.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拳击比赛；摔跤比赛； bout A bout is a boxing or wrestling match.  /  [当about的第一个音节不发音时，有些作家以'bout或bout替代about] ； bout Some writers use ' bout or bout to represent about when the first syllable is not pronounced.
boutique: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 时尚商店；时装店；精品店； A boutique is a small shop that sells fashionable clothes, shoes, or jewellery.

bow: [VERB 动词] 鞠躬，欠身打招呼或表示恭敬； bow When you bow to someone, you briefly bend your body towards them as a formal way of greeting them or showing respect.  /  [VERB 动词] 低[头]; 俯首； bow If you bow your head, you bend it downwards so that you are looking towards the ground, for example because you want to show respect or because you are thinking deeply about something.  /  [VERB 动词] 向压力或他人的意愿让步；屈从于；屈服于； bow If you bow to pressure or to someone's wishes, you agree to do what they want you to do.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 使沮丧；使不安；使无望； bow be bowed down同be bowed If you are bowed by something, you are made unhappy and anxious by it, and lose hope.
bowdlerize: [VERB 动词] 删除，删改书或电影中的部分； To bowdlerize a book or film means to take parts of it out before publishing it or showing it.

bowed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 成弓形的；弯曲的； bowed Something that is bowed is curved.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 弯腰曲背的；佝偻的； bowed See also: bow ; If a person's body is bowed , it is bent forward.
bowel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肠； Your bowels are the tubes in your body through which digested food passes from your stomach to your anus.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 大便； You can refer in a polite way to someone getting rid of the waste from their body by saying that they move, open, or empty their bowels .  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 内部；深处； bowel You can refer to the parts deep inside something such as the earth, a building, or a machine as the bowels of that thing.
bower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 花园或树林中的树阴，阴凉处； A bower is a shady, leafy shelter in a garden or wood.
bowl: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 碗；钵；盆； bowl A bowl is a round container with a wide uncovered top.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一碗之量； bowl The contents of a bowl can be referred to as a bowl of something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 碗状部分； bowl You can refer to the hollow rounded part of an object as its bowl .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 草地滚木球运动； Bowls is a game in which players try to roll large wooden balls as near as possible to a small wooden ball.

bowler hat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指过去英国商人戴的黑色圆顶硬呢帽； A bowler hat is a round, hard, black hat with a narrow brim which is worn by men, especially British businessmen.
bowlful: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一碗之量； bowlful The contents of a bowl can be referred to as a bowlful of something.
bowling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 保龄球运动； bowling Bowling is a game in which you roll a heavy ball down a narrow track towards a group of wooden objects and try to knock down as many of them as possible.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 板球等运动中的投球； In a sport such as cricket, bowling is the action or activity of bowling the ball towards the batsman.

bow out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 退出； If you bow out of something, you stop taking part in it.
bow tie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指男士在正式场合戴的蝴蝶领结； A bow tie is a tie in the form of a bow.

boxed: [ADJ 形容词] 盒装的； boxed See also: box ; A boxed set or collection of things is sold in a box.
boxer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拳击运动员；拳击选手； A boxer is someone who takes part in the sport of boxing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拳师狗； A boxer is a dog with short hair and a rather flat face.
boxer shorts: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 男式宽松平脚短裤类似拳击短裤； Boxer shorts are loose-fitting men's underpants that are shaped like the shorts worn by boxers.

boxing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 拳击运动； boxing Boxing is a sport in which two people wearing large padded gloves fight according to special rules.

box lunch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 盒装午餐；午餐盒饭； A box lunch is food, for example sandwiches, which you take to work, to school, or on a trip and eat as your lunch.
box number: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 邮政信箱号码； A box number is a number used as an address, for example one given by a newspaper for replies to a private advertisement, or one used by an organization for the letters sent to it.

boxy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 方形的；四四方方的； boxy Something that is boxy is similar to a square in shape and usually plain.
boy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男孩；男童； boy A boy is a child who will grow up to be a man.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男青年，小伙子尤用于指青年男女恋爱关系时； boy You can refer to a young man as a boy , especially when talking about relationships between boys and girls.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 儿子； boy Someone's boy is their son.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 家伙，伙计尤用于亲切谈论某人时； boy You can refer to a man as a boy , especially when you are talking about him in an affectionate way.

boy racer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指驾驶昂贵的高性能汽车的飙车小子，飙车手； boy racer British journalists sometimes refer to young men who drive very fast, especially in expensive and powerful cars, as boy racers .
Boy Scout: [N-PROPER-COLL 专有集合名词] 童子军； The Boy Scouts is an organization for boys which teaches them discipline and practical skills.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 童子军成员； A Boy Scout is a boy who is a member of the Boy Scouts.

bps: 比特/秒计算机数据传输速度的计量单位； bps bps is a measurement of the speed at which computer data is transferred, for example by a modem.
bra: 胸罩；乳罩； A bra is a piece of underwear that women wear to support their breasts.
brace: [VERB 动词] 使做好准备面对不快的事或困难； brace If you brace yourself for something unpleasant or difficult, you prepare yourself for it.  /  [VERB 动词] 为保持平衡或避免摔倒使紧靠； brace If you brace yourself against something or brace part of your body against it, you press against something in order to steady your body or to avoid falling.  /  [VERB 动词] 绷紧肩或膝； brace If you brace your shoulders or knees, you keep them stiffly in a particular position.  /  [VERB 动词] 支撑；加固； brace To brace something means to strengthen or support it with something else.
bracelet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 手镯； A bracelet is a chain or band, usually made of metal, which you wear around your wrist as jewellery.
bracing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 尤指地方、气候或活动宜人的，提神的，令人心旷神怡的，令人精神焕发的； bracing If you describe something, especially a place, climate, or activity as bracing , you mean that it makes you feel fresh and full of energy.
bracken: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 长在山上或林间的欧洲蕨； Bracken is a large plant with leaves that are divided into many thin sections.
bracket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 收入、年龄、价格等的范围，等级段； bracket If you say that someone or something is in a particular bracket , you mean that they come within a particular range, for example a range of incomes, ages, or prices.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 固定在墙上的托架，支架，角撑架； bracket Brackets are pieces of metal, wood, or plastic that are fastened to a wall in order to support something such as a shelf.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…归为一类；把…相提并论； bracket If two or more people or things are bracketed together , they are considered to be similar or related in some way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 括号，括弧[美国英语中称作parentheses] ； bracket Brackets are a pair of written marks that you place round a word, expression, or sentence in order to indicate that you are giving extra information.
brackish: [ADJ 形容词] (水) 稍咸的，味道不好的； brackish Brackish water is slightly salty and unpleasant.
brag: [VERB 动词] 吹嘘；夸耀； brag If you brag , you say in a very proud way that you have something or have done something.
Brahmin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 婆罗门印度社会等级中的最高等级成员； A Brahmin is a Hindu of the highest social rank.

braided: [ADJ 形容词] 衣服用穗带装饰的； A piece of clothing that is braided is decorated with braid.
Braille: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 布莱叶盲文点字法； Braille is a system of printing for blind people.
brain: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脑；大脑； brain Your brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 头脑；智力； brain Your brain is your mind and the way that you think.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 智力；智慧；头脑； brain If someone has brains or a good brain , they have the ability to learn and understand things quickly, to solve problems, and to make good decisions.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 智囊；出谋划策者； brain If someone is the brains behind an idea or an organization, he or she had that idea or makes the important decisions about how that organization is managed.
brainchild: [N-SING 单数名词] 思想结晶；创作成果； brainchild Someone's brainchild is an idea or invention that they have thought up or created.
brain damage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 脑损伤； brain damage If someone suffers brain damage , their brain is damaged by an illness or injury so that they cannot function normally.

brain dead: 脑死亡的； If someone is declared brain-dead , they have suffered brain death.  /  死脑筋的；愚蠢的； If you say that someone is brain-dead , you are saying in a cruel way that you think they are very stupid.
brain death: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 脑死亡； Brain death occurs when someone's brain stops functioning, even though their heart may be kept beating using a machine.

brainless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 没头脑的；愚笨的； brainless If you describe someone or something as brainless , you mean that you think they are stupid.
brainpower: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 脑力；智能；智力； brainpower Brainpower is intelligence or the ability to think.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 某组织或国家的人才队伍，人才； brainpower You can refer to the intelligent people in an organization or country as its brainpower .
brainstorm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一时糊涂；头脑发热； brainstorm If you have a brainstorm , you suddenly become unable to think clearly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 突然想到的好主意；灵感； brainstorm If you have a brainstorm , you suddenly have a clever idea.  /  [VERB 动词] 集思广益；集体献计； brainstorm brainstorming If a group of people brainstorm , they have a meeting in which they all put forward as many ideas and suggestions as they can think of.

brainy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脑子好的；聪明的；善于学习的； brainy Someone who is brainy is clever and good at learning.

branch out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 扩大范围；拓展领域； If a person or an organization branches out , they do something that is different from their normal activities or work.

brandy: [N-MASS 物质名词] 白兰地一种烈性酒，常在饭后饮用； Brandy is a strong alcoholic drink.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一杯白兰地； A brandy is a glass of brandy.
brandy snap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 白兰地姜饼，姜味薄脆卷心饼常带奶油夹心； Brandy snaps are very thin crisp biscuits in the shape of hollow cylinders.
brash: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过于自信的；盛气凌人的；自以为是的； brash brashly brashness If you describe someone or their behaviour as brash , you disapprove of them because you think that they are too confident and aggressive.
brass: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤用于制作装饰品和乐器的黄铜； brass Brass is a yellow-coloured metal made from copper and zinc.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 交响乐队的铜管乐乐器组，铜管乐器； brass The brass is the section of an orchestra which consists of brass wind instruments such as trumpets and horns.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 常见于教堂的黄铜纪念牌； See also: brass rubbing ; Brasses are flat pieces of brass with writing or a picture cut into them, which are often found in churches.  /  [N-SING-COLL 单数集合名词] 军队或其他机构的高级军官，高层人物； brass In the army or in other organizations, the brass are the people in the highest positions.
brass band: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 铜管乐队由铜管乐器和打击乐器组成； A brass band is a band that is made up of brass and percussion instruments.

brassica: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 芸苔属植物； Brassicas are vegetables such as cabbages, broccoli and turnips.
brassiere: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同bra； A brassiere is the same as a bra .
brass rubbing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 取自有图文的铜牌上的拓印图，拓片； A brass rubbing is a picture made by placing a piece of paper over a brass plate that has writing or a picture on it, and rubbing it with a wax crayon.
brassy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 音乐刺耳的，吵闹的； brassy Brassy music is bold, harsh, and loud.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 女子没有品位的，打扮花哨的，俗气的； brassy If you describe a woman's appearance or her behaviour as brassy , you think that she does not have good taste, and that she dresses or behaves in a way that is too loud or vulgar.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 黄铜色的； brassy Something that is brassy has a yellow metallic colour and sometimes looks cheap.
brat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 淘气鬼；小捣蛋； brat If you call someone, especially a child, a brat , you mean that he or she behaves badly or annoys you.
brat pack: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 当红新人，成名的年轻人尤指演员或作家； A brat pack is a group of young people, especially actors or writers, who are popular or successful at the moment.
bravado: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 虚张声势；逞能；逞强； bravado Bravado is an appearance of courage or confidence that someone shows in order to impress other people.
brave: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 勇敢的；无畏的； brave bravely Someone who is brave is willing to do things which are dangerous, and does not show fear in difficult or dangerous situations.  /  [VERB 动词] 通常为达到某目标勇敢面对； brave If you brave unpleasant or dangerous conditions, you deliberately expose yourself to them, usually in order to achieve something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指善于作战的印第安勇士； A brave is a young Native American man, especially one who is good at fighting.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 装作高兴；强作欢颜； brave If someone is putting on a brave face or is putting a brave face on a difficult situation, they are pretending that they are happy or satisfied when they are not.
brave new world: [N-SING 单数名词] 美丽新世界指人们认为会带来成功和公平的刚刚出现的新局面或新制度； brave new world If someone refers to a brave new world , they are talking about a situation or system that has recently been created and that people think will be successful and fair.
bravery: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 勇敢；勇气；无畏精神； bravery Bravery is brave behaviour or the quality of being brave.
bravo: [EXCLAM 感叹语] 好，很棒用于表达赞赏； Some people say ' bravo ' to express appreciation when someone has done something well.
bravura: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 卖弄性的技巧；精湛技艺； bravura If you say that someone is doing something with bravura , you mean that they are using unnecessary extra actions that emphasize their skill or importance.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 表演或作品精彩的，华丽的； bravura A bravura performance or piece of work is done with bravura.
brawl: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 打架；斗殴； brawl A brawl is a rough or violent fight.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 打架；斗殴； brawl brawling If someone brawls , they fight in a very rough or violent way.
brawn: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 体力；膂力； brawn Brawn is physical strength.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 碎猪肉冻； Brawn is a kind of food made from pieces of pork and jelly pressed together so that it is solid and can be sliced.
brawny: [ADJ 形容词] 身体强壮的；肌肉发达的； brawny Someone who is brawny is strong and has big muscles.
bray: [VERB 动词] 驴嘶叫； bray When a donkey brays , it makes a loud harsh sound.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出驴叫似的声音；刺耳地高声说话； bray If someone brays , they make a loud harsh sound or talk in a loud harsh way.
brazen: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无所顾忌的；肆无忌惮的； brazen brazenly If you describe a person or their behaviour as brazen , you mean that they are very bold and do not care what other people think about them or their behaviour.  /  相关词组： brazen out �
brazen out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 厚着脸皮，硬着头皮以示不觉羞愧； If you have done something wrong and you brazen it out , you behave confidently in order not to appear ashamed, even though you probably do feel ashamed.
brazier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 金属火盆，炭盆供户外取暖； A brazier is a large metal container in which coal or charcoal is burned to keep people warm when they are outside in cold weather, for example because of their work.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 烤架；烤炉； A brazier is a grill that you use for cooking, usually with charcoal.

breach: [VERB 动词] 违反，破坏条约、法律或承诺； breach If you breach an agreement, a law, or a promise, you break it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 对条约、法律或承诺的违反，破坏； breach A breach of an agreement, a law, or a promise is an act of breaking it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 关系的裂痕，破裂； breach A breach in a relationship is a serious disagreement which often results in the relationship ending.  /  [VERB 动词] 突破；攻破；给…造成缺口； breach If someone or something breaches a barrier, they make an opening in it, usually leaving it weakened or destroyed.
breach of the peace: [N-VAR 可变名词] 扰乱治安； breach of the peace A breach of the peace is noisy or violent behaviour in a public place which is illegal because it disturbs other people.
bread: [N-MASS 物质名词] 面包； bread Bread is a very common food made from flour, water, and yeast.  /  to know what side your bread is buttered on » see: butter  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 通过工作等挣得的钱财，金钱； bread If you earn your bread doing a particular job or activity, you earn your money doing it.  /  [VERB 动词] 给鱼或肉抹面包屑； bread breaded If food such as fish or meat is breaded , it is covered in tiny pieces of dry bread called breadcrumbs.
bread and butter: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 生计；谋生之道；主要收入来源； bread and butter Something that is the bread and butter of a person or organization is the activity or work that provides the main part of their income.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 最基本的；影响到大多数人的； Bread and butter issues or matters are ones which are important to most people, because they affect them personally.
bread basket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一国的产粮区，粮仓； If an area or region is described as the bread basket of a country, it provides a lot of the food for that country because crops grow very easily there.
bread bin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 面包盒； A bread bin is a wooden, metal, or plastic container for storing bread.
breadboard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 切面包板； A breadboard is a flat piece of wood used for cutting bread on.
breadbox: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同bread bin； A breadbox is the same as a bread bin .
breadcrumb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 面包屑； Breadcrumbs are tiny pieces of dry bread.
breadfruit: [N-VAR 可变名词] 面包果生长于太平洋中岛屿和美洲热带地区的面包果树上，形状大而圆，烘烤后形状、口味与面包类似； Breadfruit are large round fruit that grow on trees in the Pacific Islands and in tropical parts of America and that, when baked, look and feel like bread.
breadline: [N-SING 单数名词] 等候领取救济食品的队伍；赤贫线； breadline Someone who is on the breadline is very poor indeed.
breadth: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 宽度； breadth The breadth of something is the distance between its two sides.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 广度；广泛性； breadth The breadth of something is its quality of consisting of or involving many different things.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 到处；处处； breadth If you say that someone does something or something happens throughout or across the length and breadth of a place, you are emphasizing that it happens everywhere in that place.  /  See also: hair's breadth ; �
breadwinner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 养家糊口的人； breadwinner The breadwinner in a family is the person in it who earns the money that the family needs for essential things.
break: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 打破；摔碎； break When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 折断[骨头]; 骨折； break If you break a part of your body such as your leg, your arm, or your nose, or if a bone breaks , you are injured because a bone cracks or splits.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使表层、盖子或密封破裂；撕开； break If a surface, cover, or seal breaks or if something breaks it, a hole or tear is made in it, so that a substance can pass through.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使工具或机器损坏； When a tool or piece of machinery breaks or when you break it, it is damaged and no longer works.
breakable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易碎的； breakable 易碎物品 Breakable objects are easy to break by accident.
breakage: [N-VAR 可变名词] 破损；毁坏； breakage Breakage is the act of breaking something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 破损物品； breakage A breakage is something that has been broken.
breakaway: [ADJ 形容词] 分裂出来的；脱离组织的； breakaway A breakaway group is a group of people who have separated from a larger group, for example because of a disagreement.
