break down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 机器或车辆出毛病，损坏； If a machine or a vehicle breaks down , it stops working.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 讨论、关系或系统失败，破裂，失灵； If a discussion, relationship, or system breaks down , it fails because of a problem or disagreement.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 分解；将…分成若干部分； To break down something such as an idea or statement means to separate it into smaller parts in order to make it easier to understand or deal with.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使物质分解； When a substance breaks down or when something breaks it down , a biological or chemical process causes it to separate into the substances which make it up.
breakdown: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 关系的破裂；计划、讨论等的失败，结束； breakdown The breakdown of something such as a relationship, plan, or discussion is its failure or ending.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 神经衰弱；精神崩溃； breakdown See also: nervous breakdown ; If you have a breakdown , you become very depressed, so that you are unable to cope with your life.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 汽车或机器的故障，损坏； breakdown If a car or a piece of machinery has a breakdown , it stops working.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分类；细目列表； breakdown A breakdown of something is a list of its separate parts.
breaker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指拍击海岸的大浪花，大海浪； See also: ice-breaker ; law-breaker ; record-breaker ; strike-breaker ; Breakers are big sea waves, especially at the point when they just reach the shore.
break-even point: [N-SING 单数名词] 收支平衡点；保本点； break-even point When a company reaches break-even point , the money it makes from the sale of goods or services is just enough to cover the cost of supplying those goods or services, but not enough to make a profit.
breakfast: [N-VAR 可变名词] 早餐；早饭； breakfast See also: bed and breakfast ; continental breakfast ; English breakfast ; Breakfast is the first meal of the day.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 咸肉、蛋类等熟食早餐； A cooked breakfast or a hot breakfast is a breakfast that consists of cooked food, such as bacon and eggs.  /  [VERB 动词] 吃早饭；  breakfast When you breakfast , you have breakfast.
breakfast table: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 早餐桌； breakfast table You refer to a table as the breakfast table when it is being used for breakfast.
breakfast television: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 早餐时段的电视节目； Breakfast television refers to television programmes which are broadcast in the morning at the time when most people are having breakfast.
breakfast time: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 早餐时间；早餐时段； Breakfast time is the period of the morning when most people have their breakfast.
break-in: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 强行闯入； break-in If there has been a break-in , someone has got into a building by force.
break in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 通常指盗贼闯入，破门而入； See also: break-in ; If someone, usually a thief, breaks in , they get into a building by force.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 打断；插嘴； If you break in on someone's conversation or activity, you interrupt them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使适应新的工作或环境； If you break someone in , you get them used to a new job or situation.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使(新产品) 经使用逐渐合用；磨合； If you break in something new, you gradually use or wear it for longer and longer periods until it is ready to be used or worn all the time.
breaking point: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 崩溃点；极点；极限； breaking point If something or someone has reached breaking point , they have so many problems or difficulties that they can no longer cope with them, and may soon collapse or be unable to continue.
break into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 强行进入；闯入； break into If someone breaks into a building, they get into it by force.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 突然开始做某事； If someone breaks into something they suddenly start doing it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 成功打入，顺利进入某行业，尤指很难取得成功的领域； If you break into a profession or area of business, especially one that is difficult to succeed in, you manage to have some success in it.
breakneck: [ADJ 形容词] 速度极快的； breakneck If you say that something happens or travels at breakneck speed, you mean that it happens or travels very fast.
break off: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 折断；使断开； If part of something breaks off or if you break it off , it comes off or is removed by force.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 突然中止；突然停顿； If you break off when you are doing or saying something, you suddenly stop doing it or saying it.  /  [PHR-V-RECIP 相互动词短语] 终止，结束关系； If someone breaks off a relationship, they end it.
break out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 战争、战斗或疾病爆发； If something such as war, fighting, or disease breaks out , it begins suddenly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 越狱；逃跑； See also: breakout ; If a prisoner breaks out of a prison, they escape from it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 摆脱单调刻板的状况； break out If you break out of a dull situation or routine, you manage to change it or escape from it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 布满[汗水]; 出疹子； break out If you break out in a rash or a sweat, a rash or sweat appears on your skin.
breakout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 越狱；逃亡； breakout If there has been a break-out , someone has escaped from prison.
break through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 冲破；突破； break through If you break through a barrier, you succeed in forcing your way through it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 克服困难或障碍取得突破； break through If you break through , you achieve success even though there are difficulties and obstacles.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 显现；显露； When something that was previously hidden or could not be seen breaks through , it appears.  /  See also: breakthrough ; �
breakthrough: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 突破；重大进展； breakthrough A breakthrough is an important development or achievement.
breakup: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 婚姻、关系或联系的破裂，终结； The break-up of a marriage, relationship, or association is the act of it finishing or coming to an end because the people involved decide that it is not working successfully.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 组织或国家的分裂，解体； The break-up of an organization or a country is the act of it separating or dividing into several parts.
break-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 婚姻、关系或联系的破裂，终结； break-up The break-up of a marriage, relationship, or association is the act of it finishing or coming to an end because the people involved decide that it is not working successfully.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 组织或国家的分裂，解体； break-up The break-up of an organization or a country is the act of it separating or dividing into several parts.
break up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使分裂；被拆分；(使) 破碎； When something breaks up or when you break it up , it separates or is divided into several smaller parts.  /  [PHR-V-RECIP 相互动词短语] 恋人分手；夫妻结束关系； If you break up with your boyfriend, girlfriend, husband, or wife, your relationship with that person ends.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 婚姻关系破裂；结束婚姻关系； break up If a marriage breaks up or if someone breaks it up , the marriage ends and the partners separate.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 散[会]; 使解散； break up When a meeting or gathering breaks up or when someone breaks it up , it is brought to an end and the people involved in it leave.
breakwater: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 防波堤； A breakwater is a wooden or stone wall that extends from the shore into the sea and is built in order to protect a harbour or beach from the force of the waves.
breast: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 妇女的乳房； breast -breasted A woman's breasts are the two soft, round parts on her chest that can produce milk to feed a baby.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胸；胸部；胸膛； breast A person's breast is the upper part of his or her chest.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胸怀；内心； breast The breast is often considered to be the part of your body where your emotions are.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鸟类的胸脯； breast -breasted A bird's breast is the front part of its body.
breastbone: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胸骨； Your breastbone is the long, flat bone which goes from your throat to the bottom of your ribs and to which your ribs are attached.
breast-feed: [VERB 动词] 母乳哺育； breast-feed breast-feeding When a woman breast-feeds her baby, she feeds it with milk from her breasts, rather than from a bottle.
breastfeed: [VERB 动词] 母乳哺育； breast-feeding When a woman breast-feeds her baby, she feeds it with milk from her breasts, rather than from a bottle.
breast milk: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 母乳； Breast milk is the white liquid produced by women to breast-feed their babies.
breastplate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胸铠；护胸甲； A breastplate is a piece of armour that covers and protects the chest.
breast pocket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常在衣服内面的胸前口袋； breast pocket The breast pocket of a man's coat or jacket is a pocket, usually on the inside, next to his chest.
breaststroke: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 蛙泳； Breaststroke is a swimming stroke which you do lying on your front, moving your arms and legs horizontally in a circular motion.
breath: [N-VAR 可变名词] 呼出的气体；气息； breath Your breath is the air that you let out through your mouth when you breathe.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 吸气； breath When you take a breath , you breathe in once.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 风或气流的一丝，丝毫； breath If you say that there is not a breath of wind or air, you are emphasizing that there is no wind and the air is very still.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 微量；少许； breath A breath of something, is a small amount of it.

burqa: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 布卡伊斯兰国家妇女穿的蒙面长袍； A burqa is a long garment that covers the head and body and is traditionally worn by women in Islamic countries.

bursar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 学校的财务主管，行政主管； The bursar of a school or college is the person who is in charge of its finance or general administration.

bury: [VERB 动词] 掩埋；埋藏； bury To bury something means to put it into a hole in the ground and cover it up with earth.  /  [VERB 动词] 埋葬；安葬； bury To bury a dead person means to put their body into a grave and cover it with earth.  /  [VERB 动词] 失去亲人； If someone says they have buried one of their relatives, they mean that one of their relatives has died.  /  [VERB 动词] 掩藏；埋藏； If you bury something under a large quantity of things, you put it there, often in order to hide it.
bus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公共汽车；巴士；大客车； bus A bus is a large motor vehicle which carries passengers from one place to another.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 用大客车运送；乘坐公共汽车； bus When someone is bussed to a particular place or when they bus there, they travel there on a bus.  /  [VERB 动词] 用校车送； bus busing In some parts of the United States, when children are bused to school, they are transported by bus to a school in a different area so that children of different races can be educated together.

combat trousers: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (多口袋宽松式)作战裤，迷彩裤，休闲裤； combat trousers Combat trousers are large, loose trousers with lots of pockets.
combination: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 结合;联合;混合； combination A combination of things is a mixture of them.
combination lock: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 密码锁;暗码； combination lock A combination lock is a lock which can only be opened by turning a dial or a number of dials according to a particular series of letters or numbers.
combine: [V-RECIP-ERG ] 使结合;使组合;使综合； combine If you combine two or more things or if they combine , they exist together.  /  [V-RECIP-ERG ] 使合并;使综合； combine If you combine two or more things or if they combine , they join together to make a single thing.  /  [VERB 动词] 兼有;兼备； combine If someone or something combines two qualities or features, they have both those qualities or features at the same time.  /  [VERB 动词] 兼做;同时做(两件事)； combine If someone combines two activities, they do them both at the same time.
combined: [ADJ 形容词] 联合的;共同的； combined A combined effort or attack is made by two or more groups of people at the same time.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 总计的;总共的； combined The combined size or quantity of two or more things is the total of their sizes or quantities added together.
combine harvester: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 联合收割机； A combine harvester is a large machine which is used on farms to cut, sort, and clean grain.
combining form: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 构词成分； A combining form is a word that is used, or used with a particular meaning, only when joined to another word.
combo: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (演奏爵士乐、舞曲或流行音乐的)小型乐队； combo A combo is a small group of musicians who play jazz, dance, or popular music.
combustible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可燃的;易燃的； combustible A combustible material or gas catches fire and burns easily.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可能引起冲突的;可能带来麻烦的； combustible A combustible situation is likely to result in conflict or trouble.
combustion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 燃烧;燃烧过程； combustion See also: internal combustion engine ; Combustion is the act of burning something or the process of burning.
come: Come is used in a large number of expressions which are explained under other words in this dictionary.  /  [VERB 动词] 来;来到； come When a person or thing comes to a particular place, especially to a place where you are, they move there.  /  [VERB 动词] 来(做某事)(除了用 come to do something 表达此意，英国英语中也用 come and do something，美国英语中也用 come do something，但表示过去动作时一定要用 came and did something)； come When someone comes to do something, they move to the place where someone else is in order to do it, and they do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 抵达;到达； When you come to a place, you reach it.
come about: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 产生;发生； come about When you say how or when something came about , you say how or when it happened.
come across: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 偶然发现;偶然遇见； come across If you come across something or someone, you find them or meet them by chance.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使产生…印象;给人以…的印象； come across If someone or what they are saying comes across in a particular way, they make that impression on people who meet them or are listening to them.
come along: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤用于鼓励别人参加某活动)来吧，一起来； come along You tell someone to come along to encourage them in a friendly way to do something, especially to attend something.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 加把劲儿;赶快； You say 'come along' to someone to encourage them to hurry up, usually when you are rather annoyed with them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (偶然地)发生，来到； When something or someone comes along , they occur or arrive by chance.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 进展;进步； If something is coming along , it is developing or making progress.
come around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拜访;探访； If someone comes around or comes round to your house, they call there to see you.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 改变观点;改变看法(以接受)； If you come around or come round to an idea, you eventually change your mind and accept it or agree with it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (按照预期)发生,再度出现； When something comes around or comes round , it happens as a regular or predictable event.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 苏醒； When someone who is unconscious comes around or comes round , they recover consciousness.
come at: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 扑向;向…逼近； If a person or animal comes at you, they move towards you in a threatening way and try to attack you.
comeback: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (娱乐圈、体育明星等的)复出，东山再起； comeback If someone such as an entertainer or sports personality makes a comeback , they return to their profession or sport after a period away.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 再度流行； comeback If something makes a comeback , it becomes fashionable again.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 因受到伤害而追究他人的责任； If you have no comeback when someone has done something wrong to you, there is nothing you can do to have them punished or held responsible.
come back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 回忆起;回想起来； If something that you had forgotten comes back to you, you remember it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 重新流行;再度时兴； When something comes back , it becomes fashionable again.  /  See also: comeback ; �
come back to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 回到(话题等)上来； If you come back to a topic or point, you talk about it again later.
come between: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 离间;挑拨;妨碍； If someone or something comes between two people, or comes between a person and a thing, they make the relationship or connection between them less close or happy.
come by: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 弄到;得到； come by To come by something means to obtain it or find it.
comedian: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑稽演员;喜剧演员； A comedian is an entertainer whose job is to make people laugh, by telling jokes or funny stories.
comedic: [ADJ 形容词] 喜剧的； comedic Comedic means relating to comedy.
comedienne: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女滑稽演员;女喜剧演员； A comedienne is a female entertainer whose job is to make people laugh, by telling jokes or funny stories.
comedown: [N-SING 单数名词] 败落;失势;落魄； comedown If you say that something is a comedown , you think that it is not as good as something else that you have just done or had.
come down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (成本、水平或数量)下降，降低； come down If the cost, level, or amount of something comes down , it becomes less than it was before.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 落下;降落； If something comes down , it falls to the ground.
come down on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 支持(争论的一方)； If you come down on one side of an argument, you declare that you support that side.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 痛斥;斥责;严格对待； If you come down on someone, you criticize them severely or treat them strictly.
come down to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (问题、决定等)归结为； If a problem, decision, or question comes down to a particular thing, that thing is the most important factor involved.
come down with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 染上，得了病； If you come down with an illness, you get it.
comedy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 喜剧表演;喜剧成分;喜剧效果； comedy Comedy consists of types of entertainment, such as plays and films, or particular scenes in them, that are intended to make people laugh.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 喜剧片； A comedy is a play, film, or television programme that is intended to make people laugh.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 滑稽;诙谐;喜剧性； comedy The comedy of a situation involves those aspects of it that make you laugh.  /  See also: situation comedy ; �
come for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通常指军方、警察等为抓捕) 上门找，带走某人； If people such as soldiers or police come for you, they come to find you, usually in order to harm you or take you away, for example to prison.
come forward: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 自告奋勇;主动提供(信息)； If someone comes forward , they offer to do something or to give some information in response to a request for help.
come in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (信息)传来;(报告或电话)接收到； If information, a report, or a telephone call comes in , it is received.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (钱款)定期收到;有收入； If you have some money coming in , you receive it regularly as your income.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 加入，参与(讨论、安排或任务)； come in If someone comes in on a discussion, arrangement, or task, they join it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (新的观点、时装或产品)流行起来，上市； come in When a new idea, fashion, or product comes in , it becomes popular or available.
come in for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 遭到(批评);受到(指责)； come in for If someone or something comes in for criticism or blame, they receive it.
come into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 继承(财产、封号等)； come into If someone comes into some money, some property, or a title, they inherit it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 在…中起作用； come into If someone or something comes into a situation, they have a role in it.
comely: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (女子)标致的，秀丽的； A comely woman is attractive.
come off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 成功;达到效果； come off If something comes off , it is successful or effective.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (在比赛或冲突中)表现得； come off If someone comes off worst in a contest or conflict, they are in the worst position after it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 戒除(毒品);停止(服药)； come off If you come off a drug or medicine, you stop taking it.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 别撒谎了！别瞎说！； You say 'come off it' to someone to show them that you think what they are saying is untrue or wrong.
come-on: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指女子的)挑逗，勾引，卖弄风情； come-on A come-on is a gesture or remark which someone, especially a woman, makes in order to encourage another person to make sexual advances to them.
come on: [CONVENTION 惯用语] (表示鼓励)来吧； You say 'Come on' to someone to encourage them to do something they do not much want to do.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 快点儿;加把劲； You say 'Come on' to someone to encourage them to hurry up.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 得了吧;算了吧； come on You say 'Come on' to someone when you think that what they are saying is silly or unreasonable.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (疾病)开始； If you have an illness or a headache coming on , you can feel it starting.
come on to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 开始讨论； come on to When you come on to a particular topic, you start discussing it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 勾搭;想与…发生性关系； come on to If someone comes on to you, they show that they are interested in starting a sexual relationship with you.
come out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (书或光盘)出版，发行； When a new product such as a book or CD comes out , it becomes available to the public.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (事实)暴露，披露，显露； come out If a fact comes out , it becomes known to people.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 公开同性恋身份； come out When a gay person comes out , they let people know that they are gay.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 结果是;到头来； come out To come out in a particular way means to be in the position or state described at the end of a process or event.
come out in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 发(疹子)； If you come out in spots, you become covered with them.
come out with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 说出，提出(尤指令人惊讶的话)； If you come out with a remark, especially a surprising one, you make it.
come over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指奇怪或意外的感觉)支配，影响； If a feeling or desire, especially a strange or surprising one, comes over you, it affects you strongly.  /  [PHR-V-LINK 连系动词短语] 开始觉得;突然表现得； If someone comes over all dizzy or shy, for example, they suddenly start feeling or acting in that way.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 给人以…印象;显得； come over If someone or what they are saying comes over in a particular way, they make that impression on people who meet them or are listening to them.
comer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 到达者;到来的人； comer See also: all-comers ; latecomer ; newcomer ; You can use comers to refer to people who arrive at a particular place.
comet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 彗星； A comet is a bright object with a long tail that travels around the sun.
come through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 安然渡过(危险或难关)； come through To come through a dangerous or difficult situation means to survive it and recover from it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 显现;显露； If a feeling or message comes through , it is clearly shown in what is said or done.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指在履行完某些程序后)到来； come through If something comes through , it arrives, especially after some procedure has been carried out.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 实现(承诺);成功地完成;成功提供； come through If you come through with what is expected or needed from you, you succeed in doing or providing it.
come to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 恢复知觉;苏醒； When someone who is unconscious comes to , they recover consciousness.
come under: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 受到(袭击);遭受(压力)； If you come under attack or pressure, for example, people attack you or put pressure on you.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 受…管辖;在…控制之下； come under If something comes under a particular authority, it is managed or controlled by that authority.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 属于…范畴;列在…之下； If something comes under a particular heading, it is in the category mentioned.
come up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 走近;走到跟前； If someone comes up or comes up to you, they approach you until they are standing close to you.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 被提及;被讨论； come up If something comes up in a conversation or meeting, it is mentioned or discussed.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 即将发生;即将到来； If something is coming up , it is about to happen or take place.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 突然发生； If something comes up , it happens unexpectedly.
come up against: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 碰到;面对； If you come up against a problem or difficulty, you are faced with it and have to deal with it.
come up for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 到…的时候了； come up for When someone or something comes up for consideration or action of some kind, the time arrives when they have to be considered or dealt with.
come upon: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 偶然碰到(或发现)； If you come upon someone or something, you meet them or find them by chance.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 产生(某种态度或感觉)； If an attitude or feeling comes upon you, it begins to affect you.
comeuppance: [N-SING 单数名词] 应得的惩罚;报应； comeuppance If you say that someone has got their comeuppance , you approve of the fact that they have been punished or have suffered for something wrong that they have done.
come up to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将近;临近； To be coming up to a time or state means to be getting near to it.
come up with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 想出，提出(计划、想法等)； come up with If you come up with a plan or idea, you think of it and suggest it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 设法拿出(所需钱款)； come up with If you come up with a sum of money, you manage to produce it when it is needed.
comfort: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 舒适;舒服； comfort If you are doing something in comfort , you are physically relaxed and contented, and are not feeling any pain or other unpleasant sensations.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 舒适的生活方式;安逸； comfort Comfort is a style of life in which you have enough money to have everything you need.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 安慰;慰藉； comfort See also: cold comfort ; Comfort is what you feel when worries or unhappiness stop.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 令人感到安慰的人(或事物)； comfort If you refer to a person, thing, or idea as a comfort , you mean that it helps you to stop worrying or makes you feel less unhappy.
comfortable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (家具、衣服等)让人舒服的，舒适的； comfortable If a piece of furniture or an item of clothing is comfortable , it makes you feel physically relaxed when you use it, for example because it is soft.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (建筑物或房间)令人放松的，安逸的，舒适的； comfortable comfortably If a building or room is comfortable , it makes you feel physically relaxed when you spend time in it, for example because it is warm and has nice furniture.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人愉快放松的，舒服的； comfortable comfortably If you are comfortable , you are physically relaxed because of the place or position you are sitting or lying in.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 宽裕的;小康的； comfortable comfortably If you say that someone is comfortable , you mean that they have enough money to be able to live without financial problems.
comfortably: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 轻松地;容易地； comfortably See also: comfortable ; If you do something comfortably , you do it easily.
comfortably off: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 宽裕的;富有的； comfortably off If someone is comfortably off , they have enough money to be able to live without financial problems.
comforter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 安慰者;给人安慰的事物； comforter A comforter is a person or thing that comforts you.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 羽绒被； A comforter is a large cover filled with feathers or similar material which you put over yourself in bed instead of a sheet and blankets.
comfort food: (令人心情愉快但可能无益健康的)安慰食品； comfort food If you call something comfort food , you mean it is enjoyable to eat and makes you feel happier, although it may not be very good for your health.
comforting: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 安慰的;令人欣慰的； comforting comfortingly If you say that something is comforting , you mean it makes you feel less worried or unhappy.
comfrey: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (用于制作饮料或药物的)聚合草； Comfrey is a herb that is used to make drinks and medicines.
comfy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 舒适的;舒服的； comfy A comfy item of clothing, piece of furniture, room, or position is a comfortable one.
comic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 滑稽的;好笑的； comic If you describe something as comic , you mean that it makes you laugh, and is often intended to make you laugh.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 喜剧的； comic Comic is used to describe comedy as a form of entertainment, and the actors and entertainers who perform it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 喜剧演员； A comic is an entertainer who tells jokes in order to make people laugh.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连环画杂志;漫画书； comic A comic is a magazine that contains stories told in pictures.
comical: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 滑稽的;令人发笑的； comical comically If you describe something as comical , you mean that it makes you want to laugh because it seems funny or silly.
comic book: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连环漫画杂志;漫画书； A comic book is a magazine that contains stories told in pictures.
comic strip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连环漫画； A comic strip is a series of drawings that tell a story, especially in a newspaper or magazine.
coming: [ADJ 形容词] (事件或时间)即将到来的，即将发生的； coming See also: come ; A coming event or time is an event or time that will happen soon.
coming of age: [N-SING 单数名词] 成熟;发达； When something reaches an important stage of development and is accepted by a large number of people, you can refer to this as its coming of age .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 成年； Someone's coming of age is the time when they become legally an adult.
comings and goings: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 来来往往;进进出出； comings and goings Comings and goings refers to the way people keep arriving at and leaving a particular place.
comma: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 逗号； A comma is the punctuation mark , which is used to separate parts of a sentence or items in a list.
command: [VERB 动词] 命令;下令;指示； command If someone in authority commands you to do something, they tell you that you must do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 博得，赢得，拥有(尊重、服从等)； command If you command something such as respect or obedience, you obtain it because you are popular, famous, or important.  /  [VERB 动词] 控制;掌管； command If an army or country commands a place, they have total control over it.  /  [VERB 动词] 统率，指挥(军队)； command An officer who commands part of an army, navy, or air force is responsible for controlling and organizing it.
commandant: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词] 指挥官;司令； A commandant is an army officer in charge of a particular place or group of people.

comparative: [ADJ 形容词] (状态)相对的，比较而言的； comparative comparatively You use comparative to show that you are judging something against a previous or different situation.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (研究)比较的； comparative A comparative study is a study that involves the comparison of two or more things of the same kind.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (形容词或副词)比较级的； comparative In grammar, the comparative form of an adjective or adverb shows that something has more of a quality than something else has.
compare: [VERB 动词] 比较;对比； compare When you compare things, you consider them and discover the differences or similarities between them.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…比作； compare If you compare one person or thing to another, you say that they are like the other person or thing.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] (与…)比起来(好/差)； compare If one thing compares favourably with another, it is better than the other thing.  /  [VERB 动词] 相比； compare If you say that something does not compare with something else, you mean that it is much worse.
compared: [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 与…相比;和…比起来； compared If you say, for example, that one thing is large or small compared with another or compared to another, you mean that it is larger or smaller than the other thing.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 相对…而言;对照； compared You talk about one situation or thing compared with another or compared to another when contrasting the two situations or things.
comparison: [N-VAR 可变名词] 比较;对照； comparison When you make a comparison , you consider two or more things and discover the differences between them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 比拟;比喻； comparison When you make a comparison , you say that one thing is like another in some way.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 与…相比;与…比较而言； comparison If you say, for example, that something is large or small in comparison with , in comparison to , or by comparison with something else, you mean that it is larger or smaller than the other thing.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不能相提并论;不能相比； comparison If you say there is no comparison between one thing and another, you mean that you think the first thing is much better than the second, or very different from it.
compartment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (火车上的)分隔厢，隔间； compartment A compartment is one of the separate spaces into which a railway carriage is divided.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 格;分隔间;隔层； compartment See also: glove compartment ; A compartment is one of the separate parts of an object that is used for keeping things in.
compartmentalize: [VERB 动词] 分隔;划分； compartmentalize compartmentalized To compartmentalize something means to divide it into separate sections.
compass: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 指南针;罗盘； compass A compass is an instrument that you use for finding directions.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 圆规； Compasses are a hinged V-shaped instrument that you use for drawing circles.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 界限;范围； compass If something is within the compass of something or someone, it is within their limits or abilities.
compassion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 怜悯;同情； compassion Compassion is a feeling of pity, sympathy, and understanding for someone who is suffering.
compassionate: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有同情心的;表示同情的； compassionate compassionately If you describe someone or something as compassionate , you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.
compassionate leave: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指家人去世或病重时批准的)私事假，丧假； Compassionate leave is time away from your work that your employer allows you for personal reasons, especially when a member of your family dies or is seriously ill.
compass point: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 罗经方位点； A compass point is one of the 32 marks on the dial of a compass that show direction, for example north, south, east, and west.
compatible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (系统、想法和信仰)兼容的，可以并存的； compatible compatibility If things, for example systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible , they work well together or can exist together successfully.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 能和谐相处的;合得来的； compatible compatibility If you say that you are compatible with someone, you mean that you have a good relationship with them because you have similar opinions and interests.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (尤指与 IBM公司制造的计算机或计算机设备)兼容的； If one make of computer or computer equipment is compatible with another make, especially IBM, they can be used together and can use the same software.
compatriot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同国人;同胞； compatriot Your compatriots are people from your own country.
compel: [VERB 动词] 强迫;逼迫； compel If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 觉得必须(做…)； compel If you feel compelled to do something, you feel that you must do it, because it is the right thing to do.
compelling: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人信服的;有说服力的； compelling A compelling argument or reason is one that convinces you that something is true or that something should be done.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 非常有趣的;很有吸引力的； compelling compellingly If you describe something such as a film or book, or someone's appearance, as compelling , you mean you want to keep looking at it or reading it because you find it so interesting.
compendium: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常指书中的)概要，纲要； compendium A compendium is a short but detailed collection of information, usually in a book.
compensate: [VERB 动词] 赔偿;补偿； compensate To compensate someone for money or things that they have lost means to pay them money or give them something to replace that money or those things.  /  [VERB 动词] 弥补;补偿； compensate If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to make the situation better.  /  [VERB 动词] 抵消； compensate Something that compensates for something else balances it or reduces its effects.  /  [VERB 动词] 弥补(过失或不足)； compensate If you try to compensate for something that is wrong or missing in your life, you try to do something that removes or reduces the harmful effects.
compensation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 补偿(或赔偿)金； compensation Compensation is money that someone who has experienced loss or suffering claims from the person or organization responsible, or from the state.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (对不利事情的)补偿； compensation If something is some compensation for something bad that has happened, it makes you feel better.
compensatory: [ADJ 形容词] 赔偿的;补偿的； compensatory Compensatory payments involve money paid as compensation.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 补偿性质的;弥补性质的； compensatory Compensatory measures are designed to help people who have special problems or disabilities.
compere: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (广播、电视或现场演出的)主持人； A compere is the person who introduces the people taking part in a radio or television show or a live show.  /  [VERB 动词] 主持(节目)； compere The person who comperes a show introduces the people who take part in it.
compete: [V-RECIP 相互动词] 竞争； compete When one firm or country competes with another, it tries to get people to buy its own goods in preference to those of the other firm or country.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 与…争夺以获取； compete If you compete with someone for something, you try to get it for yourself and stop the other person getting it.  /  [VERB 动词] 参加(比赛)； compete If you compete in a contest or a game, you take part in it.  /  See also: competing ; �
competence: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 能力;才干； competence Competence is the ability to do something well or effectively.
competency: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同 competence； competency Competency means the same as competence .
competent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 能胜任的;称职的； competent competently Someone who is competent is efficient and effective.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有…能力的;能干的； competent If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.
competing: [ADJ 形容词] 相互冲突的;相互矛盾的； competing See also: compete ; Competing ideas, requirements, or interests cannot all be right or satisfied at the same time.
competition: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 竞争;角逐； competition Competition is a situation in which two or more people or groups are trying to get something which not everyone can have.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 竞争对手； competition The competition is the person or people you are competing with.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (商业)竞争； competition Competition is an activity involving two or more firms, in which each firm tries to get people to buy its own goods in preference to the other firms' goods.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 竞争产品(或商品)； competition The competition is the goods that a rival organization is selling.
competitive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 竞争的；角逐的； competitive competitively Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 好竞争的;好胜的； competitive competitively competitiveness A competitive person is eager to be more successful than other people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (商品或服务)具有竞争力的； competitive competitively competitiveness Goods or services that are at a competitive price or rate are likely to be bought, because they are less expensive than other goods of the same kind.
competitor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 竞争者;对手； competitor A company's competitors are companies who are trying to sell similar goods or services to the same people.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 选手;参赛者； competitor A competitor is a person who takes part in a competition or contest.
compilation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 汇编物;辑;集子； compilation See also: compile ; A compilation is a book, CD, or programme that contains many different items that have been gathered together, usually ones which have already appeared in other places.
compile: [VERB 动词] 汇编;编制;编纂； compile compilation When you compile something such as a report, book, or programme, you produce it by collecting and putting together many pieces of information.
compiler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 汇编者;编纂者； compiler A compiler is someone who compiles books, reports, or lists of information.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 编译程序； A compiler is a computer program which converts language that people can use into a code that the computer can understand.
complacency: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自满;沾沾自喜； complacency Complacency is being complacent about a situation.
complacent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自满的;沾沾自喜的;满不在乎的； complacent complacently A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.
complain: [VERB 动词] 抱怨;发牢骚； complain If you complain about a situation, you say that you are not satisfied with it.  /  [VERB 动词] 诉说有…病痛;主诉； complain If you complain of pain or illness, you say that you are feeling pain or feeling ill.
complainant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 原告； A complainant is a person who starts a court case in a court of law.
complainer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 爱发牢骚的人;牢骚满腹的人； complainer A complainer is someone who complains a lot about their problems or about things they do not like.
complaint: [N-VAR 可变名词] 投诉;意见;抱怨； complaint A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 投诉的原因;不满的原因； complaint A complaint is a reason for complaining.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指不严重的)疾病； complaint You can refer to an illness as a complaint , especially if it is not very serious.
complaisant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 顺从的;殷勤的； complaisant If you are complaisant , you are willing to accept what other people are doing without complaining.
complement: [VERB 动词] 使(优点)突出;衬托出； complement If one thing complements another, it goes well with the other thing and makes its good qualities more noticeable.  /  [VERB 动词] 补足;补充;与…相辅相成； complement If people or things complement each other, they are different or do something different, which makes them a good combination.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 衬托物;补足物； complement Something that is a complement to something else complements it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 装备定额;编制名额； complement The complement of things or people that something has is the number of things or people that it normally has, which enable it to function properly.
complementary: [ADJ 形容词] 相互补充的;相辅相成的； complementary complementarity Complementary things are different from each other but make a good combination.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 补充医学的(不同于西医的治疗方法，如针灸、顺势疗法)； complementary Complementary medicine refers to ways of treating patients which are different from the ones used by most Western doctors, for example acupuncture and homoeopathy.
complementation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (语言学中的)补语； In linguistics, a complementation pattern of a verb, noun, or adjective is the patterns that typically follow it.
complete: [ADJ 形容词] 完全的;十足的； complete completely You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 完整的;全部的;整个的； complete You can use complete to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something and not just part of it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 齐全的;完整的； complete completeness If something is complete , it contains all the parts that it should contain.  /  [VERB 动词] 使齐全;使完整； complete To complete a set or group means to provide the last item that is needed to make it a full set or group.
complex: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 复杂的;错综的； complex Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (句子)复合的； In grammar, a complex sentence contains one or more subordinate clauses as well as a main clause.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 综合建筑群;综合大楼； complex A complex is a group of buildings designed for a particular purpose, or one large building divided into several smaller areas.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 错综复杂的组合;复合体； complex A complex of things is a group or system of things that are connected with each other in a complicated way.
complexion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肤色;面色； complexion When you refer to someone's complexion , you are referring to the natural colour or condition of the skin on their face.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 性质;特性； complexion The complexion of something is its general nature or character.
complexities: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 错综复杂的事物； complexities The complexities of something are the many complicated factors involved in it.
complexity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 复杂性;错综复杂； complexity Complexity is the state of having many different parts connected or related to each other in a complicated way.
compliance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 遵守;服从;听从； compliance Compliance with something, for example a law, treaty, or agreement means doing what you are required or expected to do.
compliant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 服从的;顺从的;俯首帖耳的； compliant If you say that someone is compliant , you mean they willingly do what they are asked to do.
complicate: [VERB 动词] 使难以理解；使复杂化； complicate To complicate something means to make it more difficult to understand or deal with.
complicated: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 复杂的;难懂的;难处理的； complicated If you say that something is complicated , you mean it has so many parts or aspects that it is difficult to understand or deal with.
complication: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 使复杂化的难题(或困难)； complication A complication is a problem or difficulty that makes a situation harder to deal with.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 并发症； complication A complication is a medical problem that occurs as a result of another illness or disease.
complicit: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (犯罪等)同谋的，串通一气的； complicit If someone is complicit in a crime or unfair activity, they are involved in it.
complicity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同谋;串通； complicity Complicity is involvement with other people in an illegal activity or plan.
compliment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 赞美;恭维话； compliment A compliment is a polite remark that you say to someone to show that you like their appearance, appreciate their qualities, or approve of what they have done.  /  [VERB 动词] 赞美;恭维； compliment If you compliment someone, you pay them a compliment.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 赞美;赞赏； compliment If you consider something that a person says or does as a compliment , it convinces you of your own good qualities, or that the person appreciates you.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 致谢;祝贺;致意； compliment You can refer to your compliments when you want to express thanks, good wishes, or respect to someone in a formal way.
complimentary: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 赞美的;赞扬的； complimentary If you are complimentary about something, you express admiration for it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (座位、票或书)免费赠送的； complimentary A complimentary seat, ticket, or book is given to you free.
comply: [VERB 动词] 服从;遵守； comply If someone or something complies with an order or set of rules, they are in accordance with what is required or expected.
component: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 组成部分;成分； component The components of something are the parts that it is made of.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 组成的;构成的； component The component parts of something are the parts that make it up.
comport: [VERB 动词] 举止;表现； comport If you comport yourself in a particular way, you behave in that way.
compose: [VERB 动词] 组成;构成； compose The things that something is composed of are its parts or members.  /  [VERB 动词] 谱写(乐曲);作曲； compose When someone composes a piece of music, they write it.  /  [VERB 动词] 创作，写(信、诗或演讲稿)； compose If you compose something such as a letter, poem, or speech, you write it, often using a lot of concentration or skill.  /  [VERB 动词] 为照片、图像构图； compose If you compose a picture or image, you arrange it in an attractive and artistic way.
composed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 平静的;镇定的;沉着的； composed If someone is composed , they are calm and able to control their feelings.
composer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指古典音乐)作曲家； A composer is a person who writes music, especially classical music.
composite: [ADJ 形容词] 拼成的;混合成的;复合的； composite A composite object or item is made up of several different things, parts, or substances.
composition: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 组成;构成;组合方式； composition When you talk about the composition of something, you are referring to the way in which its various parts are put together and arranged.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (作曲家、画家等的)作品； composition The compositions of a composer, painter, or other artist are the works of art that they have produced.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (学生的)作文； A composition is a piece of written work that children write at school.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 艺术创作技巧； composition Composition is the technique or skill involved in creating a work of art.
compositional: [ADJ 形容词] 作曲的;创作的； compositional Compositional refers to the way composers and artists use their skills or techniques in their work.
compositor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 排字(或排版)工人； A compositor is a person who arranges the text and pictures of a book, magazine, or newspaper before it is printed.
compost: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 堆肥;混合肥料； compost Compost is a mixture of decayed plants and vegetable waste which is added to the soil to help plants grow.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] (在花盆中栽培用的)特制土； Compost is specially treated soil that you buy and use to grow seeds and plants in pots.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…制成堆肥； compost composting To compost things such as unwanted bits of plants means to make them into compost.
composure: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 冷静;镇定;沉着； composure Composure is the appearance or feeling of calm and the ability to control your feelings.
compote: [N-VAR 可变名词] 蜜饯;糖渍水果； Compote is fruit stewed with sugar or in syrup.
compound: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (作特殊用途的)大院，有围墙的场地； compound A compound is an enclosed area of land that is used for a particular purpose.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (化学中的)化合物； compound In chemistry, a compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 混合物;组合物； compound If something is a compound of different things, it consists of those things.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 复合的;组合的;混合的； compound Compound is used to indicate that something consists of two or more parts or things.
compounded: [ADJ 形容词] 由…合成的;由…组成的； compounded If something is compounded of different things, it is a mixture of those things.
compound fracture: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 哆开骨折;有创骨折； A compound fracture is a fracture in which the broken bone sticks through the skin.
compound interest: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 复利； Compound interest is interest that is calculated both on an original sum of money and on interest which has previously been added to the sum.
comprehend: [VERB 动词] 理解;领悟； comprehend If you cannot comprehend something, you cannot understand it.
comprehensible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 能懂的;可以理解的； comprehensible Something that is comprehensible can be understood.
comprehension: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 理解力；领悟力； comprehension Comprehension is the ability to understand something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 充分了解;完全明白； comprehension Comprehension is full knowledge and understanding of the meaning of something.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (听力或阅读)理解测试； comprehension When pupils do comprehension , they do an exercise to find out how well they understand a piece of spoken or written language.

conceive: [VERB 动词] 想象;相信； conceive If you cannot conceive of something, you cannot imagine it or believe it.  /  [VERB 动词] 认为； conceive If you conceive something as a particular thing, you consider it to be that thing.  /  [VERB 动词] 构思;设想;想出； conceive If you conceive a plan or idea, you think of it and work out how it can be done.  /  [VERB 动词] 怀孕； conceive When a woman conceives , she becomes pregnant.

concentration: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 全神贯注;专心;专注； concentration Concentration on something involves giving all your attention to it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 集中;汇集； concentration A concentration of something is a large amount of it or large numbers of it in a small area.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 浓度； concentration The concentration of a substance is the proportion of essential ingredients or substances in it.

confidential: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 秘密的;机密的； confidential confidentially confidentiality Information that is confidential is meant to be kept secret or private.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 悄悄的;隐秘的； confidential confidentially If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

contagion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 接触传染； contagion Contagion is the spreading of a particular disease by someone touching another person who is already affected by the disease.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (不良思想、态度、感情等的)传播，蔓延； contagion You can use contagion to refer to the spreading of ideas, or attitudes, or feelings that you consider to be bad or unacceptable from one group of people to another.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 接触传染病； A contagion is a contagious disease.
contagious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 病接触传染的； contagious A disease that is contagious can be caught by touching people or things that are infected with it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (感情、态度等)感染性的，会迅速蔓延开的； contagious A feeling or attitude that is contagious spreads quickly among a group of people.
contain: [VERB 动词] 装有;容纳； contain If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.  /  [VERB 动词] 包含;含有； contain If a substance contains something, that thing is a part of it.  /  [VERB 动词] (著作、讲话或电影中)包括，包含； contain If writing, speech, or film contains particular information, ideas, or images, it includes them.  /  [VERB 动词] (团体或组织中)有，包括； contain If a group or organization contains a certain number of people, those are the people that are in it.
container: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 容器； container A container is something such as a box or bottle that is used to hold or store things in.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 集装箱;货柜； A container is a very large metal or wooden box used for transporting goods so that they can be loaded easily onto ships and lorries.
container ship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 集装箱船； A container ship is a ship that is designed for carrying goods that are packed in large metal or wooden boxes.
containment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对他国力量的)遏制； Containment is the action or policy of keeping another country's power or area of control within acceptable limits or boundaries.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 控制;抑制； containment The containment of something dangerous or unpleasant is the act or process of keeping it under control within a particular area or place.
contaminant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 污染物； contaminant A contaminant is something that contaminates a substance such as water or food.
contaminate: [VERB 动词] 污染;弄脏； contaminate contaminated contamination If something is contaminated by dirt, chemicals, or radiation, they make it dirty or harmful.
contemplate: [VERB 动词] 考虑;思量;思忖； contemplate If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.  /  [VERB 动词] 深思熟虑;沉思;苦思冥想； contemplate contemplation If you contemplate an idea or subject, you think about it carefully for a long time.  /  [VERB 动词] 凝视;注视； contemplate contemplation If you contemplate something or someone, you look at them for a long time.
contemplative: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沉思的;冥思的； contemplative Someone who is contemplative thinks deeply, or is thinking in a serious and calm way.
contemporaneous: [ADJ 形容词] 同时发生(或存在)的;同时期的； contemporaneous contemporaneously If two events or situations are contemporaneous , they happen or exist during the same period of time.
contemporary: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 当代的;现代的； contemporary Contemporary things are modern and relate to the present time.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 同时发生的;同时期的;同时代的； contemporary Contemporary people or things were alive or happened at the same time as something else you are talking about.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同时期的人;同时代的人； Someone's contemporary is a person who is or was alive at the same time as them.
contempt: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 鄙视;蔑视;轻视； contempt If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同 contempt of court； contempt Contempt means the same as contempt of court .  /  [PHRASE 短语] 鄙视;蔑视;轻视； contempt If you hold someone or something in contempt , you feel contempt for them.
contemptible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可轻蔑的;可鄙的;卑劣的； contemptible If you feel that someone or something is contemptible , you feel strong dislike and disrespect for them.
contempt of court: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 藐视法庭罪； contempt of court Contempt of court is the criminal offence of disobeying an instruction from a judge or a court of law.
contemptuous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 蔑视的;藐视的;鄙视的； contemptuous contemptuously If you are contemptuous of someone or something, you do not like or respect them at all.
contend: [VERB 动词] 处理;对付;解决； contend If you have to contend with a problem or difficulty, you have to deal with it or overcome it.  /  [VERB 动词] 声称;争辩;主张； contend If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 竞争;争夺； contend If you contend with someone for something such as power, you compete with them to try to get it.
contender: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 竞争者;争夺者； contender A contender is someone who takes part in a competition.
content: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 所容纳的东西;所含之物； content The contents of a container such as a bottle, box, or room are the things that are inside it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (书、演讲、电视节目等的)内容； content If you refer to the content or contents of something such as a book, speech, or television programme, you are referring to the subject that it deals with, the story that it tells, or the ideas that it expresses.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (书的)目录； content The contents of a book are its different chapters and sections, usually shown in a list at the beginning of the book.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (教育项目或课程的)内容； content The content of something such as an educational course or a programme of action is the elements that it consists of.
contented: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 满足的;满意的； contented contentedly If you are contented , you are satisfied with your life or the situation you are in.
contention: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (争论或讨论时的)看法，观点； contention Someone's contention is the idea or opinion that they are expressing in an argument or discussion.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不和;争吵;争执； contention See also: bone of contention ; If something is a cause of contention , it is a cause of disagreement or argument.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 有机会获胜； contention If you are in contention in a contest, you have a chance of winning it.
contentious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有争议的;引起争论的； contentious contentiously A contentious issue causes a lot of disagreement or arguments.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 爱争论的;动辄争吵的； contentious A contentious person seems to like arguing and disagreeing with other people.
contentment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 满意;满足； contentment Contentment is a feeling of quiet happiness and satisfaction.
content provider: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 内容提供商； content provider A content provider is a company that supplies material such as text, music, or images for use on websites.
contest: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 竞赛;比赛； contest See also: beauty contest ; A contest is a competition or game in which people try to win.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (权力或控制权的)争夺，竞争； contest A contest is a struggle to win power or control.  /  [VERB 动词] 争取赢得(选举、比赛等);角逐； contest If someone contests an election or competition, they take part in it and try to win it.  /  [VERB 动词] 争辩;对…提出异议； contest If you contest a statement or decision, you object to it formally because you think it is wrong or unreasonable.
contestant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 参赛者； A contestant in a competition or quiz is a person who takes part in it.
context: [N-VAR 可变名词] (想法、事件等的)背景，环境； context The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 上下文;语境； context The context of a word, sentence, or text consists of the words, sentences, or text before and after it which help to make its meaning clear.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 在上下文中;置于背景之下； context If something is seen in context or if it is put into context , it is considered together with all the factors that relate to it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 脱离上下文;断章取义地； context If a statement or remark is quoted out of context , the circumstances in which it was said are not correctly reported, so that it seems to mean something different from the meaning that was intended.
contextual: [ADJ 形容词] 上下文的;与上下文有关的;与语境有关的； contextual A contextual issue or account relates to the context of something.
contiguous: [ADJ 形容词] 相接的;相邻的； contiguous Things that are contiguous are next to each other or touch each other.
continent: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大陆;洲； continent A continent is a very large area of land, such as Africa or Asia, that consists of several countries.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] (指英国之外的)欧洲大陆； People sometimes use the Continent to refer to the continent of Europe except for Britain.
continental: [ADJ 形容词] (除英国之外)欧洲大陆的； continental Continental means situated on or belonging to the continent of Europe except for Britain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 欧洲大陆人； A continental is someone who comes from the continent of Europe.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 典型欧洲大陆的;具欧洲大陆特征的； continental If you describe someone or something as continental , you think that they are typical of the continent of Europe.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 大洲的;大陆的； continental Continental is used to refer to something that belongs to or relates to a continent.
continental breakfast: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 欧陆式早餐;简易早餐； A continental breakfast is breakfast that consists of food such as bread, butter, jam, and a hot drink.
continental drift: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 大陆漂移； Continental drift is the slow movement of the Earth's continents towards and away from each other.
continental shelf: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 大陆架； The continental shelf is the area which forms the edge of a continent, ending in a steep slope to the depths of the ocean.
contingency: [N-VAR 可变名词] 可能发生的事;不测之事;突发事件； A contingency is something that might happen in the future.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (计划或措施)未雨绸缪的，应急的； contingency A contingency plan or measure is one that is intended to be used if a possible situation actually occurs.
contingent: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (警察、军队或军用车辆的)分遣队，小分队； contingent A contingent of police, soldiers, or military vehicles is a group of them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 代表团;代表队;代表群体； contingent A contingent is a group of people representing a country or organization at a meeting or other event.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 取决于…的;由…决定的； contingent If something is contingent on something else, the first thing depends on the second in order to happen or exist.
continual: [ADJ 形容词] 不停的;不间断的； continual continually A continual process or situation happens or exists without stopping.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 一再的;反复的;频繁的； continual continually Continual events happen again and again.
continuance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 持续;继续;延续； continuance The continuance of something is its continuation.
continuation: [N-VAR 可变名词] 持续;继续;延续； continuation The continuation of something is the fact that it continues, rather than stopping.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 续;延续部分； continuation Something that is a continuation of something else is closely connected with it or forms part of it.
continue: [VERB 动词] 继续;持续； continue If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 延续;继续； continue If something continues or if you continue it, it does not stop happening.  /  [VERB 动词] (中断后)继续，再开始； continue If you continue with something, you start doing it again after a break or interruption.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(中断后)继续； continue If something continues or if you continue it, it starts again after a break or interruption.
continuing education: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 继续教育;成人教育； continuing education Continuing education is education for adults in a variety of subjects, most of which are practical, not academic.
continuity: [N-VAR 可变名词] 连续性;连贯性； continuity Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (电影)剪辑； continuity In film making, continuity is the way that things filmed at different times are made to look as if they were filmed at the same time or in the right sequence.
continuity announcer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (电台或电视台的)节目串联主持人； A continuity announcer is someone who introduces the next programme on a radio or television station.
continuous: [ADJ 形容词] 连续不断的;持续的;不中断的； continuous continuously A continuous process or event continues for a period of time without stopping.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (线、表面等)连续的，没有间隔的； continuous A continuous line or surface has no gaps or holes in it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (动词)进行式的； In English grammar, continuous verb groups are formed using the auxiliary 'be' and the present participle of a verb, as in 'I'm feeling a bit tired' and 'She had been watching them for some time'.
continuous assessment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对学生的)连续性评估； If pupils or students undergo continuous assessment , they get qualifications partly or entirely based on the work they do during the year, rather than on exam results.
continuum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 统一体;连续体； continuum A continuum is a set of things on a scale, which have a particular characteristic to different degrees.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连续发生的事情； continuum A continuum is a continuous series of closely connected events.
contort: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] (面部、躯体等)扭曲，歪曲； contort If someone's face or body contorts or is contorted , it moves into an unnatural and unattractive shape or position.
contortion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (躯体、面部等的)扭弯，扭曲，变形； contortion Contortions are movements of your body or face into unusual shapes or positions.
contortionist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 柔术表演者;柔软杂技演员； A contortionist is someone who twists their body into strange and unnatural shapes and positions in order to entertain other people, for example in a circus.
contour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轮廓;外形； contour You can refer to the general shape or outline of an object as its contours .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (地图上的)等高线； contour A contour on a map is a line joining points of equal height and indicating hills, valleys, and the steepness of slopes.
contoured: [ADJ 形容词] 曲线的;有起伏的； contoured A contoured surface has curves and slopes on it, rather than being flat.
contraband: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 违禁物品;禁运品;走私货； contraband Contraband refers to goods that are taken into or out of a country illegally.
contraception: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 避孕法;节育法； contraception Contraception refers to methods of preventing pregnancy.
contraceptive: [ADJ 形容词] 避孕的;节育的； contraceptive A contraceptive method or device is a method or a device which a woman uses to prevent herself from becoming pregnant.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 避孕用具;避孕药物； contraceptive A contraceptive is a device or drug that prevents a woman from becoming pregnant.
contract: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 合同;契约； contract A contract is a legal agreement, usually between two companies or between an employer and employee, which involves doing work for a stated sum of money.  /  [VERB 动词] 签合同，订立契约(做某事)； contract If you contract with someone to do something, you legally agree to do it for them or for them to do it for you.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使收缩;使缩小;使缩短； contract contraction When something contracts or when something contracts it, it becomes smaller or shorter.  /  [VERB 动词] (经济、市场等)紧缩，缩小； contract When something such as an economy or market contracts , it becomes smaller.
contraction: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (分娩时的)子宫收缩，宫缩； When a woman who is about to give birth has contractions , she experiences a very strong, painful tightening of the muscles of her womb.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (词的)缩约形式； contraction A contraction is a shortened form of a word or words.  /  See also: contract ; �
contractor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 订约人;立约人;承包商； contractor A contractor is a person or company that does work for other people or organizations.
contract out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 订立合同把…承包出去； contract out If a company contracts out work, they employ other companies to do it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (正式)退出，同意不参加； contract out If a person or group contracts out of a system or scheme, they formally say that they do not want to take part in it.
contractual: [ADJ 形容词] 合同规定的;根据合约的； contractual contractually A contractual arrangement or relationship involves a legal agreement between people.
contradict: [VERB 动词] 反驳;否认;驳斥； contradict If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.  /  [VERB 动词] 与…矛盾;同… 抵触； contradict If one statement or piece of evidence contradicts another, the first one makes the second one appear to be wrong.  /  [VERB 动词] 违背;与…背道而驰； contradict If one policy or situation contradicts another, there is a conflict between them, and they cannot both exist or be successful.
contradiction: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 矛盾;不一致； contradiction If you describe an aspect of a situation as a contradiction , you mean that it is completely different from other aspects, and so makes the situation confused or difficult to understand.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 自相矛盾的说法； contradiction If you say that something is a contradiction in terms , you mean that it is described as having a quality that it cannot have.
contradictory: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 互相矛盾的;相互对立的； contradictory If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory , they state or imply that opposite things are true.
contraflow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (道路维修时暂时采取的)一侧路面双向行驶； contraflow A contraflow is a situation in which vehicles travelling on a main road in one direction have to use lanes that are normally used by traffic travelling in the opposite direction, because the road is being repaired.
contraindication: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 禁忌证； Contraindications are specific medical reasons for not using a particular treatment for a medical condition in the usual way.
contralto: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女低音;女低音歌手； contralto A contralto is a woman with a low singing voice.
contraption: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指奇怪的或不知道用途的)奇妙的装置;新奇玩意儿； contraption You can refer to a device or machine as a contraption , especially when it looks strange or you do not know what it is used for.
contrarian: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 叛逆的人;故意与众不同的人； contrarian A contrarian is a person who deliberately behaves in a way that is different from the people around them.
contrary: [ADJ 形容词] 相反的;相对的； contrary Ideas, attitudes, or reactions that are contrary to each other are completely different from each other.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 与…相反； If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 相反地； contrary You use on the contrary when you have just said or implied that something is not true and are going to say that the opposite is true.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 恰恰相反;正相反； contrary You can use on the contrary when you are disagreeing strongly with something that has just been said or implied, or are making a strong negative reply.
contrast: [N-VAR 可变名词] 差异;差别;悬殊； contrast A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 相比之下;与…相反； contrast You say by contrast or in contrast , or in contrast to something, to show that you are mentioning a very different situation from the one you have just mentioned.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 与…截然不同;与…对比鲜明； contrast If one thing is in contrast to another, it is very different from it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 截然不同的事物;差异明显的事物； contrast If one thing is a contrast to another, it is very different from it.
contravene: [VERB 动词] 违反，违背，触犯(法律或规则)； contravene contravention To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by the law or rule.
contretemps: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 令人尴尬的小争吵;口角； contretemps A contretemps is a small disagreement that is rather embarrassing.
contribute: [VERB 动词] (为…)做贡献； contribute If you contribute to something, you say or do things to help to make it successful.  /  [VERB 动词] 捐献;捐助;援助； contribute contributor To contribute money or resources to something means to give money or resources to help pay for something or to help achieve a particular purpose.  /  [VERB 动词] 促成;促使；是导致…的原因之一； contribute If something contributes to an event or situation, it is one of the causes of it.  /  [VERB 动词] (为报刊、书籍等)撰稿； contribute contributor If you contribute to a magazine, newspaper, or book, you write things that are published in it.
contribution: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 贡献； contribution If you make a contribution to something, you do something to help make it successful or to produce it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 捐款;捐资； contribution A contribution is a sum of money that you give in order to help pay for something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 稿件;投稿； A contribution to a magazine, newspaper, or book is something that you write to be published in it.
contributor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指不愉快事件的)促成因素，原因之一； contributor See also: contribute ; You can use contributor to refer to one of the causes of an event or situation, especially if that event or situation is an unpleasant one.
