crop top: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (女式)紧身短上衣； A crop top is a very short, usually tight, top worn by a girl or a woman.
crop up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (常指出其不意地)出现，发生； crop up If something crops up , it appears or happens, usually unexpectedly.
croquet: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 槌球游戏(在草地上进行，以木槌击球使之穿过金属圈)； Croquet is a game played on grass in which the players use long wooden sticks called mallets to hit balls through metal arches.
croquette: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (用土豆泥、肉馅等裹以面包屑做成的)炸丸子，炸条块； Croquettes are small amounts of mashed potato or meat rolled in breadcrumbs and fried.
cross: [VERB 动词] 穿越;越过;横过;渡过； cross If you cross something such as a room, a road, or an area of land or water, you move or travel to the other side of it.  /  [VERB 动词] (公路、铁路或桥)穿过，越过； cross A road, railway, or bridge that crosses an area of land or water passes over it.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 交叉;相交； cross Lines or roads that cross meet and go across each other.  /  [VERB 动词] 超过，超出(极限或范围)； cross If someone or something crosses a limit or boundary, for example the limit of acceptable behaviour, they go beyond it.
crossbar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (足球门等的)横梁； A crossbar is a horizontal piece of wood attached to two upright pieces, for example a part of the goal in football.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (男用自行车的)横梁； The crossbar of a man's or boy's bicycle is the horizontal metal bar between the handlebars and the saddle.
cross-border: [ADJ 形容词] (贸易)跨越国境的； cross-border Cross-border trade occurs between companies in different countries.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (袭击)跨越国境的； cross-border Cross-border attacks involve people crossing a border and going a short way into another country.
crossbow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 弩;弩弓;十字弓； A crossbow is a weapon consisting of a small, powerful bow that is fixed across a piece of wood, and aimed like a gun.
crossbreed: [V-RECIP-ERG ] 使杂交;杂交繁育； crossbreed cross-breeding If one species of animal or plant cross-breeds with another, they reproduce, and new or different animals or plants are produced.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (动物的)杂交品种； A cross-breed is an animal that is the result of cross-breeding.
cross-breed: [V-RECIP-ERG ] 使杂交;杂交繁育； cross-breed cross-breeding If one species of animal or plant cross-breeds with another, they reproduce, and new or different animals or plants are produced.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (动物的)杂交品种； A cross-breed is an animal that is the result of cross-breeding.
cross-Channel: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指乘船)穿越英吉利海峡的； cross-channel Cross-Channel travel is travel across the English Channel, especially by boat.
cross-check: [VERB 动词] 用不同方法或从不同出处反复核对,交叉检查； cross-check If you cross-check information, you check that it is correct using a different method or source from the one originally used to obtain it.
cross-country: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 越野比赛(如赛跑、自行车赛、滑雪赛等)； cross-country Cross-country is the sport of running, riding, or skiing across open countryside rather than along roads or around a running track.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 横越全国的;遍及全国的； cross-country A cross-country journey involves less important roads or railway lines, or takes you from one side of a country to the other.
cross-cultural: [ADJ 形容词] 跨文化的;涉及多种文化的； cross-cultural Cross-cultural means involving two or more different cultures.
cross-current: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (穿过其他水流的)交叉水流，逆流； A cross-current is a current in a river or sea that flows across another current.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不同的观点(或传统)； cross-current You can refer to conflicting ideas or traditions as cross-currents .
cross-dress: [VERB 动词] (尤指为获得性快感而)穿异性服装； cross-dress cross-dresser cross-dressing If someone cross-dresses , they wear the clothes of the opposite sex, especially for sexual pleasure.
cross-examine: [VERB 动词] (律师就某人所提供的证据进行)盘问，反诘； cross-examine cross-examination When a lawyer cross-examines someone during a trial or hearing, he or she questions them about the evidence that they have already given.
cross-eyed: [ADJ 形容词] 内斜视的;对眼的;斗鸡眼的； Someone who is cross-eyed has eyes that seem to look towards each other.
crossfire: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 交叉火力； Crossfire is gunfire, for example in a battle, that comes from two or more different directions and passes through the same area.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 被卷进争端； crossfire If you are caught in the crossfire , you become involved in an unpleasant situation in which people are arguing with each other, although you do not want to be involved or say which person you agree with.
crossing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 横渡； crossing A crossing is a journey by boat or ship to a place on the other side of a sea, river, or lake.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (道路的)十字路口;(线的)交叉点； A crossing is a place where two roads, paths, or lines cross.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 pedestrian crossing； crossing A crossing is the same as a pedestrian crossing .  /  See also: pelican crossing ; zebra crossing ;
cross-legged: [ADV 副词] 盘腿地； cross-legged If someone is sitting cross-legged , they are sitting on the floor with their legs bent so that their knees point outwards.
cross off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (从名单上)画掉，删掉； If you cross off words on a list, you decide that they no longer belong on the list, and often you draw a line through them to indicate this.
cross out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 画掉，删掉(字句)； If you cross out words on a page, you draw a line through them, because they are wrong or because you want to change them.
crossover: [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤指音乐或时尚风格上的)混合，融合； crossover A crossover of one style and another, especially in music or fashion, is a combination of the two different styles.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (在音乐或时尚上的)转型，改变风格； crossover In music or fashion, if someone makes a crossover from one style to another, they become successful outside the style they were originally known for.
cross-purposes: [PHRASE 短语] (谈话内容、所做之事等)互不相干，互不理解； cross-purposes If people are at cross-purposes , they do not understand each other because they are working towards or talking about different things without realizing it.
cross-question: [VERB 动词] 盘问;追问； cross-question If you cross-question someone, you ask them a lot of questions about something.
cross-reference: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (书中的)参见项，互见条，相互参照； A cross-reference is a note in a book which tells you that there is relevant or more detailed information in another part of the book.  /  [VERB 动词] (书等)加注使相互参照； cross-reference If something such as a book is cross-referenced , cross-references are put in it.
crossroads: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 十字路口； crossroads A crossroads is a place where two roads meet and cross each other.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (发展的)关键时刻，紧要关头； crossroads If you say that something is at a crossroads , you mean that it has reached a very important stage in its development where it could go one way or another.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 核心地区;汇集地； crossroads A crossroads is an important or central place.
cross-section: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 典型的一群人(或事物)； cross-section If you refer to a cross-section of particular things or people, you mean a group of them that you think is typical or representative of all of them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 横截面;剖面； cross-section A cross-section of an object is what you would see if you could cut straight through the middle of it.
cross-stitch: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 十字缝;十字形针法； Cross-stitch is a type of decorative sewing where one stitch crosses another.
crosswalk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人行横道； A crosswalk is a place where pedestrians can cross a street and where drivers must stop to let them cross.
crosswind: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 侧风；横风； A crosswind is a strong wind that blows across the direction that vehicles, boats, or aircraft are travelling in, and that makes it difficult for them to keep moving steadily forward.
crosswise: [ADV 副词] 对角横穿地;斜穿地； crosswise Crosswise means diagonally across something.
crossword: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纵横字谜;纵横填字游戏； A crossword or crossword puzzle is a word game in which you work out the answers and write them in the white squares of a pattern of small black and white squares.
crotch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (人体的)胯部，两腿分叉处； crotch Your crotch is the part of your body between the tops of your legs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (裤子等的)裆部； crotch The crotch of something such as a pair of trousers is the part that covers the area between the tops of your legs.
crotchet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 四分音符； A crotchet is a musical note that has a time value equal to two quavers.
crotchety: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脾气坏的;易怒的;动辄生气的； crotchety A crotchety person is bad-tempered and easily irritated.
crouch: [VERB 动词] 蹲;蹲伏； crouch crouch down 同 crouch If you are crouching , your legs are bent under you so that you are close to the ground and leaning forward slightly.  /  [VERB 动词] 俯身接近； crouch If you crouch over something, you bend over it so that you are very near to it.
croup: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 哮吼(儿童疾病)； Croup is a disease which children sometimes suffer from that makes it difficult for them to breathe and causes them to cough a lot.
croupier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (负责收发钱的)赌台管理员； A croupier is the person in charge of a gambling table in a casino, who collects the bets and pays money to the people who have won.
crouton: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (放在汤里的)油炸面包丁，吐司丁； crouton Croutons are small pieces of toasted or fried bread that are added to soup just before you eat it.
crow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乌鸦； A crow is a large black bird which makes a loud, harsh noise.  /  [VERB 动词] (公鸡)打鸣，啼叫； crow When a cock crows , it makes a loud sound, often early in the morning.  /  [VERB 动词] 对…洋洋自得;为…自鸣得意； crow If you say that someone is crowing about something they have achieved or are pleased about, you disapprove of them because they keep telling people proudly about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 欢叫;高兴地说； crow If someone crows , they make happy sounds or say something happily.
crowbar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 铁撬棍； A crowbar is a heavy iron bar which is used as a lever.
crowd: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 人群;观众； crowd A crowd is a large group of people who have gathered together, for example to watch or listen to something interesting, or to protest about something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (志趣相投或工作相同的)一伙人，一帮人； crowd A particular crowd is a group of friends, or a set of people who share the same interests or job.  /  [VERB 动词] 聚集在…周围;在…聚拢； crowd When people crowd around someone or something, they gather closely together around them.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使大批涌入； crowd If people crowd into a place or are crowded into a place, large numbers of them enter it so that it becomes very full.
crowded: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人多的;拥挤的； crowded If a place is crowded , it is full of people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 拥挤的;住有很多人的； crowded If a place is crowded , a lot of people live there.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 排满的;占满的； crowded If your timetable, your life, or your mind is crowded , it is full of events, activities, or thoughts.
crowd in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (问题或想法)大量涌现，涌入脑海； If problems or thoughts crowd in on you, a lot of them happen to you or affect you at the same time, so that they occupy all your attention and make you feel unable to escape.
crowd out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…排挤在外； If one thing crowds out another, it is so successful or common that the other thing does not have the opportunity to be successful or exist.
crowd-pleaser: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 取悦观众的人(或行动、事件)； If you describe a performer, politician, or sports player as a crowd-pleaser , you mean they always please their audience.
crowd-puller: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吸引大量观众的表演者(或事件)； crowd-puller If you describe a performer or event as a crowd-puller , you mean that they attract a large audience.
crown: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 王冠;皇冠;冕;(戴在头上的)冠状物； crown A crown is a circular ornament, usually made of gold and jewels, which a king or queen wears on their head at official ceremonies.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] 王国政府;王国;(英国刑事案件中的)公诉人； The government of a country that has a king or queen is sometimes referred to as the Crown .  /  [VERB 动词] 为…加冕;立…为王(或女王)； crown When a king or queen is crowned , a crown is placed on their head as part of a ceremony in which they are officially made king or queen.  /  [VERB 动词] 形成…的顶部;给…加顶； crown If one thing crowns another, it is on top of it.
Crown Court: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英格兰和威尔士的有法官和陪审团列席的)刑事法庭； Crown Court In England and Wales, a Crown Court is a court in which criminal cases are tried by a judge and jury rather than by a magistrate.
crown jewel: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (国王或女王在重要的正式场合佩戴的)王冠，权杖，珠宝； The Crown Jewels are the crown, sceptre, and other precious objects which are used on important official occasions by the King or Queen.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 最重要(或最有价值)的东西； crown jewel If you describe something as someone's crown jewel , you mean it is the most important or valuable thing they have.
Crown Prince: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 王储;皇太子； crown prince A Crown Prince is a prince who will be king of his country when the present king or queen dies.
Crown Princess: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 王储妃;皇太子妃;女王储； A Crown Princess is a princess who is the wife of a Crown Prince, or will be queen of her country when the present king or queen dies.
crown prosecutor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英国的)皇家检察官； In Britain, a crown prosecutor is a lawyer who works for the state and who prosecutes people who are accused of crimes.
crow's feet: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (眼角的)鱼尾纹； Crow's feet are wrinkles which some older people have at the outside corners of their eyes.
crow's nest: [N-SING 单数名词] (船上的)瞭望台； On a ship, the crow's nest is a small platform high up on the mast, where a person can go to look in all directions.
crucial: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 至关重要的;关键性的； crucial crucially If you describe something as crucial , you mean it is extremely important.
crucible: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 坩埚;熔炉； A crucible is a pot in which metals or other substances can be melted or heated up to very high temperatures.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 熔炉;严峻的考验;磨炼； crucible Crucible is used to refer to a situation in which something is tested or a conflict takes place, often one which produces something new.
crucifix: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (十字架)苦像;耶稣受难像； A crucifix is a cross with a figure of Christ on it.
crucifixion: [N-VAR 可变名词] 捆死(或钉死)在十字架上(罗马帝国时期常见)； crucifixion Crucifixion is a way of killing people which was common in the Roman Empire, in which they were tied or nailed to a cross and left to die.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] 耶稣受难； The Crucifixion is the crucifixion of Christ.
cruciform: [ADJ 形容词] (建筑等)十字形的； cruciform A cruciform building or object is shaped like a cross.
crucify: [VERB 动词] 把…捆在(或钉在)十字架上处死； If someone is crucified , they are killed by being tied or nailed to a cross and left to die.  /  [VERB 动词] 严厉批评;严惩； crucify To crucify someone means to criticize or punish them severely.
crude: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 粗略的;简略的;大概的； crude crudely A crude method or measurement is not exact or detailed, but may be useful or correct in a rough, general way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 粗糙的;简陋的； crude crudely If you describe an object that someone has made as crude , you mean that it has been made in a very simple way or from very simple parts.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 冒犯的;粗鲁的;不精明的； crude crudely crudity crudeness If you describe someone as crude , you disapprove of them because they speak or behave in a rude, offensive, or unsophisticated way.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 天然的;自然的； crude Crude substances are in a natural or unrefined state, and have not yet been used in manufacturing processes.
crude oil: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 原油； crude oil Crude oil is oil in its natural state before it has been processed or refined.
cruel: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 残酷的;冷酷的;残忍的;残暴的； cruel cruelly Someone who is cruel deliberately causes pain or distress to people or animals.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (处境或事件)引起痛苦的，残酷的； cruel cruelly A situation or event that is cruel is very harsh and causes people distress.
cruelty: [N-VAR 可变名词] 残暴;残忍;残酷； cruelty Cruelty is behaviour that deliberately causes pain or distress to people or animals.
cruet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (餐桌上的)调味品瓶，一组调味品瓶； cruet A cruet is a small container, or set of containers, for salt, pepper, or mustard which is used at meals.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (餐桌上盛油或醋的)调味品瓶； A cruet is a small glass bottle that contains oil or vinegar and is used at the table at meals.
cruise: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乘船游览;航游； cruise A cruise is a holiday during which you travel on a ship or boat and visit a number of places.  /  [VERB 动词] 乘船游览;航游； cruise cruising If you cruise a sea, river, or canal, you travel around it or along it on a cruise.  /  [VERB 动词] (车、船或飞机)以平稳且舒适的速度行驶，缓慢行进； cruise If a car, ship, or aircraft cruises somewhere, it moves there at a steady comfortable speed.  /  [VERB 动词] 球队或运动员轻而易举赢得，轻取； cruise If a team or sports player cruises to victory, they win easily.
cruise missile: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 巡航导弹； A cruise missile is a missile which carries a nuclear warhead and which is guided by a computer.
cruiser: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (可供住宿的)舱式游艇； cruiser See also: cabin cruiser ; A cruiser is a motor boat which has an area for people to live or sleep.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 巡洋舰； cruiser A cruiser is a large fast warship.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 巡逻警车； A cruiser is a police car.
cruiserweight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] light heavyweight 的别称； A cruiserweight is another name for a light heavyweight .
cruise ship: 大型游轮； cruise ship A cruise ship is a large ship which takes people from place to place on a cruise holiday, and on which entertainment, food, and drink are provided.
crumb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 食物碎屑;面包屑;糕饼屑； crumb Crumbs are tiny pieces that fall from bread, biscuits, or cake when you cut it or eat it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一点;少许； crumb A crumb of something, for example information, is a very small amount of it.
crumble: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使破碎;使成碎屑； crumble If something crumbles , or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.  /  [VERB 动词] 坍塌;损坏;崩裂； crumble away 同 crumble If an old building or piece of land is crumbling , parts of it keep breaking off.  /  [VERB 动词] (体系、关系或希望等)崩溃，瓦解，消亡； crumble crumble away 同 crumble If something such as a system, relationship, or hope crumbles , it comes to an end.  /  [VERB 动词] 不再抵抗;放弃奋斗;无力应付； crumble If someone crumbles , they stop resisting or trying to win, or become unable to cope.
crumbly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易碎的;脆的； crumbly Something that is crumbly is easily broken into a lot of little pieces.
crummy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 劣质的;低劣的;糟糕的； crummy Something that is crummy is unpleasant, of very poor quality, or not good enough.
crumpet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (上面有孔，烤后涂上黄油吃的)小圆烤饼； Crumpets are round, flat pieces of a substance like bread or batter with small holes in them.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对妩媚女人的蔑称)骚货； Some men refer to attractive women as crumpet .

dearth: [N-SING 单数名词] 缺乏;不足； dearth If there is a dearth of something, there is not enough of it.
death: [N-VAR 可变名词] 死;死亡； death Death is the permanent end of the life of a person or animal.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某种) 死法，死亡方式； death A particular kind of death is a particular way of dying.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 终结;结束;灭亡;破灭； death The death of something is the permanent end of it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 病危;行将就木； death If you say that someone is at death's door , you mean they are very ill indeed and likely to die.
deathbed: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 临终之病榻； deathbed If someone is on their deathbed , they are in a bed and about to die.
death blow: [N-SING 单数名词] 致命的打击;导致终结的原因； death blow If you say that an event or action deals a death blow to something such as a plan or hope, or is a death blow to something, you mean that it puts an end to it.
death camp: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指战时的) 死亡集中营； A death camp is a place where prisoners are kept, especially during a war, and where many of them die or are killed.
death certificate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死亡证明书； A death certificate is an official certificate signed by a doctor which states the cause of a person's death.
death duties: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 遗产税[现在称作 inheritance tax)； Death duties were a tax which had to be paid on the money and property of someone who had died.
death knell: [N-SING 单数名词] 丧钟;导致失败或终结、毁灭的原因； death knell If you say that something sounds the death knell for a particular person or thing, you mean it will cause that person or thing to fail, end, or cease to exist.
deathly: [ADV 副词] 死一般地； deathly If you say that someone is deathly pale or deathly still, you are emphasizing that they are very pale or still, like a dead person.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 极其;非常； deathly If you say that someone is deathly afraid, you are emphasizing that they are very afraid.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 沉默或寂静死一般的； deathly If you say that there is a deathly silence or a deathly hush, you are emphasizing that it is very quiet.
death mask: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死者的面模;模制遗容； A death mask is a model of someone's face, which is made from a mould that was taken of their face soon after they died.
death penalty: [N-SING 单数名词] 死刑;极刑； death penalty The death penalty is the punishment of death used in some countries for people who have committed very serious crimes.
death rate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死亡率； death rate The death rate is the number of people per thousand who die in a particular area during a particular period of time.
death rattle: [N-SING 单数名词] (行将终结之事物的) 征兆，前奏； death rattle If you say that one thing is the death rattle of another, you mean that the first thing is a sign that very soon the second thing will come to an end.
death row: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (监狱中的) 死囚区； death row If someone is on death row , they are in the part of a prison which contains the cells for criminals who have been sentenced to death.
death sentence: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死刑判决； death sentence A death sentence is a punishment of death given by a judge to someone who has been found guilty of a serious crime such as murder.
death squad: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (谋杀政治对手、罪犯等的)死亡小队，暗杀小组； Death squads are groups of people who operate illegally and carry out the killing of people such as their political opponents or criminals.
death taxes: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 遗产税[现在称作 inheritance tax)； Death taxes were a tax which had to be paid on the money and property of someone who had died.
death throes: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (彻底失败或终结前的)垂死挣扎； death throes The death throes of something are its final stages, just before it fails completely or ends.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 人或动物临死前痛苦的挣扎； If a person or animal is in their death throes , they are dying and making violent, uncontrolled movements, usually because they are suffering great pain.
death toll: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (事故、灾难或战争中的) 死亡人数； The death toll of an accident, disaster, or war is the number of people who die in it.
death trap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死亡陷阱;危险场所或车辆； death trap If you say that a place or vehicle is a death trap , you mean it is in such bad condition that it might cause someone's death.
death warrant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死刑执行令； A death warrant is an official document which orders that someone is to be executed as a punishment for a crime.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 自寻死路;自取灭亡； death warrant If you say that someone is signing their own death warrant , you mean that they are behaving in a way which will cause their ruin or death.
death wish: [N-SING 单数名词] (有意识或无意识的) 死亡愿望； A death wish is a conscious or unconscious desire to die or be killed.
deb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 debutante； A deb is the same as a debutante .
debacle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 彻底的失败;惨败； debacle A debacle is an event or attempt that is a complete failure.
debar: [VERB 动词] (法律或法规) 禁止； debar If you are debarred from doing something, you are prevented from doing it by a law or regulation.
debase: [VERB 动词] 降低…的价值[或质量]; 使贬值； debase debased To debase something means to reduce its value or quality.
debasement: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 贬值;质量的降低； debasement Debasement is the action of reducing the value or quality of something.
debatable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有争议的;有疑问的;未定的； debatable If you say that something is debatable , you mean that it is not certain.
debate: [N-VAR 可变名词] 各自发表不同观点的辩论，争论，讨论； debate A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (议会或其他机构就某问题在投票前进行的)辩论； debate debating A debate is a formal discussion, for example in a parliament or institution, in which people express different opinions about a particular subject and then vote on it.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 与…辩论，争论，讨论； debate If people debate a topic, they discuss it fairly formally, putting forward different views.  /  [VERB 动词] 考虑;盘算;权衡； debate If you debate whether to do something or what to do, you think or talk about possible courses of action before deciding exactly what you are going to do.
debater: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 辩论家;参加辩论者;辩手； debater A debater is someone who takes part in debates.
debauched: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 道德败坏的;放荡的;淫逸的； debauched If you describe someone as debauched , you mean they behave in a way that you think is socially unacceptable, for example because they drink a lot of alcohol or have sex with a lot of people.
debauchery: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 道德败坏;放荡;淫逸； debauchery You use debauchery to refer to the drinking of alcohol or to sexual activity if you disapprove of it or regard it as excessive.
debenture: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常由公司或政府部门发行的) 债券； A debenture is a type of savings bond which offers a fixed rate of interest over a long period.
debilitate: [VERB 动词] 使虚弱;使衰弱； debilitate debilitating debilitated If you are debilitated by something such as an illness, it causes your body or mind to become gradually weaker.  /  [VERB 动词] 削弱组织、社团或政府的力量； debilitate debilitating debilitated To debilitate an organization, society, or government means to gradually make it weaker.
debility: [N-VAR 可变名词] 尤指疾病引起的虚弱，衰弱； debility Debility is a weakness of a person's body or mind, especially one caused by an illness.
debit: [VERB 动词] 记入账户的借方； debit When your bank debits your account, money is taken from it and paid to someone else.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (银行账户的)借记，借入； debit A debit is a record of the money taken from your bank account, for example when you write a cheque.  /  See also: direct debit ; �
debit card: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 借记卡； A debit card is a bank card that you can use to pay for things.
debonair: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (男子)风流倜傥的，温文尔雅的，衣着入时的； debonair A man who is debonair is confident, charming, and well-dressed.
debrief: [VERB 动词] 听取士兵、外交官、宇航员等执行任务的情况汇报； debrief When someone such as a soldier, diplomat, or astronaut is debriefed , they are asked to give a report on an operation or task that they have just completed.
debriefing: [N-VAR 可变名词] (士兵、外交官、宇航员等的) 任务执行情况报告会； debriefing A debriefing is a meeting where someone such as a soldier, diplomat, or astronaut is asked to give a report on an operation or task that they have just completed.
debris: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 被毁物的残骸;碎片;垃圾； debris Debris is pieces from something that has been destroyed or pieces of rubbish or unwanted material that are spread around.
debt: [N-VAR 可变名词] 债务;欠款； debt See also: bad debt ; A debt is a sum of money that you owe someone.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 负债状态； debt 负债/不负债;欠债/不欠债 Debt is the state of owing money.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (表示感激) 我欠你个人情/我受你的恩惠； debt You use debt in expressions such as I owe you a debt or I am in your debt when you are expressing gratitude for something that someone has done for you.
debt burden: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 债务负担； debt burden A debt burden is a large amount of money that one country or organization owes to another and which they find very difficult to repay.
debtor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 债务人； debtor A debtor is a country, organization, or person who owes money.
debt-ridden: [ADJ 形容词] 债台高筑的;负债累累的； debt-ridden Debt-ridden countries, companies, or people owe extremely large amounts of money.
debug: [VERB 动词] 调试[程序]; 给…除错； debug When someone debugs a computer program, they look for the faults in it and correct them so that it will run properly.
debunk: [VERB 动词] 指出…的错误;揭穿…的吹嘘或虚假； debunk If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false.
debut: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (表演者或运动员的) 首次登台，初次露面；歌手的首次录音； debut The debut of a performer or sports player is their first public performance, appearance, or recording.
debutante: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (上层社会) 首次进入社交界的年轻女子； debutante A debutante is a young woman from the upper classes who has started going to social events with other young people.
decade: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 十年，十年期[尤指一个年代)； decade A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.
decadent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 堕落的;颓废的； decadent decadence If you say that a person or society is decadent , you think that they have low moral standards and are interested mainly in pleasure.
decaf: [N-MASS 物质名词] 脱咖啡因咖啡； Decaf is decaffeinated coffee.
decaff: [N-MASS 物质名词] 脱咖啡因咖啡； Decaf is decaffeinated coffee.
decaffeinated: [ADJ 形容词] (咖啡) 脱咖啡因的； Decaffeinated coffee has had most of the caffeine removed from it.
decal: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 利用加热等可转印图案的贴花纸； Decals are pieces of paper with a design on one side.
decamp: [VERB 动词] 偷偷逃走;突然离开； decamp If you decamp , you go away from somewhere secretly or suddenly.
decant: [VERB 动词] 把液体倒出[至其他容器中)； decant If you decant a liquid into another container, you put it into another container.
decanter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 玻璃斟酒瓶，盛酒瓶； A decanter is a glass container that you use for serving wine, sherry, or port.
decapitate: [VERB 动词] 将…斩首;杀…的头； decapitate decapitation If someone is decapitated , their head is cut off.
decathlon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 十项全能运动； The decathlon is a competition in which athletes compete in 10 different sporting events.
decay: [VERB 动词] (尸体或死去的植物) 腐烂，腐朽，腐败;(牙齿) 遭蛀蚀； decay decayed When something such as a dead body, a dead plant, or a tooth decays , it is gradually destroyed by a natural process.  /  [VERB 动词] (社会、制度、机构等) 衰败，衰退，衰落； decay If something such as a society, system, or institution decays , it gradually becomes weaker or its condition gets worse.
deceased: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 死者； deceased The deceased is used to refer to a particular person or to particular people who have recently died.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 近期死去的，去世的； deceased A deceased person is one who has recently died.
deceit: [N-VAR 可变名词] 欺骗;欺诈； deceit Deceit is behaviour that is deliberately intended to make people believe something which is not true.
deceitful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 欺骗的;欺诈的； deceitful If you say that someone is deceitful , you mean that they behave in a dishonest way by making other people believe something that is not true.
deceive: [VERB 动词] 欺骗;诓骗； deceive If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.  /  [VERB 动词] 欺骗，蒙骗(自己)； deceive If you deceive yourself , you do not admit to yourself something that you know is true.  /  [VERB 动词] 误导;蒙蔽； deceive If something deceives you, it gives you a wrong impression and makes you believe something that is not true.
decelerate: [VERB 动词] 降低速度;减速行驶或动转； deceleration When a vehicle or machine decelerates or when someone in a vehicle decelerates , the speed of the vehicle or machine is reduced.  /  [VERB 动词] (通货膨胀、经济增长等的速度)减缓，放慢； decelerate deceleration When the rate of something such as inflation or economic growth decelerates , it slows down.
December: [N-VAR 可变名词] 十二月； December December is the twelfth and last month of the year in the Western calendar.
decency: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 合宜;得体;正派;合乎礼仪； decency Decency is the quality of following accepted moral standards.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 出于礼貌应该做但没做…； decency If you say that someone did not have the decency to do something, you are criticizing them because there was a particular action which they did not do but which you believe they ought to have done.
decent: [ADJ 形容词] 像样的;尚好的;过得去的； decent decently Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 合宜的;得体的;适当的;正当的； decent decently Decent is used to describe something which is morally correct or acceptable.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人正派的，正直的，规矩的； decent Decent people are honest and behave in a way that most people approve of.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 做不想做但应该做的事； decent If you say that someone should do the decent thing , you mean that they should do something which they do not really want to do, but which you think they ought to do.
decentralize: [VERB 动词] 使政府或大型机构权力分散;下放…的权力； decentralize decentralization To decentralize government or a large organization means to move some departments away from the main administrative area, or to give more power to local departments.
deception: [N-VAR 可变名词] 欺骗;受骗； deception Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived by someone.
deceptive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 欺骗性的;造成假象的； deceptive deceptively If something is deceptive , it encourages you to believe something which is not true.
decibel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分贝[表示声音强度的单位)； decibel A decibel is a unit of measurement which is used to indicate how loud a sound is.
decide: [VERB 动词] 决定，拿定主意做； decide If you decide to do something, you choose to do it, usually after you have thought carefully about the other possibilities.  /  [VERB 动词] 解决;判决;裁决； decide If a person or group of people decides something, they choose what something should be like or how a particular problem should be solved.  /  [VERB 动词] 事件或事实决定，确定[某一选择或结果)； decide If an event or fact decides something, it makes it certain that a particular choice will be made or that there will be a particular result.  /  [VERB 动词] 断定;判定； decide If you decide that something is true, you form that opinion about it after considering the facts.
decided: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 确实无疑的;明白无误的;明显的； decided Decided means clear and definite.
decidedly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 明显地;显然； decidedly Decidedly means to a great extent and in a way that is very obvious.
decide on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 决定;选定； If you decide on something or decide upon something, you choose it from two or more possibilities.
decider: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 决胜场;决胜局； decider In sport, a decider is one of the games in a series, which establishes which player or team wins the series.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (足球、曲棍球等比赛中) 制胜的一球，决定胜负的一分； decider In games such as football and hockey, the decider is the last goal to be scored in a match that is won by a difference of only one goal.
deciduous: [ADJ 形容词] (树、灌木) 每年落叶的； A deciduous tree or bush is one that loses its leaves in the autumn every year.
decimal: [ADJ 形容词] 十进位的； decimal A decimal system involves counting in units of ten.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小数； decimal A decimal is a fraction that is written in the form of a dot followed by one or more numbers which represent tenths, hundredths, and so on: for example .
decimal point: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小数点； A decimal point is the dot in front of a decimal fraction.
decimate: [VERB 动词] 大批杀死;大量毁灭； decimate decimation To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.  /  [VERB 动词] 严重削弱，大幅缩减(系统或机构)； decimate decimation To decimate a system or organization means to reduce its size and effectiveness greatly.
decipher: [VERB 动词] 破译;译解； decipher If you decipher a piece of writing or a message, you work out what it says, even though it is very difficult to read or understand.
decision: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 决定;抉择； decision When you make a decision , you choose what should be done or which is the best of various possible actions.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 作决定;作抉择； decision Decision is the act of deciding something or the need to decide something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 果断;决断力； decision Decision is the ability to decide quickly and definitely what to do.
decision-making: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指大型机构或政府的) 决策过程； decision-making Decision-making is the process of reaching decisions, especially in a large organization or in government.
decisive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 决定性的;关键的;明确的； decisive decisively If a fact, action, or event is decisive , it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 果断的;决断的； decisive decisively decisiveness If someone is decisive , they have or show an ability to make quick decisions in a difficult or complicated situation.
deck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (公共汽车、船等的) 层面，一层； deck See also: flight deck ; A deck on a vehicle such as a bus or ship is a lower or upper area of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 最上层露天的甲板，舱面； deck The deck of a ship is the top part of it that forms a floor in the open air which you can walk on.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (录音机的)走带装置，匣仓;(唱机的)转盘支托面； deck A tape deck or record deck is a piece of equipment on which you play tapes or records.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (纸牌的)一副； deck A deck of cards is a complete set of playing cards.
deckchair: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常指海滩上、船上或花园里用的)帆布折叠躺椅； A deckchair is a simple chair with a folding frame, and a piece of canvas as the seat and back.
-decker: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] (用于 double, single 等形容词后)表示“…层的”； -decker -decker is used after adjectives like 'double' and 'single' to indicate how many levels or layers something has.
deckhand: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 舱面水手;普通水手； A deckhand is a person who does the cleaning and other work on the deck of a ship.
deck out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 装饰;打扮； If a person or thing is decked out with or in something, they are decorated with it or wearing it, usually for a special occasion.
deck shoe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 平底帆布鞋;休闲鞋； Deck shoes are flat casual shoes made of canvas or leather.
declaim: [VERB 动词] 慷慨陈词;高声朗诵； declaim If you declaim , you speak dramatically, as if you were acting in a theatre.

detonator: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雷管;引爆装置； A detonator is a small amount of explosive or a piece of electrical or electronic equipment which is used to explode a bomb or other explosive device.
detour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绕道;绕路;迂回； detour If you make a detour on a journey, you go by a route which is not the shortest way, because you want to avoid something such as a traffic jam, or because there is something you want to do on the way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绕行路线;迂回路线； A detour is a special route for traffic to follow when the normal route is blocked, for example because it is being repaired.  /  [VERB 动词] 绕道;绕路;绕行； detour If you detour , you make a detour.

detrimental: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有害的;不利的； detrimental Something that is detrimental to something else has a harmful or damaging effect on it.

disdain: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 轻视;鄙视;蔑视； disdain If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻视;鄙视;蔑视； disdain If you disdain someone or something, you regard them with disdain.  /  [VERB 动词] 不屑于做； disdain If you disdain to do something, you do not do it, because you feel that you are too important to do it.
disdainful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻蔑的;鄙视的； disdainful disdainfully To be disdainful means to dislike something or someone because you think they are unimportant or not worth your attention.
disease: [N-VAR 可变名词] 疾病;(动植物的)病害； disease A disease is an illness which affects people, animals, or plants, for example one which is caused by bacteria or infection.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指社会某一群体的弊病，积习，恶习； disease You can refer to a bad attitude or habit, usually one that a group of people have, as a disease .
diseased: [ADJ 形容词] 有病的;病变的;害病的； diseased Something that is diseased is affected by a disease.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (思想)病态的，不健康的； diseased If you say that someone's mind is diseased , you are emphasizing that you think it is not normal or balanced.
disembodied: [ADJ 形容词] 似脱离人而存在的;无实体的;脱离现实的； disembodied Disembodied means seeming not to be attached to or to come from anyone.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 脱离肉体的;与躯体分离的； disembodied Disembodied means separated from or existing without a body.
disembowel: [VERB 动词] 取出(人或动物)的内脏;将…开膛破肚； disembowel To disembowel a person or animal means to remove their internal organs, especially their stomach, intestines, and bowels.  /  [VERB 动词] 取出…内部的东西;把…掏空； disembowel To disembowel something means to take out the inside of it, especially in a such a way that it is destroyed or made completely useless.
disempower: [VERB 动词] 使没有权力[或影响力]; 剥夺…的权力； disempower If someone or something disempowers you, they take away your power or influence.
disenchanted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不再着迷的;不再抱有幻想的;感到幻灭的； disenchanted If you are disenchanted with something, you are disappointed with it and no longer believe that it is good or worthwhile.
disenchantment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 幻想破灭;醒悟； disenchantment Disenchantment is the feeling of being disappointed with something, and no longer believing that it is good or worthwhile.
disenfranchise: [VERB 动词] 剥夺…的选举权； disenfranchise To disenfranchise a group of people means to take away their right to vote, or their right to vote for what they really want.
disengage: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使脱离;使松开;解开;拆开； disengage If you disengage something, or if it disengages , it becomes separate from something which it has been attached to.  /  [VERB 动词] (军队)撤军； disengage If an army disengages from an area, it withdraws from that area.
disengaged: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不受牵连的;不受约束的； disengaged If someone is disengaged from something, they are not as involved with it as you would expect.
disengagement: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 脱离;分离； disengagement Disengagement is a process by which people gradually stop being involved in a conflict, activity, or organization.
disentangle: [VERB 动词] 理顺，分清，理清(复杂或混乱的情况)； disentangle If you disentangle a complicated or confused situation, you make it easier to understand or manage to understand it, by clearly recognizing each separate element.  /  [VERB 动词] 使解脱;使摆脱； disentangle If you disentangle something or someone from an undesirable thing or situation, you separate it from that thing or remove it from that situation.  /  [VERB 动词] 解开…的节;理顺； disentangle If you disentangle something, you separate it from things that are twisted around it, or things that it is twisted or knotted around.
disequilibrium: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不平衡;不稳定;失调； disequilibrium Disequilibrium is a state in which things are not stable or certain, but are likely to change suddenly.
disestablish: [VERB 动词] 废除(教会或宗教)的国教制； disestablish disestablishment To disestablish a church or religion means to take away its official status, so that it is no longer recognized as a national institution.
disfavour: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不喜欢;不赞成;受冷遇;失宠； disfavour If someone or something is in disfavour , people dislike or disapprove of them.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (表情流露出的)不喜欢,不赞成； disfavour If you look at someone or something with disfavour , the expression on your face shows that you dislike or disapprove of them.
disfigure: [VERB 动词] 使变丑;毁损…的容貌； disfigure disfigured If someone is disfigured , their appearance is spoiled.  /  [VERB 动词] 破坏…的外形;毁损…的外观； disfigure To disfigure an object or a place means to spoil its appearance.
disfigurement: [N-VAR 可变名词] (有损容貌的)缺陷;破相； disfigurement A disfigurement is something, for example a scar, that spoils a person's appearance.
disgorge: [VERB 动词] 排出;倾倒;喷吐； disgorge If something disgorges its contents, it empties them out.  /  [VERB 动词] (车、船、飞机等)下[客); (从建筑物中)涌出(人流)； disgorge If you say that a vehicle or building disgorges people, especially a lot of people, you mean that the people leave the vehicle or building.  /  [VERB 动词] (动物)吐出； disgorge If an animal disgorges something it has swallowed, it produces it again from its mouth.
disgrace: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 丢脸;耻辱;不光彩； disgrace If you say that someone is in disgrace , you are emphasizing that other people disapprove of them and do not respect them because of something that they have done.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 丢脸的事;不名誉的事； disgrace If you say that something is a disgrace , you are emphasizing that it is very bad or wrong, and that you find it completely unacceptable.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 让人蒙羞的人； disgrace You say that someone is a disgrace to someone else when you want to emphasize that their behaviour causes the other person to feel ashamed.  /  [VERB 动词] 使丢脸;使受辱； disgrace If you say that someone disgraces someone else, you are emphasizing that their behaviour causes the other person to feel ashamed.
disgraced: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人丢脸的，耻辱的，不光彩的； disgraced You use disgraced to describe someone whose bad behaviour has caused them to lose the approval and respect of the public or of people in authority.
disgraceful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 行为、情形等丢脸的，可耻的，不名誉的； disgraceful disgracefully If you say that something such as behaviour or a situation is disgraceful , you disapprove of it strongly, and feel that the person or people responsible should be ashamed of it.
disgruntled: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 恼火的;不满的;不高兴的； disgruntled If you are disgruntled , you are cross and dissatisfied because things have not happened the way that you wanted them to happen.
disguise: [N-VAR 可变名词] 假装;装扮;伪装； disguise If you are in disguise , you are not wearing your usual clothes or you have altered your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.  /  [VERB 动词] 假扮;化妆;乔装； disguise disguised If you disguise yourself , you put on clothes which make you look like someone else or alter your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.  /  [VERB 动词] 掩盖;掩饰； disguise disguised To disguise something means to hide it or make it appear different so that people will not know about it or will not recognize it.  /  a blessing in disguise » see: blessing �
disgust: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 厌恶;憎恶； disgust Disgust is a feeling of very strong dislike or disapproval.  /  [VERB 动词] 使厌恶;使憎恶； disgust To disgust someone means to make them feel a strong sense of dislike and disapproval.
disgusted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 厌恶的;憎恶的； disgusted disgustedly If you are disgusted , you feel a strong sense of dislike and disapproval at something.
disgusting: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人厌恶的;令人作呕的； disgusting If you say that something is disgusting , you are criticizing it because it is extremely unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 完全不能接受的;可怕的； disgusting If you say that something is disgusting , you mean that you find it completely unacceptable.
dish: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 盘;碟;碗； dish A dish is a shallow container with a wide uncovered top.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一盘或一碟的量； dish The contents of a dish can be referred to as a dish of something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一盘菜;菜肴;食品； dish Food that is prepared in a particular style or combination can be referred to as a dish .  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (就餐时用过的)所有餐具； dish All the objects that have been used to cook, serve, and eat a meal can be referred to as the dishes .
disharmony: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不协调;不和谐;不一致； disharmony When there is disharmony , people disagree about important things and this causes an unpleasant atmosphere.
dishcloth: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 擦碗布;擦碟布； A dishcloth is a cloth used to dry dishes after they have been washed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 洗碟布;洗碗布； A dishcloth is a cloth used for washing dishes, pans, and cutlery.
disheartened: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 灰心的;失望的;气馁的； disheartened If you are disheartened , you feel disappointed about something and have less confidence or less hope about it than you did before.
disheartening: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人灰心的;令人气馁的； If something is disheartening , it makes you feel disappointed and less confident or less hopeful.
dishevelled: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (头发、衣服、仪容等)蓬乱的，不整洁的； dishevelled If you describe someone's hair, clothes, or appearance as dishevelled , you mean that it is very untidy.
dishonest: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不诚实的;靠不住的； dishonest dishonestly If you say that a person or their behaviour is dishonest , you mean that they are not truthful or honest and that you cannot trust them.
dishonesty: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不诚实;欺诈； dishonesty Dishonesty is dishonest behaviour.
dishonour: [VERB 动词] 使丢脸;使丧失名誉； dishonour If you dishonour someone, you behave in a way that damages their good reputation.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不尊重;侮辱;丢脸； dishonour Dishonour is a state in which people disapprove of you and lose their respect for you.  /  [VERB 动词] 不遵守;不履行； dishonour If someone dishonours an agreement, they refuse to act according to its conditions.
dishonourable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不名誉的;可耻的;不光彩的； dishonourable dishonourably Someone who is dishonourable is not honest and does things which you consider to be morally unacceptable.
dish out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 分发； If you dish out something, you distribute it among a number of people.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 给予(批评、惩罚等)； dish out If someone dishes out criticism or punishment, they give it to someone.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 大加批评;严厉惩罚； If someone dishes it out to you, they strongly criticize or punish you.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 布菜;把(食物)装盘子上菜;从大盘中分菜； dish out If you dish out food, you serve it to people at the beginning of each course of a meal.
dish towel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 擦碗布； A dish towel is a cloth used to dry dishes after they have been washed.
dish up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 上菜； dish up If you dish up food, you serve it.
dishwasher: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 洗碗机； A dishwasher is an electrically operated machine that washes and dries plates, saucepans, and cutlery.
dishwater: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 洗碗水； Dishwater is water that dishes, pans, and cutlery have been washed in.
dishy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指女人眼中的男人)帅气的，迷人的； If you describe someone as dishy , you mean they are very good looking and attractive; used especially by women about men.
disillusion: [VERB 动词] 使醒悟;使不再抱幻想;使理想破灭； disillusion If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同 disillusionment； disillusion Disillusion is the same as disillusionment .
disillusioned: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 失望的;醒悟的;幻想破灭的； disillusioned If you are disillusioned with something, you are disappointed, because it is not as good as you had expected or thought.
disillusionment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 醒悟;不再抱幻想;理想破灭； disillusionment Disillusionment is the disappointment that you feel when you discover that something is not as good as you had expected or thought.
disincentive: [N-VAR 可变名词] 制止因素;阻碍因素； disincentive A disincentive is something which discourages people from behaving or acting in a particular way.
disinclination: [N-SING 单数名词] 不愿意;不喜欢;厌恶； disinclination A disinclination to do something is a feeling that you do not want to do it.
disinclined: [ADJ 形容词] 不愿意的;不喜欢的； disinclined If you are disinclined to do something, you do not want to do it.
disinfect: [VERB 动词] 为…消毒或杀菌； disinfect If you disinfect something, you clean it using a substance that kills germs.
disinfectant: [N-MASS 物质名词] 消毒剂； disinfectant Disinfectant is a substance that kills germs.
disinflation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 反通货膨胀;通货收缩； Disinflation is a reduction in the rate of inflation, especially as a result of government policies.
disinformation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 假情报;假消息； disinformation If you accuse someone of spreading disinformation , you are accusing them of spreading false information in order to deceive people.
disingenuous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不诚恳的;不坦率的;狡猾的； disingenuous disingenuously Someone who is disingenuous is slightly dishonest and insincere in what they say.
disinherit: [VERB 动词] 剥夺…的继承权； disinherit If you disinherit someone such as your son or daughter, you arrange that they will not become the owner of your money and property after your death, usually because they have done something that you do not approve of.
disintegrate: [VERB 动词] 崩溃;瓦解； disintegrate disintegration If something disintegrates , it becomes seriously weakened, and is divided or destroyed.  /  [VERB 动词] 碎裂;分裂;粉碎； disintegrate disintegration If an object or substance disintegrates , it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.
disinter: [VERB 动词] 挖掘出(尸体)； disinter When a dead body is disinterred , it is dug up from out of the ground.  /  [VERB 动词] 使重现;使复活;再度使用(很久未用过的东西)； disinter If you disinter something, you start using it again after it has not been used for a long time.
disinterest: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无兴趣;不关心;冷漠； disinterest If there is disinterest in something, people are not interested in it.
disinterested: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (指人)公正的，无私的； disinterested Someone who is disinterested is not involved in a particular situation or not likely to benefit from it and is therefore able to act in a fair and unselfish way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不感兴趣的;不关心的;冷漠的； disinterested If you are disinterested in something, you are not interested in it.
disjointed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (文字、思想、想法等)不连贯的，支离破碎的，杂乱无章的； disjointed Disjointed words, thoughts, or ideas are not presented in a smooth or logical way and are therefore difficult to understand.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (社会、体制、活动等)联系松散的，支离破碎的； disjointed Disjointed societies, systems, and activities are ones in which the different parts or elements are not as closely connected as they should be or as they used to be.
disk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 磁盘;磁碟； disk See also: disk drive ; floppy disk ; hard disk ; In a computer, the disk is the part where information is stored.
disk drive: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (计算机)磁盘驱动器； The disk drive on a computer is the part that contains the disk or into which a disk can be inserted.
diskette: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 floppy disk； A diskette is the same as a floppy disk .
dislike: [VERB 动词] 不喜欢;厌恶； dislike If you dislike someone or something, you consider them to be unpleasant and do not like them.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不喜欢;反感； dislike Dislike is the feeling that you do not like someone or something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 厌恶的事物； dislike Your dislikes are the things that you do not like.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 厌恶;嫌憎;讨厌； dislike If you take a dislike to someone or something, you decide that you do not like them.
dislocate: [VERB 动词] 使(骨头、关节)脱位;使脱臼； dislocate If you dislocate a bone or joint in your body, or in someone else's body, it moves out of its proper position in relation to other bones, usually in an accident.  /  [VERB 动词] 扰乱(制度、进程、生活方式等);使混乱;使运转不正常； dislocate To dislocate something such as a system, process, or way of life means to disturb it greatly or prevent it from continuing as normal.
dislocation: [N-VAR 可变名词] (制度、进程、生活方式等的)混乱，紊乱； dislocation Dislocation is a situation in which something such as a system, process, or way of life is greatly disturbed or prevented from continuing as normal.
dislodge: [VERB 动词] (从固定位置上)取出，去除，移动； dislodge To dislodge something means to remove it from where it was fixed or held.  /  [VERB 动词] 把(某人)逐出;把…赶下； dislodge To dislodge a person from a position or job means to remove them from it.
disloyal: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不忠实的;不忠诚的； disloyal Someone who is disloyal to their friends, family, or country does not support them or does things that could harm them.
disloyalty: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不忠； disloyalty Disloyalty is disloyal behaviour.
dismal: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忧郁的;凄凉的;令人沮丧的； dismal dismally Something that is dismal is bad in a sad or depressing way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指外表)阴暗的，阴沉的，沉闷的； dismal Something that is dismal is sad and depressing, especially in appearance.
dismantle: [VERB 动词] 拆卸;拆开;拆除； dismantle If you dismantle a machine or structure, you carefully separate it into its different parts.  /  [VERB 动词] 逐渐废除，撤销，破坏； dismantle To dismantle an organization or system means to cause it to stop functioning by gradually reducing its power or purpose.
dismay: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 惊恐;焦虑;哀伤； dismay Dismay is a strong feeling of fear, worry, or sadness that is caused by something unpleasant and unexpected.  /  [VERB 动词] 使惊恐;使焦急;使哀伤； dismay dismayed If you are dismayed by something, it makes you feel afraid, worried, or sad.
dismember: [VERB 动词] 肢解;分割…的躯体； dismember To dismember the body of a dead person or animal means to cut or pull it into pieces.  /  [VERB 动词] 分割;瓜分； dismember To dismember a country or organization means to break it up into smaller parts.
dismemberment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 肢解； dismemberment Dismemberment is the cutting or pulling into pieces of a body.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 国家或组织的分裂，瓦解； dismemberment Dismemberment is the breaking up into smaller parts of a country or organization.
dismiss: [VERB 动词] 不考虑;不理会； dismiss If you dismiss something, you decide or say that it is not important enough for you to think about or consider.  /  [VERB 动词] (从头脑中)去除;不再考虑;抛弃； dismiss If you dismiss something from your mind, you stop thinking about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 解雇;免…的职;开除； dismiss When an employer dismisses an employee, the employer tells the employee that they are no longer needed to do the job that they have been doing.  /  [VERB 动词] 让…离去;把…打发走;解散;遣散； dismiss If you are dismissed by someone in authority, they tell you that you can go away from them.
dismissal: [N-VAR 可变名词] 解雇;开除;免职； dismissal When an employee is dismissed from their job, you can refer to their dismissal .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不予考虑;不予理会； dismissal Dismissal of something means deciding or saying that it is not important.
dismissive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 拒绝考虑…的;对…轻视的;对…鄙视的； dismissive dismissively If you are dismissive of someone or something, you say or show that you think they are not important or have no value.
dismount: [VERB 动词] 下马;下车； dismount If you dismount from a horse or a bicycle, you get down from it.

drawback: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 缺点;缺陷;不利条件； drawback A drawback is an aspect of something or someone that makes them less acceptable than they would otherwise be.
drawbridge: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吊桥;开合桥； A drawbridge is a bridge that can be pulled up, for example to prevent people from getting into a castle or to allow ships to pass underneath it.
drawer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 抽屉； drawer A drawer is part of a desk, chest, or other piece of furniture that is shaped like a box and is designed for putting things in.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (尤指女式)内裤； Drawers are underpants, especially ones worn by women.  /  See also: chest of drawers ; �
draw in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (白昼)渐短；(天黑)渐早； draw in If you say that the nights, evenings, or days are drawing in , you mean that it is becoming dark at an earlier time in the evening, because autumn or winter is approaching.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使参与;使卷入； If you draw someone in or draw them into something you are involved with, you cause them to become involved with it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 深呼吸;吸入空气； If you draw in your breath, you breathe in deeply.
drawing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 素描[画]; 图画； drawing See also: draw ; A drawing is a picture made with a pencil or pen.
drawing board: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绘画板;图画板;制图板； A drawing board is a large flat board, often fixed to a metal frame so that it looks like a desk, on which you place your paper when you are drawing or designing something.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (失败后)从头再来,另起炉灶； If you say that you will have to go back to the drawing board , you mean that something which you have done has not been successful and that you will have to start again or try another idea.
drawing pin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 图钉； A drawing pin is a short pin with a broad, flat top which is used for fastening papers or pictures to a board, wall, or other surface.
drawing room: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 起居室;客厅； A drawing room is a room, especially a large room in a large house, where people sit and relax, or entertain guests.
drawl: [VERB 动词] 拉长调子说;慢吞吞地说； drawl If someone drawls , they speak slowly and not very clearly, with long vowel sounds.
drawn: + + + Drawn is the past participle of draw .  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (人或人脸)清瘦的,憔悴的,愁眉苦脸的； drawn If someone or their face looks drawn , their face is thin and they look very tired, ill, worried, or unhappy.
drawn-out: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 拖得太久的;冗长的； drawn-out You can describe something as drawn-out when it lasts or takes longer than you would like it to.
draw off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 抽出;排掉;汲出； If a quantity of liquid is drawn off from a larger quantity, it is taken from it, usually by means of a needle or pipe.
draw on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 凭借;利用;动用； If you draw on or draw upon something such as your skill or experience, you make use of it in order to do something.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (时光)渐渐过去； As a period of time draws on , it passes and the end of it gets closer.
draw out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拉长,拖长(声音、单词等)； If you draw out a sound or a word, you make it last longer than usual.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使畅所欲言;使愿意交谈； If you draw someone out , you make them feel less nervous and more willing to talk.
drawstring: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (穿在袋口、裤腰上的)拉绳,拉带,束带； drawstring A drawstring is a cord that goes through an opening, for example at the top of a bag or a pair of trousers.
draw up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 草拟;制定； draw up If you draw up a document, list, or plan, you prepare it and write it out.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把(椅子等)拉近;使接近； If you draw up a chair, you move it nearer to a person or place, for example so that you can watch something or join in with something.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 伸直背部;挺直身子； If you draw yourself up , you make your back very straight.
dray: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 四轮运货大马车;马拉板车； A dray is a large flat cart with four wheels which is pulled by horses.
dread: [VERB 动词] 非常担心;极为害怕； dread If you dread something which may happen, you feel very anxious and unhappy about it because you think it will be unpleasant or upsetting.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 忧虑;恐惧； dread Dread is a feeling of great anxiety and fear about something that may happen.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 可怕的;令人畏惧的； dread Dread means terrible and greatly feared.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 恼火的;生气的;不想要的； dread You can use dread to describe something that you, or a particular group of people, find annoying or undesirable.
dreaded: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可怕的;令人畏惧的； dreaded Dreaded means terrible and greatly feared.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 令人恼火的;不方便的;不想要的； dreaded You can use the dreaded to describe something that you, or a particular group of people, find annoying, inconvenient, or undesirable.
dreadful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 糟糕透顶的;令人不快的;劣质的； dreadful dreadfully If you say that something is dreadful , you mean that it is very bad or unpleasant, or very poor in quality.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 极严重的； dreadful dreadfully Dreadful is used to emphasize the degree or extent of something bad.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (看上去或感觉到)病得不轻的,极度疲惫的,非常沮丧的； dreadful If someone looks or feels dreadful , they look or feel very ill, tired, or upset.
dreadfully: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 糟糕透顶的;令人不快的;劣质的； dreadfully If you say that something is dreadful , you mean that it is very bad or unpleasant, or very poor in quality.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 极严重的； dreadfully Dreadful is used to emphasize the degree or extent of something bad.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (看上去或感觉到)病得不轻的,极度疲惫的,非常沮丧的； If someone looks or feels dreadful , they look or feel very ill, tired, or upset.
dreadlocked: [ADJ 形容词] 蓄“骇人”长发绺的； dreadlocked A dreadlocked person has their hair in dreadlocks.
dreadlocks: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 尤指拉斯塔法里教派成员蓄的“骇人”长发绺； dreadlocks If someone has dreadlocks , their hair is divided into a large number of tight strips, like pieces of rope.
dream: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梦； dream A dream is an imaginary series of events that you experience in your mind while you are asleep.  /  [VERB 动词] 做梦;梦见;梦到； dream When you dream , you experience imaginary events in your mind while you are asleep.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梦想;幻想;愿望； dream You can refer to a situation or event as a dream if you often think about it because you would like it to happen.  /  [VERB 动词] 梦想;渴望； dream If you often think about something that you would very much like to happen or have, you can say that you dream of it.
dreamer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梦想家;空想家;不切实际的人； dreamer If you describe someone as a dreamer , you mean that they spend a lot of time thinking about and planning for things that they would like to happen but which are improbable or impractical.
dreamily: [ADV 副词] 出神地;想入非非地;心不在焉地； dreamily If you say or do something dreamily , you say or do it in a way that shows your mind is occupied with pleasant, relaxing thoughts.
dreamland: [N-SING 单数名词] 世外桃源;似仙境之地； dreamland If you describe a place as a dreamland , you mean that it is so beautiful it is hard to believe that it is real.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 梦境;幻想世界;理想世界； dreamland If you refer to a situation as dreamland , you mean that it represents what someone would like to happen, but that it is completely unrealistic.
dreamless: [ADJ 形容词] 无梦的;酣畅安宁的； dreamless A dreamless sleep is very deep and peaceful, and without dreams.
dreamlike: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 梦幻般的;模糊的;朦胧的； dreamlike If you describe something as dreamlike , you mean it seems strange and unreal.
dreamt: + + + Dreamt is a past tense and past participle of dream .
dream team: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梦之队;最佳阵容;最佳组合； dream team A dream team is the best possible group of people to be in a sports team or to do a particular job.
dream ticket: [N-SING 单数名词] (政治竞选的)黄金拍档,最佳候选人组合； dream ticket If journalists talk about a dream ticket , they are referring to two candidates for political positions, for example President and Vice-President, or Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister, who they think will be extremely successful.
dream up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 凭空想象出;虚构出； If you dream up a plan or idea, you work it out or create it in your mind.
dreamy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 恍惚的;出神的； dreamy If you say that someone has a dreamy expression, you mean that they are not paying attention to things around them and look as if they are thinking about something pleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻柔的;柔和的;梦幻般的； dreamy If you describe something as dreamy , you mean that you like it and that it seems gentle and soft, like something in a dream.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不切实际的;爱空想的； dreamy If you describe a person or an idea as dreamy , you mean that they are not very practical.  /  See also: dreamily ; �
dreary: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沉闷的;枯燥无味的;令人沮丧的； dreary drearily If you describe something as dreary , you mean that it is dull and depressing.
dredge: [VERB 动词] 疏浚;清淤;挖掘； When people dredge a harbour, river, or other area of water, they remove mud and unwanted material from the bottom with a special machine in order to make it deeper or to look for something.  /  相关词组： dredge up �
dredger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 挖泥船;疏浚船； A dredger is a boat which is fitted with a special machine that is used to increase the size of harbours, rivers, and canals.
dredge up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 忆起;想起； dredge up If someone dredges up a piece of information they learned a long time ago, or if they dredge up a distant memory, they manage to remember it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 翻出,重提(令人不快的往事)； dredge up If someone dredges up a damaging or upsetting fact about your past, they remind you of it or tell other people about it.
dregs: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 残渣;渣滓;沉淀物； dregs The dregs of a liquid are the last drops left at the bottom of a container, together with any solid bits that have sunk to the bottom.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 渣滓;败类； dregs If you talk about the dregs of society or of a community, you mean the people in it who you consider to be the most worthless and bad.
drench: [VERB 动词] 使湿透;使浸湿； drench -drenched To drench something or someone means to make them completely wet.
dress: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连衣裙； dress A dress is a piece of clothing worn by a woman or girl.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 衣服； dress See also: evening dress ; fancy dress ; full dress ; morning dress ; You can refer to clothes worn by men or women as dress .  /  [VERB 动词] 穿衣； dress When you dress or dress yourself , you put on clothes.  /  [VERB 动词] 给…穿衣服；  dress If you dress someone, for example a child, you put clothes on them.
dressage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 花式骑术比赛； Dressage is a competition in which horse riders have to make their horse perform controlled movements.
dress circle: [N-SING 单数名词] (戏院)二楼楼厅前座； The dress circle is the lowest of the curved rows of seats upstairs in a theatre.
dress code: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 着装标准； dress code The dress code of a place is the rules about what kind of clothes people are allowed to wear there.
dress down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (比平时)穿着随便； If you dress down , you wear clothes that are less smart than usual.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 训斥;责骂； See also: dressing-down ; If you dress someone down , you speak angrily to them because they have done something bad or foolish.
dress-down Friday: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 星期五便装日(有的公司允许员工在这一天着便装上班)； dress-down Friday In some companies employees are allowed to wear clothes that are less smart than usual on a Friday.
dressed: [ADJ 形容词] 穿着衣服的;穿着整齐的；  dressed If you are dressed , you are wearing clothes rather than being naked or wearing your night clothes.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 穿着…衣服的;作…打扮的； dressed See also: well-dressed ; If you are dressed in a particular way, you are wearing clothes of a particular colour or kind.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 打扮得引人注目;打扮得花枝招展;衣着光鲜； dressed If someone is dressed to kill , they are wearing very smart or fashionable clothes because they want people to notice them and think they are attractive.
dressed up: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 穿上盛装的;装扮成…的； dressed up If someone is dressed up , they are wearing special clothes, in order to look smarter than usual or in order to disguise themselves.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 装扮成;伪装成； dressed up If you say that something is dressed up as something else, you mean that someone has tried to make it more acceptable or attractive by making it seem like that other thing.  /  dressed up to the nines » see: nine �
dresser: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梳妆台； A dresser is a chest of drawers, usually with a mirror on the top.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常指用来存放瓷器的)碗橱,餐具柜； A dresser is a piece of furniture which has cupboards or drawers in the lower part and shelves in the top part.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (剧院中协助演员穿戏服的)换装师,服装师； dresser A dresser is someone who works in a theatre and helps the actors and actresses to dress.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 穿着…的人;衣着…者； dresser You can use dresser to refer to the kind of clothes that a person wears.
dressing: [N-MASS 物质名词] (用油、醋、香料等制成的,拌色拉用的)调料； dressing A salad dressing is a mixture of oil, vinegar, and herbs or flavourings, which you pour over salad.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (保护伤口用的)敷料； dressing A dressing is a covering that is put on a wound to protect it while it heals.
dressing-down: [N-SING 单数名词] 训斥;责骂； dressing-down If someone gives you a dressing-down , they speak angrily to you because you have done something bad or foolish.
dressing gown: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 晨衣(起床后穿在睡衣外面的宽松外衣)； A dressing gown is a long, loose garment which you wear over your night clothes when you are not in bed.
dressing room: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (剧院的)化妆室； A dressing room is a room in a theatre where performers can dress and get ready for their performance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (运动员的)更衣室； A dressing room is a room at a sports stadium where players can change and get ready for their game.
dressing table: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梳妆台； A dressing table is a small table in a bedroom.
dressing-up: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (儿童的)化装游戏； When children play at dressing-up , they put on special or different clothes and pretend to be different people.
dressmaker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (女装或童装的)裁缝,服装师； A dressmaker is a person who makes women's or children's clothes.
dressmaking: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 女装裁制业； Dressmaking is the activity or job of making clothes for women or girls.
dress rehearsal: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (正式演出前的最后)彩排； The dress rehearsal of a play, opera, or show is the final rehearsal before it is performed, in which the performers wear their costumes and the lights and scenery are all used as they will be in the performance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (事件的)预演,彩排； dress rehearsal You can describe an event as a dress rehearsal for a later, more important event when it indicates how the later event will be.
dress sense: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 着装品位； dress sense Someone's dress sense is their ability to choose clothes that make them look attractive.
dress shirt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (男子的)礼服衬衫； A dress shirt is a special shirt which men wear on formal occasions.
dress up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 装扮;打扮； dress up If you dress up or dress yourself up , you put on different clothes, in order to make yourself look smarter than usual or to disguise yourself.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 给…打扮;给…装扮； If you dress someone up , you give them special clothes to wear, in order to make them look smarter or to disguise them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 修饰;美化;粉饰； dress up If you dress something up , you try to make it seem more attractive, acceptable, or interesting than it really is.  /  See also: dressed up ; dressing-up ; �
dressy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (服装)漂亮雅致的,讲究的； Dressy clothes are smart clothes which you wear when you want to look elegant or formal.
drew: + + + Drew is the past tense of draw .
dribble: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使滴下;使一点一滴地落下； dribble If a liquid dribbles somewhere, or if you dribble it, it drops down slowly or flows in a thin stream.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 点滴;少量； dribble A dribble of a liquid is a very small amount of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 运球;带球;盘球； dribble When players dribble the ball in a game such as football or basketball, they keep kicking or tapping it quickly in order to keep it moving.  /  [VERB 动词] 流口水;垂涎； dribble If a person dribbles , saliva drops slowly from their mouth.
dribs and drabs: [PHRASE 短语] 三三两两;零星； dribs and drabs If people or things arrive in dribs and drabs , they arrive in small numbers over a period of time rather than arriving all together.
dried: [ADJ 形容词] (食物或牛奶)干的,脱水的； dried See also: dry ; Dried food or milk has had all the water removed from it so that it will last for a long time.
dried fruit: [N-VAR 可变名词] 果干儿;干果;(尤指)葡萄干； Dried fruit is fruit that has been preserved by being dried; used especially to refer to currants, raisins, or sultanas, which are kinds of dried grapes.
dried-up: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人干瘪衰老的，老态龙钟的； dried-up See also: dry up ; If you describe someone as dried-up , you are saying rudely that they are old and dull, and not worth paying attention to.
drift: [VERB 动词] 飘移;漂流； drift When something drifts somewhere, it is carried there by the movement of wind or water.  /  [VERB 动词] 无意间进入;不知不觉陷入； drift If someone or something drifts into a situation, they get into that situation in a way that is not planned or controlled.  /  [VERB 动词] 流浪;漂泊； drift If you say that someone drifts around, you mean that they travel from place to place without a plan or settled way of life.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 移动;动向;趋势;逐渐变化； drift A drift is a movement away from somewhere or something, or a movement towards somewhere or something different.
drifter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 漂泊者;盲流； If you describe someone as a drifter , you mean that they do not stay in one place or in one job for very long.
drift off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 迷迷糊糊地睡去;逐渐入睡； If you drift off to sleep, you gradually fall asleep.
driftwood: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 漂流木,浮木(被海水或河流冲上岸或仍在水中漂流的木头)； Driftwood is wood which has been carried onto the shore by the motion of the sea or a river, or which is still floating on the water.
drill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 钻头;钻床;电钻； drill A drill is a tool or machine that you use for making holes.  /  [VERB 动词] 钻孔;打眼； drill When you drill into something or drill a hole in something, you make a hole in it using a drill.  /  [VERB 动词] 钻探(石油或水源)； drill drilling When people drill for oil or water, they search for it by drilling deep holes in the ground or in the bottom of the sea.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 学生的反复练习； drill A drill is a way that teachers teach their students something by making them repeat it many times.
drink: [VERB 动词] 喝;饮； drink When you drink a liquid, you take it into your mouth and swallow it.  /  [VERB 动词] 喝酒； drink drinking To drink means to drink alcohol.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一杯,一口,一份(饮料)； drink A drink is an amount of a liquid which you drink.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 酒;酒精饮料； drink A drink is an alcoholic drink.
drinkable: [ADJ 形容词] 可饮用的； Water that is drinkable is clean and safe for drinking.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 好喝的； drinkable If you say that a particular wine, beer, or other drink is drinkable , you mean that it tastes quite pleasant.
drink-drive: [ADJ 形容词] 酒后驾车;醉酒驾驶； Drink-drive means relating to drink-driving.
drinker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 常饮…者;常喝…者； drinker If someone is a tea drinker or a beer drinker , for example, they regularly drink tea or beer.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 饮酒者;(尤指)酗酒者，酒徒； drinker If you describe someone as a drinker , you mean that they drink alcohol, especially in large quantities.
drink in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 聚精会神地看(或听);尽情地欣赏;陶醉于； If you drink in something that you see or hear, you pay a lot of attention to it and enjoy it.
drinking: [ADJ 形容词] 喜欢饮酒的;经常饮酒的;贪杯的； See also: drink ; Someone's drinking friends or companions are people they regularly drink alcohol with.
drinking fountain: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (设在街头、公园、学校等的)喷水式饮水器； A drinking fountain is a device which supplies water for people to drink in places such as streets, parks, or schools.
drinking water: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 饮用水； Drinking water is water which it is safe to drink.

dumb-bell: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 哑铃； A dumb-bell is a short bar with weights on either side which people use for physical exercise to strengthen their arm and shoulder muscles.

dummy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人体模型,假人(常用于陈列服装)； dummy A dummy is a model of a person, often used to display clothes.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 仿制品;仿造样品； dummy You can use dummy to refer to things that are not real, but have been made to look or behave as if they are real.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (婴儿用的)橡皮奶嘴,橡皮奶头； A baby's dummy is a rubber or plastic object that you give the baby to suck so that he or she feels comforted.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 笨蛋;蠢货； dummy If you call someone a dummy , you mean that you think they are stupid.

dumpy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 矮胖而丑陋的； If you describe someone as dumpy , you mean they are short and fat, and are usually implying they are unattractive.
dun: [COLOUR 颜色词] 棕灰色;灰褐色;暗褐色； dun Something that is dun is a dull grey-brown colour.
