face powder: [N-MASS 物质名词] 扑面粉;定妆粉;蜜粉； Face powder is a very fine soft powder that you can put on your face in order to make it look smoother.
face-saver: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保全面子的行为(或借口)； A face-saver is an action or excuse which prevents damage to your reputation or the loss of people's respect for you.
face-saving: [ADJ 形容词] 保全面子的;挽回面子的； face-saving A face-saving action is one which prevents damage to your reputation or the loss of people's respect for you.
facet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 部分;方面； facet A facet of something is a single part or aspect of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (钻石等宝石的)琢面，饰面，切面； The facets of a diamond or other precious stone are the flat surfaces that have been cut on its outside.
facetious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (不分场合)乱开玩笑的，贫嘴的； facetious facetiously If you say that someone is being facetious , you are criticizing them because they are making humorous remarks or saying things that they do not mean in a situation where they ought to be serious.
face value: [N-SING 单数名词] (钱币、投资票据或票的)面值，面额； face value The face value of things such as coins, paper money, investment documents, or tickets is the amount of money that they are worth, and that is written on them.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 按照表面意思;(对…)信以为真； face value If you take something at face value , you accept it and believe it without thinking about it very much, even though it might be untrue.
facial: [ADJ 形容词] 面部的;脸上的； facial Facial means appearing on or being part of your face.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 面部护理;美容； A facial is a sort of beauty treatment in which someone's face is massaged, and creams and other substances are rubbed into it.
facile: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 主张、建议肤浅的，粗浅的，轻率的； facile If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile , you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.
facilitate: [VERB 动词] 促进;使便利； facilitate To facilitate an action or process, especially one that you would like to happen, means to make it easier or more likely to happen.
facilitator: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 促进者;推动者;协调者； A facilitator is a person or organization that helps another person or organization to do or to achieve a particular thing.
facility: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 设备;设施； facility Facilities are buildings, pieces of equipment, or services that are provided for a particular purpose.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 组织提供的附加服务，特色服务;(机器的)功能； facility A facility is something such as an additional service provided by an organization or an extra feature on a machine which is useful but not essential.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 天资;才能;天赋； facility If you have a facility for something, for example learning a language, you find it easy to do.
facing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (衣服的)镶边，贴边，里子； Facing is fabric which is stitched inside the edges of a piece of clothing in order to make them look neat and strengthen them.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (夹克或大衣领口和袖口的)镶边，贴边； The facings of a garment such as a jacket or coat are the parts around the neck and wrists when they are made of a different fabric from the main part, or are a different colour.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (墙的)贴面，饰面； A facing on a wall is a layer of stone, concrete, or other material that is spread over its surface in order to make it look attractive.
facsimile: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 复制品;仿制品;摹本； facsimile A facsimile of something is an copy or imitation of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 fax； A facsimile is the same as a fax .
fact: [PHRASE 短语] 考虑到…／除…外／虽然…； fact You use the fact that after some verbs or prepositions, especially in expressions such as in view of the fact that , apart from the fact that , and despite the fact that , to link the verb or preposition with a clause.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (用于强调或当从句为句子主语时)； fact You use the fact that instead of a simple that-clause either for emphasis or because the clause is the subject of your sentence.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 准确地说;确切地说； fact You use in fact , in actual fact , or in point of fact to indicate that you are giving more detailed information about what you have just said.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (用于修正、引出相反意见或对比等)事实上，其实； fact You use in fact , in actual fact , or in point of fact to introduce or draw attention to a comment that modifies, contradicts, or contrasts with a previous statement.
fact-finding: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指官方组织)实情调查的； fact-finding A fact-finding mission or visit is one whose purpose is to get information about a particular situation, especially for an official group.
faction: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (大团体中的)派系，派别，小集团； faction A faction is an organized group of people within a larger group, which opposes some of the ideas of the larger group and fights for its own ideas.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 派系之争;内讧； Faction is also used to describe argument and disagreement within a group of people.
factional: [ADJ 形容词] 派系的;宗派的;派别的； factional Factional arguments or disputes involve two or more small groups from within a larger group.
factionalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 派系冲突;派系间的争端； factionalism Factionalism refers to arguments or disputes between two or more small groups from within a larger group.
fact of life: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (令人不快却又无法改变的)生活现实； fact of life You say that something which is not pleasant is a fact of life when there is nothing you can do to change it so you must accept it.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (教给儿童的)性知识； If you tell a child about the facts of life , you tell him or her about sexual intercourse and how babies are born.
factor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 因素;要素； factor A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (增长的)倍数； factor If an amount increases by a factor of two, for example, or by a factor of eight, then it becomes two times bigger or eight times bigger.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 系数； factor You can use factor to refer to a particular level on a scale of measurement.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 因子;因数； A factor of a whole number is a smaller whole number which can be multiplied with another whole number to produce the first whole number.
factor in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将…计入;将…考虑进去； If you factor a particular cost or element into a calculation you are making, or if you factor it in , you include it.
factory: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 工厂； A factory is a large building where machines are used to make large quantities of goods.
factory farming: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 工业化养殖;工厂化饲养； Factory farming is a system of farming which involves keeping animals indoors, often with very little space, and giving them special foods so that they grow more quickly or produce more eggs or milk.
factory floor: [N-SING 单数名词] (与管理人员相对的)工人;工厂;车间； factory floor The factory floor refers to the workers in a factory, as opposed to the managers.
factory outlet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 工厂直销店;厂家直营店； factory outlet A factory outlet is a shop where a factory sells damaged or out-of-date goods directly to customers at reduced prices.
factory ship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (配有加工及冷冻设备的)大型捕鱼船； A factory ship is a large fishing boat which has equipment for processing the fish that are caught, for example by cleaning or freezing them, before it returns to port.
factotum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 勤杂工;事务总管； A factotum is a servant who is employed to do a wide variety of jobs for someone.
fact sheet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指有关广播或电视节目梗概的)情况简报，资料页； A fact sheet is a short, printed document with information about a particular subject, especially a summary of information that has been given on a radio or television programme.
factual: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 与事实有关的;真实的； factual factually Something that is factual is concerned with facts or contains facts, rather than giving theories or personal interpretations.
faculty: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 官能;能力； faculty Your faculties are your physical and mental abilities.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (大学的)院系;(大学院系的)教职工； A faculty is a group of related departments in some universities, or the people who work in them.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (大学、学院或院系的)全体教员； faculty A faculty is all the teaching staff of a university or college, or of one department.
fad: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一时的风尚;风靡一时之物； fad You use fad to refer to an activity or topic of interest that is very popular for a short time, but which people become bored with very quickly.
faddish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 风靡一时的;流行一时的； faddish If you describe something as faddish , you mean that it has no real value and that it will not remain popular for very long.
faddy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 挑食的;偏食的； faddy If you describe someone as faddy , you mean that they have very strong likes and dislikes, especially about what they eat, which you think are rather silly.
fade: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使褪色;使变暗淡； fade faded When a coloured object fades or when the light fades it, it gradually becomes paler.  /  [VERB 动词] (光线)逐渐暗淡;(声音)逐渐减弱； fade When light fades , it slowly becomes less bright.  /  [VERB 动词] (所注视之物)逐渐暗淡，逐渐模糊直至消失； fade fade away 同 fade When something that you are looking at fades , it slowly becomes less bright or clear until it disappears.  /  [VERB 动词] 变得不为人注意;变得无关紧要； fade fade away 同 fade If someone or something fades , for example, into the background, they become hardly noticeable or very unimportant.
faecal: [ADJ 形容词] 粪便的;排泄物的;与粪便有关的； Faecal means referring or relating to faeces.
faeces: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 粪便;排泄物； Faeces is the solid waste substance that people and animals get rid of from their body by passing it through the anus.
faff about: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 做事杂乱无章;东一榔头西一棒子;瞎忙活； If you say that someone is faffing about or faffing around , you mean that they are doing things in a disorganized way and not achieving very much.
fag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 香烟； A fag is a cigarette.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同性恋者； A fag is a homosexual.
fag end: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 烟蒂； A fag end is the last part of a cigarette, which people throw away when they have smoked the rest.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指枯燥乏味或不重要的)结尾，末尾； If you refer to the fag end of something, you mean the last part of it, especially when you consider this part boring or unimportant.
faggot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男同性恋者； A faggot is a homosexual man.
Fahrenheit: [ADJ 形容词] 华氏温标的;华氏的；  Fahrenheit Fahrenheit is a scale for measuring temperature, in which water freezes at 32 degrees and boils at 212 degrees.
fail: [VERB 动词] 失败;未能够;未做成； fail If you fail to do something that you were trying to do, you are unable to do it or do not succeed in doing it.  /  [VERB 动词] (活动、尝试、计划等)失败，不成功； fail If an activity, attempt, or plan fails , it is not successful.  /  [VERB 动词] 没有做，未做(应做的事)； fail If someone or something fails to do a particular thing that they should have done, they do not do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 出故障;失灵； fail If something fails , it stops working properly, or does not do what it is supposed to do.
failing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 过错;缺陷;不足； failing The failings of someone or something are their faults or unsatisfactory features.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (引出另一种选择)如果不能的话，万一不行的话； failing You say failing that to introduce an alternative, in case what you have just said is not possible.
failsafe: [ADJ 形容词] 有自动保险装置的;具有自动防故障性能的； failsafe Something that is fail-safe is designed or made in such a way that nothing dangerous can happen if a part of it goes wrong.
fail-safe: [ADJ 形容词] 有自动保险装置的;具有自动防故障性能的； Something that is fail-safe is designed or made in such a way that nothing dangerous can happen if a part of it goes wrong.
failure: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 失败;不成功； failure Failure is a lack of success in doing or achieving something, especially in relation to a particular activity.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 失败的事;败绩； failure If something is a failure , it is not a success.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 失败者;一事无成的人； failure If you say that someone is a failure , you mean that they have not succeeded in a particular activity, or that they are unsuccessful at everything they do.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 没做到;不履行； failure Your failure to do a particular thing is the fact that you do not do it, even though you were expected to do it.
faint: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (声音、颜色、标记、感觉或特性)微弱的，暗淡的，虚弱的； faint faintly A faint sound, colour, mark, feeling, or quality has very little strength or intensity.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不尽力的;敷衍的;半心半意的； faint faintly A faint attempt at something is one that is made without proper effort and with little enthusiasm.  /  [VERB 动词] 晕厥;晕倒； faint If you faint , you lose consciousness for a short time, especially because you are hungry, or because of pain, heat, or shock.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 晕眩的;虚弱无力的； faint faintness Someone who is faint feels weak and unsteady as if they are about to lose consciousness.
faintest: [ADJ-SUPERL 形容词最高级形式] (用于否定句，起强调作用)极小的，些微的，一丁点儿的； faintest You can use faintest for emphasis in negative statements.
faint-hearted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 胆怯的;畏怯的； faint-hearted If you describe someone or their behaviour as faint-hearted , you mean that they are not very confident and do not take strong action because they are afraid of failing.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不适于怯懦的人； faint-hearted If you say that something is not for the faint-hearted , you mean that it is an extreme or very unusual example of its kind, and is not suitable for people who like only safe and familiar things.
fainthearted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 胆怯的;畏怯的； If you describe someone or their behaviour as faint-hearted , you mean that they are not very confident and do not take strong action because they are afraid of failing.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不适于怯懦的人； If you say that something is not for the faint-hearted , you mean that it is an extreme or very unusual example of its kind, and is not suitable for people who like only safe and familiar things.
fair: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 合理的;公平的;公正的； fair fairly Something or someone that is fair is reasonable, right, and just.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (数量、程度、尺寸或距离)相当多(或大、长)的； fair A fair amount, degree, size, or distance is quite a large amount, degree, size, or distance.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (猜测、想法)正确的，合理的； fair A fair guess or idea about something is one that is likely to be correct.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (水平、质量)一般的，尚可的，不错的； fair If you describe someone or something as fair , you mean that they are average in standard or quality, neither very good nor very bad.
fair game: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 可攻击的目标;可批评的对象； fair game If you say that someone is fair game , you mean that it is acceptable to criticize or attack them, usually because of the way that they behave.
fairground: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 展销会场地;集市场地； A fairground is an area of land where a fair is held.
fairly: [ADV 副词] 相当;还;尚； fairly Fairly means to quite a large degree.  /  [ADV 副词] (用在形容词和副词前，代替very,表示强调，但比 very 语气弱)有些，有点，还算； fairly You use fairly instead of 'very' to add emphasis to an adjective or adverb without making it sound too forceful.  /  [ADV 副词] (表示强调)在很大程度上，简直； fairly Fairly is used to emphasize that something happens to a very great degree or extent.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 简直;几乎可以说； fairly You use fairly to suggest that a statement is probably or possibly true, and therefore deserves to be accepted or considered.
fair-minded: [ADJ 形容词] 公正的;无偏见的;公允的； fair-minded A fair-minded person always tries to be fair and reasonable, and always listens to other people's opinions.
fairness: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 公平;公道;公正； fairness Fairness is the quality of being reasonable, right, and just.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 说句公道话;公平地说;公正地说； fairness You use fairness in expressions such as in fairness to and in all fairness when you want to add a favourable comment about someone or something that you have just mentioned and to correct a false impression that you might have given.
fair play: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (态度或做事的)公道，公平； fair play If you refer to someone's attitude or behaviour as fair play , you approve of it because it shows respect and sympathy towards everyone, even towards people who are thought to be wrong or to deserve punishment.
fair sex: [N-SING 单数名词] 女性;妇女； If a man talks about the fair sex , he is referring to women in general.
fair trade: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 公平贸易(指以公道的价格从发展中国家制造商手中直接购进商品的做法)； fair trade Fair trade is the practice of buying goods directly from producers in developing countries at a fair price.
fairway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (高尔夫球场上位于开球区与果岭之间的)球道； The fairway on a golf course is the long strip of short grass between each tee and green.
fair-weather: [ADJ 形容词] 只能同甘不能共苦的;顺境中的； fair-weather You use fair-weather to refer to someone who offers help to someone, or who takes part in a particular activity, only when it is easy or pleasant for them to do so.
fairy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 仙人;小精灵； A fairy is an imaginary creature with magical powers.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兔子(指男同性恋者)； If someone describes a man as a fairy , they mean that he is a homosexual and they disapprove of this.
fairy godmother: [N-SING 单数名词] 女恩人;女救星； fairy godmother If you call a woman your fairy godmother , you are saying in a slightly humorous way that she has been very helpful in your life, often at times when you thought you had problems that could not be solved.
fairyland: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 仙国;仙界； Fairyland is the imaginary place where fairies live.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 仙境;美妙之地； fairyland If you describe a place as a fairyland , you mean that it has a delicate beauty.
fairy lights: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (装饰用的)小彩灯； Fairy lights are small, coloured electric lights that are hung up as decorations, for example on a Christmas tree.
fairy story: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 神话;童话； A fairy story is the same as a fairy tale .
fait accompli: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 既成事实;木已成舟之事； fait accompli If something is a fait accompli , it has already been decided or done and cannot be changed.
faith: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 相信;信任； faith If you have faith in someone or something, you feel confident about their ability or goodness.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 宗教； faith A faith is a particular religion, for example Christianity, Buddhism, or Islam.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 宗教信仰； faith Faith is strong religious belief in a particular God.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 背弃;对…不忠;脱离； faith If you break faith with someone you made a promise to or something you believed in, you stop acting in a way that supports them.
faithful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忠实的;忠诚的;忠贞不渝的； faithful 忠诚的人;支持者 faithfully Someone who is faithful to a person, organization, idea, or activity remains firm in their belief in them or support for them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (对丈夫、妻子或恋人)忠诚的，忠贞的； faithful Someone who is faithful to their husband, wife, or lover does not have a sexual relationship with anyone else.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (宗教的)忠实信徒，虔诚信徒； faithful The faithful are the group of people who believe in a particular religion.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (叙述、翻译或抄本)如实的，忠实原文的； faithful faithfully A faithful account, translation, or copy of something represents or reproduces the original accurately.
faithfully: [CONVENTION 惯用语] (用作正式信函或商业信函末尾署名前的套语)您的忠实的； See also: faithful ; When you start a formal or business letter with 'Dear Sir' or 'Dear Madam', you write Yours faithfully before your signature at the end.
faith healer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 信仰疗法治疗者(相信用祈祷或超自然的力量可以给人治病)； A faith healer is someone who believes they can treat and heal sick people using prayer or supernatural powers.
faith healing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 信仰疗法(用祈祷或超自然力量治病)； Faith healing is the treatment of a sick person by someone who believes that they are able to heal people through prayer or a supernatural power.
faithless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 背信弃义的;不忠实的;不诚实的； faithless If you say that someone is faithless , you mean that they are disloyal or dishonest.
fake: [ADJ 形容词] (毛皮、画作)假冒的，伪造的； fake 假货;赝品 A fake fur or a fake painting, for example, is a fur or painting that has been made to look valuable or genuine, usually in order to deceive people.  /  [VERB 动词] 伪造;仿制； fake If someone fakes something, they try to make it look valuable or genuine, although in fact it is not.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 骗子;冒充者； Someone who is a fake is not what they claim to be, for example because they do not have the qualifications that they claim to have.  /  [VERB 动词] 假装;装作； fake If you fake a feeling, emotion, or reaction, you pretend that you are experiencing it when you are not.
falcon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鹰;隼;猎鹰； A falcon is a bird of prey that can be trained to hunt other birds and animals.
falconer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 训隼人;放鹰狩猎人； A falconer is someone who trains and uses falcons for hunting.

fallible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可能出错的;会犯错的； fallible fallibility If you say that someone or something is fallible , you mean that they are not perfect and are likely to make mistakes or to fail in what they are doing.

fallout: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 核辐射； fallout Fallout is the radiation that affects a particular place or area after a nuclear explosion has taken place.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 余波;后果； fallout If you refer to the fallout from something that has happened, you mean the unpleasant consequences that follow it.
fall over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 摔倒;跌倒;倒下； If a person or object that is standing falls over , they accidentally move from their upright position so that they are then lying on the ground or on the surface supporting them.
fallow: [ADJ 形容词] (土地)犁过而未耕种的;(尤指)休耕的； fallow Fallow land has been dug or ploughed but nothing has been planted in it, especially so that its quality or strength has a chance to improve.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (某段时期)无甚成就的，无作为的； fallow A fallow period is a time when very little is being achieved.

false: [ADJ 形容词] 不正确的;虚假的;错误的； false falsely falsity If something is false , it is incorrect, untrue, or mistaken.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 人造的;伪造的;假的； false You use false to describe objects which are artificial but which are intended to look like the real thing or to be used instead of the real thing.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人虚伪的;(举动)装腔作势的； false falsely If you describe a person or their behaviour as false , you are criticizing them for being insincere or for hiding their real feelings.

false move: [PHRASE 短语] 走错一步;稍有差池； false move You use one false move to introduce the very bad or serious consequences which will result if someone makes a mistake, even a very small one.
false positive: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 假阳性;错误的测试结果； false positive A false positive is a mistaken result of a scientific test.
false start: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (由于准备不充分而引起的)起步失误，失败的开端； false start A false start is an attempt to start something, such as a speech, project, or plan, which fails because you were not properly prepared or ready to begin.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (赛跑的)抢跑，起跑犯规； If there is a false start at the beginning of a race, one of the competitors moves before the person who starts the race has given the signal.

falsify: [VERB 动词] 篡改;伪造； falsify falsification If someone falsifies something, they change it or add untrue details to it in order to deceive people.
falter: [VERB 动词] 衰退;停步不前； falter If something falters , it loses power or strength in an uneven way, or no longer makes much progress.  /  [VERB 动词] (因不自信)畏缩不前，开始出错;犹疑； falter If you falter , you lose your confidence and stop doing something or start making mistakes.  /  [VERB 动词] (说话)迟疑，吞吞吐吐，支吾； falter If your voice falters when you are speaking, you hesitate or pause, because you are unsure about what you are saying or are upset.

fame: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 声誉;名望； fame If you achieve fame , you become very well-known.

familial: [ADJ 形容词] 家庭或家族的;家庭(或家族)特有的； familial Familial means relating to families in general, or typical of a family.
familiar: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 熟悉的;熟知的； familiar familiarity If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 熟悉;熟知； familiar familiarity If you are familiar with something, you know or understand it well.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过分亲昵的;过于随便的;放肆的； familiar familiarity familiarly If someone you do not know well behaves in a familiar way towards you, they treat you very informally in a way that you might find offensive.

family: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 家;家庭;家族； family A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.  /  [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 子女;孩子； family When people talk about a family , they sometimes mean children.  /  [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 祖先;祖辈； family When people talk about their family , they sometimes mean their ancestors.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 家族的;家庭的;家里的； family You can use family to describe things that belong to a particular family.
family doctor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 家庭医生； family doctor A family doctor is a doctor who does not specialize in any particular area of medicine, but who has a medical practice in which he or she treats all types of illness.

famous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 著名的;有名的； famous Someone or something that is famous is very well known.
famously: [ADV 副词] (通常指由于突出或极端而)著名地，出名地； famously You use famously to refer to a fact that is well known, usually because it is remarkable or extreme.  /  [ADV 副词] 友好地;融洽地； famously If you get on or get along famously with someone, you are very friendly with each other and enjoy meeting and being together.
fan: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 迷(尤指对某位名人或某项体育运动极为喜爱和感兴趣的人)； fan If you are a fan of someone or something, especially a famous person or a sport, you like them very much and are very interested in them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 扇子； A fan is a flat object that you hold in your hand and wave in order to move the air and make yourself feel cooler.  /  [VERB 动词] 给…扇风； fan If you fan yourself or your face when you are hot, you wave a fan or other flat object in order to make yourself feel cooler.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电扇;风扇； fan A fan is a piece of electrical or mechanical equipment with blades that go round and round.
fanatic: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (政治、宗教等的)狂热分子； fanatic If you describe someone as a fanatic , you disapprove of them because you consider their behaviour or opinions to be very extreme, for example in the way they support particular religious or political ideas.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对某一活动、运动、生活方式)入迷者，痴狂者； fanatic If you say that someone is a fanatic , you mean that they are very enthusiastic about a particular activity, sport, or way of life.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 同 fanatical； Fanatic means the same as fanatical .
fanatical: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行为或看法)狂热的，极端的； fanatical fanatically If you describe someone as fanatical , you disapprove of them because you consider their behaviour or opinions to be very extreme.
fanaticism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 狂热;狂热的行为； fanaticism Fanaticism is fanatical behaviour or the quality of being fanatical.
fanbase: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (流行歌星或乐队的)所有崇拜者;粉丝团； fan base The fan base of someone such as a pop star or a pop group is their fans, considered as a whole.

fancier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 饲养者;培育者;动植物爱好者； fancier See also: fancy ; An animal or plant fancier is a person who breeds animals or plants of a particular type or who is very interested in them.
fanciful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 空想的;异想天开的； fanciful If you describe an idea as fanciful , you disapprove of it because you think it comes from someone's imagination, and is therefore unrealistic or unlikely to be true.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 奇异的;古怪的;花哨的； fanciful If you describe the appearance of something as fanciful , you mean that it is unusual and elaborate rather than plain and simple.
fan club: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (流行歌手、流行乐队等的)…迷俱乐部，粉丝会； A fan club is an organized group of people who all admire the same person or thing, for example a pop singer or pop group.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (某人的)支持者群体，喜爱者群体； fan club If you say that you are a member of someone's fan club , you mean that you like them a lot or approve of them strongly.
fancy: [VERB 动词] 想要;想做； fancy If you fancy something, you want to have it or to do it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指一时的)喜好，渴望； fancy A fancy is a liking or desire for someone or something, especially one that does not last long.  /  [VERB 动词] 爱慕;对(异性)着迷； fancy If you fancy someone, you feel attracted to them, especially in a sexual way.  /  [VERB 动词] 想让自己成为;想让自己做； fancy If you fancy yourself as a particular kind of person or fancy yourself doing a particular thing, you like the idea of being that kind of person or doing that thing.

fantasy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 憧憬;幻想； A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you think about and that you want to happen, especially one that is unlikely to happen.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 奇幻故事;幻想的场景； fantasy You can refer to a story or situation that someone creates from their imagination and that is not based on reality as fantasy .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 幻想;想象； fantasy Fantasy is the activity of imagining things.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 虚拟比赛(游戏)(玩家选择一个虚拟的团队，以团队成员在真实比赛中的实际表现来计分)； fantasy Fantasy football, baseball, or another sport is a game in which players choose an imaginary team and score points based on the actual performances of the members of their team in real games.

farce: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 荒诞剧;滑稽剧;闹剧； A farce is a humorous play in which the characters become involved in complicated and unlikely situations.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (表演或写作的一种风格)荒诞,滑稽； farce Farce is the style of acting and writing that is typical of farces.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 滑稽的场面(或事件);闹剧； farce If you describe a situation or event as a farce , you mean that it is so disorganized or ridiculous that you cannot take it seriously.

fare: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旅费;路费;车费； fare A fare is the money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (饭店或咖啡店的)餐点，饮食，饭菜； fare The fare at a restaurant or caff is the type of food that is served there.  /  [VERB 动词] 进展;进行； fare If you say that someone or something fares well or badly, you are referring to the degree of success they achieve in a particular situation or activity.

fledgling: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 刚长羽毛的小鸟;刚学飞的幼鸟； A fledgling is a young bird that has its feathers and is learning to fly.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 新手的;(组织或系统)新建的，没有经验的； fledgling You use fledgling to describe a person, organization, or system that is new or without experience.
flee: [VERB 动词] 逃离;逃避； flee If you flee from something or someone, or flee a person or thing, you escape from them.
fleece: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 羊毛； A sheep's fleece is the coat of wool that covers it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一只羊一次剪下的羊毛； A fleece is the wool that is cut off one sheep in a single piece.  /  [VERB 动词] 欺诈;诈骗;敲诈； fleece If you fleece someone, you get a lot of money from them by tricking them or charging them too much.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 绒头织物;绒头织物服装； Fleece is a soft warm artificial fabric.
fleecy: [ADJ 形容词] 起绒织物制的； fleecy Fleecy clothes, blankets, or other objects are made of a soft light material.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (看上去)又轻又软的； fleecy Something that is fleecy is light and soft in appearance.
fleet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 船队;舰队； fleet A fleet is a group of ships organized to do something together, for example to fight battles or to catch fish.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指同一机构或统一行动的)车队； fleet A fleet of vehicles is a group of them, especially when they all belong to a particular organization or business, or when they are all going somewhere together.
fleeting: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 短暂的;飞逝的； fleeting fleetingly Fleeting is used to describe something which lasts only for a very short time.
Fleet Street: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 舰队街(指英国报界)； Fleet Street Fleet Street is used to refer to British national newspapers and to the journalists who work for them.
Flemish: [ADJ 形容词] (北欧的)佛兰德地区的，佛兰芒人的，佛兰芒语的； Flemish Flemish means belonging or relating to the region of Flanders in northern Europe, or to its people, language, or culture.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (比利时的)佛兰芒语； Flemish is a language spoken in Belgium.
flesh: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 肉； flesh Flesh is the soft part of a person's or animal's body between the bones and the skin.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 肉体;肌肤； flesh You can use flesh to refer to human skin and the human body, especially when you are considering it in a sexual way.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 果肉;蔬菜的可食部分； flesh The flesh of a fruit or vegetable is the soft inside part of it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 血肉之躯； flesh You use flesh and blood to emphasize that someone has human feelings or weaknesses, often when contrasting them with machines.
flesh-coloured: [ADJ 形容词] 肉色的;肉粉色的； Something that is flesh-coloured is yellowish pink in colour.
flesh wound: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 皮肉之伤;轻伤； A flesh wound is a wound that breaks the skin but does not damage the bones or any of the body's important internal organs.
fleshy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 多肉的;肥胖的； fleshy If you describe someone as fleshy , you mean that they are slightly too fat.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肉厚的;肉质的;多果肉的； fleshy Fleshy parts of the body or fleshy plants are thick and soft.
flew: + + + Flew is the past tense of fly .
flex: [N-VAR 可变名词] (电器用)花线，皮线； A flex is an electric cable containing two or more wires that is connected to an electrical appliance.  /  [VERB 动词] 活动，屈伸(肌肉或身体某一部分)； flex If you flex your muscles or parts of your body, you bend, move, or stretch them for a short time in order to exercise them.  /  to flex your muscles » see: muscle �
flexible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可弯曲的;柔韧的； flexible flexibility A flexible object or material can be bent easily without breaking.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易变通的;适应性强的;灵活的； flexible flexibly flexibility Something or someone that is flexible is able to change easily and adapt to different conditions and circumstances as they occur.
flexitime: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 弹性工作制； Flexitime is a system that allows employees to vary the time that they start or finish work, provided that an agreed total number of hours are spent at work.
flick: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 轻弹;轻击;轻快地移动； flick If something flicks in a particular direction, or if someone flicks it, it moves with a short, sudden movement.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻弹;轻拭； flick If you flick something away, or off something else, you remove it with a quick movement of your hand or finger.  /  [VERB 动词] 抽打;挥动； flick If you flick something such as a whip or a towel, or flick something with it, you hold one end of it and move your hand quickly up and then forward, so that the other end moves.  /  [VERB 动词] (快速地)按(开关等)； flick If you flick a switch, or flick an electrical appliance on or off, you press the switch sharply so that it moves into a different position and works the equipment.
flicker: [VERB 动词] (灯光等)闪烁，摇曳； flicker If a light or flame flickers , it shines unsteadily.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (情感的)闪现，一闪而过； flicker If you experience a flicker of emotion, you feel that emotion only for a very short time, and not very strongly.  /  [VERB 动词] (表情)掠过，闪过； flicker If an expression flickers across your face, it appears very briefly.  /  [VERB 动词] (眼睛)瞟过； flicker If someone's eyes flicker towards something, they look at it quickly.
flick-knife: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 弹簧折刀;弹簧刀； A flick-knife is a knife with a blade in the handle that springs out when a button is pressed.
flight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 飞行;航行； flight A flight is a journey made by flying, usually in an aeroplane.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 航班;客机； flight You can refer to an aeroplane carrying passengers on a particular journey as a particular flight .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 飞行;飞行能力； flight Flight is the action of flying, or the ability to fly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鸟群； flight A flight of birds is a group of them flying together.
flight attendant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 航空乘务员;空姐； On an aeroplane, the flight attendants are the people whose job is to look after the passengers and serve their meals.
flight deck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (航空母舰上的)飞行甲板； On an aircraft carrier, the flight deck is the flat open surface on the deck where aircraft take off and land.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (飞机的)驾驶舱； On a large aeroplane, the flight deck is the area at the front where the pilot works and where all the controls are.
flightless: [ADJ 形容词] (鸟或昆虫)不能飞的，没有飞行能力的； flightless A flightless bird or insect is unable to fly because it does not have the necessary type of wings.
flight lieutenant: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词] (英国)空军上尉； In the British air force, a flight lieutenant is an officer of the rank below squadron leader.
flight of capital: [N-SING 单数名词] 资本外逃； flight of capital When people lose confidence in a particular economy or market and withdraw their investment from it, you can refer to a flight of capital from that economy or market.
flight recorder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 black box； On an aeroplane, the flight recorder is the same as the black box .
flighty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻浮的;见异思迁的;反复无常的； flighty If you say that someone is flighty , you disapprove of them because they are not very serious or reliable and keep changing from one activity, idea, or partner to another.
flimsy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不结实的;劣质的;不牢固的； flimsy A flimsy object is weak because it is made of a weak material, or is badly made.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服或布料)薄的，不御寒的； flimsy Flimsy cloth or clothing is thin and does not give much protection.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 站不住脚的;不足信的； flimsy If you describe something such as evidence or an excuse as flimsy , you mean that it is not very good or convincing.
flinch: [VERB 动词] 退缩;畏缩； flinch If you flinch , you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.  /  [VERB 动词] 躲避;回避;不愿意做； flinch If you flinch from something unpleasant, you are unwilling to do it or think about it, or you avoid doing it.
fling: [VERB 动词] 猛掷;用力抛； fling If you fling something somewhere, you throw it there using a lot of force.  /  [VERB 动词] 突然冲向;突然跳向； If you fling yourself somewhere, you move or jump there suddenly and with a lot of force.  /  [VERB 动词] 急伸，猛动(尤指头或手臂)； If you fling a part of your body in a particular direction, especially your arms or head, you move it there suddenly.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…摔倒； If you fling someone to the ground, you push them very roughly so that they fall over.
flint: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 燧石;火石； flint Flint is a very hard greyish-black stone that was used in former times for making tools.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 打火石； A flint is a small piece of flint which can be struck with a piece of steel to produce sparks.
flintlock: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 明火枪;燧发枪； A flintlock gun is a type of gun that was used in former times.
flinty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 冷酷的;冰冷的;铁石心肠的； flinty If you describe a person or someone's character or expression as flinty , you mean they are harsh and show no emotion.
flip: [VERB 动词] 迅速打开(或关掉)(装置);按(开关)； flip If you flip a device on or off, or if you flip a switch, you turn it on or off by pressing the switch quickly.  /  [VERB 动词] 快速翻阅;浏览； flip If you flip through the pages of a book, for example, you quickly turn over the pages in order to find a particular one or to get an idea of the contents.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使移动;使转动;使翻动； flip If something flips over, or if you flip it over or into a different position, it moves or is moved into a different position.  /  [VERB 动词] (用拇指)弹，抛，掷； flip If you flip something, especially a coin, you use your thumb to make it turn over and over, as it goes through the air.
flip-flop: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 人字拖鞋； Flip-flops are open shoes which are held on your feet by a strap that goes between your toes.  /  [VERB 动词] (尤指政客)改变决定，转持相反观点； flip-flop If you say that someone, especially a politician, flip-flops on a decision, you are critical of them because they change their decision, so that they do or think the opposite.
flippant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻率的;轻浮的;不严肃的； flippant flippancy flippantly If you describe a person or what they say as flippant , you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.
flipper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脚蹼;橡皮脚掌;鸭脚板； Flippers are flat pieces of rubber that you can wear on your feet to help you swim more quickly, especially underwater.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (海豹等的)鳍状肢，鳍足； The flippers of an animal that lives in water, for example a seal or a penguin, are the two or four flat limbs which it uses for swimming.
flipping: [ADV 副词] (尤用于恼火时加强语气)可恶的，该死的； flipping Some people use flipping to emphasize what they are saying, especially when they are annoyed.
flip side: [N-SING 单数名词] (没有主打歌曲的)唱片反面； flip side The flip side of a record is the side that does not have the main song on it.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (情况的)不明显的一面，反面，负面； flip side The flip side of a situation consists of the less obvious or less pleasant aspects of it.
flirt: [V-RECIP 相互动词] (和…)调情;(和…)打情骂俏； flirt flirtation If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 调情老手； Someone who is a flirt likes to flirt a lot.  /  [VERB 动词] 不认真地考虑;有…的念头(或想法)； flirt flirtation If you flirt with the idea of something, you consider it but do not do anything about it.
flirtatious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 调情的;卖弄风情的； flirtatious Someone who is flirtatious behaves towards someone else as if they are sexually attracted to them, usually not in a very serious way.
flirty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 调情的;轻浮的； flirty If you describe someone as flirty , you mean that they behave towards people in a way which suggests they are sexually attracted to them, usually in a playful or not very serious way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服)性感的，有女人味的； flirty Flirty clothes are feminine and sexy.
flit: [VERB 动词] 辗转;穿梭； flit If you flit around or flit between one place and another, you go to lots of places without staying for very long in any of them.  /  [VERB 动词] (在不同情况间)转变，转换； flit If someone flits from one thing or situation to another, they move or turn their attention from one to the other very quickly.  /  [VERB 动词] 飞过;掠过;闪过； flit If something such as a bird or a bat flits about, it flies quickly from one place to another.  /  [VERB 动词] (表情或念头)闪现，闪过； flit If an expression flits across your face or an idea flits through your mind, it is there for a short time and then goes again.
float: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使漂浮;使浮动； float If something or someone is floating in a liquid, they are in the liquid, on or just below the surface, and are being supported by it.  /  [VERB 动词] 漂;浮； float Something that floats lies on or just below the surface of a liquid when it is put in it and does not sink.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 浮体;浮板;救生圈； A float is a light object that is used to help someone or something float.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (钓鱼用的)鱼漂浮子； A float is a small object attached to a fishing line which floats on the water and moves when a fish has been caught.
floating voter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 游离选民(并无坚决拥护的党派的投票者)； A floating voter is a person who is not a firm supporter of any political party, and whose vote in an election is difficult to predict.
flock: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] (鸟、羊)群； flock A flock of birds, sheep, or goats is a group of them.  /  [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 成群结队;一大群； flock You can refer to a group of people or things as a flock of them to emphasize that there are a lot of them.  /  [VERB 动词] 蜂拥;群集； flock If people flock to a particular place or event, a very large number of them go there, usually because it is pleasant or interesting.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (到牧师所在教堂做礼拜或属于其辖区的)全体教徒，教众群体； A clergyman's flock is the group of Christians who come to his church or live in the area that he has responsibility for.
flog: [VERB 动词] 出售;卖掉； flog If someone tries to flog something, they try to sell it.  /  [VERB 动词] 鞭笞;棒打； flog flogging If someone is flogged , they are hit very hard with a whip or stick as a punishment.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 做徒劳无益的事;白忙活； If you say that someone is flogging a dead horse , you mean that they are trying to achieve something impossible.
flood: [N-VAR 可变名词] 洪水;水灾； flood If there is a flood , a large amount of water covers an area which is usually dry, for example when a river flows over its banks or a pipe bursts.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 淹没;使充满水； flood flooded If something such as a river or a burst pipe floods an area that is usually dry or if the area floods , it becomes covered with water.  /  [VERB 动词] (尤指暴雨后河水)泛滥； flood If a river floods , it overflows, especially after very heavy rain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大量;大批； flood If you say that a flood of people or things arrive somewhere, you are emphasizing that a very large number of them arrive there.
floodgates: [PHRASE 短语] 打开闸门;使…一发不可收拾； floodgates If events open the floodgates to something, they make it possible for that thing to happen much more often or much more seriously than before.
flooding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 洪水泛滥;水灾； flooding If flooding occurs, an area of land that is usually dry is covered with water after heavy rain or after a river or lake flows over its banks.
floodlight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 泛光灯;强光灯； Floodlights are very powerful lamps that are used outside to light public buildings, sports grounds, and other places at night.  /  [VERB 动词] 以泛光灯照亮； floodlight If a building or place is floodlit , it is lit by floodlights.
flood plain: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 洪泛区;涝原;漫滩； A flood plain is a flat area on the edge of a river, where the ground consists of soil, sand, and rock left by the river when it floods.
floor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 地面;地板； floor The floor of a room is the part of it that you walk on.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 层;楼层； floor A floor of a building is all the rooms that are on a particular level.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (海洋、山谷的)底部； floor The ocean floor is the ground at the bottom of an ocean.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 议事厅;(尤指)议员席； floor The place where official debates and discussions are held, especially between members of parliament, is referred to as the floor .
floored: [ADJ 形容词] 以…为地面材料的;铺有…地板的； floored (亦可用于构词) A room or part of a room that is floored with a particular material has a floor made of that material.
flooring: [N-MASS 物质名词] 室内地面材料； flooring Flooring is a material that is used to make the floor of a room.
floor lamp: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 落地灯； A floor lamp is a tall electric light which stands on the floor in a living room.
floor show: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (夜总会)系列节目表演； A floor show is a series of performances by dancers, singers, or comedians at a night club.
floozy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 荡妇;破鞋； If you refer to a woman as a floozy , you disapprove of her sexual behaviour and the fact that she wears vulgar clothes.
flop: [VERB 动词] 猛然坐下;重重地坐下； flop If you flop into a chair, for example, you sit down suddenly and heavily because you are so tired.  /  [VERB 动词] 凌乱地垂下;猛落下； flop If something flops onto something else, it falls there heavily or untidily.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 彻底失败;惨败； flop If something is a flop , it is completely unsuccessful.  /  [VERB 动词] 彻底失败;惨败； flop If something flops , it is completely unsuccessful.
flophouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 廉价旅馆;低级旅社； A flophouse is a kind of cheap hotel in a city for people who have no home and very little money.
floppy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 松散的;松垂的;松软的； floppy Something that is floppy is loose rather than stiff, and tends to hang downwards.
floppy disk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 软盘； A floppy disk is a small magnetic disk that is used for storing computer data and programs.
flora: [N-UNCOUNT-COLL 不可数集合名词] (尤指某一地区的)植物群落； flora You can refer to plants as flora , especially the plants growing in a particular area.
floral: [ADJ 形容词] 有花形图案的;绘有花的； floral A floral fabric or design has flowers on it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 由花组成的;有鲜花装饰的； floral You can use floral to describe something that contains flowers or is made of flowers.
floret: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (复花花序的)小花； On a flowering plant, a floret is a small flower that is part of a larger flower.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (花椰菜等蔬菜的)花部； On vegetables such as broccoli and cauliflower, a floret is one of the small, flower-shaped pieces which make up the part of the vegetable that you eat.
florid: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过分花哨的;过分修饰的； florid If you describe something as florid , you disapprove of the fact that it is complicated and extravagant rather than plain and simple.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (脸色)发红的，红润的； florid Someone who is florid always has a red face.
florin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 弗罗林(英国旧时所用的价值 2 先令的硬币)； A florin was a British coin that was worth two shillings.
florist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 花店店主;花商； A florist is a shopkeeper who arranges and sells flowers and sells house plants.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鲜花店;花坊； A florist or a florist's is a shop where flowers and house plants are sold.
floss: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 丝棉;丝线； floss See also: candyfloss ; dental floss ; You can use floss to refer to fine soft threads of some kind.  /  [VERB 动词] 用牙线剔牙； floss When you floss , you use a special kind of strong string to clean between your teeth and gums.

fuck: [EXCLAM 感叹语] (表示愤怒或恼火)他妈的，该死的； Fuck is used to express anger or annoyance.  /  [EXCLAM 感叹语] (表示愤怒或不关心)见他妈的鬼/滚你妈的蛋/真他妈见鬼； If someone uses an expression such as ' fuck it ', ' fuck you ', or ' fuck that ', they are expressing anger or the fact that they do not care about someone or something.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 和…性交;操； To fuck someone means to have sex with them.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 一点儿也不； Fuck all is used to mean 'nothing at all'.
fucker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 混蛋;笨蛋;蠢货； If someone calls a person a fucker , they are insulting them.
fucking: [ADJ 形容词] (尤用于愤怒或恼火时加强语气)他妈的，该死的； Fucking is used by some people to emphasize a word or phrase, especially when they are feeling angry or annoyed.
fuddled: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 稀里糊涂的;迷迷糊糊的;昏醉的； Someone who is fuddled cannot think clearly, for example because they are very tired or slightly drunk.
fuddy-duddy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 老古板;老古董； fuddy-duddy If you describe someone as a fuddy-duddy , you are criticizing or making fun of them because they are old-fashioned in their appearance or attitudes.
fudge: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 乳脂软糖； Fudge is a soft brown sweet that is made from butter, cream, and sugar.  /  [VERB 动词] 回避;敷衍;搪塞;对…态度暧昧； fudge If you fudge something, you avoid making a clear and definite decision, distinction, or statement about it.
fuel: [N-MASS 物质名词] 燃料； fuel Fuel is a substance such as coal, oil, or petrol that is burned to provide heat or power.  /  [VERB 动词] 刺激;使变得更糟;使加剧； fuel To fuel a situation means to make it become worse or more intense.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (对…)火上浇油； fuel If something adds fuel to a conflict or debate, or adds fuel to the fire , it makes the conflict or debate more intense.
fuel injection: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 燃料喷射;喷油； Fuel injection is a system in the engines of some vehicles which forces fuel directly into the part of the engine where it is burned.
fuelled: [ADJ 形容词] (以…)作为燃料的； fuelled A machine or vehicle that is fuelled by a particular substance works by burning that substance.
fuel rod: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (核反应堆的)燃料棒； Fuel rods are metal tubes containing nuclear fuel.
fug: [N-SING 单数名词] 烟雾腾腾的空气;污浊空气;闷滞空气； fug People refer to the atmosphere somewhere as a fug when it is smoky and smelly and there is no fresh air.
fugitive: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 逃亡者;亡命者;(通常指)逃犯； fugitive A fugitive is someone who is running away or hiding, usually in order to avoid being caught by the police.
fugue: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 赋格曲； A fugue is a piece of music that begins with a simple tune which is then repeated by other voices or instrumental parts with small variations.
-ful: [SUFFIX 后缀] (用于构成名词)表示“充满…所需的量”； You use -ful to form nouns that refer to the quantity of a substance that an object contains or can contain.
fulcrum: [N-SING 单数名词] (活动或情形的)支点，支柱； fulcrum If you say that someone or something is the fulcrum of an activity or situation, you mean that they have a very important effect on what happens.
fulfil: [VERB 动词] 履行;实现;使应验； fulfil If you fulfil something such as a promise, dream, or hope, you do what you said or hoped you would do.  /  [VERB 动词] 实行;执行;完成； fulfil To fulfil a task, role, or requirement means to do or be what is required, necessary, or expected.  /  [VERB 动词] 满足;使满意;使有成就感； fulfil fulfilled fulfilling If something fulfils you, or if you fulfil yourself , you feel happy and satisfied with what you are doing or with what you have achieved.
fulfilment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 满足感;成就感； fulfilment Fulfilment is a feeling of satisfaction that you get from doing or achieving something, especially something useful.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 履行;实现;完成;满足； fulfilment The fulfilment of a promise, threat, request, hope, or duty is the event or act of it happening or being made to happen.
full: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 满的;装满的； full If something is full , it contains as much of a substance or as many objects as it can.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有大量…的;满是…的； full If a place or thing is full of things or people, it contains a large number of them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 充满(某一情感或特质)的； full If someone or something is full of a particular feeling or quality, they have a lot of it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 满员的;没有空位(或空间)的； full You say that a place or vehicle is full when there is no space left in it for any more people or things.
full-back: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (橄榄球或足球中的)防守后卫； In rugby or football, a full-back is a defending player whose position is towards the goal which their team is defending.
fullback: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (橄榄球或足球中的)防守后卫； In rugby or football, a full-back is a defending player whose position is towards the goal which their team is defending.
full-blooded: [ADJ 形容词] 全力以赴的;热情洋溢的； full-blooded Full-blooded behaviour and actions are carried out with great commitment and enthusiasm.

full board: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 全食宿(指住宿及全部伙食均由旅馆提供)； If the price at a hotel includes full board , it includes all your meals.
full dress: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 礼服;盛装； full dress Someone who is in full dress is wearing all the clothes needed for a ceremony or formal occasion.
full-flavoured: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 味浓的;味醇的； full-flavoured Full-flavoured food or wine has a pleasant fairly strong taste.
full-fledged: [ADJ 形容词] 同 fully fledged； Full-fledged means the same as fully fledged .
full-frontal: [ADJ 形容词] 正面全裸的;裸露前身的； full-frontal If there is full-frontal nudity in a photograph or film, you can see the whole of the front part of someone's naked body, including the genitals.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (批评等)正面的，直接的； full-frontal If you use full-frontal to describe someone's criticism or way of dealing with something, you are emphasizing that it is very strong and direct.
full-grown: [ADJ 形容词] (动物或植物)发育完全的，完全长成的，成熟的； full-grown An animal or plant that is full-grown has reached its full adult size and stopped growing.
full house: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (剧院的)满座，爆满； full house If a theatre has a full house for a particular performance, it has as large an audience as it can hold.
full-length: [ADJ 形容词] (书籍、唱片或电影)标准长度的，未经删节的； full-length A full-length book, record, or film is the normal length, rather than being shorter than normal.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (上衣或裙子)长及小腿(或脚踝)的;(衣袖)长及手腕的； A full-length coat or skirt is long enough to reach the lower part of a person's leg, almost to the ankles.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (窗帘等)长及地面的，落地的； Full-length curtains or other furnishings reach to the floor.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (镜子或画像)全身的； A full-length mirror or painting shows the whole of a person.
full marks: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (考试等中的)满分； full marks If you get full marks in a test or exam, you get everything right and gain the maximum number of marks.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 赞扬;赞誉； If you say that someone gets full marks for something, you are praising them for being very clever or for showing some other good quality.
full monty: [N-SING 单数名词] 一应俱全;一样不缺； full monty You use the full monty to describe something that impresses you because it includes everything that you could possibly expect it to include.
fullness: » see: full  /  [PHRASE 短语] 在适当的时候;待时机成熟时;最终； fullness If you say that something will happen in the fullness of time , you mean that it will eventually happen after a long time or after a long series of events.
full-on: [ADJ 形容词] 具有一应特征的;完全的;彻底的;绝对的； full-on Full-on is used to describe things or activities that have all the characteristics of their type, or are done in the strongest or most extreme way possible.
full-page: [ADJ 形容词] (报纸、杂志上)整版的，整页的； A full-page advertisement, picture, or article in a newspaper or magazine uses a whole page.
full-scale: [ADJ 形容词] 完全的;彻底的;最大限度的； full-scale Full-scale means as complete, intense, or great in extent as possible.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 与实物一样大小的;原尺寸的； full-scale A full-scale drawing or model is the same size as the thing that it represents.
full-size: [ADJ 形容词] 与原物一样大小的； full-size A full-size or full-sized model or picture is the same size as the thing or person that it represents.
full stop: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 句号； A full stop is the punctuation mark which you use at the end of a sentence when it is not a question or exclamation.
full-throated: [ADJ 形容词] 高声的;大声的； full-throated A full-throated sound coming from someone's mouth, such as a shout or a laugh, is very loud.
full-time: [ADJ 形容词] 全职的;专职的;全日制的； full-time Full-time work or study involves working or studying for the whole of each normal working week rather than for part of it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 费时费力的活； full-time If you describe a regular activity or task as a full-time job , you mean that it takes up so much of your time it is like doing a paid job.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (足球等的)比赛结束，终场； full-time In games such as football, full-time is the end of a match.
full-timer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 全职工作者;专职员工； full-timer A full-timer is someone who works full-time.
full up: [ADJ 形容词] 挤满的;占满的； full up Something that is full up has no space left for any more people or things.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 吃饱的;喝足的； If you are full up you have eaten or drunk so much that you do not want to eat or drink anything else.
fully: [ADV 副词] 完全地;最大程度地； fully Fully means to the greatest degree or extent possible.  /  [ADV 副词] 完全(结束)地； fully You use fully to say that a process is completely finished.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 全面地;充分地;彻底地； fully If you describe, answer, or deal with something fully , you leave out nothing that should be mentioned or dealt with.  /  [ADV 副词] (用于强调数量)整整，足足，至少； Fully is used to emphasize how great an amount is.
fulminate: [VERB 动词] 强烈谴责;怒斥； fulminate fulmination If you fulminate against someone or something, you criticize them angrily.
fulsome: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (赞扬、道歉、感激等)虚伪的，夸张的，过度的； fulsome fulsomely If you describe expressions of praise, apology, or gratitude as fulsome , you disapprove of them because they are exaggerated and elaborate, so that they sound insincere.
fumble: [VERB 动词] 乱摸;摸索;笨拙地处理； fumble If you fumble for something or fumble with something, you try and reach for it or hold it in a clumsy way.  /  [VERB 动词] 笨嘴拙舌地说话;结结巴巴地说话； fumble When you are trying to say something, if you fumble for the right words, you speak in a clumsy and unclear way.
fume: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (难闻且常为有害的)烟,气体； fume Fumes are the unpleasant and often unhealthy smoke and gases that are produced by fires or by things such as chemicals, fuel, or cooking.  /  [VERB 动词] 发怒;生气； fume If you fume over something, you express annoyance and anger about it.
fumigate: [VERB 动词] (为除菌、杀虫等用特殊化学药剂)烟熏，熏蒸； fumigate fumigation If you fumigate something, you get rid of germs or insects from it using special chemicals.
fun: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 趣事;乐趣； fun You refer to an activity or situation as fun if you think it is pleasant and enjoyable and it causes you to feel happy.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 有趣的人;好玩的人； fun If you say that someone is fun , you mean that you enjoy being with them because they say and do interesting or amusing things.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人愉快的;让人开心的;有趣的； fun If you describe something as a fun thing, you mean that you think it is enjoyable.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 荒唐可笑的人;引人嘲笑的人； Someone who is a figure of fun is considered ridiculous, so that people laugh at them or make jokes about them.
function: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 功能;作用;职责； function The function of something or someone is the useful thing that they do or are intended to do.  /  [VERB 动词] 工作;运转;运行； function If a machine or system is functioning , it is working or operating.  /  [VERB 动词] 发挥功能;起作用;行使职责； function If someone or something functions as a particular thing, they do the work or fulfil the purpose of that thing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (计算机的)功能(指执行的一系列操作)； A function is a series of operations that a computer performs, for example when a single key or a combination of keys is pressed.
functional: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 实用的;为实用而设计的； functional Functional things are useful rather than decorative.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 工作(或运转)方式的;功能性的； functional functionally Functional means relating to the way in which something works or operates, or relating to how useful it is.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 在工作的;在起作用的;运转正常的； functional Functional equipment works or operates in the way that it is supposed to.
functionalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指建筑和家具的)实用主义，功能主义； functionalist Functionalism is the idea that the most important aspect of something, especially the design of a building or piece of furniture, is how it is going to be used or its usefulness.
functionality: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (计算机等的)功能性； functionality The functionality of a computer or other machine is how useful it is or how many functions it can perform.
functionary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指为政府或政党服务的)行政人员，官员； A functionary is a person whose job is to do administrative work, especially for a government or a political party.
function key: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 功能键； function key Function keys are the keys along the top of a computer keyboard, usually numbered from F1 to F12.
fund: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (尤指为某一特定目的给予的)资金，钱款； fund See also: fund-raising ; Funds are amounts of money that are available to be spent, especially money that is given to an organization or person for a particular purpose.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某一特定的)基金，专款； fund See also: trust fund ; A fund is an amount of money that is collected or saved for a particular purpose.  /  [VERB 动词] 资助;为…提供资金； fund -funded When a person or organization funds something, they provide money for it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大量;充足； fund If you have a fund of something, you have a lot of it.
fundamental: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 基本的;根本的;主要的;基础的； fundamental You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 根本性的;固有的;根深蒂固的； fundamental You use fundamental to describe something which exists at a deep and basic level, and is therefore likely to continue.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 必需的;不可或缺的； fundamental If one thing is fundamental to another, it is absolutely necessary to it, and the second thing cannot exist, succeed, or be imagined without it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 最根本的;最重要的； fundamental You can use fundamental to show that you are referring to what you consider to be the most important aspect of a situation, and that you are not concerned with less important details.
fundamentalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 原教旨主义;基要主义； fundamentalism fundamentalist Fundamentalism is the belief in the original form of a religion or theory, without accepting any later ideas.
fundamentally: [ADV-GRADED 副词] (表示强调)基本地，从根本上说； fundamentally You use fundamentally for emphasis when you are stating an opinion, or when you are making an important or general statement about something.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 根本性地； fundamentally You use fundamentally to indicate that something affects or relates to the deep, basic nature of something.
fundamentals: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 基础;基本原则(或原理)； fundamentals The fundamentals of something are its simplest, most important elements, ideas, or principles, in contrast to more complicated or detailed ones.
funding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (政府或机构提供的)资金，款项，拨款； funding Funding is money which a government or organization provides for a particular purpose.
fundraiser: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 筹款活动;募捐会； fundraiser A fundraiser is an event which is intended to raise money for a particular purpose, for example, for a charity.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 筹集资金者;募捐者； fundraiser A fundraiser is someone who works to raise money for a particular purpose, for example, for a charity.
fundraising: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 筹款;募捐； Fund-raising is the activity of collecting money to support a charity or political campaign or organization.
fund-raising: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 筹款;募捐； fund-raising Fund-raising is the activity of collecting money to support a charity or political campaign or organization.
funeral: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 葬礼;丧礼； funeral A funeral is the ceremony that is held when the body of someone who has died is buried or cremated.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 这是你自作自受;那你可要倒霉了； funeral If someone says to you ' It's your funeral ', they think your decision or your actions will have bad consequences for you, but they are unwilling to interfere.
funeral director: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 丧葬承办人;殡仪员； A funeral director is a person whose job is to arrange funerals.
funeral home: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 殡仪馆； A funeral home is a place where a funeral director works and where dead people are prepared for burial or cremation.
funeral parlour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 殡仪馆； A funeral parlour is a place where a funeral director works and where dead people are prepared for burial or cremation.
funerary: [ADJ 形容词] 葬礼用的;丧葬的； funerary Funerary means relating to funerals, burials, or cremations.
funereal: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 适于葬礼的;似丧葬的;悲哀而庄严的； funereal A funereal tone, atmosphere, or colour is very sad and serious and would be suitable for a funeral.
funfair: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (流动)游艺节； funfair A funfair is an event held in a park or field at which people pay to ride on various machines for amusement or try to win prizes in games.
fungal: [ADJ 形容词] 真菌引起的;真菌的;真菌构成的； fungal Fungal means caused by, consisting of, or relating to fungus.
fungi: (fungus 的复数)； Fungi is the plural of fungus .
fungicide: [N-MASS 物质名词] 杀真菌剂； A fungicide is a chemical that can be used to kill fungus or to prevent it from growing.
fungus: [N-MASS 物质名词] 真菌； A fungus is a plant that has no flowers, leaves, or green colouring, such as a mushroom or a toadstool.
funicular: [N-SING 单数名词] (用缆索牵引车辆的)缆索铁路,登山铁道； A funicular or a funicular railway is a type of railway which goes up a very steep hill or mountain.
funk: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (由爵士乐和布鲁斯发展而来的)乡土爵士乐，放克音乐； funk Funk is a style of dance music based on jazz and blues, with a strong, repeated bass part.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤因处于自己无法控制的情形中而出现的)恐慌，惊恐； funk If someone is in a funk , they are frightened, especially because they are in a situation they cannot control.  /  [VERB 动词] (因害怕而)逃避； funk If you funk something, you avoid doing it because you are afraid.
funky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (音乐)乡土爵士乐风格的，放克风格的； funky Funky jazz, blues, or pop music has a very strong, repeated bass part.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不从习俗(或传统)的;不寻常的;与众不同的； funky If you describe something or someone as funky , you like them because they are unconventional or unusual.
funnel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 漏斗； A funnel is an object with a wide, circular top and a narrow short tube at the bottom.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (蒸汽轮船或机车的)烟囱； funnel A funnel is a metal chimney on a ship or railway engine powered by steam.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 漏斗状物； funnel You can describe as a funnel something that is narrow, or narrow at one end, through which a substance flows and is directed.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使通过狭窄空间； funnel If something funnels somewhere or is funnelled there, it is directed through a narrow space.
funnily: [PHRASE 短语] 说来也巧;奇怪的是； You use funnily enough to indicate that, although something is surprising, it is true or really happened.

furious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 狂怒的;暴怒的； furious furiously Someone who is furious is extremely angry.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 大力的;猛烈的;激烈的； furious furiously Furious is also used to describe something that is done with great energy, effort, speed, or violence.
furl: [VERB 动词] 收拢(伞等);卷起，收卷(帆、旗等)； furl When you furl something made of fabric such as an umbrella, sail, or flag, you roll or fold it up because it is not going to be used.

furnishings: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 家具陈设;室内陈设； The furnishings of a room or house are the furniture, curtains, carpets, and decorations such as pictures.
furniture: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 家具； furniture Furniture consists of large objects such as tables, chairs, or beds that are used in a room for sitting or lying on or for putting things on or in.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 被认作当然的人(或事物);习以为常的人(或事物)； If you describe someone or something as part of the furniture , you are suggesting that they have been somewhere such as their place of work for such a long time that it is hard to imagine that place without them.

furrier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 毛皮加工者;皮货商； A furrier is a person who makes or sells clothes made from fur.

furry: [ADJ 形容词] (动物)毛皮覆盖的，毛茸茸的； furry A furry animal is covered with thick, soft hair.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 毛皮般柔软的； furry If you describe something as furry , you mean that it has a soft rough texture like fur.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (通常指因生病而)长舌苔的； If you have a furry tongue, your tongue is covered with a layer of a soft greyish-white substance, usually because you are unwell.

furtherance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 促进;推进;增进； furtherance The furtherance of something is the activity of helping it to be successful or be achieved.

furthermore: [ADV 副词] 而且;此外;再者； Furthermore is used to introduce a piece of information or opinion that adds to or supports the previous one.
furthermost: [ADJ 形容词] 最远的； furthermost The furthermost one of a number of similar things is the one that is the greatest distance away from a place.
furthest: Furthest is a superlative form of far .  /  [ADV-SUPERL 副词最高级形式] 在最大程度上;在最大范围内;最大限度地； furthest Furthest means to a greater extent or degree than ever before or than anything or anyone else.  /  [ADV-SUPERL 副词最高级形式] (距离上)最远地，最往前； furthest Furthest means at a greater distance from a particular point than anyone or anything else, or for a greater distance than anyone or anything else.
furtive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 偷偷摸摸的;鬼鬼祟祟的;秘密的； furtive furtively If you describe someone's behaviour as furtive , you disapprove of them behaving as if they want to keep something secret or hidden.
fury: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 狂怒;暴怒； fury Fury is violent or very strong anger.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 异常愤怒;怒不可遏； fury If you are in a fury , you are very angry.
fuse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保险丝;熔丝； fuse A fuse is a safety device in an electric plug or circuit.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(电器等)因保险丝熔断而停止工作； fuse When an electric device fuses or when you fuse it, it stops working because of a fault.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 导火线;引信;信管； fuse A fuse is a device on a bomb or firework which delays the explosion so that people can move a safe distance away.  /  [V-RECIP-ERG ] 使熔接;使熔合;使结合； fuse When things fuse or are fused , they join together physically or chemically, usually to become one thing.

fusillade: [N-SING 单数名词] (枪炮等的)齐射，连发； fusillade A fusillade of shots or objects is a large number of them fired or thrown at the same time.
fusion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (不同特质、思想等的)合成体，融合体； fusion A fusion of different qualities, ideas, or things is something new that is created by joining them together.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 合为一体;融合； fusion The fusion of two or more things involves joining them together to form one thing.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (物理学上的)核聚变； fusion In physics, fusion is the process in which atomic particles combine and produce a large amount of nuclear energy.
fuss: [N-SING 单数名词] 紧张不安;大惊小怪;忙乱； fuss Fuss is anxious or excited behaviour which serves no useful purpose.  /  [VERB 动词] 紧张不安;大惊小怪;瞎忙活； fuss If you fuss , you worry or behave in a nervous, anxious way about unimportant matters or rush around doing unnecessary things.  /  [VERB 动词] (对…)关爱备至，过分体贴； fuss If you fuss over someone, you pay them a lot of attention and do things to make them happy or comfortable.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 引起骚动;大吵大闹;大发牢骚； fuss If you make a fuss or kick up a fuss about something, you become angry or excited about it and complain.
fussed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (不) 关心的;不在意的； fussed If you say you are not fussed about something, you mean you do not mind about it or do not mind what happens.
fussy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过分注重细节的;爱挑剔的;难以取悦的； fussy fussily fussiness Someone who is fussy is very concerned with unimportant details and is difficult to please.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过分装饰的;过于繁琐的； fussy fussily If you describe things such as clothes and furniture as fussy , you are criticizing them because they are too elaborate or detailed.
fusty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (想法或人)过时的，守旧的； fusty If you describe something or someone as fusty , you disapprove of them because they are old-fashioned in attitudes or ideas.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 发霉味的;朽霉的； fusty A fusty place or thing has a smell that is not fresh or pleasant.
futile: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无益的;无用的;徒劳的； futile If you say that something is futile , you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.
futility: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无益;无用;徒劳;白费； futility Futility is a total lack of purpose or usefulness.
futon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (可折叠成椅的)日本床垫;沙发床； A futon is a piece of furniture which consists of a thin mattress on a low wooden frame which can be used as a bed or folded up to make a chair.
future: [N-SING 单数名词] 未来;将来;将来发生的事； future The future is the period of time that will come after the present, or the things that will happen then.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 未来的;将来的； future Future things will happen or exist after the present time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 前途;前景； future Someone's future , or the future of something, is what will happen to them or what they will do after the present time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 成功的可能;未来的希望； future If you say that someone or something has a future , you mean that they are likely to be successful or to survive.
futurism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 未来主义(20世纪早期的现代艺术和文学运动)； Futurism was a modern artistic and literary movement in the early twentieth century.
futurist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 未来主义者;未来派艺术家;未来派作家； Futurists were artists and writers who were followers of futurism.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 预测未来的人;未来学家； A futurist is someone who makes predictions about what is going to happen, on the basis of facts about what is happening now.
futuristic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 未来派的;极其前卫现代的； futuristic Something that is futuristic looks or seems very modern and unusual, like something from the future.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (电影或小说)幻想未来的； futuristic A futuristic film or book tells a story that is set in the future, when things are different.

fuzz: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 短而卷曲的毛发;细毛;绒毛； fuzz Fuzz is a mass of short, curly hairs.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 警察;警方； The fuzz are the police.
fuzzy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (毛发)柔软卷曲的； fuzzy Fuzzy hair sticks up in a soft, curly mass.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 覆有细绒毛的;绒毛状的;毛茸茸的； fuzzy If something is fuzzy , it has a covering that feels soft and like fur.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (图片、声音等)不清楚的，模糊的； fuzzy A fuzzy picture, image, or sound is unclear and hard to see or hear.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (人或头脑)稀里糊涂的，迷迷糊糊的； fuzzy If you or your thoughts are fuzzy , you are confused and cannot think clearly.

gag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 使人不能说话的封口布，塞口物； gag A gag is something such as a piece of cloth that is tied around or put inside someone's mouth in order to stop them from speaking.  /  [VERB 动词] 用布封住或堵住…的嘴； gag If someone gags you, they tie a piece of cloth around your mouth in order to stop you from speaking or shouting.  /  [VERB 动词] 压制…的言论自由；迫使…缄默； gag If a person is gagged by someone in authority, they are prevented from expressing their opinion or from publishing certain information.  /  [VERB 动词] 噎住；噎得作呕； gag If you gag , you cannot swallow and nearly vomit.

gamer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电脑游戏玩家； A gamer is someone who plays computer games.
