gleam: [VERB 动词] 闪光；闪烁； gleam If an object or a surface gleams , it reflects light because it is shiny and clean.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 反光；闪光； gleam You can refer to the light reflected from something as a gleam .  /  [VERB 动词] 日、月等发微光；闪烁； gleam If a light or the sun or moon gleams , it shines faintly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 微光；一丝光线； gleam A gleam of light is a pale, clear light.
glean: [VERB 动词] 耐心学习，仔细收集信息、知识等； glean If you glean something such as information or knowledge, you learn or collect it slowly and patiently, and perhaps indirectly.
glee: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 欢喜；兴奋；常指幸灾乐祸； glee Glee is a feeling of happiness and excitement, often caused by someone else's misfortune.
gleeful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 欣喜的；激动的；常指幸灾乐祸的； gleeful gleefully Someone who is gleeful is happy and excited, often because of someone else's bad luck.
glen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指苏格兰或爱尔兰的峡谷； A glen is a deep, narrow valley, especially in the mountains of Scotland or Ireland.
glib: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻率的；随便说出口的； glib glibly If you describe what someone says as glib , you disapprove of it because it implies that something is simple or easy, or that there are no problems involved, when this is not the case.
glide: [VERB 动词] 滑动；滑行；悄悄地走； glide If you glide somewhere, you move silently and in a smooth and effortless way.  /  [VERB 动词] 滑翔； glide When birds or aeroplanes glide , they float on air currents.
glider: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑翔机； A glider is an aircraft without an engine, which flies by floating on air currents.
gliding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 滑翔运动； Gliding is the sport or activity of flying in a glider.
glimmer: [VERB 动词] 发微光；隐约闪烁； glimmer If something glimmers , it produces or reflects a faint, gentle, often unsteady light.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 常指闪烁的微光； glimmer A glimmer is a faint, gentle, often unsteady light.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一丝；少许； glimmer A glimmer of something is a faint sign of it.
glimmering: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 微弱的迹象；蒙眬的显现； glimmering A glimmering of something is a faint sign of it.
glimpse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一瞥；扫视； glimpse If you get a glimpse of someone or something, you see them very briefly and not very well.  /  [VERB 动词] 瞥见； glimpse If you glimpse someone or something, you see them very briefly and not very well.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 短暂的感受；初步的认识； glimpse A glimpse of something is a brief experience of it or an idea about it that helps you understand or appreciate it better.
glint: [VERB 动词] 闪闪发光；闪亮； glint If something glints , it produces or reflects a quick flash of light.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 闪光；闪烁； glint A glint is a quick flash of light.  /  [VERB 动词] 眼睛闪光，闪动，闪亮； glint If someone's eyes glint , they shine and express a particular emotion.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 眼神的闪光，闪动，闪亮； glint A glint in someone's eyes is a brightness that expresses a particular emotion.
glisten: [VERB 动词] 因湿润或油腻而闪闪发光； glisten If something glistens , it shines, usually because it is wet or oily.  /  [VERB 动词] 眼睛闪闪发光，闪烁光芒； glisten If you say that someone's eyes glisten , you mean their eyes are shining.
glitch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小故障；小毛病；小差错； glitch A glitch is a problem which stops something from working properly or being successful.
glitter: [VERB 动词] 闪烁；闪亮； glitter If something glitters , light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 激动、感兴趣等情感闪现，流露； glitter If someone's eyes glitter , they are bright and express a particular emotion such as excitement or interest.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 粘在物体上作装饰用的小发光物； glitter Glitter consists of tiny shining pieces of metal.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 外在的吸引力；魅力； glitter You can use glitter to refer to superficial attractiveness or to the excitement connected with something.
glitterati: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 知名人士；时髦人物； glitterati The glitterati are rich and famous people such as actors and rock stars.
glittering: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 辉煌的；成功的； glittering You use glittering to indicate that something is very impressive or successful.
glittery: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 闪闪发亮的； glittery Something that is glittery shines with a lot of very small points of light.
glitz: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 耀眼；华丽；浮华； glitz You use glitz to refer to something that is exciting and attractive in a showy way.
glitzy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 浮华的；华丽的；光彩夺目的； Something that is glitzy is exciting and attractive in a showy way.
gloat: [VERB 动词] 洋洋得意；幸灾乐祸； gloat If someone is gloating , they are showing pleasure at their own success or at other people's failure in an arrogant and unpleasant way.
glob: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一小滴；一小团； glob A glob of something soft or liquid is a small round amount of it.
global: [ADJ 形容词] 全球的；全世界的； global globally You can use global to describe something that happens in all parts of the world or affects all parts of the world.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 全面的；整体的；总括的； global A global view or vision of a situation is one in which all the different aspects of it are considered.
globalize: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] [使)全球化； globalize globalization When industry globalizes or is globalized , companies from one country link with companies from another country in order to do business with them.
global positioning system: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 全球定位系统[缩略形式为GPS)； A global positioning system is a system that uses signals from satellites to find out the position of an object.
global reach: [N-SING 单数名词] 开拓国际市场的能力； global reach When people talk about the global reach of a company or industry, they mean its ability to have customers in many different parts of the world.
global village: [N-SING 单数名词] 地球村指整个世界由电子通信设施，尤其是因特网连接为一个社会； global village People sometimes refer to the world as a global village when they want to emphasize that all the different parts of the world form one community linked together by electronic communications, especially the Internet.
global warming: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 全球变暖；地球大气层变暖； global warming Global warming is the gradual rise in the earth's temperature caused by high levels of carbon dioxide and other gases in the atmosphere.
globe: [N-SING 单数名词] 地球，世界用于强调其广大或某事在许多地区发生； globe You can refer to the world as the globe when you are emphasizing how big it is or that something happens in many different parts of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 地球仪； globe A globe is a ball-shaped object with a map of the world on it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 球状物；球体； globe Any ball-shaped object can be referred to as a globe .
globetrot: [VERB 动词] 环球旅行；周游世界； globe-trotting globe-trotter If someone spends their time globe-trotting , they spend a lot of time travelling to different parts of the world.
globe-trot: [VERB 动词] 环球旅行；周游世界； globe-trot globe-trotting globe-trotter If someone spends their time globe-trotting , they spend a lot of time travelling to different parts of the world.
globular: [ADJ 形容词] 球形的；球体的；球状的； globular A globular object is shaped like a ball.
globule: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小滴；小团； globule Globules of a liquid or of a soft substance are tiny round particles of it.
glockenspiel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 用木槌敲击发声的钟琴； A glockenspiel is a musical instrument which consists of metal bars of different lengths arranged like the keyboard of a piano.
gloom: [N-SING 单数名词] 阴暗；昏暗； gloom The gloom is a state of near darkness.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 忧郁；愁闷；无望； gloom Gloom is a feeling of sadness and lack of hope.
gloomy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 昏暗的；幽暗的； gloomy If a place is gloomy , it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忧伤的；沮丧的；无望的； gloomy gloomily If people are gloomy , they are unhappy and have no hope.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 前景黯淡的；悲观的； gloomy If a situation is gloomy , it does not give you much hope of success or happiness.
glorified: [ADJ 形容词] 吹嘘的；美化的； glorified You use glorified to indicate that something is less important or impressive than its name suggests.
glorify: [VERB 动词] 赞美；颂扬；吹捧；美化； glorify glorification To glorify something means to praise it or make it seem good or special, usually when it is not.  /  [VERB 动词] 颂扬，赞美上帝； glorify If you glorify God, you praise Him.
glorious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 宏伟的；壮丽的； glorious gloriously Something that is glorious is very beautiful and impressive.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人愉快的；美好的； glorious gloriously If you describe something as glorious , you are emphasizing that it is wonderful and it makes you feel very happy.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 辉煌的；光荣的；荣耀的； glorious gloriously A glorious career, victory, or occasion involves great fame or success.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 天气晴好的，阳光灿烂的； glorious gloriously Glorious weather is hot and sunny.
glory: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 光荣；荣耀； glory Glory is the fame and admiration that you gain by doing something impressive.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 辉煌时刻；巅峰； A person's glories are the occasions when they have done something people greatly admire which makes them famous.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 壮丽；壮观； glory The glory of something is its great beauty or impressive nature.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 引以为荣的事物； The glories of a culture or place are the things that people admire most about it.
gloss: [N-SING 单数名词] 光泽；色泽；光亮； gloss A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 虚假的外表；假象；虚饰； gloss Gloss is an appearance of attractiveness or good quality which sometimes hides less attractive features or poor quality.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 粉饰；掩饰； gloss If you put a gloss on a bad situation, you try to make it seem more attractive or acceptable by giving people a false explanation or interpretation of it.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 同gloss paint； Gloss is the same as gloss paint .
glossary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 术语汇编；词汇表； A glossary of special, unusual, or technical words or expressions is an alphabetical list of them giving their meanings, for example at the end of a book on a particular subject.
glossies: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 用高光纸印刷的杂志；精美杂志； The glossies are expensive magazines which are printed on thick, shiny paper.
gloss over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 粉饰；掩盖；掩饰； gloss over If you gloss over a problem, a mistake, or an embarrassing moment, you try and make it seem unimportant by ignoring it or by dealing with it very quickly.
gloss paint: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 亮光涂料；亮光漆； Gloss paint is paint that forms a shiny surface when it dries.
glossy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 光滑的；有光泽的； glossy Glossy means smooth and shiny.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 虚饰的；浮华的；虚有其表的； glossy You can describe something as glossy if you think that it has been designed to look attractive but has little practical value or may have hidden faults.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 杂志等用高光纸印刷的； glossy Glossy magazines, leaflets, books, and photographs are produced on expensive, shiny paper.
glove: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分手指的手套； glove Gloves are pieces of clothing which cover your hands and wrists and have individual sections for each finger.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 正合适；完全相配； If you say that something fits like a glove , you are emphasizing that it fits exactly.  /  See also: kid gloves ; hand in glove » see: hand �
glove compartment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 汽车前部挡风玻璃下的储物箱，杂物箱； The glove compartment in a car is a small cupboard or shelf below the front windscreen.
gloved: [ADJ 形容词] 戴手套的； gloved A gloved hand has a glove on it.
glow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 微弱稳定的光；暗淡的光； glow A glow is a dull, steady light, for example the light produced by a fire when there are no flames.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 脸上的红光，红晕，红润； glow A glow is a pink colour on a person's face, usually because they are healthy or have been exercising.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 一股，满腔满足感等； glow If you feel a glow of satisfaction or achievement, you have a strong feeling of pleasure because of something that you have done or that has happened.  /  [VERB 动词] 发微弱而稳定的光；发暗淡的光； glow If something glows , it produces a dull, steady light.
glower: [VERB 动词] 怒视；瞪眼看； glower If you glower at someone or something, you look at them angrily.
glowering: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 气愤的；脾气暴躁的； glowering If you describe a person as glowering , you mean they look angry and bad tempered.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 阴森昏暗的； glowering If you describe a place as glowering , you mean that it looks dark and threatening.
glowing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 热烈赞扬的；热情洋溢的； glowing glowingly See also: glow ; A glowing description or opinion about someone or something praises them highly or supports them strongly.
glow-worm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 萤火虫； A glow-worm is a type of beetle which produces light from its body.
glucose: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 葡萄糖； Glucose is a type of sugar that gives you energy.
glue: [N-MASS 物质名词] 胶；胶水； glue Glue is a sticky substance used for joining things together, often for repairing broken things.  /  [VERB 动词] 用胶水粘； glue If you glue one object to another, you stick them together using glue.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 完全吸引；使专注于； glue 目不转睛地看 If you say that someone is glued to something, you mean that they are giving it all their attention.
glue sniffing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 为获得迷幻效果的吸胶毒； Glue sniffing is the practice of breathing the vapour from glue in order to become intoxicated.
glum: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 闷闷不乐的；忧郁的；愁闷的； glum glumly Someone who is glum is sad and quiet because they are disappointed or unhappy about something.
glut: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 供过于求；供应过剩； glut If there is a glut of something, there is so much of it that it cannot all be sold or used.  /  [VERB 动词] 充斥；使供应过剩； glut If a market is glutted with something, there is a glut of that thing.
gluten: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 谷蛋白；面筋； Gluten is a substance found in cereal grains such as wheat.
glutinous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 黏的；胶质的；胶似的； glutinous Something that is glutinous is very sticky.
glutton: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 贪吃的人；食量大的人；饕餮； glutton If you think that someone eats too much and is greedy, you can say they are a glutton .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 酷爱…的人；急需…的人； glutton If you say that someone is a glutton for something, you mean that they enjoy or need it very much.

gluttony: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 贪吃；暴食； Gluttony is the act or habit of eating too much and being greedy.
glycerine: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 甘油；丙三醇； Glycerine is a thick, sweet, colourless liquid that is used especially in making medicine, explosives, and antifreeze for cars.

gnat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 叮人的小飞虫；蚋；蠓； A gnat is a very small flying insect that bites people and usually lives near water.

Great Britain: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 大不列颠岛由英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士组成，与北爱尔兰一起构成联合王国； Great Britain is the island consisting of England, Scotland, and Wales, which together with Northern Ireland makes up the United Kingdom.
greatcoat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指作为制服的厚长大衣； greatcoat A greatcoat is a long thick coat that is worn especially as part of a uniform.
greater: [great的比较级] ； Greater is the comparative of great .  /  [ADJ 形容词] 与大城市的名称连用，指包括附近城区及郊区在内的整个城市大的； Greater is used with the name of a large city to refer to the city together with the surrounding urban and suburban area.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 与某国名称连用，指包括该国和曾属该国或者人们认为应属该国的地区在内的更广阔的区域大的； greater Greater is used with the name of a country to refer to a larger area which includes that country and other land which used to belong to it, or which some people believe should belong to it.
greatly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 非常地；极大地； greatly You use greatly to emphasize the degree or extent of something.
grebe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鸊鷉一种水鸟； A grebe is a type of water bird.
Grecian: [ADJ 形容词] 古希腊式的；古希腊风格的； Grecian Grecian is used to describe something which is in the style of things from ancient Greece.
greed: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 贪婪；贪心；贪欲； greed Greed is the desire to have more of something, such as food or money, than is necessary or fair.
greedy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 贪婪的；贪心的；贪吃的； greedy greedily If you describe someone as greedy , you mean that they want to have more of something such as food or money than is necessary or fair.
Greek: [ADJ 形容词] 希腊的； Greek Greek means belonging or relating to Greece.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 希腊人； Greek A Greek is a person who comes from Greece.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 希腊语； Greek Greek is the language used in Greece.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 古希腊语； Greek Greek or Ancient Greek was the language used in Greece in ancient times.
green: [COLOUR 颜色词] 绿；绿色； green Green is the colour of grass or leaves.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 长满青草的；绿油油的；碧绿的； green greenness A place that is green is covered with grass, plants, and trees and not with houses or factories.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 环境保护的；主张环境保护的； Green issues and political movements relate to or are concerned with the protection of the environment.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有利于环境的；环保的；绿色的； green greenness If you say that someone or something is green , you mean they harm the environment as little as possible.
greenback: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 钞票；纸币； A greenback is a banknote such as a dollar bill.
green bean: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 青刀豆；四季豆； Green beans are long narrow beans that are eaten as a vegetable.
green belt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 城市周围的绿化带； A green belt is an area of land with fields or parks around a town or city, where people are not allowed to build houses or factories by law.
Green Beret: [N-COUNT 可数名词] “绿色贝雷帽”,“绿帽”兵指英国或美国的突击队员； A Green Beret is a British or American commando .
green card: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绿卡允许外国公民在美国生活和居住的证件； green card A green card is a document showing that someone who is not a citizen of the United States has permission to live and work there.
greenery: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 绿色植物；青葱的草木； greenery Plants that make a place look attractive are referred to as greenery .
greenfield: [ADJ 形容词] 未开发地区的；待开发地区的； Greenfield is used to refer to land that has not been built on before.
greenfly: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蚜虫； Greenfly are small green winged insects that damage plants.
greengage: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 西洋李；青梅子；青李子； A greengage is a greenish-yellow plum with a sweet taste.
greengrocer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蔬菜水果商； A greengrocer is a shopkeeper who sells fruit and vegetables.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蔬菜水果店； A greengrocer or a greengrocer's is a shop where fruit and vegetables are sold.
greenhouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 温室；暖房； A greenhouse is a glass building in which you grow plants that need to be protected from bad weather.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 温室效应的；引起温室效应的； Greenhouse means relating to or causing the greenhouse effect.
greenhouse effect: [N-SING 单数名词] 温室效应； The greenhouse effect is the problem caused by increased quantities of gases such as carbon dioxide in the air.
greenhouse gas: [N-VAR 可变名词] 温室气体主要为二氧化碳； Greenhouse gases are the gases which are responsible for causing the greenhouse effect.
greening: [N-SING 单数名词] 环保意识的增强； greening The greening of a person or organization means that the person or organization is becoming more aware of environmental issues.
greenish: [ADJ 形容词] 浅绿色的；略带绿色的； greenish 亦可用于构词 Greenish means slightly green in colour.
greenmail: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 绿票讹诈收购方以收购公司为要挟而迫使某公司溢价回购股票； greenmail Greenmail is when a company buys enough shares in another company to threaten a takeover and makes a profit if the other company buys back its shares at a higher price.
green onion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大葱； Green onions are small onions with long green leaves.
Green Paper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绿皮书英国供民众讨论的政府提案文件； In Britain, a Green Paper is a document containing ideas about a particular subject that is published by the Government so that people can discuss them before any decisions are made.
Green Party: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 绿党关注环保的政党； The Green Party is a political party that is particularly concerned about protecting the environment.
green pepper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 青椒； A green pepper is an unripe pepper that is used in cooking or eaten raw in salads.
Green Revolution: [N-SING 单数名词] 绿色革命尤指发展中国家为增加粮食产量而采用新品种和新耕种方法的举措； The green revolution is the increase in agricultural production that has been made possible by the use of new types of crops and new farming methods, especially in developing countries.
greenroom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 剧场、演播室等的演员休息室； A greenroom is a room in a theatre or television studio where performers can rest.
green salad: [N-VAR 可变名词] 蔬菜色拉；生菜色拉； A green salad is a salad made mainly with lettuce and other green vegetables.
greeny: [ADJ 形容词] 微绿的；浅绿的； greeny 亦可用于构词 Greeny means slightly green in colour.
greet: [VERB 动词] 同…打招呼;向…问好；欢迎；迎接； greet When you greet someone, you say 'Hello' or shake hands with them.  /  [VERB 动词] 对…作出反应；回应； greet If something is greeted in a particular way, people react to it in that way.  /  [VERB 动词] 呈现在…面前；映入…眼帘；最先被…感觉到； greet If you are greeted by something, it is the first thing you notice in a particular place.
greeting: [N-VAR 可变名词] 问候；招呼；致意； greeting A greeting is something friendly that you say or do when you meet someone.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 旧时的祝词，贺词，问候语； ' Greetings ' is an old-fashioned greeting.
greetings card: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 贺卡； A greetings card is a folded card with a picture on the front and greetings inside that you give or send to someone, for example on their birthday.
gregarious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 爱交际的；合群的； gregarious Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 动物、鸟等群居的； gregarious Gregarious animals or birds normally live in large groups.
gremlin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指机器出现不明故障时人们假想出来的捣乱的小妖精； gremlin A gremlin is a tiny imaginary evil spirit that people say is the cause of a problem, especially in a machine, which they cannot explain properly or locate.
grenade: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 手榴弹；榴弹； grenade A grenade or a hand grenade is a small bomb that can be thrown by hand.
grew: + + + Grew is the past tense of grow .
grey: [COLOUR 颜色词] 灰色； grey Grey is the colour of ashes or of clouds on a rainy day.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 头发灰白的； grey You use grey to describe the colour of people's hair when it changes from its original colour, usually as they get old.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 天气昏暗的，阴沉的； grey greyness If the weather is grey , there are many clouds in the sky and the light is dull.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沉闷的；阴郁的；暗淡的； grey greyness If you describe a situation as grey , you mean that it is dull, unpleasant, or difficult.
grey area: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灰色地带，中间区域界线不明、责任不清、难以处理的领域或情形； grey area If you refer to something as a grey area , you mean that it is unclear, for example because nobody is sure how to deal with it or who is responsible for it, or it falls between two separate categories of things.
greyhound: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灵犭是身细、腿瘦长、善奔跑的狗； A greyhound is a dog with a thin body and long thin legs, which can run very fast.
greying: [ADJ 形容词] 头发灰白的，花白的； greying If someone has greying hair, there is a lot of grey hair mixed with the person's natural colour.
greyish: [ADJ 形容词] 略带灰色的；浅灰色的； greyish 亦可用于构词 Greyish means slightly grey in colour.
grey market: [N-SING 单数名词] 灰市，水货市场经非正式渠道购买商品再以低于市价的价格售卖出去； Grey market goods are bought unofficially and then sold to customers at lower prices than usual.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 证券灰色市场，暗盘市场指公开发行前将股票售给投资人； grey market Grey market shares are sold to investors before they have been officially issued.
grey matter: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 头脑；智力； grey matter You can refer to your intelligence or your brains as grey matter .
grid: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 网格；地图上的坐标方格； grid See also: cattle grid ; A grid is something which is in a pattern of straight lines that cross over each other, forming squares.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 输送电力等的系统网络； grid A grid is a network of wires and cables by which sources of power, such as electricity, are distributed throughout a country or area.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 赛车起跑线； grid The grid or the starting grid is the starting line on a car-racing track.
griddle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 圆烤盘；平底锅； A griddle is a round, flat, heavy piece of metal which is placed on a cooker or fire and used for cooking.
gridiron: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 美式橄榄球； gridiron American football is sometimes referred to as gridiron .
gridlock: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 交通瘫痪；交通大堵塞； gridlock Gridlock is the situation that exists when all the roads in a particular place are so full of vehicles that none of them can move.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 僵局； gridlock You can use gridlock to refer to a situation in an argument or dispute when neither side is prepared to give in, so no agreement can be reached.
grief: [N-VAR 可变名词] 悲伤；悲痛； grief Grief is a feeling of extreme sadness.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 事情失败；人受挫，遭到不幸； grief If something comes to grief , it fails.  /  [EXCLAM 感叹语] 表示惊奇或震惊哎呀，天哪； grief Some people say ' Good grief ' when they are surprised or shocked.
grief-stricken: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极度悲伤的；悲恸欲绝的； grief-stricken If someone is grief-stricken , they are extremely sad about something that has happened.
grievance: [N-VAR 可变名词] 委屈；不满；不平；抱怨； grievance If you have a grievance about something that has happened or been done, you believe that it was unfair.
grieve: [VERB 动词] 尤指因某人的亡故而悲痛，悲伤，伤心； grieve If you grieve over something, especially someone's death, you feel very sad about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 使难过；使悲伤； grieve If you are grieved by something, it makes you unhappy or upset.
grievous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极其严重的；令人担忧的； grievous grievously If you describe something such as a loss as grievous , you mean that it is extremely serious or worrying in its effects.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 剧烈的；极痛苦的；疼痛难耐的； grievous grievously A grievous injury to your body is one that causes you great pain and suffering.
grievous bodily harm: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 严重人身伤害罪[缩略形式为GBH] ； grievous bodily harm If someone is accused of grievous bodily harm , they are accused of causing very serious physical injury to someone.
griffin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 神话故事中的狮身鹰首兽； In mythology, a griffin is a winged creature with the body of a lion and the head of an eagle.
grill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 烤炉内的烤架； grill A grill is a part of a stove which produces strong heat to cook food that has been placed underneath it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 置于火上的烤架； A grill is a flat frame of metal bars on which food can be cooked over a fire.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 烧烤；烤炙； grill grilling When you grill food, or when it grills , you cook it using very strong heat directly above or below it.  /  [VERB 动词] 追问；盘问；审问； grill grilling If you grill someone about something, you ask them a lot of questions for a long period of time.
grille: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗户等前的铁栅，护栅，金属网罩； A grille is a framework of metal bars or wire which is placed in front of a window or a piece of machinery, in order to protect it or to protect people.
grim: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 严峻的；令人不快的；让人沮丧的；令人难以接受的； grim grimness A situation or piece of information that is grim is unpleasant, depress ing, and difficult to accept.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 地方无吸引力的，阴森的，凄凉的； grim A place that is grim is unattractive and depressing in appearance.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 严肃的；坚定的；沉重的； grim grimly If a person or their behaviour is grim , they are very serious, usually because they are worried about something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 糟糕的；讨厌的；丑陋的；令人沮丧的； grim If you say that something is grim , you think that it is very bad, ugly, or depressing.
grimace: [VERB 动词] 因厌恶、痛苦等做鬼脸，扮怪相，脸部扭曲； grimace If you grimace , you twist your face in an ugly way because you are annoyed, disgusted, or in pain.
grime: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 污垢；尘垢； grime Grime is dirt which has collected on the surface of something.
Grim Reaper: [N-SING 单数名词] 狰狞的持镰收割者指死神，形如骷髅，身披黑色斗篷，手持镰刀； The Grim Reaper is an imaginary character who represents death.
grimy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 满是污垢的；肮脏的； grimy Something that is grimy is very dirty.
grin: [VERB 动词] 露齿而笑；咧嘴大笑； grin When you grin , you smile broadly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 露齿的笑；咧嘴的笑； grin A grin is a broad smile.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 苦笑着忍受；默默承受； grin If you grin and bear it , you accept a difficult or unpleasant situation without complaining because you know there is nothing you can do to make things better.
grind: [VERB 动词] 磨碎；碾碎； 将…磨成粉； grind grind up同grind If you grind a substance such as corn, you crush it between two hard surfaces or with a machine until it becomes a fine powder.  /  [VERB 动词] 用力挤压；用劲擦； grind 磨牙 If you grind something into a surface, you press and rub it hard into the surface using small circular or sideways movements.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…磨锋利；把…磨快；把…磨光； grind If you grind something, you make it smooth or sharp by rubbing it against a hard surface.  /  [VERB 动词] 刺耳地缓慢移动； grind If a vehicle grinds somewhere, it moves there very slowly and noisily.
grind down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 虐待；折磨；欺压； If you say that someone grinds you down , you mean that they treat you very harshly and cruelly, reducing your confidence or your will to resist them.
grinder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 研磨机，碾磨机厨用电器； grinder In a kitchen, a grinder is a device for crushing food such as coffee or meat into small pieces or into a powder.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 磨床；砂轮； A grinder is a machine or tool for sharpening, smoothing, or polishing the surface of something.
grinding: [ADJ 形容词] 没完没了的；无休止的；毫无起色的； grinding grindingly If you describe a bad situation as grinding , you mean it never gets better, changes, or ends.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 突然停顿下来； grinding If you say that something comes to a grinding halt , you are emphasizing that it stops very suddenly, especially before it was meant to.  /  See also: grind ; �
grind on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 令人厌烦地继续下去； If you say that something grinds on , you disapprove of the fact that it continues to happen in the same way for a long time.
grind out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 机械地做； To grind something out means to produce it in a boring or routine manner.
grindstone: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 磨石；砂轮； A grindstone is a large round stone that turns like a wheel and is used for sharpening knives and tools.
gringo: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外国佬，尤指美国佬，英国佬拉美人用语，可能具冒犯意味； Gringo is sometimes used by people from Latin America to refer to people from other countries, especially the United States and Britain.
grip: [VERB 动词] 紧握；抓牢； grip If you grip something, you take hold of it with your hand and continue to hold it firmly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 紧握；抓牢； grip A grip is a firm, strong hold on something.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 掌握；支配；控制； grip Someone's grip on something is the power and control they have over it.  /  [VERB 动词] 强烈地影响； grip If something grips you, it affects you very strongly.
gripe: [VERB 动词] 抱怨；发牢骚； griping If you say that someone is griping , you mean they are annoying you because they keep on complaining about something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 抱怨；牢骚； gripe A gripe is a complaint about something.
griping: [ADJ 形容词] 肠或胃绞痛的； A griping pain is a sudden, sharp pain in your stomach or bowels.
grisly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人极度厌恶的；恐怖的；可怕的； grisly also grizzly.
grist: [PHRASE 短语] 对…有用的东西或有利的事； If you say that something is grist to the mill , you mean that it is useful for a particular purpose or helps support someone's point of view.
gristle: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤指次等肉中的软骨； Gristle is a tough, rubbery substance found in meat, especially in meat of poor quality, which is unpleasant to eat.
grit: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 沙粒；沙砾； grit Grit is very small pieces of stone.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 勇气；坚毅；果敢； grit If someone has grit , they have the determination and courage to continue doing something even though it is very difficult.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 粗玉米粉，玉米渣美国南部常食用； Grits are coarsely ground grains of corn which are cooked and eaten for breakfast or as part of a meal in the southern United States.  /  [VERB 动词] 通常指因愤怒而咬紧牙关，咬牙切齿； grit If you grit your teeth , you press your upper and lower teeth tightly together, usually because you are angry about something.
gritty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 含沙砾的；覆有沙砾的；沙砾般的； gritty Something that is gritty contains grit, is covered with grit, or has a texture like that of grit.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坚毅的；勇敢的； gritty Someone who is gritty is brave and determined.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 对艰难或令人反感的情形的描述逼真的，真实的，活生生的； gritty A gritty description of a tough or unpleasant situation shows it in a very realistic way.
grizzled: [ADJ 形容词] 头发灰白的，花白的； grizzled A grizzled person or a person with grizzled hair has hair that is grey or partly grey.
grizzly: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灰熊；银光熊； grizzly A grizzly or a grizzly bear is a large, fierce, greyish-brown bear.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 小孩不断啼哭的，耍脾气的； grizzly If children are grizzly , they complain or cry a lot, often because they are unwell or tired.  /  See also: grisly ; �
groan: [VERB 动词] 呻吟；叹息； groan If you groan , you make a long, low sound because you are in pain, or because you are upset or unhappy about something.  /  [VERB 动词] 不高兴地低声说；咕哝； groan If you groan something, you say it in a low, unhappy voice.  /  [VERB 动词] 抱怨；发牢骚； groan If you groan about something, you complain about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 树木等发出嘎吱声； groan If wood or something made of wood groans , it makes a loud sound when it moves.
grocer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 食品杂货商； A grocer is a shopkeeper who sells foods such as flour, sugar, and tinned foods.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 食品杂货店； A grocer or a grocer's is a shop where foods such as flour, sugar, and tinned foods are sold.
grocery: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 食品杂货店； A grocery or a grocery store is a grocer's shop.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 食品杂货； Groceries are foods you buy at a grocer's or at a supermarket such as flour, sugar, and tinned foods.
grog: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 格洛格酒用朗姆酒、威士忌等加水勾兑； Grog is a drink made by mixing a strong spirit, such as rum or whisky, with water.
groggy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 体弱无力的；站立不稳的；踉踉跄跄的； groggy If you feel groggy , you feel weak and rather ill.
groin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 腹股沟； Your groin is the front part of your body between your legs.
groom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同bridegroom； groom A groom is the same as a bridegroom .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 马夫；马倌； A groom is someone whose job is to look after the horses in a stable and to keep them clean.  /  [VERB 动词] 洗刷[动物]; 给动物梳毛； groom If you groom an animal, you clean its fur, usually by brushing it.  /  [VERB 动词] 训练；培养； groom If you are groomed for a special job, someone prepares you for it by teaching you the skills you will need.
groomed: [ADJ 形容词] 打扮得干净利落或邋遢的； groomed You use groomed in expressions such as well groomed and badly groomed to say how neat, clean, and smart a person is.
grooming: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 打扮；装束；梳洗； grooming Grooming refers to the things that people do to keep themselves clean and make their face, hair, and skin look nice.
groove: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沟；槽；辙； groove A groove is a deep line cut into a surface.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 流行音乐的节奏； groove In popular music, a groove is a rhythm.
grooved: [ADJ 形容词] 有沟的；有槽的； grooved Something that is grooved has grooves on its surface.
groovy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 吸引人的；时髦的；刺激的； If you describe something as groovy , you mean that it is attractive, fashionable, or exciting.
grope: [VERB 动词] 摸索；探寻； grope If you grope for something that you cannot see, you try to find it by moving your hands around in order to feel it.  /  [VERB 动词] 摸索着走； grope If you grope your way to a place, you move there, holding your hands in front of you and feeling the way because you cannot see anything.  /  [VERB 动词] 探索；努力寻求； grope groping If you grope for something, for example the solution to a problem, you try to think of it, when you have no real idea what it could be.  /  [VERB 动词] 抚摸；猥亵； grope If one person gropes another, they touch or take hold of them in a rough, sexual way.
gross: [ADJ 形容词] 重大的；严重的；极端的； gross grossly You use gross to describe something unacceptable or unpleasant to a very great amount, degree, or intensity.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 言语、行为极端粗俗的，下流的； gross If you say that someone's speech or behaviour is gross , you think it is very rude or unacceptable.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人不快的；让人恶心的；令人厌恶的； gross If you describe something as gross , you think it is very unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肥胖难看的；臃肿的； gross If you describe someone as gross , you mean that they are extremely fat and unattractive.
gross domestic product: [N-VAR 可变名词] 国内生产总值； A country's gross domestic product is the total value of all the goods it has produced and the services it has provided in a particular year, not including its income from investments in other countries.
gross national product: [N-VAR 可变名词] 国民生产总值； A country's gross national product is the total value of all the goods it has produced and the services it has provided in a particular year, including its income from investments in other countries.
gross out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 令…恶心；使…作呕； If something grosses you out , it makes you feel disgusted.
grotesque: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 古怪的；怪诞的；荒唐的； grotesque grotesquely You say that something is grotesque when it is so unnatural, unpleasant, and exaggerated that it upsets or shocks you.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 丑陋的；奇形怪状的；极其难看的； grotesque grotesquely If someone or something is grotesque , they are very ugly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指小说或绘画中的怪异的人，丑八怪； grotesque A grotesque is a person who is very ugly in a strange or unnatural way, especially one in a novel or painting.
grotto: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 洞穴；岩洞；岩穴； grotto A grotto is a small cave with interesting or attractively shaped rocks.
grotty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人厌恶的；让人不悦的;低劣的； grotty If you describe something as grotty , you mean that it is unpleasant or of poor quality and you dislike it strongly.
grouch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 好抱怨的人；常发牢骚的人； grouch A grouch is someone who is always complaining in a bad-tempered way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 抱怨；牢骚； grouch A grouch is a bad-tempered complaint.
grouchy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脾气坏并常发牢骚的；好抱怨的； grouchy If someone is grouchy , they are very bad-tempered and complain a lot.
ground: [N-SING 单数名词] 地；地面； ground 在地面下/在地面上 The ground is the surface of the earth.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 相对于空中的地面； ground If you say that something takes place on the ground , you mean it takes place on the surface of the earth and not in the air.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 土；土地；土壤； ground The ground is the soil and rock on the earth's surface.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤指建筑物极少或具有某种特性的土地； ground You can refer to land as ground , especially when it has very few buildings or when it is considered to be special in some way.
groundbait: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 为捕鱼投入河或湖的鱼饵； Groundbait is food that you throw on to a river or lake when you are fishing in order to attract the fish.
groundbreaking: [ADJ 形容词] 开创性的；创新的；革新的； groundbreaking You use groundbreaking to describe things which you think are significant because they provide new and positive ideas, and influence the way people think about things.
groundcloth: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 扎营时用的防潮地席； A groundcloth is a piece of waterproof material which you put on the ground to sleep on when you are camping.
ground crew: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 机场的地勤人员； ground crew At an airport, the people who look after the planes when they are on the ground are called the ground crew .
grounded: 头脑清醒的；理智的；脚踏实地的； grounded If you say that someone is grounded , you mean that they are sensible and reasonable, and that they understand the importance of ordinary things in life.
ground floor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 底层；一楼； ground floor The ground floor of a building is the floor that is level or almost level with the ground outside.  /  See usage note at: floor �
groundhog: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 美洲旱獭；土拨鼠； A groundhog is a type of small animal with reddish-brown fur that is found in North America.
grounding: [N-SING 单数名词] 基础训练；基础知识；基础； grounding If you have a grounding in a subject, you know the basic facts or principles of that subject, especially as a result of a particular course of training or instruction.
groundless: [ADJ 形容词] 恐惧、指控、报道等无理由的，无根据的； groundless If you say that a fear, accusation, or story is groundless , you mean that it is not based on evidence and is unlikely to be true or valid.
ground level: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 地面相对于高处或地下而言； ground level If something is at ground level , it is at the same level as the ground, as opposed to being higher up or below the surface.
groundnut: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同peanut； A groundnut is a peanut .
ground plan: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 英国英语底楼平面图；美国英语楼层平面图； In British English, a ground plan is a plan of the ground floor of a building.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 初步计划；大纲； A ground plan is a basic plan for future action.
ground rent: [N-VAR 可变名词] 地租； ground rent Ground rent is rent that is paid by the owner of a flat or house to the owner of the land on which it is built.
ground rule: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 基本原则；基本准则； ground rule The ground rules for something are the basic principles on which future action will be based.
groundsheet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 露营时用的铺地防潮布； A groundsheet is a piece of waterproof material which you put on the ground to sleep on when you are camping.
groundskeeper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同groundsman； A groundskeeper is the same as a groundsman .
groundsman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 运动场地管理员；公园管理员； A groundsman is a person whose job is to look after a park or sports ground.
ground staff: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 运动场管理员； ground staff The people who are paid to maintain a sports ground are called the ground staff .  /  [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 机场的地勤人员； ground staff At an airport, the ground staff are the employees of aeroplane companies who do not fly with the planes, but who work in the airport helping passengers and providing information.
groundswell: [N-SING 单数名词] 公众情绪、支持度等的迅速高涨； groundswell A sudden growth of public feeling or support for something is often called a groundswell .
groundwater: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 地下水； groundwater Groundwater is water that is found under the ground.
groundwork: [N-SING 单数名词] 基础；根基； groundwork The groundwork for something is the early work on it which forms the basis for further work.
group: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 一组；一群；一批； group A group of people or things is a number of people or things which are together in one place at one time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 集体；群体；团体； group A group is a set of people who have the same interests or aims, and who organize themselves to work or act together.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 具有共同点而被放在一起考虑的组，群，类； group A group is a set of people, organizations, or things which are considered together because they have something in common.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 企业集团； group A group is a number of separate commercial or industrial firms which all have the same owner.
groupie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 到处跟随偶像的流行乐团迷，流行歌手迷，粉丝尤指少女； A groupie is someone, especially a young woman, who is a fan of a particular pop group, singer, or other famous person, and follows them around.
grouping: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 具有共同点的一类人[或事物]; 小团体；小圈子； grouping A grouping is a set of people or things that have something in common.
group therapy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 集体治疗法一组病人相互讨论各自问题的一种心理治疗法； Group therapy is a form of psychiatric treatment in which a group of people discuss their problems with each other.
grouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 松鸡； grouse 松鸡肉 A grouse is a wild bird with a round body.  /  [VERB 动词] 抱怨；发牢骚； grouse If you grouse , you complain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 抱怨；牢骚； grouse A grouse is a complaint.
grout: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 用于墙上瓷砖间抹缝的勾缝剂，薄胶泥； Grout is a thin mixture of sand, water, and cement or lime, which is used to fill in the spaces between tiles that are fixed to a wall.  /  [VERB 动词] 给瓷砖等灌浆；为…涂薄胶泥； grout If you grout the tiles on a wall, you use grout to fill in the spaces between the tiles.
grove: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 树丛；小树林； grove A grove is a group of trees that are close together.  /  [N-IN-NAMES 名称名词] 常用于街道名街，路； Grove is often used as part of the name of a street.
grovel: [VERB 动词] 卑躬屈膝；奴颜婢膝； grovel If you say that someone grovels , you think they are behaving too respectfully towards another person, for example because they are frightened or because they want something.  /  [VERB 动词] 为找东西等爬行，匍匐； grovel If you grovel , you crawl on the ground, for example in order to find something.
grow: [VERB 动词] 生长；长大；发育； grow When people, animals, and plants grow , they increase in size and change physically over a period of time.  /  [VERB 动词] 成活；生长； grow If a plant or tree grows in a particular place, it is alive there.  /  [VERB 动词] 栽种；种植； grow If you grow a particular type of plant, you put seeds or young plants in the ground and look after them as they develop.  /  [VERB 动词] 毛发、指甲等变长； grow When someone's hair grows , it gradually becomes longer.
grow apart: [PHR-V-RECIP 相互动词短语] 关系变得有隔阂，逐渐疏远； If people who have a close relationship grow apart , they gradually start to have different interests and opinions from each other, and their relationship starts to fail.
grow away from: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 与…逐渐疏远； If you grow away from someone, you gradually have fewer interests and opinions in common with them.
grower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 种植者；栽培者；种植商； grower A grower is a person who grows large quantities of a particular plant or crop in order to sell them.
growing pains: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 发展初期的暂时困难； growing pains If a person or organization suffers from growing pains , they experience temporary difficulties and problems at the beginning of a particular stage of development.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 儿童的生长痛，发育期痛； If children suffer from growing pains , they have pain in their muscles or joints that is caused by unusually fast growth.
growing season: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 植物或作物的生长季节； growing season The growing season in a particular country or area is the period in each year when the weather and temperature is right for plants and crops to grow.
grow into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 长得适合穿； grow into When a child grows into an item of clothing, they become taller or bigger so that it fits them properly.
growl: [VERB 动词] 狗等低声吼叫； growl When a dog or other animal growls , it makes a low noise in its throat, usually because it is angry.  /  [VERB 动词] 人发出低沉的怒吼，咆哮； growl If someone growls something, they say something in a low, rough, and angry voice.  /  [VERB 动词] 隆隆作响；轰鸣； growl If you say that something growls , you mean that it makes a deep low noise.
grown: [ADJ 形容词] 成年的；成熟的；长大的； grown See also: full-grown ; A grown man or woman is one who is fully developed and mature, both physically and mentally.
grown-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 用作儿语成年人，大人； grown-up A grown-up is an adult; used by or to children.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 成熟的；成年的；长大的； grown-up Someone who is grown-up is physically and mentally mature and no longer depends on their parents or another adult.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 似成人的；成熟的； grown-up If you say that someone is grown-up , you mean that they behave in an adult way, often when they are in fact still a child.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 适于成人的；成人的； grown-up Grown-up things seem suitable for or typical of adults.
grow on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 越来越被…喜欢；逐渐为…所喜爱； grow on If someone or something grows on you, you start to like them more and more.
grow out: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使头发长长以让原来的发式消失； If you grow out a hairstyle or let it grow out , you let your hair grow so that the style changes or so that you can cut off the part that you do not want.
grow out of: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 因自身长大或改变而改掉或戒除习惯、爱好等； grow out of If you grow out of a type of behaviour or an interest, you stop behaving in that way or having that interest, as you develop or change.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 孩子长大穿不下原来的衣服； When a child grows out of an item of clothing, they become so tall or big that it no longer fits them properly.
growth: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 发展；增长；兴起； growth The growth of something such as an industry, organization, or idea is its development in size, wealth, or importance.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 增加；增多；增长； growth The growth in something is the increase in it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 发展的；增长的； growth A growth industry, area, or market is one which is increasing in size or activity.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 性格的成长，发展； growth Someone's growth is the development and progress of their character.
grow up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 长大成人；成熟； See also: grown-up ; When someone grows up , they gradually change from being a child into being an adult.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 别犯傻；别孩子气； If you tell someone to grow up , you are telling them to stop behaving in a silly or childish way.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 形成；兴起；逐渐发展； If something grows up , it starts to exist and then becomes larger or more important.
grub: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 昆虫的幼虫，蛆； A grub is a young insect which has just come out of an egg and looks like a short fat worm.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 食物；吃的； grub Grub is food.  /  [VERB 动词] 翻找；搜寻； grub If you grub around, you search for something.  /  相关词组： grub up �
grubby: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肮脏的；污秽的； grubby A grubby person or object is rather dirty.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 卑鄙的；可鄙的； grubby If you call an activity or someone's behaviour grubby , you mean that it is not completely honest or respectable.
grub up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 掘出，挖出植物； If you grub up trees or plants, or grub them out , you dig them out of the ground, usually because they are no longer wanted.
grudge: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不满；积怨；怨恨； grudge If you have or bear a grudge against someone, you have unfriendly feelings towards them because of something they did in the past.
grudge match: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 势不两立的比赛；了结恩怨的比赛； grudge match You can call a contest between two people or groups a grudge match when they dislike each other.
grudging: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 勉强的；不情愿的； grudging grudgingly A grudging feeling or action is felt or done very unwillingly.

if: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (表示条件或假设)假如，如果，要是； if You use if in conditional sentences to introduce the circumstances in which an event or situation might happen, might be happening, or might have happened.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (用于间接疑问句)是否； if You use if in indirect questions where the answer is either 'yes' or 'no'.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (表示与句子主要部分的陈述稍有不同)即便，纵然，虽然； if You use if to suggest that something might be slightly different from what you are stating in the main part of the sentence, for example that there might be slightly more or less of a particular quality.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 如果…可以的话(通常与can，could, may 或 might 连用,在谈话中礼貌地提出自己的观点、转换话题或打断对方)； if You use if , usually with 'can', 'could', 'may', or 'might', at a point in a conversation when you are politely trying to make a point, change the subject, or interrupt another speaker.

illuminate: [VERB 动词] 照亮;照明;照射； illuminate To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.  /  [VERB 动词] 阐释;说明； illuminate illuminating If you illuminate something that is unclear or difficult to understand, you make it clearer by explaining it carefully or giving information about it.

inhalation: [N-VAR 可变名词] (空气等的)吸入； inhalation Inhalation is the process or act of breathing in, taking air and sometimes other substances into your lungs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吸入药;吸入剂;吸入物； An inhalation is a treatment for colds and other illnesses in which you dissolve substances in hot water and breathe in the vapour.
inhale: [VERB 动词] 吸气;吸入(烟等)； When you inhale , you breathe in.
inhaler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吸入器;人工呼吸器； An inhaler is a small device that helps you to breathe more easily if you have asthma or a bad cold.
inherent: [ADJ 形容词] 内在的;固有的;生来就有的； inherent inherently The inherent qualities of something are the necessary and natural parts of it.
inherit: [VERB 动词] 继承(金钱或财产)； inherit If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.  /  [VERB 动词] (从前人、前任等)接过,得到； inherit If you inherit something such as a task, problem, or attitude, you get it from the people who used to have it, for example because you have taken over their job or been influenced by them.  /  [VERB 动词] 经遗传获得(特征、特质等)； inherit If you inherit a characteristic or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors also had it.
inheritance: [N-VAR 可变名词] 遗产;继承物； inheritance An inheritance is money or property which you receive from someone who has died.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 转接物;沿袭物； inheritance If you get something such as job, problem, or attitude from someone who used to have it, you can refer to this as an inheritance .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 得自遗传的特征； inheritance Your inheritance is the particular characteristics or qualities which your family or ancestors had and which you are born with.
inheritance tax: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 遗产税;继承税； An inheritance tax is a tax which has to be paid on the money and property of someone who has died.
inheritor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (传统的)继承者； inheritor The inheritors of something such as a tradition are the people who live or arrive after it has been established and are able to benefit from it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (金钱或财产的)继承人； inheritor An inheritor is someone who inherits money or property from someone who has died.
inhibit: [VERB 动词] 抑制;约束； inhibit If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.  /  [VERB 动词] 禁止;阻止； inhibit To inhibit someone from doing something means to prevent them from doing it, although they want to do it or should be able to do it.
inhibited: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 受抑制的;受约束的;拘谨的； inhibited If you say that someone is inhibited , you mean they find it difficult to behave naturally and show their feelings, and that you think this is a bad thing.
inhibition: [N-VAR 可变名词] 顾虑;禁忌； inhibition Inhibitions are feelings of fear or embarrassment that make it difficult for you to behave naturally.
inhospitable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (地方等)不适合居住的； inhospitable An inhospitable place is unpleasant to live in.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不好客的;不友好的； If someone is inhospitable , they do not make people welcome when they visit.
in-house: [ADJ 形容词] 组织内部的;机构内部进行的； in-house In-house work or activities are done by employees of an organization or company, rather than by workers outside the organization or company.
inhuman: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不人道的;野蛮的;残酷的； inhuman If you describe treatment or an action as inhuman , you mean that it is extremely cruel.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 非人类的;怪异可怕的； inhuman If you describe someone or something as inhuman , you mean that they are strange or bad because they do not seem human in some way.
inhumane: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不人道的;残忍的； inhumane If you describe something as inhumane , you mean that it is extremely cruel.
inhumanity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无人性;野蛮;残酷； inhumanity You can describe extremely cruel actions as inhumanity .
inimical: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有害的;不利的； inimical Conditions that are inimical to something make it difficult for that thing to exist or do well.
inimitable: [ADJ 形容词] 不能模仿的;无与伦比的； inimitable You use inimitable to describe someone, especially a performer, when you like or admire them because of their special qualities.
iniquitous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极不公正的;邪恶的； iniquitous If you describe something as iniquitous , you mean that it is very unfair or morally bad.
iniquity: [N-VAR 可变名词] 邪恶;极不公正； iniquity You can refer to wicked actions or very unfair situations as iniquity .
initial: [ADJ 形容词] 开始的;最初的； initial You use initial to describe something that happens at the beginning of a process.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (姓名的)首字母(例如 Michael Dennis Stocks 的首字母缩写为 M.D.S.)； initial Initials are the capital letters which begin each word of a name.  /  [VERB 动词] 用姓名的首字母签名于； initial If someone initials an official document, they write their initials on it, for example to show that they have seen it or that they accept or agree with it.
initially: [ADV 副词] 最初;开始； initially Initially means soon after the beginning of a process or situation, rather than in the middle or at the end of it.
initiate: [VERB 动词] 开始;创始;发起； initiate If you initiate something, you start it or cause it to happen.  /  [VERB 动词] 使初步了解;向…传授基本技巧(或基础知识)； initiate If you initiate someone into something, you introduce them to a particular skill or type of knowledge and teach them about it.  /  [VERB 动词] (通过仪式)接纳，使加入； initiate If someone is initiated into something such as a religion, secret society, or social group, they become a member of it by taking part in ceremonies at which they learn its special knowledge or customs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有初步知识的成员;新入会的人； initiate An initiate is a person who has been accepted as a member by a particular group or club and been taught its secrets and skills.
initiation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 开始;创始;发起； initiation The initiation of something is the starting of it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (常包含特殊仪式的)入会，加入； initiation Someone's initiation into a particular group is the act or process by which they officially become a member, often involving special ceremonies.
initiative: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 积极的行动;倡议； initiative An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 主动权； initiative In a fight or contest, if you have the initiative , you are in a better position than your opponents to decide what to do next.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 主动性;积极性;进取心； initiative If you have initiative , you have the ability to decide what to do next and to do it, without needing other people to tell you what to do.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 采取主动;首先采取行动； initiative If you take the initiative in a situation, you are the first person to act, and are therefore able to control the situation.
initiator: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 创始人;发起者； initiator The initiator of a plan or process is the person who was responsible for thinking of it or starting it.
inject: [VERB 动词] 给…注射； inject To inject someone with a substance such as a medicine means to put it into their body using a device with a needle called a syringe.  /  [VERB 动词] 添加,注入(某种特性)； inject If you inject a new, exciting, or interesting quality into a situation, you add it.  /  [VERB 动词] 投入(金钱或资源)； inject If you inject money or resources into a business or organization, you provide more money or resources for it.
injection: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 注射;打针； injection If you have an injection , a doctor or nurse puts a medicine into your body using a device with a needle called a syringe.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (金钱或资源的)投入； injection An injection of money or resources into an organization is the act of providing it with more money or resources, to help it become more efficient or profitable.
injudicious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不明智的;缺乏判断力的;考虑不周到的； injudicious If you describe a person or something that they have done as injudicious , you are critical of them because they have shown very poor judgment.
injunction: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (法院下的)强制令，禁制令； injunction An injunction is a court order, usually one telling someone not to do something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 命令;指令;训谕； injunction An injunction to do something is an order or strong request to do it.
injure: [VERB 动词] 伤害;使受伤； injure If you injure a person or animal, you damage some part of their body.
injured: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 受伤的;有伤的； injured 受伤的人 An injured person or animal has physical damage to part of their body, usually as a result of an accident or fighting.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (感情)受到伤害的； injured If you have injured feelings, you feel upset because you believe someone has been unfair or unkind to you.
injured party: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 受害人;受害方； injured party The injured party in a court case or dispute about unfair treatment is the person who says they were unfairly treated.
injurious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有害的;致伤的； injurious Something that is injurious to someone or to their health or reputation is harmful or damaging to them.
injury: [N-VAR 可变名词] 伤害;损伤；  injury An injury is damage done to a person's or an animal's body.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (感情、名誉上的)伤害,损害； injury If someone suffers injury to their feelings, they are badly upset by something.  /  to add insult to injury »see: See insult ; �
injury time: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (足球比赛中的)伤停补时； Injury time is the period of time added to the end of a football game because play was stopped during the match when players were injured.
injustice: [N-VAR 可变名词] 非正义;不公平;不公正； injustice Injustice is a lack of fairness in a situation.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不公正地评判;不公正地对待； injustice If you say that someone has done you an injustice , you mean that they have been unfair in the way that they have judged you or treated you.
ink: [N-MASS 物质名词] 墨水;油墨； ink Ink is the coloured liquid used for writing or printing.  /  [VERB 动词] 使沾上墨水(或油墨等)； ink If you ink something, you put ink on it.
inkling: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 略知;模糊的概念； inkling If you have an inkling of something, you have a vague idea about it.
inkwell: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (桌上的)墨水池； An inkwell is a container for ink on a desk.
inky: [ADJ 形容词] 墨黑的;漆黑的； inky (亦可用于构词) Inky means black or very dark blue.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 沾有墨水的； inky If something is inky , it is covered in ink.
inlaid: [ADJ 形容词] 镶嵌的;嵌饰的;嵌花样的； inlaid An object that is inlaid has a design on it which is made by putting materials such as wood, gold, or silver into the surface of the object.
inland: [ADV 副词] 在内地(或内陆);向内地(或内陆)； inland If something is situated inland , it is away from the coast, towards or near the middle of a country.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 内地的;内陆的； inland Inland areas, lakes, and places are not on the coast, but in or near the middle of a country.

Inland Revenue Service: [N-PROPER 专有名词] (美国)国家税务局(缩略形式为 IRS)； In the United States, the Inland Revenue Service is the government authority which collects taxes.
in-laws: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 姻亲； Your in-laws are the parents and close relatives of your husband or wife.
inlay: [N-VAR 可变名词] 镶嵌装饰;镶嵌图案； inlay An inlay is a design or pattern on an object which is made by putting materials such as wood, gold, or silver into the surface of the object.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 镶嵌工艺； inlay Inlay is the technique of putting designs or patterns onto the surfaces of objects.
inlet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (海或湖伸向陆地的狭长)水湾，小湾，小港； inlet An inlet is a narrow strip of water which goes from a sea or lake into the land.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (机器上液体的)进口,入口； inlet An inlet is a part of a machine through which a flow of liquid enters.
inmate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 被收容者;监犯;(精神病院的)住院者； The inmates of a prison or mental hospital are the prisoners or patients who are living there.
inmost: [ADJ 形容词] 同 innermost； inmost Inmost means the same as innermost .
inn: [N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词] 小旅馆;小客栈;小酒馆； An inn is a small hotel or pub, usually an old one.
innards: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 内脏； The innards of a person or animal are the organs inside their body.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (机器的)内部构造； A machine's innards are the parts inside it.
innate: [ADJ 形容词] 天生的;天然的;固有的； innate innately An innate quality or ability is one which a person is born with.
inner: [ADJ 形容词] 内部的;里面的； inner The inner parts of something are the parts which are contained or are enclosed inside the other parts, and which are closest to the centre.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 内心的； inner Your inner feelings are feelings which you have but do not show to other people.
inner child: [N-SING 单数名词] 内在孩童(指人心中孩童般的情感)； inner child Some psychologists refer to a person's childish feelings as his or her inner child .
inner circle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 核心集团； inner circle An inner circle is a small group of people within a larger group who have a lot of power, influence, or special information.
inner city: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (大城市常存在社会、经济问题的)市中心贫民区； inner city You use inner city to refer to the areas in or near the centre of a large city where people live and where there are often social and economic problems.
innermost: [ADJ 形容词] 内心深处的;最隐秘的； innermost Your innermost thoughts and feelings are your most personal and secret ones.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 最接近中心的;最里面的;最深处的； innermost The innermost thing is the one that is nearest to the centre.
inner tube: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (轮胎的)内胎； inner tube An inner tube is a rubber tube containing air which is inside a car tyre or a bicycle tyre.
inning: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (棒球比赛中双方各上场击球一次的)局,回合； An inning is one of the nine periods that a standard baseball game is divided into.
innings: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (板球比赛中某队击球的)局,回合； innings An innings is a period in a game of cricket during which a particular team or player is batting.
innit: 不是吗(isn't it 的另一种说法)； innit Innit can be used at the end of a statement to make it into a question.
innkeeper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小旅店(或小客栈)老板;小酒馆掌柜； An innkeeper is someone who owns or manages a small hotel or pub.
innocence: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 天真;单纯； innocence Innocence is the quality of having no experience or knowledge of the more complex or unpleasant aspects of life.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 清白;无罪； innocence If someone proves their innocence , they prove that they are not guilty of a crime.
innocent: [ADJ 形容词] 清白的;无罪的； innocent If someone is innocent , they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 天真的;幼稚的;不谙世故的； innocent 天真无邪的人;涉世不深的人;幼稚的人 innocently If someone is innocent , they have no experience or knowledge of the more complex or unpleasant aspects of life.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 无辜(受害)的； innocent Innocent people are those who are not involved in a crime or conflict, but are injured or killed as a result of it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 没有恶意的;无冒犯之意的； innocent An innocent question, remark, or comment is not intended to offend or upset people, even if it does so.
innocently: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 故作天真地;佯装无知地； innocently See also: innocent ; If you say that someone does or says something innocently , you mean that they are pretending not to know something about a situation.
innocuous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无害的;无冒犯之意的； innocuous Something that is innocuous is not at all harmful or offensive.
innovate: [VERB 动词] 革新;创新;改革； innovate To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.
innovation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 新事物;新方法； innovation An innovation is a new thing or a new method of doing something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 革新;创新;改革； innovation Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.
innovative: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 革新的;新颖的； innovative Something that is innovative is new and original.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 富有革新精神的； innovative An innovative person introduces changes and new ideas.
innovator: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 革新者;创新者； innovator An innovator is someone who introduces changes and new ideas.
innovatory: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 同innovative； innovatory Innovatory means the same as innovative .
innuendo: [N-VAR 可变名词] 影射;暗讽； innuendo Innuendo is indirect reference to something rude or unpleasant.
innumerable: [ADJ 形容词] 无数的;数不清的； innumerable Innumerable means very many, or too many to be counted.
inoculate: [VERB 动词] 给…免疫接种;给…打预防针； inoculate inoculation To inoculate a person or animal means to inject a weak form of a disease into their body as a way of protecting them against the disease.
inoffensive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尽管可能乏味但)无害的，不冒犯人的，不让人讨厌的； inoffensive If you describe someone or something as inoffensive , you mean that they are not unpleasant or unacceptable in any way, but are perhaps rather dull.
inoperable: [ADJ 形容词] 不宜动手术的;手术无法治愈的； inoperable An inoperable medical condition is one that cannot be cured by a surgical operation.
inoperative: [ADJ 形容词] (规则、原则、税项等)无效的，不能生效的，不起作用的； An inoperative rule, principle, or tax is one that does not work any more or that cannot be made to work.
inopportune: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不合时宜的;不合适的； inopportune If you describe something as inopportune or if you say that it happens at an inopportune time, you mean that it happens at an unfortunate or unsuitable time, and causes trouble or embarrassment because of this.
inordinate: [ADJ 形容词] 极度的;非常的;过度的； inordinate inordinately If you describe something as inordinate , you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively great in amount or degree.
inorganic: [ADJ 形容词] 无机的； inorganic Inorganic substances are substances such as stone and metal that do not come from living things.
in-patient: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 住院病人； in-patient An in-patient is someone who stays in hospital while they receive their treatment.
input: [N-VAR 可变名词] 投入物(指信息、资源等)； input Input consists of information or resources that a group or project receives.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 输入信息； Input is information that is put into a computer.  /  [VERB 动词] 输入(信息)； input If you input information into a computer, you feed it in, for example by typing it on a keyboard.
input device: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (键盘等)输入设备； input device An input device is a piece of computer equipment such as a keyboard which enables you to put information into a computer.
inquest: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (调查死因的)讯问； inquest When an inquest is held, a public official hears evidence about someone's death in order to find out the cause.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (失败原因的)调查,查究； inquest You can refer to an investigation by the people involved into the causes of a defeat or failure as an inquest .
inquire: [VERB 动词] 询问;查询;打听； inquire If you inquire about something, you ask for information about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 调查;查究； inquire If you inquire into something, you investigate it carefully.  /  相关词组： inquire after �
inquire after: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 问候;问好； inquire after If you inquire after someone, you ask how they are or what they are doing.
inquirer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 询问者;查询者； inquirer An inquirer is a person who asks for information about something or someone.  /  [N-IN-NAMES 名称名词] (用于某些报刊名称)； Inquirer is used in the names of some newspapers and magazines.
inquiring: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 好问的;爱探索的； inquiring If you have an inquiring mind, you have a great interest in learning new things.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (表情等)探询的,审视的； inquiringly inquiring If someone has an inquiring expression on their face, they are showing that they want to know something.
inquiry: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 询问;查询;打听； inquiry An inquiry is a question which you ask in order to get some information.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (官方的)调查,查问； inquiry An inquiry is an official investigation.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 询问(或调查)过程； inquiry Inquiry is the process of asking about or investigating something in order to find out more about it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 协助警方调查； If you say that someone is helping the police with their inquiries , you mean that the police are questioning them about a crime, but have not yet charged them with it.

intrigue: [N-VAR 可变名词] 阴谋;诡计； intrigue Intrigue is the making of secret plans to harm or deceive people.  /  [VERB 动词] (尤指奇怪的事物)迷住，激起…的好奇心； intrigue If something, especially something strange, intrigues you, it interests you and you want to know more about it.

intro: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 引子;简介;前奏； intro The intro to a song, programme, or book is the first part, which comes before the main part.

introduction: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 引言;序言;导论； introduction The introduction to a book or talk is the part that comes at the beginning and tells you what the rest of the book or talk is about.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 入门书;初阶读物； introduction If you refer to a book as an introduction to a particular subject, you mean that it explains the basic facts about that subject.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外来品;新引进的东西； introduction You can refer to a new product as an introduction when it becomes available in a place for the first time.  /  See also: introduce ;

introverted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 内向的;羞赧的;不爱交际的； introverted Introverted people are quiet and shy and find it difficult to talk to other people.

intruder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 侵入者;闯入者； An intruder is a person who goes into a place where they are not supposed to be.
intrusion: [N-VAR 可变名词] 打扰;侵扰； intrusion If someone disturbs you when you are in a private place or having a private conversation, you can call this event an intrusion .  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 干扰;影响； intrusion An intrusion is something that disturbs your mood or your life in a way you do not like.
intrusive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 打扰的;侵扰的； intrusive Something that is intrusive disturbs your mood or your life in a way you do not like.

invaluable: [ADJ 形容词] 非常宝贵的;极为有用的； invaluable If you describe something as invaluable , you mean that it is extremely useful.

invasive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 侵袭的;扩散的； invasive You use invasive to describe something undesirable which spreads very quickly and which is very difficult to stop from spreading.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 开刀的;手术的； invasive An invasive medical procedure involves operating on a patient or examining the inside of their body.
invective: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 咒骂;痛骂； invective Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at people they hate or are angry with.
inveigh: [VERB 动词] 猛烈抨击;痛骂； inveigh If you inveigh against something, you criticize it strongly.
inveigle: [VERB 动词] 诱骗;引诱； inveigle If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.
invent: [VERB 动词] 发明;创造;首创； invent If you invent something such as a machine or process, you are the first person to think of it or make it.  /  [VERB 动词] 编造;捏造;虚构； invent If you invent a story or excuse, you try to make other people believe that it is true when in fact it is not.

inventory: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 详细目录;清单； inventory An inventory is a written list of all the objects in a particular place.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 储备;存货； inventory An inventory is a supply or stock of something.
inverse: [ADJ 形容词] 相反的;成反比的;相逆的； inverse inversely If there is an inverse relationship between two things, one of them becomes larger as the other becomes smaller.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 相反的事物;对立面； inverse The inverse of something is its exact opposite.

inverted commas: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 引号(写作''或“”)； Inverted commas are punctuation marks that are used in writing to show where speech or a quotation begins and ends.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (表示不够准确、无法接受或引用别人的话)加引号的，所谓的； inverted commas If you say in inverted commas after a word or phrase, you are indicating that it is inaccurate or unacceptable in some way, or that you are quoting someone else.

investment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 投资； investment Investment is the activity of investing money.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 投资金额;投资物； investment An investment is an amount of money that you invest, or the thing that you invest it in.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有用的投资物;值得买的东西； investment If you describe something you buy as an investment , you mean that it will be useful, especially because it will help you to do a task more cheaply or efficiently.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (时间、精力的)投入； investment Investment of time or effort is the spending of time or effort on something in order to make it a success.
investor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 投资者;投资机构； investor An investor is a person or organization that buys stocks or shares, or pays money into a bank in order to receive a profit.
inveterate: [ADJ 形容词] 积习不改的;上瘾的;根深蒂固的； inveterate If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.
invidious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (任务、工作)招致不满的，引起反感的； invidious If you describe a task or job as invidious , you mean that it is unpleasant because it is likely to make you unpopular.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (比较、选择)不公平的，难以决定的； invidious An invidious comparison or choice between two things is an unfair one because the two things are very different or are equally good or bad.

invincible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不可战胜的;所向披靡的； invincible invincibility If you describe an army or sports team as invincible , you believe that they cannot be defeated.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (信念、态度)不可动摇的，不可改变的； invincible If someone has an invincible belief or attitude, it cannot be changed.
inviolable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不可触犯的;不可违背的； inviolable If a law or principle is inviolable , you must not break it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 不可更改的;不可侵犯的； inviolable inviolability If a country says its borders are inviolable , it means they must not be changed or crossed without permission.
inviolate: [ADJ 形容词] 不受侵害的;未受损害的;不受影响的； inviolate If something is inviolate , it has not been or cannot be harmed or affected by anything.
invisible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 看不见的;隐形的； invisible invisibly If you describe something as invisible , you mean that it cannot be seen, for example because it is transparent, hidden, or very small.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 无形的； invisible invisibly You can use invisible when you are talking about something that cannot be seen but has a definite effect.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 被人忽视的;不为人注意的； invisible invisibility If you say that you feel invisible , you are complaining that you are being ignored by other people.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (故事中的人或事物)隐身的，隐形的； In stories, invisible people or things have a magic quality which makes people unable to see them.
invitation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 邀请； invitation An invitation is a written or spoken request to come to an event such as a party, a meal, or a meeting.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 请帖;请柬； invitation An invitation is the card or paper on which an invitation is written or printed.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 诱因;招致…的行为； invitation If you believe that someone's action is likely to have a particular result, especially a bad one, you can refer to the action as an invitation to that result.
