isolate: [VERB 动词] 使孤立;使脱离(朋友、支持者)； isolate isolated isolation To isolate a person or organization means to cause them to lose their friends or supporters.  /  [VERB 动词] 使隔离;使与世隔绝； isolate If you isolate yourself , or if something isolates you, you become physically or socially separated from other people.  /  [VERB 动词] 单独考虑;区别看待； isolate If you isolate something such as an idea or a problem, you separate it from others that it is connected with, so that you can concentrate on it or consider it on its own.  /  [VERB 动词] 使离析;分离； isolate To isolate a substance means to obtain it by separating it from other substances using scientific processes.
isolated: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 偏远的;偏僻的； isolated An isolated place is a long way away from large towns and is difficult to reach.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 孤独的;孤寂的;孤立无援的； isolated If you feel isolated , you feel lonely and without friends or help.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (事例)孤立的,个别的； isolated An isolated example is an example of something that is not very common.
isolation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 孤独;孤寂;孤立无援； isolation See also: isolate ; Isolation is the state of feeling alone and without friends or help.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 孤立地;脱离…地； isolation If something is considered in isolation from other things that it is connected with, it is considered separately, and those other things are not considered.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 单独地;独自地； isolation If someone does something in isolation , they do it without other people being present or without their help.
isolationism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 孤立主义(指避免与别国关系过密或在别国之间的冲突中持中立态度)； isolationism isolationist If you refer to isolationism , you are referring to a country's policy of avoiding close relationships with other countries and of not taking sides in disputes between other countries.
isometrics: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 静力锻炼法;等长收缩肌肉锻炼法； Isometrics or isometric exercises are exercises in which you make your muscles work against each other or against something else, for example by pressing your hands together.
isotope: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同位素； isotope Isotopes are atoms that have the same number of protons and electrons but different numbers of neutrons and therefore have different physical properties.
ISP: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 因特网服务供应商； An ISP is a company that provides Internet and e-mail services.
Israeli: [ADJ 形容词] 以色列的;以色列人的;以色列文化的； Israeli Israeli means belonging or relating to Israel, or to its people or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 以色列人;以色列后裔； An Israeli is an Israeli citizen, or a person of Israeli origin.
issue: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 重要问题;议题;争论的问题； issue See also: side issue ; An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 首要事项;要点;问题的要害； issue If something is the issue , it is the thing you consider to be the most important part of a situation or discussion.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (报刊的)期,号,版次； issue An issue of something such as a magazine or newspaper is the version of it that is published, for example, in a particular month or on a particular day.  /  [VERB 动词] 发表;发布； issue If you issue a statement or a warning, you make it known formally or publicly.
issue price: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (股票)发行价格； issue price The issue price of shares is the price at which they are offered for sale when they first become available to the public.
-ist: [SUFFIX 后缀] (替换 -ism,构成可数名词和形容词] 表示“…主义者”，“…信仰者”，“…主义的”，“信仰…的”； -ist is used in place of -ism to form count nouns and adjectives.  /  [SUFFIX 后缀] (用于构成可数名词)表示“…专业人员”，“…专家”，“从事…的人”； -ist is used to form count nouns referring to people who do a particular kind of work.  /  [SUFFIX 后缀] (用于表示乐器的名词后构成名词)表示“…演奏家”， “…演奏者”； -ist is added to nouns referring to musical instruments, in order to form nouns that refer to people who play these instruments.
isthmus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 地峡； An isthmus is a narrow piece of land connecting two very large areas of land.
it: [PRON-SING 单数型代词] 它(指物体、动物或上文已提及的其他事物)； it You use it to refer to an object, animal, or other thing that has already been mentioned.  /  [PRON-SING 单数型代词] (指小孩或婴儿)它； it You use it to refer to a child or baby whose sex you do not know or whose sex is not relevant to what you are saying.  /  [PRON-SING 单数型代词] (笼统指代刚描述过的情景)； it You use it to refer in a general way to a situation that you have just described.  /  [PRON-SING 单数型代词] (用于某些名词、形容词、动词前说明对某情况的感受、观点)； it You use it before certain nouns, adjectives, and verbs to introduce your feelings or point of view about a situation.
Italian: [ADJ 形容词] 意大利的;意大利人的;意大利语的;意大利文化的； Italian Italian means belonging or relating to Italy, or to its people, language, or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 意大利人;意大利人后裔； An Italian is an Italian citizen, or a person of Italian origin.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 意大利语； Italian is the language spoken in Italy, and in parts of Switzerland.
italic: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 斜体;斜体字； Italics are letters which slope to the right.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 斜体的； italic Italic letters slope to the right.
itch: [VERB 动词] 发痒； itch itching When a part of your body itches , you have an unpleasant feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch.  /  [VERB 动词] 渴望;迫切想要； itch If you are itching to do something, you are very eager or impatient to do it.
itchy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 发痒的;令人感到瘙痒的； itchy If a part of your body or something you are wearing is itchy , you have an unpleasant feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 漫游的渴望;旅行的渴望； itchy If you have itchy feet , you have a strong desire to leave a place and to travel.
it'd: (it would 的一种口语形式)； It'd is a spoken form of 'it would'.  /  (it had 的口语形式，尤用于 had 用作助动词时)； It'd is a spoken form of 'it had', especially when 'had' is an auxiliary verb.
item: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (系列物品或清单中的)一件； item See also: collector's item ; An item is one of a collection or list of objects.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 项目;条目;条款； item An item is one of a list of things for someone to do, deal with, or talk about.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一篇报道(或文章);(新闻等的)一条,一则； item An item is a report or article in a newspaper or magazine, or on television or radio.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (关系亲密的)一对； item If you say that two people are an item , you mean that they are having a romantic or sexual relationship.
itemize: [VERB 动词] 详细登记;逐条记录； If you itemize a number of things, you make a list of them.
It-girl: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 时尚派对女郎;社交名媛； Journalists sometimes use It-girl to describe a young woman who is well-known because she goes to the most fashionable places and events and knows famous people.
itinerant: [ADJ 形容词] (工人)巡回的，流动的； itinerant An itinerant worker travels around a region, working for short periods in different places.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 四处奔波的人;流浪者； An itinerant is someone whose way of life involves travelling around, usually someone who is poor and homeless.
itinerary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 路线;旅程； itinerary An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.
it'll: (it will 的一种口语形式)； it'll It'll is a spoken form of 'it will'.
its: 它的，他的，她的(用于表示某物属于某东西、地方、动物、婴儿等)； its You use its to indicate that something belongs or relates to a thing, place, or animal that has just been mentioned or whose identity is known.
it's: (it is 的常用口语形式)； It's is the usual spoken form of 'it is'.  /  (it has 的常用口语形式,尤用于 has 用作助动词时)； It's is the usual spoken form of 'it has', especially when 'has' is an auxiliary verb.
itself: [PRON-REFL 反身代词] 它自己;它本身； itself Itself is used as the object of a verb or preposition when it refers to something that is the same thing as the subject of the verb.  /  [PRON-REFL-EMPH 强调反身代词] (表示强调)自身，本身； itself You use itself to emphasize the thing you are referring to.  /  [PRON-REFL-EMPH 强调反身代词] (加在抽象名词之后)极度,非常； itself If you say that someone is, for example, politeness itself or kindness itself , you are emphasizing they are extremely polite or extremely kind.  /  an end in itself »see: See end ; �
ITV: [N-PROPER-COLL 专有集合名词] 独立电视公司(英国的一个商业电视集团)； ITV ITV refers to the group of British commercial television companies that broadcasts programmes on one channel.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] (英国)独立电视频道； ITV ITV is the television channel that is run by ITV.
-ity: [SUFFIX 后缀] (加在形容词后,有时替换 -ious 以构成名词)表示“…状态”，“…特征”，“…行为”； -ity is added to adjectives, sometimes in place of '-ious', to form nouns referring to the state, quality, or behaviour described by the adjective.
IUD: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 宫内避孕器;节育环； An IUD is a piece of plastic or metal which is put inside a woman's womb in order to prevent her from becoming pregnant.
I've: (I have 的常用口语形式，尤其当 have 用作助动词时)； I've I've is the usual spoken form of 'I have', especially when 'have' is an auxiliary verb.
IVF: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 体外受精； IVF is a method of helping a woman to have a baby in which an egg is removed from one of her ovaries, fertilized outside her body, and then replaced in her womb.
ivory: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 象牙； ivory Ivory is a hard cream-coloured substance which forms the tusks of elephants.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 象牙色;乳白色； Ivory is a creamy-white colour.
ivory tower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 象牙塔(指脱离实际生活的小天地)； ivory tower If you describe someone as living in an ivory tower , you mean that they have no knowledge or experience of the practical problems of everyday life.
ivy: [N-VAR 可变名词] 常春藤； Ivy is an evergreen plant that grows up walls or along the ground.
Ivy League: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 常春藤联合会(指美国东北部八所名牌大学)； Ivy League The Ivy League is a group of eight universities in the north-eastern part of the United States, which have high academic and social status.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (时尚、态度)典型常春藤大学生的； Ivy League You use Ivy League to describe fashions and attitudes typical of students at Ivy League universities.
-ize: [SUFFIX 后缀] (作为许多动词的结尾形式)表示“使…化”，“使处于…的新状态”； Verbs that can end in either '-ize' or '-ise' are dealt with in this dictionary at the '-ize' spelling.
J: [N-VAR 可变名词] 英语字母表的第10个字母； J is the tenth letter of the English alphabet.  /  [用于首字母为j的一些单词的缩写，如joule或Jack] ； J or j is an abbreviation for words beginning with j, such as 'joule' or 'Jack'.
jab: [VERB 动词] 戳；刺；捅； jab If you jab one thing into another, you push it there with a quick, sudden movement and with a lot of force.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 戳；捅；猛击； jab A jab is a sudden, sharp punch.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 注射；接种；预防针； jab A jab is an injection of something into your blood to prevent illness.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 抨击；攻击； jab You can refer to a sudden and unpleasant critical remark as a jab .
jabber: [VERB 动词] 急促而含混不清地说；激动而口齿不清地说； jabber If you say that someone is jabbering , you mean that they are talking very quickly and excitedly, and you cannot understand them.
jack: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 千斤顶；起重器； A jack is a device for lifting a heavy object off the ground, for example a car.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纸牌中的J牌，杰克； A jack is a playing card whose value is between a ten and a queen.  /  See also: jack-of-all-trades ; Union Jack ;  /  相关词组： jack in jack up �
jackal: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 豺，胡狼生活在非洲和南亚； A jackal is a wild animal that looks like a dog, has long legs and pointed ears, and lives in Africa and Southern Asia.
jackboot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 长筒靴；长筒军靴； Jackboots are heavy boots that come up to the knee, such as the ones worn by some soldiers.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 处于暴政下；处于专制统治下； If a country or group of people is under the jackboot , they are suffering because the government is cruel and undemocratic.
jackdaw: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 寒鸦； A jackdaw is a large black and grey bird that is similar to a crow, and lives in Europe and Asia.
jacket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 短上衣；夹克衫； jacket A jacket is a short coat with long sleeves.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 带皮烤土豆的土豆皮； Potatoes baked in their jackets are baked with their skin on.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 书籍的护封，书套； The jacket of a book is the paper cover that protects the book.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 唱片套； A record jacket is the cover in which a record is kept.
jacket potato: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 带皮烤土豆； A jacket potato is a large potato that has been baked with its skin on.
jack in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 结束，放弃活动或工作； If you jack in something such as an activity or job, you stop doing it.
jack-in-the-box: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 打开匣盖玩偶即可跳出的玩偶匣； A jack-in-the-box is a child's toy that consists of a box with a doll inside it that jumps out when the lid is opened.
jack-knife: [VERB 动词] 铰接卡车失控时弯成V字形，弯折； jack-knife If a truck that is in two parts jack-knifes , the back part swings around at a sharp angle to the front part in an uncontrolled way as the truck is moving.
jack-of-all-trades: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 万金油；万能博士；杂而不精的人； If you refer to someone as a jack-of-all-trades , you mean that they are able to do a variety of different jobs.
jackpot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 游戏或彩票的头奖，最高奖；尤指游戏中的累积赌注金； jackpot A jackpot is the most valuable prize in a game or lottery, especially when the game involves increasing the value of the prize until someone wins it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 取得巨大成功；赢了一大笔钱；交好运； If you hit the jackpot , you have a great success, for example by winning a lot of money or having a piece of good luck.
jack up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 用千斤顶托起汽车等； If you jack up a heavy object such as a car, you raise it off the ground using a jack.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 不合理地抬高，哄抬[价格]; 大幅度增加数量； jack up To jack up the price or amount of something means to increase it to an unreasonable or unacceptable level.
Jacobean: [ADJ 形容词] 建筑、家具或艺术品具有英王詹姆斯一世时期风格的； Jacobean A Jacobean building, piece of furniture, or work of art was built or produced in Britain in the style of the period between 1603 and 1625.
Jacuzzi: [N-COUNT 可数名词] “极可意”涡流式浴缸；按摩浴缸； A Jacuzzi is a large circular bath which is fitted with a device that makes the water move around.
jade: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 玉；碧玉；翡翠； Jade is a hard stone, usually green in colour, that is used for making jewellery and ornaments.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 绿玉色；翠绿； Something that is jade or jade green is bright green in colour.
jaded: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 精疲力竭的；厌倦的；腻烦的；无兴致的； jaded If you are jaded , you feel bored, tired, and not enthusiastic, for example because you have had too much of the same thing.
jagged: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 凹凸不平的；锯齿状的；有尖突的； jagged Something that is jagged has a rough, uneven shape or edge with lots of sharp points.
jaguar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 美洲豹；美洲虎； A jaguar is a large animal of the cat family with dark spots on its back.
jail: [N-VAR 可变名词] 监狱；看守所； jail A jail is a place where criminals are kept in order to punish them, or where people waiting to be tried are kept.  /  [VERB 动词] 使入狱；监禁； jail If someone is jailed , they are put into jail.
jailbird: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 囚犯；犯人；坐过牢的人； If you refer to someone as a jailbird , you mean that they are in prison, or have been in prison.
jailbreak: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 越狱； A jailbreak is an escape from jail.
jailer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 监狱看守；狱卒； A jailer is a person who is in charge of a jail and the prisoners in it.
jailhouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小型监狱，看守所； A jailhouse is a small prison.
jam: [N-MASS 物质名词] 果酱； jam Jam is a thick sweet food that is made by cooking fruit with a large amount of sugar, and that is usually spread on bread.  /  [VERB 动词] 硬推；硬塞；使劲放； jam If you jam something somewhere, you push or put it there roughly.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 机器卡住；使卡住；使不能运转； jam If something such as a part of a machine jams , or if something jams it, the part becomes fixed in position and is unable to move freely or work properly.  /  [VERB 动词] 车辆堵住，堵塞道路； jam Jam jammed If vehicles jam a road, there are so many of them that they cannot move.
Jamaican: [ADJ 形容词] 牙买加的；牙买加人的；牙买加文化的； Jamaican means belonging or relating to Jamaica or to its people or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 牙买加人； A Jamaican is a person who comes from Jamaica.
jamb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 门窗边框； A jamb is a post that forms the side part or upright of a door frame or window frame.
jamboree: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大型聚会；庆祝会；狂欢活动； A jamboree is a party, celebration, or other gathering where there is a large number of people and a lot of excitement, fun, and enjoyment.
jammy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 走运的；运气好的； jammy If you describe someone as jammy , you mean that they are very lucky because something good has happened to them, without their making much effort or deserving such luck.
jam-packed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 挤满的；拥挤的； jam-packed If somewhere is jam-packed , it is so full of people or things that there is no room for any more.
jangle: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使发出刺耳声；使发出丁零当啷的声音； jangle Jangle When objects strike against each other and make an unpleasant ringing noise, you can say that they jangle or are jangled .  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 神经紧张；刺激，烦扰神经； jangle If your nerves are jangling or if something jangles them, you are very anxious.
janitor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 建筑物的管理人，看管人，门房； A janitor is a person whose job is to look after a building.
January: [N-VAR 可变名词] 一月； January January is the first month of the year in the Western calendar.
Japanese: [ADJ 形容词] 日本的；日本人的；日语的；日本文化的； Japanese Japanese means belonging or relating to Japan, or to its people, language, or culture.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 日本人； The Japanese are the people of Japan.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 日语； Japanese is the language spoken in Japan.
jape: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 玩笑；恶作剧；戏弄； A jape is a silly trick that you play on someone which is quite funny and which does not really involve upsetting them.
jar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 用于存放食物的有盖的玻璃罐，罐子， 坛子，广口瓶； jar A jar is a glass container with a lid that is used for storing food.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一罐，一坛的量或物； jar You can use jar to refer to a jar and its contents, or to the contents only.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一杯酒； jar If you have a jar , you have a drink with friends in a pub.  /  [VERB 动词] 令人不快；使人不安；让人震惊； jar jarring If something jars on you, you find it unpleasant, disturbing, or shocking.
jargon: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 行话；行业术语；黑话； jargon You use jargon to refer to words and expressions that are used in special or technical ways by particular groups of people, often making the language difficult to understand.
jasmine: [N-VAR 可变名词] 茉莉；素馨； Jasmine is a climbing plant which has small white or yellow flowers with a pleasant smell.
jaundice: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 黄疸病； Jaundice is an illness that makes your skin and eyes become yellow.

kindergarten: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 幼儿园； kindergarten A kindergarten is an informal kind of school for very young children, where they learn things by playing.
kind-hearted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 仁慈的；体贴的；宽容的； kind-hearted If you describe someone as kind-hearted , you mean that they are kind, caring, and generous.
kindle: [VERB 动词] 激起[感情]; 使感受到； kindle If something kindles a particular emotion in someone, it makes them start to feel it.  /  [VERB 动词] 点燃； kindle If you kindle a fire, you light paper or wood in order to start it.
kindling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 引火柴；引火物； Kindling is small pieces of dry wood and other materials that you use to start a fire.
kindly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 仁慈的；体贴的；有同情心的； kindly kindliness A kindly person is kind, caring, and sympathetic.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 体贴地；友好地； kindly If someone kindly does something for you, they act in a thoughtful and helpful way.  /  [ADV 副词] 表示因有权让人做某事或对其恼怒劳驾，请； kindly If someone asks you to kindly do something, they are asking you in a way which shows that they have authority over you, or that they are angry with you.  /  See also: kind ;
kindness: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 仁慈；体贴；友好； kindness Kindness is the quality of being gentle, caring, and helpful.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 友好或体贴的举动； A kindness is a helpful or considerate act.
kindred: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 统称家人，亲属； kindred Your kindred are your family, and all the people who are related to you.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 类似的；相似的； kindred Kindred things are similar to each other.
kindred spirit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 志同道合的人；志趣相投的人； A kindred spirit is a person who has the same view of life or the same interests as you.
kinetic: [ADJ 形容词] 运动的； In physics, kinetic is used to describe something that is concerned with movement.
kinetic energy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 动能； In physics, kinetic energy is the energy that is produced when something moves.
king: [N-TITLE; N-COUNT 头衔名词；可数名词] 君主；国王； king A king is a man who is the most important member of the royal family of his country, and who is considered to be the Head of State of that country.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 最重要者；首屈一指者；…之王； king If you describe a man as the king of something, you mean that he is the most important person doing that thing or he is the best at doing it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纸牌中的老K； king A king is a playing card with a picture of a king on it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 国际象棋中的王； In chess, the king is the most important piece.
kingdom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 王国； kingdom A kingdom is a country or region that is ruled by a king or queen.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 管辖范围；领域； kingdom A kingdom is a place or area that is thought to be under the control of a person or organization.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 动物或植物界； All the animals, birds, and insects in the world can be referred to together as the animal kingdom .
kingfisher: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 翠鸟； A kingfisher is a brightly-coloured bird which lives near rivers and lakes and catches fish.
kingly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 国王似的；国王的；君主的； kingly Kingly means like a king, or related to the duties of a king.
kingpin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 组织中的主要人物，领袖； kingpin If you describe someone as the kingpin of an organization, you mean that they are the most important person involved in it.
kingship: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 国王身份；王位； kingship Kingship is the fact or position of being a king.
king-size: [ADJ 形容词] 大于正常尺寸的；特大的； king-size A king-size or king-sized version of something is a larger size than the standard version, and may be the largest size available.
kink: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 直线物体上的弯，结； kink A kink is a curve or twist in something which is otherwise or normally straight.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使弯曲；使扭结；使绞缠； kink If something kinks or is kinked , it has, or it develops a curve or twist in it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指古怪念头;奇想，怪癖； kink A kink is a particular quality or feature of a person's mind or character, especially one which is thought to be unusual or abnormal.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 解决问题； kink If someone works out the kinks in a situation, they resolve the problems associated with it.
kinky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指性行为)变态的,反常的； kinky If you describe something, usually a sexual practice or preference, as kinky , you mean that it is unusual and would be considered strange by most people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 卷曲的；缠绕的； kinky Something that is kinky has a lot of curves or twists.
kinsfolk: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 亲戚；亲属； kinsfolk Your kinsfolk or kinfolk are the people who are related to you.
kinship: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 亲属关系； kinship Kinship is the relationship between members of the same family.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 因背景、感觉或想法相似而产生的亲切感； kinship If you feel kinship with someone, you feel close to them, because you have a similar background or similar feelings or ideas.
kinsman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男性亲属，亲戚； Someone's kinsman is their male relative.
kinswoman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女性亲属，亲戚； Someone's kinswoman is their female relative.
kiosk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 出售三明治或报纸等的售货亭，小亭； kiosk A kiosk is a small building or structure from which people can buy things such as sandwiches or newspapers through an open window.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公用电话亭； kiosk A kiosk or a telephone kiosk is a public telephone box.
kip: [N-SING 单数名词] 睡觉； kip Kip is sleep.  /  [VERB 动词] 通常指不是在自己家或床上睡觉； kip If you kip somewhere, usually somewhere that is not your own home or bed, you sleep there.
kipper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 烟熏鲱鱼； A kipper is a fish, usually a herring, which has been preserved by being hung in smoke.
kirk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 教堂； kirk A kirk is a church.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] 苏格兰教会； The Kirk is the Church of Scotland, the main Protestant church in Scotland.
kirsch: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 通常指餐后饮用的樱桃白兰地，樱桃酒； Kirsch is a strong, colourless, alcoholic drink made from cherries which is usually drunk after a meal.
kiss: [V-RECIP 相互动词] 吻；亲吻； kiss If you kiss someone, you touch them with your lips to show affection or sexual desire, or to greet them or say goodbye.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻吻以示尊敬； kiss If you kiss something, you touch it lightly with your lips, usually as a sign of respect.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻拂；轻触； kiss If you say that something kisses another thing, you mean that it touches that thing very gently.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 飞吻； kiss If you blow someone a kiss or blow a kiss , you touch the palm of your hand lightly with your lips, and then blow across your hand towards the person, in order to show them your affection.
kiss-and-tell: [ADJ 形容词] 泄露与名人的私情的； kiss-and-tell If someone who has had a love affair with a famous person tells the story of that affair in public, for example in a newspaper or book, you can refer to this as a kiss-and-tell story.
kiss of death: [N-SING 单数名词] 肯定会导致失败的事物；死亡之吻； kiss of death If you say that a particular event is the kiss of death for something, you mean that it is certain to make them fail or be a disaster.
kiss of life: [N-SING 单数名词] 口对口人工呼吸； kiss of life If you give someone who has stopped breathing the kiss of life , you put your mouth onto their mouth and breathe into their lungs to make them start breathing again.
kit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 成套工具；成套设备； kit A kit is a group of items that are kept together, often in the same container, because they are all used for similar purposes.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤指某运动的全套衣服和装备； kit Kit is special clothing and equipment that you use when you take part in a particular activity, especially a sport.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 配套元件； kit A kit is a set of parts that can be put together in order to make something.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 脱掉所有衣服/不脱掉所有衣服； kit If someone gets their kit off or takes their kit off , they take off all their clothes.
kitbag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指帆布做的士兵或水手的行囊，背包； A kitbag is a long narrow bag, usually made of canvas, in which soldiers or sailors keep their clothing and personal possessions.
kitchen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 厨房； See also: soup kitchen ; A kitchen is a room that is used for cooking and for household jobs such as washing dishes.
kitchen cabinet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (首相或总统的)厨房内阁，私人顾问团尤为记者用语，表示不满； Journalists sometimes refer to the unofficial advisers of a prime minister or president as that person's kitchen cabinet , especially if they disapprove of the influence that the advisers seem to have.
kitchenette: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小厨房；房间里用作厨房的一角； A kitchenette is a small kitchen, or a part of a larger room that is used for cooking.
kitchen garden: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 家庭菜园花园中用作种蔬菜、香草及水果的部分； A kitchen garden is a garden, or part of a garden, in which vegetables, herbs, and fruit are grown.
kite: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 风筝； A kite is an object, usually used as a toy, which is flown in the air.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鸢一种猛禽； A kite is a bird of prey which hunts and kills small animals for food.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 试探舆论或反应； kite If you say that someone is flying a kite , you are critical of them for putting forward new ideas just to see how people react, rather than with the intention of putting those ideas into practice.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 极度兴奋的；被酒精或毒品麻醉的； kite If you say that someone is as high as a kite , you mean that they are very excited or that they are greatly affected by alcohol or drugs.
Kitemark: [N-SING 单数名词] 风筝标记在英国此标记表明商品达到一定的安全和质量标准； In Britain, the Kitemark is a symbol which is put on products that have met certain standards of safety and quality.
kith and kin: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 亲戚朋友； You can refer to your friends and family as your kith and kin .
kit out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使…装备起来； If someone or something is kitted out , they have everything they need at a particular time, such as clothing, equipment, or furniture.
kitsch: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 庸俗的艺术作品；迎合低级趣味的拙劣作品； kitsch You can refer to a work of art or an object as kitsch if it is showy and thought by some people to be in bad taste.
kitten: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小猫； A kitten is a very young cat.
kitty: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 共同凑集的一笔钱； kitty A kitty is an amount of money gathered from several people, which is meant to be spent on things that these people will share or use together.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 全部赌注； kitty A kitty is the total amount of money which is bet in a gambling game, and which is taken by the winner or winners.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有时用作昵称猫咪，小猫； Kitty is sometimes used as an affectionate way of referring to a cat or kitten.
kiwi: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同kiwi fruit； A kiwi is the same as a kiwi fruit .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 几维新西兰鸟，不能飞； A kiwi is a type of bird that lives in New Zealand.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 新西兰人可能具冒犯意味； People who come from New Zealand are sometimes referred to as Kiwis .
kiwi fruit: [N-VAR 可变名词] 猕猴桃；奇异果； A kiwi fruit is a fruit with a brown hairy skin and green flesh.
KKK: [N-PROPER-COLL 专有集合名词] KKK is an abbreviation for (缩略=) Ku Klux Klan.
Klansman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三K党人； A Klansman is a man who is a member of the Ku Klux Klan .
klatch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指女性参加的非正式的社交聚会，咖啡聚会； A coffee klatch or Kaffee Klatsch is an informal social event at which people, usually women, talk and drink coffee.
Kleenex: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 舒洁纸巾；纸巾； Kleenex A Kleenex is a piece of soft tissue paper that is used as a handkerchief.
kleptomaniac: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有盗窃癖者； A kleptomaniac is a person who cannot control their desire to steal things, usually because of a medical condition.
kludge: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指计算机问题的简单而有效的解决方案； You can refer to an unsophisticated but fairly effective solution to a problem as a kludge .
klutz: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 笨蛋；傻瓜； You can refer to someone who is very clumsy or who seems stupid as a klutz .
km: + + + km is a written abbreviation for (书面缩略=) kilometre .
knack: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 诀窍；本领； knack A knack is a particularly clever or skilful way of doing something successfully, especially something which most people find difficult.
knacker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 废马屠夫买下老马并将其屠宰以获取其肉、骨、皮的人； knacker A knacker is someone who buys up old horses and then kills them for their meat, bones, or leather.
knackered: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 筋疲力尽的；疲惫不堪的； knackered If you say that you are knackered , you are emphasizing that you are extremely tired.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 破或旧得不能用了的； knackered If you say that something is knackered , you mean that it is completely broken or worn out.
knapsack: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 帆布或皮背包； A knapsack is a canvas or leather bag that you carry on your back or over your shoulder, for example when you are walking in the countryside.
knave: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不诚实的人；无赖；恶棍； If someone calls a man a knave , they mean that he is dishonest and should not be trusted.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] [纸牌游戏中jack的另一种说法] ； In card games, knave is another word for jack .
knead: [VERB 动词] 揉，捏面团或其他食物； knead kneading When you knead dough or other food, you press and squeeze it with your hands so that it becomes smooth and ready to cook.  /  [VERB 动词] 揉捏；按摩；推拿； knead If you knead a part of someone's body, you press or squeeze it with your fingers.
knee: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 膝；膝盖；膝关节； knee Your knee is the place where your leg bends.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 坐下时大腿朝上的面； knee If something or someone is on your knee or on your knees , they are resting or sitting on the upper part of your legs when you are sitting down.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 裤子的膝部； knee The knee on a piece of clothing is the part that covers your knee.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 膝部； knee If you are on your knees , your legs are bent and your knees are on the ground.
kneecap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 膝盖骨；髌骨； Your kneecaps are the bones at the front of your knees.
kneecapping: [N-VAR 可变名词] 用枪击穿膝盖骨恐怖组织中使用的一种刑罚； Knee-capping is the act of shooting someone in the knee and is carried out by some terrorist organizations as a form of punishment.
knee-capping: [N-VAR 可变名词] 用枪击穿膝盖骨恐怖组织中使用的一种刑罚； Knee-capping is the act of shooting someone in the knee and is carried out by some terrorist organizations as a form of punishment.
knee-deep: [ADJ 形容词] 齐膝深的； knee-deep Something that is knee-deep is as high as your knees.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 没膝的； knee-deep If a person or a place is knee-deep in something such as water, the level of the water comes up to a person's knees.
knee-high: [ADJ 形容词] 齐膝高的； knee-high Something that is knee-high is as tall or high as an adult's knees.
knee-jerk: [ADJ 形容词] 未经思考作出的；依靠本能作出的； knee-jerk If you call someone's response to a question or situation a knee-jerk reaction, you mean that they react in a very predictable way, without thinking.
kneel: [VERB 动词] 跪下；跪着； kneel kneel down 同 kneel When you kneel , you bend your legs so that your knees are touching the ground.
knees-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 社交聚会；庆祝活动； A knees-up is a party or celebration.
knelt: + + + Knelt is a past tense and past participle of kneel .
knew: + + + Knew is the past tense of know .
knickers: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 女士短衬裤； knickers Knickers are a piece of underwear worn by women and girls which have holes for the legs and elastic around the waist to hold them up.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 恼火；烦闷； knickers If someone is getting their knickers in a twist about something, they are getting annoyed or upset about it without good reason.
knick-knacks: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 小装饰物；小摆设； knick-knacks Knick-knacks are small objects which people keep as ornaments or toys, rather than for a particular use.
knife: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 刀； knife A knife is a tool for cutting or a weapon and consists of a flat piece of metal with a sharp edge on the end of a handle.  /  [VERB 动词] 用刀伤害； knife To knife someone means to attack and injure them with a knife.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 手术刀； A surgeon's knife is a piece of equipment used to cut flesh and organs during operations.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 接受手术；动手术； knife If you go under the knife , you have an operation in a hospital.
knife-edge: [PHRASE 短语] 形势难料；结果未卜； knife-edge To be on a knife-edge means to be in a situation in which nobody knows what is going to happen next, or in which one thing is just as likely to happen as another.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 形势难料的； knife-edge You can use knife-edge to refer to something that is very exciting or tense because you do not know what is going to happen next.
knifeman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 持刀伤或杀人者； knifeman A knifeman is someone who has attacked or killed someone with a knife.
knifepoint: [PHRASE 短语] 在刀子威胁下； knifepoint If you are attacked or robbed at knifepoint , someone threatens you with a knife while they attack or steal from you.
knifing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 持刀行凶事件； See also: knife ; A knifing is an incident in which someone is attacked and injured with a knife.
knight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 中世纪的骑士； In medieval times, a knight was a man of noble birth, who served his king or lord in battle.  /  [VERB 动词] 封…为爵士； knight If someone is knighted , they are given a knighthood.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 爵士； A knight is a man who has been knighted.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 国际象棋中的马； In chess, a knight is a piece which is shaped like a horse's head.
knighthood: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 英国国王或女王授予的爵士头衔，骑士头衔，爵士称号，骑士称号[其名前冠以Sir] ； A knighthood is a title that is given to a man by a British king or queen for his achievements or his service to his country.
knit: [VERB 动词] 编织；针织；机织； knit 亦可用于构词 knitter If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.  /  [VERB 动词] 使紧密结合；使严密；使紧凑； knit 亦可用于构词 If someone or something knits things or people together , they make them fit or work together closely and successfully.  /  [VERB 动词] 骨头愈合，接合； knit When broken bones knit , the broken pieces grow together again.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 皱眉表示恼怒、担忧； knit If you knit your brows or knit your eyebrows , you frown because you are angry or worried.
knitting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 编织物；针织品； knitting Knitting is something, such as an article of clothing, that is being knitted.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 编织；针织； knitting Knitting is the action or process of knitting.
knitting needle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 塑料或金属制的编织针，毛衣针； Knitting needles are thin plastic or metal rods which you use when you are knitting.
knitwear: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 针织衫；针织衣物； knitwear Knitwear is clothing that has been knitted.
knives: [knife的复数] ； Knives is the plural of knife .

leaderboard: [N-SING 单数名词] 尤指高尔夫锦标赛的选手积分榜； leaderboard The leaderboard is a board that shows the names and positions of the leading competitors in a competition, especially a golf tournament.
leadership: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 领导层；领导班子； leadership You refer to people who are in control of a group or organization as the leadership .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 领导；领导权；领导地位； leadership Someone's leadership is their position or state of being in control of a group of people.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 领导才能；领导方法；领导作风； leadership Leadership refers to the qualities that make someone a good leader, or the methods a leader uses to do his or her job.
lead-free: [ADJ 形容词] 汽油、油漆等无铅的，不含铅的； Something such as petrol or paint which is lead-free , is made without lead, or has no lead added to it.
lead-in: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 引子；前奏；开场白； lead-in A lead-in is something that is said or done as an introduction before the main subject or event, especially before a radio or television programme.
leading: [ADJ 形容词] 最重要的；卓著的；显赫的； leading The leading person or thing in a particular area is the one which is most important or successful.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 主角的；主演的； The leading role in a play or film is the main role.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 在比赛或行列中首位的，居前的； The leading group, vehicle, or person in a race or procession is the one that is at the front.
leading article: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 报纸中的社评，社论； A leading article in a newspaper is a piece of writing which gives the editor's opinion on an important news item.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 报纸的要闻，头条； A leading article in a newspaper is the most important story in it.
leading edge: [N-SING 单数名词] 尖端领域；高新领域；最前沿； leading edge leading-edge The leading edge of a particular area of research or development is the area of it that seems most advanced or sophisticated.

lead singer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乐队的主唱； lead singer The lead singer of a pop group is the person who sings most of the songs.
lead time: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 研制时间；开发周期； lead time Lead time is the time between the original design or idea for a particular product and its actual production.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 从订货到交货的交付周期； Lead time is the period of time that it takes for goods to be delivered after someone has ordered them.

leaf: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 树叶；叶子； leaf See also: -leaved ; The leaves of a tree or plant are the parts that are flat, thin, and usually green.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 书页； A leaf is one of the pieces of paper of which a book is made.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 师法；效法；以某人为榜样； leaf If you take a leaf from someone's book you behave in the same way as them because you want to be like that person or as successful as they are.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 重新开始；洗心革面；改过自新； leaf If you say that you are going to turn over a new leaf , you mean that you are going to start to behave in a better or more acceptable way.

league: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 联盟；同盟； A league is a group of people, clubs, or countries that have joined together for a particular purpose, or because they share a common interest.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 体育运动队的联合会，联赛； A league is a group of teams that play the same sport or activity against each other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 级别；档次；水平； league You use the word league to make comparisons between different people or things, especially in terms of their quality.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 沆瀣一气；勾结； league If you say that someone is in league with another person to do something bad, you mean that they are working together to do that thing.
league table: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 名次表；排名表； league table A league table is a list that shows how successful an organization such as a sports team or a business is when it is compared to other similar organizations.

lean towards: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 倾向于；偏向于； lean towards If you lean towards or lean toward a particular idea, belief, or type of behaviour, you have a tendency to think or act in a particular way.

learner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 学习者；初学者； learner A learner is someone who is learning about a particular subject or how to do something.

lease: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 租约；租契；出租协议； lease A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.  /  [VERB 动词] 租借；租用；出租； lease If you lease property or something such as a car from someone or if they lease it to you, they allow you to use it in return for regular payments of money.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 较昔日更加焕发生机；重振雄风； lease If you say that someone or something has been given a new lease of life , you are emphasizing that they are much more lively or successful than they have been in the past.

less: Less is often considered to be the comparative form of little .  /  [DET 限定词] 数量较小或少的；更小或少的[前面可用a little，a lot，a bit，far和much等修饰] ； less You use less to indicate that there is a smaller amount of something than before or than average.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 用在数字或数量前少于，低于，比…少； less You use less than before a number or amount to say that the actual number or amount is smaller than this.  /  [ADV-COMPAR 副词比较级形式] 某一特性的程度与以往或一般情况相比较轻地，较差地； less You use less to indicate that something or someone has a smaller amount of a quality than they used to or than is average or usual.

lethargy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 慵懒；倦怠；没精打采； lethargy Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic.
let in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 允许空气、光线、水等进入； If an object lets in something such as air, light, or water, it allows air, light, or water to get into it, for example because the object has a hole in it.

let into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使知道秘密； If you let someone into a secret, you allow them to know it.
let off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 准许…不必做或不必工作； If someone in authority lets you off a task or duty, they give you permission not to do it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 对…宽大处理； If you let someone off , you give them a lighter punishment than they expect or no punishment at all.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使炸药等爆炸；开枪、炮等； let off If you let off an explosive or a gun, you explode or fire it.

letter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 信;信函； letter If you write a letter to someone, you write a message on paper and send it to them, usually by post.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 字母； letter Letters are written symbols which represent one of the sounds in a language.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 校队队衣的校名首字母标志以嘉许优秀运动员； letter If a student earns a letter in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.  /  [VERB 动词] 赢得佩戴校名首字母标志的荣誉； letter If a student letters in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.

level pegging: [ADJ 形容词] 不相伯仲的；势均力敌的； If two opponents in a competition or contest are level pegging , they are equal with each other.
lever: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 操作机械的杆，柄，把手； lever See also: gear lever ; A lever is a handle or bar that is attached to a piece of machinery and which you push or pull in order to operate the machinery.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 杠杆；撬棒； A lever is a long bar, one end of which is placed under a heavy object so that when you press down on the other end you can move the object.  /  [VERB 动词] 撬动；撬起；用力移动； lever If you lever something in a particular direction, you move it there, especially by using a lot of effort.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 用作施加压力等的手段，方法； lever A lever is an idea or action that you can use to make people do what you want them to do, rather than what they want to do.
leverage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 能够操控形势的影响力，手段，优势； leverage Leverage is the ability to influence situations or people so that you can control what happens.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 杠杆力；杠杆作用； leverage Leverage is the force that is applied to an object when something such as a lever is used.  /  [VERB 动词] 举债经营；为…融资； leveraged leverage To leverage a company or investment means to use borrowed money in order to buy it or pay for it.

levitate: [VERB 动词] 升空；悬浮；飘浮； levitate levitation If someone or something levitates , they appear to rise and float in the air without any support from other people or objects.

lexicon: [N-SING 单数名词] 某一学科、个人或群体的全部词汇； lexicon The lexicon of a particular subject is all the terms associated with it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 某一语言或学科的词汇表； A lexicon is an alphabetical list of the words in a language or the words associated with a particular subject.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指希腊语、希伯来语等古老语言的词典，字典； A lexicon is a dictionary, especially of a very old language such as Greek or Hebrew.

Libra: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 天秤宫，天秤座黄道十二宫之一。出生于9月23日至10月22日之间的人属此星座； Libra is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 出生于天秤宫时段的人； A Libra is a person whose sign of the zodiac is Libra.
librarian: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 图书馆馆长；图书馆管理员； A librarian is a person who is in charge of a library or who has been specially trained to work in a library.
library: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公共图书馆； library A public library is a building where things such as books, newspapers, videos, and music are kept for people to read, use, or borrow.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 私人收藏的图书或唱片等； library A private library is a collection of things such as books or music, that is normally only used with the permission of the owner.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 书房；书斋； library In some large houses the library is the room where most of the books are kept.

lice: [louse的复数] ； Lice is the plural of louse .
licence: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 执照; 证书; 许可证； licence A licence is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 放纵；放肆；无法无天； licence If you say that something gives someone licence or a licence to act in a particular way, you mean that it gives them an excuse to behave in an irresponsible or excessive way.  /  See also: poetic licence ;  /  [PHRASE 短语] 暴利的；一本万利的； licence If you describe a commercial activity as a licence to print money , you mean that it allows people to gain a lot of money with little effort or responsibility.
license: [VERB 动词] 批准；许可； license To license a person or activity means to give official permission for the person to do something or for the activity to take place.

lichen: [N-MASS 物质名词] 地衣； Lichen is a group of tiny plants that looks like moss and grows on the surface of things such as rocks, trees, and walls.

lido: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 露天游泳池；海滨浴场；海滨游乐场； A lido is an outdoor swimming pool or a part of a beach which is used by the public for swimming or water sports.

life-affirming: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 积极向上的；励志的； life-affirming A life-affirming activity or attitude emphasizes the positive aspects of life.

life cycle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生物的生活史，生活周期； life cycle The life cycle of an animal or plant is the series of changes and developments that it passes through from the beginning of its life until its death.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 想法、产品、组织等的存在周期； life cycle The life cycle of something such as an idea, product, or organization is the series of developments that take place in it from its beginning until the end of its usefulness.

life expectancy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 预期寿命；平均期望寿命； life expectancy The life expectancy of a person, animal, or plant is the length of time that they are normally likely to live.
life force: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 生命力； Life force is energy that some people believe exists in all living things and keeps them alive.
life form: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生物；活物；生命形式； A life form is any living thing such as an animal or plant.

life history: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 个人经历；生平； life history The life history of a person is all the things that happen to them during their life.

life insurance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人寿保险； life insurance Life insurance is a form of insurance in which a person makes regular payments to an insurance company, in return for a sum of money to be paid to them after a period of time, or to their family if they die.
life jacket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 救生衣； A life jacket is a sleeveless jacket which helps you to float when you have fallen into deep water.
lifeless: [ADJ 形容词] 死的；像死了一般的； lifeless If a person or animal is lifeless , they are dead, or are so still that they appear to be dead.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 无生命的； lifeless If you describe an object or a machine as lifeless , you mean that they are not living things, even though they may resemble living things.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无生物的； lifeless A lifeless place or area does not have anything living or growing there at all.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无生气的；沉闷的；单调的； lifeless If you describe a person, or something such as an artistic performance or a town as lifeless , you mean they lack any lively or exciting qualities.

lifeline: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生命线；命脉； lifeline A lifeline is something that enables an organization or group to survive or to continue with an activity.

light-hearted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻松愉快的；无忧无虑的； light-hearted Someone who is light-hearted is cheerful and happy.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不严肃的；随便的；为了好玩的； light-hearted Something that is light-hearted is intended to be entertaining or amusing, and not at all serious.
light heavyweight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 体重为160至175磅的轻重量级职业拳击手；体重为165至179磅的轻重量级业余拳击手； A light heavyweight is a professional boxer who weighs between 160 and 175 pounds, or an amateur boxer who weighs between 165 and 179 pounds.
lighthouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灯塔； A lighthouse is a tower containing a powerful flashing lamp that is built on the coast or on a small island.
light industry: [N-VAR 可变名词] 轻工业； Light industry is industry in which only small items are made, for example household goods and clothes.
lighting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 照明；灯光； lighting The lighting in a place is the way that it is lit, for example by electric lights, by candles, or by windows, or the quality of the light in it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 电影、戏剧等的布光，灯光； lighting The lighting in a film or play is the use of different electric lights to give a particular effect.
lightning: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 闪电； lightning See also: forked lightning ; Lightning is the very bright flashes of light in the sky that happen during thunderstorms.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 闪电似的；极快的； lightning Lightning describes things that happen very quickly or last for only a short time.
lightning bug: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 萤火虫； A lightning bug is a type of beetle that produces light from its body.
lightning conductor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 避雷针； A lightning conductor is a long thin piece of metal on top of a building that attracts lightning and allows it to reach the ground safely.
lightning rod: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同lightning conductor； A lightning rod is the same as a lightning conductor .  /  [PHRASE 短语] 招引…的人； lightning rod If you say that someone is a lightning rod for something, you mean that they attract that thing to themselves.
lightning strike: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 事先没有警告的闪电式罢工； lightning strike A lightning strike is a strike in which workers stop work suddenly and without any warning, in order to protest about something.
light on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 忽然注意到；突然发现； If you light on something or light upon it, you suddenly notice it or find it.
lightship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 导航用的灯船； A lightship is a small ship that stays in one place and has a powerful flashing lamp.
light up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 照亮；发亮； light up If you light something up or if it lights up , it becomes bright, usually when you shine light on it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 现出吃惊的神情；露出喜色； light up If your face or your eyes light up you suddenly look very surprised or happy.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 点烟；开始吸烟； If you light up , you make a cigarette, cigar, or pipe start burning and you start smoking it.
lightweight: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻量的；轻质的；比通常重量轻的； lightweight Something that is lightweight weighs less than most other things of the same type.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 拳击、柔道、赛艇等运动中的轻量级； lightweight 轻量级运动员 Lightweight is a category in some sports, such as boxing, judo, or rowing, based on the weight of the athlete.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无足轻重的人；无能的人； lightweight If you describe someone as a lightweight , you are critical of them because you think that they are not very important or skilful in a particular area of activity.
light year: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 光年指光在1年中所经过的距离； light year A light year is the distance that light travels in a year.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 极大的差距；极远的距离；极长的时期； light year You can say that two things are light years apart to emphasize a very great difference or a very long distance or period of time between them.
like: [PREP 介词] 像；像…一样； like If you say that one person or thing is like another, you mean that they share some of the same qualities or features.  /  [PREP 介词] 是…样的人或事物； like If you talk about what something or someone is like , you are talking about their qualities or features.  /  [PREP 介词] 比如；例如； like You can use like to introduce an example of the set of things or people that you have just mentioned.  /  [PREP 介词] 与…情形一样； like You can use like to say that someone or something is in the same situation as another person or thing.
-like: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] 与名词连用构成形容词表示“像…的”，“有…特征的”； -like -like combines with nouns to form adjectives which describe something as being similar to the thing referred to by the noun.
likeable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可爱的；讨人喜欢的； likeable Someone or something that is likeable is pleasant and easy to like.
likelihood: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 可能；可能性； likelihood The likelihood of something happening is how likely it is to happen.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 可能的事； likelihood If something is a likelihood , it is likely to happen.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 十之八九；极有可能； likelihood If you say that something will happen in all likelihood , you mean that it will probably happen.

like-minded: [ADJ 形容词] 想法相同的；志趣相投的； like-minded Like-minded people have similar opinions, ideas, attitudes, or interests.
liken: [VERB 动词] 把…比作；把…比拟为； liken If you liken one thing or person to another thing or person, you say that they are similar.
likeness: [N-SING 单数名词] 相像；相似； likeness If two things or people have a likeness to each other, they are similar to each other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肖像；画像；照片；塑像； likeness A likeness of someone is a picture or sculpture of them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 照片与本人的相似； likeness If you say that a picture of someone is a good likeness , you mean that it looks just like them.
likewise: [ADV 副词] 同样地；类似地； likewise You use likewise when you are comparing two methods, states, or situations and saying that they are similar.  /  [ADV 副词] 照样地； likewise If you do something and someone else does likewise , they do the same or a similar thing.
liking: [N-SING 单数名词] 喜爱；爱好；嗜好； liking If you have a liking for something or someone, you like them.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不合某人的意； liking If something is, for example, too fast for your liking , you would prefer it to be slower.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 合某人的意；对某人的胃口； liking If something is to your liking , it suits your interests, tastes, or wishes.
lilac: [N-VAR 可变名词] 丁香树； lilac 丁香花 A lilac or a lilac tree is a small tree which has sweet-smelling purple, pink, or white flowers in large, cone-shaped groups.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 丁香紫；淡紫色；淡雪青； lilac Something that is lilac is pale pinkish-purple in colour.
lilt: [N-SING 单数名词] 说话声调的欢快，抑扬顿挫； lilt If someone's voice has a lilt in it, the pitch of their voice rises and falls in a pleasant way, as if they were singing.
lilting: [ADJ 形容词] 说话声调或歌曲节奏欢快的； lilting A lilting voice or song rises and falls in pitch in a pleasant way.
lily: [N-VAR 可变名词] 百合； A lily is a plant with large flowers.
lily of the valley: [N-VAR 可变名词] 铃兰； Lily of the valley are small plants with large leaves and small, white, bell-shaped flowers.
lima bean: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 利马豆； Lima beans are flat round beans that are light green in colour and are eaten as a vegetable.
limb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肢；臂；腿； limb Your limbs are your arms and legs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 树枝； limb The limbs of a tree are its branches.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 冒着遭受失败或指责的风险；处于孤立无援的境地； limb If someone goes out on a limb , they do something they strongly believe in even though it is risky or extreme, and is likely to fail or be criticized by other people.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 撕裂…的肢体； limb If someone threatens to tear you limb from limb , they mean that they are extremely angry with you, and may use violence against you.
-limbed: [COMB in ADJ-GRADED ] 与形容词连用构成形容词表示“有…肢的”； -limbed -limbed combines with adjectives to form other adjectives which indicate that a person or animal has limbs of a particular type or appearance.
limber up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 比赛等前做准备活动，热身； limber up If you limber up , you prepare for an energetic physical activity such as a sport by moving and stretching your body.
limbo: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不确定的状态； limbo If you say that someone or something is in limbo , you mean that they are in a situation where they seem to be caught between two stages and it is unclear what will happen next.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 林波舞西印度群岛的一种舞蹈，舞者需后仰，从离地越来越近的杆下通过； The limbo is a West Indian dance in which you have to pass under a low bar while leaning backwards.
lime: [N-VAR 可变名词] 酸橙； lime A lime is a green fruit that tastes like a lemon.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 酸橙味饮料； lime Lime is a drink that tastes of limes.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 欧椴树； lime A lime is a large tree with pale green leaves.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 石灰； lime 亦可用于构词 Lime is a substance containing calcium.
lime green: [COLOUR 颜色词] 酸橙绿；暗黄绿色； lime green Something that is lime green is light yellowish-green in colour.
limelight: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 公众注意的中心； limelight If someone is in the limelight , a lot of attention is being paid to them, because they are famous or because they have done something very unusual or exciting.
limerick: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 五行打油诗； A limerick is a humorous poem which has five lines.
limestone: [N-MASS 物质名词] 灰岩；石灰岩； limestone Limestone is a whitish-coloured rock which is used for building and for making cement.
limey: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有些美国人对英国人的称呼英国佬一些人认为此用法具冒犯意味； Some Americans refer to British people as limeys .
limit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 极限； limit A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 特定的限期，限额，限度； limit A limit of a particular kind is the largest or smallest amount of something such as time or money that is allowed because of a rule, law, or decision.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 区域的界限； limit The limit of an area is its boundary or edge.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 可能行动或结果的范围； limit The limits of a situation are the facts involved in it which make only some actions or results possible.
limitation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 限制；控制； limitation The limitation of something is the act or process of controlling or reducing it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 起限制作用的规则或决定； limitation A limitation on something is a rule or decision which prevents that thing from growing or extending beyond certain limits.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 能力的局限； limitation If you talk about the limitations of someone or something, you mean that they can only do some things and not others, or cannot do something very well.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 限制性事实或情形； limitation A limitation is a fact or situation that allows only some actions and makes others impossible.
limited: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有限的；有限度的； limited Something that is limited is not very great in amount, range, or degree.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 公司有限责任的； limited A limited company is one whose owners are legally responsible for only a part of any money that it may owe if it goes bankrupt.
limited edition: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 限量版； A limited edition is a work of art, such as a book which is only produced in very small numbers, so that each one will be valuable in the future.
limitless: [ADJ 形容词] 无限的；无穷无尽的； limitless If you describe something as limitless , you mean that there is or appears to be so much of it that it will never be exhausted.
limo: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同limousine； limo A limo is a limousine .
limousine: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常由专职司机驾驶的大型高级轿车，豪华轿车； A limousine is a large and very comfortable car.
limp: [VERB 动词] 一瘸一拐地走；跛行；蹒跚； limp If a person or animal limps , they walk with difficulty or in an uneven way because one of their legs or feet is hurt.  /  [VERB 动词] 进展缓慢；艰难地行进； limp If you say that something such as an organization, process, or vehicle limps along , you mean that it continues slowly or with difficulty, for example because it has been weakened or damaged.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 软弱的；无力的； limp limply If you describe something as limp , you mean that it is soft or weak when it should be firm or strong.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 四肢无力的；身体一动不动的； limp If someone is limp , their body has no strength and is not moving, for example because they are asleep or unconscious.
limpet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 紧紧附着在岩石上的虫戚； A limpet is a small sea animal with a cone-shaped shell which attaches itself tightly to rocks.
limpid: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 清澈的；透明的； limpid If you say that something is limpid , you mean that it is very clear and transparent.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 清晰的；畅达的； limpid If you describe speech, writing, or music as limpid , you like it because it is clear, simple and flowing.
linchpin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 关键；关键性人物或事物； If you refer to a person or thing as the linchpin of something, you mean that they are the most important person or thing involved in it.
linden: [N-VAR 可变名词] 椴树； A linden or a linden tree is a large tree with pale green leaves which is often planted in parks in towns and cities.
line: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 线条； line A line is a long thin mark which is drawn or painted on a surface.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指脸部的皱纹，纹路； line The lines on some-one's skin, especially on their face, are long thin marks that appear there as they grow older.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 排成的行，列； line A line of people or things is a number of them arranged one behind the other or side by side.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人、车辆等在等候时排成的队，队伍； line A line of people or vehicles is a number of them that are waiting one behind another, for example in order to buy something or to go in a particular direction.
lineage: [N-VAR 可变名词] 家系；家族；血统； lineage Someone's lineage is the series of families from which they are directly descended.
lineal: [ADJ 形容词] 直系的； A lineal descendant of a particular person or family is someone in a later generation who is directly related to them.
linear: [ADJ 形容词] 过程或发展线性的； linear A linear process or development is one in which something changes or progresses straight from one stage to another, and has a starting point and an ending point.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 线构的；利用线条的； linear A linear shape or form consists of straight lines.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 运动或力成一直线的，沿直线的； Linear movement or force occurs in a straight line rather than in a curve.

lined: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有皱纹的； lined If someone's face or skin is lined , it has lines on it as a result of old age, tiredness, worry, or illness.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 纸张画有横线的； Lined paper has lines printed across it to help you write neatly.  /  See also: line ; �

line drawing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 线条画； A line drawing is a drawing which consists only of lines.
line manager: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 部门经理； Your line manager is the person at work who is in charge of your department, group, or project.
linen: [N-MASS 物质名词] 亚麻布；亚麻织品； linen Linen is a kind of cloth that is made from a plant called flax.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 桌布、床单、枕套等家庭日用织品； linen Linen is tablecloths, sheets, pillowcases, and similar things made of cloth that are used in the home.  /  to wash your dirty linen in public » see: dirty �

line of vision: [N-SING 单数名词] 同line of sight； line of vision Your line of vision is the same as your line of sight .
liner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指度假时乘坐的邮轮，客轮； liner See also: bin liner ; A liner is a large ship in which people travel long distances, especially on holiday.
liner note: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 唱片封套上的内容简介，小段说明文字； The liner notes on record jackets are short pieces of writing that tell you something about the record or the musicians playing on the record.

line up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使某一批人排成行；使列队； If people line up or if you line them up , they move so that they are standing in a line.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使某一批物排列成行； line up If you line things up , you move them into a straight row.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-RECIP-ERG ] 使对齐； line up If you line one thing up with another, or one thing lines up with another, the first thing is moved into its correct position in relation to the second.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 组织；邀集； If you line up an event or activity, you arrange for it to happen.

linger: [VERB 动词] 继续存留； linger When something such as an idea, feeling, or illness lingers , it continues to exist for a long time, often much longer than expected.  /  [VERB 动词] 留恋；不愿离开；继续逗留； linger If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.
lingerie: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 女式贴身内衣裤；女内衣；女睡衣； Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes.
lingo: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指不会说或听不懂的外国语，外国话； lingo People sometimes refer to a foreign language, especially one that they do not speak or understand, as a lingo .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 行话；隐语； lingo A lingo is a range of words or a style of language which is used in a particular situation or by a particular group of people.
