Main Street: [N-PROPER 专有名词] (美国小城镇的)大街，主街； In small towns in the United States, the street where most of the shops are is often called Main Street .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 新闻用语，指居住在小城镇的或并不富裕的普通大众，老百姓； Main Street is used by journalists to refer to the ordinary people of America who live in small towns rather than big cities or are not very rich.
maintain: [VERB 动词] 维持;保持； maintain If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.  /  [VERB 动词] 断言;宣称;坚称； maintain If you say that someone maintains that something is true, you mean that they have stated their opinion strongly but not everyone agrees with them or believes them.  /  [VERB 动词] 保持，维持在某一比率或水平上； maintain If you maintain something at a particular rate or level, you keep it at that rate or level.  /  [VERB 动词] 维修;保养； maintain If you maintain a road, building, vehicle, or machine, you keep it in good condition by regularly checking it and repairing it when necessary.
maintenance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 对建筑物、道路、机器等的定期维修，检修，保养； maintenance The maintenance of a building, vehicle, road, or machine is the process of keeping it in good condition by regularly checking it and repairing it when necessary.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 赡养费；生活费； maintenance Maintenance is money that someone gives regularly to another person to pay for the things that the person needs.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 状态、进程等的维持，保持； maintenance If you ensure the maintenance of a state or process, you make sure that it continues.
maisonette: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公寓套房大多为两层，带独立门栋； maisonette A maisonette is a flat that usually has a separate door to the outside from other flats in the same building.
maize: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 玉米;玉蜀黍； maize Maize is a tall plant which produces long objects covered with yellow seeds called sweetcorn.
Maj: (书面缩略 =)  Maj when it is used as a title.
majestic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 壮丽的;庄严的;雄伟的； majestic majestically If you describe something or someone as majestic , you think they are very beautiful, dignified, and impressive.
majesty: [N-VOC 称呼名词] 陛下(对国王或王后的尊称)； You use majesty in expressions such as Your Majesty or Her Majesty when you are addressing or referring to a King or Queen.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 壮观;庄严;雄伟； majesty Majesty is the quality of being beautiful, dignified, and impressive.
major: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 较重要的;较重大的;主要的； major You use major when you want to describe something that is more important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.  /  [N-COUNT; N-TITLE; N-VOC] [可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词] (英国)陆军(或海军陆战队)少校;(美国)陆军(或空军、海军陆战队)少校； major A major is an officer who is one rank above captain in the British army or the United States army, air force, or marines.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (美国大学中的)主修课程，专业； major At a university or college in the United States, a student's major is the main subject that they are studying.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (美国大学中)主修…的学生，…专业的学生； major At a university or college in the United States, if a student is, for example, a geology major , geology is the main subject they are studying.
majorette: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乐队女队长;乐队女指挥； A majorette is one of a group of girls or young women who march at the front of a musical band in a procession.
major general: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE; N-VOC] [可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词] (英国)陆军少将;(美国)陆军(或空军、海军陆战队)少将； In Britain, a major general is a senior officer in the army, one rank above a brigadier.
majority: [N-SING-COLL 单数集合名词] 多数;大多数； majority 占多数；拥有多数；过半数 The majority of people or things in a group is more than half of them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 多数票;超过对方的票数； majority A majority is the difference between the number of votes or seats in parliament or legislature that the winner gets in an election, and the number of votes or seats that the next person or party gets.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (观点、决定、体制等)多数人支持的，多数人拥护的； majority Majority is used to describe opinions, decisions, and systems of government that are supported by more than half the people involved.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 法定成年年龄(英国和美国大多数州规定为18周岁)； majority Majority is the state of legally being an adult.
major league: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 职业体育总会;(尤指美国)职业棒球联合会，职业棒球大联盟； major league The major leagues are groups of professional sports teams that compete against each other, especially in American baseball.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 职业棒球联合会的； major league Major league means connected with the major leagues in baseball.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 重要的;成功的； Major league people or institutions are important or successful.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 跻身成功人士行列； major league If someone moves into the major league or makes it into the major league , they become very successful in their career.
make: Make is used in a large number of expressions which are explained under other words in this dictionary.  /  [VERB 动词] (与大量名词连用，表示做动作、说某事等)做出，作出； make You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something.  /  [VERB 动词] (与某些名词连用)把…做好，把…搞糟； make You can use make with certain nouns to indicate that someone does something well or badly.  /  [VERB 动词] 摆出…的姿态;做出…的样子； If you make as if to do something or make to do something, you behave in a way that makes it seem that you are just about to do it.
make-believe: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 虚构；虚幻； make-believe If someone is living in a make-believe world, they are pretending that things are better, different, or more exciting than they really are instead of facing up to reality.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 孩子们玩的假装，假扮游戏； make-believe You use make-believe to refer to the activity involved when a child plays a game in which they pretend something, for example that they are someone else.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 虚假的;虚幻的;虚构的;假装的； make-believe You use make-believe to describe things, for example in a play or film, that imitate or copy something real, but which are not what they appear to be.
make for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 向…走去;朝…前进； If you make for a place, you move towards it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 导致;有利于； If something makes for another thing, it causes or helps to cause that thing to happen or exist.
make of: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 理解;看待； make of If you ask a person what they make of something, you want to know what their impression, opinion, or understanding of it is.
make off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 匆忙离开;逃走； If you make off , you leave somewhere as quickly as possible, often in order to escape.
make off with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 偷走;拿走； If you make off with something, you steal it and take it away with you.
make out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 勉强地辨认出，看出，听出； make out If you make something out , you manage with difficulty to see or hear it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…弄清楚;理解;明白； make out If you try to make something out , you try to understand it or decide whether or not it is true.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 力图说成;努力证明； make out If you make out that something is the case or make something out to be the case, you try to cause people to believe that it is the case.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 举例证明…是最好的);证实[…是对的； make out If you make out a case for something, you try to establish or prove that it is the best thing to do.
make over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 依法转让所有权； If you make something over to someone, you legally transfer the ownership of it to them.
makeover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指通过专业人士作出的外表的改观，美容，改头换面； makeover If a person or room is given a makeover , their appearance is improved, usually by an expert.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 重大改造；革新； makeover If an organization or system is given a makeover , important changes are made in order to improve it.
maker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生产商;制造商； maker The maker of a product is the firm that manufactures it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 制造者;制作人； maker You can refer to the person who makes something as its maker .  /  See also: peacemaker ; �
makeshift: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 权宜的;临时凑合的； makeshift Makeshift things are temporary and usually of poor quality, but they are used because there is nothing better available.
make up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 组成;构成； make up The people or things that make up something are the members or parts that form that thing.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 编造;虚构； make up If you make up something such as a story or excuse, you invent it, sometimes in order to deceive people.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 给…化妆;为…打扮； make up If you make yourself up or if someone else makes you up , make-up such as powder or lipstick is put on your face.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 凑足;补齐； If you make up an amount, you add something to it so that it is as large as it should be.
makeup: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 化妆品； makeup Make-up consists of things such as lipstick, eye shadow, and powder which some women put on their faces to make themselves look more attractive or which actors use to change or improve their appearance.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 天性;性格； makeup Some-one's make-up is their nature and the various qualities in their character.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 组成成分;构成方式； The make-up of something consists of its different parts and the way these parts are arranged.
make-up: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 化妆品； make-up Make-up consists of things such as lipstick, eye shadow, and powder which some women put on their faces to make themselves look more attractive or which actors use to change or improve their appearance.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 天性;性格； Some-one's make-up is their nature and the various qualities in their character.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 组成成分;构成方式； make-up The make-up of something consists of its different parts and the way these parts are arranged.
make up for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 弥补;补足； make up for To make up for a bad experience or the loss of something means to make the situation better or make the person involved happier.
make up to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 尤指因自己的过失向…弥补，补偿； If you say that you will make it up to someone, you are promising that you will do something good for them after they have been upset or disappointed, especially by you.
makeweight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 凑数的人[或物]; 无关紧要的人或物； makeweight If you describe someone or something as a makeweight , you think that they are not good or valuable and that they have been included in an activity in order to fill up a gap.
making: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 制作;制造;形成； making The making of something is the act or process of producing or creating it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 在成长中;在形成中； making If you describe a person or thing as something in the making , you mean that they are going to become known or recognized as that thing.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 是…成功(或改善)的原因； making If something is the making of a person or thing, it is the reason that they become successful or become very much better than they used to be.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 具备成为…的素质(或内在因素、必要条件、潜在能力)； making If you say that a person or thing has the makings of something, you mean it seems possible or likely that they will become that thing, as they have the necessary qualities.
mal-: [PREFIX 前缀] (用于某些词之前构成新词)表示“坏”，“不良”，“不当”； Mal- is added to words in order to form new words which describe things that are bad or unpleasant, or that are unsuccessful or imperfect.
maladjusted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 心理失调的;不能适应环境的;适应不良的； maladjusted If you describe a child as maladjusted , you mean that they have psychological problems and behave in a way which is not acceptable to society.
maladministration: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 管理不善;执行不公;弊政； maladministration Maladministration is the act or process of running a system or organization incorrectly.
maladroit: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不灵巧的;笨拙的;迟钝的;不老练的； maladroit If you describe someone as maladroit , you mean that they are clumsy or handle situations badly.
malady: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 病；疾病； malady A malady is an illness or disease.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (书面语中，指社会、环境等的)严重问题，弊病，弊端； In written English, people sometimes use maladies to refer to serious problems in a society or situation.
malaise: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (社会或群体的)痼疾； malaise Malaise is a state in which there is something wrong with a society or group, for which there does not seem to be a quick or easy solution.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不适;不安;不快； malaise Malaise is a state in which people feel dissatisfied or unhappy but feel unable to change, usually because they do not know what is wrong.
malaria: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 疟疾； Malaria is a serious disease carried by mosquitoes which causes periods of fever.
malarial: [ADJ 形容词] 疟疾的；患疟疾的；地区感染疟疾的； malarial You can use malarial to refer to things connected with malaria or areas which are affected by malaria.
Malay: [ADJ 形容词] 马来西亚的;马来人的;马来语的;马来文化的； Malay Malay means belonging or relating to the people, language, or culture of the largest racial group in Malaysia.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 马来人； Malay A Malay is a member of the largest racial group in Malaysia.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 马来语； Malay is a language that is spoken in Malaysia and in parts of Indonesia.
Malaysian: [ADJ 形容词] 马来西亚的;马来西亚人的； Malaysian 马来西亚人 Something that is Malaysian belongs or relates to Malaysia or to its people.
malcontent: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不满现状者； malcontent You can describe people as malcontents when you disapprove of the fact that they are dissatisfied with a situation and want it to change.
male: [ADJ 形容词] 男人的;男性的； male maleness Someone who is male is a man or a boy.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男子;男性； male Men and boys are sometimes referred to as males when they are being considered as a type.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 男人的;男性的； male Male means relating, belonging, or affecting men rather than women.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雄性； male You can refer to any creature that belongs to the sex that cannot lay eggs or have babies as a male .
male chauvinism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 大男子主义;大男子作风； If you accuse a man of male chauvinism , you disapprove of him because his beliefs and behaviour show that he thinks men are naturally superior to women.
male chauvinist: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 态度、言语等大男子主义的； male chauvinist 大男子主义者 If you describe an attitude or remark as male chauvinist , you are critical of it because you think it is based on the belief that men are naturally superior to women.
male-dominated: [ADJ 形容词] 在社会、机构或某活动领域等男人主宰的，男权占主导地位的； male-dominated A male-dominated society, organization, or area of activity is one in which men have most of the power and influence.
malefactor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 罪犯;坏人； malefactor A malefactor is someone who has done something bad or illegal.
malevolent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 狠毒的;恶毒的；存心不良的； malevolent malevolence malevolently A malevolent person deliberately tries to cause harm or evil.
malformation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指天生的畸形； malformation A malformation in a person's body is a part which does not have the proper shape or form, especially when it has been like this since birth.
malformed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 尤指先天性的畸形的，变形的，残缺的； malformed If people or parts of their body are malformed , they do not have the shape or form that they are supposed to, especially when they have been like this since birth.
malfunction: [VERB 动词] 机器失灵，出故障；人体器官机能失常，出现功能障碍； malfunction If a machine or part of the body malfunctions , it fails to work properly.
malice: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恶意;怨恨； malice Malice is behaviour that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.
malicious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 心怀恶意的;恶毒的;怀恨的； malicious maliciously If you describe someone's words or actions as malicious , you mean that they are intended to harm people or their reputation, or cause them embarrassment and upset.
malign: [VERB 动词] 诽谤;中伤;污蔑； malign If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有害的;不良的； malign If something is malign , it causes harm.  /  See also: much-maligned ; �
malignancy: [N-VAR 可变名词] 恶性肿瘤或疾病； malignancy A tumour or disease in a state of malignancy is out of control and is likely to cause death.
malignant: [ADJ 形容词] (肿瘤或疾病)恶性的； malignant A malignant tumour or disease is out of control and likely to cause death.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人恶意的，恶毒的； malignant If you say that someone is malignant , you think they are cruel and like to cause harm.
malinger: [VERB 动词] 为逃避工作而装病； malinger If someone is malingering , they pretend to be ill in order to avoid working.
mall: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 封闭式大型购物区，购物中心； A mall is a very large enclosed shopping area.
mallard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绿头鸭一种常见野鸭； A mallard is a kind of wild duck which is very common.
malleable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人温顺的，易受影响的，顺从的； malleable If you say that someone is malleable , you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 材料柔软的，可锻的，可塑的，有延展性的； malleable A substance that is malleable is soft and can easily be made into different shapes.
mallet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 木锤； A mallet is a wooden hammer with a square head.
mall rat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 喜欢结伴逛商场的年轻人;逛街狂； mall rat Mall rats are young people who spend a lot of time hanging around in shopping malls with their friends.
malnourished: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 营养不良的；营养失调的； malnourished If someone is malnourished , they are physically weak because they do not eat enough food or do not eat the right kind of food.
malnutrition: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 营养不良；营养失调； malnutrition If someone is suffering from malnutrition , they are physically weak and extremely thin because they have not eaten enough food.
malodorous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 恶臭的;难闻的； malodorous Something that is malodorous has an unpleasant smell.
malpractice: [N-VAR 可变名词] 营私舞弊;玩忽职守;渎职； malpractice If you accuse someone of malpractice , you are accusing them of breaking the law or the rules of their profession in order to gain some advantage for themselves.
malt: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 用以酿制威士忌、啤酒和其他酒类的麦芽； malt Malt is a substance made from grain that has been soaked in water and then dried in a hot oven.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 同 malt whisky； Malt is the same as malt whisky .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (用麦乳精与其他调味品制成的)麦乳精饮料； A malt is a drink made from malted milk and sometimes other flavourings.
malted: [ADJ 形容词] (大麦)被制成麦芽的； Malted barley has been soaked in water and then dried in a hot oven.
malted milk: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麦乳精；麦乳精饮料； Malted milk is a drink made from hot or cold milk flavoured with a powder containing malt.
Maltese: [ADJ 形容词] 马耳他的;马耳他人的;马耳他语或文化的； Maltese Maltese means belonging or relating to Malta, or to its people, language, or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 马耳他人； A Maltese is a Maltese citizen, or a person of Maltese origin.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 马耳他语； Maltese is a language spoken by people who live in Malta.
maltreat: [VERB 动词] 虐待;粗暴对待； maltreat If a person or animal is maltreated , they are treated badly, especially by being hurt.
maltreatment: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 对人或动物的虐待;粗暴的对待； maltreatment Maltreatment is cruel behaviour, especially involving hurting a person or animal.
malt whisky: [N-MASS 物质名词] 麦芽威士忌酒； malt whisky 一杯麦芽威士忌酒 Malt whisky or malt is whisky that is made from malt.
mam: [N-FAMILY 家庭成员名词] 妈妈； Mam is used to mean mother.
mama: [N-FAMILY 家庭成员名词] 同mother； Mama means the same as mother .  /  » see: mamma �
mamma: [N-FAMILY 家庭成员名词] 同mother； Mamma means the same as mother .
mammal: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 哺乳动物； Mammals are animals such as humans, dogs, lions, and whales.
mammalian: [ADJ 形容词] 哺乳类的；哺乳动物的； mammalian In zoology, mammalian means relating to mammals.
mammary: [ADJ 形容词] 乳房的； mammary Mammary means relating to the breasts.

Mammon: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 拜金;贪财； Mammon You can use Mammon to refer to money and business activities if you want to show your disapproval of people who think that becoming rich is the most important thing in life.
mammoth: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 改变巨大的，重大的；任务庞大的，艰巨的； mammoth You can use mammoth to emphasize that a task or change is very large and needs a lot of effort to achieve.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 猛犸，毛象一种史前动物； A mammoth was an animal like an elephant, with very long tusks and long hair, that lived a long time ago but no longer exists.

man: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男人;男子； man A man is an adult male human being.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 人，人类此用法仍有争议； man Man and men are sometimes used to refer to all human beings, including both males and females.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有某类嗜好的人； man If you say that a man is, for example, a gambling man or an outdoors man , you mean that he likes gambling or outdoor activities.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 来自某地的人；在某地上过学的人； man If you say that a man is, for example, a London man or an Oxford man , you mean that he comes from London or Oxford, or went to university there.
-man: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] (与数词连用构成形容词，表示人数) ； -man -man combines with numbers to make adjectives which indicate that something involves or is intended for that number of people.
manacle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 手铐;脚镣;镣铐； Manacles are metal devices attached to a prisoner's wrists or legs in order to prevent him or her from moving or escaping.  /  [VERB 动词] 给囚犯上手铐或脚镣； manacle If a prisoner is manacled , their wrists or legs are put in manacles in order to prevent them from moving or escaping.
manage: [VERB 动词] 管理;经营;掌管； manage If you manage an organization, business, or system, or the people who work in it, you are responsible for controlling them.  /  [VERB 动词] 谨慎地使用，好好地利用(时间、金钱等)； manage If you manage time, money, or other resources, you deal with them carefully and do not waste them.  /  [VERB 动词] 设法做到;成功完成； manage If you manage to do something, especially something difficult, you succeed in doing it.  /  [VERB 动词] 成功对付;设法应对； manage If you manage , you succeed in coping with a difficult situation.
manageable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 容易管理的;容易对付的； manageable Something that is manageable is of a size, quantity, or level of difficulty that people are able to deal with.
management: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 商务或机构的管理，经营； management Management is the control and organizing of a business or other organization.  /  [N-VAR-COLL 可变集合名词] 资方;管理部门;经营者； management You can refer to the people who control and organize a business or other organization as the management .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 管理;安排;驾驭； management Management is the way people control different parts of their lives.
management consultant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (公司聘请的)管理咨询顾问； management consultant A management consultant is someone whose job is to advise companies on the most efficient ways to run their business.
manager: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 经理;管理人； manager A manager is a person who is responsible for running part of or the whole of a business organization.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (明星、艺人等的)经纪人，业务管理人； The manager of a pop star or other entertainer is the person who looks after their business interests.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (球队的)主教练(在美国英语中，该词只用于棒球球队，其他运动则用 coach 一词指主教练)； The manager of a sports team is the person responsible for training the players and organizing the way they play.
manageress: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女经理，女管理人[有些女性更愿意被称为manager] ； manageress The manageress of a shop, restaurant, or other small business is the woman who is responsible for running it.
managerial: [ADJ 形容词] 经理的;管理上的;经营上的； managerial Managerial means relating to the work of a manager.
managing director: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 总裁，总经理[缩略形式为MD] ； The managing director of a company is the most important working director, and is in charge of the way the company is managed.
mandarin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 新闻用语政界要人，政府高官； mandarin Journalists sometimes use mandarin to refer to someone who has an important job in the Civil Service.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 汉语普通话； Mandarin is the commonly-used language of China.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 柑橘； A mandarin or a mandarin orange is a small orange whose skin comes off easily.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (中国古代的)官僚，大臣； A mandarin was, in former times, an important government official in China.
mandate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (政府或经选举组建的机构的)授权，委托； mandate If a government or other elected body has a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they have the authority to carry it out as a result of winning an election or vote.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 授权;委托;委任； mandate If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 任期；在任期；统治期； mandate You can refer to the fixed length of time that a country's leader or government remains in office as their mandate .  /  [VERB 动词] 授权;委任； mandate When someone is mandated to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.
mandatory: [ADJ 形容词] 强制性的; 法定的;义务的； mandatory If an action or procedure is mandatory , people have to do it, because it is a rule or a law.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (惩罚)强制性的，法定的； mandatory If a crime carries a mandatory punishment, that punishment is fixed by law for all cases, in contrast to crimes for which the judge or magistrate has to decide the punishment for each particular case.
mandible: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (人、动物的)下颌骨； A mandible is the bone in the lower jaw of a person or animal.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (昆虫的)颚； An insect's mandibles are the two parts of its mouth which it uses for biting, similar to an animal's jaws.
mandolin: [N-VAR 可变名词] 曼陀林(外形类似小吉他，有四组金属弦的乐器)； A mandolin is a musical instrument that looks like a small guitar and has four pairs of strings.
mane: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (马或狮子的)鬃毛； The mane on a horse or lion is the long thick hair that grows from its neck.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 浓密的头发； mane If you refer to a person's hair as their mane , you mean that they have a lot of hair.
man-eating: [ADJ 形容词] 吃人的;食人的； man-eating A man-eating animal is one that has killed and eaten human beings, or that people think might do so.
manfully: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 尤指男人英勇地;果断地； manfully If you say that someone, especially a man, does something manfully , you mean that they do it in a very determined or brave way.
manganese: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 锰； Manganese is a greyish-white metal that is used in making steel.
manger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (牛、马等的)食槽； A manger is a low open container which cows, horses, and other animals feed from when indoors.
mangetout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 糖荚豌豆一种荚和豆均可吃的豌豆； Mangetout are a type of pea whose pods are eaten as well as the peas inside them.
mangle: [VERB 动词] 毁坏;损坏;使残缺不全； mangle If a physical object is mangled , it is crushed or twisted very forcefully, so that it is difficult to see what its original shape was.  /  [VERB 动词] 因发音、书写错误或表达不清晰而扭曲，改变词语、信息的意思； mangle If you say that someone mangles words or information, you are criticizing them for not speaking or writing clearly or correctly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (旧时由两个木制滚筒辗压衣服的) 轧干机，脱水机； A mangle is an old-fashioned machine for removing water from clothes that have been washed.
mango: [N-VAR 可变名词] 芒果； mango 芒果树 A mango is a large sweet yellowish fruit which grows on a tree in hot countries.
mangrove: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 红树(生长于热带国家的沿海或江河之畔，其须根高于地面)； mangrove A mangrove or mangrove tree is a tree with roots which are above the ground and that grows along coasts or on the banks of large rivers in hot countries.
mangy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 动物肮脏的，患病的，无人看管的，邋遢的； mangy A mangy animal looks dirty, uncared for or ill.
manhandle: [VERB 动词] 粗暴地对待;推搡； manhandle If someone is manhandled , they are physically held or pushed, for example when they are being taken somewhere.  /  [VERB 动词] 用人力搬动大或重的物体； manhandle If you manhandle something big or heavy somewhere, you move it there by hand.
manhole: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (位于街面，盖有金属盖，供工人检修、疏浚下水道时出入的)出入孔，检修孔，人孔； A manhole is a large hole in a road or path, covered by a metal plate that can be removed.
manhood: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (男性的)成年期，成人； manhood Manhood is the state of being a man rather than a boy.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (男人的)成年期； manhood Manhood is the period of a man's life during which he is a man rather than a boy.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (总称)男人，男子； manhood If you refer to American manhood or French manhood for example, you are referring to American men or French men considered as a group.
man-hour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 工时(每人每小时的工作量)； man-hour A man-hour is the average amount of work that one person can do in an hour.
manhunt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对逃亡者或失踪者的)追捕，追踪； A manhunt is a major search for someone who has escaped or disappeared.
mania: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 狂热;癖好； mania If you say that a person or group has a mania for something, you mean that they enjoy it very much or spend a lot of time on it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 躁狂症； mania Mania is a mental illness which causes the sufferer to become very worried or concerned about something.
maniac: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 疯子;狂人； maniac A maniac is a mad person who is violent and dangerous.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 极其愚蠢的;疯狂的； maniac If you describe someone's behaviour as maniac , you are emphasizing that it is extremely foolish and uncontrolled.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (宗教或体育的)狂热分子，过激分子； maniac If you call someone, for example, a religious maniac or a sports maniac , you are critical of them because they have such a strong interest in religion or sport.
maniacal: [ADJ 形容词] 行为极端的，疯狂的，狂躁的； maniacal maniacally If you describe someone's behaviour as maniacal , you mean that it is extreme, violent, or very determined, as if the person were insane.
manic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 发狂的;狂躁的;非常激动的； manic manically If you describe someone as manic , you mean that they do things extremely quickly or energetically, often because they are very excited or anxious about something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 微笑、笑声或幽默过度的，失常的； manic If you describe someone's smile, laughter, or sense of humour as manic , you mean that it seems excessive or strange, as if they were insane.
manic-depressive: [ADJ 形容词] (躁狂和抑郁交替发作的)狂躁抑郁症的，患躁郁症的； manic-depressive 狂躁抑郁症患者 If someone is manic-depressive , they have a medical condition in which they sometimes feel excited and confident and at other times very depressed.
manicure: [VERB 动词] 修指甲;美甲;手部护理； manicure If you manicure your hands or nails, you care for them by softening your skin and cutting and polishing your nails.
manicured: [ADJ 形容词] 草坪、花园修剪整齐的； manicured A manicured lawn, park, or garden has very short neatly cut grass.
manicurist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 指甲美容师;美甲师； A manicurist is a person whose job is mani-curing people's hands and nails.
manifest: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 明显的;显而易见的； manifest manifestly If you say that something is manifest , you mean that it is clearly true and that nobody would disagree with it if they saw it or considered it.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 显示;显露； manifest If you manifest a particular quality, feeling, or illness, or if it manifests itself , it becomes visible or obvious.
manifestation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 表现;显示;表示； manifestation A manifestation of something is one of the different ways in which it can appear.
manifesto: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指政党或政府的宣言，声明； manifesto A manifesto is a statement published by a person or group of people, especially a political party, or a government, in which they say what their aims and policies are.
manifold: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 多样的;各种各样的； manifold Things that are manifold are of many different kinds.
manila: [ADJ 形容词] 马尼拉纸的； A manila envelope or folder is made from a strong paper that is usually light brown.
manipulate: [VERB 动词] 摆布，操纵，控制(他人)； manipulate manipulation If you say that someone manipulates people, you disapprove of them because they skilfully force or persuade people to do what they want.  /  [VERB 动词] 摆布，操纵，处理(事件或局势)； manipulate manipulation If you say that someone manipulates an event or situation, you disapprove of them because they use or control it for their own benefit, or cause it to develop in the way they want.  /  [VERB 动词] 操作; 使用； manipulate manipulation If you manipulate something that requires skill, such as a complicated piece of equipment or a difficult idea, you operate it or process it.  /  [VERB 动词] 使脱臼复位;用推拿术治疗； manipulate manipulation If someone manipulates your bones or muscles, they skilfully move and press them with their hands in order to push the bones into their correct position or make the muscles less stiff.
manipulative: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 操纵的;控制的;善于摆布他人的； manipulative If you describe someone as manipulative , you disapprove of them because they skilfully force or persuade people to act in the way that they want.
manipulator: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 善于操控者;善于左右时局的人； manipulator If you describe someone as a manipulator , you mean that they skilfully control events, situations, or people, often in a way that other people disapprove of.
mankind: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人，人类该用法存有争议； mankind You can refer to all human beings as mankind when considering them as a group.
manly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有男子气概的;阳刚的； manly manliness If you describe a man's behaviour or appearance as manly , you approve of it because it shows qualities that are considered typical of a man, such as strength or courage.
man-made: [ADJ 形容词] 人造的;人工的;人为的； man-made Man-made things are created or caused by people, rather than occurring naturally.
man management: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人员管理;人力管理； Man management involves controlling and organizing the people who work in a business or organization.
manna: [PHRASE 短语] 天赐之物;(从天而降的)恩赐； manna If you say that something unexpected is manna from heaven , you mean that it is good and happened just at the time that it was needed.
manned: [ADJ 形容词] 载人的;由人操纵的； manned See also: man ; A manned vehicle such as a spacecraft has people in it who are operating its controls.
mannequin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指商店橱窗中用以展示服装的人体模型； A mannequin is a life-sized model of a person which is used to display clothes, especially in shop windows.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] [尤指T台或平面] 时装模特； A mannequin is a person who displays clothes, hats, or shoes by wearing them, especially in fashion shows or in fashion photographs.
manner: [N-SING 单数名词] 做法;方式； manner The manner in which you do something is the way that you do it.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 用…的方式;以…的风格； manner If something is done in the manner of something else, it is done in the style of that thing.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 态度;举止； manner -mannered Someone's manner is the way in which they behave and talk when they are with other people, for example whether they are polite, confident, or bad-tempered.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 有礼貌/没礼貌； manner If someone has good manners , they are polite and observe social customs.
mannered: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 矫揉造作的;不自然的;做作的； mannered If you describe some-one's behaviour or a work of art as mannered , you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有礼貌的;彬彬有礼的； mannered Mannered behaviour is polite and observes social customs.
mannerism: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 某人特有的说话或动作的习性，习气，习惯； mannerism Someone's mannerisms are the gestures or ways of speaking which are very characteristic of them, and which they often use.
mannish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (女人)男人似的，像男人的，男性化的； mannish If you describe a woman's appearance or behaviour as mannish , you mean it is more like a man's appearance or behaviour than a woman's.
manoeuvrable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 容易移动的;操纵灵活的； manoeuvrable Something that is manoeuvrable can be easily moved into different positions.
manoeuvre: [VERB 动词] (熟练地)移动，调动，转动，操纵； manoeuvre If you manoeuvre something into or out of an awkward position, you skilfully move it there.  /  [VERB 动词] 操纵;控制;耍花招； manoeuvre manoeuvring If you manoeuvre a situation, you change it in a clever and skilful way so that you can benefit from it.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 军事演习； manoeuvre Military manoeuvres are training exercises which involve the movement of soldiers and equipment over a large area.  /  room for manoeuvre » see: room �
manor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指中世纪庄园，领地； manor A manor is a large private house in the country, usually built in the Middle Ages, and also includes the land and smaller buildings around it.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 警区;警察管辖区； manor Some people, especially police officers, refer to the area where they work as their manor .
manor house: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (中世纪庄园主的)宅邸； A manor house is the main house that is or was on a medieval manor.
manpower: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人力;劳动力； manpower Workers are sometimes referred to as manpower when they are being considered as a part of the process of producing goods or providing services.
manse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 牧师住宅； manse In some Christian churches, a manse is the house provided for a clergyman to live in.
manservant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男仆；男佣； manservant A manservant is a man who works as a servant in a private house.
mansion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 宅邸;大厦； mansion A mansion is a very large house.  /  [N-IN-NAMES 名称名词] 常用于公寓楼的专有名称中公寓，大厦； Mansions is often used in the names of blocks of flats.
manslaughter: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 过失杀人;非预谋杀人罪； manslaughter Manslaughter is the illegal killing of a person by someone who did not intend to kill them.
mantel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 壁炉架;壁炉台； mantel A mantel is a mantelpiece.
mantelpiece: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 壁炉架;壁炉台； mantelpiece A mantelpiece is a wood or stone shelf which is the top part of a border round a fireplace.
mantelshelf: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 壁炉架； mantelshelf A mantelshelf is a mantelpiece.
mantle: [N-SING 单数名词] (指某一职业或要职的)责任，职责； mantle If you take on the mantle of something such as a profession or an important job, you take on the responsibilities and duties which must be fulfilled by anyone who has this profession or job.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 覆盖物;幕;罩； mantle A mantle of something is a layer of it covering a surface, for example a layer of snow on the ground.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旧时的披风，斗篷； A mantle is a piece of clothing without sleeves that people used to wear over their other clothes in former times.  /  See also: mantel ; �

manual: [ADJ 形容词] 人力的;体力的；手工的； manual Manual work is work in which you use your hands or your physical strength rather than your mind.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 用手的;手工的； manual Manual is used to talk about movements which are made by someone's hands.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 手动的;用手操作的； manual manually Manual means operated by hand, rather than by electricity or a motor.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 使用手册;说明书； manual A manual is a book which tells you how to do something or how a piece of machinery works.
manufacture: [VERB 动词] 通常指大量制造，生产； manufacture manufacturing To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 产品；制造品;工业品； manufacture Manufactures are goods or products which have been made in a factory.  /  [VERB 动词] 虚构;捏造； manufacture If you say that someone manufactures information, you are criticizing them because they invent information that is not true.
manufacturer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生产商;制造商； manufacturer A manufacturer is a business or company which makes goods in large quantities to sell.
manure: [N-MASS 物质名词] 粪肥;肥料； manure Manure is animal faeces, sometimes mixed with chemicals, that is spread on the ground in order to make plants grow healthy and strong.

marina: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (停泊游艇的)小船坞； A marina is a small harbour for small boats that are used for leisure.

marine: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 水兵;海军陆战队士兵； A marine is a member of an armed force, for example the US Marine Corps or the Royal Marines, who is specially trained for military duties at sea as well as on land.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 海洋的;海生的;海产的； marine Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the animals and plants that live in the sea.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 海船的;海运的;海事的； marine Marine is used to describe things relating to ships and their movement at sea.

mean: [VERB 动词] 意思是;表示…的意思;作…解释； mean If you want to know what a word, code, signal, or gesture means , you want to know what it refers to or what its message is.  /  [VERB 动词] 意指;表示;意思是说； mean If you ask someone what they mean , you are asking them to explain exactly what or who they are referring to or what they are intending to say.  /  [VERB 动词] (某事)对(某人)很重要，要紧,意义重大； mean If something means something to you, it is important to you in some way.  /  [VERB 动词] 表明…存在;表示…属实； mean If one thing means another, it shows that the second thing exists or is true.

meaning: [N-VAR 可变名词] 意思;意义;含义； meaning The meaning of a word, expression, or gesture is the thing or idea that it refers to or represents and which can be explained using other words.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (言语、书、电影等的)含义，主旨，意图； meaning The meaning of what someone says or of something such as a book or film is the thoughts or ideas that are intended to be expressed by it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (活动、行为等的)意义，价值； meaning If an activity or action has meaning , it has a purpose and is worthwhile.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (由于缺乏经历、资质等)不理解这个词的含义，不知道什么叫…； meaning If you mention something and say that someone doesn't know the meaning of the word , you are emphasizing that they have never experienced the thing mentioned or do not have the quality mentioned.
meaningful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 严肃的;重要的;有意义的； meaningful meaningfully If you describe something as meaningful , you mean that it is serious, important, or useful in some way.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 指眼神、姿势意味深长的，意在言外的； meaningful meaningfully A meaningful look or gesture is one that is intended to express something, usually to a particular person, without anything being said.  /  See also: meaningfully ; �
meaningfully: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 有用意地;有目的地;意味深长地； meaningfully See also: meaningful ; You use meaningfully to indicate that someone has deliberately chosen their words in order to express something in a way which is not obvious but which is understood by the person they are talking to.
meaningless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 指话语、所写内容意思不明确的，无法理解的，没有意义的； meaningless If something that someone says or writes is meaningless , it has no meaning, or appears to have no meaning.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不重要的;不相关的； meaningless Something that is meaningless in a particular situation is not important or relevant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无目的的;无价值的； meaningless If something that you do is meaningless , it has no purpose and is not at all worthwhile.
means: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 方法;手段;工具(means 用于此意时单复数同形)； means A means of doing something is a method, instrument, or process which can be used to do it.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 收入;财富;金钱； means You can refer to the money that someone has as their means .  /  [PHRASE 短语] 超出财力；入不敷出/在财力之内；量入为出； means If someone is living beyond their means , they are spending more money than they can afford.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 用;以;通过； means If you do something by means of a particular method, instrument, or process, you do it using that method, instrument, or process.
means test: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 个人收入调查(以判定其是否可领取政府补助金)； A means test is a test in which your income is calculated in order to decide whether you qualify for a grant or benefit from the state.
means-tested: [ADJ 形容词] 补助金等经过收入调查的，根据收入调查结果而确定的； means-tested A grant or benefit that is means-tested varies in amount depending on a means test.
meant: + + + Meant is the past tense and past participle of mean .  /  [ADJ 形容词] 原本打算的;理应的； meant You use meant to to say that something or someone was intended to be or do a particular thing, especially when they have failed to be or do it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 为…而做的;为…而准备的； meant If something is meant for particular people or for a particular situation, it is intended for those people or for that situation.  /  [PHR-MODAL 情态动词短语] 理应发生;应该； meant If you say that something is meant to happen, you mean that it is expected to happen or that it ought to happen.
meantime: [PHRASE 短语] 在此期间;其间； meantime In the meantime or meantime means in the period of time between two events.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 目前;眼下;暂时； meantime For the meantime means for a period of time from now until something else happens.
meanwhile: [ADV 副词] 同时;与此同时； meanwhile Meanwhile means while a particular thing is happening.  /  [ADV 副词] 在此期间;其间； in the meanwhile 同 meanwhile meanwhile Meanwhile means in the period of time between two events.  /  [ADV 副词] (引出某一情形的另一方面，尤指与前面提到的完全相反时)与之相比，然而； meanwhile You use meanwhile to introduce a different aspect of a particular situation, especially one that is completely opposite to the one previously mentioned.
measles: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麻疹； Measles is an infectious illness that gives you a high temperature and red spots on your skin.
measly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 数目、数量、大小微不足道的，少得可怜的； measly If you describe an amount, quantity, or size as measly , you are critical of it because it is very small or inadequate.
measurable: [ADJ 形容词] 可觉察到的;明显的;显著的； measurable measurably If you describe something as measurable , you mean that it is large enough to be noticed or to be significant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可测量的；可计量的； measurable Something that is measurable can be measured.
measure: [VERB 动词] 衡量；估量;评估;判定； measure If you measure the quality, value, or effect of something, you discover or judge how great it is.  /  [VERB 动词] 测量;度量;计量； measure If you measure a quantity that can be expressed in numbers, such as the length of something, you discover it using a particular instrument or device, for example a ruler.  /  [VERB 动词] 距离(或长度、宽度、数量等)为…； measure If something measures a particular length, width, or amount, that is its size or intensity, expressed in numbers.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 相当数量;一定程度； measure A measure of a particular quality, feeling, or activity is a fairly large amount of it.
measured: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 仔细的;谨慎小心的； measured You use measured to describe something that is careful and deliberate.
measurement: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常以数字形式呈现的测量结果； measurement A measurement is a result, usually expressed in numbers, that you obtain by measuring something.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 测量;计量； Measurement of something is the process of measuring it in order to obtain a result expressed in numbers.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 质量、价值或影响的衡量，评估，估量； measurement The measurement of the quality, value, or effect of something is the activity of deciding how great it is.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 三围；(身材)尺寸； Your measurements are the size of your waist, chest, hips, and other parts of your body, which you need to know when you are buying clothes.
measure out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (按所需)量出,量取； If you measure out a certain amount of something, you measure that amount and take it or mark it because it is the amount that you want or need.
measure up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 符合(标准);达到(期望)； measure up If you do not measure up to a standard or to someone's expectations, you are not good enough to achieve the standard or fulfil the person's expectations.
measuring: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指烹饪时)测量或称量用的(壶、杯、匙等)； A measuring jug, cup, or spoon is specially designed for measuring quantities, especially in cooking.
meat: [N-MASS 物质名词] (供食用的)肉； meat Meat is flesh taken from a dead animal that people cook and eat.  /  See also: luncheon meat ; red meat ; white meat ;  /  [PHRASE 短语] 喜欢做的事;感兴趣的事； meat If you say something is meat and drink to someone, you mean that they enjoy it very much.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 最基本的部分;根本部分;关键； meat If you refer to the meat and potatoes of something, you mean its most basic, simple, and essential parts.
meatball: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肉丸通常蘸酱吃； Meatballs are small balls of chopped meat.
meat grinder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绞肉机； A meat grinder is a machine which cuts meat into very small pieces by forcing it through very small holes.
meat loaf: [N-VAR 可变名词] (用肉糜做的)肉糕； Meat loaf is chopped meat made into the shape of a loaf of bread.
meaty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 食物含肉的，多肉的； meaty Food that is meaty contains a lot of meat.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 文章、电影等内容丰富的； meaty You can describe something such as a piece of writing or a part in a film as meaty if it contains a lot of interesting or important material.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (身体部位)肥厚的，粗壮的； meaty You can describe a part of someone's body as meaty if it is big and strong.
mecca: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 麦加(沙特阿拉伯城市，伊斯兰教圣城,先知穆罕默德的诞生地，穆斯林祈祷时朝拜的方向)； Mecca is a city in Saudi Arabia, which is the holiest city in Islam because the Prophet Mohammed was born there.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 众人向往的地方;圣地;胜地； mecca If you describe a place as a mecca or Mecca for a particular thing or activity, you mean that many people who are interested in it go there.
mechanic: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指修理汽车的技工，机修工，修理工； mechanic A mechanic is someone whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially car engines.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 过程、系统、动作等运作方式;(具体的)方法，技巧； mechanic The mechanics of a process, system, or activity are the way in which it works or the way in which it is done.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 力学;机械学； mechanic Mechanics is the part of physics that deals with the natural forces that act on moving or stationary objects.
mechanical: [ADJ 形容词] 机械的;机动的； mechanical mechanically A mechanical device has parts that move when it is working, often using power from an engine or from electricity.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 机械方面的;机械原理的； mechanical mechanically Mechanical means relating to machines and engines and the way they work.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人精通机械的;擅长于机械原理的； mechanical mechanically If you describe a person as mechanical , you mean they are naturally good at understanding how machines work.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 行为机械的，呆板的，不动脑筋的； mechanical mechanically If you describe someone's action as mechanical , you mean that they do it automatically, without thinking about it.
mechanism: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 机械装置;机件； mechanism In a machine or piece of equipment, a mechanism is a part, often consisting of a set of smaller parts, which performs a particular function.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 方法;途径;程序;机制； mechanism A mechanism is a special way of getting something done within a particular system.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (人为生存、对付困境的)机制，行为方式； mechanism A mechanism is a part of your behaviour that is automatic and that helps you to survive or to cope with a difficult situation.  /  See also: defence mechanism ; �
mechanistic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 观点或解释机械论的； mechanistic If you describe a view or explanation of something as mechanistic , you are criticizing it because it describes a natural or social process as if it were a machine.
mechanize: [VERB 动词] 使机械化；使机器化； mechanize mechanized mechanization If someone mechanizes a process, they cause it to be done by a machine or machines, when it was previously done by people.
medal: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 奖章;勋章；奖牌； A medal is a small metal disc which is given as an award for bravery or as a prize in a sporting event.
medallion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指用链子挂于颈部的)圆形金属饰物； A medallion is a round metal disc which some people wear as an ornament, especially on a chain round their neck.
medallist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (体育比赛中的)奖章获得者，奖牌获得者； medallist A medallist is a person who has won a medal in sport.
meddle: [VERB 动词] 管闲事;干涉;干预； meddle meddler If you say that someone meddles in something, you are criticizing the fact that they try to influence or change it without being asked.
meddlesome: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 好干预的;爱管闲事的； meddlesome If you describe a person as meddlesome , you are criticizing them because they try to influence or change things that do not concern them.
media: [N-SING-COLL 单数集合名词] 媒体，传播工具，传播媒介(如电视、广播、报纸和杂志等)； media See also: mass media ; multimedia ; You can refer to television, radio, newspapers, and magazines as the media .  /  (medium 的复数之一)； Media is a plural of medium .
media circus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 媒体关注的焦点;媒体云集的盛会； media circus If an event is described as a media circus , a large group of people from the media is there to report on it and take photographs.
median: [ADJ 形容词] 中间值的;中位数的;中间的； The median value of a set of values is the middle one when they are arranged in order.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 median strip； A median is the same as a median strip .
median strip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 主干道上通常铺有草坪的中央分隔带,中央分道区,中间安全区； The median strip is the strip of ground, often covered with grass, that separates the two sides of a major road.
mediate: [VERB 动词] 调解;调停;斡旋； mediate mediation mediator If someone mediates between two groups of people, or mediates an agreement between them, they try to settle an argument between them by talking to both groups and trying to find things that they can both agree to.  /  [VERB 动词] 调节;影响； mediate mediation If something mediates a particular process or event, it allows that process or event to happen and influences the way in which it happens.
medic: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 医生;医科学生； A medic is a doctor or medical student.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (随军)卫生员； medic A medic is a doctor who works with the armed forces, as part of a medical corps.
medical: [ADJ 形容词] 医学的;医疗的;医术的； medical medically Medical means relating to illness and injuries and to their treatment or prevention.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 体格检查;体检； A medical is a thorough examination of your body by a doctor, for example before you start a new job.
medical examiner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 法医;验尸官； A medical examiner is a medical expert who is responsible for investigating the deaths of people who have died in a sudden, violent, or unusual way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (申请健康保险或求职时负责体检的)特约体检医生； A medical examiner is a doctor whose job is to examine people, for example when they apply for a job or for health insurance.
medicated: [ADJ 形容词] (肥皂、洗发液等)含药物的，药制的； A medicated soap or shampoo contains substances which are intended to kill bacteria and therefore make your skin or hair healthier.
medication: [N-VAR 可变名词] 药物;药； medication Medication is medicine that is used to treat and cure illness.
medicinal: [ADJ 形容词] 有疗效的;药用的;治病的； medicinal medicinally Medicinal substances or substances with medicinal effects can be used to treat and cure illnesses.
medicine: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 医学;疗法;医疗； medicine Medicine is the treatment of illness and injuries by doctors and nurses.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 吞服的药，药物，药剂； medicine Medicine is a substance that you drink or swallow in order to cure an illness.
medieval: [ADJ 形容词] 中世纪的(指公元476年西罗马帝国灭亡至公元1500年左右这段时期)； medieval Something that is medieval relates to or was made in the period of European history between the end of the Roman Empire in 476 AD and about 1500 AD.
mediocre: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 事物普通的，平庸的，一般的； mediocre If you describe something as mediocre , you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.
mediocrity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 平庸;平凡;普通； mediocrity If you refer to the mediocrity of something, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 庸人;平庸之辈； If you refer to someone as a mediocrity , you think that they are not very good at what they do.
meditate: [VERB 动词] 沉思;深思;仔细考虑； meditate If you meditate on something, you think about it very carefully and deeply for a long time.  /  [VERB 动词] 宗教中冥想，默想，打坐； If you meditate you remain in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training or so that you are more able to deal with the problems and difficulties of everyday life.
meditation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 宗教中默想，打坐，冥想； meditation See also: transcendental meditation ; Meditation is the act of remaining in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training, or so that you are more able to deal with the problems of everyday life.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 深思熟虑;苦思冥想； meditation Meditation is the act of thinking about something very carefully and deeply for a long time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 关于某主题的感想,沉思录； meditation A meditation on a particular subject is something such as a piece of writing or a speech which expresses deep thoughts about that subject.
meditative: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沉思的;深思的； meditative meditatively Meditative describes things that are related to the act of meditating or the act of thinking very deeply about something.
Mediterranean: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 地中海； The Mediterranean is the sea between southern Europe and North Africa.  /  [N-PROPER 专有名词] 地中海地区(指欧洲南部地中海附近地区)； Mediterranean The Mediterranean refers to the southern part of Europe, which is next to the Mediterranean Sea.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 地中海的;地中海地区的;地中海居民的； Mediterranean Something that is Mediterranean is characteristic of or belongs to the people or region around the Mediterranean Sea.
medium: [ADJ 形容词] 中等的;中间的;中号的； medium If something is of medium size, it is neither large nor small, but approximately half way between the two.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 中间的;平均的； medium You use medium to describe something which is average in degree or amount, or approximately half way along a scale between two extremes.  /  [COMB in COLOUR 与颜色词构成的词] (颜色)不深不浅的，适中的； medium If something is of a medium colour, it is neither light nor dark, but approximately half way between the two.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (表现)方式;(交流)手段； medium A medium is a way or means of expressing your ideas or of communicating with people.
medium-dry: [ADJ 形容词] (葡萄酒或雪利酒)中等甜度的，不太甜的； Medium-dry wine or sherry is not very sweet.
medium-sized: [ADJ 形容词] 中号的;中型的;中等大小的； medium-sized Medium-sized means neither large nor small, but approximately half way between the two.
medium-term: [N-SING 单数名词] 中期； medium-term The medium-term is the period of time which lasts a few months or years beyond the present time, in contrast with the short term or the long term.
medium wave: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无线电广播的中波； medium wave Medium wave is a range of radio waves which are used for broadcasting.
medley: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 集成曲;集锦;音乐串烧； medley In music, a medley is a collection of different tunes or songs that are played one after the other as a single piece of music.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 混合泳； In sport, a medley is a swimming race in which the four main strokes are used one after the other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 杂烩;什锦;混合物； medley A medley of different foods or other things is a mixture of them.
meek: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 温顺的;顺从的； meek 温顺的人 meekly meekness If you describe a person as meek , you think that they are gentle and quiet, and likely to do what other people say.
meet: [V-RECIP 相互动词] 碰到;遇见； meet up同 meet If you meet someone, you happen to be in the same place as them and start talking to them.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] (约定在某处)相会，碰头； meet meet up 同 meet If two or more people meet , they go to the same place, which they have earlier arranged to do, so that they can talk or do something together.  /  [VERB 动词] 被引见给;认识;结识； meet If you meet someone, you are introduced to them and begin talking to them and getting to know them.  /  [VERB 动词] 初次见面;认识;结识； meet You use meet in expressions such as ' Pleased to meet you ' and ' Nice to have met you ' when you want to politely say hello or goodbye to someone you have just met for the first time.
meeting: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 会议;集会； meeting . 参加会议的人;与会人员 A meeting is an event in which a group of people come together to discuss things or make decisions.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (有意或无意的)碰见，遇上； meeting When you meet someone, either by chance or by arrangement, you can refer to this event as a meeting .
meeting house: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某些基督教徒，如贵格会教徒等的)礼拜会所； A meeting house is a building in which certain groups of Christians, for example Quakers, meet in order to worship together.
meeting place: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 聚会处;会场;会面地点； A meeting place is a place where people meet.
mega: [ADV 副词] 置于形容词和副词前，表示强调； mega Young people sometimes use mega in front of adjectives or adverbs in order to emphasize them.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (用于名词前)特别好的，异常巨大的，非常重要的； mega Young people sometimes use mega in front of nouns in order to emphasize that the thing they are talking about is very good, very large, or very impressive.
mega-: [PREFIX 前缀] (加在计量单位之前)表示“兆”，“百万”； Mega- is added to nouns that refer to units of measurement in order to form other nouns referring to units that are a million times bigger.  /  [PREFIX 前缀] (与名词、形容词构成合成词，强调大小、性质或重要性)； mega- Mega- combines with nouns and adjectives in order to emphasize the size, quality, or importance of something.
megabyte: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兆字节;百万字节； In computing, a megabyte is one million bytes of data.
megahertz: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兆赫； megahertz A megahertz is a unit of frequency, used especially for radio frequencies.
megalomania: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自大狂;夸大狂;妄自尊大； Megalomania is the belief that you are more powerful and important than you really are.
megalomaniac: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有自大狂的人;妄自尊大的人； If you describe someone as a megalomaniac , you are criticizing them because they enjoy being powerful, or because they believe that they are more powerful or important than they really are.
megamall: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 超级大商场;超级购物中心； A megamall is a very large shopping area containing very many shops, cinemas, and restaurants.
megaphone: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 扩音器;传声筒;喇叭； A megaphone is a cone-shaped device for making your voice sound louder in the open air.
megapixel: 数码相机、扫描仪等的兆像素，百万像素； A megapixel is one million pixels: used as a measure of the quality of the picture created by a digital camera, scanner, or other device.
megaton: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兆吨，百万吨级(可用于计算核爆炸力，相当于100万吨梯恩梯炸药的爆炸威力)； You can use megaton to refer to the power of a nuclear weapon.
megawatt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兆瓦;百万瓦特； megawatt A megawatt is a unit of power.
-meister: [COMB in N-COUNT] [COMB in ADJ] (与名词连用构成名词)表示“…高手”，“…能手”，“…专家”； -meister -meister combines with nouns to form nouns which refer to someone who is extremely good at a particular activity.
melancholia: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 极度忧郁(或抑郁)； melancholia Melancholia is a feeling of great sadness, especially one that lasts a long time.
melancholic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忧郁的;忧伤的； melancholic 忧郁的人 If you describe someone or something as melancholic , you mean that they are very sad.
melancholy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 使人忧郁的;令人忧伤的； melancholy You describe something that you see or hear as melancholy when it gives you an intense feeling of sadness.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (习惯性或气质上的)忧郁，忧伤； melancholy Melancholy is an intense feeling of sadness which lasts for a long time and which strongly affects your behaviour and attitudes.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忧郁的;悲伤的； melancholy If someone feels or looks melancholy , they feel or look very sad.
melange: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指吸引人或令人兴奋的混合物,大杂烩； melange A melange of things is a mixture of them, especially when this is attractive or exciting.
melanin: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 黑色素； Melanin is a dark substance in the skin, eyes, and hair of people and animals, which gives them colour and can protect them against strong sunlight.
melanoma: [N-VAR 可变名词] (恶性)黑素瘤； A melanoma is an area of cancer cells in the skin which is caused by very strong sunlight.
melee: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 混战； melee A melee is a noisy confusing fight between the people in a crowd.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 混乱的情况;无序的局面； melee A melee of things is a large, confusing, disorganized group of them.
mellifluous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 悦耳的;流畅的;动听的； mellifluous A mellifluous voice or piece of music is smooth and gentle and very pleasant to listen to.
mellow: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (颜色)柔和的,温暖的； mellow Mellow is used to describe things that have a pleasant, soft, rich colour, usually red, orange, yellow, or brown.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (声音)悦耳的，圆润的;(味道)香醇的； mellow A mellow sound or flavour is pleasant, smooth, and rich.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使变平和;使变得成熟； mellow If someone mellows or if something mellows them, they become kinder or less extreme in their behaviour, especially as a result of growing older.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指喝过酒或品尝过美食后)怡然自得的； mellow If someone is mellow , they feel very relaxed and cheerful, especially as the result of alcohol or good food.
melodic: [ADJ 形容词] 旋律上的； melodic melodically Melodic means relating to melody.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 旋律优美的;悦耳动听的； melodic melodically Music that is melodic has beautiful tunes in it.
melodious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 优美的;悦耳的;动听的； melodious A melodious sound is pleasant to listen to.
melodrama: [N-VAR 可变名词] (情节离奇而夸张的)惊险故事，传奇剧，情节剧； A melodrama is a story or play in which there are a lot of exciting or sad events and in which people's emotions are very exaggerated.
melodramatic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过分严肃的;夸张的;小题大做的； melodramatic melodramatically Melodramatic behaviour is behaviour in which someone treats a situation as much more serious than it really is.
melody: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旋律;曲调； A melody is a tune.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 婉转;悦耳； melody Melody is the quality of having a pleasant tune.
melon: [N-VAR 可变名词] 瓜;甜瓜； A melon is a large fruit which is sweet and juicy inside and has a hard green or yellow skin.
melt: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使熔化;使融化； melt When a solid substance melts or when you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.  /  [VERB 动词] (情绪等)消失,消散,平息； melt melt away 同 melt If something such as your feelings melt , they suddenly disappear and you no longer feel them.  /  [VERB 动词] 逐渐融入(黑暗、人群等);与…融为一体； melt If a person or thing melts into something such as darkness or a crowd of people, they become difficult to see, for example because they are moving away from you or are the same colour as the background.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使心软化； melt If someone or something melts your heart, or if your heart melts , you start to feel love or sympathy towards them.
melt away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (人群)逐渐散去； melt away See also: melt ; If a crowd of people melts away , members of the crowd gradually leave until there is no-one left.
meltdown: [N-VAR 可变名词] (核反应堆的)堆芯熔毁； meltdown If there is meltdown in a nuclear reactor, the fuel rods start melting because of a failure in the system, and radiation starts to escape.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (公司、机构或系统的)崩溃，彻底失败； meltdown The meltdown of a company, organization, or system is its sudden and complete failure.
melt down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 熔化，熔毁(以再利用)； melt down If an object is melted down , it is heated until it melts, so that the material can be used to make something else.
melting point: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 熔点； The melting point of a substance is the temperature at which it melts when you heat it.
melting pot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 熔炉(指不同民族或思想融合混杂的地方或状况)； melting pot A melting pot is a place or situation in which people or ideas of different kinds gradually get mixed together.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 仍在变化的;尚未定型的;难以预料的； melting pot If something is in the melting pot , you do not know what is going to happen to it.
member: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 团体的成员，一分子； member A member of a group is one of the people, animals, or things belonging to that group.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 会员;成员； member A member of an organization such as a club or a political party is a person who has officially joined the organization.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (某国际组织的)会员国，成员国； member A member country or member state is one of the countries that has joined an international organization or group.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 议员； member A member or Member is a person who has been elected to a parliament or legislature.
Member of Congress: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (美国的)国会议员； A Member of Congress is a person who has been elected to the United States Congress.
Member of Parliament: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (议会中代表某一地区的)议员(常用其缩略形式 MP)； A Member of Parliament is a person who has been elected by the people in a particular area to represent them in a country's parliament.
membership: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 会员身份;成员资格； membership Membership of an organization is the state of being a member of it.  /  [N-VAR-COLL 可变集合名词] 全体会员(或成员);全体会员(或成员)人数； membership The membership of an organization is the people who belong to it, or the number of people who belong to it.
membrane: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连接或覆盖身体某些部位的膜,薄膜； A membrane is a thin piece of skin which connects or covers parts of a person's or animal's body.
memento: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纪念物;纪念品； memento A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special occasion.
memo: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (公司或组织内部的)公务便条，备忘录； A memo is a short official note that is sent by one person to another within the same company or organization.
memoir: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 传记;传略； memoir A memoir is a book or article that you write about someone who you have known well.
memorabilia: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (与某人或某组织相关的)收藏品,纪念品； Memorabilia are things that you collect because they are connected with a person or organization in which you are interested.
memorable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 难忘的;值得纪念的； memorable memorably Something that is memorable is worth remembering or likely to be remembered, because it is special or very enjoyable.
memorandum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 备忘录； memorandum A memorandum is a written report that is prepared for a person or committee in order to provide them with information about a particular matter.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (外交)备忘录； memorandum A memorandum is an informal communication between governments which often states a particular diplomatic purpose or point of view.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (公司或组织内部的)公务便条，备忘录； A memorandum is a short official note that is sent by one person to another within the same company or organization.
memorial: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纪念碑； memorial A memorial is a structure built in order to remind people of a famous person or event.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 对逝者纪念的;悼念的;追思的； memorial A memorial event, object, or prize is in honour of someone who has died, so that they will be remembered.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 追忆逝者的纪念物,纪念品； memorial If you say that something will be a memorial to someone who has died, you mean that it will continue to exist and remind people of them.
Memorial Day: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 阵亡将士纪念日(美国的法定假日，在大多数州为5月的最后一个星期一)； In the United States, Memorial Day is a public holiday when people honour the memory of Americans who have died in wars.
memorialize: [VERB 动词] 纪念;使记住； memorialize If a person or event is memorialized , something is produced that will continue to exist and remind people of them.
memorize: [VERB 动词] 熟记;记住； memorize If you memorize something, you learn it so that you can remember it exactly.
memory: [N-VAR 可变名词] 记忆力;记性； memory Your memory is your ability to remember things.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 记忆;记忆中的事物;回忆； memory A memory is something that you remember from the past.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 存储器;内存； memory A computer's memory is the part of the computer where information is stored, especially for a short time before it is transferred to disks or magnetic tapes.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (对死者的)怀念，记忆； memory If you talk about the memory of someone who has died, especially someone who was loved or respected, you are referring to the thoughts, actions, and ceremonies by which they are remembered.
memory card: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (数码相机等的)内存卡,存储卡，记忆卡； A memory card is a type of card containing computer memory that is used in digital cameras and other devices.
memory chip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (计算机的)存储芯片，内存芯片； In a computer, the memory chip is the microchip in which information is stored.
memsahib: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE; N-VOC] [可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词] 夫人，太太(尤在英国统治时期用作对居住在印度的白人妇女的尊称，有时也用来称呼印度上层社会的妇女)； Memsahib was used to refer to or address white women in India, especially during the period of British rule, or sometimes to refer to or address upper-class Indian women.
men: (man 的复数)； Men is the plural of man .
menace: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 威胁;危险人物;祸害； menace If you say that someone or something is a menace to other people or things, you mean that person or thing is likely to cause serious harm.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 惹麻烦的人(或物);惹人讨厌的人(或物)； menace You can refer to someone or something as a menace when you want to say that they cause you trouble or annoyance.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 威胁性;危险气氛； menace Menace is a quality or atmosphere that gives you the feeling that you are in danger or that someone wants to harm you.  /  [VERB 动词] 危及;威胁； menace If you say that one thing menaces another, you mean that the first thing is likely to cause the second thing serious harm.
menacing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 威胁的;威吓的;危险的； menacing menacingly If someone or something looks menacing , they give you a feeling that they are likely to cause you harm or put you in danger.
menage: [N-SING 单数名词] 家庭;一家;住在同一所房子里的人； A menage is a group of people living together in one house.
menage a trois: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指有性关系的三人同居； A menage a trois is a situation where three people live together, especially when one of them is having a sexual relationship with both of the others.
menagerie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (私人豢养或向公众展览的)一群野生动物； A menagerie is a collection of wild animals.
mend: [VERB 动词] 修理;修补； mend If you mend something that is broken or not working, you repair it, so that it works properly or can be used.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使康复;使痊愈;使愈合； mend If a person or a part of their body mends or is mended , they get better after they have been ill or have had an injury.  /  [VERB 动词] 弥合(分歧);解决(争端)； mend If you try to mend divisions between people, you try to end the disagreements or quarrels between them.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (关系)正在改善;(形势)正在好转； mend If a relationship or situation is on the mend after a difficult or unsuccessful period, it is improving.
mendacious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人撒谎的，虚伪的;声明不真实的,捏造的； A mendacious person is someone who tells lies.
mendacity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 撒谎;虚假;捏造； mendacity Mendacity is lying, rather than telling the truth.
mending: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对衣服的)修补，缝补； mending See also: mend ; Mending is the sewing and repairing of clothes that have got holes in them.
menfolk: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (家庭中或社会上的)男人们； When women refer to their menfolk , they mean the men in their family or society.
menial: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 工作枯燥的,低级的，报酬低的； menial Menial work is very boring, and the people who do it have a low status and are usually badly paid.
meningitis: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 脑脊膜炎； Meningitis is a serious infectious illness which affects your brain and spinal cord.
menopause: [N-SING 单数名词] 更年期，绝经期(通常在50岁左右)； menopausal The menopause is the time during which a woman gradually stops menstruating, usually when she is about fifty years old.
men's room: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男厕所;男盥洗室； The men's room is a toilet for men in a public building.
menstrual: [ADJ 形容词] 月经的； menstrual Menstrual means relating to menstruation.
menstruate: [VERB 动词] 行经;来月经； menstruate menstruation When a woman menstruates , a flow of blood comes from her womb.
menswear: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 男装； menswear Menswear is clothing for men.
-ment: [SUFFIX 后缀] (加在某些动词后构成名词)表示“动作”、“过程”、“状态”； -ment is added to some verbs to form nouns that refer to actions, processes, or states.
mental: [ADJ 形容词] 智力的;脑力的;思考的； mental mentally Mental means relating to the process of thinking.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 心理上的;精神上的； mental mentally Mental means relating to the state or the health of a person's mind.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 内心的;在头脑中进行的； mental mentally A mental act is one that involves only thinking and not physical action.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 疯狂的;发疯的； mental If you say that someone is mental , you mean that you think they are mad.
mental age: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 智力年龄;心理年龄； A person's mental age is the age which they are considered to have reached in their ability to think or reason.
mental hospital: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 精神病院； A mental hospital is a hospital for people who are suffering from mental illness.
mentality: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 心态;思维方式； mentality Your mentality is your attitudes and your way of thinking.
menthol: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 薄荷脑;薄荷醇； Menthol is a substance that smells a bit like peppermint and is used to flavour things such as cigarettes and toothpaste.
mention: [VERB 动词] (简短地)谈及，说起，提到； mention If you mention something, you say something about it, usually briefly.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 提及;论及； mention A mention is a reference to something or someone.  /  [VERB 动词] 在文章中提到，谈及(某人的名字)； mention If someone is mentioned in writing, a reference is made to them by name, often to criticize or praise something that they have done.  /  [VERB 动词] 提名;推荐； mention If someone is mentioned as a candidate for something such as a job, it is suggested that they might become a candidate.
mentor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指工作方面的)导师，指导者； A person's mentor is someone who gives them help and advice over a period of time, especially help and advice related to their job.  /  [VERB 动词] 为…出谋划策;指导;辅导； mentor mentoring To mentor someone means to give them help and advice over a period of time, especially help and advice related to their job.
menu: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 菜单； menu In a restaurant or café or at a formal meal, the menu is a list of the food and drinks that are available.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 饭菜;菜肴； menu A menu is the food that you serve at a meal.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (电脑屏幕上的)菜单，功能选择单，选项单； On a computer screen, a menu is a list of choices.
MEP: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 欧洲议会议员； An MEP is a person who has been elected to the European Parliament.
mercantile: [ADJ 形容词] 商业的;贸易的； mercantile Mercantile means relating to or involved in trade.
mercenary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (外籍)雇佣兵； A mercenary is a soldier who is paid to fight by a country or group that they do not belong to.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 唯利是图的;见钱眼开的； If you describe someone as mercenary , you are criticizing them because you think that they are only interested in the money that they can get from a particular person or situation.
merchandise: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 商品;货物； Merchandise is goods that are bought, sold, or traded.
merchandiser: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 商人;商家； merchandiser A merchandiser is a person or company that sells goods to the public.
merchandising: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (与影片、运动队、流行乐队等相关的)附带商品，文化衍生品； merchandising Merchandising consists of goods such as toys and clothes that are linked with something such as a film, sports team, or pop group.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 推销;商品拓销;销售规划； merchandising Merchandising is used to refer to the way shops and businesses organize the sale of their products, for example the way they are displayed and the prices that are chosen.
merchant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指外贸)商人，批发商； merchant A merchant is a person who buys or sells goods in large quantities, especially one who imports and exports them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 店主;商人； merchant A merchant is a person who owns or runs a shop, store, or other business.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 海上货运的;商船的； merchant Merchant seamen or ships are involved in carrying goods for trade.
