mini-: [PREFIX 前缀] (用于名词前构成名词)表示“小型的”，“微型的”； mini- Mini- is used before nouns to form nouns which refer to something which is a smaller version of something else.
miniature: [ADJ 形容词] 微小的;尤指微型的，微缩版的； miniature Miniature is used to describe something which is very small, especially a smaller version of something which is normally much bigger.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 微型的；缩微的； miniature If you describe one thing as another thing in miniature , you mean that it is much smaller in size or scale than the other thing, but is otherwise exactly the same.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 常指人物的微型画，袖珍画像； A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often of a person.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小瓶装烈酒； A miniature is a very small bottle of strong alcohol such as whisky or brandy, and usually contains enough for one or two drinks.
miniaturize: [VERB 动词] 使小型化；使微型化； miniaturize miniaturization If you miniaturize something such as a machine, you produce a very small version of it.
minibar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (宾馆房间装酒的)小冰箱； In a hotel room, a minibar is a small fridge containing alcoholic drinks.
mini-break: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 短暂的假期； mini-break A mini-break is a short holiday.
minibus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小型公共汽车;中巴； minibus A minibus is a large van which has seats in the back for passengers, and windows along its sides.
minicab: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 需要电话预约的小型出租汽车； minicab A minicab is a taxi which you have to arrange to pick you up by telephone.
minicam: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小型电视摄像机； A minicam is a very small television camera.
minidisc: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小型碟片;迷你光碟； A minidisc is a small compact disc which you can record music or data on.
minidish: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 迷你卫星碟(一种接收电视、因特网等的通讯卫星信号的碟形天线)； A minidish is a small satellite dish that can receive signals from communications satellites for media such as television programmes and the Internet.
minim: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 二分音符；半音符； A minim is a musical note that has a time value equal to two crotchets or two quarter notes.
minimal: [ADJ 形容词] 最小的;极少的;最低限度的； minimal minimally Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.
minimalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 极简风格； minimalism Minimalism is a style in which a small number of very simple things are used to create a particular effect.
minimalist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 极简派设计师；极简派艺术家； minimalist A minimalist is an artist or designer who uses minimalism.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极简派风格的;受极简主义影响的； minimalist Minimalist is used to describe ideas, artists, or designers that are influenced by minimalism.
minimize: [VERB 动词] 使减至最低程度;使保持最低程度； minimize If you minimize a risk, problem, or unpleasant situation, you reduce it to the lowest possible level, or prevent it increasing beyond that level.  /  [VERB 动词] 对…轻描淡写；使显得不重要； minimize If you minimize something, you make it seem smaller or less significant than it really is.  /  [VERB 动词] 把(计算机屏幕上的窗口)最小化； minimize If you minimize a window on a computer screen, you make it very small, because you do not want to use it.
minimum: [ADJ 形容词] 最小的;最低限度的； minimum You use minimum to describe an amount which is the smallest that is possible, allowed, or required.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (数量)极少的； minimum You use minimum to state how small an amount is.  /  [ADV 副词] 最低;至少； minimum If you say that something is a particular amount minimum , you mean that this is the smallest amount it should be or could possibly be, although a larger amount is acceptable or very possible.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 至少;最小； minimum You use at a minimum , or at the minimum , when you want to indicate that something is the very least which could or should happen.
minimum security prison: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对犯人限制较少的)低度设防监狱； A minimum security prison is a prison where there are fewer restrictions on prisoners than in a normal prison.
minimum wage: [N-SING 单数名词] 法律或协议规定的最低工资； The minimum wage is the lowest wage that an employer is allowed to pay an employee, according to a law or agreement.
mining: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 采矿;采矿业； mining Mining is the industry and activities connected with getting valuable or useful minerals from the ground, for example coal, diamonds, or gold.
minion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指从事无关紧要或乏味工作的仆从，下属，小卒； minion If you refer to someone's minions , you are referring to people who have to do what that person tells them to do, especially unimportant or boring tasks.
mini-series: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常在一周内分两至三集播完的电视连续短片，迷你剧； A mini-series is a drama shown on television in two or three parts, usually in one week.
mini-skirt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 超短裙;迷你裙； A mini-skirt is a very short skirt.
miniskirt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 超短裙;迷你裙； A mini-skirt is a very short skirt.
minister: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (政府)部长，大臣；  minister In Britain and some other countries, a minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (比大使低一级的)公使，外交使节； minister A minister is a person who officially represents their government in a foreign country and has a lower rank than an ambassador.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指新教的)神父，牧师； minister A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.  /  [VERB 动词] 满足(…的需要);服侍；帮助； minister If you minister to people or to their needs, you serve them or help them, for example by making sure that they have everything they need or want.
ministerial: [ADJ 形容词] 部长的；大臣的； ministerial You use ministerial to refer to people, events, or jobs that are connected with government ministers.
ministrations: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 尤指对身体虚弱或生病之人的服务，照顾，服侍； ministrations A person's ministrations are the things they do to help or care for someone in a particular situation, especially someone who is weak or ill.
ministry: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (政府的)部； In Britain and some other countries, a ministry is a government department which deals with a particular thing or area of activity, for example trade, defence, or transport.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 圣职;神职； ministry The ministry of a religious person is the work that they do that is based on or inspired by their religious beliefs.  /  [N-SING-COLL 单数集合名词] 基督教的全体牧师； ministry Members of the clergy belonging to some branches of the Christian church are referred to as the ministry .
mink: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 水貂； mink 貂皮 A mink is a small animal with highly valued fur.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 貂皮大衣;貂皮衣服； mink A mink is a coat or other garment made from the fur of a mink.
minnow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鲦鱼，米诺鱼(一种极小的淡水鱼)； A minnow is a very small fish that lives in lakes and rivers.
minor: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不重要的;不严重的；次要的； minor You use minor when you want to describe something that is less important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (疾病)不严重的，轻微的;(手术)小的； minor A minor illness or operation is not likely to be dangerous to someone's life or health.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 小音阶的;小调的； minor In European music, a minor scale is one in which the third note is three semitones higher than the first.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 未成年人(在英国和美国多数州指未满18岁的人，在法律上仍然视为儿童)； minor A minor is a person who is still legally a child.
minority: [N-SING 单数名词] 少数; 少数派； minority 属于少数派；占少数 If you talk about a minority of people or things in a larger group, you are referring to a number of them that forms less than half of the larger group, usually much less than half.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 少数民族；少数群体； minority A minority is a group of people of the same race, culture, or religion who live in a place where most of the people around them are of a different race, culture, or religion.
minstrel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (中世纪云游各地为贵族表演的)吟游歌手，吟游乐师； In medieval times, a minstrel was a singer and musician who travelled around and entertained noble families.
mint: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 薄荷； mint Mint is a herb with fresh-tasting leaves.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 薄荷糖； A mint is a sweet with a peppermint flavour.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 铸币厂； mint The mint is the place where the official coins of a country are made.  /  [VERB 动词] 铸造(硬币、奖章)； mint minting To mint coins or medals means to make them in a mint.
minted: [ADJ 形容词] 崭新的；新制作的；刚完成的； minted If you describe something as newly minted or freshly minted , you mean that it is very new, and that it has only just been produced or completed.
mint sauce: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 薄荷酱(一种用薄荷叶、醋和糖制成的酱，常与羊肉一起食用)； Mint sauce is a sauce made from mint leaves, vinegar, and sugar, which is often eaten with lamb.
minuet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 流行于17、18世纪的米奴哀舞曲;小步舞曲； In the music of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, a minuet is a piece of music with three beats in a bar which is played at moderate speed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 米奴哀舞;小步舞； A minuet is a fairly slow and formal dance which was popular in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
minus: [CONJ-COORD 连词] 减;减去； minus You use minus to show that one number or quantity is being subtracted from another.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 负的;小于零的； minus Minus before a number or quantity means that the number or quantity is less than zero.  /  减(指学校评分中某一等级中的“略差”，但又好于下一个等级)； minus Teachers use minus in grading work in schools and colleges.  /  [PREP 介词] 失去;缺少； minus To be minus something means not to have that thing.
minuscule: [ADJ 形容词] 极小的;微小的； minuscule If you describe something as minuscule , you mean that it is very small.
minus sign: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 负号;减号； A minus sign is the sign – which is put between two numbers in order to show that the second number is being subtracted from the first one.
minute: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分;分钟； minute A minute is one of the sixty parts that an hour is divided into.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 会议记录； minute The minutes of a meeting are the written records of the things that are discussed or decided at it.  /  [VERB 动词] 将…记入会议记录； minute When someone minutes something that is discussed or decided at a meeting, they make a written record of it.  /  See also: up-to-the-minute ;
minutely: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 仔细地;详细地； minutely You use minutely to indicate that something is done in great detail.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 微小地;很少地； minutely You use minutely to indicate that the size or extent of something is very small.
minutiae: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 琐碎细节;细枝末节； minutiae The minutiae of something such as someone's job or life are the very small details of it.
miracle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 奇迹;出人意料的事； miracle If you say that a good event is a miracle , you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (药物或产品)神奇的，不可思议的； miracle A miracle drug or product does something that was thought almost impossible.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (上帝创造的)神迹，圣迹； miracle A miracle is a wonderful and surprising event that is believed to be caused by God.
miracle worker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 奇迹的创造者； miracle worker If you describe someone as a miracle worker , you mean that they have achieved or are able to achieve success in something that other people have found very difficult.
miraculous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 神奇的;奇迹般的;不可思议的； miraculous miraculously If you describe a good event as miraculous , you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 超自然的；神奇的； miraculous miraculously If someone describes a wonderful event as miraculous , they believe that the event was caused by God.
mirage: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 海市蜃楼;幻境； mirage A mirage is something which you see when it is extremely hot, for example in the desert, and which appears to be quite near but is actually a long way away or does not really exist.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 妄想;幻想； mirage If you describe something as a mirage , you mean that it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.
mire: [N-SING 单数名词] 泥潭;困境;艰难处境； mire You can refer to an unpleasant or difficult situation as a mire of some kind.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 灰尘;烂泥;污泥； mire Mire is dirt or mud.
mirror: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 镜子； mirror mirrored A mirror is a flat piece of glass which reflects light, so that when you look at it you can see yourself reflected in it.  /  [VERB 动词] 反映;再现;与…相似； mirror If something mirrors something else, it has similar features to it, and therefore seems like a copy or representation of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 水照出，映出； mirror If you see something reflected in water, you can say that the water mirrors it.
mirror image: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 映像;翻版;倒影；反像;完全相同之物； mirror image If something is a mirror image of something else, it is like a reflection of it, either because it is exactly the same or because it is the same but reversed.
mirror site: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 镜像网站与另一网站内容相同，但网址略有不同，方便更多人登录受欢迎的网站； A mirror site is a website which is the same as another website operated by the same person or organization but has a slightly different address.
mirth: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 欢笑;欢乐； mirth Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.
mirthless: [ADJ 形容词] 并不快乐的;忧郁的； mirthless If someone gives a mirthless laugh or smile, it is obvious that they are not really amused.
mis-: [PREFIX 前缀] (用于动词和名词前，构成新的动词和名词)表示“坏的”，“错误的”，“糟糕地”，“不当地”； Mis- is added to some verbs and nouns to form new verbs and nouns which indicate that something is done badly or wrongly.
misadventure: [N-VAR 可变名词] 不幸事件；灾难； misadventure A misadventure is an unfortunate incident.
misanthrope: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 遁世者;厌恶世人者； A misanthrope is a person who does not like other people.
misanthropic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 遁世的;厌恶世人的； misanthropic If you describe a person or their feelings as misanthropic , you mean that they do not like other people.
misanthropy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 遁世;厌世； Misanthropy is a general dislike of people.
misapplication: [N-VAR 可变名词] 误用;滥用； misapplication If you talk about the misapplication of something, you mean it is used for a purpose it was not intended for.
misapply: [VERB 动词] 误用;滥用； If something is misapplied , it is used for a purpose for which it is not intended or not suitable.
misapprehension: [N-VAR 可变名词] 误解;误会； misapprehension A misapprehension is a wrong idea or impression that you have about something.
misappropriate: [VERB 动词] 盗用;挪用;侵吞； misappropriate misappropriation If someone misappropriates money which does not belong to them, they take it without permission and use it for their own purposes.
misbehave: [VERB 动词] (尤指儿童)行为不当，举止失礼； misbehave If someone, especially a child, misbehaves , they behave in a way that is not acceptable to other people.
misbehaviour: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 不当行为;失礼的举止； misbehaviour Misbehaviour is behaviour that is not acceptable to other people.
miscalculate: [VERB 动词] 判断错误;算错;误算； miscalculate miscalculation If you miscalculate , you make a mistake in judging a situation or in making a calculation.
miscarriage: [N-VAR 可变名词] 小产;流产； If a pregnant woman has a miscarriage , her baby dies and she gives birth to it before it is properly formed.
miscarriage of justice: [N-VAR 可变名词] 审判不公；误判；司法不公； miscarriage of justice A miscarriage of justice is a wrong decision made by a court, as a result of which an innocent person is punished.
miscarry: [VERB 动词] 小产;流产； miscarry If a woman miscarries , she has a miscarriage.
miscast: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 演员角色不合适的； If someone who is acting in a play or film is miscast , the role that they have is not suitable for them, so that they appear silly or unconvincing to the audience.
miscellaneous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 混杂的;五花八门的;各式各样的； miscellaneous A miscellaneous group consists of many different kinds of things or people that are difficult to put into a particular category.
miscellany: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 各式各样的东西;大杂烩； miscellany A miscellany of things is a collection or group of many different kinds of things.
mischief: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恶作剧;淘气;使坏的念头； mischief Mischief is playing harmless tricks on people or doing things you are not supposed to do.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 惹麻烦之事;引起问题的行为；损害;麻烦； mischief Mischief is behaviour that is intended to cause trouble for people.
mischief-maker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 挑拨离间的人;搬弄是非者； mischief-maker If you say that someone is a mischief-maker , you are criticizing them for saying or doing things which are intended to cause trouble between people.
mischievous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 调皮的;淘气的;恶作剧的； mischievous mischievously A mischievous person likes to have fun by playing harmless tricks on people or doing things they are not supposed to do.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 恶意的;不友善的;捣乱的； mischievous mischievously A mischievous act or suggestion is intended to cause trouble.
misconceived: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (计划、方法)设想错误的，不合适的； misconceived If you describe a plan or method as misconceived , you mean it is not the right one for dealing with a particular problem or situation.
misconception: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 错误观念;错误看法;误解； misconception A misconception is an idea that is not correct.
misconduct: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指专业人员的)渎职，不端行为，不当行为； misconduct Misconduct is bad or unacceptable behaviour, especially by a professional person.
misconstrue: [VERB 动词] 曲解;误解； misconstrue If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.
miscreant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不法之徒;恶棍;歹徒； miscreant A miscreant is someone who has done something illegal or behaved badly.
misdeed: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不端行为;恶行； misdeed A misdeed is a bad or evil act.
misdemeanour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不端行为;不检点的行为； misdemeanour A misdemeanour is an act that some people consider to be wrong or unacceptable.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 美国等国家的轻罪； misdemeanour In the United States and other countries where the legal system distinguishes between very serious crimes and less serious ones, a misdemeanour is a less serious crime.
misdirect: [VERB 动词] 对…使用不当;错用;误用； misdirect misdirected If resources or efforts are misdirected , they are used in the wrong way or for the wrong purposes.  /  [VERB 动词] 将…引错方向;给…指错方向； misdirect If you misdirect someone, you send them in the wrong direction.
miser: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吝啬鬼;守财奴； miser If you say that someone is a miser , you disapprove of them because they seem to hate spending money, and to spend as little as possible.
miserable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 苦恼的;痛苦的； miserable miserably If you are miserable , you are very unhappy.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (地方、形势)令人难受的，令人抑郁的； miserable If you describe a place or situation as miserable , you mean that it makes you feel unhappy or depressed.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (天气)阴郁的，令人苦恼的； miserable If you describe the weather as miserable , you mean that it makes you feel depressed, because it is raining or dull.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脾气坏的;不友善的;乖戾的； miserable If you describe someone as miserable , you mean that you do not like them because they are bad-tempered or unfriendly.

mythology: [N-VAR 可变名词] 神话;神话故事； mythology mythological Mythology is a group of myths, especially all the myths from a particular country, religion, or culture.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 错误的信念;谬误； mythology You can use mythology to refer to the beliefs or opinions that people have about something, when you think that they are false or untrue.

[CONVENTION 惯用语] 不适用;没货;没空； N.

naive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 天真的;幼稚的； naive naively naivety If you describe someone as naive , you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

nowhere: [ADV-INDEF-NEG 否定不定副词] 任何地方都不;没有别的地方会； nowhere You use nowhere to emphasize that a place has more of a particular quality than any other places, or that it is the only place where something happens or exists.  /  [ADV-INDEF-NEG 否定不定副词] 没有任何地方;无处； nowhere You use nowhere when making negative statements to say that a suitable place of the specified kind does not exist.  /  [ADV 副词] 没有踪影;找不到； nowhere You use nowhere to indicate that something or someone cannot be seen or found.  /  [ADV 副词] 在不重要的地方;在无趣之处； nowhere You can use nowhere to refer in a general way to small, unimportant, or uninteresting places.

numberless: [ADJ 形容词] 无数的;数不胜数的； numberless If there are numberless things, there are too many to be counted.

numbers game: [N-SING 单数名词] (通常为误导他人的)数字游戏； numbers game If you say that someone is playing the numbers game , you think that they are concentrating on the aspects of something which can be expressed in statistics, usually in order to mislead people.  /  See also: number ; �

numeracy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 识数;计算能力； numeracy Numeracy is the ability to do arithmetic.

nuptial: [ADJ 形容词] 结婚的;婚姻的； nuptial Nuptial is used to refer to things relating to a wedding or to marriage.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 结婚典礼;婚礼； nuptial Someone's nuptials are their wedding celebrations.
nurse: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE; N-VOC] [可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词] 护士； nurse A nurse is a person whose job is to care for people who are ill.  /  [VERB 动词] 护理;照顾;照料； nurse If you nurse someone, you care for them when they are ill.  /  [VERB 动词] 调养，调治(伤病)； nurse If you nurse an illness or injury, you allow it to get better by resting as much as possible.  /  [VERB 动词] 怀有，抱有(强烈的希望、愿望等)； nurse If you nurse an emotion or desire, you feel it strongly for a long time.
nursemaid: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保姆;保育员； A nursemaid is a woman or girl who is paid to look after young children.

nut: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 坚果;坚果仁； See also: groundnut ; hazelnut ; peanut ; The firm shelled fruit of some trees and bushes are called nuts .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 螺母;螺帽； nut A nut is a thick metal ring which you screw onto a metal rod called a bolt.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 对…着迷的人;…迷； nut If you describe someone as, for example, a football nut or a health nut , you mean that they are extremely enthusiastic about the thing mentioned.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 狂热的;执著的； nut If you are nuts about something or someone, you like them very much.

nutty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有坚果味的;坚果般的； nutty If you describe food as nutty , you mean that it tastes of nuts, has the texture of nuts, or is made with nuts.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 发疯的;疯疯癫癫的;痴呆的； nutty If you describe someone as nutty , you mean that their behaviour is very strange or foolish.

oblivion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无意识状态;沉睡;昏迷； oblivion Oblivion is the state of not being aware of what is happening around you, for example because you are asleep or unconscious.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 被遗忘的状态；湮没； oblivion Oblivion is the state of having been forgotten or of no longer being considered important.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 被摧毁；被毁灭；被夷为平地； oblivion If you say that something is bombed or blasted into oblivion , you are emphasizing that it is completely destroyed.

observable: [ADJ 形容词] 能看得见的；能察觉到的； observable Something that is observable can be seen.
observance: [N-VAR 可变名词] 对法律、习俗等的遵守，奉行； observance The observance of something such as a law or custom is the practice of obeying or following it.

observer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 观察者；观测者；目击者； observer You can refer to someone who sees or notices something as an observer .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 观察家;评论员； observer An observer is someone who studies current events and situations, especially in order to comment on them and predict what will happen next.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 监督重大事件或局势的观察员； observer An observer is a person who is sent to observe an important event or situation, especially in order to make sure it happens as it should, or so that they can tell other people about it.

occidental: [ADJ 形容词] 西方的；西方国家的；欧美的； occidental Occidental means relating to the countries of Europe and America.

occupation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 职业;工作； occupation Your occupation is your job or profession.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 消遣；日常需做的事务； occupation An occupation is something that you spend time doing, either for pleasure or because it needs to be done.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 占领;占据;侵占； occupation The occupation of a country happens when it is entered and controlled by a foreign army.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 对建筑物的占用,居住,使用； occupation The occupation of a building is the act or fact of someone living or working in it.
occupational: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 职业的；工作的； occupational occupationally Occupational means relating to a person's job or profession.

occupational therapy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 帮助患者或伤者培养或恢复技能的职业疗法； occupational therapy Occupational therapy is a method of helping people who have been ill or injured to develop skills or get skills back by giving them certain activities to do.
occupier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 房屋、公寓、土地的占用者，居住人，使用人； See also: owner-occupier ; The occupier of a house, flat, or piece of land is the person who lives or works there.
occupy: [VERB 动词] 居住，使用建筑物或某地； occupy The people who occupy a building or a place are the people who live or work there.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 占用，使用房间、座位等； If a room or something such as a seat is occupied , someone is using it, so that it is not available for anyone else.  /  [VERB 动词] 占领；占据；侵占； occupy If a group of people or an army occupies a place or country, they move into it, using force in order to gain control of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 担任[…职务]; 居于…地位； occupy If someone or something occupies a particular place in a system, process, or plan, they have that place.
occur: [VERB 动词] 发生； occur When something occurs , it happens.  /  [VERB 动词] 存在；出现；有； occur When something occurs in a particular place, it exists or is present there.  /  [VERB 动词] 想法或主意被想到，被想起，浮现于脑海中； occur If a thought or idea occurs to you, you suddenly think of it or realize it.
occurrence: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 发生的事情；事件； occurrence An occurrence is something that happens.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 发生；出现； occurrence The occurrence of something is the fact that it happens or is present.

oceanography: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 海洋学； oceanography oceanographer oceanographic Oceanography is the scientific study of sea currents, the sea bed, and the fish and animals that live in the sea.
och: [CONVENTION 惯用语] 表示惊讶，或强调赞同或反对啊，哦，呀，哟； Och is used to express surprise at something, or to emphasize agreement or disagreement with what has just been said.
ochre: [COLOUR 颜色词] 赭色；淡橘黄色； ochre Something that is ochre is a yellowish orange colour.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 赭石用于制作染料或颜料，通常为红色或黄色； Ochre is coloured earth, usually red or yellow, that is used to make dyes and paints.

octagon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 八边形；八角形； An octagon is a shape that has eight straight sides.
octagonal: [ADJ 形容词] 八边形的;八角形的； octagonal Something that is octagonal has eight straight sides.

octave: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 八度音阶；八度； An octave is a series of eight notes in a musical scale.
octet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 八重唱组合；八重奏乐团； An octet is a group of eight singers or musicians.

octogenarian: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 80至89岁的人；八旬老人； An octogenarian is a person who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old.
octopus: [N-VAR 可变名词] 章鱼； 作为食物的章鱼肉 An octopus is a soft sea creature with eight long arms called tentacles which it uses to catch food.
ocular: [ADJ 形容词] 眼睛的；视觉的； ocular Ocular means relating to the eyes or the ability to see.
OD: [VERB 动词] 同 overdose； OD To OD means the same as to overdose .
odd: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 奇怪的；古怪的；奇特的；异常的； odd oddly oddness See also: odd-looking ; If you describe someone or something as odd , you think that they are strange or unusual.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 用于名词前少量的，微小的，不重要的； odd You use odd before a noun to indicate that you are not mentioning the type, size, or quality of something because it is not important.  /  [ADV 副词] 用于数字后大约，左右，略多； odd You use odd after a number to indicate that it is only approximate.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 奇数的；单数的； odd Odd numbers, such as 3 and 17, are those which cannot be divided exactly by the number two.
oddball: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 行为古怪的人；怪人； oddball If you refer to someone as an oddball , you think they behave in a strange way.
oddity: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 怪人；怪事； oddity An oddity is someone or something that is very strange.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 奇怪；古怪；奇特； The oddity of something is the fact that it is very strange.
odd-job man: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指受雇于私人家庭的打零工者，干杂活者； An odd-job man is a man who is paid to do various jobs such as cleaning or repairing things, usually in someone's home.
odd-looking: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 相貌奇特的；外表怪异的;奇形怪状的； odd-looking If you describe someone or something as odd-looking , you think that they look strange or unusual.
oddly: [ADV 副词] 奇怪的是；说来也怪； oddly See also: odd ; You use oddly to indicate that what you are saying is true, but that it is not what you expected.
oddment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 边角料；残余物；零碎物品； oddment Oddments are unimportant objects of any kind, usually ones that are old or left over from a larger group of things.
odds: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 机会；可能性；几率； odds See also: odds-on ; You refer to how likely something is to happen as the odds that it will happen.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 赌博中的赔率； odds In betting, odds are expressions with numbers such as '10 to 1' and '7 to 2' that show how likely something is thought to be, for example how likely a particular horse is to lose or win a race.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 与…不和；与…有矛盾；与…意见不一致； odds If someone is at odds with someone else, or if two people are at odds , they are disagreeing or quarrelling with each other.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 成功可能性小，希望渺茫； odds If you say that the odds are against something or someone, you mean that they are unlikely to succeed.
odds and ends: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 零碎东西；琐碎的事； odds and ends You can refer to a disorganized group of things of various kinds as odds and ends .
odds-on: [ADJ 形容词] 大有可能发生的；大有希望的； odds-on If there is an odds-on chance that something will happen, it is very likely that it will happen.
ode: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 颂诗；颂歌； An ode is a poem, especially one that is written in praise of a particular person, thing, or event.
odious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人厌恶的；令人讨厌的；可憎的； odious If you describe people or things as odious , you think that they are extremely unpleasant.
odium: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 通常指因他人做过某事而对其产生的憎恨，厌恶，不满； odium Odium is the dislike, disapproval, or hatred that people feel for a particular person, usually because of something that the person has done.
odometer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 里程表；计程器； An odometer is a device in a vehicle which shows how far the vehicle has travelled.
odour: [N-VAR 可变名词] 气味； odour See also: body odour ; An odour is a particular and distinctive smell.
odourless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无气味的；无臭的； odourless An odourless substance has no smell.
odyssey: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 漫长而又刺激的行程； odyssey An odyssey is a long exciting journey on which a lot of things happen.

oestrogen: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 雌激素； oestrogen Oestrogen is a hormone produced in the ovaries of female animals.
of: In addition to the uses shown below, of is used after some verbs, nouns, and adjectives in order to introduce extra information.  /  [PREP 介词] 用于连接两个名词，其中前者表示后者的特定方面； of You use of to combine two nouns when the first noun identifies the feature of the second noun that you want to talk about.  /  [PREP 介词] 用于连接两个名词或名词与现在分词，其中后者对前者进行界定或补充信息； of You use of to combine two nouns, or a noun and a present participle, when the second noun or present participle defines or gives more information about the first noun.  /  [PREP 介词] 用于指称动作的名词后说明该动作的对象或主体； of You use of after nouns referring to actions to specify the person or thing that is affected by the action or that performs the action.

offal: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 供食用的动物内脏，杂碎； Offal is the internal organs of animals, for example their hearts and livers, when they are cooked and eaten.

offbeat: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不寻常的；非常规的；非正统的； offbeat If you describe something or someone as offbeat , you think that they are different from normal.

off-chance: [PHRASE 短语] 心存侥幸地；怀着渺茫希望地； off-chance If you do something on the off-chance , you do it because you hope that it will succeed, although you think that this is unlikely.
off-colour: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不舒服的；身体欠佳的； off-colour If you say that you are feeling off-colour , you mean that you are slightly ill.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 表现差强人意的；状态不佳的； off-colour If you say that someone's performance is off-colour , you mean that they are not performing as well as they usually do.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 笑话、言语近乎下流的，不成体统的； An off-colour joke or remark is rather rude or offensive.

offence: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 违法行为；罪行； offence An offence is a crime that breaks a particular law and requires a particular punishment.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 冒犯；得罪； offence Offence or an offence is behaviour which causes people to be upset or embarrassed.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 体育运动中的进攻队，进攻方； In sports such as American football or basketball, the offense is the team which has possession of the ball and is trying to score.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 冒犯；得罪；惹恼； offence If you cause offence or give offence to someone, you say or do something rude which upsets or embarrasses them.

offensive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 冒犯的；得罪人的；唐突的;无礼的； offensive offensively Something that is offensive upsets or embarrasses people because it is rude or insulting.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 进攻； offensive A military offensive is a carefully planned attack made by a large group of soldiers.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 表示愤怒或反对的强硬行动； offensive See also: charm offensive ; If you conduct an offensive , you take strong action to show how angry you are about something or how much you disapprove of something.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 体育运动中球队进攻的，攻方的； offensive In sports such as American football or basketball, the offensive team is the team which has possession of the ball and is trying to score.

outfitter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 专门的服装商店，装备商店； outfitter also outfitters.
outfitters: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 专门的服装商店，装备商店； outfitters also outfitters.
outflank: [VERB 动词] 侧翼包抄； outflank In a battle, when one group of soldiers outflanks another, it succeeds in moving past the other group in order to be able to attack it from the side.  /  [VERB 动词] 占…的上风； outflank If you outflank someone, you succeed in getting into a position where you can defeat them, for example in an argument.
outflow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 金钱、人等的外流，流出； outflow When there is an outflow of money or people, a large amount of money or people move from one place to another.
outfox: [VERB 动词] 智胜；谋略上比…更胜一筹； outfox If you outfox someone, you defeat them in some way because you are cleverer than they are.
outgoing: [ADJ 形容词] 即将离职的；快要卸任的； outgoing You use outgoing to describe a person in charge of something who is soon going to leave that position.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 离去的；往外去的； outgoing Outgoing things such as planes, mail, and passengers are leaving or being sent somewhere.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 外向的；友好的；喜欢交际的； outgoing Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.
outgoings: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 经常性开支，开销； outgoings Your outgoings are the regular amounts of money which you have to spend every week or every month, for example in order to pay your rent or bills.
outgrow: [VERB 动词] 小孩长得穿不下衣服； outgrow If a child outgrows a piece of clothing, they grow bigger, so that it no longer fits them.  /  [VERB 动词] 因长大而放弃以前的行为或想法； outgrow If you outgrow a particular way of behaving or thinking, you change and become more mature, so that you no longer behave or think in that way.
outgrowth: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 产物；自然发展的结果； outgrowth Something that is an outgrowth of another thing has developed naturally as a result of it.
outguess: [VERB 动词] 猜出…的意图；看透； outguess If you outguess someone, you try to predict what they are going to do in order to gain some advantage.
outgun: [VERB 动词] 在火力上超过，压过； outgun In a battle, if one army is outgunned , they are in a very weak position because the opposing army has more or better weapons.  /  [VERB 动词] 在竞赛中超过，胜过； outgun If you are outgunned in a contest, you are beaten because your rival is stronger or better than you.
outhouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 附属建筑；外围建筑；外屋； An outhouse is a small building attached to a house or very close to the house, used, for example, for storing things in.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 户外厕所； An outhouse is an outside toilet.
outing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指集体远足，短途旅行； outing An outing is a short enjoyable trip, usually with a group of people, away from your home, school, or place of work.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 体育比赛； outing In sport, an outing is an occasion when a player competes in a particular contest or competition.  /  See also: out ; �
outlandish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 稀奇古怪的；异乎寻常的；不切实际的； outlandish If you describe something as outlandish , you disapprove of it because you think it is very unusual, strange, or unreasonable.
outlast: [VERB 动词] 比…活得长；比…持久； outlast If one thing outlasts another thing, the first thing lives or exists longer than the second.
outlaw: [VERB 动词] 宣布…为非法；使成为非法； outlaw When something is outlawed , it is made illegal.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 逃犯；亡命之徒； outlaw An outlaw is a criminal who is hiding from the authorities.
outlay: [N-VAR 可变名词] 必要的费用，开支； outlay Outlay is the amount of money that you have to spend in order to buy something or start a project.
outlet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 经销店；专营店； outlet An outlet is a shop or organization which sells the goods made by a particular manufacturer.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 廉价商品经销店；折扣店； outlet An outlet or an outlet store is a place which sells slightly damaged or outdated goods from a particular manufacturer, or goods that it made in greater quantities than needed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 情感的发泄途径；思想的表达方式； outlet If someone has an outlet for their feelings or ideas, they have a means of expressing and releasing them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 出口；排放管； outlet An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow away.
outline: [VERB 动词] 概述；概括； outline If you outline an idea or a plan, you explain it in a general way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 概要；梗概； outline An outline is a general explanation or description of something.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 因背后的光线显示…的轮廓或外形； outline You say that an object is outlined when you can see its general shape because there is light behind it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指模糊的轮廓，外形； outline The outline of something is its general shape, especially when it cannot be clearly seen.
outlive: [VERB 动词] 比…活得长;比…持久； outlive If one person outlives another, they are still alive after the second person has died.
outlook: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 世界观；人生观；对生活的观点，看法； outlook Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 展望；前景；可能性； outlook The outlook for something is what people think will happen in relation to it.
outlying: [ADJ 形容词] 偏僻的；边远的；远离城市的； outlying Outlying places are far away from the main cities of a country.
outmanoeuvre: [VERB 动词] 智胜；比…技高一筹； outmanoeuvre If you outmanoeuvre someone, you gain an advantage over them in a particular situation by behaving in a clever and skilful way.
outmoded: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过时的；老式的；废弃的；无用的； outmoded If you describe something as outmoded , you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.
outnumber: [VERB 动词] 在数量上压倒，比…多； outnumber If one group of people or things outnumbers another, the first group has more people or things in it than the second group.
out-of-body: [ADJ 形容词] 体验离体的，灵魂出窍的； An out-of-body experience is one in which you feel as if you are outside your own body, watching it and what is going on around it.
out of date: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 过时的；陈旧的；老式的；废弃的； out of date Something that is out of date is old-fashioned and no longer useful.
out of doors: 在户外；在露天； out of doors also out-of-doors.
out-of-pocket: [ADJ 形容词] 费用自掏腰包垫付的； out-of-pocket See also: pocket ; Out-of-pocket expenses are those which you pay out of your own money on behalf of someone else, and which are often paid back to you later.
out-of-the-way: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 偏僻的；人迹罕至的； out-of-the-way Out-of-the-way places are difficult to reach and are therefore not often visited.
out of touch: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不了解最新情况的； out of touch Someone who is out of touch with a situation is not aware of recent changes in it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 与某人未有联系的，失去音讯的； out of touch If you are out of touch with someone, you have not been in contact with them recently and are not familiar with their present situation.
out-of-town: [ADJ 形容词] 城外的；市郊的； out-of-town Out-of-town shops or facilities are situated away from the centre of a town or city.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 外来的；非本地的； out-of-town Out-of-town is used to describe people who do not live in a particular town or city, but have travelled there for a particular purpose.
out of work: [ADJ 形容词] 失业的；下岗的； out of work Someone who is out of work does not have a job.
outpace: [VERB 动词] 比…快；超过；胜过； outpace To outpace someone or something means to perform a particular action faster or better than they can.
outpatient: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 门诊病人； outpatient An outpatient is someone who receives treatment at a hospital but does not spend the night there.
outperform: [VERB 动词] 做得比…好；比…更高效； outperform If one thing outperforms another, the first is more successful or efficient than the second.
outplacement: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 新职介绍；再就业服务； An outplacement agency gives advice to managers and other professional people who have recently become unemployed, and helps them find new jobs.
outplay: [VERB 动词] 在体育比赛中打得比…好，战胜，击败； outplay In sports, if one person or team outplays an opposing person or team, they play much better than their opponents.
outpoint: [VERB 动词] 在拳击比赛中以点数战胜； outpoint In boxing, if one boxer outpoints another, they win the match by getting more points than their opponent.
outpost: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 贸易站；前哨基地；设在国外的军事基地； outpost An outpost is a small group of buildings used for trading or military purposes, either in a distant part of your own country or in a foreign country.
outpouring: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 感情、反应等的迸发，爆发，倾泻； outpouring An outpouring of something such as an emotion or a reaction is the expression of it in an uncontrolled way.
output: [N-VAR 可变名词] 产量；输出量；排出量； output Output is used to refer to the amount of something that a person or thing produces.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 计算机、文字处理器等的输出信息，输出文件； output The output of a computer or word processor is the information that it displays on a screen or prints on paper as a result of a particular program.
outrage: [VERB 动词] 使震怒;激怒； outrage outraged If you are outraged by something, it makes you extremely shocked and angry.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 愤慨；义愤； outrage Outrage is an intense feeling of anger and shock.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 暴行；骇人听闻的事件； outrage You can refer to an act or event which you find very shocking as an outrage .
outrageous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人无法容忍的；骇人的； outrageous outrageously If you describe something as outrageous , you are emphasizing that it is unacceptable or very shocking.
outran: + + + Outran is the past tense of outrun .
outrank: [VERB 动词] 级别高于…；职位在…之上； outrank If one person outranks another person, he or she has a higher position or grade within an organization than the other person.
outreach: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 外展服务；扩大服务； outreach Outreach programmes and schemes try to find people who need help or advice rather than waiting for those people to come and ask for help.
outrider: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 为官方车辆开道的摩托车警卫，骑士护卫； outrider Outriders are people such as policemen who ride on motorcycles or horses beside or in front of an official vehicle, in order to protect the people in the vehicle.
outright: [ADJ 形容词] 直率的；公开的；直截了当的； outright You use outright to describe behaviour and actions that are open and direct, rather than indirect.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 完全的；彻底的；全部的； outright 当场或立即死亡 Outright means complete and total.
outrun: [VERB 动词] 跑得比…快； outrun If you outrun someone, you run faster than they do, and therefore are able to escape from them or to arrive somewhere before they do.  /  [VERB 动词] 超过；超出；发展快于； outrun If one thing outruns another thing, the first thing develops faster than the second thing.
outsell: [VERB 动词] 比…卖得快；销量胜过； outsell If one product outsells another product, the first product is sold more quickly or in larger quantities than the second.
outset: [PHRASE 短语] 在开始时/ 从一开始； outset If something happens at the outset of an event, process, or period of time, it happens at the beginning of it.
outshine: [VERB 动词] 比…更优秀；比…更出色；胜过； outshine If you outshine someone at a particular activity, you are much better at it than they are.
outside: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外面；外部；外表； outside The outside of something is the part which surrounds or encloses the rest of it.  /  [ADV 副词] 在外面；在室外；在建筑物近旁； outside If you are outside , you are not inside a building but are quite close to it.  /  [PREP 介词] 在房间的外面； outside If you are outside a room, you are not in it but are in the passage or area next to it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 外部世界的；外界的； outside When you talk about the outside world, you are referring to things that happen or exist in places other than your own home or community.
outside broadcast: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 现场录制的节目；实地拍摄的节目； An outside broadcast is a radio or television programme that is not recorded or filmed in a studio, but in another building or in the open air.
outsider: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 某个团体或组织外部的人； outsider An outsider is someone who does not belong to a particular group or organization.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不为某一团体所接受或感觉不属其中的外人； outsider An outsider is someone who is not accepted by a particular group, or who feels that they do not belong in it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 在竞赛中不大可能获胜的人或队伍； outsider In a competition, an outsider is a competitor who is unlikely to win.
outsize: [ADJ 形容词] 超大型的；极大的； outsize Outsize or outsized things are much larger than usual or much larger than you would expect.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 衣服超大号的，加大码的； outsize Outsize clothes are clothes for very large people.
outskirts: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 市郊；郊区； outskirts The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its centre.
outsmart: [VERB 动词] 智胜；比…更机灵；比…更精明； outsmart If you outsmart someone, you defeat them or gain an advantage over them in a clever and sometimes dishonest way.
outsold: + + + Outsold is the past tense and past participle of outsell .
outsource: [VERB 动词] 将…外包；外购； outsource outsourcing If a company outsources work or things, it pays workers from outside the company to do the work or supply the things.
outspoken: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坦率的；直言不讳的； outspoken outspokenness Someone who is outspoken gives their opinions about things openly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.
outstanding: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 杰出的；出众的；优秀的； outstanding If you describe someone or something as outstanding , you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 款项未支付的，未结清的； outstanding Money that is outstanding has not yet been paid and is still owed to someone.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 未解决的；未完成的； outstanding Outstanding issues or problems have not yet been resolved.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 重要的；显著的；突出的； outstanding Outstanding means very important or obvious.
outstandingly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 表示强调极其，非常； outstandingly You use outstandingly to emphasize how good, or occasionally how bad, something is.
outstretched: [ADJ 形容词] 张开的；伸开的；展开的； outstretched If a part of the body of a person or animal is outstretched , it is stretched out as far as possible.
outstrip: [VERB 动词] 超过；胜过； outstrip If one thing outstrips another, the first thing becomes larger in amount, or more successful or important, than the second thing.
outtake: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 影片、唱片等的弃用片段； An out-take is a piece of film or a song that is not in the final version of a programme, film, or record, for example because it contains a mistake.
out-take: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 影片、唱片等的弃用片段； out-take An out-take is a piece of film or a song that is not in the final version of a programme, film, or record, for example because it contains a mistake.
out-there: [ADJ 形容词] 极端的；异乎寻常的； out-there Someone or something that is out-there is very extreme or unusual.
out tray: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 办公室的发文篮，发件盘； also out-tray.
outvote: [VERB 动词] 通过投票击败；以多数票击败； outvote If you are outvoted , more people vote against what you are suggesting than vote for it, so that your suggestion is defeated.
outward: [ADJ 形容词] 向外的;外出的； outward An outward journey is a journey that you make away from a place that you are intending to return to later.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 外表的；表面上的； outward The outward feelings, qualities, or attitudes of someone or something are the ones they appear to have rather than the ones that they actually have.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 特定方面可见的，外部的； outward The outward features of something are the ones that you can see from the outside.  /  See also: outwards ; �
outwardly: [ADV 副词] 外表上；表面上； outwardly You use outwardly to indicate the feelings or qualities that a person or situation may appear to have, rather than the ones that they actually have.
outwards: [ADV 副词] 向外;朝外； outwards If something moves or faces outwards , it moves or faces away from the place you are in or the place you are talking about.  /  [ADV 副词] 注意力向外地，对外地； outwards If you say that a person or a group of people, such as a government, looks outwards , you mean that they turn their attention to another group that they are interested in or would like greater involvement with.
outweigh: [VERB 动词] 在重要性、益处、意义等上重于，大于，超过； outweigh If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.
outwit: [VERB 动词] 智胜；用计击败或超过； outwit If you outwit someone, you use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or to gain an advantage over them.
outwith: [PREP 介词] 苏格兰英语中同 outside； outwith In Scottish English, outwith means outside.
outworn: [ADJ 形容词] 信仰、习俗过时的，陈腐的，废弃的，无用的； outworn If you describe a belief or custom as outworn , you mean that it is old-fashioned and no longer has any meaning or usefulness.
ouzo: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 希腊的茴香烈酒； 一杯茴香烈酒 Ouzo is a strong aniseed-flavoured alcoholic drink that is made in Greece.
ova: [ovum 的复数] ； Ova is the plural of ovum .
oval: [ADJ 形容词] 椭圆形的；卵形的； oval Oval things have a shape that is like a circle but is wider in one direction than the other.
ovarian: [ADJ 形容词] 卵巢的； ovarian Ovarian means in or relating to the ovaries.
ovary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 卵巢； A woman's ovaries are the two organs in her body that produce eggs.
ovation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 热烈欢迎；热烈鼓掌； ovation See also: standing ovation ; An ovation is a large amount of applause from an audience for a particular performer or speaker.
oven: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 烤箱；烤炉； oven An oven is a device for cooking that is like a box with a door.
ovenproof: [ADJ 形容词] 盘等适于烤箱内用的，耐热的； An ovenproof dish is one that has been specially made to be used in an oven without being damaged by the heat.
over: In addition to the uses shown below, over is used after some verbs, nouns, and adjectives in order to introduce extra information.  /  [PREP 介词] 在…的上方；在…的上面；在…的上空； over If one thing is over another thing or is moving over it, the first thing is directly above the second, either resting on it, or with a space between them.  /  [PREP 介词] 搭挂在…的上面； over If one thing is over another thing, it is supported by it and its ends are hanging down on each side of it.  /  [PREP 介词] 部分或完全地覆盖在…的上面； over If one thing is over another thing, it covers part or all of it.
over-: [PREFIX 前缀] 用于形容词或动词后表示“过分”，“过度”； over- You can add over- to an adjective or verb to indicate that a quality exists or an action is done to too great an extent.
overachieve: [VERB 动词] 在学业或工作上过于强求成功，过于争强好胜； overachieve overachiever If someone overachieves in something such as school work or a job, they work very hard, especially in a way that makes them tired or unhappy.
overact: [VERB 动词] 通常指在戏剧中表演得过于夸张，感情或动作过火； overact If you say that someone overacts , you mean they exaggerate their emotions and movements, usually when acting in a play.
over-age: [ADJ 形容词] 超过规定或合格年龄的； over-age If you are over-age , you are officially too old to do something.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 过老的；扮嫩的； over-age You use over-age to describe someone who is doing something that is usually done by much younger people, and which therefore seems inappropriate or silly.
overall: [ADJ 形容词] 总的；总体的；全面的； overall You use overall to indicate that you are talking about a situation in general or about the whole of something.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 上下连身的工作服，防护服； overall Overalls consist of a single piece of clothing that combines trousers and a jacket.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 吊带工装裤； overall Overalls are trousers that are attached to a piece of cloth which covers your chest and which has straps going over your shoulders.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 工作时穿的罩衣； An overall is a piece of clothing shaped like a coat that you wear over your clothes in order to protect them while you are working.
overall majority: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 选举或投票时的压倒性多数票，绝对多数票； If a political party wins an overall majority in an election or vote, they get more votes than the total number of votes or seats won by all their opponents.
overarching: [ADJ 形容词] 包罗万象的；影响一切的； overarching You use overarching to indicate that you are talking about something that includes or affects everything or everyone.
overarm: [ADJ 形容词] 投球等上手的，举手过肩的； overarm You use overarm to describe actions, such as throwing a ball, in which you stretch your arm over your shoulder.
overawe: [VERB 动词] 使极为敬畏；慑服； overawe overawed If you are overawed by something or someone, you are very impressed by them and a little afraid of them.
overbalance: [VERB 动词] 失去平衡；跌倒； overbalance If you overbalance , you fall over or nearly fall over, because you are not standing properly.
overbearing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 傲慢的；专横的；盛气凌人的；飞扬跋扈的； overbearing An overbearing person tries to make other people do what he or she wants in an unpleasant and forceful way.
overblown: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 夸张的；过分的；夸大其词的； overblown Something that is overblown makes something seem larger, more important, or more significant than it really is.
overboard: [ADV 副词] 向舷外； overboard If you fall overboard , you fall over the side of a boat into the water.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 做得过分或过火； overboard If you say that someone goes overboard , you mean that they do something to a greater extent than is necessary or reasonable.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 抛弃，丢弃想法、建议等； overboard If you throw something overboard , for example an idea or suggestion, you reject it completely.
overbook: [VERB 动词] 航空公司、剧团等超额预订； overbook If an organization such as an airline or a theatre company overbooks , they sell more tickets than they have places for.
overbooked: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 旅馆、公共汽车、飞机等超额预订的； overbooked If something such as a hotel, bus, or aircraft is overbooked , more people have booked than the number of places that are available.
overburdened: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 系统、机构等负担过重的，不堪重负的； overburdened If a system or organization is overburdened , it has too many people or things to deal with and so does not function properly.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人因工作、问题等负担过重的，不堪应付的； overburdened If you are overburdened with something such as work or problems, you have more of it than you can cope with.
overcame: + + + Overcame is the past tense of overcome .
overcapacity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 生产能力过剩； overcapacity If there is overcapacity in a particular industry or area, more goods have been produced than are needed, and the industry is therefore less profitable than it could be.
overcast: [ADJ 形容词] 多云的；阴沉的；阴天的； overcast If it is overcast , or if the sky or the day is overcast , the sky is completely covered with cloud and there is not much light.
overcharge: [VERB 动词] 对…要价或收费过高； overcharge overcharging If someone overcharges you, they charge you too much for their goods or services.
overcoat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大衣；厚外套； An overcoat is a thick warm coat that you wear in winter.
overcome: [VERB 动词] 克服；控制；战胜； overcome If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.  /  [VERB 动词] 感情上受到极大影响，承受不起； overcome If you are overcome by a feeling or event, it is so strong or has such a strong effect that you cannot think clearly.  /  [VERB 动词] 烟、毒气等熏倒，使受不了； overcome If you are overcome by smoke or a poisonous gas, you become very ill or die from breathing it in.
overcrowded: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 地方过度拥挤的； overcrowded An overcrowded place has too many things or people in it.
overcrowding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 过度拥挤；拥挤不堪； overcrowding If there is a problem of overcrowding , there are more people living in a place than it was designed for.
overdo: [VERB 动词] 把…做得过分；把…做得过火；对…过于夸张； overdo If someone overdoes something, they behave in an exaggerated or extreme way.  /  [VERB 动词] 超出体力负荷地做； overdo If you overdo an activity, you try to do more than you can physically manage.
overdone: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 煮得过久的；煮得太烂的； overdone If food is overdone , it has been spoiled by being cooked for too long.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 做得过分的；做得夸张的； overdone If you say that something is overdone , you mean that you think it is excessive or exaggerated.
overdose: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 药物等的过量；致死或中毒剂量； overdose If someone takes an overdose of a drug, they take more of it than is safe.  /  [VERB 动词] 过量服用[药物]; 过量吸食毒品； overdose If someone overdoses on a drug, they take more of it than is safe.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指有害物的过量，过多； overdose You can refer to too much of something, especially something harmful, as an overdose .  /  [VERB 动词] 过多拥有；沉溺； overdose You can say that someone overdoses on something if they have or do too much of it.
overdraft: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 透支；透支额； overdraft If you have an overdraft , you have spent more money than you have in your bank account, and so you are in debt to the bank.
overdrawn: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 透支的； overdrawn If you are overdrawn or if your bank account is overdrawn , you have spent more money than you have in your account, and so you are in debt to the bank.
overdressed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 穿得过于正式或讲究的； If you say that someone is overdressed , you are criticizing them for wearing clothes that are not appropriate for the occasion because they are too formal or too smart.
overdrive: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 汽车的超速挡，超速变速器； overdrive The overdrive in a vehicle is a very high gear that is used when you are driving at high speeds.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 加倍努力或紧张； overdrive If you go into overdrive , you begin to work very hard or perform a particular activity in a very intense way.
overdue: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 变化或事件早该发生的； overdue If you say that a change or an event is overdue , you mean that you think it should have happened before now.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 钱款到期未付的，拖欠的； overdue Overdue sums of money have not been paid, even though it is later than the date on which they should have been paid.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 图书馆的书逾期未还的； An overdue library book has not been returned to the library, even though the date on which it should have been returned has passed.
overeat: [VERB 动词] 暴食；吃得过量；吃撑； overeat overeater overeating If you say that someone overeats , you mean they eat more than they need to or more than is healthy.
overemphasis: [N-SING 单数名词] 过分强调；过分注重； overemphasis If you say that there is an overemphasis on a particular thing, you mean that more importance or attention is given to it than is necessary.
overemphasize: [VERB 动词] 过分强调；过分注重； overemphasize If you say that someone overemphasizes something, you mean that they give it more importance than it deserves or than you consider appropriate.  /  [VERB 动词] 再怎么强调都不为过； overemphasize If you say that something cannot be overemphasized , you are emphasizing that you think it is very important.
overestimate: [VERB 动词] 过高估计数量、重要性等； overestimate overestimation If you say that someone overestimates something, you mean that they think it is greater in amount or importance than it really is.  /  [VERB 动词] 再怎么估量都不为过； overestimate If you say that something cannot be overestimated , you are emphasizing that you think it is very important.  /  [VERB 动词] 过高评价某人； overestimate If you overestimate someone, you think that they have more of a skill or quality than they really have.
overexcited: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 兴奋过头的；兴奋得忘乎所以的； If you say that someone is over-excited , you mean that they are more excited than you think is desirable.
over-excited: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 兴奋过头的；兴奋得忘乎所以的； over-excited If you say that someone is over-excited , you mean that they are more excited than you think is desirable.
overexposed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 照片曝光过度的； An overexposed photograph is of poor quality because the film has been exposed to too much light, either when the photograph was taken or during the developing process.
overextended: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 经济或体力上参与过多活动的，捉襟见肘的； overextended If a person or organization is overextended , they have become involved in more activities than they can financially or physically manage.
overflight: [N-VAR 可变名词] 飞越领空； overflight An overflight is the passage of an aircraft from one country over another country's territory.
overflow: [VERB 动词] 漫出；溢出；泛滥； overflow If a liquid or a river overflows , it flows over the edges of the container or place it is in.  /  [VERB 动词] 充满；挤满；装满； overflow If a place or container is overflowing with people or things, it is too full of them.  /  [VERB 动词] 洋溢着[情感]; 情感溢于言表； overflow If someone is overflowing with a feeling or if the feeling overflows , the person is experiencing it very strongly and shows this in their behaviour.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 过多而容纳不下的人或东西； overflow The overflow is the extra people or things that something cannot contain or deal with because it is not large enough.
overfly: [VERB 动词] 飞越；飞过； overfly When an aircraft overflies an area, it flies over it.
overground: [ADJ 形容词] 交通系统在地面上的； overground In an overground transport system, vehicles run on the surface of the ground, rather than below it.
overgrown: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 杂草丛生的；植被蔓生的； overgrown If a garden or other place is overgrown , it is covered with a lot of untidy plants because it has not been looked after.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 成年人不成熟的，孩子气的； overgrown If you describe an adult as an overgrown child, you mean that their behaviour and attitudes are like those of a child, and that you dislike this.
overhang: [VERB 动词] 悬于…之上；凸出于…之上； overhang If one thing overhangs another, it sticks out over and above it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 垂悬物；凸出物； overhang An overhang is the part of something that sticks out over and above something else.  /  [VERB 动词] 搭挂在…之上； overhang If one thing overhangs another, it is supported by it and hangs down its sides.
overhaul: [VERB 动词] 大修；彻底检修；全面检查； overhaul If a piece of equipment is overhauled , it is cleaned, checked thoroughly, and repaired if necessary.  /  [VERB 动词] 对…进行彻底革新；全面修订； overhaul If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.  /  [VERB 动词] 尤指在体育比赛中赶上，超过，超越； overhaul If someone overhauls a person who is ahead of them, especially in a sports competition, they pass them or become more successful than them.
overhead: [ADJ 形容词] 在头顶上的；在上面的；高架的； overhead You use overhead to indicate that something is above you or above the place that you are talking about.
overhead projector: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 高射投影器[缩略形式为OHP] ； An overhead projector is a machine that has a light inside it and makes the writing or pictures on a sheet of plastic appear on a screen or wall.
overheads: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 企业的间接费用，营运费用，经常性开支； overheads The overheads of a business are its regular and essential expenses, such as salaries, rent, electricity, and telephone bills.
overhear: [VERB 动词] 偶然听到；无意中听到；偷听到； overhear If you overhear someone, you hear what they are saying when they are not talking to you and they do not know that you are listening.
overheat: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 把…加热过度；使变得过热； overheat overheated If something overheats or if you overheat it, it becomes hotter than is necessary or desirable.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使经济发展过快；使发展过热； overheat overheated If a country's economy overheats or if conditions overheat it, it grows so rapidly that inflation and interest rates rise very quickly.
overheated: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 十分愤怒的；过于激烈的； overheated Someone who is overheated is very angry about something.
overhung: + + + Overhung is the past tense and past participle of overhang .
overindulge: [VERB 动词] 过于沉溺[于]; 通常指过多地吃或喝； overindulge If you overindulge , or overindulge in something that you like very much, usually food or drink, you allow yourself to have more of it than is good for you.
overjoyed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 欣喜若狂的；万分高兴的； overjoyed If you are overjoyed , you are extremely pleased about something.
overkill: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 过分；过火的行为； overkill You can say that something is overkill when you think that there is more of it than is necessary or appropriate.
overland: [ADJ 形容词] 经由陆路的；横跨陆地的； overland An overland journey is made across land rather than by ship or aeroplane.
overlap: [V-RECIP-ERG ] 与…互搭；与…复叠；使相叠； overlap If one thing overlaps another, or if you overlap them, a part of the first thing occupies the same area as a part of the other thing.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 在主题、人物、时间等上与…部分相同，与…部分交叉； overlap If one idea or activity overlaps another, or overlaps with another, they involve some of the same subjects, people, or periods of time.
overlay: [VERB 动词] 在…上覆盖或铺、涂； If something is overlaid with something else, it is covered by it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 覆盖物；涂层； overlay You can use overlay to refer to a substance which covers the surface of something.  /  [VERB 动词] 以某一情感、特性等遮掩； overlay If something is overlaid with a feeling or quality, that feeling or quality is the most noticeable one, but there may be deeper and more important ones involved.
overleaf: [ADV 副词] 在书页、杂志页等的背面；在页后； overleaf Overleaf is used in books and magazines to say that something is on the other side of the page you are reading.
overload: [VERB 动词] 使超载；使负载过重； overload overloaded If you overload something such as a vehicle, you put more things or people into it than it was designed to carry.  /  [VERB 动词] 使负担过重；给予…过多的工作或问题、信息等； overload overloaded To overload someone with work, problems, or information means to give them more work, problems, or information than they can cope with.  /  [VERB 动词] 使电力系统过载；使超过负荷； overload If you overload an electrical system, you cause too much electricity to flow through it, and so damage it.
overlook: [VERB 动词] 俯瞰；俯视；眺望； overlook If a building or window overlooks a place, you can see the place clearly from the building or window.  /  [VERB 动词] 忽略；忽视；未注意到； overlook If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.  /  [VERB 动词] 宽容；宽恕； overlook If you overlook someone's faults or bad behaviour, you forgive them and take no action.
overlord: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 霸主；巨头； overlord If you refer to someone as an overlord , you mean that they have great power and are likely to use it in a bad way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旧时的君主，领主； overlord In former times, an overlord was someone who had power over many people.
overly: [ADV 副词] 过度地；过分地； overly Overly means more than is normal, necessary, or reasonable.
overmanned: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人员过多的；人浮于事的； overmanned If you say that a place or an industry is overmanned , you mean that you think there are more people working there or doing the work than is necessary.
overmanning: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人员过多；人浮于事； If there is a problem of overmanning in an industry, there are more people working there or doing the work than is necessary.
overmuch: [ADV 副词] 过多；太多；很多； overmuch If something happens overmuch , it happens too much or very much.
overnight: [ADV 副词] 在整个夜间；在夜里的某一时刻； overnight If something happens overnight , it happens throughout the night or at some point during the night.  /  [ADV 副词] 突然；一下子；一夜之间； overnight You can say that something happens overnight when it happens very quickly and unexpectedly.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 只供一两晚使用的； overnight Overnight bags or clothes are ones that you take when you go and stay somewhere for one or two nights.  /  [VERB 动词] 过夜； overnight If you overnight somewhere, you spend the night there.
overpaid: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 报酬过高的；工资过高的； overpaid See also: overpay ; If you say that someone is overpaid , you mean that you think they are paid more than they deserve for the work they do.
overpass: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 天桥；跨线桥；上跨式立交桥； overpass An overpass is a structure which carries one road over the top of another one.
overpay: [VERB 动词] 给…过高报酬；多付； overpay See also: overpaid ; If you overpay someone, or if you overpay for something, you pay more than is necessary or reasonable.
overplay: [VERB 动词] 夸大…的重要性；过分强调； overplay If you say that someone is overplaying something such as a problem, you mean that they are making it seem more important than it really is.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 过高估计自己的形势； overplay If someone overplays their hand , they act more confidently than they should because they believe that they are in a stronger position than they actually are.
overpopulated: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人口过剩的；人口过密的； overpopulated If an area is overpopulated , there are problems because it has too many people living there.
overpopulation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 人口过剩；人口过密； overpopulation If there is a problem of overpopulation in an area, there are more people living there than can be supported properly.
overpower: [VERB 动词] 制服； overpower If you overpower someone, you manage to take hold of and keep hold of them, although they struggle a lot.  /  [VERB 动词] 情感等压倒，使难以承受； overpower If a feeling overpowers you, it suddenly affects you very strongly.  /  [VERB 动词] 在体育比赛中轻松战胜； overpower In a sports match, when one team or player overpowers the other, they play much better than them and beat them easily.  /  [VERB 动词] 颜色、气味等盖过，比…强烈得多； overpower If something such as a colour or flavour overpowers another colour or flavour, it is so strong that it makes the second one less noticeable.
overpowering: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 情感等强烈得令人难以承受的，不可抗拒的； overpowering An overpowering feeling is so strong that you cannot resist it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 气味、声音等盖过一切的，过于强烈的； overpowering An overpowering smell or sound is so strong that you cannot smell or hear anything else.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人个性极强的，专横的； overpowering An overpowering person makes other people feel uncomfortable because they have such a strong personality.
overpriced: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 价格过高的；定价太高的； overpriced If you say that something is overpriced , you mean that you think it costs much more than it should.
overran: + + + Overran is the past tense of overrun .
overrate: [VERB 动词] 对…评价过高；高估； overrate overrated If you say that something or someone is overrated , you mean that people have a higher opinion of them than they deserve.
overreach: [VERB 动词] 令自己不自量力；使自己因目标过高而失败； overreach If you say that someone overreaches themselves , you mean that they fail at something because they are trying to do more than they are able to.
overreact: [VERB 动词] 反应过火；反应过激； overreact overreaction If you say that someone overreacts to something, you mean that they have and show more of an emotion than is necessary or appropriate.
override: [VERB 动词] 凌驾于；优先于；比…更重要； override If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.  /  [VERB 动词] 以更大的权力撤销，推翻，否决； override If someone in authority overrides a person or their decisions, they cancel their decisions.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 对决定等的撤销，推翻，否决； override An override is an attempt to cancel someone's decisions by using your authority over them or by gaining more votes than them in an election or contest.
overriding: [ADJ 形容词] 压倒一切的；首要的；最为重要的； overriding In a particular situation, the overriding factor is the one that is the most important.
overrule: [VERB 动词] 否决；驳回；宣布…无效； overrule If someone in authority overrules a person or their decision, they officially decide that the decision is incorrect or not valid.
overrun: [VERB 动词] 迅速侵占，占领； overrun If an army or an armed force overruns a place, area, or country, it succeeds in occupying it very quickly.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 横行的；泛滥的；肆虐的； overrun If you say that a place is overrun with things that you consider undesirable, you mean that there are a large number of them there.  /  [VERB 动词] 超过时限； If an event or meeting overruns by, for example, ten minutes, it continues for ten minutes longer than it was intended to.  /  [VERB 动词] 费用等超支，超出预算； overrun If costs overrun , they are higher than was planned or expected.
