passionate: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 热情的；狂热的； passionate passionately A passionate person has very strong feelings about something or a strong belief in something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 热恋的；情欲强烈的； passionate passionately A passionate person has strong romantic or sexual feelings and expresses them in their behaviour.
passion fruit: [N-VAR 可变名词] 西番莲果；鸡蛋果；百香果； A passion fruit is a small, round, brown fruit that is produced by certain types of tropical flower.
passionless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 冷淡的；没有激情的； passionless If you describe someone or something as passionless , you mean that they do not have or show strong feelings.
passive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 被动的；顺从的；听之任之的； passive passively passivity If you describe someone as passive , you mean that they do not take action but instead let things happen to them.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 消极的； passive A passive activity involves watching, looking at, or listening to things rather than doing things.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 抵抗非暴力的； passive Passive resistance involves showing opposition to the people in power in your country by not co-operating with them and protesting in non-violent ways.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 被动态；被动式； In grammar, the passive or the passive voice is formed using 'be' and the past participle of a verb.
passive smoking: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 被动吸烟； passive smoking Passive smoking involves breathing in the smoke from other people's cigarettes because you happen to be near them.
passivize: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 把…变成被动态； If you can passivize a verb or clause, or if it can passivize , you can put the verb in the passive voice.
pass off: 顺利地进行，举行； If an event passes off without any trouble, it happens and ends without any trouble.
pass off as: 把…装成；把…冒充为； If you pass something off as another thing, you convince people that it is that other thing.
pass on: 将…传给；将…交给； pass on If you pass something on to someone, you give it to them so that they have it instead of you.  /  将…转移给；将…转嫁给； pass on If you pass on costs or savings to someone else, you make them pay for your costs or allow them to benefit from your savings.  /  去世；逝世； You can say that someone passed on to mean that they died, if you want to avoid using the word 'die' because you think it might upset or offend people.  /  See also: pass ; �
pass out: 昏倒；晕过去； If you pass out , you faint or collapse.  /  警校、军校学员毕业； When a police, army, navy, or air force cadet passes out , he or she completes his or her training.
pass over: 任命或晋升时跳过，不考虑； If someone is passed over for a job or position, they do not get the job or position and someone younger or less experienced is chosen instead.  /  在谈话或演讲中不提及，忽略，跳过； If you pass over a topic in a conversation or speech, you do not talk about it.
Passover: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 犹太人的逾越节自3月或4月开始，持续七八天； Passover Passover is a Jewish festival that begins in March or April and lasts for seven or eight days.
passport: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 护照； passport Your passport is an official document containing your name, photograph, and personal details, which you need to show when you enter or leave a country.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 进身之阶；获取成功或幸福的途径，手段； passport If you say that a thing is a passport to success or happiness, you mean that this thing makes success or happiness possible.
pass up: 放弃，错过机会； pass up If you pass up a chance or an opportunity, you do not take advantage of it.
password: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 口令；密码； password A password is a secret word or phrase that you must know in order to be allowed to enter a place such as a military base, or to be allowed to use a computer system.
past: In addition to the uses shown below, past is used in the phrasal verb 'run past'.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 过去；往昔； past 生活在过去；留恋往昔 The past is the time before the present, and the things that have happened.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 经历；过去之事； past Your past consists of all the things that you have done or that have happened to you.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 过去的；以前的； past [past亦用于时间段之后] Past events and things happened or existed before the present time.
pasta: [N-MASS 物质名词] 面食如意大利面条、通心粉等； Pasta is a type of food made from a mixture of flour, eggs, and water that is formed into different shapes and then boiled.
paste: [N-MASS 物质名词] 糊糊；糨糊； paste Paste is a soft, wet, sticky mixture of a substance and a liquid, which can be spread easily.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 肉、水果或蔬菜弄碎做成的酱； paste Paste is a soft smooth mixture made of crushed meat, fruit, or vegetables.  /  [VERB 动词] 粘贴；黏合； paste If you paste something on a surface, you put glue or paste on it and stick it on the surface.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 制造人造宝石的铅玻璃； paste Paste is a hard shiny glass that is used for making imitation jewellery.
pastel: [ADJ 形容词] 色彩淡的，柔和的； pastel Pastel colours are pale rather than dark or bright.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 彩色粉笔； pastel Pastels are also small sticks of different coloured chalks that are used for drawing pictures.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 彩色粉笔画；彩粉画； pastel A pastel is a picture that has been done using pastels.
pasteurized: [ADJ 形容词] 牛奶、奶油、奶酪等经巴氏法灭菌的； Pasteurized milk, cream, or cheese has had bacteria removed from it by a special heating process to make it safer to eat or drink.
pastiche: [N-VAR 可变名词] 文学作品、音乐等的模仿作品；融合各种风格的集成之作； pastiche A pastiche is something such as a piece of writing or music in which the style is copied from somewhere else, or which contains a mixture of different styles.
pastille: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 糖锭；锭剂；含片； A pastille is a small, round sweet or piece of candy that has a fruit flavour.
pastime: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 消遣；娱乐； pastime A pastime is something that you do in your spare time because you enjoy it or are interested in it.
pasting: [N-SING 单数名词] 严厉批评； pasting If something or someone takes a pasting , they are severely criticized.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 惨败； If a sports team or political party is given a pasting , they are heavily defeated.
past master: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 能手；老手；行家； past master If you are a past master at something, you are very skilful at it because you have had a lot of experience doing it.
pastor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 某些新教教会的牧师； A pastor is a member of the Christian clergy in some Protestant churches.
pastoral: [ADJ 形容词] 牧师的；牧灵的；教牧的； pastoral The pastoral duties of a priest or other religious leader involve looking after the people he or she has responsibility for, especially by helping them with their personal problems.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 教师对学生生活辅导的； pastoral If a school offers pastoral care, it is concerned with the personal needs and problems of its pupils, not just with their schoolwork.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 田园式的； pastoral A pastoral place, atmosphere, or idea is characteristic of peaceful country life and scenery.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 畜牧的；放牧的； pastoral A pastoral way of life is one in which people keep animals such as cows and sheep that feed off the land.
past participle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 过去分词； In grammar, the past participle of a verb is a form that is usually the same as the past form and so ends in '-ed'.
past perfect: [ADJ 形容词] 过去完成时； In grammar, the past perfect tenses of a verb are the ones used to talk about things that happened before a specific time.
pastrami: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 五香熏牛肉； Pastrami is strongly seasoned smoked beef.
pastry: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 油酥面饼；油酥面皮； Pastry is a food made from flour, fat, and water that is mixed together, rolled flat, and baked in the oven.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 油酥点心；油酥糕饼； A pastry is a small cake made with sweet pastry.
pasture: [N-VAR 可变名词] 牧场；牧草地； pasture Pasture is land with grass growing on it for farm animals to eat.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 更好的地方[或工作、条件]; 更好的前程； pasture If someone leaves for greener pastures , or in British English pastures new , they leave their job, their home, or the situation they are in for something they think will be much better.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 放牧； If you put animals out to pasture , you move them out into the fields so they can eat the grass.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 让…退休；使赋闲； pasture If you say that someone is being put out to pasture , you mean they are no longer being employed because they are considered to be too old or no longer useful.
pasty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脸色苍白的； pasty If you are pasty or if you have a pasty face, you look pale and unhealthy.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 馅饼； See also: Cornish pasty ; In Britain, a pasty is a small pie which consists of pastry folded around meat, vegetables, or cheese.
pat: [VERB 动词] 轻拍；轻敲； pat If you pat something or someone, you tap them lightly, usually with your hand held flat.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 黄油等的小块； A pat of butter or something else that is soft is a small lump of it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 敷衍的；过于简单的； pat If you say that an answer or explanation is pat , you disapprove of it because it is too simple and sounds as if it has been prepared in advance.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 赞许；表扬； pat If you give someone a pat on the back or if you pat them on the back , you show them that you think they have done well and deserve to be praised.
patch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 表面上与周围不同的部分； patch A patch on a surface is a part of it which is different in appearance from the area around it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 种有某种植物或农作物的小块土地； patch A patch of land is a small area of land where a particular plant or crop grows.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 补丁；补片； patch A patch is a piece of material which you use to cover a hole in something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保护受伤眼睛的眼罩； patch See also: eye patch ; A patch is a small piece of material which you wear to cover an injured eye.
patch together: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拼凑； If you patch something together , you form it from a number of parts in a quick, hurried way.
patch up: [PHR-V-RECIP 相互动词短语] 平息[争吵]; 修补关系； patch up If you patch up a quarrel or relationship, you try to be friendly again and not to quarrel any more.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 修理；修补； patch up If you patch up something which is damaged, you mend it or patch it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 为…处理伤口；包扎，处理伤口； If doctors patch someone up or patch their wounds up , they treat their injuries.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 艰难达成协议等； If people or countries patch up a deal, they manage to agree on it after difficult discussions.
patchwork: [ADJ 形容词] 拼缀的；拼缝的； patchwork A patchwork quilt, cushion, or piece of clothing is made by sewing together small pieces of material of different colours or patterns.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 拼凑物；混杂物； patchwork If you refer to something as a patchwork , you mean that it is made up of many different parts, pieces or colours.
patchy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 分布不均衡的；散落的；斑驳的； patchy A patchy substance or colour exists in some places but not in others, or is thick in some places and thin in others.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 时好时坏的；不稳定的；差强人意的； patchy If something is patchy , it is not completely reliable or satisfactory because it is not always good.
pate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 头顶； pate Your pate is the top of your head.
patent: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 专利权； patent A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.  /  [VERB 动词] 得到…的专利权； patent If you patent something, you obtain a patent for it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 尤指坏事物明显的，显而易见的； patent patently You use patent to describe something, especially something bad, in order to indicate in an emphatic way that you think its nature or existence is clear and obvious.
patent leather: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 漆皮；漆革； patent leather Patent leather is leather which has a shiny surface.
paternal: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 父亲的；父亲般的； paternal Paternal is used to describe feelings or actions which are typical of those of a kind father towards his child.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 父系的；父亲一方的； paternal A paternal relative is one that is related through a person's father rather than their mother.
paternalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 家长制；家长作风； paternalism Paternalism means taking all the decisions for the people you govern, employ, or are responsible for, so that they cannot or do not have to make their own decisions.
paternalist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 家长式人物； paternalist A paternalist is a person who acts in a paternalistic way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 同paternalistic； paternalist Paternalist means the same as paternalistic .
paternalistic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 家长式的；家长作风的； paternalistic Someone who is paternalistic takes all the decisions for the people they govern, employ, or are responsible for.
paternity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 父亲身份； paternity Paternity is the state or fact of being the father of a particular child.
paternity leave: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 陪产假；父亲亲子假； If a man has paternity leave , his employer allows him some time off work because his child has just been born.
paternity suit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生父确认诉讼； If a woman starts or takes out a paternity suit , she asks a court of law to help her to prove that a particular man is the father of her child, often in order to claim financial support from him.
path: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小路；小径； path A path is a long strip of ground which people walk along to get from one place to another.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 前面的道路，通道； path Your path is the space ahead of you as you move along.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 路线；轨迹； path The path of something is the line which it moves along in a particular direction.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 行动路线；途径； path A path that you take is a particular course of action or way of achieving something.
pathetic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可怜的；令人怜悯的；悲惨的； pathetic pathetically If you describe a person or animal as pathetic , you mean that they are sad and weak or helpless, and they make you feel very sorry for them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 差劲的；软弱的；令人生厌的； pathetic pathetically If you describe someone or something as pathetic , you mean that they make you feel impatient or angry, often because they are weak or not very good.
pathfinder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 探路者；开路人； A pathfinder is someone whose job is to find routes across areas.
pathogen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 病原体； A pathogen is any organism which can cause disease in a person, animal, or plant.
pathogenic: [ADJ 形容词] 病原的；致病的； A pathogenic organism can cause disease in a person, animal, or plant.
pathological: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 走极端的；无法控制的；病态的； pathological You describe a person or their behaviour as pathological when they behave in an extreme and unacceptable way, and have very powerful feelings which they cannot control.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 病理学的； pathological Pathological means relating to pathology or illness.
pathologist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 病理学家； A pathologist is someone who studies or investigates diseases and illnesses, and examines dead bodies in order to find out the cause of death.
pathology: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 病理学； Pathology is the study of the way diseases and illnesses develop.
pathos: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 情形、电影、戏剧等中的引人怜悯的特质，感伤力； pathos Pathos is a quality in a situation, film, or play that makes people feel sadness and pity.
pathway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小路；路径； pathway A pathway is a path which you can walk along or a route which you can take.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 途径；行动路线； pathway A pathway is a particular course of action or a way of achieving something.
patience: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 容忍；耐心；忍耐力； patience If you have patience , you are able to stay calm and not get annoyed, for example when something takes a long time, or when someone is not doing what you want them to do.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 单人纸牌游戏； patience Patience is a card game for only one player.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 考验…的耐心；使忍无可忍； patience If someone tries your patience or tests your patience , they annoy you so much that it is very difficult for you to stay calm.
patient: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 患者；病人；  patient A patient is a person who is receiving medical treatment from a doctor or hospital.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 能忍耐的；有耐心的； patient patiently If you are patient , you stay calm and do not get annoyed, for example when something takes a long time, or when someone is not doing what you want them to do.
patina: [N-SING 单数名词] 物体表面形成的薄层； patina A patina is a thin layer of something that has formed on the surface of something.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 旧东西年深日久产生的包浆，光泽； patina The patina on an old object is an attractive soft shine that has developed on its surface, usually because it has been used a lot.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 有点儿…的样子； patina If you say that someone has a patina of a quality or characteristic, you mean that they have a small but impressive amount of this quality or characteristic.
patio: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 挨着房子的露台，平台； A patio is an area of flat blocks or concrete next to a house, where people can sit and relax or eat.
patio door: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 露台玻璃门； Patio doors are glass doors that lead onto a patio.
patisserie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 糕点店； patisserie A patisserie is a shop where cakes and pastries are sold.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 糕点； patisserie Patisserie is cakes and pastries.
patois: [N-VAR 可变名词] 尤指法语的方言，土语； patois A patois is a form of a language, especially French, that is spoken in a particular area of a country.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 混合语； patois A patois is a language that has developed from a mixture of other languages.
patriarch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男性家长，族长，酋长； patriarch A patriarch is the male head of a family or tribe.  /  [N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词] 基督教东派教会的大牧首，宗主教； A patriarch is the head of one of a number of Eastern Christian Churches.
patriarchal: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 男性家长制的，族长制的；父权制的； patriarchal A patriarchal society, family, or system is one in which the men have all or most of the power and importance.
patriarchy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 男性家长制；父权制； patriarchy Patriarchy is a system in which men have all or most of the power and importance in a society or group.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 父权社会；父系社会； A patriarchy is a patriarchal society.
patrician: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 贵族；豪门子弟； patrician A patrician is a person who comes from a family of high social rank.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 贵族的；有贵族气派的； patrician If you describe someone as patrician , you mean that they behave in a sophisticated way, and look as though they are from a high social rank.
patrimony: [N-SING 单数名词] 祖传财产；世袭财产； patrimony Someone's patrimony is the possessions that they have inherited from their father or ancestors.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 国家的文物，遗产； patrimony A country's patrimony is its land, buildings, and works of art.
patriot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 爱国者； patriot Someone who is a patriot loves their country and feels very loyal towards it.
patriotic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 爱国的； patriotic Someone who is patriotic loves their country and feels very loyal towards it.
patriotism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 爱国主义；爱国精神； patriotism Patriotism is love for your country and loyalty towards it.

play: [VERB 动词] 玩；玩耍； play When children, animals, or perhaps adults play , they spend time doing enjoyable things, such as using toys and taking part in games.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 参加体育活动、比赛等； play When you play a sport, game, or match, you take part in it.  /  [VERB 动词] 和…比赛； play When one person or team plays another or plays against them, they compete against them in a sport or game.  /  [VERB 动词] 比赛等中打出，踢出，击出球； play When you play the ball or play a shot in a game or sport, you kick or hit the ball.
play-act: [VERB 动词] 装扮；假装；装腔作势； If someone is play-acting , they are pretending to have attitudes or feelings that they do not really have.
play-acting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 装扮；假装；装腔作势； play-acting Play-acting is behaviour where someone pretends to have attitudes or feelings that they do not really have.
play along: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 暂且对…附和；暂时与…合作； play along If you play along with a person, with what they say, or with their plans, you appear to agree with them and do what they want, even though you are not sure whether they are right.
play around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 逗乐；玩闹； If you play around , you behave in a silly way to amuse yourself or other people.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 反复琢磨；自由调换…的排列顺序； play around If you play around with a problem or an arrangement of objects, you try different ways of organizing it in order to find the best solution or arrangement.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 鬼混；搞不正当性关系； If someone plays around , they have sex with people other than the person they are married to or having a serious relationship with.  /  See also: play ; �
play at: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 对…敷衍了事；儿戏似地做； If you say that someone is playing at something, you disapprove of the fact that they are doing it casually and not very seriously.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 尤指儿童假扮…玩，玩…游戏； If someone, especially a child, plays at being someone or doing something, they pretend to be that person or do that thing as a game.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 搞…名堂；想…念头； If you do not know what someone is playing at , you do not understand what they are doing or what they are trying to achieve.
playback: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 已录好的录音带、录像带的回放，重放； playback The playback of a tape is the operation of playing it on a machine in order to listen to the sound or watch the pictures recorded on it.
play back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 录完后播放，放送磁带、电影等； See also: playback ; When you play back a tape or film, you listen to the sounds or watch the pictures after recording them.
playboy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 花花公子；寻欢作乐的有钱男子； playboy You can refer to a rich man who spends most of his time enjoying himself as a playboy .
Play-Doh: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 培乐多泥胶； Play-Doh is a soft coloured substance like clay which children use for making models.
play down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 降低…的重要性；贬低；淡化； If you play down something, you try to make people believe that it is not particularly important.
player: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 运动员；选手；参加运动者； player A player in a sport or game is a person who takes part, either as a job or for fun.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乐器演奏者； player You can use player to refer to a musician.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 重要参与者； player If a person, country, or organization is a player in something, they are involved in it and important in it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 演员；表演者； player A player is an actor.
player-manager: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 足球和一些其他体育运动中的队员兼主教练； In football and some other sports, a player-manager is a person who plays for a team and also manages the team.
player piano: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有自动演奏装置的自动钢琴； A player piano is a type of mechanical piano.
playful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 姿态或人嬉戏的，闹着玩的，不当真的； playful playfully playfulness A playful gesture or person is friendly or humorous.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 动物喜玩耍的，活泼的； playful A playful animal is lively and cheerful.
playground: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 学校的操场，运动场；儿童游乐场； See also: adventure playground ; A playground is a piece of land, at school or in a public area, where children can play.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 某一群体的游憩胜地，度假场所； playground If you describe a place as a playground for a certain group of people, you mean that those people like to enjoy themselves there or go on holiday there.
playgroup: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 学前游戏班；幼儿游戏组； A playgroup is an informal school for very young children, where they learn things by playing.
playhouse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 剧场；戏院； playhouse A playhouse is a theatre.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 儿童游戏房；玩具房； playhouse A playhouse is a small house made for children to play in.
playing card: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纸牌；扑克牌； Playing cards are thin pieces of cardboard with numbers or pictures printed on them, which are used to play various games.
playing field: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 操场；运动场； playing field A playing field is a large area of grass where people play sports.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 公平竞争的环境；机会均等的环境； playing field You talk about a level playing field to mean a situation that is fair, because no competitor or opponent in it has an advantage over another.
playlist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电台的音乐播放表； playlist A playlist is a list of songs, albums, and artists that a radio station broadcasts.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…排入播放表； playlist If a song, album, or artist is playlisted , it is put on a radio station's playlist.
playmate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 游戏的伙伴；玩伴； playmate A child's playmate is another child who often plays with him or her.
playoff: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 平分后要决出胜负的附加赛； playoff A playoff is an extra game which is played to decide the winner of a sports competition when two or more people have got the same score.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 常规赛季之后的季后赛； playoff You use playoffs to refer to a series of games between the winners of different leagues, to decide which teams will play for a championship.
play-off: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 平分后要决出胜负的附加赛； play-off A playoff is an extra game which is played to decide the winner of a sports competition when two or more people have got the same score.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 常规赛季之后的季后赛； You use playoffs to refer to a series of games between the winners of different leagues, to decide which teams will play for a championship.
play off against: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 为从中渔利而使…相斗，挑拨离间； If you play people off against each other, you make them compete or argue, so that you gain some advantage.
play on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 利用恐惧、弱点或过失； If you play on someone's fears, weaknesses, or faults, you deliberately use them in order to persuade that person to do something, or to achieve what you want.
play on words: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同pun； A play on words is the same as a pun .
play out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使戏剧性的事件逐渐发生；使展开； If a dramatic event is played out , it gradually takes place.
play park: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 儿童游乐场； A play park is a children's playground.
playpen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 供婴儿或幼儿在里面玩的游戏围栏； A playpen is a small structure which is designed for a baby or young child to play safely in.
playroom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 儿童游戏室； A playroom is a room in a house for children to play in.
playschool: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 游戏学校；学前游戏班； A playschool is an informal type of school for very young children where they learn things by playing.
PlayStation: PS 游戏机； A PlayStation is a type of games console.
plaything: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 玩具；供玩耍的东西； plaything A plaything is a toy or other object that a child plays with.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 玩物；被玩弄的人； plaything If you say that someone is treating you as a plaything , you think that they are using you for their amusement or advantage, and do not care about you.
playtime: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 学校里低龄孩子的课间游戏时间； playtime In a school for young children, playtime is the period of time between lessons when they can play outside.
play up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 强调…的重要性；夸大；渲染； If you play up something, you emphasize it and try to make people believe that it is important.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 机器、身体部位等给…制造麻烦，使痛苦； If something such as a machine or a part of your body is playing up or is playing you up , it is causing problems because it is not working properly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 小孩淘气，不听话； When children play up , they are naughty and difficult to control.
play upon: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 同 play on； To play upon something means the same as to play on it.
playwright: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 剧作家； A playwright is a person who writes plays.
plaza: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 城市中的露天广场； plaza A plaza is an open square in a city.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 购物中心，商业区彼此相连或拥有公共区域的一组店铺或建筑； A plaza is a group of stores or buildings that are joined together or share common areas.
PLC: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 在英国通常用于公司名称后公开股份有限公司； In Britain, plc means a company whose shares can be bought by the public and is usually used after the name of a company.
plea: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 恳求；请求； plea A plea is an appeal or request for something, made in an intense or emotional way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 法庭上表明对于被指控的罪名服或不服的申诉，答辩，抗辩； plea In a court of law, a person's plea is the answer that they give when they have been charged with a crime, saying whether or not they are guilty of that crime.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 辩由；借口；托词； plea A plea is a reason which is given, to a court of law or to other people, as an excuse for doing something or for not doing something.
plea bargain: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一些法律体系中被告承认有罪以减轻刑罚的认罪辩诉协议； plea bargain In some legal systems, a plea bargain is an agreement that, if an accused person says they are guilty, they will be charged with a less serious crime or will receive a less severe punishment.  /  [VERB 动词] 被告接受认罪辩诉协议； plea bargaining plea bargain If an accused person plea bargains , they accept a plea bargain.
plead: [VERB 动词] 恳求；请求； plead If you plead with someone to do something, you ask them in an intense, emotional way to do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 作有罪或无罪的答辩； plead When someone charged with a crime pleads guilty or not guilty in a court of law, they officially state that they are guilty or not guilty of the crime.  /  [VERB 动词] 为…辩护；维护；声援； plead If you plead the case or cause of someone or something, you speak out in their support or defence.  /  [VERB 动词] 提出…为理由；把…作为借口； plead If you plead a particular thing as the reason for doing or not doing something, you give it as your excuse.
pleading: [ADJ 形容词] 表情或姿态恳求的，请求的； pleading pleadingly A pleading expression or gesture shows someone that you want something very much.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恳求；请求；吁请； pleading See also: special pleading ; Pleading is asking someone for something you want very much, in an intense or emotional way.
pleasant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人愉快的；舒适的；合意的； pleasant pleasantly Something that is pleasant is nice, enjoyable, or attractive.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 友好的；可亲的；讨人喜欢的； pleasant Someone who is pleasant is friendly and likeable.
pleasantry: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻松诙谐的话；寒暄；客套； Pleasantries are casual, friendly remarks which you make in order to be polite.
please: [ADV 副词] 表示有礼貌地请求或邀请请，烦劳； please You say please when you are politely asking or inviting someone to do something.  /  [ADV 副词] 表示客气地接受谢谢，行； please You say please when you are accepting something politely.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 表示要求对方停止做某事或别再开口请别，请不必； You can say please to indicate that you want someone to stop doing something or stop speaking.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 用于吸引对方注意、特别是儿童对老师或其他成人时请问，对不起； You can say please in order to attract someone's attention politely.
pleased: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 高兴的；喜欢的；满意的； pleased If you are pleased , you are happy about something or satisfied with something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 高兴做…的；乐意做…的； pleased If you say you will be pleased to do something, you are saying in a polite way that you are willing to do it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 对…满意的；对…赞赏的； pleased You can tell someone that you are pleased with something they have done in order to express your approval.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不高兴的；不满意的； pleased If someone is not too pleased or is none too pleased , they are annoyed about something or do not think something is acceptable.
pleasing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人愉快的；使人满意的； pleasing pleasingly Something that is pleasing gives you pleasure and satisfaction.
pleasurable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人愉快的；使人高兴的； pleasurable pleasurably Pleasurable experiences or sensations are pleasant and enjoyable.
pleasure: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 愉快；高兴；快乐；满足； pleasure If something gives you pleasure , you get a feeling of happiness, satisfaction, or enjoyment from it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤指工作、职责之外的娱乐，消遣； pleasure Pleasure is the activity of enjoying yourself, especially rather than working or doing what you have a duty to do.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乐趣；乐事；给人愉快的事物； pleasure A pleasure is an activity, experience or aspect of something that you find very enjoyable or satisfying.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 很高兴见到…/…莅临的荣幸； pleasure If you meet someone for the first time, you can say, as a way of being polite, that it is a pleasure to meet them.

pleat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 衣褶；褶裥； A pleat in a piece of clothing is a permanent fold that is made in the cloth by folding one part over the other and sewing across the top end of the fold.
pleated: [ADJ 形容词] 打褶的；有褶裥的； pleated A pleated piece of clothing has pleats in it.
pleb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 平头百姓；市井小民；粗俗的人； If someone refers to people as plebs , they mean they are of a low social class or do not appreciate culture.

plebiscite: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公民投票； A plebiscite is a direct vote by the people of a country or region in which they say whether they agree or disagree with a particular policy, for example whether a region should become an independent state.
pledge: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保证；诺言；誓言； pledge When someone makes a pledge , they make a serious promise that they will do something.  /  [VERB 动词] 保证，许诺，发誓[做]; 保证给予； pledge When someone pledges to do something, they promise in a serious way to do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 许诺拨[款]; 许诺给予； pledge If you pledge a sum of money to an organization or activity, you promise to pay that amount of money to it at a particular time or over a particular period.  /  [VERB 动词] 使保证，使许诺，使发誓遵循或支持； pledge If you pledge yourself to something, you commit yourself to following a particular course of action or to supporting a particular person, group, or idea.
plenary: [ADJ 形容词] 全体出席的； plenary A plenary session or plenary meeting is one that is attended by everyone who has the right to attend.

plentiful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 丰富的；充足的；多的； plentiful plentifully Things that are plentiful exist in such large amounts or numbers that there is enough for people's wants or needs.
plenty: [QUANT 数量词] 尤指足够的或超出需要的丰富，充足，大量； plenty If there is plenty of something, there is a large amount of it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 富裕；富足；繁荣； plenty Plenty is a situation in which people have a lot to eat or a lot of money to live on.  /  [ADV 副词] 用于形容词或副词前非常，十分，很； plenty You use plenty in front of adjectives or adverbs to emphasize the degree of the quality they are describing.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 丰富地；充足地；大量地； plenty If there are things in plenty , those things exist or happen in large amounts or numbers.
plenum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 全体会议； A plenum is a meeting that is attended by all the members of a committee or conference.
plethora: [N-SING 单数名词] 大量；尤指过多，过剩； plethora A plethora of something is a large amount of it, especially an amount of it that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

pliers: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 钳子；老虎钳； Pliers are a tool with two handles at one end and two hard, flat, metal parts at the other.
plight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 困境；苦境； plight If you refer to someone's plight , you mean that they are in a difficult or distressing situation that is full of problems.
plimsoll: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胶底帆布鞋； Plimsolls are canvas shoes with flat rubber soles.
plinth: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 底座；柱基； A plinth is a rectangular block of stone on which a statue or pillar stands.
plod: [VERB 动词] 沉重缓慢地走；步履艰难地走； plod If someone plods , they walk slowly and heavily.  /  [VERB 动词] 缓慢地进行； plod plodding If you say that someone plods on or plods along with a job, you mean that the job is taking a long time.

plonk: [VERB 动词] 重重放下；随意放下； plonk If you plonk something somewhere, you put it or drop it there heavily and carelessly.  /  [VERB 动词] 使重重坐下；使随意坐下； plonk If you plonk yourself somewhere, you sit down carelessly without paying attention to the people around you.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 廉价酒；劣质酒； Plonk is cheap or poor quality wine.  /  [N-SING; SOUND 单数名词；声音词] 砰的一声；扑通声； plonk A plonk is a heavy, hollow sound.
plonker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指男子傻瓜，笨蛋； If someone calls a person, especially a man, a plonker , they think he is stupid.
plop: [N-COUNT; SOUND 可数名词；声音词] 某物落入水中而未溅泼的扑通声，啪嗒声； plop A plop is a soft, gentle sound, like the sound made by something dropping into water without disturbing the surface much.  /  [VERB 动词] 扑通落下；啪嗒落下； plop If something plops somewhere, it drops there with a soft, gentle sound.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻轻地放下；轻巧地放下； plop If you plop something somewhere, you drop it there gently and without making a loud noise.  /  相关词组： plop down �
plop down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻快地坐下； If you plop down or plop yourself down somewhere, you sit down quickly but gently.
plot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 阴谋；密谋； plot A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, usually against a person or a government.  /  [VERB 动词] 图谋；密谋； plot If people plot to do something or plot something that is illegal or wrong, they plan secretly to do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 计划；制订； plot When people plot a strategy or a course of action, they carefully plan each step of it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 电影、小说或戏剧的情节； See also: sub-plot ; The plot of a film, novel, or play is the connected series of events which make up the story.
plotline: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 书、电影或戏剧的情节主线，主要情节； plotline The plotline of a book, film, or play is its plot and the way in which it develops.
plotter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指针对个人或政府的密谋者，阴谋分子； plotter A plotter is a person who secretly plans with others to do something that is illegal or wrong, usually against a person or government.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 标绘者；标绘器； A plotter is a person or instrument that marks the position of something such as a ship on a map or chart.
plough: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 犁； See also: snowplough ; A plough is a large farming tool with sharp blades which is pulled across the soil to turn it over, usually before seeds are planted.  /  [VERB 动词] 犁[地]; 耕地； plough ploughing When someone ploughs an area of land, they turn over the soil using a plough.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 土地被开垦成耕地； plough If an area of land is under the plough , it is used for growing crops.  /  to plough a furrow » see: furrow
plough back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把利润再投资到； If profits are ploughed back into a business, they are used to increase the size of the business or to improve it.
plough into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 猛力冲入；猛撞； If something, for example a car, ploughs into something else, it goes out of control and crashes violently into it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把大笔资金投入； If you say that money is ploughed into something such as a business or a service, you are emphasizing that the amount of money which is invested in it or spent on it in order to improve it is very large.
ploughman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 犁地者；尤指使用马或牛拉犁的把犁人，扶犁手； A ploughman is a man whose job it is to plough the land, especially with a plough pulled by horses or oxen.
ploughman's lunch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常指在酒馆吃的，包括面包、乳酪、色拉和泡菜的农夫午餐； A ploughman's lunch or a ploughman's is a meal consisting of bread, cheese, salad, and pickle, usually eaten in a pub.
plough on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 奋力前进；奋力从事； plough on If you plough on , you continue moving or trying to complete something, even though it takes a lot of effort to go on.
ploughshare: [PHRASE 短语] 铸剑为犁；化干戈为玉帛； If you say that swords have been turned into ploughshares or beaten into ploughshares , you mean that a state of conflict between two or more groups of people has ended and a period of peace has begun.
plough through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 终于完成；奋力完成； plough through If you plough through something such as a large meal or a long piece of work, you finally finish it although it takes a lot of effort.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 尤指费很大力气地通过，冲破； plough through If someone ploughs through a place or if a ship ploughs through water, they move through it, especially with great effort.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车辆或导弹猛力穿过，失控冲过； If a vehicle or a missile ploughs through something, it goes violently or carelessly through it as though it is out of control.
plough up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 通常指为种植作物而犁地，翻土； plough up If someone ploughs up an area of land, they plough it, usually in order to turn it into land used for growing crops.
plover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鸻； A plover is a bird with a rounded body, a short tail, and a short beak that is found by the sea or by lakes.
ploy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 计策；计谋；手段； ploy A ploy is a way of behaving that someone plans carefully and secretly in order to gain an advantage for themselves.
pls: Pls is a written abbreviation for (书面缩略=) please .
pluck: [VERB 动词] 采；摘； pluck If you pluck a fruit, flower, or leaf, you take it between your fingers and pull it in order to remove it from its stalk where it is growing.  /  [VERB 动词] 拔；拉；抽；扯； pluck If you pluck something from somewhere, you take it between your fingers and pull it sharply from where it is.  /  [VERB 动词] 弹，拨乐器； pluck If you pluck a guitar or other musical instrument, you pull the strings with your fingers and let them go, so that they make a sound.  /  [VERB 动词] 拔除鸡或其他死禽的毛； pluck If you pluck a chicken or other dead bird, you pull its feathers out to prepare it for cooking.
pluck at: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻轻地拔，拉，拽； If you pluck at something, you take it between your fingers and pull it sharply but gently.
plucky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有勇气的；有胆量的； plucky If someone, for example a sick child, is described as plucky , it means that although they are weak, they face their difficulties with courage.
plug: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 插头； A plug on a piece of electrical equipment is a small plastic object with two or three metal pins which fit into the holes of an electric socket and connects the equipment to the electricity supply.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 插座； A plug is an electric socket.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 浴缸或水槽的塞子； plug A plug is a thick, circular piece of rubber or plastic that you use to block the hole in a bath or sink when it is filled with water.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 木头、塑料或蜡制的堵洞塞子，栓； plug A plug is a small, round piece of wood, plastic, or wax which is used to block holes.
plug-and-play: [ADJ 形容词] 计算机设备即插即用的，随插随用的； plug-and-play Plug-and-play is used to describe computer equipment, for example a printer, that is ready to use immediately when you connect it to a computer.
plug away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 埋头苦干；孜孜不倦地做； If you plug away , you keep trying very hard to do something or achieve something even though you find it difficult.
plughole: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 浴缸或水槽的排水孔，出水口； A plughole is a small hole in a bath or sink which allows the water to flow away and into which you can put a plug.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 失败；丢失；白白浪费； plughole If you say that something has gone down the plughole , you mean that it has failed or has been lost or wasted.
plug in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将插头插入插座给…接通电源； If you plug a piece of electrical equipment into an electricity supply or if you plug it in , you push its plug into an electric socket so that it can work.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把某一电器与另一电器连接； If you plug one piece of electrical equipment into another or if you plug it in , you make it work by connecting the two.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 某一电器以电线或导线连接电源，与另一电器相接； plug in If one piece of electrical equipment plugs in or plugs into another piece of electrical equipment, it works by being connected by an electrical cord or lead to an electricity supply or to the other piece of equipment.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将…塞入； 用…堵住； If you plug something into a hole, you push it into the hole.
plug-in: [ADJ 形容词] 插入式的；带插头接点的； plug-in A plug-in machine is a piece of electrical equipment that is operated by being connected to an electricity supply or to another piece of electrical equipment by means of a plug.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 插件；插件程序； plug-in A plug-in is something such as a piece of software that can be added to a computer system to give extra features or functions.
plug into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 接入计算机系统； plug into If you plug into a computer system, you are able to use it or see the information stored on it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 探究；设法了解； If you plug into a group of people or their ideas, you find out about them and try to understand them.  /  See also: plug-in ; �
plum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 李子；梅子； A plum is a small, sweet fruit with a smooth red or yellow skin and a stone in the middle.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 紫红色；青紫色； plum Something that is plum or plum-coloured is a dark reddish-purple colour.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 工作、合同、角色等令人垂涎的，吸引人的； plum A plum job, contract, or role is a very good one that a lot of people would like.
plumage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 鸟的全身羽毛； A bird's plumage is all the feathers on its body.
plumb: [VERB 动词] 探索；探究； plumb If you plumb something mysterious or difficult to understand, you succeed in understanding it.  /  [ADV 副词] 恰恰；正好； plumb If something is plumb in a particular place, it is exactly in that place.  /  [VERB 动词] 为建筑物敷设水管； plumb When someone plumbs a building, they put in all the pipes for carrying water.  /  [ADV 副词] 完全地；不折不扣地； plumb Plumb is used to give emphasis to an adjective or verb that describes a feeling or condition.
plumber: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 管子工；水暖工； A plumber is a person whose job is to connect and repair things such as water and drainage pipes, baths, and toilets.
plumb in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 给…接通给水和排水管道； plumb in When someone plumbs in a device such as a washing machine, toilet, or bath, they connect it to the water and waste pipes in a building.
plumbing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 建筑物的水管装置，水暖设备； plumbing The plumbing in a building consists of the water and drainage pipes, baths, and toilets in it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 水管工程；管道工程； plumbing Plumbing is the work of connecting and repairing things such as water and drainage pipes, baths, and toilets.
plumb line: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 检查垂直度的铅垂线； A plumb line is a piece of string with a weight attached to the end that is used to check that something such as a wall is vertical or that it slopes at the correct angle.
plume: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尘、火、水等升起的一股，一团； plume A plume of smoke, dust, fire, or water is a large quantity of it that rises into the air in a column.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 羽毛；大羽； plume A plume is a large, soft bird's feather.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 战士头盔等的羽饰； A plume is a bunch of long, thin pieces of material which is used to decorate something such as a soldier's helmet.
plumed: [ADJ 形容词] 用羽毛装饰的； plumed Plumed means decorated with a plume or plumes.
plummet: [VERB 动词] 数量、比率或价格骤然下跌，暴跌； plummet If an amount, rate, or price plummets , it decreases quickly by a large amount.  /  [VERB 动词] 通常指从高处快速落下，陡直掉下； plummet If someone or something plummets , they fall very fast towards the ground, usually from a great height.
plummy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 声音或腔调故作上流社会人士的； plummy If you say that someone has a plummy voice or accent, you mean that they sound very upper-class.
plump: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 丰满的；胖乎乎的；圆滚滚的； plump plumpness You can describe someone or something as plump to indicate that they are rather fat or rounded.  /  [VERB 动词] 通过摇抖或拍打使膨松，使松软鼓起； plump plump up 同 plump If you plump a pillow or cushion, you shake it and hit it gently so that it goes back into a rounded shape.  /  [VERB 动词] 常指经过犹豫或深思熟虑后选择，选中； plump If you plump for someone or something, you choose them, often after hesitating or thinking carefully.
plum pudding: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 圣诞节吃的浓味干果布丁，葡萄干布丁； Plum pudding is a special pudding eaten at Christmas which is made with dried fruit, spices, and suet.
plum tomato: [N-VAR 可变名词] 李形番茄；蛋形番茄； Plum tomatoes are long egg-shaped tomatoes.
plunder: [VERB 动词] 劫掠；掠夺；窃取； plunder If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 劫掠物；侵吞物；赃物； plunder Plunder is property that is stolen.
plunge: [VERB 动词] 尤指向水中纵身投入，一头进入； plunge If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.  /  [VERB 动词] 将…投入；将…插入；将…刺进； plunge If you plunge an object into something, you push it quickly or violently into it.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使突然陷入；使突然遭受； plunge If a person or thing is plunged into a particular state or situation, or if they plunge into it, they are suddenly in that state or situation.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使投身；使突然开始从事； plunge If you plunge into an activity or are plunged into it, you suddenly get very involved in it.
plunger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 疏通管道用的搋子； A plunger is a device for clearing waste pipes.
plunging: [ADJ 形容词] 女服领口低V字形的，深开的； A dress or blouse with a plunging neckline is cut in a very low V-shape at the front.
plunk: [VERB 动词] 随意地放下；漫不经心地放下； plunk If you plunk something somewhere, you put it there without great care.  /  [VERB 动词] 使砰地坐下；使重重地坐下； plunk If you plunk yourself somewhere, or plunk down , you sit down heavily and clumsily.
pluperfect: [N-SING 单数名词] 同 past perfect； The pluperfect is the same as the past perfect .
plural: [ADJ 形容词] 复数的；复数形式的； plural The plural form of a word is the form that is used when referring to more than one person or thing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 复数；复数形式； plural The plural of a noun is the form of it that is used to refer to more than one person or thing.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 多元的；多种群体的； plural A plural society or system involves different kinds of people.
pluralism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 多元化；多元性； pluralism If there is pluralism within a society, it has many different groups and political parties.
pluralist: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 多元化的；多元性的； pluralist A pluralist society is one in which many different groups and political parties are allowed to exist.
pluralistic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 同 pluralist； pluralistic Pluralistic means the same as pluralist .
plurality: [QUANT-PLURAL 复数数量词] 多数状态；诸多；众多； plurality If there is a plurality of things, a number of them exist.  /  [QUANT-PLURAL 复数数量词] 超过其他任何一方的多数； plurality If a candidate, political party, or idea has the support of a plurality of people, they have more support than any other candidate, party, or idea.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 指选举中获胜者得到的不及其他所有候选人得票总和的相对多数票； plurality A plurality in an election is the number of votes that the winner gets, when this is less than the total number of votes for all the other candidates.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 指选举中获得最多票数的候选人与得票数第二的候选人之间的票数差额； plurality A plurality in an election is the difference in the number of votes between the candidate who gets the most votes and the candidate who comes second.
plus: [CONJ-COORD 连词] 加；加上； plus You say plus to show that one number or quantity is being added to another.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 正数的；在零以上的； plus Plus before a number or quantity means that the number or quantity is greater than zero.  /  [CONJ-COORD 连词] 而且；还有； plus You can use plus when mentioning an additional item or fact.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 用于数字或数量后多于…的； plus You use plus after a number or quantity to indicate that the actual number or quantity is greater than the one mentioned.
plus-fours: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 过去狩猎或打高尔夫球时穿的宽大运动裤，灯笼裤； Plus-fours are short wide trousers fastened below the knees which people used to wear when hunting or playing golf.
plush: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 豪华的；奢华的；舒适的； plush If you describe something as plush , you mean that it is very smart, comfortable, or expensive.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤用于地毯和给家具覆面的长毛绒； plush Plush is a thick soft material like velvet, used especially for carpets and to cover furniture.
plus sign: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 加号，正号＋； A plus sign is the sign + which is put between two numbers in order to show that the second number is being added to the first.
plutocracy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 富豪或财阀统治的国家；富豪或财阀统治阶级； plutocracy A plutocracy is a country which is ruled by its wealthiest people, or a class of wealthy people who rule a country.
plutocrat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 富豪；财阀； plutocrat If you describe someone as a plutocrat , you disapprove of them because you believe they are powerful only because they are rich.
plutonium: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 钚尤用于核武器及用作核电站燃料的一种放射性元素； Plutonium is a radioactive element used especially in nuclear weapons and as a fuel in nuclear power stations.
ply: [VERB 动词] 不断供给； If you ply someone with food or drink, you keep giving them more of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 不断问；追问； If you ply someone with questions, you keep asking them questions.  /  [VERB 动词] 从事，经营尤指街头销售或服务； ply If you ply a trade, you do a particular kind of work regularly as your job, especially a kind of work that involves trying to sell goods or services to people outdoors.  /  [VERB 动词] 船、飞机或车辆定期往返于； ply If a ship, aircraft, or vehicle plies a route, it makes regular journeys along that route.
-ply: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] 用于数字后表示“股”； -ply You use -ply after a number to indicate how many pieces are twisted together to make a type of wool, thread, or rope.
plywood: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 胶合板； plywood Plywood is wood that consists of thin layers of wood stuck together.

pneumonia: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 肺炎； pneumonia Pneumonia is a serious disease which affects your lungs and makes it difficult for you to breathe.

poach: [VERB 动词] 侵入他人地界偷猎，偷捕； poach poacher poaching If someone poaches fish, animals, or birds, they illegally catch them on someone else's property.  /  [VERB 动词] 挖其他机构的成员或顾客； poach poaching If an organization poaches members or customers from another organization, they secretly or dishonestly persuade them to join them or become their customers.  /  [VERB 动词] 窃取，盗用他人的想法； poach If someone poaches an idea, they dishonestly or illegally use the idea.  /  [VERB 动词] 把鸡蛋打入沸水中煮； poach When you poach an egg, you cook it gently in boiling water without its shell.
PO Box: 用于数字之前邮政信箱； PO Box is used before a number as a kind of address.

pressure: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 压力； pressure Pressure is force that you produce when you press hard on something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 压力；气压；压强； pressure The pressure in a place or container is the force produced by the quantity of gas or liquid in that place or container.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 向某人施加的压力； pressure If there is pressure on a person, someone is trying to persuade or force them to do something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 工作等的压力； pressure If you are experiencing pressure , you feel that you must do a lot of tasks or make a lot of decisions in very little time, or that people expect a lot from you.

pressure group: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 为说服政府或其他权力机关而组织的压力集团； pressure group A pressure group is an organized group of people who are trying to persuade a government or other authority to do something, for example to change a law.

pressy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 礼物；礼品； A pressy is something that you give to someone, for example at Christmas, or when you visit them.
prestige: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 声望；威望；威信； prestige If a person, a country, or an organization has prestige , they are admired and respected because of the position they hold or the things they have achieved.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 气派的；贵重的；令人敬仰的； prestige Prestige is used to describe products, places, or activities which people admire because they are associated with being rich or having a high social position.
prestigious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有威望的；有声望的；有威信的；受尊敬的； prestigious A prestigious institution, job, or activity is respected and admired by people.

presumptuous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 放肆的；冒昧的；自作主张的； presumptuous If you describe someone or their behaviour as presumptuous , you disapprove of them because they are doing something that they have no right or authority to do.

pretender: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 职位的觊觎者，冒充者； pretender A pretender to a position is someone who claims the right to that position, and whose claim is disputed by others.
pretension: [N-VAR 可变名词] 自命不凡；虚荣；矫饰； pretension If you say that someone has pretensions , you disapprove of them because they claim or pretend that they are more important than they really are.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 声称；标榜；自称； pretension If someone has pretensions to something, they claim to be or do that thing.

pretzel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 通常为纽结状或棒状的咸脆饼干； A pretzel is a small, crisp, shiny biscuit, which has salt on the outside.

prevalent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 流行的；盛行的；普遍的； prevalent prevalence A condition, practice, or belief that is prevalent is common.

prevent: [VERB 动词] 防止；预防；阻止； prevent prevention To prevent something means to ensure that it does not happen.  /  [VERB 动词] 阻止；制止；阻碍；  prevent To prevent someone from doing something means to make it impossible for them to do it.

price war: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 价格战； price war If competing companies are involved in a price war , they each try to gain an advantage by lowering their prices as much as possible in order to sell more of their products and damage their competitors financially.

prompt: [VERB 动词] 促使；推动；引起； prompt To prompt someone to do something means to make them decide to do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 鼓励，提示[说话者]; 给演员提词； prompt If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 迅速的；即刻的；立即的；及时的； prompt A prompt action is done without any delay.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 敏捷的；迅速的；及时的； prompt If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

prone: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有不好的倾向的；易于…的；很可能…的； prone 与名词连用构成形容词表示“易受…影响的” See also: accident prone ; To be prone to something, usually something bad, means to have a tendency to be affected by it or to do it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 俯卧的；面部或腹部朝下的； prone If you are lying prone , you are lying on your front.

puce: [COLOUR 颜色词] 紫褐色；深紫色； puce Something that is puce is a dark purple colour.
puck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 冰球运动中的冰球； In the game of ice hockey, the puck is the small rubber disc that is used instead of a ball.
pucker: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使脸起皱；使嘴撅起； pucker puckered When a part of your face puckers or when you pucker it, it becomes tight or stretched, often because you are trying not to cry or are going to kiss someone.

pud: [N-VAR 可变名词] 同pudding； pud Pud is the same as pudding .
pudding: [N-VAR 可变名词] 布丁； pudding A pudding is a cooked sweet food made with flour, fat, and eggs, and usually served hot.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 一餐中的甜点，甜食； pudding Some people refer to the sweet course of a meal as the pudding .  /  See also: Yorkshire pudding ;  /  [PHRASE 短语] 布丁好坏，不尝不知；试过才知好坏； If you say the proof of the pudding or the proof of the pudding is in the eating , you mean that something new can only be judged to be good or bad after it has been tried or used.
pudding basin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 调拌食物的深盆；布丁蒸盘； A pudding basin is a deep round bowl that is used in the kitchen, especially for mixing or for cooking puddings.
puddle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 水坑；小坑；水洼； puddle A puddle is a small, shallow pool of liquid that has spread on the ground.
pudgy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肥胖的；胖墩墩的； pudgy If you describe someone as pudgy , you mean that they are rather fat in an unattractive way.
puerile: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 幼稚的；孩子气的；愚蠢的； puerile If you describe someone or something as puerile , you mean that they are silly and childish.
puff: [VERB 动词] 吸，抽香烟等； puff If someone puffs at a cigarette, cigar, or pipe, they smoke it.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 吹；喷；吐； puff puff out同puff If you puff smoke or moisture from your mouth or if it puffs from your mouth, you breathe it out.  /  [VERB 动词] 引擎、烟囱或锅炉冒烟或气； puff If an engine, chimney, or boiler puffs smoke or steam, clouds of smoke or steam come out of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 吹出的一缕，一股； puff A puff of something such as air or smoke is a small amount of it that is blown out from somewhere.
puffball: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 马勃菌； A puffball is a round fungus which bursts when it is ripe and sends a cloud of seeds into the air.
puffed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肿的；肿胀的； puffed If a part of your body is puffed or puffed up , it is swollen because of an injury or because you are unwell.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 气喘吁吁的；上气不接下气的； puffed If you are puffed or puffed out , you are breathing with difficulty because you have been using a lot of energy.
puffed up: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自满的；自负的； puffed up See also: puffed ; If you describe someone as puffed up , you disapprove of them because they are very proud of themselves and think that they are very important.
puffin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 角嘴海雀；海鹦； A puffin is a black and white seabird with a large, brightly-coloured beak.
puff out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 鼓起双颊； See also: puff ; If you puff out your cheeks, you make them larger and rounder by filling them with air.
puff pastry: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 千层酥面团；油酥面团； Puff pastry is a type of pastry which is very light and consists of a lot of thin layers.
puff up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 肿胀；肿起； See also: puffed up ; If part of your body puffs up as a result of an injury or illness, it becomes swollen.
puffy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 尤指脸部肿胀的，浮肿的； puffy puffiness If a part of someone's body, especially their face, is puffy , it has a round, swollen appearance.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 云朵白色棉团状的； puffy If you describe a cloud as puffy , you mean that it looks like a large ball of white cotton wool.
pug: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 哈巴狗； A pug is a small, fat, short-haired dog with a flat face.
pugilist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拳击运动员；拳击手； A pugilist is a boxer.
pugnacious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 好斗的；好争吵的；好战的； pugnacious Someone who is pugnacious is always ready to quarrel or start a fight.
pugnacity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 好斗；好争；好战； pugnacity Pugnacity is the quality of being pugnacious.
puke: [VERB 动词] 呕；吐；呕吐； puke puke up同puke When someone pukes , they vomit.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同vomit； puke Puke is the same as vomit .
pukka: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 真正的；第一流的； pukka If you describe something or someone as pukka , you mean that they are real or genuine, and of good quality.
pull: [VERB 动词] 拉；拖；牵；扯； pull When you pull something, you hold it firmly and use force in order to move it towards you or away from its previous position.  /  [VERB 动词] 拿出；抽出； pull When you pull an object from a bag, pocket, or cupboard, you put your hand in and bring the object out.  /  [VERB 动词] 拉，拖车或机械装置； pull When a vehicle, animal, or person pulls a cart or piece of machinery, they are attached to it or hold it, so that it moves along behind them when they move forward.  /  [VERB 动词] 挣脱；移开；抽出； pull If you pull yourself or pull a part of your body in a particular direction, you move your body or a part of your body with effort or force.
pull away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车辆开始驶离；驾车者开走车辆； pull away When a vehicle or driver pulls away , the vehicle starts moving forward.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 远离；疏远； pull away If you pull away from someone that you have had close links with, you deliberately become less close to them.
pull back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 退出；退却； pull back If someone pulls back from an action, they decide not to do it or continue with it, because it could have bad consequences.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使撤退；使撤离； pull back If troops pull back or if their leader pulls them back , they go some or all of the way back to their own territory.
pull down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拆毁；摧毁；拆掉； pull down To pull down a building or statue means to deliberately destroy it.
pulley: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑轮；皮带轮； pulley A pulley is a device consisting of a wheel over which a rope or chain is pulled in order to lift heavy objects.
pull in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车停下；驾车者停车； When a vehicle or driver pulls in somewhere, the vehicle stops there.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 逮捕；把…抓起来； If the police pull someone in , they arrest them and take them to the police station.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 挣；获得；赚取； pull in If you pull in an amount of money, you earn or collect that amount.  /  »see: pull 9 ; �
pull into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使驶入停下； When a vehicle or driver pulls into a place, the vehicle moves into the place and stops there.
Pullman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 豪华型的普尔曼式列车或车厢； A Pullman is a type of train or railway carriage which is extremely comfortable and luxurious.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 卧铺车厢； A Pullman or a Pullman car on a train is a railway car that provides beds for passengers to sleep in.
pull off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 成功完成，做成困难的事情； If you pull off something very difficult, you succeed in achieving it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车或驾车者停靠路边； If a vehicle or driver pulls off the road, the vehicle stops by the side of the road.
pull out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车或驾车者驶离路边，开向路中间； pull out When a vehicle or driver pulls out , the vehicle moves out into the road or nearer the centre of the road.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 退出，撤出协议、比赛或组织； pull out If you pull out of an agreement, a contest, or an organization, you withdraw from it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使撤退；使退出； pull out If troops pull out of a place or if their leader pulls them out , they leave it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使摆脱[经济衰退]; 使恢复； pull out If a country pulls out of recession or if someone pulls it out , it begins to recover from it.
pull-out: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 报纸或杂志中的活页； pull-out In a newspaper or magazine, a pull-out is a section which you can remove easily and keep.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 军队的撤出，撤退； pull-out When there is a pull-out of armed forces from a place, troops which have occupied an area of land withdraw from it.
pull over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车驶向路边停下；驾车者靠路边停车； pull over When a vehicle or driver pulls over , the vehicle moves closer to the side of the road and stops there.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 通常因司机危险驾驶，警察令驾车者或车辆停靠路边； If the police pull over a driver or vehicle, they make the driver stop at the side of the road, usually because the driver has been driving dangerously.  /  See also: pullover ; �
pullover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 套头毛衣； A pullover is a piece of woollen clothing that covers the upper part of your body and your arms.
pull through: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 大病后康复；经历困境后恢复正常； pull through If someone with a serious illness or someone in a very difficult situation pulls through , they recover.
pull together: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 齐心协力；团结起来；通力合作； pull together If people pull together , they help each other or work together in order to deal with a difficult situation.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 保持镇定；克制自己；振作起来； If you are upset or depressed and someone tells you to pull yourself together , they are telling you to control your feelings and behave calmly again.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…串到一起；把…连成一个整体； pull together If you pull together different facts or ideas, you link them to form a single theory, argument, or story.
pull up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车或驾车者减速停下； When a vehicle or driver pulls up , the vehicle slows down and stops.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把椅子拉到近处坐下； If you pull up a chair, you move it closer to something or someone and sit on it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使突然停下；使猛地停住； If you pull up or if something pulls you up , you suddenly stop what you are doing.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 提高；改进； If someone pulls you up or if you pull yourself up , you improve your situation or your skill at something.
pull up on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 责备；责骂； If someone pulls you up on something, they criticize you for something wrong that you have done.
pulmonary: [ADJ 形容词] 肺的；肺部的； pulmonary Pulmonary means relating to your lungs.
pulp: [N-SING 单数名词] 泥；酱；浆；糊； pulp If an object is pressed into a pulp , it is crushed or beaten until it is soft, smooth, and wet.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 果肉；蔬菜的肉质部分； pulp In fruit or vegetables, the pulp is the soft part inside the skin.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 木浆造纸原料； Wood pulp is material made from crushed wood.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 故事或小说粗制滥造的，庸俗刺激的，耸人听闻的； pulp People refer to stories or novels as pulp fiction when they consider them to be of poor quality and intentionally shocking or sensational.
pulpit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 讲坛；布道坛； A pulpit is a small raised platform with a rail or barrier around it in a church, where a member of the clergy stands to speak.
pulpy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 多果肉的；多汁的；浆状的；软糊状的； pulpy Something that is pulpy is soft, smooth, and wet, often because it has been crushed or beaten.
pulsar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脉冲星； A pulsar is a star that spins very fast and cannot be seen but produces regular radio signals.
pulsate: [VERB 动词] 有节奏地搏动，跳动，震动； pulsate pulsation If something pulsates , it beats, moves in and out, or shakes with strong, regular movements.
pulse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脉搏；脉动； pulse Your pulse is the regular beating of blood through your body, which you can feel when you touch particular parts of your body, especially your wrist.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拍子；节奏；常指鼓点； pulse In music, a pulse is a regular beat, which is often produced by a drum.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脉冲； pulse A pulse of electrical current, light, or sound is a temporary increase in its level.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 意向；心态； pulse If you refer to the pulse of a group in society, you mean the ideas, opinions, or feelings they have at a particular time.

puma: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 美洲狮； A puma is a wild animal that is a member of the cat family.
pumice: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 浮石，浮岩，轻石一种火山石，用于去污以及柔肤等； Pumice is a kind of grey stone from a volcano and is very light in weight.
pumice stone: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 浮石，浮岩，轻石用于清洁皮肤或使皮肤光滑等； A pumice stone is a piece of pumice that you rub over your skin in order to clean the skin or make it smoother.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同pumice； Pumice stone is the same as pumice .
pummel: [VERB 动词] 连续猛击；反复拳打；捶打； pummel If you pummel someone or something, you hit them many times using your fists.
pump: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 泵；抽水机；打气筒； pump A pump is a machine or device that is used to force a liquid or gas to flow in a particular direction.  /  [VERB 动词] 抽吸；抽运；泵送； pump To pump a liquid or gas in a particular direction means to force it to flow in that direction using a pump.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 汽油加油泵； pump A petrol or gas pump is a machine with a tube attached to it that you use to fill a car with petrol.  /  [VERB 动词] 洗胃； pump If someone has their stomach pumped , doctors remove the contents of their stomach, for example because they have swallowed poison or drugs.
pumpernickel: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤指德国的裸麦粗面包，黑面包； Pumpernickel is a dark brown, heavy bread, which is eaten especially in Germany.
pumpkin: [N-VAR 可变名词] 南瓜；倭瓜； pumpkin A pumpkin is a large, round, orange vegetable with a thick skin.
pump out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 大量生产或提供； To pump out something means to produce or supply it continually and in large amounts.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 流行音乐等响亮地奏出，喧闹地传出； If pop music pumps out , it plays very loudly.
pump up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 用泵或气筒给…打气； pump up If you pump up something such as a tyre, you fill it with air using a pump.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 尤指通过自我心理暗示给自己打气，自我鼓励； If you pump yourself up for something, you prepare yourself for it mentally, especially by telling yourself that you can succeed.
pun: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 双关诙谐语；双关语； A pun is a clever and amusing use of a word or phrase with two meanings, or of words with the same sound but different meanings.  /  [VERB 动词] 谐用双关语； pun punning If you pun , you try to amuse people by making a pun.
punch: [VERB 动词] 用拳猛击或攻击； punch 美国英语中punch out同punch puncher If you punch someone or something, you hit them hard with your fist.  /  [VERB 动词] 挥舞拳头； punch If you punch the air , you put one or both of your fists forcefully above your shoulders as a gesture of delight or victory.  /  [VERB 动词] 按[键等]; 压按钮等； punch If you punch something such as the buttons on a keyboard, you touch them in order to store information on a machine such as a computer or to give the machine a command to do something.  /  [VERB 动词] 戳，刺洞； punch If you punch holes in something, you make holes in it by pushing or pressing it with something sharp.
Punch and Judy show: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 《潘趣和朱迪》木偶戏英国儿童木偶剧，常在集市或海边演出，主角潘趣和朱迪常常拌嘴； A Punch and Judy show is a puppet show for children, often performed at fairs or at the seaside.
punchbag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沙袋； A punchbag is a heavy leather bag, filled with a firm material, that hangs on a rope.
punch bowl: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 潘趣酒碗； A punch bowl is a large bowl in which drinks, especially punch, are mixed and served.
punch-drunk: [ADJ 形容词] 被击晕的；晕头转向的； A punch-drunk boxer shows signs of brain damage, for example by being unsteady and unable to think clearly, after being hit too often on the head.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 精疲力竭的；头昏脑涨的； punch-drunk If you say that someone is punch-drunk , you mean that they are very tired or confused, for example because they have been working too hard.
punch in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将信息输入计算机； If you punch in a number on a machine or punch numbers into it, you push the machine's buttons or keys in order to give it a command to do something.
punching bag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 punchbag； A punching bag is the same as a punchbag .
punchline: 笑话结尾处的包袱，妙语，笑点； also punch line, punchline.
punch-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 打架；斗殴； punch-up A punch-up is a fight in which people hit each other.
punchy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 简洁有力的；言简意赅的； punchy If you describe something as punchy , you mean that it expresses its meaning in a forceful or effective way.

pundit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 行家；权威；专家； pundit A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a subject and is often asked to give information or opinions about it to the public.

putative: [ADJ 形容词] 公认的；推定的； putative If you describe someone or something as putative , you mean that they are generally thought to be the thing mentioned.

put back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拖延；推迟； put back To put something back means to delay it or arrange for it to happen later than you previously planned.
put by: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 积蓄；储存； put by If you put money by , you save it so that you can use it later.
put down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 写下；记录；键入； put down If you put something down somewhere, you write or type it there.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 付定金； put down If you put down some money, you pay part of the price of something, and will pay the rest later.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 镇压暴乱或叛乱； put down When soldiers, police, or the government put down a riot or rebellion, they stop it by using force.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 贬低；奚落；使窘迫； put down See also: put-down ; If someone puts you down , they treat you in an unpleasant way by criticizing you in front of other people or making you appear foolish.
