related: [ADJ 形容词] 相关的;有联系的； related If two or more things are related , there is a connection between them.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 有亲属关系的;属同一家族的； related People who are related belong to the same family.  /  (动物)有亲缘关系的;(语言)同源的； related If you say that different types of animal or different languages are related , you mean that they have developed from the same type of animal or language.
relation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (人、团体或国家之间的)联系，关系，往来； relation See also: industrial relations ; public relations ; race relations ; Relations between people, groups, or countries are contacts between them and the way in which they behave towards each other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (两者之间的)关系，联系，关联； relation If you talk about the relation of one thing to another, you are talking about the ways in which they are connected.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 亲戚;亲属;家庭成员； relation See also: poor relation ; Your relations are the members of your family.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 与…相比； relation You can talk about something in relation to something else when you want to compare the size, condition, or position of the two things.
relationship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (人、团体等之间的)关系，关联； relationship The relationship between two people or groups is the way in which they feel and behave towards each other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 恋爱关系；性关系；感情关系； relationship A relationship is a close friendship between two people, especially one involving romantic or sexual feelings.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (事物之间的)关系，关联，联系； relationship The relationship between two things is the way in which they are connected.
relative: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 亲戚;亲属;家属； relative Your relatives are the members of your family.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 相对的； relative You use relative to say that something is true to a certain degree, especially when compared with other things of the same kind.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 相对的;比较而言的； relative You use relative when you are comparing the quality or size of two things.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 与…相比;与…有关;涉及;关于； relative Relative to something means with reference to it or in comparison with it.
relative clause: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 关系从句； In grammar, a relative clause is a subordinate clause which specifies or gives information about a person or thing.
relatively: [ADV 副词] 相对而言;比较起来;某种程度上； relatively Relatively means to a certain degree, especially when compared with other things of the same kind.
relative pronoun: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 关系代词； A relative pronoun is a word such as 'who', 'that', or 'which' that is used to introduce a relative clause.
relativism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 相对论;相对主义； relativism Relativism is the belief that the truth is not always the same but varies according to circumstances.
relativist: [ADJ 形容词] 相对论的;相对主义的； relativist 相对论者;相对主义者 A relativist position or argument is one according to which the truth is not always the same, but varies according to circumstances.
relativity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 相对论； The theory of relativity is Einstein's theory concerning space, time, and motion.
relaunch: [VERB 动词] 重新开办公司;重新推出(产品)；重新实施计划； relaunch To relaunch something such as a company, a product, or a scheme means to start it again or to produce it in a different way.
relax: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使放松;使松弛； relax If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] (使) 身体)放松;[使松弛； relax When a part of your body relaxes , or when you relax it, it becomes less stiff or firm.  /  [VERB 动词] 松手;放开;放松； relax If you relax your grip or hold on something, you hold it less tightly than before.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 放宽，放松，削弱(规定或控制)； relax If you relax a rule or your control over something, or if it relaxes , it becomes less firm or strong.
relaxation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 放松;松弛;休息； relaxation Relaxation is a way of spending time in which you rest and feel comfortable.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (规定或控制的)放松，放宽，削弱； relaxation If there is relaxation of a rule or control, it is made less firm or strong.
relaxed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 放松的;松弛的;安心的;轻松的； relaxed If you are relaxed , you are calm and not worried or tense.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (地方或情形)轻松的，舒适的，使人安心的； relaxed If a place or situation is relaxed , it is calm and peaceful.
relaxing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 愉快的;放松的； relaxing Something that is relaxing is pleasant and helps you to relax.
relay: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 接力比赛(如赛跑或游泳)； relay A relay or a relay race is a race between two or more teams, for example teams of runners or swimmers.  /  [VERB 动词] 转播，传送，传输(电视或收音机信号)； relay To relay television or radio signals means to send them or broadcast them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (接受和发送电视或广播信号的)转播设备，中继设备； relay A relay is a piece of equipment that receives television or radio signals from one place and sends them to another place.  /  [VERB 动词] 传[话]; 转述； relay If you relay something that has been said to you, you repeat it to another person.
release: [VERB 动词] 释放;放出； release If a person or animal is released from somewhere where they have been locked up or looked after, they are set free or allowed to go.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 释放;出院； release When someone is released, you refer to their release .  /  [VERB 动词] 使免除;使免于； release If someone or something releases you from a duty, task, or feeling, they free you from it.  /  [VERB 动词] 发泄，释放(情感);展示(能力)； release To release feelings or abilities means to allow them to be expressed.
relegate: [VERB 动词] 贬黜;把…降级;把…降格； relegate If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.  /  [VERB 动词] 使(球队)降级； relegate relegation If a sports team that competes in a league is relegated , it has to compete in a lower division in the next competition, because it was one of the least successful teams in the higher division.
relent: [VERB 动词] 变宽厚;变温和;心软； relent If you relent , you allow someone to do something that you had previously refused to allow them to do.  /  [VERB 动词] (天气)转晴，缓和，转好； relent If bad weather relents , it improves.
relentless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不停的;不懈的;不间断的；未减轻的； relentless relentlessly Something bad that is relentless never stops or never becomes less intense.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坚韧的;不屈不挠的； relentless relentlessly Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.
relevance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对…的)重要性，意义，相关性； relevance Something's relevance to a situation or person is its importance or significance in that situation or to that person.
relevant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 相关的;相应的;有重要性的； relevant Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 适当的;合适的;确切的； relevant The relevant thing of a particular kind is the one that is appropriate.
reliable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 可靠的;可信赖的； reliable reliably reliability People or things that are reliable can be trusted to work well or to behave in the way that you want them to.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (信息)可靠的，可信的,确凿的； reliable reliably reliability Information that is reliable or that is from a reliable source is very likely to be correct.
reliance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 依赖；依靠； reliance A person's or thing's reliance on something is the fact that they need it and often cannot live or work without it.
reliant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 依赖的;依靠的； reliant See also: self-reliant ; A person or thing that is reliant on something needs it and often cannot live or work without it.
relic: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 遗物;遗迹;纪念物； relic If you refer to something or someone as a relic of an earlier period, you mean that they belonged to that period but have survived into the present.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (有历史价值的)遗物，遗迹，遗址； relic A relic is something which was made or used a long time ago and which is kept for its historical significance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 圣物;圣骨； A relic is the body of a saint or something else associated with a saint, which some people regard as holy.
relief: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 宽慰;安心;欣慰;解脱； relief If you feel a sense of relief , you feel happy because something unpleasant has not happened or is no longer happening.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (疼痛或苦痛的)解除，免除，减轻，缓解； relief If something provides relief from pain or distress, it stops the pain or distress.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 救济;救援物资； relief Relief is money, food, or clothing that is provided for people who are very poor, or who have been affected by war or a natural disaster.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 代班人;换班工人； relief A relief worker is someone who does your work when you go home, or who is employed to do it instead of you when you are sick.
relieve: [VERB 动词] 缓和，缓解，减轻，解除(不愉快的情绪或形势)； relieve If something relieves an unpleasant feeling or situation, it makes it less unpleasant or causes it to disappear completely.  /  [VERB 动词] 使解脱;使摆脱； relieve If someone or something relieves you of an unpleasant feeling or difficult task, they take it from you.  /  [VERB 动词] 使从…中解脱出来； relieve If someone relieves you of something, they take it away from you.  /  [VERB 动词] 接替…的职位;代…的班； relieve If you relieve someone, you take their place and continue to do the job or duty that they have been doing.
relieved: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 感到宽慰的;感到安心的;宽心的； relieved If you are relieved , you feel happy because something unpleasant has not happened or is no longer happening.
religion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 宗教信仰;宗教活动； religion Religion is belief in a god or gods and the activities that are connected with this belief, such as praying or worshipping in a building such as a church or temple.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 宗教;教派； religion A religion is a particular system of belief in a god or gods and the activities that are connected with this system.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (突然)信教，皈依某种宗教； religion If you say that someone has got religion , you are referring in a mocking way to the fact that they have suddenly decided to follow a particular religion.
religiosity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (过度)虔诚;笃信宗教； religiosity If you refer to a person's religiosity , you are referring to the fact that they are religious in a way which seems exaggerated and insincere.
religious: [ADJ 形容词] 宗教的;信教的； religious religiously You use religious to describe things that are connected with religion or with one particular religion.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 虔诚的;宗教信仰坚定的； religious Someone who is religious has a strong belief in a god or gods.  /  See also: religiously ; �
religiously: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 笃信地;严谨地;认真地； religiously If you do something religiously , you do it very regularly because you feel you have to.  /  See also: religious ; �
relinquish: [VERB 动词] 放弃，出让(权力或控制)； relinquish If you relinquish something such as power or control, you give it up.
reliquary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (保存圣人遗物的)圣骨匣, 遗骨匣, 圣物箱； A reliquary is a container where religious objects connected with a saint are kept.
relish: [VERB 动词] 喜爱;玩味;欣赏;品味； relish If you relish something, you get a lot of enjoyment from it.  /  [VERB 动词] 盼望;期待;享受； relish If you relish the idea, thought, or prospect of something, you are looking forward to it very much.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 开胃小菜;调味品； Relish is a sauce or pickle that you eat with other food in order to give the other food more flavour.
relive: [VERB 动词] 在记忆或想象中再次体验，回味，重温； relive If you relive something that has happened to you in the past, you remember it and imagine that you are experiencing it again.
reload: [VERB 动词] 再次给枪上膛;再装填； reload If someone reloads a gun, they load it again by putting in more bullets or explosive.
relocate: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使迁移;使搬迁;重新安置； relocate relocation If people or businesses relocate or if someone relocates them, they move to a different place.
relocation expenses: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 安置费;安家费； Relocation expenses are a sum of money that a company pays to someone who moves to a new area in order to work for the company.
reluctant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 勉强的;不情愿的； reluctant reluctantly reluctance If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.
rely: [VERB 动词] 依赖;依靠； If you rely on someone or something, you need them and depend on them in order to live or work properly.  /  [VERB 动词] 信赖;信任； rely If you can rely on someone to work well or to behave as you want them to, you can trust them to do this.
REM: [ADJ 形容词] 睡眠快速眼部运动的； REM sleep is a period of sleep that is very deep, during which your eyes and muscles make many small movements.
remain: [V-LINK 连系动词] 保持;继续;持续； remain If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.  /  [VERB 动词] 留在，停留于(某处)； remain If you remain in a place, you stay there and do not move away.  /  [VERB 动词] 仍然存在;继续存在； remain You can say that something remains when it still exists.  /  [V-LINK 连系动词] 遗留;剩余； remain If something remains to be done, it has not yet been done and still needs to be done.
remainder: [QUANT 数量词] 剩余部分;剩余物;余下的人(或物)； remainder The remainder of a group are the things or people that still remain after the other things or people have gone or have been dealt with.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (算术中的)余数； In arithmetic, the remainder is the amount that remains when one amount cannot be exactly divided by another.  /  [VERB 动词] (因为滞销而)廉价出售图书； remainder If a book is remaindered , it is sold at a reduced price because it has not been selling very well and will not be published again.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 廉价销售的书； A remainder is a book that has been remaindered.
remaining: [ADJ 形容词] 余下的;剩余的； remaining The remaining things or people out of a group are the things or people that still exist, are still present, or have not yet been dealt with.  /  See also: remain ; �
remake: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 重新摄制的作品；翻拍的电影； remake A remake is a film that has the same story, and often the same title, as a film that was made earlier.  /  [VERB 动词] 重拍，翻拍(电影)； If a film is remade , a new film is made that has the same story, and often the same title, as a film that was made earlier.  /  [VERB 动词] (尤指以更好的方式)重新做，改造，翻新； If you have something remade , you ask someone to make it again, especially in a way that is better than before.
remand: [VERB 动词] 将…还押候审;使取保候审； remand If a person who is accused of a crime is remanded in custody or on bail, they are told to return to the court at a later date, when their trial will take place.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 还押候审[期]; 取保候审期； remand Remand is used to refer to the process of remanding someone in custody or on bail, or to the period of time until their trial begins.
remand centre: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英国)拘留所，在押候审中心； In Britain, a remand centre is an institution where people who are accused of a crime are sent until their trial begins or until a decision about their punishment has been made.
remark: [VERB 动词] 说;谈到； remark If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 评论;意见； remark If you make a remark about something, you say something about it.
remarkable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不同寻常的;非凡的;引人注目的； remarkable remarkably Someone or something that is remarkable is unusual or special in a way that makes people notice them and be surprised or impressed.
remarriage: [N-VAR 可变名词] 再婚； remarriage Remarriage is the act of remarrying.
remarry: [VERB 动词] (离婚或丧偶后)再婚； If someone remarries , they marry again after they have obtained a divorce from their previous husband or wife, or after their previous husband or wife has died.
remaster: [VERB 动词] 重新录制(电影);重新灌录(唱片)； remaster If a film or musical recording is remastered , a new recording is made of the old version, using modern technology to improve the quality.
rematch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (因为平局或有争议而进行的)复赛，再赛，重赛； rematch A rematch is a second game that is played between two people or teams, for example because their first match was a draw or because there was a dispute about some aspect of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (比赛或竞赛对手之间的)复赛，二次交手； rematch A rematch is a second game or contest between two people or teams who have already faced each other.
remedial: [ADJ 形容词] 补习的;辅导的； remedial Remedial education is intended to improve a person's ability to read, write, or do mathematics, especially when they find these things difficult.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 治疗的;帮助康复的； remedial Remedial activities are intended to improve a person's health when they are ill.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 补救的;纠正的； remedial Remedial action is intended to correct something that has been done wrong or that has not been successful.
remedy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (问题的)解决方法，解决良方； remedy A remedy is a successful way of dealing with a problem.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 药品;治疗方法； A remedy is something that is intended to cure you when you are ill or in pain.  /  [VERB 动词] 纠正;补救;矫正； remedy If you remedy something that is wrong or harmful, you correct it or improve it.
remember: [VERB 动词] 记得;记起;想起； remember If you remember people or events from the past, you still have an idea of them in your mind and you are able to think about them.  /  [VERB 动词] (经过一段时间后)忆起，回忆起； remember If you remember that something is the case, you become aware of it again after a time when you did not think about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 用于否定记起，想起； remember If you cannot remember something, you are not able to bring it back into your mind when you make an effort to do so.  /  [VERB 动词] 记住，记得(做某事)； remember If you remember to do something, you do it when you intend to.
remembrance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对逝者的)怀念，纪念，缅怀； remembrance If you do something in remembrance of a dead person, you do it as a way of showing that you want to remember them and that you respect them.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 记忆;回忆； remembrance A remembrance is a memory that you have of someone or something.
Remembrance Day: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 阵亡将士纪念日(英国纪念两次世界大战中阵亡者的日子，在每年最接近11月11日的周日)； Remembrance Day In Britain, Remembrance Day or Remembrance Sunday is the Sunday nearest to the 11th of November, when people honour the memory of those who died in the two world wars.
remind: [VERB 动词] 使想起;使记起;提醒； remind If someone reminds you of a fact or event that you already know about, they say something which makes you think about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 让我提醒你…/我能提醒你…； remind You use remind in expressions such as Let me remind you that and May I remind you that to introduce a piece of information that you want to emphasize.  /  [VERB 动词] 提醒(某人做某事);使想起(做某事)； remind If someone reminds you to do a particular thing, they say something which makes you remember to do it.  /  [VERB 动词] (因为相似)使联想到；  remind If you say that someone or something reminds you of another person or thing, you mean that they are similar to the other person or thing and that they make you think about them.
reminder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 提示;使人回忆起某事的事物； reminder Something that serves as a reminder of another thing makes you think about the other thing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 缴费单;催缴单;催缴通知； reminder A reminder is a letter or note that is sent to tell you that you have not done something such as pay a bill or return library books.
reminisce: [VERB 动词] 追忆;回忆;叙旧； reminisce If you reminisce about something from your past, you write or talk about it, often with pleasure.
reminiscence: [N-VAR 可变名词] 回忆;旧事;追忆的往事； reminiscence Someone's reminiscences are things that they remember from the past, and which they talk or write about.
reminiscent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 使人想起的;使人忆起的； reminiscent If you say that one thing is reminiscent of another, you mean that it reminds you of it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 怀旧的;缅怀过去的； reminiscent reminiscently A reminiscent look or smile is a look or smile which shows that you are remembering something from the past, usually with pleasure.
remiss: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 懈怠的;疏忽的;不负责任的； remiss If someone is remiss , they are careless about doing things which ought to be done.
remission: [N-VAR 可变名词] (疾病的)减轻，缓和； remission If someone who has had a serious disease such as cancer is in remission or if the disease is in remission , the disease has been controlled so that they are not as ill as they were.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 减刑； remission If someone in prison gets remission , their prison sentence is reduced, usually because they have behaved well.
remit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 职责;职权范围； remit Someone's remit is the area of activity which they are expected to deal with, or which they have authority to deal with.  /  [VERB 动词] 汇款;寄钱； remit If you remit money to someone, you send it to them.  /  [VERB 动词] 将(案件)发回原审判法庭重审； remit In an appeal court, if a case is remitted to the court where it was originally dealt with, it is sent back to be dealt with there.
remittance: [N-VAR 可变名词] (一笔)汇款； remittance A remittance is a sum of money that you send to someone.
remix: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 混音版音乐;重混乐； remix A remix is a new version of a piece of music which has been created by putting together the individual instrumental and vocal parts in a different way.  /  [VERB 动词] 重新合成乐曲； remix To remix a piece of music means to make a new version of it by putting together the individual instrumental and vocal parts in a different way.
remnant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 剩余部分;残余部分;残迹;残存物； remnant The remnants of something are small parts of it that are left over when the main part has disappeared or been destroyed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 布头;边角余料； A remnant is a small piece of cloth that is left over when most of the cloth has been sold.
remodel: [VERB 动词] 重建;改造;重塑； remodel remodelling To remodel something such as a building or a room means to give it a different form or shape.
remonstrate: [VERB 动词] 抗议;表示异议;反对； remonstrate remonstration If you remonstrate with someone, you protest to them about something you do not approve of or agree with, and you try to get it changed or stopped.
remorse: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 懊悔;自责;悔恨； remorse Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.
remorseful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 懊悔的;悔恨的;自责的； remorseful remorsefully If you are remorseful , you feel very guilty and sorry about something wrong that you have done.
remorseless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指令人不快的事情)无休止的，持续不断的，不停的； remorseless remorselessly If you describe something, especially something unpleasant, as remorseless , you mean that it goes on for a long time and cannot be stopped.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无怜悯之心的;冷酷的； remorseless remorselessly Someone who is remorseless is prepared to be cruel to other people and feels no pity for them.
remote: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 偏僻的;遥远的;边远的； remote remoteness Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (过去或未来)遥远的，久远的； remote The remote past or remote future is a time that is many years distant from the present.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 关系不紧密的;关系疏远的;相距甚远的； remote remoteness If something is remote from a particular subject or area of experience, it is not relevant to it because it is very different.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (可能性或机会)渺茫的，微乎其微的； remote If you say that there is a remote possibility or chance that something will happen, you are emphasizing that there is only a very small chance that it will happen.
remote access: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 远程登录； remote access Remote access is a system which allows you to gain access to a particular computer or network using a separate computer.
remote control: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 遥控(系统或装置)； remote control Remote control is a system of controlling a machine or a vehicle from a distance by using radio or electronic signals.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 遥控器； The remote control for a television or video recorder is the device that you use to control the machine from a distance, by pressing the buttons on it.
remote-controlled: [ADJ 形容词] 受遥控的； remote-controlled A remote-controlled machine or device is controlled from a distance by the use of radio or electronic signals.
remotely: [ADV 副词] (用于否定句)丝毫，根本； remotely You use remotely with a negative statement to emphasize the statement.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 遥远地;偏远地； remotely If someone or something is remotely placed or situated, they are a long way from other people or places.
remote sensing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 遥感;遥测； remote sensing Remote sensing is the gathering of information about something by observing it from space or from the air.
remould: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 翻新轮胎； A remould is an old tyre which has been given a new surface or tread and can be used again.  /  [VERB 动词] 改造，重塑(想法或经济)； remould To remould something such as an idea or an economy means to change it so that it has a new structure or is based on new principles.
remount: [VERB 动词] 再骑上(自行车或马)； remount When you remount a bicycle or horse, you get back on it after you have got off it or fallen off it.
removable: [ADJ 形容词] 可移动的;可拆装的;可活动的； removable A removable part of something is a part that can easily be moved from its place or position.
removal: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 消除;去除； removal The removal of something is the act of removing it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 搬家;搬移;搬迁； removal Removal is the process of transporting furniture or equipment from one building to another.
removal man: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 搬家工人;搬运工； Removal men are men whose job is to move furniture or equipment from one building to another.
remove: [VERB 动词] 移动;搬动;取出； remove If you remove something from a place, you take it away.  /  [VERB 动词] 脱下(衣服)； remove If you remove clothing, you take it off.  /  [VERB 动词] (用化学品)去除，洗掉(污渍)； remove If you remove a stain from something, you make the stain disappear by treating it with a chemical or by washing it.  /  [VERB 动词] 免除(职务)； remove If people remove someone from power or from something such as a committee, they stop them being in power or being a member of the committee.
removed: [ADJ 形容词] 相异的;不同的； removed If you say that an idea or situation is far removed from something, you mean that it is very different from it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 亲属关系隔代的，隔辈的； If someone is your cousin once removed , they are your cousin's child or your parent's cousin.
remover: [N-MASS 物质名词] (污渍等的)去除剂，清除剂； remover Remover is a substance that you use for removing an unwanted stain, mark, or coating from a surface.
remunerate: [VERB 动词] 给…报酬； remunerate If you are remunerated for work that you do, you are paid for it.
remuneration: [N-VAR 可变名词] 酬劳;薪酬； remuneration Someone's remuneration is the amount of money that they are paid for the work that they do.
remunerative: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有报酬的;有酬劳的;有偿的； remunerative Remunerative work is work that you are paid for.
renaissance: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 文艺复兴时期； The Renaissance was the period in Europe, especially Italy, in the 14th, 15th, and 16th centuries, when there was a new interest in art, literature, science, and learning.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 复兴;复活;复燃； renaissance If something experiences a renaissance , it becomes popular or successful again after a time when people were not interested in it.
Renaissance man: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指在艺术和科学方面)多才多艺者，兴趣广泛者，通才； If you describe a man as a Renaissance man , you mean that he has a wide range of abilities and interests, especially in the arts and sciences.
renal: [ADJ 形容词] 肾脏的;肾的； renal Renal describes things that concern or are related to the kidneys.
rename: [VERB 动词] 重命名;改名;更名； rename If you rename something, you change its name to a new name.
rend: [VERB 动词] 撕碎;撕裂;扯破； rend To rend something means to tear it.  /  [VERB 动词] (声音)响彻，刺破； rend If a loud sound rends the air, it is sudden and violent.  /  See also: heart-rending ; �
render: [VERB 动词] 致使;造成； render You can use render with an adjective that describes a particular state to say that someone or something is changed into that state.  /  [VERB 动词] 给予(帮助);提供(服务)； render If you render someone help or service, you help them.  /  [VERB 动词] 宣布，作出(判决、决定或回应)； render When a jury or authority renders a verdict, decision, or response, they announce it.  /  [VERB 动词] 翻译； render To render something in a particular language or in a particular way means to translate it into that language or in that way.
rendering: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (剧本、诗歌或音乐作品的)演绎，表演； rendering A rendering of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 翻译； rendering A rendering of an expression or piece of writing or speech is a translation of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (涂抹墙壁的)灰泥，水泥； The rendering on a wall is a layer of plaster or cement which covers and protects it.
rendezvous: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (常指秘密的)约会，会面，会合； rendezvous A rendezvous is a meeting, often a secret one, that you have arranged with someone for a particular time and place.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 约会地点;见面地点； rendezvous A rendezvous is the place where you have arranged to meet someone, often secretly.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 与…约会;和…会面； rendezvous If you rendezvous with someone or if the two of you rendezvous , you meet them at a time and place that you have arranged.
rendition: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (剧本、诗歌或音乐作品的)演出，表演，演绎； rendition A rendition of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.
renegade: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 叛徒;变节者;改变宗教信仰或政见者； A renegade is a person who abandons the religious, political, or philosophical beliefs that he or she used to have, and accepts opposing or different beliefs.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 离经叛道的;叛逆的;变节的； renegade Renegade is used to describe a member of a group or profession who behaves in a way that is opposed to the normal behaviour or beliefs of that group or profession.
renege: [VERB 动词] 食言;反悔； renege If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.
renew: [VERB 动词] 重新开始;更新； renew If you renew an activity, you begin it again.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 恢复，重新建立(关系)； renew If you renew a relationship with someone, you start it again after you have not seen them or have not been friendly with them for some time.  /  [VERB 动词] 延长(执照、合同等)的有效期;使续签； renew When you renew something such as a licence or a contract, you extend the period of time for which it is valid.  /  [VERB 动词] 使[受到损毁或丢失后)重获新生； renew You can say that something is renewed when it grows again or is replaced after it has been destroyed or lost.
renewable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (资源)可再生的，可更新的； renewable Renewable resources are natural ones such as wind, water, and sunlight which are always available.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 可再生资源； Renewables are natural energy sources such as wind, water, and sunlight which are always available.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (合同或协议)可延期的，可续签的； renewable If a contract or agreement is renewable , it can be extended when it reaches the end of a fixed period of time.
renewal: [N-SING 单数名词] (活动或状态的)恢复，重新开始，复兴； renewal If there is a renewal of an activity or a situation, it starts again.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (执照、合同等的)续签，延期； renewal The renewal of a document such as a licence or a contract is an official increase in the period of time for which it remains valid.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恢复;更新;再生;重建； renewal Renewal of something lost, dead, or destroyed is the process of it growing again or being replaced.
renounce: [VERB 动词] 宣布放弃，抛弃(信仰或行为方式)； renounce If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you decide and declare publicly that you no longer have that belief or will no longer behave in that way.  /  [VERB 动词] 正式放弃(要求、官阶或头衔)； renounce If you renounce a claim, rank, or title, you officially give it up.
renovate: [VERB 动词] 修复;改造;翻新； renovate renovation If someone renovates an old building, they repair and improve it and get it back into good condition.
renown: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 名望;声望； renown A person of renown is well known, usually because they do or have done something good.
renowned: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有名的;有声望的； renowned A person or place that is renowned for something, usually something good, is well known because of it.
rent: [VERB 动词] 租来;租借； rent If you rent something, you regularly pay its owner a sum of money in order to be able to have it and use it yourself.  /  [VERB 动词] 出租;租给； rent rent out 同 rent If you rent something to someone, you let them have it and use it in exchange for a sum of money which they pay you regularly.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 租金;租用费； rent Rent is the amount of money that you pay regularly to use a house, flat, or piece of land.  /  + + + Rent is the past tense and past participle of rend .
rental: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 租用;出租;租赁； rental The rental of something such as a car or piece of equipment is the activity or process of renting it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 租金;租用费； rental The rental is the amount of money that you pay when you rent something such as a car, property, or piece of equipment.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 租用的;出租的； rental You use rental to describe things that are connected with the renting out of goods, properties, and services.
rent boy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男妓； A rent boy is a boy or young man who has sex with men for money.
rent-free: [ADJ 形容词] 免租金的;免费的； rent-free If you have a rent-free house or office, you do not have to pay anything to use it.
renunciation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 对信仰或行为方式的放弃，抛弃； renunciation The renunciation of a belief or a way of behaving is the public declaration that you reject it and have decided to stop having that belief or behaving in that way.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对声明、官衔等的)正式放弃； renunciation The renunciation of a claim, title, or privilege is the act of officially giving it up.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (因道德或宗教原因)克己，自我克制； renunciation Renunciation is the act of not allowing yourself certain pleasures for moral or religious reasons.
reopen: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使重新开业;使重新营业； reopen If you reopen a public building such as a factory, airport, or school, or if it reopens , it opens and starts working again after it has been closed for some time.  /  [VERB 动词] 重新审理；重新调查； reopen If police or the courts reopen a legal case, they investigate it again because it has never been solved or because there was something wrong in the way it was investigated before.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使谈判等重新开始;使恢复； reopen If people or countries reopen talks or negotiations or if talks or negotiations reopen , they begin again after they have stopped for some time.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 重新建立，恢复(联系或关系)； reopen If people or countries reopen ties or relations, they start being friendly again after a time when they were not friendly.
reorganize: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 改组;改造;改编;重新安排； reorganize reorganization To reorganize something or to reorganize means to change the way in which something is organized, arranged, or done.
rep: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 销售代表，销售专员[全写为 representative] ； rep See also: holiday rep ; A rep is a person whose job is to sell a company's products or services, especially by travelling round and visiting other companies.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (组织、团体的)代表，发言人； rep A rep is a person who acts as a representative for a group of people, usually a group of people who work together.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (戏剧中)同repertory； rep In the theatre, rep is the same as repertory .
repaid: + + + Repaid is the past tense and past participle of repay .
repair: [VERB 动词] 修理;修补； repair repairer If you repair something that has been damaged or is not working properly, you mend it.  /  [VERB 动词] 补救，挽救(关系或声誉)； repair If you repair a relationship or someone's reputation after it has been damaged, you do something to improve it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 修理;修补;补救； repair A repair is something that you do to mend a machine, building, piece of clothing, or other thing that has been damaged or is not working properly.  /  [VERB 动词] 到…去;前去； repair If someone repairs to a particular place, they go there.
repairman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 维修工； repairman A repairman is a man who mends broken machines such as televisions and telephones.
reparation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (战败国支付的)赔款； reparation Reparations are sums of money that are paid after a war by the defeated country for the damage and injuries it caused in other countries.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 赔偿;弥补； reparation Reparation is help or payment that someone gives you for damage, loss, or suffering that they have caused you.
repartee: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 妙语连珠的对话;机智的谈话； repartee Repartee is conversation that consists of quick, witty comments and replies.
repast: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 饭食;一餐； A repast is a meal.
repatriate: [VERB 动词] 遣返;遣送回国； repatriate repatriation If a country repatriates someone, it sends them back to their home country.  /  [VERB 动词] 把(海外利润) 调回国内； repatriate repatriation If a company repatriates profits that it has made in another country, it brings them back into its home country.
repay: [VERB 动词] 偿还，偿付(贷款或债务)； repay If you repay a loan or a debt, you pay back the money that you owe to the person who you borrowed or took it from.  /  [VERB 动词] 报答，回报恩惠等； repay If you repay a favour that someone did for you, you do something for them in return.
repayable: [ADJ 形容词] (在一定期限内)可偿还的，必须偿还的； repayable A loan that is repayable within a certain period of time must be paid back within that time.
repayment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分期偿付款； repayment Repayments are amounts of money which you pay at regular intervals to a person or organization in order to repay a debt.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 偿还;偿付； repayment The repayment of money is the act or process of paying it back to the person you owe it to.
repeal: [VERB 动词] 废止;废除;撤销； repeal If the government repeals a law, it officially ends it, so that it is no longer valid.
repeat: [VERB 动词] 重复;重写； repeat If you repeat something, you say or write it again.  /  [VERB 动词] 复述;转述； repeat If you repeat something that someone else has said or written, you say or write the same thing, or tell it to another person.  /  [VERB 动词] 反复说;说话反反复复； repeat If you repeat yourself , you say something which you have said before, usually by mistake.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 再说一次;重申一遍； repeat People sometimes say repeat before saying again a word they have just said, in order to emphasize it or to make sure that people hear it.
repeated: [ADJ 形容词] 重复的;反复发生的； repeated Repeated actions or events are ones which happen many times.
repeatedly: [ADV 副词] 重复地;反复地;再三地； repeatedly If you do something repeatedly , you do it many times.
repeat offender: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 惯犯;累犯； A repeat offender is someone who commits the same sort of crime more than once.
repeat prescription: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 依以前用过的处方重新取药的重复处方； A repeat prescription is a prescription for a medicine that you have taken before or that you use regularly.
repel: [VERB 动词] 击退;驱逐； repel When an army repels an attack, they successfully fight and drive back soldiers from another army who have attacked them.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] (磁极、电荷之间)排斥； repel When a magnetic pole repels another magnetic pole, it gives out a force that pushes the other pole away.  /  [VERB 动词] 使厌恶;使讨厌； repel repelled If something repels you, you find it horrible and disgusting.
repellent: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 讨厌的;令人厌恶的;令人排斥的； repellent If you think that something is horrible and disgusting you can say that it is repellent .  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 驱虫剂； repellent Insect repellent is a product containing chemicals that you spray into the air or on your body in order to keep insects away.
repent: [VERB 动词] 后悔;忏悔;悔悟； repent If you repent , you show or say that you are sorry for something wrong you have done.
repentance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 后悔;悔改;悔意;忏悔； repentance If you show repentance for something wrong that you have done, you make it clear that you are sorry for doing it.
repentant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 后悔的;悔改的;有悔改表现的； repentant Someone who is repentant shows or says that they are sorry for something wrong they have done.
repercussion: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (不良)反响，反应，影响； repercussion If an action or event has repercussions , it causes unpleasant things to happen some time after the original action or event.
repertoire: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一个演员所能表演的全部节目，曲目； repertoire A per-former's repertoire is all the plays or pieces of music that he or she has learned and can perform.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 全部技能或才能； repertoire The repertoire of a person or thing is all the things of a particular kind that the person or thing is capable of doing.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 某个种类的全部剧目(或曲目)； repertoire You can refer to all the plays or music of a particular kind as, for example, the classical repertoire or the jazz repertoire .
repertory: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 剧目轮演;轮流上演选定剧目； repertory A repertory company is a group of actors and actresses who perform a small number of plays for just a few weeks at a time.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 一个演员所能表演的全部剧目(或曲目)； repertory A performer's repertory is all the plays or pieces of music that he or she has learned and can perform.
repetition: [N-VAR 可变名词] (常指令人不快的事件的)反复发生，重复出现，重演； repetition If there is a repetition of an event, usually an undesirable event, it happens again.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (词语的)重复； repetition Repetition means using the same words again.
repetitious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 反复的;重复乏味的； repetitious Something that is repetitious involves actions or elements that are repeated many times and is therefore boring.

responsive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 反应敏捷的;易流露感情的;易受影响的； responsive responsiveness A responsive person is quick to react to people or events and to show emotions such as pleasure and affection.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 反应迅速的;积极响应的； responsive responsiveness If someone or something is responsive , they react quickly and favourably.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 回应的;应答的;回答的； responsive A responsive action is made as a reaction to something that has just been said or done.

rest area: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (高速公路旁的)休息区，服务区； A rest area is a place beside a motorway or freeway where you can buy petrol and other things, or have a meal.

restaurant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 餐馆;饭店；  restaurant A restaurant is a place where you can eat a meal and pay for it.

restaurateur: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 餐馆老板;饭店主人； A restaurateur is a person who owns and manages a restaurant.
rested: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 精力充沛的;精神焕发的； rested If you feel rested , you feel more energetic because you have just had a rest.
restful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 宁静的;平静的;让人放松的； restful Something that is restful helps you to feel calm and relaxed.
rest home: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 old people's home； A rest home is the same as an old people's home .

restive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不耐烦的;厌烦的;不满的； restive restiveness If you are restive , you are impatient, bored, or dissatisfied.
restless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 焦躁不安的;不耐烦的;不满的； restless restlessness If you are restless , you are bored, impatient, or dissatisfied, and you want to do something else.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坐立不安的;不安宁的； restless restlessness restlessly If someone is restless , they keep moving around because they find it difficult to keep still.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 难以入睡的;辗转反侧的； restless If you have a restless night, you do not sleep properly and when you wake up you feel tired and uncomfortable.
restock: [VERB 动词] 为商店等备办新货;给冰箱补充食物； restock If you restock something such as a shelf, fridge, or shop, you fill it with food or other goods to replace what you have used or sold.  /  [VERB 动词] 给湖补充鱼苗； restock To restock a lake means to put more fish in it because there are very few left.
Restoration: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 王政复辟指1660年英王查理二世复辟； The Restoration was the event in 1660 when Charles the Second became King of England, Scotland, and Ireland after a period when there had been no King or Queen.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 戏剧、建筑等王政复辟时期的； Restoration is used to refer to the style of drama and architecture that was popular during and just after the rule of Charles the Second in England.

restraint: [N-VAR 可变名词] 限制;制约因素;管制措施； restraint Restraints are rules or conditions that limit or restrict someone or something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 克制;抑制;遏制； restraint Restraint is calm, controlled, and unemotional behaviour.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 限制;控制； restraint Restraint of something is the act of preventing it from increasing too much or from being done freely.

restrictive practice: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某一行业的人维护自身利益的)限制竞争协议，限制竞争的行为； restrictive practice Restrictive practices are ways in which people involved in an industry, trade, or profession protect their own interests, rather than having a system which is fair to the public, employers, and other workers.
rest room: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公共卫生间;公共厕所； In a restaurant, theatre, or other public place, a rest room is a room with a toilet for customers to use.

rest stop: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旅途中在公路旁的休息，歇脚； On a long journey by road, a rest stop is a short period when you stop and leave your vehicle, for example to eat or go to the toilet.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 高速公路旁的停车区，休息站； A rest stop is a place beside a motorway or freeway where you can buy petrol and other things, or have a meal.

resume: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使重新开始;使继续进行； resume resumption If you resume an activity or if it resumes , it begins again.  /  [VERB 动词] 恢复(职位);回到座位； If you resume your seat or position, you return to the seat or position you were in before you moved.  /  [VERB 动词] 继续说;接着说； resume If someone resumes , they begin speaking again after they have stopped for a short time.

resuscitate: [VERB 动词] 使复活;使苏醒;救活； resuscitate resuscitation If you resuscitate someone who has stopped breathing, you cause them to start breathing again.  /  [VERB 动词] 使复苏;使重新兴盛； resuscitate resuscitation If you resuscitate something, you cause it to become active or successful again.
retail: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 零售;零卖； retail Retail is the activity of selling goods direct to the public, usually in small quantities.  /  [ADV 副词] 以零售方式； If something is sold retail , it is sold in ordinary shops direct to the public.  /  [VERB 动词] 以…价格零售，零卖； retail If an item in a shop retails at or for a particular price, it is on sale at that price.  /  [VERB 动词] 热情而详细地讲述;详述； retail See also: retailing ; If someone retails a story or event, they tell it to someone else, often in detail and in an exciting way.

retiree: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 退休人员;退职者； retiree A retiree is a retired person.

rookie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 新手;菜鸟;尤指新兵，新警员； rookie A rookie is someone who has just started doing a job and does not have much experience, especially someone who has just joined the army or police force.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (第一年参加体育比赛的)新队员； A rookie is a person who has been competing in a professional sport for less than a year.
room: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 房间;屋子;室;房间里的所有人； room A room is one of the separate sections or parts of the inside of a building.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 私人房间尤指卧室或办公室； room If you talk about your room , you are referring to the room that you alone use, especially your bedroom at home or your office at work.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (宾馆的)房间； room A room is a bedroom in a hotel.  /  [VERB 动词] 同住;合租； room If you room with someone, you share a rented room, apartment, or house with them, for example when you are a student.

roomful: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一屋子人或物； roomful A roomful of things or people is a room that is full of them.

roost: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (鸟类或蝙蝠的)栖息处，窝； A roost is a place where birds or bats rest or sleep.  /  [VERB 动词] 栖息； roost When birds or bats roost somewhere, they rest or sleep there.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 自食苦果;得到惩罚;遭到报应； roost If bad or wrong things that someone has done in the past have come home to roost , or if their chickens have come home to roost , they are now experiencing the unpleasant effects of these actions.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 当家;作主;主宰;领导； roost If you say that someone rules the roost in a particular place, you mean that they have control and authority over the people there.
rooster: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雄鸡;公鸡； A rooster is an adult male chicken.
root: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 根;根茎； root The roots of a plant are the parts of it that grow under the ground.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使生根成长； root If you root a plant or cutting or if it roots , roots form on the bottom of its stem and it starts to grow.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (蔬菜、作物等)块根的，根茎可食用的； root Root vegetables or root crops are grown for their roots which are large and can be eaten.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (头发或牙齿的)根，根部； root The root of a hair or tooth is the part of it that is underneath the skin.

root for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 支持;为…鼓劲； root for If you are rooting for someone, you are giving them your support while they are doing something difficult or trying to defeat another person.
root ginger: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 姜根常用于中餐和印度餐； Root ginger is the stem of the ginger plant.
rootless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 居无定所的;无固定工作的;无归属的;漂泊的； rootless rootlessness If someone has no permanent home or job and is not settled in any community, you can describe them as rootless .
root out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 铲除;清除； root out If you root out a person, you find them and force them from the place they are in, usually in order to punish them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 根除;杜绝;彻底解决； root out If you root out a problem or an unpleasant situation, you find out who or what is the cause of it and put an end to it.
rope: [N-VAR 可变名词] 粗绳;绳索;缆绳； rope A rope is a thick cord or wire that is made by twisting together several thinner cords or wires.  /  [VERB 动词] (用绳索)捆，绑，拴； rope If you rope one thing to another, you tie the two things together with a rope.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (拳击或摔跤场地的)围绳，圈绳； rope The ropes refers to the fence made of rope that surrounds a boxing ring or a wrestling ring.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 任由…自作自受;任…作茧自缚;任…出丑； rope If you give someone enough rope to hang themselves , you give them the freedom to do a job in their own way because you hope that their attempts will fail and that they will look foolish.

ropey: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 差劲的;劣质的;差强人意的； ropey If you say that something is ropey , you mean that its quality is poor or unsatisfactory.
rosary: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指天主教徒念经时用的念珠;玫瑰经； rosary A rosary is a string of beads that members of certain religions, especially Catholics, use for counting prayers.
rose: + + + Rose is the past tense of rise .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 玫瑰花;蔷薇花； rose A rose is a flower, often with a pleasant smell, which grows on a bush with stems that have sharp points called thorns on them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蔷薇;玫瑰； rose A rose is bush that roses grow on.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 玫瑰色;红粉色； rose Something that is rose is reddish-pink in colour.
rosebud: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 玫瑰花苞； A rosebud is a young rose whose petals have not yet opened out fully.

rosemary: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 迷迭香； Rosemary is a herb used in cooking.

rostrum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 演讲台;领奖台;指挥台； rostrum A rostrum is a raised platform on which someone stands when they are speaking to an audience, receiving a prize, or conducting an orchestra.
rosy: [ADJ 形容词] (脸颊)红润的，红扑扑的； rosy If you say that someone has a rosy face, you mean that they have pink cheeks and look very healthy.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 红粉色的;玫瑰色的； rosy Something that is rosy is reddish-pink in colour.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 充满希望的;前景美好的;有望成功的； rosy If you say that a situation looks rosy or that the picture looks rosy , you mean that the situation seems likely to be good or successful.

rota: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 值班表;值勤表;勤务薄； rota A rota is a list which gives details of the order in which different people have to do a particular job.

rot away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 彻底腐烂;完全腐败； When something rots away , it decays until it falls to pieces or none of it remains.
rote: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 死记硬背； rote Rote learning or learning by rote is learning things by repeating them without thinking about them or trying to understand them.
rotor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (直升机的)旋翼； The rotors or rotor blades of a helicopter are the four long, flat, thin pieces of metal on top of it which go round and lift it off the ground.
rotten: [ADJ 形容词] 腐烂的;腐臭的;腐朽的； rotten If food, wood, or another substance is rotten , it has decayed and can no longer be used.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (事物)非常糟糕的，很差劲的，极其拙劣的； rotten If you describe something as rotten , you think it is very unpleasant or of very poor quality.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人极讨厌的，坏透了的，非常不友善的； rotten If you describe someone as rotten , you are insulting them or criticizing them because you think that they are very unpleasant or unkind.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 感到不适的;感到抱歉的;难受的； rotten If you feel rotten , you feel bad, either because you are ill or because you are sorry about something.
rotten apple: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 害群之马； rotten apple You can use rotten apple to talk about a person who is dishonest and therefore causes a lot of problems for the group or organization they belong to.

rotund: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 胖乎乎的;圆胖的;肥胖的； rotund If someone is rotund , they are round and fat.
rotunda: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指带球形圆屋顶的圆形建筑，圆形房间； rotunda A rotunda is a round building or room, especially one with a round bowl-shaped roof.

rouge: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 胭脂;腮红； Rouge is a red powder or cream which women and actors can put on their cheeks in order to give them more colour.  /  [VERB 动词] 涂胭脂;抹腮红;涂口红； rouge If a woman or an actor rouges their cheeks or lips, they put red powder or cream on them to give them more colour.

ruffle: [VERB 动词] 为表示喜爱抚弄(他人头发)； If you ruffle someone's hair, you move your hand backwards and forwards through it as a way of showing your affection towards them.  /  [VERB 动词] 吹皱;使泛起涟漪;使起伏不平； ruffle When the wind ruffles something such as the surface of the sea, it causes it to move gently in a wave-like motion.  /  [VERB 动词] 使惊慌;使失去信心;激怒;使沮丧； ruffle If something ruffles someone, it causes them to panic and lose their confidence or to become angry or upset.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] (鸟类)竖起(羽毛)； ruffle If a bird ruffles its feathers or if its feathers ruffle , they stand out on its body, for example when it is cleaning itself or when it is frightened.

rug: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小地毯;垫子； rug A rug is a piece of thick material that you put on a floor.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (盖肩膀或膝盖以保暖的)围毯，小毯子； rug A rug is a small blanket which you use to cover your shoulders or your knees to keep them warm.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不再支持;停止帮助； rug If someone pulls the rug from under a person or thing or pulls the rug from under someone's feet , they stop giving their help or support.

rugged: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 崎岖不平的;高低起伏的;多岩石的； rugged ruggedly ruggedness A rugged area of land is uneven and covered with rocks, with few trees or plants.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 男子强壮的，健壮的，粗犷的； rugged ruggedly If you describe a man as rugged , you mean that he has strong, masculine features.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坚强的;坚毅的;吃苦耐劳的； If you describe someone's character as rugged , you mean that they are strong and determined, and have the ability to cope with difficult situations.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坚固耐用的;结实的； rugged ruggedness A rugged piece of equipment is strong and is designed to last a long time, even if it is treated roughly.
rugger: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同rugby； rugger Rugger is the same as rugby .

rule: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 规则;规定;章程;条例； rule Rules are instructions that tell you what you are allowed to do and what you are not allowed to do.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 行事准则;指导方针;应做的事； rule A rule is a statement telling people what they should do in order to achieve success or a benefit of some kind.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 语言或科学中的规律，法则； rule The rules of something such as a language or a science are statements that describe the way that things usually happen in a particular situation.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 普遍情况;常规;惯例； rule If something is the rule , it is the normal state of affairs.

rum: [N-MASS 物质名词] 朗姆酒； rum 一杯朗姆酒 Rum is an alcoholic drink made from sugar.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 古怪的;奇怪的;奇特的； rum If you describe people or things as rum , you mean that they are rather strange.
rumba: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 伦巴舞； The rumba is a popular dance that comes from Cuba, or the music that the dance is performed to.
rumble: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 低沉而持续的声音;隆隆声;轰隆声； rumble A rumble is a low continuous noise.  /  [VERB 动词] 发着轰隆声缓慢移动； rumble If a vehicle rumbles somewhere, it moves slowly forward while making a low continuous noise.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 低沉的声音； rumble If you refer to the rumble of someone's voice, you mean their voice sounds very low, making it hard to hear exactly what they are saying.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出隆隆声;发出持续而低沉的声音； rumble If something rumbles , it makes a low, continuous noise.
rumble on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (争吵等)长久地继续； rumble on If you say that something such as an argument rumbles on , you mean that it continues for a long time after it should have been settled.
rumbling: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 持续而低沉的声音;隆隆声;辘辘声;咕噜声； rumbling A rumbling is a low continuous noise.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 情况恶化的迹象，传闻;怨言； rumbling Rumblings are signs that a bad situation is developing or that people are becoming annoyed or unhappy.
rumbustious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 欢闹的;闹腾的； rumbustious A rumbustious person is energetic in a cheerful, noisy way.
ruminate: [VERB 动词] 沉思;琢磨;认真考虑； ruminate If you ruminate on something, you think about it very carefully.  /  [VERB 动词] 动物反刍； When animals ruminate , they bring food back from their stomach into their mouth and chew it again.
rumination: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沉思;认真的考虑； rumination Your ruminations are your careful thoughts about something.
ruminative: [ADJ 形容词] 沉思的;反复思考的;认真考虑的;冥思苦想的； ruminative ruminatively If you are ruminative , you are thinking very deeply and carefully about something.
rummage: [VERB 动词] 搜寻;翻找;乱翻； rummage rummage about 和 rummage around 同 rummage If you rummage through something, you search for something you want by moving things around in a careless or hurried way.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 捐赠品;捐赠物； rummage Rummage is old or unwanted things that people give away to charities.
rummage sale: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旧杂物义卖； A rummage sale is a sale of cheap used goods that is usually held to raise money for charity.
rummy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 拉米纸牌游戏； Rummy is a card game in which players try to collect cards of the same value or cards in a sequence in the same suit.
rumour: [N-VAR 可变名词] 谣言;流言;传闻； rumour A rumour is a story or piece of information that may or may not be true, but that people are talking about.

rump: [N-SING 单数名词] 残余分子;残存力量； rump The rump of a group, organization, or country consists of the members who remain in it after the rest have left.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 动物的尾部，臀部； rump An animal's rump is its rear end.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 臀肉牛排； Rump or rump steak is meat cut from the rear end of a cow.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人的屁股，臀部； rump A person's rump is his or her bottom.
rumple: [VERB 动词] (因喜爱而)弄乱，抚弄(某人的头发)； rumple If you rumple someone's hair, you move your hand backwards and forwards through it as your way of showing affection to them.
rumpled: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 弄皱的;凌乱的； rumpled Rumpled means creased or untidy.
rumpus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 喧闹;吵闹;争论； rumpus If someone or something causes a rumpus , they cause a lot of noise or argument.

runabout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻便汽车;小汽车； runabout A runabout is a small car used mainly for short journeys.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小汽艇;小型摩托艇； A runabout is a small, light boat with a motor.
run across: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 偶然碰见;和…不期而遇； If you run across someone or something, you meet them or find them unexpectedly.
run after: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (因为爱慕而)追求； If you are running after someone, you are trying to start a relationship with them, usually a sexual relationship.
run along: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (让小孩)离开，走开； If you tell a child to run along , you mean that you want them to go away.
run around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 东奔西跑;四处奔忙； If you run around , you go to a lot of places and do a lot of things, often in a rushed or disorganized way.

runaway: [ADJ 形容词] 迅速的;无法控制的;失控的； runaway You use runaway to describe a situation in which something increases or develops very quickly and cannot be controlled.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 离家出走者(尤指小孩)； runaway A runaway is someone, especially a child, who leaves home without telling anyone or without permission.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (车辆、动物等)失控的； runaway A runaway vehicle or animal is moving forward quickly, and its driver or rider has lost control of it.
run away with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (想象、情绪等)失去控制，按捺不住； run away with If you let your imagination or your emotions run away with you, you fail to control them and cannot think sensibly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻松取胜;轻易赢得； If someone runs away with a competition, race, or prize, they win it easily.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻率接受(某种错误想法)； run away with If you run away with a particular idea, you accept it without thinking about it carefully, even though it is wrong.
run by: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (为征求意见) 把某事告诉某人； If you run something by someone, you tell them about it or mention it, to see if they think it is a good idea, or can understand it.
run-down: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 疲惫不堪的;累病的;衰弱的； run-down If someone is run-down , they are tired or slightly ill.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (建筑物、地区等)破旧不堪的，破败的，失修的； run-down A run-down building or area is in very poor condition.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 萧条的;不景气的； run-down A run-down place of business is not as active as it used to be or does not have many customers.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 行业、组织等规模的缩减，紧缩； When the run-down of an industry or organization takes place, its size or the amount of work that it does is reduced.
run down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 严厉批评;斥责;贬低； If you run people or things down , you criticize them strongly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 压缩;削减;减少； run down If people run down an industry or an organization, they deliberately reduce its size or the amount of work that it does.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 减少;降低； run down If someone runs down an amount of something, they reduce it or allow it to decrease.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 车辆把…撞伤，撞倒； If a vehicle or its driver runs someone down , the vehicle hits them and injures them.

rung: + + + Rung is the past participle of ring .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梯级;横档； rung The rungs on a ladder are the wooden or metal bars that form the steps.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (事业、组织、进程中的)级别，等级，地位； rung If you reach a particular rung in your career, in an organization, or in a process, you reach that level in it.

runner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 跑步者;赛跑者； runner A runner is a person who runs, especially for sport or pleasure.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 参加赛马的马匹;赛马； runner The runners in a horse race are the horses taking part.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 走私者;偷运者； A drug runner or gun runner is someone who illegally takes drugs or guns into a country.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 送信人;信使;收账员;听差； runner Someone who is a runner for a particular person or company is employed to take messages, collect money, or do other small tasks for them.

run-off: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (得分相同时的)加赛，决胜赛;(得票相同时的)决胜投票，决胜选举； run-off A run-off is an extra vote or contest which is held in order to decide the winner of an election or competition, because no-one has yet clearly won.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 径流，溢流指流入河流中的雨水； Run-off is rainwater that forms a stream rather than being absorbed by the ground.
run-of-the-mill: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 普通的;一般的;平凡的;不突出的； run-of-the-mill A run-of-the-mill person or thing is very ordinary, with no special or interesting features.
run out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 用完;耗尽； run out If you run out of something, you have no more of it left.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 被用完;耗尽； If something runs out , it becomes used up so that there is no more left.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (法律文件)到期，失效； When a legal document runs out , it stops being valid.
run out on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 抛弃;离弃;背弃;遗弃； run out on If someone runs out on you, they go away and abandon you, leaving you with problems.
run over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (车辆)撞倒，碾过，轧过； run over If a vehicle or its driver runs a person or animal over , it knocks them down or drives over them.
run past: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 同 run by； To run something past someone means the same as to run it by them.
runt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一胎中最弱小的仔畜； runt The runt of a group of animals born to the same mother at the same time is the smallest and weakest of them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 表厌恶或不满矮子； runt You call a small person a runt when you are annoyed with them and are expressing your dislike for them.
run through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 匆匆浏览;匆匆阅读;匆匆提及； If you run through a list of items, you read or mention all the items quickly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 排练;排演;练习； If you run through a performance or a series of actions, you practise it.  /  See also: run-through ; �
run-through: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 排练;排演;练习； run-through A run-through for a show or event is a practice for it.
run time: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (程序的)运行时间，操作时间； Run time is the time during which a computer program is running.
run to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 求助;询问； run to If you run to someone, you go to them for help or to tell them something.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 达到(一定数量或规模)； If something runs to a particular amount or size, it is that amount or size.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 支付得起;有钱购买； run to If you cannot run to a particular item, you cannot afford to buy it or pay for it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 喜欢;偏爱;偏好； run to If your tastes or interests run to a particular type of thing, that is the type of thing you like.
run up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 积欠(账款、债务等)； If someone runs up bills or debts, they acquire them by buying a lot of things or borrowing money.  /  See also: run-up ; �
run-up: [N-SING 单数名词] 前奏;预备期； run-up The run-up to an event is the period of time just before it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (投掷、跳高、跳远等之前的)助跑； run-up In sport, a run-up is the run made by a player or athlete, for example before throwing a ball or a javelin, or before jumping.
run up against: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 突然遇到(问题);突然碰到(困难)； If you run up against problems, you suddenly begin to experience them.
runway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (飞机场的)跑道； runway At an airport, the runway is the long strip of ground with a hard surface which an aeroplane takes off from or lands on.
rupee: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 卢比印度、巴基斯坦等国的货币单位； rupee A rupee is a unit of money that is used in India, Pakistan, and some other countries.
rupture: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (体内组织的)破裂;(尤指)脱肠，疝气； A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, especially the part between the bowels and the abdomen.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(体内组织)破裂，爆裂； rupture If a person or animal ruptures a part of their body or if it ruptures , it tears or bursts open.  /  [VERB 动词] 使器官破裂;形成疝;患脱肠； rupture If you rupture yourself , you rupture a part of your body, usually because you have lifted something heavy.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使破裂;使爆裂； rupture If an object ruptures or if something ruptures it, it bursts open.
rural: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 乡下的;乡村的;农村的； rural Rural places are far away from large towns or cities.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有乡村特色的;田园的;有乡土气息的； rural Rural means having features which are typical of areas that are far away from large towns or cities.
ruse: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 诡计;计谋;计策； ruse A ruse is an action or plan which is intended to deceive someone.
rush: [VERB 动词] 猛冲;快速行进； rush If you rush somewhere, you go there quickly.  /  [VERB 动词] 赶忙做;赶紧做； rush If people rush to do something, they do it as soon as they can, because they are very eager to do it.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 仓促;匆忙;急忙； rush A rush is a situation in which you need to go somewhere or do something very quickly.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 热潮;争做;争先恐后； rush If there is a rush for something, many people suddenly try to get it or do it.
rush hour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (上下班的)交通高峰时间，交通拥挤时段； rush hour The rush hour is one of the periods of the day when most people are travelling to or from work.
rush out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 赶制[产品]; 赶印文件； If a document or product is rushed out , it is produced very quickly.
rush through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 加急处理;匆忙处理； If you rush something through , you deal with it quickly so that it is ready in a shorter time than usual.
rusk: [N-VAR 可变名词] (婴幼儿食用的)甜面包干，脆饼干； Rusks are hard, dry biscuits that are given to babies and young children.
russet: [COLOUR 颜色词] 赤褐色的;红褐色的； russet Russet is used to describe things that are reddish-brown in colour.
Russian: [ADJ 形容词] 俄罗斯的;俄罗斯人的;俄语的;俄罗斯文化的； Russian Russian means belonging or relating to Russia, or to its people, language, or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 俄罗斯人； Russian A Russian is a Russian citizen, or a person of Russian origin.
Russian doll: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 俄罗斯套娃； A Russian doll is a hollow wooden doll that is made in two halves.
Russian roulette: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 玩命的行为； Russian roulette If you say that someone is playing Russian roulette , or that what they are doing is like playing Russian roulette , you mean that what they are doing is very dangerous because it involves unpredictable risks.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 俄罗斯轮盘赌； If someone plays Russian roulette , they fire a gun with only one bullet at their head without knowing whether it will shoot them.
rust: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 锈;铁锈； rust Rust is a brown substance that forms on iron or steel, for example when it comes into contact with water.  /  [VERB 动词] 生锈； rust When a metal object rusts , it becomes covered in rust and often loses its strength.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 铁锈色;赭色;深褐色； rust Rust is sometimes used to describe things that are reddish-brown in colour.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (植物的)锈病，锈菌； Rust is a disease which affects plants.
rust away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 锈蚀;锈坏;锈烂； When a metal object rusts away , it is gradually weakened and destroyed by rust.
Rust Belt: [N-SING 单数名词] 衰退地区，铁锈地带指美国等已陷入经济困境的老工业区； In the United States and some other countries, the Rust Belt is a region which used to have a lot of manufacturing industry, but whose economy is now in difficulty.
rustic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 乡村的;质朴的;有乡村风味的； rustic You can use rustic to describe things or people that you approve of because they are simple or unsophisticated in a way that is typical of the countryside.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乡下人;乡巴佬； rustic You can refer to someone who comes from the countryside as a rustic if you find their behaviour amusing or very different from that of people who live in towns and cities.
rusticity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 田园生活； rusticity You can refer to the simple, peaceful character of life in the countryside as rusticity .
rustle: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使发出沙沙声;使沙沙作响； rustle rustling When something thin and dry rustles or when you rustle it, it makes soft sounds as it moves.  /  See also: rustling ;  /  相关词组： rustle up �
rustler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 偷牲口的贼(尤指偷牛、马和羊的人)； rustler Rustlers are people who steal farm animals, especially cattle, horses, and sheep.
rustle up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 很快弄到，匆匆准备好(食物或饮料)； rustle up If you rustle up something to eat or drink, you make or prepare it quickly, with very little planning.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 很快弄到； rustle up If you rustle something up , you provide or obtain it quickly, with very little planning.
rustling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 偷牲口(尤指偷牛)； rustling Rustling is the activity of stealing farm animals, especially cattle.  /  See also: rustle ; �
rusty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 生锈的； rusty A rusty metal object such as a car or a machine is covered with rust, which is a brown substance that forms on iron or steel when it comes into contact with water.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (技术、知识等)荒废的，生疏的； rusty If a skill that you have or your knowledge of something is rusty , it is not as good as it used to be, because you have not used it for a long time.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 铁锈色的;赭色的;深褐色的； rusty Rusty is sometimes used to describe things that are reddish-brown in colour.
rut: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人、生活或工作刻板乏味，一成不变，老一套； rut If you say that someone is in a rut , you disapprove of the fact that they have become fixed in their way of thinking and doing things, and find it difficult to change.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 车辙； rut A rut is a deep, narrow mark made in the ground by the wheels of a vehicle.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (动物的)发情期； rut The rut is the period of the year when some animals such as deer are sexually active, and the males fight each other to mate with the females.  /  See also: rutted ; rutting ; �
rutabaga: [N-VAR 可变名词] 芜菁甘蓝； A rutabaga is a round yellow root vegetable with a brown or purple skin.

rutted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (道路)有车辙的； rutted A rutted road or track is very uneven because it has long, deep, narrow marks in it made by the wheels of vehicles.  /  See also: rut ; �
rutting: [ADJ 形容词] (雄性动物)发情的； rutting Rutting male animals such as deer are in a period of sexual excitement and activity.  /  See also: rut ; �
RV: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旅行房车;娱乐休闲车； RV An RV is a van which is equipped with such things as beds and cooking equipment, so that people can live in it, usually while they are on holiday.
rye: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 黑麦;裸麦； rye Rye is a cereal grown in cold countries.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 黑麦面包;裸麦面包； rye Rye is bread made from rye.

sabbatical: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (大学教师等的)休假,公休假； sabbatical A sabbatical is a period of time during which someone such as a university teacher can leave their ordinary work and travel or study.
sable: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 黑貂;紫貂； 貂皮;貂毛 sable A sable is a small furry animal with valued fur.
sabotage: [VERB 动词] 蓄意破坏，阴谋摧毁(机器、铁路、桥梁)； sabotage If a machine, railway line, or bridge is sabotaged , it is deliberately damaged or destroyed, for example in a war or as a protest.  /  [VERB 动词] 阻挠,妨碍,暗中破坏(计划的实施或会议的进行)； sabotage If someone sabotages a plan or a meeting, they deliberately prevent it from being successful.
saboteur: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蓄意破坏者;从事破坏活动者;(英国)阻挠捕猎活动者； saboteur A saboteur is a person who deliberately damages or destroys things such as machines, railway lines, and bridges in order to weaken an enemy or to make a protest.
sabre: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (旧时骑兵用的)军刀，马刀，弯刀； A sabre is a heavy sword with a curved blade that was used in the past by soldiers on horseback.
sabre-rattling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 威吓;(尤指)武力恫吓，武力威胁； sabre-rattling If you describe a threat, especially a threat of military action, as sabre-rattling , you do not believe that the threat will actually be carried out.
sac: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (动物体内的)囊，液囊，气囊； sac A sac is a small part of an animal's body, shaped like a little bag.
saccharin: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指减肥时代替食糖使用的)糖精； Saccharin is a very sweet chemical substance that some people use instead of sugar, especially when they are trying to lose weight.
saccharine: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 甜得发腻的;过于感伤的;故作多情的； saccharine You describe something as saccharine when you find it unpleasantly sweet and sentimental.
sachet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (密封的塑料或纸质的)小袋； sachet A sachet is a small closed plastic or paper bag, containing a small quantity of something.
sack: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 麻布袋;粗布袋;厚纸袋;大口袋； sack A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material.  /  [VERB 动词] 解雇;开除;炒鱿鱼； sack If your employers sack you, they tell you that you can no longer work for them because you have done something that they did not like or because your work was not good enough.  /  [VERB 动词] 抢劫，洗劫，破坏(城镇或城市)； sack When an army sacks a town or city, they destroy it, taking away all valuable things.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 床； Some people refer to bed as the sack .
sackcloth: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麻袋布;粗麻布； sackcloth Sackcloth is rough woven material that is used to make sacks.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 忏悔;痛悔； sackcloth If you talk about sackcloth or sackcloth and ashes you are referring to an exaggerated attempt by someone to show that they are sorry for doing something wrong.
sackful: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一满袋;一整包； sackful A sackful is the amount of something that a sack contains or could contain.
sacking: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麻袋布;粗麻布； Sacking is rough woven material that is used to make sacks.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 解雇;开除;炒鱿鱼； sacking A sacking is when an employer tells a worker to leave their job.
sacrament: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (基督教)圣事，圣礼； sacrament A sacrament is a Christian religious ceremony such as communion, baptism, or marriage.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (天主教)圣餐面包;(英国国教会)圣饼和葡萄酒； In the Roman Catholic church, the Sacrament is the holy bread eaten at the Eucharist.
sacramental: [ADJ 形容词] 圣事的;圣礼的； sacramental Something that is sacramental is connected with a Christian religious ceremony.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 神圣的;宗教的； sacramental Sacramental is used to describe something that is considered holy or religious.
sacred: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 神圣的;上帝的;神的； sacred sacredness Something that is sacred is believed to be holy and to have a special connection with God.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 宗教的;用于宗教仪式的； sacred Something connected with religion or used in religious ceremonies is described as sacred .  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不可侵犯的;不容干涉的;不可变更的； sacred sacredness You can describe something as sacred when it is regarded as too important to be changed or interfered with.
sacred cow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不容批评(或怀疑)的信念(或习俗、制度);不容冒犯的事物； sacred cow If you describe a belief, custom, or institution as a sacred cow , you disapprove of people treating it with too much respect and being afraid to criticize or question it.
sacrifice: [VERB 动词] 牺牲;舍弃;献出； sacrifice See also: self-sacrifice ; If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.  /  [VERB 动词] 献祭;以…为祭品； sacrifice To sacrifice an animal or person means to kill them in a special religious ceremony as an offering to a god.
sacrificial: [ADJ 形容词] 献祭的;用于献祭的； sacrificial Sacrificial means connected with or used in a sacrifice.

sacrilege: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对圣地或圣物的)亵渎,渎圣； sacrilege Sacrilege is behaviour that shows great disrespect for a holy place or object.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对名人或普遍信仰的)大不敬,冒犯,无礼； sacrilege You can use sacrilege to refer to disrespect that is shown for someone who is widely admired or for a belief that is widely accepted.
sacrilegious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 亵渎神圣的;大不敬的;无礼的； sacrilegious If someone's behaviour or actions are sacrilegious , they show great disrespect towards something holy or towards something that people think should be respected.
sacristy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (教堂的)圣器收藏室，圣职人员更衣室，祭衣间； A sacristy is the room in a church where the priest or minister changes into their official clothes and where holy objects are kept.
sacrosanct: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 神圣不可侵犯的;不容指责的;不可变更的； sacrosanct If you describe something as sacrosanct , you consider it to be special and are unwilling to see it criticized or changed.
SAD: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] SAD is an abbreviation for (缩略=) seasonal affective disorder .
