Scottish: [ADJ 形容词] 苏格兰的;苏格兰人的;苏格兰语的； Scottish Something that is Scottish belongs or relates to Scotland, its people, or its language.
scoundrel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 恶棍;流氓;无赖； scoundrel If you refer to a man as a scoundrel , you mean that he behaves very badly towards other people, especially by cheating them or deceiving them.
scour: [VERB 动词] 四处搜索;细查； scour If you scour something such as a place or a book, you make a thorough search of it to try to find what you are looking for.  /  [VERB 动词] 擦净;擦亮； scour If you scour something such as a sink, floor, or pan, you clean its surface by rubbing it hard with something rough.
scourge: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灾难;祸害； scourge A scourge is something that causes a lot of trouble or suffering to a group of people.  /  [VERB 动词] 使痛苦;危害;折磨； scourge If something scourges a place or group of people, it causes great pain and suffering to people.
Scout: [N-PROPER-COLL 专有集合名词] 童子军； The Scouts is an organization for children and young people which teaches them to be practical, sensible, and helpful.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 童子军队员； Scout A Scout is a member of the Scouts.
scout around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 四处寻觅； If you scout around or scout round for something, you go to different places looking for it.
scoutmaster: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 童子军团长;童子军小队长； A scoutmaster is a man who is in charge of a troop of Scouts.
scout out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (经过寻找)发现，觅得； scout out If you scout something out , you succeed in finding it after you have been through an area searching for it.
scowl: [VERB 动词] 作怒容;沉下脸;绷着脸； scowl When someone scowls , an angry or hostile expression appears on their face.
scrabble: [VERB 动词] 乱扒;乱摸;(尤指在看不见时)摸索着寻找； scrabble scrabble around 或 scrabble about 同 scrabble If you scrabble for something, especially something that you cannot see, you move your hands or your feet about quickly and hurriedly in order to find it.  /  [VERB 动词] 急于;苦求； scrabble scrabble around 同 scrabble If you say that someone is scrabbling to do something, you mean that they are having difficulty because they are in too much of a hurry, or because the task is almost impossible.
scraggly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (头发、植物)参差不齐的，稀疏的； scraggly Scraggly hair or plants are thin and untidy.
scraggy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 骨瘦如柴的;皮包骨头的； scraggy If you describe a person or animal as scraggy , you mean that they look unattractive because they are so thin.
scramble: [VERB 动词] (迅速地)爬,攀登； scramble If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you.  /  [VERB 动词] 仓促行动;慌忙前往； scramble If you scramble to a different place or position, you move there in a hurried, awkward way.  /  [VERB 动词] 争夺;抢夺； scramble If a number of people scramble for something, they compete energetically with each other for it.  /  [VERB 动词] 炒蛋； scramble scrambled If you scramble eggs, you break them, mix them together and then heat and stir the mixture in a pan.
scrambler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 扰频器;倒频器； A scrambler is an electronic device which alters the sound of a radio or telephone message so that it can only be understood by someone who has special equipment.
scrap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 碎片;小块;一丁点儿； scrap A scrap of something is a very small piece or amount of it.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 残羹剩饭;吃剩的东西； scrap Scraps are pieces of unwanted food which are thrown away or given to animals.  /  [VERB 动词] 除掉;取消;废弃； scrap If you scrap something, you get rid of it or cancel it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (金属、纸张)废弃的,报废的； scrap Scrap metal or paper is no longer wanted for its original purpose, but may have some other use.
scrapbook: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 剪贴簿;剪报资料收贴簿； A scrapbook is a book with empty pages on which you can stick things such as pictures or newspaper articles in order to keep them.
scrape: [VERB 动词] (尤指用锋利物)刮落,削掉，擦掉； scrape If you scrape something from a surface, you remove it, especially by pulling a sharp object over the surface.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 摩擦使发出刺耳声;擦伤;蹭破； scrape scraping If something scrapes against something else or if someone or something scrapes something else, it rubs against it, making a noise or causing slight damage.  /  [VERB 动词] 擦伤，刮破(身体部位)； If you scrape a part of your body, you accidentally rub it against something hard and rough, and damage it slightly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (自己导致的)窘境，困境； scrape If you are in a scrape , you are in a difficult situation which you have caused yourself.
scrape by: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 勉强生活;勉强糊口； If someone scrapes by , they earn just enough money to live on with difficulty.
scraper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 刮刀;刮板;刮削器； A scraper is a tool that has a small handle and a metal or plastic blade and can be used for scraping a particular surface clean.
scrape through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 勉强通过(考试);(在竞争、选举中)勉强获胜； scrape through If you scrape through an examination, you just succeed in passing it.
scrape together: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (艰难地)凑齐，筹集； scrape together If you scrape together an amount of money or a number of things, you succeed in obtaining it with difficulty.
scrapheap: [N-SING 单数名词] 遭解雇;失业； scrapheap If you say that someone has been thrown on the scrapheap , you mean that they have been forced to leave their job by an uncaring employer and are unlikely to get other work.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 废物堆； If things such as machines or weapons are thrown on the scrapheap , they are thrown away because they are no longer needed.
scrapings: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 刮屑;削片； scrapings Scrapings are small amounts or pieces that have been scraped off something.
scrappy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 计划不周的;不连贯的;散乱的； scrappy If you describe something as scrappy , you disapprove of it because it seems to be badly planned or untidy.
scrapyard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (废汽车、船只等的)废料场，废品场； A scrapyard is a place where old machines such as cars or ships are destroyed and where useful parts are saved.
scratch: [VERB 动词] 给…搔痒;给…挠痒； scratch If you scratch yourself , you rub your fingernails against your skin because it is itching.  /  [VERB 动词] 划伤;划出痕迹； scratch If a sharp object scratches someone or something, it makes small shallow cuts on their skin or surface.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 划痕;擦痕； scratch Scratches on someone or something are small shallow cuts.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 从零开始;从头做起;白手起家； scratch If you do something from scratch , you do it without making use of anything that has been done before.
scratch card: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 刮刮卡;刮奖卡； A scratch card is a card with hidden words or symbols on it.
scratch file: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 临时文件； A scratch file is a temporary computer file which you use as a work area or as a store while a program is operating.
scratch pad: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 便笺式存储器;暂存器； A scratch pad is a temporary storage memory in a computer.
scratchy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沙哑的;发出沙沙声的； scratchy Scratchy sounds are thin and harsh.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服、织物)粗糙扎人的，使人发痒的； scratchy Scratchy clothes or fabrics are rough and uncomfortable to wear next to your skin.
scrawl: [VERB 动词] 潦草地写;马马虎虎地写； scrawl If you scrawl something, you write it in a careless and untidy way.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 潦草的笔迹;不工整的字迹； scrawl You can refer to writing that looks careless and untidy as a scrawl .
scrawny: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 骨瘦如柴的;皮包骨头的； scrawny If you describe a person or animal as scrawny , you mean that they look unattractive because they are so thin.
scream: [VERB 动词] (因痛苦、恐惧等)尖叫，惊呼； scream When someone screams , they make a very loud, high-pitched cry, for example because they are in pain or are very frightened.  /  [VERB 动词] 尖叫着说;高声喊出； scream If you scream something, you shout it in a loud, high-pitched voice.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出尖锐刺耳的声音； scream When something makes a loud, high-pitched noise, you can say that it screams .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 极其滑稽可笑的人； If you say that someone is a scream , you think they are very funny.
screamingly: [ADV 副词] 极其； screamingly If you say that something is, for example, screamingly funny or screamingly boring, you mean that it is extremely funny or extremely boring.
scree: [N-VAR 可变名词] 山麓碎石;岩屑堆； scree Scree is a mass of loose stones on the side of a mountain.
screech: [VERB 动词] (车辆、汽车轮胎)发出刺耳声； screech If a vehicle screeches somewhere or if its tyres screech , its tyres make an unpleasant high-pitched noise on the road.  /  [VERB 动词] 尖声喊出； screech When you screech something, you shout it in a loud, unpleasant, high-pitched voice.  /  [VERB 动词] (鸟、动物等)尖叫，尖鸣，发出刺耳声； screech When a bird, animal, or thing screeches , it makes a loud, unpleasant, high-pitched noise.
screen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (电视、电脑的)屏幕;(电影的)银幕； See also: big screen ; small screen ; widescreen ; A screen is a flat vertical surface on which pictures or words are shown.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (总称)电影，电视； screen You can refer to film or television as the screen .  /  [VERB 动词] 放映(电影);播放(电视节目)； screen screening When a film or a television programme is screened , it is shown in the cinema or broadcast on television.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 屏风;隔板； screen A screen is a vertical panel which can be moved around.
screen door: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (防止昆虫进入的)纱门； A screen door is a door made of fine netting which is on the outside of the main door of a house.
screen name: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 网名； screen name Someone's screen name is a name that they use when communicating with other people on the Internet.
screen off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (用屏风等)隔开； If part of a room or area is screened off , it is made into a separate area, using a screen.
screen out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 驱逐，剔除(可能会惹麻烦的人)； If an organization or country screens out certain people, it keeps them out because it thinks they may cause problems.
screenplay: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电影剧本； A screenplay is the words to be spoken in a film, and instructions about what will be seen in it.
screensaver: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 屏幕保护程序； A screensaver is a picture which appears or is put on a computer screen when the computer is not used for a while.
screen test: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (挑选电影演员的)试镜； When a film studio gives an actor a screen test , they film a short scene in order to test how good he or she would be in films.
screenwriter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电影剧本作家；编剧； A screenwriter is a person who writes screenplays.
screenwriting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 电影剧本创作； Screenwriting is the process of writing screenplays.
screw: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 螺丝钉； screw A screw is a metal object similar to a nail, with a raised spiral line around it.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 用螺钉固定； screw If you screw something somewhere or if it screws somewhere, you fix it in place by means of a screw or screws.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (盖子、配件)带螺旋的； screw A screw lid or fitting is one that has a raised spiral line on the inside or outside of it, so that it can be fixed in place by twisting.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 旋紧;拧紧； screw If you screw something somewhere or if it screws somewhere, you fix it in place by twisting it round and round.
screwball: [ADJ 形容词] (喜剧)荒唐可笑的，怪诞的； screwball Screwball comedy is silly and eccentric in an amusing and harmless way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 怪人;疯子； If you say that someone is a screwball , you mean that they do strange or crazy things.
screwdriver: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 螺丝刀;螺丝起子； A screwdriver is a tool that is used for turning screws.
screwed up: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 困惑的;担忧的;神经质的； screwed up If you say that someone is screwed up , you mean that they are very confused or worried, or that they have psychological problems.
screw-top: [ADJ 形容词] (瓶子、罐子)带螺旋盖的； A screw-top bottle or jar has a lid that is secured by being twisted on.
screw up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 眯起(眼睛);扭曲(面部)； If you screw up your eyes or your face, you tighten your eye or face muscles, for example because you are in pain or because the light is too bright.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把纸揉成一团； If you screw up a piece of paper, you squeeze it tightly so that it becomes very creased and no longer flat, usually when you are throwing it away.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 弄糟;搞乱;毁坏； To screw something up , or to screw up , means to cause something to fail or be spoiled.
scribble: [VERB 动词] 潦草地写;匆匆地写； scribble If you scribble something, you write it quickly and roughly.  /  [VERB 动词] 乱涂;乱画； scribble To scribble means to make meaningless marks or rough drawings using a pencil or pen.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 潦草的字迹;涂鸦； scribble Scribble is something that has been written or drawn quickly and roughly.  /  相关词组： scribble down �
scribble down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 草草写下;匆匆记下； scribble down If you scribble down something, you write it quickly or roughly.
scribbler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蹩脚文人;三流作家； scribbler People sometimes refer to writers as scribblers when they think they are not very good writers.
scribe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (印刷术发明前的)抄写员； In the days before printing was common, a scribe was a person who wrote copies of things such as letters or documents.
scrimp: [VERB 动词] 节省;精打细算;省吃俭用； scrimp If you scrimp on things, you live cheaply and spend as little money as possible.
scrip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 股份证明;股票凭证； scrip A scrip is a certificate which shows that an investor owns part of a share or stock.
script: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (戏剧、电影)剧本;(电视节目)广播稿； script The script of a play, film, or television programme is the written version of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 为(电影等)写剧本;为(广播、电视节目)撰稿； script The person who scripts a film or a radio or television play writes it.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (一种语言的)书写系统，字母表； script You can refer to a particular system of writing as a particular script .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 期待;计划； script If you say that something which has happened is not in the script , or that someone has not followed the script , you mean that something has happened which was not expected or intended to happen.
scripted: [ADJ 形容词] (讲话)照稿子念的，照本宣科的； scripted A scripted speech has been written in advance, although the speaker may pretend that it is spoken without preparation.
scriptural: [ADJ 形容词] 《圣经》中的;源自《圣经》的;根据《圣经》的； scriptural Scriptural is used to describe things that are written in or based on the Christian Bible.
scripture: [N-VAR 可变名词] (宗教的)经典，经文，圣典； scripture Scripture or the scriptures refers to writings that are regarded as holy in a particular religion, for example the Bible in Christianity.
scriptwriter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 电影编剧;广播(或电视)节目的撰稿人； A scriptwriter is a person who writes scripts for films or for radio or television programmes.
scroll: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (带有文字的)卷轴，长纸卷； scroll A scroll is a long roll of paper or a similar material with writing on it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (绘制或雕刻的)涡卷形装饰； scroll A scroll is a painted or carved decoration made to look like a scroll.  /  [VERB 动词] (在屏幕上)滚动(文档),滚屏； scroll If you scroll through text on a computer screen, you move the text up or down to find the information that you need.
scroll bar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (屏幕上的)滚动条； On a computer screen, a scroll bar is a long thin box along one edge of a window, which you click on with the mouse to move the text up, down, or across the window.
Scrooge: [N-VAR 可变名词] 吝啬鬼;守财奴； Scrooge If you call someone a Scrooge , you disapprove of them because they are very mean and hate spending money.
scrotum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 阴囊； A man's scrotum is the bag of skin that contains his testicles.
scrounge: [VERB 动词] 乞讨;索要； scrounge scrounger If you say that someone scrounges something such as food or money, you disapprove of them because they get it by asking for it, rather than by buying it or earning it.
scrub: [VERB 动词] 用力擦洗;刷净； scrub If you scrub something, you rub it hard in order to clean it, using a stiff brush and water.  /  [VERB 动词] 擦掉(灰尘、污渍)； scrub If you scrub dirt or stains off something, you remove them by rubbing hard.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指少雨地区的)低矮丛林，灌木丛； scrub Scrub consists of low trees and bushes, especially in an area that has very little rain.
scrubber: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 荡妇;婊子； If someone refers to a woman as a scrubber , they are suggesting in a very rude way that she has had sex with a lot of men.
scrubby: [ADJ 形容词] (地表)崎岖干燥的,灌木丛生的； scrubby Scrubby land is rough and dry and covered with scrub.
scrubland: [N-VAR 可变名词] 灌木丛林地； scrubland Scrubland is an area of land which is covered with low trees and bushes.
scruff: [PHRASE 短语] (从后面)揪住脖颈,抓住衣领； scruff If someone takes you by the scruff of the neck , they take hold of the back of your neck or collar suddenly and roughly.
scruffy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 邋遢的;不整洁的； scruffy Someone or something that is scruffy is dirty and untidy.
scrum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英式橄榄球)并列争球，密集争球； In rugby, a scrum is a tight group formed by players from both sides pushing against each other with their heads down in an attempt to get the ball.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拥挤的人群； scrum A scrum is a group of people who are close together and pushing against each other.
scrummage: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英式橄榄球)同 scrum； In rugby, a scrummage is the same as a scrum .
scrumptious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (食物)非常美味的，极其可口的； scrumptious If you describe food as scrumptious , you mean that it tastes extremely good.
scrumpy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 烈性苹果酒； scrumpy Scrumpy is a strong alcoholic drink made from apples.
scrunch: [VERB 动词] (挤压、压碎时)发出喀嚓声，发出嘎吱声； scrunch If something scrunches , it makes a loud sound as it is pressed or crushed or as it presses or crushes something else.  /  [VERB 动词] 挤扁;掰弯;使变形;使压碎； scrunch scrunch up 同scrunch If you scrunch something, you squeeze it or bend it so that it is no longer in its natural shape and is often crushed.
scruple: [N-VAR 可变名词] (道德上的)顾忌,顾虑;良心不安； scruple Scruples are moral principles or beliefs that make you unwilling to do something that seems wrong.
scrupulous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 正直的;有道德原则的;有良心的； scrupulous scrupulously Someone who is scrupulous takes great care to do what is fair, honest, or morally right.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 细致的;缜密的;一丝不苟的； scrupulous scrupulously Scrupulous means thorough, exact, and careful about details.
scrutineer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (竞选的)监票员;(比赛的)监督员； A scrutineer is a person who checks that an election or a race is carried out according to the rules.
scrutinize: [VERB 动词] 详细检查;仔细察看； scrutinize If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.
scrutiny: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 详细的检查(或审查);仔细的观察； scrutiny If a person or thing is under scrutiny , they are being studied or observed very carefully.
scuba diving: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 戴水肺的潜水;斯库巴潜水； scuba dive Scuba diving is the activity of swimming underwater using special breathing equipment.
scud: [VERB 动词] (云彩)掠过； scud If clouds scud along, they move quickly and smoothly through the sky.
scuff: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使磨损;使磨坏； scuff scuffed If you scuff something or if it scuffs , you mark the surface by scraping it against other things or by scraping other things against it.  /  [VERB 动词] 拖着脚走； scuff If you scuff your feet, you pull them along the ground as you walk.

seem: [V-LINK 连系动词] 好像;似乎;看来； seem You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe.  /  [V-LINK 连系动词] (在描述自己的感觉、想法、经历时用于缓和语气)好像，似乎； seem You use seem when you are describing your own feelings or thoughts, or describing something that has happened to you, in order to make your statement less forceful.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 似乎不能;好像无法； seem If you say that you cannot seem or could not seem to do something, you mean that you have tried to do it and were unable to.  /  See also: seeming ; �
seeming: [ADJ 形容词] 表面上的;貌似的;似是而非的； seeming Seeming means appearing to be the case, but not necessarily the case.
seemingly: [ADV 副词] 貌似，看似(但可能并非如此)； seemingly If something is seemingly the case, you mean that it appears to be the case, even though it may not really be so.  /  [ADV 副词] 似乎，好像(是事实)； seemingly You use seemingly when you want to say that something seems to be true.
seemly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 得体的;适当的;合乎礼仪的； seemly Seemly behaviour or dress is appropriate in the particular circumstances.
seen: + + + Seen is the past participle of see .
see off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 打败;战胜； see off If you see off an opponent, you defeat them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 为…送行;送别； When you see someone off , you go with them to the station, airport, or port that they are leaving from, and say goodbye to them there.
seep: [VERB 动词] 渗透;渗漏； seep If something such as liquid or gas seeps somewhere, it flows slowly and in small amounts into a place where it should not go.  /  [VERB 动词] (秘密)逐渐外泄;(不快的情感)逐渐释放； seep If something such as secret information or an unpleasant emotion seeps somewhere, it comes out gradually.
seepage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 渗;渗透;渗入； seepage Seepage is the slow flow of a liquid through something.
seer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 预言者;先知； seer A seer is a person who tells people what will happen in the future.
seesaw: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 跷跷板； seesaw A seesaw is a long board which is balanced on a fixed part in the middle.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 来回往复的;拉锯式的； seesaw In a seesaw situation, something continually changes from one state to another and back again.  /  [VERB 动词] (感情或某种局面)摇摆不定，不断反复，来回波动； seesaw If someone's emotions see-saw , or a particular situation seesaws , they continually change from one state to another and back again.
seethe: [VERB 动词] 强压怒火;生闷气； seethe When you are seething , you are very angry about something but do not express your feelings about it.  /  [VERB 动词] 充满，遍布，到处都是(人或物)； seethe If you say that a place is seething with people or things, you are emphasizing that it is very full of them and that they are all moving about.
see-through: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服)薄得透明的，透视的； See-through clothes are made of thin cloth, so that you can see a person's body or underwear through them.
see through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 看透;看穿;识破； See also: see-through ; If you see through someone or their behaviour, you realize what their intentions are, even though they are trying to hide them.
see to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 照料;处理;照看； If you see to something that needs attention, you deal with it.
segment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 部分;片段； segment A segment of something is one part of it, considered separately from the rest.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (橘子、葡萄柚等水果的)瓣； A segment of fruit such as an orange or grapefruit is one of the sections into which it is easily divided.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 圆缺;弓形； A segment of a circle is one of the two parts into which it is divided when you draw a straight line through it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (市场)细分的部分； segment A segment of a market is one part of it, considered separately from the rest.
segmentation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 分割;分段;划分； Segmentation is the dividing of something into parts which are loosely connected.
segmented: [ADJ 形容词] 分割的;切断的;划分的； segmented Segmented means divided into parts that are loosely connected to each other.
segregate: [VERB 动词] 使隔离;使分开;使分离； segregate To segregate two groups of people or things means to keep them physically apart from each other.
segregated: [ADJ 形容词] (因种族、性别、宗教不同而)隔离的，分开的； segregated Segregated buildings or areas are kept for the use of one group of people who are the same race, sex, or religion, and no other group is allowed to use them.
segregation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (因种族、性别、宗教不同而采取的)隔离措施，隔离政策； segregation Segregation is the official practice of keeping people apart, usually people of different sexes, races, or religions.
segregationist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 种族隔离主义者； segregationist A segregationist is someone who thinks people of different races should be kept apart.
segue: [VERB 动词] (直接)转到，接入(另一首曲子、另一段对话)； segue If something such as a piece of music or conversation segues into another piece of music or conversation, it changes into it or is followed by it without a break.
seismic: [ADJ 形容词] 地震的;地震引起的； seismic Seismic means caused by or relating to an earthquake.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (转变、变化)突如其来的，巨大的，急剧的； seismic A seismic shift or change is a very sudden or dramatic change.
seismograph: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 地震仪;测震仪； A seismograph is an instrument for recording and measuring the strength of earthquakes.
seismology: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 地震学； seismological seismologist Seismology is the scientific study of earthquakes.
seize: [VERB 动词] (迅速有力地)抓住，捉住； If you seize something, you take hold of it quickly, firmly, and forcefully.  /  [VERB 动词] (通过暴力突然迅速地)夺取，攻占，控制； seize When a group of people seize a place or seize control of it, they take control of it quickly and suddenly, using force.  /  [VERB 动词] (通常指通过武力)起获，没收，扣押； seize If a government or other authority seize someone's property, they take it from them, often by force.  /  [VERB 动词] 逮捕;捉拿;俘获； seize When someone is seized , they are arrested or captured.
seize on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 对…大为关注;抓住(有用的事物)； If you seize on something or seize upon it, you show great interest in it, often because it is useful to you.
seize up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (身体某部分因紧张或上了年纪而)发僵，无法动弹； seize up If a part of your body seizes up , it suddenly stops working, because you have strained it or because you are getting old.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (发动机等)停止运转，发生故障； seize up If something such as an engine seizes up , it stops working, because it has not been properly cared for.
seizure: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指心脏病或脑部疾病的)突然发作，侵袭； seizure If someone has a seizure , they have a sudden violent attack of an illness, especially one that affects their heart or brain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对权力、土地的)夺取;(突然的)占领，控制； seizure If there is a seizure of power or a seizure of an area of land, a group of people suddenly take control of the place, using force.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对非法物品的)起获，查封； seizure When an organization such as the police or customs service makes a seizure of illegal goods, they find them and take them away.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (因欠款未还而采取的)没收，充公； seizure If a financial institution or a government makes a seizure of someone's assets, they take their money or property from them because they have not paid money that they owe.
seldom: [ADV-BRD-NEG 广义否定结构副词] 不常;很少;难得； seldom If something seldom happens, it happens only occasionally.
select: [VERB 动词] 选择;挑选;选拔； select If you select something, you choose it from a number of things of the same kind.  /  [VERB 动词] (在屏幕上)选定(某文件或某段文本以作特别处理)； select If you select a file or a piece of text on a computer screen, you click on it so that it is marked in a different colour, usually in order for you to give the computer an instruction relating to that file or piece of text.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 精选的;作为…精华的;优等的； select A select group is a small group of some of the best people or things of their kind.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 第一流的;只为富人(或上层人士)而设的;高级的； select If you describe something as select , you mean it has many desirable features, but is available only to people who have a lot of money or who belong to a high social class.
select committee: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (议会中为调查某问题设立的)特别委员会； A select committee is a committee of members of a parliament which is set up to investigate and report on a particular matter.
selection: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 选拔;挑选;选择； selection Selection is the act of selecting one or more people or things from a group.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 挑选出来的一批人(或事物)； selection A selection of people or things is a set of them that have been selected from a larger group.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (商店内)可供挑选的某类商品； selection The selection of goods in a shop is the particular range of goods that it has available and from which you can choose what you want.
selective: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 选择性的;有选择的;选取少量的； selective selectively selectivity A selective process applies only to a few things or people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 仔细挑选的;严格筛选的； selective selectively When someone is selective , they choose things carefully, for example the things that they buy or do.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (记忆)选择性的，只记一部分的； selective selectively If you say that someone has a selective memory, you disapprove of the fact that they remember certain facts about something and deliberately forget others, often because it is convenient for them to do so.
selective service: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (按年龄、体格等条件选征服役者的)选拔征兵，义务兵役； In the United States, selective service is a system of selecting and ordering young men to serve in the armed forces for a limited period of time.
selector: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (挑选运动队员或参赛运动员的)选拔委员，选拔人； selector A selector is someone whose job is to choose which people will be in a particular sports team or will take part in a particular sports contest.

self: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 自身;本性;本我； self Your self is your basic personality or nature, especially considered in terms of what you are really like as a person.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 个性;自我； self A person's self is the essential part of their nature which makes them different from everyone and everything else.
self-absorbed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 只顾自己的;自我专注的； Someone who is self-absorbed thinks so much about things concerning themselves that they do not notice other people or the things around them.
self-access: [ADJ 形容词] 自主学习的(由学生自选材料并自学)； self-access In a school or college, a self-access centre is a place where students can choose and use books, tapes, or other materials.
self-addressed: [ADJ 形容词] (信封)写明发信人地址的，回邮的； self-addressed A self-addressed envelope is an envelope which you have written your address on and which you send to someone in another envelope so that they can send something back to you.
self-adhesive: [ADJ 形容词] (一面涂胶)自黏的,自粘的； self-adhesive Something that is self-adhesive is covered on one side with a sticky substance like glue, so that it will stick to surfaces.
self-aggrandizement: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (在名利、权势上的)自我扩张，自我提升； If you say that someone is guilty of self-aggrandizement , you mean that they do certain things in order to make themselves more powerful, wealthy, or important.
self-appointed: [ADJ 形容词] 自己任命的;自封的； self-appointed A self-appointed leader or ruler has taken the position of leader or ruler without anyone else asking them or choosing them to have it.
self-assembly: [ADJ 形容词] (家具等)自行组装的； self-assembly Self-assembly is used to refer to furniture and other goods that you buy in parts and that you have to put together yourself.
self-assertion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 主见;自我主张； self-assertion Self-assertion is confidence that you have in speaking firmly about your opinions and demanding the rights that you believe you should have.
self-assertive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有主见的； self-assertive Someone who is self-assertive acts in a confident way, speaking firmly about their opinions and demanding the rights that they believe they should have.
self-assessment: [N-SING 单数名词] 自行估税； In Britain, self-assessment refers to a system for paying tax in which people have to fill in an official form giving details of how much money they have earned in the previous year.
self-assurance: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自信;胸有成竹； Someone who has self-assurance shows confidence in the things that they say and do because they are sure of their abilities.
self-assured: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自信的;胸有成竹的； self-assured Someone who is self-assured shows confidence in what they say and do because they are sure of their own abilities.
self-aware: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自知的;自明的;自觉的； self-aware self-awareness Someone who is self-aware knows and judges their own character well.
self-belief: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自信； Self-belief is confidence in your own abilities or judgment.
self-catering: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自理膳食的;自供伙食的； self-catering If you go on a self-catering holiday or you stay in self-catering accommodation, you stay in a place where you have to make your own meals.
self-centred: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自我中心的;只顾自己的;自私自利的； self-centred Someone who is self-centred is only concerned with their own wants and needs and never thinks about other people.
self-confessed: [ADJ 形容词] 自己承认的;自己坦白的； self-confessed If you describe someone as a self-confessed murderer or a self-confessed romantic, for example, you mean that they admit openly that they are a murderer or a romantic.
self-confidence: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自信； self-confidence If you have self-confidence , you behave confidently because you feel sure of your abilities or value.
self-confident: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自信的； self-confident Someone who is self-confident behaves confidently because they feel sure of their abilities or value.
self-congratulation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 洋洋自得;沾沾自喜； self-congratulation If someone keeps emphasizing how well they have done or how good they are, you can refer to their behaviour as self-congratulation .
self-congratulatory: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沾沾自喜的;自吹自擂的； self-congratulatory If you describe someone or their behaviour as self-congratulatory , you mean that they keep emphasizing how well they have done or how good they are.
self-conscious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忸怩的;害羞的;难为情的;不自然的； self-conscious self-consciously self-consciousness Someone who is self-conscious is easily embarrassed and nervous because they feel that everyone is looking at them and judging them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有强烈自我意识的;高度自觉的； self-conscious self-consciously If you describe someone or something as self-conscious , you mean that they are strongly aware of who or what they are.
self-contained: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自给的;独立自足的； self-contained You can describe someone or something as self-contained when they are complete and separate and do not need help or resources from outside.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (住宿场所)设施齐全的，独门独户的； Self-contained accommodation such as a flat has all its own facilities, so that a person living there does not have to share rooms such as a kitchen or bathroom with other people.
self-contradictory: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自相矛盾的； self-contradictory If you say or write something that is self-contradictory , you make two statements which cannot both be true.
self-control: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自制力;自我克制； self-control Self-control is the ability to not show your feelings or not do the things that your feelings make you want to do.
self-controlled: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 能控制感情的;有自制力的； self-controlled Someone who is self-controlled is able to not show their feelings or not do the things that their feelings make them want to do.
self-deception: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自欺;自我欺骗； self-deception Self-deception involves allowing yourself to believe something about yourself that is not true, because the truth is more unpleasant.
self-declared: [ADJ 形容词] 同 self-proclaimed； self-declared Self-declared means the same as self-proclaimed .
self-defeating: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 适得其反的;弄巧成拙的;事与愿违的； self-defeating A plan or action that is self-defeating is likely to cause problems or difficulties instead of producing useful results.
self-defence: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (采取武力的)自卫，自我保护； self-defence Self-defence is the use of force to protect yourself against someone who is attacking you.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (对待坏事的)自卫,自我保护； self-defence Self-defence is the action of protecting yourself against something bad.
self-delusion: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自我欺骗;自我蒙蔽； self-delusion Self-delusion is the state of having a false idea about yourself or the situation you are in.
self-denial: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自我剥夺;自我牺牲;克己忘我； self-denial Self-denial is the habit of refusing to do or have things that you would like, either because you cannot afford them, or because you believe it is morally good for you not to do them or have them.
self-denying: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自我剥夺的;自我牺牲的;克己忘我的； self-denying Someone who is self-denying refuses to do or have things that they would like, either because they cannot afford them, or because they believe it is morally good for them not to do them or have them.
self-deprecating: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自我贬低的;过分谦虚的； self-deprecating If you describe someone's behaviour as self-deprecating , you mean that they criticize themselves or represent themselves as foolish in a light-hearted way.
self-destruct: [VERB 动词] 自毁； self-destruct If someone self-destructs , they do something that seriously damages their chances of success.
self-destructive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自毁的； self-destructive Self-destructive behaviour is harmful to the person who behaves in that way.
self-determination: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (国家的)自立，自主权； Self-determination is the right of a country to be independent, instead of being controlled by a foreign country, and to choose its own form of government.
self-discipline: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自我约束;律己； self-discipline Self-discipline is the ability to control yourself and to make yourself work hard or behave in a particular way without needing anyone else to tell you what to do.
self-disciplined: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有自我约束力的;能律己的； self-disciplined Someone who is self-disciplined has the ability to control themselves and to make themselves work hard or behave in a particular way without needing anyone else to tell them what to do.
self-doubt: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自我怀疑;不自信； Self-doubt is a lack of confidence in yourself and your abilities.
self-drive: [ADJ 形容词] 租车人自己驾驶的； self-drive A self-drive car is one which you hire and drive yourself.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (度假)自己驾车的,自驾游的； self-drive A self-drive holiday is one where you drive yourself to the place where you are staying, rather than being taken there by plane or coach.

semolina: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (用于做布丁或意大利面食的)粗面粉； Semolina consists of small hard grains of wheat that are used for making sweet puddings with milk and for making pasta.

send down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 开除;勒令退学； If a student is sent down from their university or college, they are made to leave because they have behaved very badly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 判…入狱； If someone who is on trial is sent down , they are found guilty and sent to prison.

send in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 呈递，提交，邮寄(参赛作品、求职信等)； send in If you send in something such as a competition entry or a letter applying for a job, you post it to the organization concerned.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 派遣,调来(警察、军队等以应付危机或困难)； send in When a government sends in troops or police officers, it orders them to deal with a crisis or problem somewhere.
sending-off: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (足球比赛中球员的)被罚下场； sending-off If there is a sending-off during a game of football, a player is told to leave the field by the referee, as a punishment for seriously breaking the rules.
send-off: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 欢送会;送行;送别； send-off If a group of people give someone who is going away a send-off , they come together to say goodbye to them.
send off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 寄出，寄走(信或包裹)； When you send off a letter or package, you send it somewhere by post.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将(足球运动员)罚下场； See also: sending-off ; If a football player is sent off , the referee makes them leave the field during a game, as a punishment for seriously breaking the rules.

send out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 分发;散发； If you send out things such as letters or bills, you send them to a large number of people at the same time.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 发出(信号、声音、光、热等)； send out To send out a signal, sound, light, or heat means to produce it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 生出，长出(根茎、枝芽等)； send out When a plant sends out roots or shoots, they grow.

send up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通过滑稽模仿)取笑，嘲弄； See also: send-up ; If you send someone or something up , you imitate them in an amusing way that makes them appear foolish.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 判…入狱;对…判刑； If someone who is on trial is sent up , they are found guilty and sent to prison.
send-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑稽讽刺的模仿作品(或表演)； send-up A send-up is a piece of writing or acting in which someone or something is imitated in an amusing way that makes them appear foolish.

senile: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 老糊涂的;老态龙钟的;年老而无力自理的； senility If old people become senile , they become confused, can no longer remember things, and are unable to look after themselves.

senior: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (在组织或专业领域中)级别高的，资深的； senior The senior people in an organization or profession have the highest and most important jobs.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 职位高于…的;资格比…老的;更资深的； senior 上级;上司;前辈 If someone is senior to you in an organization or profession, they have a higher and more important job than you or they are considered to be superior to you because they have worked there for longer and have more experience.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 较年长的人;比…大…岁的人； senior Senior is used when indicating how much older one person is than another.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (中学或大学里的)高年级学生，毕业班学生； Seniors are students in a high school, university, or college who are the oldest and who have reached an advanced level in their studies.
senior citizen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (已退休或领取养老金的)老年人，长者； A senior citizen is an older person who has retired or receives an old age pension.
seniority: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 资历;地位;级别； seniority A person's seniority in an organization is the importance and power that they have compared with others, or the fact that they have worked there for a long time.
sensation: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (身体上的)感觉，知觉； sensation A sensation is a physical feeling.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指)触觉;感觉能力;知觉； sensation Sensation is your ability to feel things physically, especially through your sense of touch.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某种经历所产生的)整体感觉，总体印象； sensation You can use sensation to refer to the general feeling or impression caused by a particular experience.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 引起轰动的人(或事件、情况)； sensation If a person, event, or situation is a sensation , it causes great excitement or interest.
sensational: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (结果、事件、局势)轰动性的，引起哗然的； sensational sensationally A sensational result, event, or situation is so remarkable that it causes great excitement and interest.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (故事、报道)耸人听闻的，哗众取宠的； sensational You can describe stories or reports as sensational if you disapprove of them because they present facts in a way that is intended to cause feelings of shock, anger, or excitement.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 极好的;绝妙的； sensational sensationally You can describe something as sensational when you think that it is extremely good.
sensationalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (报道的)耸人听闻，哗众取宠； sensationalism Sensationalism is the presenting of facts or stories in a way that is intended to produce strong feelings of shock, anger, or excitement.
sensationalist: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (新闻报道、电视广播节目)耸人听闻的，追求轰动效应的； sensationalist Sensationalist news reports and television and radio programmes present the facts in a way that makes them seem worse or more shocking than they really are.
sensationalize: [VERB 动词] 耸人听闻地夸大;大肆渲染； If someone sensationalizes a situation or event, they make it seem worse or more shocking than it really is.
sense: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 感觉官能(即视觉、嗅觉、听觉、触觉、味觉)； sense See also: sixth sense ; Your senses are the physical abilities of sight, smell, hearing, touch, and taste.  /  [VERB 动词] 感觉到;觉察到;意识到； sense If you sense something, you become aware of it or you realize it, although it is not very obvious.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 感觉;意识； sense See also: sense of occasion ; If you have a sense that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you may not have firm, clear evidence for this belief.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (负罪或释然的)感觉； sense If you have a sense of guilt or relief, for example, you feel guilty or relieved.
senseless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无意义的;无目的的;没有益处的； senseless If you describe an action as senseless , you think it is wrong because it has no purpose and produces no benefit.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 失去知觉的;不省人事的； senseless If someone is senseless , they are unconscious.
sense of direction: [N-SING 单数名词] 方向感； sense of direction Your sense of direction is your ability to know roughly where you are, or which way to go, even when you are in an unfamiliar place.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 目标明确； sense of direction If you say that someone has a sense of direction , you mean that they seem to have clear ideas about what they want to do or achieve.

sense of occasion: [N-SING 单数名词] 盛会的感觉;隆重感； sense of occasion If there is a sense of occasion when a planned event takes place, people feel that something special and important is happening.
sense organ: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 感觉器官;感官； Your sense organs are the parts of your body, for example your eyes and your ears, which enable you to be aware of things around you.
sensibility: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 感受力;感悟力;鉴赏力； sensibility Sensibility is the ability to experience deep feelings.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 敏感;善感;感情； sensibility Someone's sensibility is their tendency to be influenced or offended by things.
sensible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行为或决定)明智的，理智的，合理的； sensible sensibly Sensible actions or decisions are good because they are based on reasons rather than emotions.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人明智的，理智的，通情达理的； sensible Sensible people behave in a sensible way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服、鞋子)耐用的，朴素而实用的； sensible sensibly Sensible shoes or clothes are practical and strong rather than fashionable and attractive.
sensitive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 体恤的;体贴的;善解人意的； sensitive sensitively sensitivity If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you show understanding and awareness of them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易生气的;易担忧的;敏感的； sensitive sensitivity If you are sensitive about something, you are easily worried and offended when people talk about it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (问题、话题)敏感的，棘手的，易引起纷争的，须谨慎对待的； sensitive sensitivity A sensitive subject or issue needs to be dealt with carefully because it is likely to cause disagreement or make people angry or upset.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (文件、报告)机密的，须小心对待的，须妥善保管的； sensitive Sensitive documents or reports contain information that needs to be kept secret and dealt with carefully.
sensitize: [VERB 动词] 使敏感;使意识到； sensitize If you sensitize people to a particular problem or situation, you make them aware of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 使对…有反应;使敏化;使过敏； sensitize If a substance is sensitized to something such as light or touch, it is made sensitive to it.

sent: + + + Sent is the past tense and past participle of send .

sentimental: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 感伤的;多情的;多愁善感的； sentimental sentimentally sentimentality Someone or something that is sentimental feels or shows pity or love, sometimes to an extent that is considered exaggerated and foolish.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 情感上的;(尤指)(出于)怀旧的； sentimental Sentimental means relating to or involving feelings such as pity or love, especially for things in the past.

separated: [ADJ 形容词] 分居的； separated Someone who is separated from their wife or husband lives apart from them, but is not divorced.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (与家人等)分离的，不在一起的； separated If you are separated from someone, for example your family, you are not able to be with them.

separation: [N-VAR 可变名词] 分离;分开;分散;隔离； separation The separation of two or more things or groups is the fact that they are separate or become separate, and are not linked.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 分离期;离别;分开； separation During a separation , people who usually live together are not together.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 分居； separation If a couple who are married or living together have a separation , they decide to live apart.

sepia: [COLOUR 颜色词] 深棕色;旧照片色； sepia Something that is sepia is deep brown in colour, like the colour of very old photographs.

shaving cream: [N-MASS 物质名词] 剃须膏;修面霜； shaving cream Shaving cream is a soft soapy substance which men put on their face before they shave.
shawl: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (女用)围巾，披巾;襁褓； A shawl is a large piece of woollen cloth which a woman wears over her shoulders or head, or which is wrapped around a baby to keep it warm.
she: (用于指先前已提到的女性或雌性动物)她，它； she You use she to refer to a woman, girl, or female animal who has already been mentioned or whose identity is clear.  /  (用于泛指未指明性别的人，以避免总是用 he。有些人更倾向于使用 he or she 或 they 来表示泛指)； she Some writers may use she to refer to a person who is not identified as either male or female.  /  (用以指代国家)； she She is sometimes used to refer to a country or nation.  /  (用以指代汽车、机器、船等)； she Some people use she to refer to a car or a machine.
sheaf: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一叠，一沓，一扎纸； sheaf A sheaf of papers is a number of them held or fastened together.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一束，一捆(收割的谷物)； A sheaf of corn or wheat is a number of corn or wheat plants that have been cut down and tied together.
shear: [VERB 动词] 剪(羊毛)； shear shearing To shear a sheep means to cut its wool off.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (尤指修剪篱笆用的)大剪刀； shear A pair of shears is a garden tool like a very large pair of scissors.  /  相关词组： shear off �
shear off: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 切断，剪切;(使金属等)断裂； If something such as a piece of metal shears off , or if it is sheared off , it breaks.
sheath: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (刀、剑的)鞘，套； A sheath is a covering for the blade of a knife.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 保险套;避孕套； A sheath is a rubber covering for a man's penis and is used during sex as a contraceptive or as a protection against disease.
sheathe: [VERB 动词] 用…盖住;将…包起来； sheathe If something is sheathed in a material or other covering, it is closely covered with it.  /  [VERB 动词] 将刀插入鞘中； sheathe When someone sheathes a knife, they put it in its sheath.
sheaves: (sheaf 的复数)； Sheaves is the plural of sheaf .
shebang: [PHRASE 短语] 整个事情;这一切;整个情况； The whole shebang is the whole situation or business that you are describing.
she'd: (尤其当had为助动词时, she had 的口语形式)； she'd She'd is the usual spoken form of 'she had', especially when 'had' is an auxiliary verb.  /  (she would 的口语形式)； she'd She'd is a spoken form of 'she would'.
shed: (用于储存园艺工具等的)简易房，小棚屋，小屋； shed A shed is a small building that is used for storing things such as garden tools.  /  (车站、港口、工厂等里面的)棚式建筑物，厂房,工棚,库房； shed A shed is a large shelter or building, for example at a railway station, port, or factory.  /  落叶;蜕皮;脱毛； shed When a tree sheds its leaves, its leaves fall off in the autumn.  /  摆脱;去除;抛弃； shed To shed something means to get rid of it.
sheen: [N-SING 单数名词] 光泽;光辉;光彩； sheen If something has a sheen , it has a smooth and gentle brightness on its surface.
sheep: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 羊;绵羊； sheep A sheep is a farm animal which is covered with thick curly hair called wool.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 盲从者;随波逐流者； If you say that a group of people are like sheep , you disapprove of them because if one person does something, all the others copy that person.  /  See also: black sheep ; �
sheepdog: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 牧羊犬； A sheepdog is a breed of dog.
sheepish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 窘迫的;难为情的;尴尬的； sheepish sheepishly If you look sheepish , you look slightly embarrassed because you feel foolish or you have done something silly.
sheepskin: [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤指用于制作大衣或毛毯的)带毛的羊皮，羊毛皮革； sheepskin Sheepskin is the skin of a sheep with the wool still attached to it, used especially for making coats and rugs.
sheer: [ADJ 形容词] (用于强调)纯粹的，完全的，十足的； sheer You can use sheer to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 陡峭的;垂直的； sheer A sheer cliff or drop is extremely steep or completely vertical.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极薄的;极轻的;精致的； sheer Sheer material is very thin, light, and delicate.
sheet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 被单;床单； sheet A sheet is a large rectangular piece of cotton or other cloth that you sleep on or cover yourself with in a bed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一页，一张纸； sheet A sheet of paper is a rectangular piece of paper.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 简要记录;纪要； sheet You can use sheet to refer to a piece of paper which gives information about something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (玻璃、金属、木头等的)大块薄片，薄板； sheet A sheet of glass, metal, or wood is a large, flat, thin piece of it.
sheeting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (金属、塑料等的)薄片，压片，片材，薄膜； sheeting Sheeting is metal, plastic, or other material that is made in the form of sheets.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 被单布;床单布； sheeting Sheeting is cloth that is used for making sheets.
sheet metal: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 金属薄板； Sheet metal is metal which has been made into thin sheets.
sheet music: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 活页乐谱;散页乐谱； sheet music Sheet music is music that is printed on sheets of paper without a hard cover.
sheikh: [N-TITLE; N-COUNT 头衔名词；可数名词] (阿拉伯的男性)酋长，族长，首领，村长； A sheikh is a male Arab chief or ruler.
sheikhdom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 酋长管辖的领土;酋长国； A sheikhdom is a country or region that is ruled by a sheikh.
shelf: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (固定在墙上或橱柜上的)架子，搁板； shelf A shelf is a flat piece of wood, metal, or glass which is attached to a wall or to the sides of a cupboard.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 搁板状岩石;突出的岩石;(水下的)暗礁，陆架； shelf See also: continental shelf ; A shelf is a section of rock on a cliff or mountain or underwater that sticks out like a shelf.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 现成的;不用定制的； shelf If you buy something off the shelf , you buy something that is not specially made for you.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 搁置的;闲置的;没人要的； shelf If you say that someone or something is on the shelf , you mean that no one wants them.
shelf life: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指食品等的)货架期，保存期； shelf life The shelf life of a product, especially food, is the length of time that it can be kept in a shop or at home before it becomes too old to sell or use.
she'll: (she will 的常用口语形式)； she'll She'll is the usual spoken form of 'she will'.
shell: (蛋、坚果等的)壳； shell 壳质;壳料 The shell of a nut or egg is the hard covering which surrounds it.  /  (龟、蜗牛、蟹等的)壳； The shell of an animal such as a tortoise, snail, or crab is the hard protective covering that it has around its body or on its back.  /  贝壳； shell Shells are hard objects found on beaches.  /  剥…的壳;去…的皮； shell If you shell nuts, peas, prawns, or other food, you remove their natural outer covering.
shellac: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (用于家具抛光的)虫胶清漆； Shellac is a kind of natural varnish which you paint on to wood to give it a shiny surface.
shell company: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 控股公司;空壳公司； shell company A shell company is a company that another company takes over in order to use its name to gain an advantage.
shellfire: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 炮火;炮击;炮轰； shellfire Shellfire is the firing of large military guns.
shellfish: [N-VAR 可变名词] (海生)贝类;甲壳类海生动物； shellfish Shellfish are small creatures that live in the sea and have a shell.
shell out: 为…花费一大笔钱； shell out If you shell out for something, you spend a lot of money on it.
shell program: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 壳程序(一种基本程序，计算机用户可用其开发适合自己需要的程序)； A shell program is a basic computer program that provides a framework within which the user can develop the program to suit their own needs.
shell shock: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 炮弹休克，弹震症(一种因曾置身战火而引起的精神紧张或错乱)； shell shock Shell shock is the confused or nervous mental condition of people who have been under fire in a war.
shell-shocked: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (通常指因为发生某些不好的事而)非常震惊的，极度惊恐的； shell-shocked If you say that someone is shell-shocked , you mean that they are very shocked, usually because something bad has happened.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 患炮弹休克症的； shell-shocked If someone is shell-shocked , they have a confused or nervous mental condition as a result of a shocking experience such as being in a war or an accident.
shell suit: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (薄尼龙制成的)休闲装，休闲服； shell suit A shell suit is a casual suit which is made of thin nylon.
shell-suit: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (声音)刺耳的，尖厉的； shrilly shrillness A shrill sound is high-pitched and unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (要求、抗议、声明等)尖刻的，强硬的，不依不饶的； If you describe a demand, protest, or statement as shrill , you disapprove of it and do not like the strong, forceful way it is said.  /  [VERB 动词] (铃、哨)发出尖锐的声音，发出刺耳的声音； If a bell or whistle shrills , it makes a loud, high-pitched sound.  /  [VERB 动词] 尖声说出;尖声喊出； If someone with a high-pitched voice shrills something, they say it loudly.
shelter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (躲避恶劣天气或危险的)遮蔽物，庇护处，掩体； shelter A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指躲避恶劣天气或危险的)遮蔽，庇护，掩蔽； shelter If a place provides shelter , it provides you with a place to stay or live, especially when you need protection from bad weather or danger.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 收容所;庇护所； shelter A shelter is a building where homeless people can sleep and get food.  /  [VERB 动词] 躲避;避难； shelter If you shelter in a place, you stay there and are protected from bad weather or danger.
sheltered: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不受风雨侵袭的;有遮蔽物的； sheltered A sheltered place is protected from wind and rain.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 受庇护的;处处受保护的； sheltered If you say that someone has led a sheltered life, you mean that they have been protected from difficult or unpleasant experiences.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (住所或工作)适于老人(或残疾人)的，福利性的； sheltered Sheltered accommodation or work is designed for old or disabled people.  /  See also: shelter ; �
shelve: [VERB 动词] 搁置，停止执行，暂不进行(计划、项目)； shelve If someone shelves a plan or project, they decide not to continue with it, either for a while or permanently.  /  [VERB 动词] (近海或海底陆地)向下倾斜,成斜坡； shelve If an area of ground next to or under the sea shelves , it slopes downwards.  /  (shelf 的复数)； Shelves is the plural of shelf .
shelving: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 一套架子;一组搁板;搁板料； shelving Shelving is a set of shelves, or material which is used for making shelves.
shenanigans: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (尤指可笑、有趣的)恶作剧，诡计，鬼把戏； shenanigans You can use shenanigans to refer to rather dishonest or immoral behaviour, especially when you think it is amusing or interesting.
shepherd: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指男性)牧羊人，羊倌； A shepherd is a person, especially a man, whose job is to look after sheep.  /  [VERB 动词] 带领;引领;护送； shepherd If you are shepherded somewhere, someone takes you there to make sure that you arrive at the right place safely.
shepherdess: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 牧羊女;女牧羊人； A shepherdess is a woman whose job is to look after sheep.
shepherd's pie: [N-VAR 可变名词] (通常指羔羊肉馅的)肉馅土豆泥饼； Shepherd's pie is a dish consisting of minced meat, usually lamb, covered with a layer of mashed potato.
sherbet: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 果味汽水粉糖； sherbet Sherbet is a sweet dry powder that tastes fizzy and is eaten as a sweet.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 果汁冰糕； sherbet Sherbet is like ice cream but made with fruit juice, sugar, and water.
sheriff: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词] (美国由选举产生的)县治安官； sheriff In the United States, a sheriff is a person who is elected to make sure that the law is obeyed in a particular county.  /  [N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词] (苏格兰的)郡法官,区法官； In Scotland, a sheriff is a legal officer whose chief duty is to act as judge in a Sheriff Court.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英格兰和威尔士境内挂名的名誉)郡长，郡督； In England and Wales, the Sheriff of a city or county is a person who is elected or appointed to carry out mainly ceremonial duties.
sherry: [N-MASS 物质名词] 雪利酒(原产自西班牙西南部的烈性葡萄酒，通常于餐前饮用)； sherry 一杯雪利酒 Sherry is a type of strong wine that is made in south-western Spain.
she's: (she is 的常用口语形式)； She's is the usual spoken form of 'she is'.  /  (尤在 has 为助动词时，she has 的口语形式)； She's is a spoken form of 'she has', especially when 'has' is an auxiliary verb.
shiatsu: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 指压按摩(用于治疗疾病或减轻疼痛)； Shiatsu is a form of massage that is used to cure illness and reduce pain.
shibboleth: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 过时的观点;陈旧的原则;错误的信念； shibboleth If you describe an idea or belief as a shibboleth , you mean that it is thought important by a group of people but may be old-fashioned or wrong.
shield: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 屏障;保护物;保护人； shield Something or someone which is a shield against a particular danger or risk provides protection from it.  /  [VERB 动词] 保护;掩护;庇护； shield If something or someone shields you from a danger or risk, they protect you from it.  /  [VERB 动词] (为阻挡阳光直射而)挡住，遮住(眼睛)； shield If you shield your eyes, you put your hand above your eyes to protect them from direct sunlight.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 盾;盾牌； A shield is a large piece of metal or leather which soldiers used to carry to protect their bodies while they were fighting.
shift: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使移动;使挪动;使转移； shift If you shift something or if it shifts , it moves slightly.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] (意见、情况、政策)有所变动，稍作改变;使发生些许变化； shift If someone's opinion, a situation, or a policy shifts or is shifted , it changes slightly.  /  [VERB 动词] 推卸，推诿，转嫁(责任)； shift If someone shifts the responsibility or blame for something onto you, they unfairly make you responsible or make people blame you for it, instead of them.  /  [VERB 动词] 销售，出售(滞销商品)； shift If a shop or company shifts goods, they sell goods that are difficult to sell.

shilling: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 先令(1971 年以前英国的货币单位，1先令值 5 便士，20 先令合1英镑)； A shilling was a unit of money used in Britain until 1971 which was the equivalent of 5p.
shilly-shally: [VERB 动词] 犹豫;踌躇不决； shilly-shally If you say that someone is shilly-shallying , you disapprove of the fact that they are hesitating when they should make a decision.
shimmer: [VERB 动词] 闪着微弱的光;闪烁； shimmer If something shimmers , it shines with a faint, unsteady light or has an unclear, unsteady appearance.
shimmy: [VERB 动词] (抖动着肩膀和臀部)跳希米舞;一扭一摆地走； If you shimmy , you dance or move in a way that involves shaking your hips and shoulders from side to side.
shin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胫;胫部;小腿； shin Your shins are the front parts of your legs between your knees and your ankles.  /  相关词组： shin up �
shindig: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 盛大聚会;盛大舞会； A shindig is a large, noisy, enjoyable party.
shine: [VERB 动词] 发光;照耀； When the sun or a light shines , it gives out bright light.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…照向;使…的光投向； shine If you shine a torch or other light somewhere, you point it there, so that you can see something when it is dark.  /  [VERB 动词] (因反射而)发光，发亮； Something that shines is very bright and clear because it is reflecting light.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 光亮;光泽； shine Something that has a shine is bright and clear because it is reflecting light.

shining: [ADJ 形容词] (成就)辉煌的，值得钦佩的;(品质)出色的,卓越的； shining See also: shine ; A shining achievement or quality is a very good one which should be greatly admired.

shin up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (快速轻巧地)爬(树或竿)； If you shin up a tree or a pole, you climb it quickly and easily, using your hands and legs to grip it.
shiny: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 闪亮的;反光的;有光泽的； shiny Shiny things are bright and reflect light.
ship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大船;轮船;舰； ship A ship is a large boat which carries passengers or cargo.  /  [VERB 动词] 运送;运输;船运； ship If people or things are shipped somewhere, they are sent there on a ship or by some other means of transport.  /  See also: shipping ;  /  相关词组： ship out �
shipboard: [ADJ 形容词] 船上发生的;在船上的； shipboard Shipboard means taking place on a ship.
shipbuilder: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 造船工人;造船公司;造船厂； A shipbuilder is a company or a person that builds ships.
shipbuilding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 造船业； Shipbuilding is the industry of building ships.
shipload: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 船舶装载量； shipload A shipload of people or goods is as many people or goods as a ship can carry.
shipmate: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同船的船员;同船的水手； shipmate Sailors who work together on the same ship are shipmates .
shipment: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 运输的货物； shipment A shipment is an amount of a particular kind of cargo that is sent to another country on a ship, train, aeroplane, or other vehicle.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 运输;运送;装运； shipment The shipment of a cargo somewhere is the sending of it there by ship, train, aeroplane, or some other vehicle.
ship out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指乘船)离开； ship out If someone ships out , they leave a place, especially by ship.
shipowner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 船主;船东;船舶公司合伙人； A shipowner is someone who owns a ship or ships or who has shares in a shipping company.

shrunk: + + + Shrunk is the past participle of shrink .
