shuck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 壳;荚;外皮； shuck The shuck of something is its outer covering, for example the leaves round an ear of corn, or the shell of a shellfish.  /  [VERB 动词] 剥…的壳(或荚);去…的外皮； shuck If you shuck something such as corn or shellfish, you remove it from its outer covering.  /  [VERB 动词] 脱去(衣服)； shuck If you shuck something that you are wearing, you take it off.  /  [EXCLAM 感叹语] (表示尴尬、失望或厌烦)哎，呸,什么，哪有的事； shuck Shucks is an exclamation that is used to express embarrassment, disappointment, or annoyance.
shudder: [VERB 动词] (因担忧、恐惧、厌恶或寒冷)发抖，打颤，战栗； shudder If you shudder , you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.  /  [VERB 动词] (机器、交通工具等)强烈震动，剧烈抖动； shudder If something such as a machine or vehicle shudders , it shakes suddenly and violently.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 担忧;恐惧;害怕； shudder If something sends a shudder or shudders through a group of people, it makes them worried or afraid.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不敢设想;想到…不寒而栗； shudder If you say that you shudder to think what would happen in a particular situation, you mean that you expect it to be so bad that you do not really want to think about it.
shuffle: [VERB 动词] 拖着脚走； shuffle If you shuffle somewhere, you walk there without lifting your feet properly off the ground.  /  [VERB 动词] (通常因不舒服或难为情)挪动双脚，坐立不安； shuffle If you shuffle around , you move your feet about while standing or you move your bottom about while sitting, often because you feel uncomfortable or embarrassed.  /  [VERB 动词] 洗牌； If you shuffle playing cards, you mix them up before you begin a game.  /  [VERB 动词] 将(纸张等)变换位置;打乱…的次序； shuffle If you shuffle things such as pieces of paper, you move them around so that they are in a different order.
shun: [VERB 动词] 刻意避开;有意回避； shun If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.
shunt: [VERB 动词] (通常因为不方便而)将…转移至别处，将…调往别处； shunt If a person or thing is shunted somewhere, they are moved or sent there, usually because someone finds them inconvenient.  /  [VERB 动词] 使(火车车皮或车厢)转轨； shunt When railway engines shunt wagons or carriages, they push or pull them from one railway line to another.
shush: [CONVENTION 惯用语] (要某人安静)嘘，别出声； You say shush when you are telling someone to be quiet.  /  [VERB 动词] (通过嘘声等)使安静； shush If you shush someone, you tell them to be quiet by saying 'shush' or 'sh', or by indicating in some other way that you want them to be quiet.
shut: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 关闭;关上;合上； shut If you shut something such as a door or if it shuts , it moves so that it fills a hole or a space.  /  [VERB 动词] 闭上(眼睛)； shut If you shut your eyes, you lower your eyelids so that you cannot see anything.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 闭上(嘴巴);(嘴巴)合上； shut If your mouth shuts or if you shut your mouth, you place your lips firmly together.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(商店、酒吧等公共场所)关门，停止营业，休息； shut When a store, bar, or other public building shuts or when someone shuts it, it is closed and you cannot use it until it is open again.
shut away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通常因沮丧)把自己关起来，独自躲起来； If you shut yourself away , you avoid going out and seeing other people, usually because you are feeling depressed.
shutdown: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (工厂、商店等的)停业，歇业，关闭，倒闭； shutdown A shutdown is the closing of a factory, shop, or other business, either for a short time or for ever.
shut down: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使(工厂、公司等)关闭,歇业，停业； shut down See also: shutdown ; If a factory or business shuts down or if someone shuts it down , work there stops or it no longer trades as a business.
shuteye: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 合眼;睡觉； Shut-eye is sleep.
shut-eye: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 合眼;睡觉； shut-eye Shut-eye is sleep.
shut-in: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 长期抱恙在家的人;卧病在床的人； shut-in A shut-in is someone who is ill for a long time, and has to stay in bed or at home.
shut in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…关在(房间)里面;把…关起来； If you shut someone or something in a room, you close the door so that they cannot leave it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把自己关起来； If you shut yourself in a room, you stay in there and make sure nobody else can get in.  /  See also: shut-in ; �
shut off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 关闭;关上;使停止运转； shut off If you shut off something such as an engine or an electrical item, you turn it off to stop it working.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通常因沮丧而)躲开他人，不见人，不与人来往； If you shut yourself off , you avoid seeing other people, usually because you are feeling depressed.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 切断，停止(…的供应)； shut off If an official organization shuts off the supply of something, they no longer send it to the people they supplied in the past.
shut out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…关在门外;使…不能进入； shut out If you shut something or someone out , you prevent them from getting into a place, for example by closing the doors.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 摒弃，阻断(念头、情感等)； shut out If you shut out a thought or a feeling, you prevent yourself from thinking or feeling it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…排除在外； If you shut someone out of something, you prevent them from having anything to do with it.
shutter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (照相机的)快门； shutter The shutter in a camera is the part which opens to allow light through the lens when a photograph is taken.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 百叶窗； shutter Shutters are wooden or metal covers fitted on the outside of a window.
shuttered: [ADJ 形容词] 关上百叶窗的； shuttered A shuttered window, room, or building has its shutters closed.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 装有百叶窗的； shuttered A shuttered window, room, or building has shutters fitted to it.
shuttle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同space shuttle； A shuttle is the same as a space shuttle .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 往来于两地之间的航班(或班车、火车)； shuttle A shuttle is a plane, bus, or train which makes frequent journeys between two places.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使频繁往来于(两地之间)； shuttle If someone or something shuttles or is shuttled from one place to another place, they frequently go from one place to the other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (织布用的)梭； A shuttle is a piece of equipment used in weaving.
shuttlecock: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 羽毛球； A shuttlecock is the small object that you hit over the net in a game of badminton.
shuttle diplomacy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 穿梭外交(指国家元首拒绝直接对话的国家之间解决争端的外交方式)； shuttle diplomacy Shuttle diplomacy is the movement of diplomats between countries whose leaders refuse to talk directly to each other, in order to try to settle the argument between them.
shut up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使住口;使闭嘴； shut up If someone shuts up or if someone shuts them up , they stop talking.
-shy: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] (用于名词之后构成形容词)表示“不喜欢…的”“竭力避开…的”； -shy -shy is added to nouns to form adjectives which indicate that someone does not like a particular thing, and tries to avoid it.
shy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 害羞的;腼腆的;怕生的； shy shyly shyness A shy person is nervous and uncomfortable in the company of other people.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 犹豫的;不情愿的;害怕的;有所顾忌的； shy If you are shy of doing something, you are unwilling to do it because you are afraid of what might happen.  /  [VERB 动词] 马惊走，惊退； When a horse shies , it moves away suddenly, because something has frightened it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳;一回吃亏两回学乖； You say ' once bitten, twice shy ' when you want to indicate that someone will not do something a second time because they had a bad experience the first time they did it.
shy away from: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (因害怕或信心不足而)回避，躲避，避免做； shy away from If you shy away from doing something, you avoid doing it, often because you are afraid or not confident enough.
shyster: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 奸诈之徒，卑鄙小人，不择手段之人 (尤指律师或政客)； If you refer to someone, especially a lawyer or politician, as a shyster , you mean that they are dishonest and immoral.
Siamese cat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 暹罗猫； A Siamese cat is a type of cat with short cream and brown fur, blue eyes, dark ears, and a dark tail.
Siamese twin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 连体婴儿;连体双胞胎； Siamese twins are twins who are born with their bodies joined.
sibilant: [ADJ 形容词] 发咝咝音的； sibilant Sibilant sounds are soft 's' sounds.
sibling: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兄弟姐妹； sibling Your siblings are your brothers and sisters.
sic: (置于括号中，注于某看似古怪或拼写有误的单词或词组后)原文如此，故意如此； sic You write sic in brackets after a word or expression when you want to indicate to the reader that although the word looks odd or wrong, you intended to write it like that or the original writer wrote it like that.
Sicilian: [ADJ 形容词] 西西里的;西西里人的;西西里文化的； Sicilian Sicilian means belonging or relating to Sicily, or to its people or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 西西里人;西西里岛人的后裔； A Sicilian is a Sicilian citizen, or a person of Sicilian origin.
sick: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (常指在生理上，有时也指在精神上)生病的，有病的； sick 病人 If you are sick , you are ill.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 呕吐的;恶心的;想吐的； sick If you are sick , the food that you have eaten comes up from your stomach and out of your mouth.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 呕吐物； Sick is vomit.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 厌倦的;厌烦的;厌恶的； sick If you say that you are sick of something or sick and tired of it, you are emphasizing that you are very annoyed by it and want it to stop.
sick bay: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指船上、海军基地、英国学校里的)病室，医务室； sick bay A sick bay is an area, especially on a ship or navy base, or in Britain in a school or university, where medical treatment is given and where beds are provided for people who are ill.
sickbed: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 病榻;病床； sickbed Your sickbed is the bed that you are lying in while you are ill.
sick building syndrome: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 病态建筑综合征，大楼病综合征(指因办公楼空气不好而引起的头痛、眼睛疼痛、疲劳等症状)； Sick building syndrome is a group of conditions, including headaches, sore eyes, and tiredness, which people who work in offices may experience because the air there is not healthy to breathe.
sicken: [VERB 动词] 使厌恶;使作呕； sicken If something sickens you, it makes you feel disgusted.  /  [VERB 动词] 患病;得病;生病； sicken If you sicken , you become ill.
sickening: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人恐惧的;令人厌恶的;令人作呕的； sickening sickeningly You describe something as sickening when it gives you feelings of horror or disgust, or makes you feel sick in your stomach.
sickie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 称病缺勤;假病假； sickie If someone takes a sickie , they take a day off work saying that they are ill, especially when they are not actually ill.
sickle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 镰刀； A sickle is a tool that is used for cutting grass and grain crops.
sick leave: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 病假； sick leave Sick leave is the time that a person spends away from work because of illness or injury.
sickle-cell anaemia: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 镰状细胞性贫血； Sickle-cell anaemia is an inherited illness in which the red blood cells become curved, causing a number of health problems.
sickly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 常生病的;虚弱的;健康欠佳的； sickly A sickly person or animal is weak, unhealthy, and often ill.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (通常指因为太甜而)让人恶心的，令人作呕的； sickly A sickly smell or taste is unpleasant and makes you feel slightly sick, often because it is extremely sweet.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (颜色、灯光等)暗淡的，苍白的，微弱的； sickly A sickly colour or light is unpleasantly pale or weak.
sickness: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 患病;生病;不健康； sickness Sickness is the state of being ill or unhealthy.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恶心;呕吐感； sickness See also: morning sickness ; travel sickness ; Sickness is the uncomfortable feeling that you are going to vomit.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 病症;疾病； sickness A sickness is a particular illness.
sickness benefit: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (由政府发放给因病不能工作的人的)疾病补助金，疾病津贴； Sickness benefit is money that you receive regularly from the government when you are unable to work because of illness.
sick note: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (有医生签名的)病假条； A sick note is an official note signed by a doctor which states that someone is ill and needs to stay off work for a particular period of time.
sick pay: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 病假工资； sick pay When you are ill and unable to work, sick pay is the money that you get from your employer instead of your normal wages.
sickroom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 病房;病室； sickroom A sickroom is a room in which a sick person is lying in bed.
side: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一侧;一边;一旁； side The side of something is a position to the left or right of it, rather than in front of it, behind it, or on it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 侧面； side The side of an object, building, or vehicle is any of its flat surfaces which is not considered to be its front, its back, its top, or its bottom.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (洞或容器垂直的)内侧面，内壁； side The sides of a hollow or a container are its inside vertical surfaces.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 边;边缘； side The sides of an area or surface are its edges.
sidearm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 随身佩带的武器(通常指小手枪)； sidearm Sidearms are weapons, usually small guns, that you can wear on a belt.
sideboard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 餐具柜;餐柜； A sideboard is a long cupboard which is about the same height as a table.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 同 sideburns； Sideboards are the same as sideburns .
sideburns: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (男子的)鬓角； sideburns If a man has sideburns , he has a strip of hair growing down the side of each cheek.
sidecar: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (附于摩托车旁可载人的)边车，跨斗，侧车； A sidecar is a kind of box with wheels which you can attach to the side of a motorcycle so that you can carry a passenger in it.
-sided: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] (与数词或形容词连用)表示“有…个边的”，“有…面的”； -sided See also: one-sided ; -sided combines with numbers or adjectives to describe how many sides something has, or what kind of sides something has.
side dish: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (与主菜一起上的)配菜； side dish A side dish is an amount of a particular food that is served at the same time as the main dish.
side-effect: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常指药物不良的)副作用； side-effect The side-effects of a drug are the effects, usually bad ones, that the drug has on you in addition to its function of curing illness or pain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常指令人不快的)附带后果，意外后果； A side-effect of a situation is something unplanned and usually unpleasant that happens in addition to the main effects of that situation.
sidefoot: [VERB 动词] 用脚侧踢球； sidefoot In football, if a player side-foots the ball, they kick it with the side of their foot.
side issue: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 次要问题;枝节问题； side issue A side issue is an issue or subject that is not considered to be as important as the main one.
sidekick: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 助手;副手； sidekick Someone's sidekick is a person who accompanies them and helps them, and who you consider to be less intelligent or less important than the other person.
sidelight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (车辆前面的)位置灯，边灯； The sidelights on a vehicle are the small lights at the front that help other drivers to notice the vehicle and to judge its width.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (车辆两侧的)侧灯； The sidelights on a vehicle are lights on its sides.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (有关某情况的)侧面消息，趣闻，附带信息； sidelight A sidelight on a particular situation is a piece of information about that situation which is interesting but which is not particularly important.
sideline: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兼职;副业； sideline A sideline is something that you do in addition to your main job in order to earn extra money.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (球场等的)边线； The sidelines are the lines marking the long sides of the playing area, for example on a football field or tennis court.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (某一情况的)外围，局外； sideline If you are on the sidelines in a situation, you do not influence events at all, either because you have chosen not to be involved, or because other people have not involved you.  /  [VERB 动词] 把…排除在外;使靠边;不重视； sideline If someone or something is sidelined , they are made to seem unimportant and not included in what people are doing.
sidelong: [ADJ 形容词] 斜着眼看的;侧眼看的;睨视的； sidelong If you give someone a sidelong look, you look at them out of the corner of your eyes.
side-on: [ADJ 形容词] (碰撞、视线)侧面的，侧向的； side-on A side-on collision or view is a collision or view from the side of an object.
side order: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (主菜之外)另点的配菜； side order A side order is an amount of a food that you order in a restaurant to be served at the same time as the main dish.
side road: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 支线;岔路;旁路； A side road is a road which leads off a busier, more important road.
side-saddle: [ADV 副词] 坐在横鞍上地;偏坐在鞍上地； side-saddle When you ride a horse side-saddle , you sit on a special saddle with both your legs on one side rather than one leg on each side of the horse.
side salad: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 用作配菜的单份色拉； A side salad is a bowl of salad for one person which is served with a main meal.
sideshow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 次要活动;附带事件;附属活动； sideshow A sideshow is a less important or less significant event or situation related to a larger, more important one that is happening at the same time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (马戏或游园会中穿插的)小节目，助兴表演,杂耍； At a circus or fair, a sideshow is a performance that you watch or a game of skill that you play, that is provided in addition to the main entertainment.
side-splitting: [ADJ 形容词] 令人捧腹大笑的;令人笑破肚皮的； side-splitting Something that is side-splitting is very funny and makes you laugh a lot.
sidestep: [VERB 动词] 回避，规避(问题等)； sidestep If you sidestep a problem, you avoid discussing it or dealing with it.  /  [VERB 动词] 横跨一步躲过;侧移一步闪开； sidestep If you sidestep , you step sideways in order to avoid something or someone that is coming towards you or going to hit you.
side street: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (安静的)小路，小街； A side street is a quiet, often narrow street which leads off a busier street.
sideswipe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 借机抨击;借题发挥的批评;顺带的贬损； sideswipe If you take a sideswipe at someone, you make an unexpected critical remark about them while you are talking about something else.
sidetrack: [VERB 动词] 使分散思路;使转变话题;使转移目标； sidetrack If you are sidetracked by something, it makes you forget what you intended to do or say, and start instead doing or talking about a different thing.
sidewalk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人行道； sidewalk A sidewalk is a path with a hard surface by the side of a road.
sideways: [ADV 副词] 往(或从、向)一侧； sideways Sideways means from or towards the side of something or someone.  /  [ADV 副词] (调动工作)平级地； sideways If you are moved sideways at work, you move to another job at the same level as your old job.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 使大为吃惊;使极为困惑;使大为不快； sideways If you are knocked sideways by something, it makes you feel very surprised, confused, or upset.
siding: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (铁路线的)侧线，岔道； A siding is a short railway track beside the main tracks, where engines and carriages are left when they are not being used.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (建筑外墙的)墙板，壁板； Siding is a wooden or metal covering on the outside walls of a building.
sidle: [VERB 动词] 悄悄地走;小心翼翼地走； sidle If you sidle somewhere, you walk there in a quiet or cautious way, as if you do not want anyone to notice you.
SIDS: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 婴儿猝死综合征； SIDS SIDS is used to talk about the sudden death of a baby while it is asleep, when it had not previously been ill.

simile: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 明喻； A simile is an expression which describes a person or thing as being similar to someone or something else.

simper: [VERB 动词] 傻笑;痴笑； simper When someone simpers , they smile in a rather silly way.
simple: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 简单的;简明的;易于理解的； simple simply If you describe something as simple , you mean that it is not complicated, and is therefore easy to understand.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 简朴的;朴素的;不加装饰的； simple simply If you describe people or things as simple , you mean that they have all the basic or necessary things they require, but nothing extra.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 好办的;容易的;易解决的;简单的； simple If a problem is simple or if its solution is simple , the problem can be solved easily.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易做的;易完成的;易解决的； simple simply A simple task is easy to do.
simple interest: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 单利； Simple interest is interest that is calculated on an original sum of money and not also on interest which has previously been added to the sum.
simple-minded: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 头脑简单的;天真的;愚蠢的； simple-minded simple-mindedness If you describe someone as simple-minded , you believe that they interpret things in a way that is too simple and do not understand how complicated things are.
simpleton: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 傻瓜;呆子;容易受骗的人； simpleton If you call someone a simpleton , you think they are easily deceived or not very intelligent.

simplify: [VERB 动词] 简化;使易懂;使简洁； simplify simplified If you simplify something, you make it easier to understand or you remove the things which make it complex.
simplistic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (观点、阐述)过分简单化的； simplistic simplistically A simplistic view or interpretation of something makes it seem much simpler than it really is.
simply: [ADV 副词] 简单地;只不过;仅仅;纯粹； simply You use simply to emphasize that something consists of only one thing, happens for only one reason, or is done in only one way.  /  [ADV 副词] (用于强调)简直，根本； simply You use simply to emphasize what you are saying.  /  See also: simple ; �

simulcast: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (广播和电视上或多个电视频道的)联播节目； simulcast A simulcast is a programme which is broadcast at the same time on radio and television, or on more than one channel.  /  [VERB 动词] (在广播和电视上或多个电视频道)联播，同步播出； simulcast To simulcast a programme means to broadcast it at the same time on radio and television, or on more than one channel.
simultaneous: [ADJ 形容词] 同时发生的;同时出现的;同步的； simultaneous simultaneously Things which are simultaneous happen or exist at the same time.

since: [PREP 介词] (表示某情况自过去某时间点或某个事件以来一直持续到现在)自…以后，从…以来； since You use since when you are mentioning a time or event in the past and indicating that a situation has continued from then until now.  /  [PREP 介词] (表示某事件或情况从过去某时间或某个事件之后一直发生)自…以来,在…之后； since You use since to mention a time or event in the past when you are describing an event or situation that has happened after that time.  /  [ADV 副词] (表示过去某事或某情况发生后不久又发生了另一件事)此后，后来； since When you are talking about an event or situation in the past, you use since to indicate that another event happened at some point later in time.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 早就； since If you say that something has long since happened, you mean that it happened a long time ago.
sincere: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 诚恳的;真挚的;真诚的； sincere sincerity If you say that someone is sincere , you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

sinew: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肌腱;筋； sinew A sinew is a cord in your body that connects a muscle to a bone.
sinewy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肌肉发达的;精壮的;强健的； sinewy Someone who is sinewy has a lean body with strong muscles.
sinful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不道德的;邪恶的； sinful sinfulness If you describe someone or something as sinful , you mean that they are wicked or immoral.
sing: 唱歌;演唱； sing When you sing , you make musical sounds with your voice, usually producing words that fit a tune.  /  (鸟类或昆虫)鸣叫，啼，啁啾，啼啭； sing When birds or insects sing , they make pleasant high-pitched sounds.  /  (尤指同一组织里的人)口径一致，意见一致； sing If you say that people, especially people in the same organization, are singing from the same hymn sheet or are singing from the same song sheet , you mean that they are saying the same things in public about something and appear to agree about it.  /  See also: singing ; to sing someone's praises » see: praise

single out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 单独挑出;特别选出； single out If you single someone out from a group, you choose them and give them special attention or treatment.

singular: [ADJ 形容词] 单数的;单数形式的； singular The singular form of a word is the form that is used when referring to one person or thing.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (名词的)单数，单数形式； singular The singular of a noun is the form of it that is used to refer to one person or thing.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 非凡的;突出的;显著的； singular singularly Singular means very great and remarkable.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 异常的;奇特的;奇怪的； singular singularity If you describe someone or something as singular , you mean that they are strange or unusual.

sinister: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 邪恶的;有害的;不祥的； sinister Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.
sink: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (厨房里的)洗涤池，洗碗槽，水槽； sink A sink is a large fixed container in a kitchen, with taps to supply water.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 washbasin 或 basin； sink A sink is the same as a washbasin or basin .  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使下沉;使沉没； sink sinking If a boat sinks or if someone or something sinks it, it disappears below the surface of a mass of water.  /  [VERB 动词] 下沉;沉没； sink If something sinks , it disappears below the surface of a mass of water.
sinker: [PHRASE 短语] 完全地;毫无保留地； sinker You can use hook, line, and sinker to emphasize that someone is tricked or forced into a situation completely.

sinus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鼻窦； sinus Your sinuses are the spaces in the bone behind your nose.

sleep: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 睡眠;睡觉； sleep Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind does not think.  /  [VERB 动词] 睡觉;睡着;入睡； sleep When you sleep , you rest with your eyes closed and your mind and body inactive.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一段睡眠时间;一觉； sleep A sleep is a period of sleeping.  /  [VERB 动词] (大楼、房间等)可供(若干人)住宿，睡得下(若干人)； sleep If a building or room sleeps a particular number of people, it has beds for that number of people.
sleep around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 到处与人上床;滥交； sleep around If you say that someone sleeps around , you disapprove of them because they have sex with a lot of different people.

sleeping: [ADJ 形容词] 同住宿有关的;睡觉的； sleeping See also: sleep ; You use sleeping to describe places where people sleep or things concerned with where people sleep.
sleeping bag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 睡袋； A sleeping bag is a large deep bag with a warm lining, used for sleeping in, especially when you are camping.
sleeping car: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (火车的)卧铺车厢； A sleeping car is a railway carriage containing beds for passengers to sleep in at night.
sleeping giant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沉睡中的巨人(指力量巨大但没有充分展示其威力的人)； sleeping giant If you refer to someone or something as a sleeping giant , you mean that they are powerful but they have not yet shown the full extent of their power.
sleeping partner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不参与实际经营的合伙人;匿名合伙人； A sleeping partner is a person who provides some of the capital for a business but who does not take an active part in managing the business.
sleeping pill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 安眠药； A sleeping pill is a pill that you can take to help you sleep.
sleeping sickness: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 昏睡病； Sleeping sickness is a serious tropical disease which causes great tiredness and often leads to death.
sleeping tablet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 sleeping pill； A sleeping tablet is the same as a sleeping pill .
sleepless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不睡觉的;不眠的； sleepless A sleepless night is one during which you do not sleep.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 睡不着的;失眠的； sleepless sleeplessness Someone who is sleepless is unable to sleep.
sleep off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 用睡眠消除(旅途劳顿、暴饮暴食等行为所引起的反应)； If you sleep off the effects of too much travelling, drink, or food, you recover from it by sleeping.
sleep over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指小孩)不在家过夜,在外过夜； sleep over If someone, especially a child, sleeps over in a place such as a friend's home, they stay there for one night.
sleepover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 在外过夜;不在家过夜； A sleepover is an occasion when someone, especially a child, sleeps for one night in a place such as a friend's home.
sleep through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 未被…搅醒;在…中沉睡不醒； sleep through If you sleep through something, it does not wake you up.
sleep together: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通常指尚未结婚的两个人)发生性关系； If two people are sleeping together , they are having a sexual relationship, but are not usually married to each other.
sleepwalk: [VERB 动词] 梦游； sleepwalk sleepwalker If someone is sleepwalking , they are walking around while they are asleep.
sleep with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 与…性交;与…上床； sleep with If you sleep with someone, you have sex with them.
sleepy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 困的;瞌睡的； sleepy sleepily sleepiness If you are sleepy , you are very tired and are almost asleep.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 寂静的;死气沉沉的； sleepy A sleepy place is quiet and does not have much activity or excitement.
sleet: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 雨夹雪;雨夹雹;冻雨； sleet Sleet is rain that is partly frozen.
sleeve: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 袖子； sleeve The sleeves of a coat, shirt, or other item of clothing are the parts that cover your arms.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (唱片)封套； sleeve A record sleeve is the stiff envelope in which a record is kept.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 流露自己的感情;把喜怒挂在脸上； If someone wears their heart on their sleeve , they behave in a way that makes their feelings very obvious, for example when they are in love with someone.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 藏有…想法;留有锦囊妙计;心中另有…高招； sleeve If you have something up your sleeve , you have an idea or plan which you have not told anyone about.
-sleeved: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] (加在 long，short 等形容词之后)表示“有…袖子的”； -sleeved -sleeved is added to adjectives such as 'long' and 'short' to form adjectives which indicate that an item of clothing has long or short sleeves.
sleeveless: [ADJ 形容词] 无袖的； sleeveless A sleeveless dress, top, or other item of clothing has no sleeves.
sleeve note: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 唱片套上的文字说明； The sleeve notes are short pieces of writing on the covers of records, which tell you something about the music or the musicians.
sleigh: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪橇； A sleigh is a vehicle which can slide over snow.
sleight of hand: [N-VAR 可变名词] (偷东西或变戏法时)敏捷而熟练的手法;空空妙手； sleight of hand Sleight of hand is the deceiving of someone in a skilful way.
slender: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 苗条的;纤细的;修长的； slender A slender person is attractively thin and graceful.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 微弱的;薄弱的;不足的;不充分的； slender You can use slender to describe a situation which exists but only to a very small degree.

slew: + + + Slew is the past tense of slay .  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(车辆失控)滑行,使侧滑； slew If a vehicle slews or is slewed across a road, it slides across it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 许多;大量； slew A slew of things is a large number of them.

sliced: [ADJ 形容词] (面包)已切成片的； sliced Sliced bread has been cut into slices before being wrapped and sold.
slick: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 技法娴熟的;灵巧的;巧妙的； slick slickly slickness A slick performance, production, or advertisement is skilful and impressive.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 利索的;流畅的;不费力的； slick A slick action is done quickly and smoothly, and without any obvious effort.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人油嘴滑舌的，巧舌如簧的； slick slickness A slick person speaks easily in a way that is likely to convince people, but is not sincere.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 oil slick； slick A slick is the same as an oil slick .
slicker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (长且大的)油布雨衣，雨衣； A slicker is a long loose waterproof coat.  /  See also: slick ; �
slide: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 滑动;溜； When something slides somewhere or when you slide it there, it moves there smoothly over or against something.  /  [VERB 动词] 麻利而无声地移动;悄悄地溜到； If you slide somewhere, you move there smoothly and quietly.  /  [VERB 动词] 不自觉地陷入(某种情绪、态度或情境)； To slide into a particular mood, attitude, or situation means to gradually start to have that mood, attitude, or situation often without intending to.  /  [VERB 动词] (货币)贬值;(物价)下跌； slide If currencies or prices slide , they gradually become worse or lower in value.
slide rule: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 计算尺;滑尺； A slide rule is an instrument that you use for calculating numbers.
sliding door: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑门;推拉门； Sliding doors are doors which slide together rather than swinging on hinges.
sliding scale: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (工资、税率等按情况变化而调整的)滑准计算法，浮动制； sliding scale Payments such as wages or taxes that are calculated on a sliding scale are higher or lower depending on various different factors.
slight: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻微的;少量的;小的； slight Something that is slight is very small in degree or quantity.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人瘦弱的，瘦小的； slight slightly A slight person has a fairly thin and delicate looking body.  /  [VERB 动词] 不理睬;藐视;轻蔑;冷落； slight slighting If you are slighted , someone does or says something that insults you by treating you as if your views or feelings are not important.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (用于加强陈述的否定语气)一点也不； slight You use in the slightest to emphasize a negative statement.
slightly: [ADV 副词] 略微;稍微； slightly Slightly means to some degree but not to a very large degree.
slim: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 苗条的;纤细的;修长的； slim A slim person has an attractively thin and well-shaped body.  /  [VERB 动词] (通过节食)减肥，变苗条； slim slim down 同 slim slimmer slimming If you are slimming , you are trying to make yourself thinner and lighter by eating less food.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (书、钱包等)薄的； slim A slim book, wallet, or other object is thinner than usual.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (可能性)不大的，微乎其微的； slim A slim chance or possibility is a very small one.
slim down: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 精简(机构);裁减(人员)； slim down If a company or other organization slims down or is slimmed down , it employs fewer people, in order to save money or become more efficient.  /  »see: slim 2 ; �
slime: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 黏滑的污垢;烂泥； slime Slime is a thick, wet substance which covers a surface or comes from the bodies of animals such as snails.
slimline: [ADJ 形容词] 瘦长的;细长的； slimline Slimline objects are thinner or narrower than normal ones.
slimy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 泥泞的;黏糊糊的;黏滑的； slimy Slimy substances are thick, wet, and unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 假意奉承的;口蜜腹剑的;滑头的;卑鄙的； slimy If you describe someone as slimy , you dislike them because they are friendly and pleasant in an insincere way.
sling: [VERB 动词] 摔;扔;投;掷； sling If you sling something somewhere, you throw it there carelessly.  /  [VERB 动词] (往肩膀上)挎;搭(在椅背上)； If you sling something over your shoulder or over something such as a chair, you hang it there loosely.  /  [VERB 动词] (在两点之间)吊起，悬挂； If a rope, blanket, or other object is slung between two points, someone has hung it loosely between them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (用以吊运物品的)吊索，吊链； sling A sling is an object made of ropes, straps, or cloth that is used for carrying things.
slingshot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 弹弓； A slingshot is a catapult .
slink: [VERB 动词] 偷偷摸摸地走;悄悄走;溜走； slink If you slink somewhere, you move there quietly because you do not want to be seen.
slinky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (女服)紧身的，性感的； slinky Slinky clothes fit very closely to a woman's body in a way that makes her look sexually attractive.
slip: [VERB 动词] 滑;滑倒； slip If you slip , you accidentally slide and lose your balance.  /  [VERB 动词] 滑落;脱落； slip If something slips , it slides out of place or out of your hand.  /  [VERB 动词] 迅速而悄无声息地走(到某处);溜(到某处)； slip If you slip somewhere, you go there quickly and quietly.  /  [VERB 动词] 迅速而不被注意地放置;偷偷塞进； slip If you slip something somewhere, you put it there quickly in a way that does not attract attention.

slipper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拖鞋； Slippers are loose, soft shoes that you wear at home.
slippery: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 滑溜溜的;滑的； slippery Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 滑头的;靠不住的;狡猾的； slippery You can describe someone as slippery if you think that they are dishonest in a clever way and cannot be trusted.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 滑向深渊的道路； slippery If someone is on a slippery slope , they are involved in a course of action that is difficult to stop and that will eventually lead to failure or trouble.

slip through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 蒙混过关； slip through If something slips through a set of checks or rules, it is accepted when in fact it should not be.
slip up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 出现疏漏;出小差错； See also: slip-up ; If you slip up , you make a small or unimportant mistake.
slip-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻微的过错;疏漏； slip-up A slip-up is a small or unimportant mistake.
slipway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 船台(船只下水用的滑道)； A slipway is a large platform that slopes down into the sea, from which boats are put into the water.

slithery: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 滑溜的； slithery Something that is slithery is wet or smooth, and so slides easily over things or is easy to slip on.

slob: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 邋遢的懒人； slob If you call someone a slob , you mean that they are very lazy and untidy.
slobber: [VERB 动词] 流口水； slobber If a person or an animal slobbers , they let liquid fall from their mouth.
sloe: [N-VAR 可变名词] 黑刺李，野梅(常用作杜松子酒调味剂)； A sloe is a small, sour fruit that has a dark purple skin.

sloop: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 单桅小帆船； A sloop is a small sailing boat with one mast.
slop: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使溢出;使溅出;使泼出； slop If liquid slops from a container or if you slop liquid somewhere, it comes out over the edge of the container, usually accidentally.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 残羹剩饭;泔脚； slop You can use slop or slops to refer to liquid waste containing the remains of food.

sneaky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 秘密的;鬼祟的;偷偷摸摸的； sneaky If you describe someone as sneaky , you disapprove of them because they do things secretly rather than openly.
sneer: [VERB 动词] 讥笑;嘲笑;讥讽； sneer If you sneer at someone or something, you express your contempt for them by the expression on your face or by what you say.
sneeringly: [ADV-GRADED 副词] 讽刺地;讥笑地； sneeringly To refer sneeringly to someone or something means to refer to them in a way that shows your contempt for them.
sneeze: [VERB 动词] 打喷嚏； sneeze When you sneeze , you suddenly take in your breath and then blow it down your nose noisily without being able to stop yourself, for example because you have a cold.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不容忽视;值得拥有； sneeze If you say that something is not to be sneezed at , you mean that it is worth having.
snicker: [VERB 动词] 窃笑;暗笑； snicker If you snicker , you laugh quietly in a disrespectful way, for example at something rude or embarrassing.
snide: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 刻毒的;讽刺的;恶意的； snide snidely A snide comment or remark is one which criticizes someone in an unkind and often indirect way.
sniff: [VERB 动词] (忍住不哭或表示不赞成时)抽鼻子； sniff When you sniff , you breathe in air through your nose hard enough to make a sound, for example when you are trying not to cry, or in order to show disapproval.  /  [VERB 动词] 闻;嗅； sniff If you sniff something or sniff at it, you smell it by sniffing.  /  [VERB 动词] 嗤之以鼻地表示;轻蔑地说； sniff You can use sniff to indicate that someone says something in a way that shows their disapproval or contempt.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻视;蔑视； sniff If you say that something is not to be sniffed at , you think it is very good or worth having.
sniff around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 打探情况;刺探消息； sniff around If a person is sniffing around , they are trying to find out information about something, especially information that someone else does not want known.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 试图抢走(心上人);企图挖走(员工、顾客等)； If a person or organization is sniffing around someone, they are trying to get them, for example as a lover, employee, or client.

sniffle: [VERB 动词] (哭泣或感冒时)不断抽鼻子； sniffle If you sniffle , you keep sniffing, usually because you are crying or have a cold.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻微感冒； A sniffle is a slight cold.
sniff out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 发现;找到； sniff out If you sniff out something, you discover it after some searching.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 狗嗅找(炸药、毒品等)； sniff out When a dog used by a group such as the police sniffs out hidden explosives or drugs, it finds them using its sense of smell.
sniffy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 轻蔑的;鄙夷的； sniffy sniffily Someone who is sniffy about something does not think it is of high quality, perhaps unfairly.
snifter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 少量烈酒； A snifter is a small amount of an alcoholic drink.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (盛白兰地用的)小口大肚酒杯； A snifter is a bowl-shaped glass used for drinking brandy.
snigger: [VERB 动词] 暗笑;窃笑； snigger If someone sniggers , they laugh quietly in a disrespectful way, for example at something rude or unkind.
snip: [VERB 动词] 剪;剪下;剪断； snip If you snip something, or if you snip at or through something, you cut it quickly using sharp scissors.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 货真价实之物;物美价廉的物品； snip If you say that something is a snip , you mean that it is very good value.
snipe: [VERB 动词] 批评;攻击;中伤； sniping If someone snipes at you, they criticize you.  /  [VERB 动词] 狙击;放冷枪； snipe To snipe at someone means to shoot at them from a hidden position.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鹬;沙锥； A snipe is a type of bird with a very long beak which lives in wet areas of land.
sniper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 狙击手； A sniper is someone who shoots at people from a hidden position.
snippet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小片;小部分;零星片段； snippet A snippet of something is a small piece of it.
snitch: [VERB 动词] (向当权者)告发，告密； snitch To snitch on a person means to tell someone in authority that the person has done something bad or wrong.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 告密者;告发者； A snitch is a person who snitches on other people.  /  [VERB 动词] 偷窃； snitch If you snitch something, you steal it quickly and quietly.
snivel: [VERB 动词] (令人讨厌地)啜泣，抽抽噎噎地哭，抽鼻子； snivel If someone is snivelling , they are crying or sniffing in a way that irritates you.
snob: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 势利小人； snob If you call someone a snob , you disapprove of them because they admire upper-class people and have a low opinion of lower-class people.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 自以为(在智力或品位方面)高人一等的人； snob If you call someone a snob , you disapprove of them because they behave as if they are superior to other people because of their intelligence or taste.
snobbery: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 势利态度;势利眼； Snobbery is the attitude of a snob.
snobbish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (对自身社会地位、才智、品位等)过分自傲的，势利的； snobbish snobbishness If you describe someone as snobbish , you disapprove of them because they are too proud of their social status, intelligence, or taste.
snobby: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 同 snobbish； Snobby means the same as snobbish .
snog: [V-RECIP 相互动词] (长时间地)拥抱接吻； snog If one person snogs another, they kiss and hold that person for a period of time.
snook: [PHRASE 短语] 对(权威或机构)进行侮辱(或表示轻蔑)； snook If you cock a snook at someone in authority or at an organization, you do something that they cannot punish you for, but which insults them or expresses your contempt.
snooker: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 斯诺克； snooker Snooker is a game involving balls on a large table.  /  [VERB 动词] 阻止…采取行动;使…不如愿； snooker If you are snookered by something, it is difficult or impossible for you to take action or do what you want to do.
snoop: [VERB 动词] 窥探;刺探;打探； snoop snooper If someone snoops around a place, they secretly look around it in order to find out things.  /  [VERB 动词] 窥探(某人的生活)； snoop snooper If someone snoops on a person, they watch them secretly in order to find out things about their life.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 snooper； snoop A snoop is the same as a snooper .
snooty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 傲慢自大的;自以为高人一等的； snooty If you say that someone is snooty , you disapprove of them because they behave as if they are superior to other people.
snooze: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指在白天的)小睡，打盹儿； A snooze is a short, light sleep, especially during the day.  /  [VERB 动词] 小睡;打盹儿； snooze If you snooze , you sleep lightly for a short period of time.
snore: [VERB 动词] 打鼾;打呼噜； snore When someone who is asleep snores , they make a loud noise each time they breathe.
snorkel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (潜水者使用的)通气管，水下呼吸管； A snorkel is a tube through which a person swimming just under the surface of the sea can breathe.  /  [VERB 动词] 用通气管潜泳； snorkel When someone snorkels , they swim under water using a snorkel.
snort: [VERB 动词] (人或牲畜)喷鼻息;(人表示不赞成、可笑等)哼鼻子，嗤之以鼻； snort When people or animals snort , they breathe air noisily out through their noses.  /  [VERB 动词] (表示轻蔑)哼着鼻子说； snort If someone snorts something, they say it in a way that shows contempt.  /  [VERB 动词] 吸食(毒品)； snort To snort a drug such as cocaine means to breathe it in quickly through your nose.
snot: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 鼻涕； Snot is the substance that is produced inside your nose.
snotty: [ADJ 形容词] 流着鼻涕的;满是鼻涕的； snotty Something that is snotty produces or is covered in snot.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 傲慢自大的;自以为高人一等的； snotty If you describe someone as snotty , you disapprove of them because they have a very proud and superior attitude to other people.
snout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (猪等的)长鼻，口鼻部； snout The snout of an animal such as a pig is its long nose.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 口吻状物(如车头、枪管等)； snout Writers sometimes refer to the front of a car or the barrel of a gun as its snout .
snow: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 雪； snow Snow consists of a lot of soft white bits of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 降雪;雪季； snow You can refer to a great deal of snow in an area as the snows .  /  [VERB 动词] 下雪； snow When it snows , snow falls from the sky.  /  [VERB 动词] 用花言巧语鼓动(或迷惑)； snow If someone snows you, they persuade you to do something or convince you of something by flattering or deceiving you.
snowball: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪球； A snowball is a ball of snow.  /  [VERB 动词] (项目、运动等)迅速增长，滚雪球般增长； snowball If something such as a project or campaign snowballs , it rapidly increases and grows.
snowboard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滑雪板； A snowboard is a narrow board that you stand on in order to slide quickly down snowy slopes as a sport or for fun.
snowboarding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 滑雪板运动； snowboarding snowboarder Snowboarding is the sport or activity of travelling down snowy slopes using a snowboard.
snowbound: [ADJ 形容词] (人或车)被大雪困住的，因大雪而受阻的； snowbound If people or vehicles are snowbound , they cannot go anywhere because of heavy snow.
snow-capped: [ADJ 形容词] 山顶积雪的； snow-capped A snow-capped mountain is covered with snow at the top.
snow-covered: [ADJ 形容词] 被雪覆盖的； snow-covered Snow-covered places and things are covered over with snow.
snowdrift: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (被风吹聚成的)雪堆； A snowdrift is a deep pile of snow formed by the wind.

snowed under: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (因工作或事情多而)穷于应付的，忙得不可开交的； snowed under If you say that you are snowed under , you are emphasizing that you have a lot of work or other things to deal with.
snowfall: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 降雪量； snowfall The snowfall in an area or country is the amount of snow that falls there during a particular period.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (一场)降雪； A snowfall is a fall of snow.
snowfield: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪地;雪原； A snowfield is a large area which is always covered in snow.
snowflake: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪花； A snowflake is one of the soft, white bits of frozen water that fall as snow.
snowman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪人； A snowman is a large shape which is made out of snow, especially by children, and is supposed to look like a person.
snowmobile: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 摩托雪橇;雪地机动车； A snowmobile is a small vehicle built to move across snow and ice.
snow pea: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 糖荚豌豆； Snow peas are a type of pea whose pods are eaten as well as the peas inside them.
snowplough: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪犁;扫雪机； A snowplough is a vehicle which is used to push snow off roads or railway lines.
snowshoe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雪鞋； Snowshoes are oval frames which have a strong net stretched across them and which you fasten to your feet so that you can walk on deep snow.
snowstorm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 暴风雪； A snowstorm is a very heavy fall of snow, usually when there is also a strong wind blowing at the same time.
snow-white: [ADJ 形容词] 雪白的； Something that is snow-white is of a bright white colour.
snowy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 积雪覆盖的;大雪纷飞的； snowy A snowy place is covered in snow.
Snr: 老，大(置于人名之后，用以与家族中较年轻的同名成员相区别)； Snr Snr is the written abbreviation for (书面缩略=) Senior .
snub: [VERB 动词] 冷落;怠慢;不理睬； snub If you snub someone, you deliberately insult them by ignoring them or by behaving or speaking rudely towards them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 冷落;怠慢； snub If you snub someone, your behaviour or your remarks can be referred to as a snub .  /  [ADJ 形容词] (鼻子)短而略向上翘的； Someone who has a snub nose has a short nose which points slightly upwards.
snuck: (美国英语中 sneak 的过去式和过去分词之一)； Snuck is a past tense and past participle of sneak in American English.
snuff: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 鼻烟； Snuff is powdered tobacco which people take by breathing it in quickly through their nose.  /  [VERB 动词] 断气;死去； snuff If someone snuffs it , they die.  /  相关词组： snuff out �
snuffle: [VERB 动词] (因伤风等)抽鼻子； snuffle If a person or an animal snuffles , they breathe in noisily through their nose, for example because they have a cold.

snug: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指寒冷天气中)暖烘烘的，温暖舒适的； snug snugly If you feel snug or are in a snug place, you are very warm and comfortable, especially because you are protected from cold weather.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服等)紧身的，贴身的； snug snugly Something such as a piece of clothing that is snug fits very closely or tightly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 酒馆内的雅间； A snug is a small room in a pub.

so: [ADV 副词] 如此，这样(指已经提到的事)； so You use so to refer back to something that has just been mentioned.  /  [ADV 副词] 同样，也一样(指后者跟前者一样)； so You use so when you are saying that something which has just been said about one person or thing is also true of another one.  /  [CONJ-COORD 连词] (表示两个事件或情况在某方面相似)正如…，也…； so You use the structures as.  /  [ADV 副词] (指某一情况)就是这样，事实如此； so If you say that a state of affairs is so , you mean that it is the way it has been described.
soak: [VERB 动词] 浸;泡； soak If you soak something or leave it to soak , you put it into a liquid and leave it there.  /  [VERB 动词] 使湿透;浸湿； soak If a liquid soaks something or if you soak something with a liquid, the liquid makes the thing very wet.  /  [VERB 动词] 渗透； soak If a liquid soaks through something, it passes through it.  /  [VERB 动词] (长时间地)泡热水澡； soak If someone soaks , they spend a long time in a hot bath, because they enjoy it.

soaked: [ADJ 形容词] 湿透的;浸透的； soaked If someone or something gets soaked or soaked through , water or some other liquid makes them extremely wet.
soaking: [ADJ 形容词] 湿透的;湿淋淋的； soaking If something is soaking or soaking wet , it is very wet.

so-and-so: [PRON-SING 单数型代词] (泛指)某某人，某某事； so-and-so You use so-and-so instead of a word, expression, or name when you are talking generally rather than giving a specific example of a particular thing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 讨厌鬼，笨蛋(用以代替脏字眼)； so-and-so People sometimes refer to another person as a so-and-so when they are annoyed with them or think that they are foolish.
soap: [N-MASS 物质名词] 肥皂； soap Soap is a substance that you use with water for washing yourself or sometimes for washing clothes.  /  [VERB 动词] 用肥皂擦洗;往…上面抹肥皂； soap If you soap yourself , you rub soap on your body in order to wash yourself.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 soap opera； A soap is the same as a soap opera .
soapbox: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (作户外演讲时用的)临时小讲台； soapbox A soapbox is a small temporary platform on which a person stands when he or she is making a speech outdoors.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (针对某事自己有强烈看法的)演讲，发表意见，书写感受； soapbox If you say that someone is on their soapbox , you mean that they are speaking or writing about something they have strong feelings about.
soap opera: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 肥皂剧； A soap opera is a popular television drama series about the daily lives and problems of a group of people who live in a particular place.
soapy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 满是肥皂泡的;涂满肥皂的； soapy Something that is soapy is full of soap or covered with soap.
soar: [VERB 动词] (数量、价值、水平、规模等)急升，猛涨； soar If the amount, value, level, or volume of something soars , it quickly increases by a great deal.  /  [VERB 动词] (鸟等)高飞，翱翔，升腾； soar If something such as a bird soars into the air, it goes quickly up into the air.  /  [VERB 动词] (树木、建筑等)高耸，屹立； soar Trees or buildings that soar upwards are very tall.  /  [VERB 动词] (音乐)音量猛地增大，音调陡然升高； soar If music soars , it rises greatly in volume or pitch.
soaraway: [ADJ 形容词] 腾飞的;进展神速的； soaraway If you describe something as a soaraway success, you mean that its success has suddenly increased.
sob: [VERB 动词] 抽噎;呜咽;啜泣； sob sobbing When someone sobs , they cry in a noisy way, breathing in short breaths.  /  [VERB 动词] 呜咽着说;哭诉； sob If you sob something, you say it while you are crying.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 呜咽声； A sob is one of the noises that you make when you are crying.

spigot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 龙头;开关； A spigot is a faucet or tap.
spike: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 金属钉状物;尖锥;尖钉； spike A spike is a long piece of metal with a sharp point.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 细长的尖状物； spike Any long pointed object can be referred to as a spike .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (价格、数量的)突然上升，剧增； spike If there is a spike in the price, volume, or amount of something, the price, volume, or amount of it suddenly increases.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (跑步运动员穿的)钉鞋，跑鞋； Spikes are a pair of sports shoes with pointed pieces of metal attached to the soles.
spiked: [ADJ 形容词] 有尖顶的；装有尖钉的； spiked Something that is spiked has one or more spikes on it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (头发)短而竖立的； If someone has spiked hair, their hair is short and sticks up all over their head.  /  See also: spike ; �
spike heels: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 细高跟鞋； Spike heels are women's shoes with very high narrow heels.
spiky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有尖顶的；成锥形的； spiky Something that is spiky has one or more sharp points.
spill: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使溢出;使泼出;使洒出； spill If a liquid spills or if you spill it, it accidentally flows over the edge of a container.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 溢出量;溢出物； spill A spill is an amount of liquid that has spilled from a container.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(袋子、盒子等中盛放的东西)洒出，涌出； spill If the contents of a bag, box, or other container spill or are spilled , they come out of the container onto a surface.  /  [VERB 动词] 蜂拥而出； spill If people or things spill out of a place, they come out of it in large numbers.
spillage: [N-VAR 可变名词] 溢出;溢出物； spillage If there is a spillage , a substance such as oil escapes from its container.
spill out: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 泄露;泄密； spill out If you spill out information or if it spills out , you tell someone about it in a hurried way, because you cannot or do not want to keep it secret.
spillover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 伴随的结果(或影响)； spillover A spillover is a situation or feeling that starts in one place but then begins to happen or have an effect somewhere else.
spilt: Spilt is a past tense and past participle form of spill .
spin: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使旋转； spin If something spins or if you spin it, it turns quickly around a central point.  /  [VERB 动词] (用甩干机或洗衣机)甩干衣服，给…脱水； spin When you spin washing, it is turned round and round quickly in a spin drier or a washing machine to get the water out.  /  [VERB 动词] (因醉酒、生病或兴奋而)头晕； spin If your head is spinning , you feel unsteady or confused, for example because you are drunk, ill, or excited.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 带倾向性的解释(或说法)； spin See also: spin doctor ; If someone puts a certain spin on an event or situation, they interpret it and try to present it in a particular way.
spina bifida: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 先天性脊椎裂(常引起瘫痪)； Spina bifida is a condition of the spine that some people are born with.
spinach: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 菠菜； Spinach is a vegetable with large dark green leaves that you chop up and boil in water before eating.
spinal: [ADJ 形容词] 脊椎的； spinal Spinal means relating to your spine.
spinal column: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脊椎;脊柱； Your spinal column is your spine.
spinal cord: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脊髓； Your spinal cord is a thick cord of nerves inside your spine which connects your brain to nerves in all parts of your body.
spindle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (机器的)轴，心轴； A spindle is a rod in a machine, around which another part of the machine turns.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (手纺用的)绕线杆； A spindle is a pointed rod which you use when you are spinning wool by hand.
spindly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 细长而瘦弱的;瘦长的； spindly Something that is spindly is long and thin and looks very weak.
spin doctor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (善于公关、为政党出谋划策的)媒体顾问，舆论导向专家； In politics, a spin doctor is someone who is skilled in public relations and who advises political parties on how to present their policies and actions.
spine: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脊椎;脊柱； Your spine is the row of bones down your back.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 书脊； The spine of a book is the narrow stiff part which the pages and covers are attached to.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (动物身体上的)棘状突起;(植物上的)棘，刺，针； Spines are also long, sharp points on an animal's body or on a plant.
spine-chilling: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 非常可怖的;令人毛骨悚然的； A spine-chilling film or story makes you feel very frightened.
spineless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 没有骨气的;懦弱的； spineless If you say that someone is spineless , you mean that they are afraid to take action or oppose people when they should.
spine-tingling: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (电影或音乐)激动人心的，扣人心弦的； spine-tingling A spine-tingling film or piece of music is enjoyable because it causes you to feel a strong emotion such as excitement or fear.
spinnaker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (帆船前桅上的)大三角帆； A spinnaker is a large, light, triangular sail that is attached to the front mast of a boat.
spinner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 投旋转球的板球投手； A spinner is a cricketer who makes the ball spin when he or she bowls it so that it changes direction when it hits the ground or the bat.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纺纱者;纺纱工； A spinner is a person who makes thread by spinning.
spinney: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小树林； A spinney is a small area covered with trees.
spinning wheel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (旧时家用的)纺车； A spinning wheel is a wooden machine that people used in their homes to make thread from wool, in former times.
spin-off: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 副产品;派生产品； spin-off A spin-off is an unexpected but useful or valuable result of an activity that was designed to achieve something else.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (受欢迎的书籍、电影、电视连续剧等的)派生产品； A spin-off is a book, film, or television series that comes after and is related to a successful book, film, or television series.
spin out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拖长;拉长； spin out If you spin something out , you make it last longer than it normally would.  /  See also: spin off ; �
spinster: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 老处女;未婚中年(或老年)女子； A spinster is a woman who has never been married; used especially when talking about an old or middle-aged woman.
spiny: [ADJ 形容词] (动植物)带刺的； spiny A spiny plant or animal is covered with long sharp points.
spiral: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 螺旋形； spiral A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使盘旋着生长(或移动)； spiral If something spirals or is spiralled somewhere, it grows or moves in a spiral curve.  /  [VERB 动词] (数量、水平)急遽增长； spiral If an amount or level spirals , it rises quickly and at an increasing rate.  /  [VERB 动词] (数量、水平)急遽变化； spiral If an amount or level spirals downwards, it falls quickly and at an increasing rate.
spire: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (教堂等建筑物顶部的)尖塔，尖顶； The spire of a building such as a church is the tall pointed structure on the top.
spirit: [N-SING 单数名词] 精神;心灵； spirit See also: kindred spirit ; Your spirit is the part of you that is not physical and that consists of your character and feelings.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灵魂； spirit A person's spirit is the non-physical part of them that is believed to remain alive after their death.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鬼魂;幽灵； spirit See also: Holy Spirit ; A spirit is a ghost or supernatural being.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 勇气;意志； spirit Spirit is the courage and determination that helps people to survive in difficult times and to keep their way of life and their beliefs.
-spirited: [COMB in ADJ-GRADED ] (与形容词连用)表示“性格…的”，“有…精神的”； -spirited See also: high-spirited ; public-spirited ; -spirited combines with adjectives to describe a person's character, attitude, or behaviour.
spirited: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行动)坚决有力的，激烈的，猛烈的； spirited spiritedly A spirited action shows great energy and courage.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人活泼的，生气勃勃的，自信的； spirited A spirited person is very active, lively, and confident.
spiritless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 没精打采的;垂头丧气的； spiritless If someone is spiritless , they lack energy, courage, and liveliness.
spirit level: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (气泡)水准仪； A spirit level is a device for testing to see if a surface is level.
spiritual: [ADJ 形容词] 精神上的;心灵上的； spiritual spiritually spirituality Spiritual means relating to people's thoughts and beliefs, rather than to their bodies and physical surroundings.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 宗教上的；宗教信仰上的； spiritual Spiritual means relating to people's religious beliefs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 灵歌(原为美国黑奴所唱的一种宗教歌曲)； A spiritual is a religious song of the type originally sung by black slaves in America.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 精神家园;精神故乡； Your spiritual home is the place where you feel that you belong, usually because your ideas or attitudes are the same as those of the people who live there.
spiritualism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 招魂论，通灵术(相信死人的灵魂能与活人相沟通)； spiritualist Spiritualism is the belief that the spirits of people who are dead can communicate with people who are still alive.
spit: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 唾液，唾沫(常指唾沫星子)； Spit is the watery liquid produced in your mouth.  /  [VERB 动词] 吐唾沫(常表示憎恨或轻蔑)； spit If someone spits , they force an amount of liquid out of their mouth, often to show hatred or contempt.  /  [VERB 动词] 吐出(少量液体或食物)； spit If you spit liquid or food somewhere, you force a small amount of it out of your mouth.  /  [VERB 动词] (机器) 噼啪作响;(煮着的食物)毕剥作响； spit If something such as a machine or food that is cooking spits , it sends out small amounts of something, making a series of short, sharp noises.
spite: [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 尽管;不顾;虽然； spite You use in spite of to introduce a fact which makes the rest of the statement you are making seem surprising.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 不由自主地;不禁； spite If you do something in spite of yourself , you do it although you did not really intend to or expect to.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恶意;怨恨； spite If you do something cruel out of spite , you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.  /  [VERB 动词] (故意做坏事来)伤害，激怒； spite If you do something cruel to spite someone, you do it in order to hurt or upset them.
spiteful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 怀有恶意的;怀恨在心的； spiteful spitefully Someone who is spiteful does cruel things to hurt people they dislike.
spittle: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 唾液;唾沫； Spittle is the watery liquid which is produced in your mouth.
spiv: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (无固定职业而)靠诈骗过日子的人;黑市商人； A spiv is a man who does not have a regular job and who makes money by business deals which are usually illegal.
splash: [VERB 动词] 在水中嬉戏；戏水； splash If you splash about or splash around in water, you hit or disturb the water in a noisy way, causing some of it to fly up into the air.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使溅泼;使飞溅;使洒落； splash If you splash a liquid somewhere or if it splashes , it hits someone or something and scatters in a lot of small drops.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 溅泼声;扑通声； splash A splash is the sound made when something hits water or falls into it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 洒泼上去的一点儿;添加进去的少量； splash A splash of a liquid is a small quantity of it that falls on something or is added to something.
splashdown: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (宇宙飞船在海洋上的)溅落； A splashdown is the landing of a spacecraft in the sea after a flight.
splash out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 花大笔钱(买奢侈品)； splash out If you splash out on something, especially on a luxury, you buy it even though it costs a lot of money.
splat: [N-SING; SOUND 单数名词；声音词] (湿物落在平面上发出的)啪嗒声，溅泼声； splat Splat is used to describe the sound of something wet hitting a surface with a lot of force.
splatter: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 溅泼；洒落； splatter If a thick wet substance splatters on something or is splattered on it, it drops or is thrown over it.
splay: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(物体的多个末端)向外张开； splay If things splay or are splayed , their ends are spread out away from each other.
spleen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脾;脾脏； Your spleen is an organ near your stomach that controls the quality of your blood.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 大发脾气;大怒； spleen Spleen is great and bitter anger.
splendid: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极好的;绝妙的;出色的； splendid splendidly If you say that something is splendid , you mean that it is very good.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (建筑、艺术作品)壮丽的，华丽的，美妙的； splendid splendidly If you describe a building or work of art as splendid , you mean that it is beautiful, impressive, and extremely well made.  /  [EXCLAM 感叹语] 好极了(表示赞同)； You can say ' splendid ' in a conversation to indicate that you approve of a particular situation or something that someone has said.
splendour: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 壮丽辉煌;光彩夺目； splendour The splendour of something is its beautiful and impressive appearance.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 华丽;豪华;奢华； splendour The splendours of a place or way of life are its beautiful and impressive features.
splenetic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脾气坏的;易怒的； splenetic If you describe someone as splenetic , you mean that they easily become very angry about things.
splice: [VERB 动词] 绞接(绳子);粘接(胶片、磁带等)； splice If you splice two pieces of rope, film, or tape together, you join them neatly at the ends so that they make one continuous piece.  /  [V-PASSIVE 被动动词] 结婚； splice When two people get spliced , they get married.
spliff: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大麻烟卷； A spliff is a cigarette which contains cannabis or marijuana.
splint: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (治疗骨折用的)夹板； A splint is a long piece of wood or metal that is fastened to a broken arm, leg, or back to keep it still.
splinter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (木头、玻璃等硬物的)尖细碎片，破片，裂片； splinter A splinter is a very thin, sharp piece of wood, glass, or other hard substance, which has broken off from a larger piece.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使裂成碎片； splinter If something splinters or is splintered , it breaks into thin, sharp pieces.
splinter group: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (常因意见不合而从一团体中)分裂出来的小派别； A splinter group is a group of people who break away from a larger group and form a separate organization, usually because they no longer agree with the views of the larger group.
split: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使断裂;使裂开;分割； split If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(团体)意见不合；使分裂； split If an organization splits or is split , one group of members disagrees strongly with the other members, and may form a group of their own.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (团体中的)意见分歧； split A split in an organization is a disagreement between its members.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 区分；不同； split A split between two things is a division or difference between them.
split ends: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 发梢开叉； If you have split ends , some of your hairs are split at the ends because they are dry or damaged.
split infinitive: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分裂不定式(在 to 和动词不定式之间插有副词，有些人认为该用法不正确)； A split infinitive is a structure in which an adverb is put between 'to' and the infinitive of a verb, as in 'to really experience it'.
split-level: [ADJ 形容词] (房屋)错层式的； A split-level house or room has part of the ground floor at a different level from another part, usually because the house has been built on ground that slopes.
split off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (从团体中)分裂出去； split off If people split off from a group, they stop being part of the group and become separated from it.
split personality: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 分裂人格； If you say that someone has a split personality , you mean that their moods can change so much that they seem to have two separate personalities.
split-screen: [ADJ 形容词] 分画面的，分屏的(指屏幕左右两半同时放映两套不同电影或电视节目的技术)； split-screen Split-screen is used to describe the technique in making films and television programmes in which two different pieces of film are shown at the same time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (计算机上的)分屏，拆分窗口； On a computer screen, a split-screen is a display of two different things in separate parts of the screen.
split second: [N-SING 单数名词] 一刹那;一瞬间； split second A split second is an extremely short period of time.
splitting: [ADJ 形容词] (头痛)欲裂的； A splitting headache is a very severe and painful one.
split up: [PHRASAL VERB-RECIP-ERG ] 使分手;使离婚； split up If two people split up , or if someone or something splits them up , they end their relationship or marriage.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使分离;使分道扬镳； split up If a group of people split up or are split up , they go away in different directions.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 拆分;(把…)分成若干较小部分； split up If you split something up , or if it splits up , you divide it so that it is in a number of smaller separate sections.
splodge: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指某种液体的)大块污渍,大斑块； A splodge is a large uneven mark or stain, especially one that has been caused by a liquid.
splotch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指某种液体的)大块污渍，大斑块； A splotch is a large uneven mark or stain, especially one that has been caused by a liquid.
splurge: [VERB 动词] 挥霍； splurge If you splurge on something, you spend a lot of money, usually on things that you do not need.
splutter: [VERB 动词] (因窘迫或生气而)结结巴巴地说，语无伦次地说，气急败坏地说； splutter If someone splutters , they make short sounds and have difficulty speaking clearly, for example because they are embarrassed or angry.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出噼啪声； splutter If something splutters , it makes a series of short, sharp sounds.
spoil: [VERB 动词] 弄糟;损坏;破坏； spoil If you spoil something, you prevent it from being successful or satisfactory.  /  [VERB 动词] 溺爱，宠坏(孩子)； spoil spoilt, spoiled If you spoil children, you give them everything they want or ask for.  /  [VERB 动词] 犒赏自己或他人； spoil If you spoil yourself or spoil another person, you give yourself or them something nice as a treat or do something special for them.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(食物)变坏;使腐坏； spoil If food spoils or if it is spoilt , it is no longer fit to be eaten.
spoilage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (通常指食物)腐败，变质，变坏； When spoilage occurs, something, usually food, decays or is harmed, so that it is no longer fit to be used.
spoiler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 捣乱的人(或事物);搞破坏的人(或事物)； spoiler If you describe someone or something as a spoiler , you mean that they try to spoil the performance of other people or things.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (飞机的)扰流器;(汽车的)气流偏导器； A spoiler is an object which forms part of an aircraft's wings or part of the body of a car.
spoil for: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 渴望;切望； If you are spoiling for a fight, you are very eager for it to happen.
spoilsport: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 叫人扫兴的人;败兴者； If you say that someone is a spoilsport , you mean that they are behaving in a way that ruins other people's pleasure or enjoyment.
spoilt: + + + Spoilt is a past participle and past tense of spoil .
spoke: + + + Spoke is the past tense of speak .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (车轮的)辐条； The spokes of a wheel are the bars that connect the outer ring to the centre.
spoken: + + + Spoken is the past participle of speak .
-spoken: [COMB in ADJ-GRADED ] (与副词或形容词连用构成形容词)表示“以…方式说话的”； -spoken -spoken combines with adverbs and adjectives to form adjectives which indicate how someone speaks.
spoken word: [N-SING 单数名词] 口头说的话(相对书面语言或音乐而言)； spoken word The spoken word is used to refer to language expressed in speech, for example in contrast to written texts or music.
