storekeeper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 店主;商店经理； A storekeeper is a shopkeeper.
storeroom: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 贮藏室； storeroom A storeroom is a room in which you keep things until they are needed.
store up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 储备;囤积； If you store something up , you keep it until you think that the time is right to use it.
-storey: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] (用于数字后构成形容词)表示“有…层高的”； -storey See also: multi-storey ; -storey is used after numbers to form adjectives that indicate that a building has a particular number of floors or levels.
storey: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (楼房的)层，楼层； storey A storey of a building is one of its different levels, which is situated above or below other levels.
-storeyed: [COMB in ADJ 与形容词构成的词] 同 -storey； -storeyed -storeyed means the same as -storey .
stork: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鹳(一种长喙长腿的大鸟，通常生活在水边)； A stork is a large bird with a long beak and long legs, which lives near water.
storm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 暴风雨； storm A storm is very bad weather, with heavy rain, strong winds, and often thunder and lightning.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 强烈的反应;群情激愤;激动人心； storm If something causes a storm , it causes an angry or excited reaction from a large number of people.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (掌声等的)爆发，迸发； storm A storm of applause or other noise is a sudden loud amount of it made by an audience or other group of people in reaction to something.  /  [VERB 动词] 气冲冲地疾走;冲;闯； storm If you storm into or out of a place, you enter or leave it quickly and noisily, because you are angry.
storm cloud: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 暴风云； Storm clouds are the dark clouds which are seen before a storm.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 不祥的预兆;凶兆； storm cloud You can use storm clouds to refer to a sign that something very unpleasant is going to happen.
storm trooper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (纳粹军队的)冲锋队员，突击队员； Storm troopers were members of a private Nazi army who were well-known for being violent.
stormy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有暴风雨的； stormy If there is stormy weather, there are strong winds and heavy rain.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (大海)波涛汹涌的，波浪滔天的； stormy Stormy seas have very large strong waves because there are strong winds.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 争吵激烈的;群情激愤的； stormy If you describe a situation as stormy , you mean it involves a lot of angry argument or criticism.
story: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (虚构的)故事，小说； story A story is a description of imaginary people and events, which is written or told in order to entertain.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指口头的)叙述，描述； story A story is a description of an event or something that happened to someone, especially a spoken description of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 传记;史话;纪事； story The story of something is a description of all the important things that have happened to it since it began.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 谎言;假话;虚构之事； story If someone invents a story , they give a false explanation or account of something.
storyboard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (电影或广告等的)情节梗概系列图片，故事脚本； A storyboard is a set of pictures which show what will happen in something such as a film or advertisement that is being planned.
storybook: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 儿童故事书;童话书； storybook A storybook is a book of stories for children.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 童话般美好的;结局圆满的;皆大欢喜的； storybook A storybook relationship, situation, or life is one that is perfect and ends happily, just as many fairy stories do.
storyline: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (书、电影或戏剧的)故事情节； storyline The storyline of a book, film, or play is its story and the way in which it develops.
storyteller: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 讲故事的人;说书人;小说作家； storyteller A storyteller is someone who tells or writes stories.
storytelling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 讲故事;说书;写小说； storytelling Storytelling is the activity of telling or writing stories.
stout: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 肥胖的;肥壮的； stout A stout person is rather fat.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 结实的;厚实的;粗壮的； stout Stout shoes, branches, or other objects are thick and strong.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行动、态度或信念)坚定的，坚决的，强有力的； stout stoutly If you use stout to describe someone's actions, attitudes, or beliefs, you approve of them because they are strong and determined.  /  [N-MASS 物质名词] 烈性黑啤酒； stout Stout is a strong dark-coloured beer.
stove: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (取暖或做饭用的)炉子，火炉； stove A stove is a piece of equipment which provides heat, either for cooking or for heating a room.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 厨灶;炉头； A stove is the top of a cooker.
stow: [VERB 动词] 保存;妥善放置； stow If you stow something somewhere, you carefully put it there until it is needed.  /  相关词组： stow away �
stowage: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (船、飞机上的)装载空间； Stowage is the space that is available for stowing things on a ship or aeroplane.
stow away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (秘密地或无票)偷乘； If someone stows away , they hide in a ship, aeroplane, or other vehicle in order to make a journey secretly or without paying.
stowaway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无票偷乘者;偷渡者； stowaway A stowaway is a person who hides in a ship, aeroplane, or other vehicle in order to make a journey secretly or without paying.
straddle: [VERB 动词] 骑;跨坐;叉开双腿坐； If you straddle something, you put or have one leg on either side of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 横跨，跨越(河流、道路、边境等)； straddle If something straddles a river, road, border, or other place, it stretches across it or exists on both sides of it.  /  [VERB 动词] 横跨，跨越，同属(不同时期、群体或活动领域等)； straddle Someone or something that straddles different periods, groups, or fields of activity exists in, belongs to, or takes elements from them all.
strafe: [VERB 动词] (从低空)扫射，轰炸； strafe To strafe an enemy means to attack them with a lot of bombs or bullets from a low-flying aircraft.
straggle: [VERB 动词] 散乱地移动;零星地走； straggle If people straggle somewhere, they move there slowly, in small groups with large, irregular gaps between them.  /  [VERB 动词] 散乱地分布;散布； straggle If a small quantity of things straggle over an area, they cover it in an uneven or untidy way.
straggler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 掉队者;落伍者;拖后腿的人； straggler The stragglers are the people in a group who are moving more slowly or making less progress than the others.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某项活动中)留到最后的人； straggler The stragglers at an event such as a party are the people who are still there after most of the other people have left.
straggly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (头发)散乱的;(植物)蔓生的； straggly Straggly hair or a straggly plant is thin and grows or spreads out untidily in different directions.
straight: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 直的;笔直的； straight A straight line or edge continues in the same direction and does not bend or curve.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (头发)直的，不卷曲的； straight Straight hair has no curls or waves in it.  /  [ADV 副词] 笔直地;径直地； straight You use straight to indicate that the way from one place to another is very direct, with no changes of direction.  /  [ADV 副词] 立刻;马上； straight If you go straight to a place, you go there immediately.
straight arrow: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 循规蹈矩的人;安分守己的人； A straight arrow is someone who is very traditional, honest, and moral.
straight away: [ADV 副词] 立刻;马上;毫不迟疑地； straight away If you do something straight away , you do it immediately and without delay.
straighten: [VERB 动词] 把…整理好;使端正； straighten If you straighten something, you make it tidy or put it in its proper position.  /  [VERB 动词] 挺直，端正(身体)； straighten straighten up 同 straighten If you are standing in a relaxed or slightly bent position and then you straighten , you make your back or body straight and upright.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使变直;使变正； straighten straighten out 同 straighten If you straighten something, or it straightens , it becomes straight.  /  相关词组： straighten out straighten up �
straighten out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 理清，整顿(混乱的局面)； straighten out If you straighten out a confused situation, you succeed in getting it organized and tidied up.  /  »see: straighten 3 ; �
straight-faced: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 一本正经的;绷着脸的； straight-faced A straight-faced person appears not to be amused in a funny situation.
straightforward: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 简单明了的;易懂的； straightforward straightforwardly If you describe something as straightforward , you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坦率的;率直的;坦诚的； straightforward straightforwardly If you describe a person or their behaviour as straightforward , you approve of them because they are honest and direct, and do not try to hide their feelings.
strain: [N-VAR 可变名词] 压力;负担;重负； strain If strain is put on an organization or system, it has to do more than it is able to do.  /  [VERB 动词] 使不堪承受;使紧张； strain To strain something means to make it do more than it is able to do.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (精神上的)压力，重负，紧张； strain Strain is a state of worry and tension caused by a difficult situation.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 带来压力的情况;造成紧张的因素； strain If you say that a situation is a strain , you mean that it makes you worried and tense.
strained: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 焦虑的;紧张的;担忧的； strained If someone's appearance, voice, or behaviour is strained , they seem worried and nervous.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 关系紧张的，不友好的，互相猜测的； strained If relations between people are strained , those people do not like or trust each other.
strainer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 滤器;滤网； strainer A strainer is an object with holes which you pour a liquid through in order to separate the liquid from the solids in it.
strait: [N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词] 海峡;(连接两大海域的)水道； strait You can refer to a narrow strip of sea which joins two large areas of sea as a strait or the straits .  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (通常指因缺钱造成的)困境，窘迫； strait If someone is in dire or desperate straits , they are in a very difficult situation, usually because they do not have much money.
straitened: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 经济拮据的;穷困潦倒的； straitened If someone is living in straitened circumstances, they do not have as much money as they used to, and are finding it very hard to buy or pay for everything that they need.
straitjacket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (用以约束行为狂暴者的)约束服，紧身衣； straitjacket A straitjacket is a special jacket used to tie the arms of a violent person tightly around their body.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 约束;桎梏;束缚； straitjacket If you describe an idea or a situation as a straitjacket , you mean that it is very limited and restricting.
strait-laced: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (道德方面)一本正经的，古板的，拘谨保守的； strait-laced If you describe someone as strait-laced , you disapprove of them because they have very strict views about what kind of behaviour is moral or acceptable.
strand: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (头发、电线或纱线等的)股，缕； strand A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (计划或理论的)部分，方面； strand A strand of a plan or theory is a part of it.  /  [VERB 动词] (坏天气等)使滞留，使搁浅； strand If you are stranded , you are prevented from leaving a place, for example because of bad weather.
strange: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 奇怪的;怪异的;意料之外的； strange strangely strangeness Something that is strange is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 陌生的;不熟悉的； strange A strange place is one that you have never been to before.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 局促不安的;不自在的;不舒服的； strange If you feel strange , you have an unpleasant or uncomfortable feeling, either physical or emotional.  /  See also: stranger ; �
strangely: [ADV 副词] (表示强调)奇怪地，异常地，不可思议地； strangely See also: strange ; You use strangely to emphasize that what you are saying is surprising.
stranger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 陌生人； stranger A stranger is someone you have never met before.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 互不相识的人； stranger If two people are strangers , they do not know each other.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外乡人;外地人； stranger If you are a stranger in a place, you do not know the place well.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 生手;外行;(对…)一无所知的人； stranger If you are a stranger to something, you have had no experience of it or do not understand it.
strangle: [VERB 动词] 勒死;扼死;绞死;掐死； strangle strangler To strangle someone means to kill them by squeezing their throat tightly so that they cannot breathe.  /  [VERB 动词] 抑制;制止;扼杀； strangle To strangle something means to prevent it from succeeding or developing.
strangled: [ADJ 形容词] (说话声、哭声)哽塞的，哽咽的，顿住的； strangled A strangled voice or cry sounds unclear because the throat muscles of the person speaking or crying are tight.
stranglehold: [N-SING 单数名词] 控制;约束;钳制； stranglehold To have a stranglehold on something means to have control over it and prevent it from being free or from developing.
strangulation: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 勒死;扼死;绞死;掐死； strangulation Strangulation is the act of killing someone by squeezing their throat tightly so that they cannot breathe.
strap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 带子;皮带;布带； strap A strap is a narrow piece of leather, cloth, or other material.  /  [VERB 动词] 用带子系(或绑、捆、扎)； strap If you strap something somewhere, you fasten it there with a strap.
strapless: [ADJ 形容词] (连衣裙或胸罩)无肩带的，无吊带的； strapless A strapless dress or bra does not have the usual narrow bands of material over the shoulders.
strapped: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 手头拮据的;缺钱的； strapped See also: cash-strapped ; If someone is strapped for money, they do not have enough money to buy or pay for the things they want or need.
strapping: [ADJ 形容词] 高大健壮的;强健的； strapping If you describe someone as strapping , you mean that they are tall and strong, and look healthy.
strata: (stratum 的复数)； Strata is the plural of stratum .
stratagem: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常指蒙蔽别人的)花招，计谋，诡计； stratagem A stratagem is a plan that is intended to achieve a particular effect, often by deceiving people.
strategic: [ADJ 形容词] 战略性的;策略上的； strategic strategically Strategic means relating to the most important, general aspects of something such as a military operation or political policy, especially when these are decided in advance.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (武器)战略性的； strategic Strategic weapons are very powerful missiles that can be fired only after a decision to use them has been made by a political leader.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (位置)具有战略意义的，重要的，合适的； strategic strategically If you put something in a strategic position, you place it cleverly in a position where it will be most useful or have the most effect.
strategist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指军事)战略家，善于策划的人； strategist A strategist is someone who is skilled in planning the best way to gain an advantage or to achieve success, especially in war.
strategy: [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤指长期的)战略，策略，行动计划； strategy A strategy is a general plan or set of plans intended to achieve something, especially over a long period.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指战争中的)战略，战略学； strategy Strategy is the art of planning the best way to gain an advantage or achieve success, especially in war.
stratification: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指社会的)分层，形成阶层； stratification Stratification is the division of something, especially society, into different classes or layers.
stratified: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 有不同社会阶层的;等级分化的； stratified A stratified society is one that is divided into different classes or social layers.
stratosphere: [N-SING 单数名词] 平流层;同温层； The stratosphere is the layer of the earth's atmosphere which lies between 10 and 50 kilometres above the earth.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 最高层;最高水平;顶峰； stratosphere If you say that someone or something climbs or is sent into the stratosphere , you mean that they reach a very high level.
stratospheric: [ADJ 形容词] 平流层的;同温层的； stratospheric Stratospheric means found in or related to the stratosphere.
stratum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 社会阶层； stratum A stratum of society is a group of people in it who are similar in their education, income, or social status.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 岩层； Strata are different layers of rock.
straw: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (干的)稻草，麦秆，禾秆； straw Straw consists of the dried, yellowish stalks from crops such as wheat or barley.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (喝饮料用的)吸管； straw A straw is a thin tube of paper or plastic, which you use to suck a drink into your mouth.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 抓救命稻草;采取极端措施;作绝望的挣扎； straw If you are clutching at straws or grasping at straws , you are trying unusual or extreme ideas or methods because other ideas or methods have failed.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草;最终使人不堪忍受的事； straw If an event is the last straw or the straw that broke the camel's back , it is the latest in a series of unpleasant or undesirable events, and makes you feel that you cannot tolerate a situation any longer.
strawberry: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 草莓； strawberry A strawberry is a small red fruit which is soft and juicy and has tiny yellow seeds on its skin.
strawberry blonde: [ADJ 形容词] (头发)金色中略带红色的，草莓金黄色的； Strawberry blonde hair is reddish blonde.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 金黄色头发中略带红色的人;(尤指)长着淡红色金发的女郎； A strawberry blonde is a person, especially a woman, who has strawberry blonde hair.
straw-coloured: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指头发)麦秆色的，淡黄色的； If you describe something, especially hair, as straw-coloured , you mean that it is pale yellow.
straw poll: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 非正式民意测验； straw poll A straw poll is the unofficial questioning of a group of people to find out their opinion about something.
stray: [VERB 动词] 迷路;偏离;走失； stray If someone strays somewhere, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (狗、猫)走失的，迷路的，无主的； stray A stray dog or cat has wandered away from its owner's home.  /  [VERB 动词] 走神;(视线)偏离，往别处看； stray If your mind or your eyes stray , you do not concentrate on or look at one particular subject, but start thinking about or looking at other things.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 零星的;离散的;散落的； stray You use stray to describe something that exists separated from other similar things.
streak: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 条纹;条痕； streak A streak is a long stripe or mark on a surface which contrasts with the surface because it is a different colour.  /  [VERB 动词] 在…上留下条纹(或条痕);使布满条纹(或条痕)； streak -streaked If something streaks a surface, it makes long stripes or marks on the surface.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 性格特征;特点； streak If someone has a streak of a particular type of behaviour, they sometimes behave in that way.  /  [VERB 动词] 飞奔;疾驰； streak If something or someone streaks somewhere, they move there very quickly.
streaker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 裸奔者； A streaker is someone who runs quickly through a public place wearing no clothes, as a joke.

tailor-make: [VERB 动词] 为…特别制作;专为…制作;为…量身定做； tailor-make See also: tailor-made ; If someone tailor-makes something for you, they make or design it to suit your requirements.
tailpipe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (汽车的)排气管，尾气喷管； A tailpipe is the end pipe of a car's exhaust system.
tailwind: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (从行驶的交通工具后面吹来的)顺风； tailwind A tailwind is a wind that is blowing from behind an aeroplane, boat, or other vehicle, making it move faster.
taint: [VERB 动词] 玷污，毁坏，损害，败坏(地位、名誉)； taint tainted If a person or thing is tainted by something bad or undesirable, their status or reputation is harmed because they are associated with it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (地位、名誉的)玷污，污点，瑕疵； taint A taint is an undesirable quality which spoils the status or reputation of someone or something.  /  [VERB 动词] 污染，毁坏(食品、药品)； taint If an unpleasant substance taints food or medicine, the food or medicine is spoiled or damaged by it.
take: Take is used in combination with a wide range of nouns, where the meaning of the combination is mostly given by the noun.  /  [VERB 动词] 后接名词，用于描述动作或事件； take You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun.  /  [VERB 动词] 与一系列名词连用，代替意义更为具体的动词； take In ordinary spoken or written English, people use take with a range of nouns instead of using a more specific verb.  /  [VERB 动词] 拿;取； take If you take something, you reach out for it and hold it.
take after: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (在外表、举止、性格方面)像(某家庭成员)； If you take after a member of your family, you resemble them in your appearance, your behaviour, or your character.
take against: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (常指无缘无故地)开始讨厌，开始厌恶； If you take against someone or something, you develop a dislike for them, often for no good reason.
take apart: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拆开;拆散;拆解； If you take something apart , you separate it into the different parts that it is made of.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 仔细分析，剖析[以指出不足或缺点)； take apart If you take apart something such as an argument or an idea, you show what its weaknesses are, usually by analyzing it carefully.
take away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拿走;夺走； If you take something away from someone, you remove it from them, so that they no longer possess it or have it with them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 从…中减去;从…中扣除； If you take one number or amount away from another, you subtract one number from the other.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 带走，抓走(送去监狱、医院等)； To take someone away means to bring them from their home to an institution such as a prison or hospital.  /  See also: takeaway ; �
takeaway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外卖店;外卖餐馆； A takeaway is a shop or restaurant which sells hot cooked food that you eat somewhere else.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (商店、餐馆的)外卖食品； takeaway A takeaway is hot cooked food that you buy from a shop or restaurant and eat somewhere else.
take away from: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 减损;贬低； take away from If something takes away from an achievement, success, or quality, or takes something away from it, it makes it seem lower in value or worth than it should be.
take back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 退回;退还;归还； If you take something back , you return it to the place where you bought it or where you borrowed it from, because it is unsuitable or broken, or because you have finished with it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 收回，撤回(所说的话或想法)； If you take something back , you admit that something that you said or thought is wrong.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 让…回家;准许…回来； take back If you take someone back , you allow them to come home again, after they have gone away because of a quarrel or other problem.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 使回想起;使回忆起； If you say that something takes you back , you mean that it reminds you of a period of your past life and makes you think about it again.
take down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (从高处)取下，拿下，够下来； If you take something down , you reach up and get it from a high place such as a shelf.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拆掉;拆毁； If you take down a structure, you remove each piece of it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 写下;记录； If you take down a piece of information or a statement, you write it down.
take-home pay: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (扣除税款等之后的)实发工资； take-home pay Your take-home pay is the amount of your wages or salary that is left after income tax and other payments have been subtracted.
take in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 收留，收容(尤指无家可归者或逃难者)； If you take someone in , you allow them to stay in your house or your country, especially when they do not have anywhere to stay or are in trouble.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (警察)带走，抓走； If the police take someone in , they remove them from their home in order to question them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 欺骗;使上当； If you are taken in by someone or something, you are deceived by them, so that you get a false impression of them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 理解;领会;领悟； take in If you take something in , you pay attention to it and understand it when you hear it or read it.
taken: + + + Taken is the past participle of take .  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 对…感兴趣的;为…所吸引的； taken If you are taken with something or someone, you are very interested in them or attracted to them.
takeoff: [N-VAR 可变名词] (飞机的)起飞，升空； takeoff Takeoff is the beginning of a flight, when an aircraft leaves the ground.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对某人动作的滑稽)模仿； takeoff A takeoff of someone is a humorous imitation of the way in which they behave.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (经济、生意等的)开始腾飞，迅速发展； Takeoff is the point in the development of something, such as an economy or a business, when it begins to be successful.
take off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (飞机)起飞； When an aeroplane takes off , it leaves the ground and starts flying.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (产品、活动、事业等)腾飞，突然成功； take off If something such as a product, an activity, or someone's career takes off , it suddenly becomes very successful.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (突然)离开，走开，走掉； If you take off or take yourself off , you go away, often suddenly and unexpectedly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 脱下，脱掉(衣物)； If you take a garment off , you remove it.
take on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 承担，接受(尤指艰巨工作或重大责任)； take on If you take on a job or responsibility, especially a difficult one, you accept it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 呈现，显出(新面貌或新特点)； If something takes on a new appearance or quality, it develops that appearance or quality.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (公共汽车、船舶等)上客，装货，补充(燃料)； take on If a vehicle such as a bus or ship takes on passengers, goods, or fuel, it stops in order to allow them to get on or to be loaded on.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 雇用;录用； If you take someone on , you employ them to do a job.
take out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 去除;除掉； take out If you take something out , you remove it permanently from its place.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 取得，获得，领到(贷款、执照、保单等)； take out If you take out something such as a loan, a licence, or an insurance policy, you obtain it by fulfilling the conditions and paying the money that is necessary.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 邀请…外出，带…出去[吃饭、看电影等)； If you take someone out , they go to something such as a restaurant or theatre with you after you have invited them, and usually you pay for them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 干掉;摞倒； If you take someone out , you kill them, or injure them so badly that they can no longer fight or do anything to harm you.
takeout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外卖店;外卖餐馆； A takeout is a store or restaurant which sells hot cooked food that you eat somewhere else.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 外卖饭菜;外卖食物； A takeout or takeout food is hot cooked food which you buy from a store or restaurant and eat somewhere else.
take out on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 拿…出气;向…发泄； If you take something out on someone, you behave in an unpleasant way towards them because you feel angry or upset, even though this is not their fault.
takeover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 收购;接管;接收； takeover A takeover is the act of gaining control of a company by buying more of its shares than anyone else.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (武装)占领，接管，控制； takeover A takeover is the act of taking control of a country, political party, or movement by force.
take over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 接收，接管(公司)； take over If you take over a company, you get control of it, for example by buying its shares.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (武力)占领，接管，控制； If someone takes over a country or building, they get control of it by force, for example with the help of the army.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 接替;接任;接手； If you take over a job or role or if you take over , you become responsible for the job after someone else has stopped doing it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 取代;代替;占上风； If one thing takes over from something else, it becomes more important, successful, or powerful than the other thing, and eventually replaces it.
taker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 接受…的人； taker If there are no takers for something such as an investment or a challenge, nobody is willing to accept it.
-taker: [COMB in N-COUNT] [COMB in ADJ] (和名词连用，构成新名词)表示“做出某动作的人”； -taker -taker combines with nouns to form other nouns which refer to people who take things, for example decisions or notes.
take to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指短时间接触后)喜欢上，喜爱； take to If you take to someone or something, you like them, especially after knowing them or thinking about them for only a short time.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 养成(做…)的习惯;开始定时(做…)； If you take to doing something, you begin to do it as a regular habit.
take-up: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 申请率；购买率； take-up Take-up is the rate at which people apply for or buy something which is offered, for example financial help from the government or shares in a company.
take up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 开始从事;喜欢上； take up If you take up an activity or a subject, you become interested in it and spend time doing it, either as a hobby or as a career.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 开始处理;讨论如何处理； take up If you take up a question, problem, or cause, you act on it or discuss how you are going to act on it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 开始从事，开始干(工作)； take up If you take up a job, you begin to work at it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 接受，答应(提议或挑战)； If you take up an offer or a challenge, you accept it.
take up on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 接受，同意(提议或邀请)； If you take someone up on their offer or invitation, you accept it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 追问;要求…解释； If you take a person up on something, you ask them to explain something that they have just said or done, for example because you think it is wrong or strange.
take up with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 和…混在一起;和…好上了;和…关系暧昧； You say that someone has taken up with someone unsuitable when they have begun a sexual or friendly relationship with them, and you disapprove of this.  /  [PHR-V-PASSIVE 被动动词短语] 忙于； If you are taken up with something, it keeps you busy or fully occupied.
takings: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (企业一定时期的)销售额，收入； takings You can use takings to refer to the amount of money that a business such as a shop or a cinema gets from selling its goods or tickets during a particular period.
talc: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同 talcum powder； Talc is the same as talcum powder .
talcum powder: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 爽身粉;滑石粉； Talcum powder is fine powder with a pleasant smell which people put on their bodies after they have had a bath or a shower.
tale: [N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词] (常包含魔法或惊险内容的)传说，故事； tale A tale is a story, often involving magic or exciting events.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对真人真事精彩的或夸张的)描述，讲述； tale You can refer to an interesting, exciting, or dramatic account of a real event as a tale .  /  See also: fairy tale ; old wives' tale ; tall tale ;  /  [PHRASE 短语] 大难不死;逃过劫难;幸免于难； tale If you survive a dangerous or frightening experience and so are able to tell people about it afterwards, you can say that you lived to tell the tale .
talent: [N-VAR 可变名词] 天资;天赋； talent See also: talent show ; Talent is the natural ability to do something well.
talented: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 天资聪颖的;天赋高的； talented Someone who is talented has a natural ability to do something well.
talent scout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (演员、足球运动员、音乐人才等的)星探，新秀物色者，伯乐； A talent scout is someone whose job is to find people who have talent, for example as actors, footballers, or musicians, so that they can be offered work.
talent show: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (普通人为赢取奖项的)才艺表演，大奖赛； talent show A talent show , talent competition , or talent contest is a show where ordinary people perform an act on stage, usually in order to try to win a prize for the best performance.
talisman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 护身符;避邪物； A talisman is an object which you believe has magic powers to protect you or bring you luck.
talk: [VERB 动词] 讲话;说话； talk When you talk , you use spoken language to express your thoughts, ideas, or feelings.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 交谈;谈话； talk If you talk to someone, you have a conversation with them.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 谈心，倾诉，诉说心事； talk If you talk to someone, you tell them about the things that are worrying you.  /  [VERB 动词] 发表谈话;发表观点； talk If you talk on or about something, you make an informal speech telling people what you know or think about it.
talkative: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 爱说话的;话多的;健谈的； talkative Someone who is talkative talks a lot.
talk back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 回嘴;顶撞;犟嘴； talk back If you talk back to someone in authority such as a parent or teacher, you answer them in a rude way.
talk down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (紧急情况下)引导(飞行员)安全降落； To talk down someone who is flying an aircraft in an emergency means to give them instructions so that they can land safely.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 贬低;贬损； If someone talks down a particular thing, they make it less interesting, valuable, or likely than it originally seemed.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 说服(或劝服)…降低要价； talk down To talk someone down in negotiations means to persuade them to accept less money than they originally asked for.
talk down to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 以居高临下(或自命不凡)的口气说话； If you say that someone talks down to you, you disapprove of the way they talk to you, treating you as if you are not very intelligent or not very important.
talker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 健谈的人;以某种方式说话的人； talker You can use talker to refer to someone when you are considering how much they talk, or how good they are at talking to people.
talkie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有声电影； talkie A talkie is a cinema film made with sound, as opposed to a silent film.
talking head: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (在电视讨论或访谈节目中的) 专家，权威的评论家； Talking heads are people who appear in television discussion programmes and interviews to give their opinions about a topic.
talking point: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (讨论、辩论的)话题，论题，焦点； talking point A talking point is an interesting subject for discussion or argument.
talking shop: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (只说不做的)清谈会;清谈委员会； If you say that a conference or a committee is just a talking shop , you disapprove of it because nothing is achieved as a result of what is discussed.
talking-to: [N-SING 单数名词] 责骂;申斥;严厉批评； talking-to If you give someone a talking-to , you speak to them severely, usually about something unacceptable that they have done, in order to show them they were wrong.
talk into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 说服，劝服(尤指做错事或蠢事)； If you talk a person into doing something they do not want to do, especially something wrong or stupid, you persuade them to do it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通过谈话)取得，进入； If you talk yourself into a particular situation or state, you get yourself into it by talking.
talk out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 详细商谈;透彻讨论； If you talk out something such as a problem, you discuss it thoroughly in order to settle it.
talk out of: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 说服…放弃;劝服…不做； If you talk someone out of doing something they want or intend to do, you persuade them not to do it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通过谈话)摆脱，甩掉,避开； If you talk yourself out of a particular situation or state, you get yourself out of it by talking.
talk over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 详细探讨;坦诚交谈； If you talk something over , you discuss it thoroughly and honestly.
talk round: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 说服;劝说…回心转意； talk round If you talk someone round , you persuade them to change their mind so that they agree with you, or agree to do what you want them to do
talk show: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (电视或广播上的)名人访谈节目，脱口秀； A talk show is a television or radio show in which famous people talk to each other in an informal way and are asked questions about different topics.
talk through: [PHR-V-RECIP 相互动词短语] 详细讨论;讨论清楚； If you talk something through with someone, you discuss it with them thoroughly.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 向…仔细讲解;向…详细解释； If someone talks you through something that you do not know, they explain it to you carefully.
talk up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 夸大;过分夸奖;吹捧； If someone talks up a particular thing, they make it sound more interesting, valuable, or likely than it originally seemed.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 说服…提高出价;抬高…的价格； To talk someone or something up in negotiations means to persuade someone to pay more money than they originally offered or wanted to.
tall: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 高的;高大的； tall Someone or something that is tall has a greater height than is normal or average.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (用于指高度)有…高的，身高…的；  tall You use tall to ask or talk about the height of someone or something.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 难办的事情;棘手的问题； tall If something is a tall order , it is very difficult.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 昂首挺胸;理直气壮； If you say that someone walks tall , you mean that they behave in a way that shows that they have pride in themselves and in what they are doing.
tallow: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (用于制造蜡烛、肥皂的)动物油脂； Tallow is hard animal fat that is used for making candles and soap.
tall ship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 高桅横帆船； A tall ship is a sailing ship which has very tall masts and square sails.
tall tale: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 荒诞不经的故事;奇闻怪事； tall tale A tall tale is a long and complicated story that is difficult to believe because most of the events it describes seem unlikely or impossible.
tally: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 账目;积分;得分； tally A tally is a record of amounts or numbers which you keep changing and adding to as the activity which affects it progresses.  /  [V-RECIP 相互动词] 与…一致;与…相同;与…吻合； tally If one number or statement tallies with another, they agree with each other or are exactly the same.  /  [VERB 动词] 计算;合计;清点； tally tally up 同 tally If you tally numbers, items, or totals, you count them.
Talmud: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 《塔木德经》(犹太教法典)； The Talmud is the collection of ancient Jewish laws which governs the religious and non-religious life of Orthodox Jews.
talon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (猛禽的)爪，利爪； The talons of a bird of prey are its hooked claws.
tamarind: [N-VAR 可变名词] 罗望子果实;罗望子树； A tamarind is a fruit which grows on a tropical evergreen tree which has pleasant-smelling flowers.
tamarisk: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 多见于地中海和亚洲的柽柳； A tamarisk is a bush or small tree which grows mainly around the Mediterranean and in Asia, and has pink or white flowers.
tambourine: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 手鼓;铃鼓； A tambourine is a musical instrument which you shake or hit with your hand.
tame: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (动物)驯化的，驯服的； tame A tame animal or bird is one that is not afraid of humans.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 乏味的;没劲的； tame tamely If you say that something or someone is tame , you are criticizing them for being weak and uninteresting, rather than forceful or shocking.  /  [VERB 动词] 驯化，驯服(野生动物或鸟)； tame If someone tames a wild animal or bird, they train it not to be afraid of humans and to do what they say.  /  [VERB 动词] 制服;控制;驾驭； tame If you tame someone or something that is dangerous, uncontrolled, or likely to cause trouble, you bring them under control.
tamoxifen: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (治疗乳腺癌的)他莫昔芬，三苯氧胺； Tamoxifen is a drug that is used for treating women who have breast cancer.

tampon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 卫生棉条;月经棉塞； A tampon is a tube made of cotton wool that a woman puts inside her vagina in order to absorb blood during menstruation.
tan: [N-SING 单数名词] 晒黑的皮肤； tan If you have a tan , your skin has become darker than usual because you have been in the sun.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使(皮肤)晒黑； tan tanned If a part of your body tans or if you tan it, your skin becomes darker than usual because you spend a lot of time in the sun.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 棕黄色;黄褐色； tan Something that is tan is a light brown colour.  /  [VERB 动词] 鞣革;硝皮； tan To tan animal skins means to make them into leather by treating them with tannin or other chemicals.
tandem: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 双人自行车； A tandem is a bicycle designed for two riders, on which one rider sits behind the other.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 与…同时(发生)； tandem If one thing happens or is done in tandem with another thing, the two things happen at the same time.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 与…协作;配合； tandem If one person does something in tandem with another person, the two people do it by working together.
tandoori: [ADJ 形容词] 唐杜里烹饪法(印度一种用泥炉烹调的方法)； Tandoori dishes are Indian meat dishes which are cooked in a clay oven.
tang: [N-SING 单数名词] 浓烈刺鼻的气味(或味道)； tang A tang is a strong, sharp smell or taste.
tangent: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 切线； A tangent is a line that touches the edge of a curve or circle at one point, but does not cross it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 突然偏离原来的思路;突然离题； tangent If someone goes off at a tangent , they start saying or doing something that is not directly connected with what they were saying or doing before.
tangential: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 关系不大的;不直接相干的； tangential If you describe something as tangential , you mean that it has only a slight or indirect connection with the thing you are concerned with, and is therefore not worth considering seriously.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 切线的;相切的； tangential If something is tangential to something else, it is at a tangent to it.
tangerine: 橘子;柑橘； tangerines A tangerine is a small sweet orange.
tangible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 清晰可见的;摸得着的;感觉得到的;明显的； tangible tangibly If something is tangible , it is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.
tangle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 缠结;纠结;乱糟糟的一团； tangle A tangle of something is a mass of it twisted together in an untidy way.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使缠绕;使缠结； tangle If something is tangled or tangles , it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 混乱;纷乱;乱成一团； tangle You can refer to a confusing or complicated situation as a tangle .  /  [VERB 动词] (思想、局势变得)纷乱，混乱； tangle tangled If ideas or situations are tangled , they become confused and complicated.
tangle up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 被绕住;被缠住； If a person or thing is tangled up in something such as wire or ropes, they are caught or trapped in it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 陷入，卷进(困境)； If you are tangled up in a complicated or unpleasant situation, you are involved in it and cannot get free of it.

tango: [N-SING 单数名词] 探戈舞； The tango is a South American dance in which two people hold each other closely, walk quickly in one direction, then walk quickly back again.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 探戈舞曲； tango A tango is a piece of music intended for tango dancing.  /  [VERB 动词] 跳探戈舞； tango If you tango , you dance the tango.

tanner: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 制革工;鞣皮工； A tanner is someone whose job is making leather from animal skins.
tannin: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 丹宁酸，鞣酸(用于制革、染色)； Tannin is a yellow or brown chemical that is found in plants such as tea.

tantalize: [VERB 动词] 使(某人)想要却得不到(某物);逗引;挑逗;撩拨； tantalize tantalizing tantalizingly If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have what they appeared to offer.
tantamount: [ADJ 形容词] (用于强调非常糟糕、难以接受或不幸)几乎是…，简直是…，无异于…； tantamount If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

tantrum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 发脾气;耍性子； tantrum If a child has a tantrum , they lose their temper in a noisy and uncontrolled way.

tap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 龙头;阀门;旋塞； tap A tap is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas from a pipe or container, for example on a sink.  /  [VERB 动词] 轻打;轻拍;轻叩； tap If you tap something, you hit it with a quick light blow or a series of quick light blows.  /  [VERB 动词] (尤指听音乐时，用手指或脚)敲节拍，打拍子； tap If you tap your fingers or feet, you make a regular pattern of sound by hitting a surface lightly and repeatedly with them, especially while you are listening to music.  /  [VERB 动词] 开发，发掘，利用(资源、形势)； tap If you tap a resource or situation, you make use of it by getting from it something that you need or want.
tapas: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (西班牙的)下酒菜，开胃菜； In Spain, tapas are small plates of food that are served with drinks or before a main meal.
tap dancer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 踢踏舞者； A tap dancer is a dancer who does tap dancing.
tap dancing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 踢踏舞； Tap dancing is a style of dancing in which the dancers wear special shoes with pieces of metal on the heels and toes.
tape: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 磁带;录音带;录像带； tape Tape is a narrow plastic strip covered with a magnetic substance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (盒式或卷盘式)录音带，录像带； tape A tape is a cassette or spool with magnetic tape wound round it.  /  [VERB 动词] (用录音机、录像机)录制(音乐、声音或电视画面)； tape taping If you tape music, sounds, or television pictures, you record them using a tape recorder or a video recorder.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (捆扎东西或注明衣物主人的)布条，布带； tape A tape is a strip of cloth used to tie things together or to identify who a piece of clothing belongs to.
tape deck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 录音机；录放机； A tape deck is the machine on which you can play or record cassette tapes.
tape measure: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 钢尺;卷尺;软尺； A tape measure is a strip of metal, plastic, or cloth which has numbers marked on it and is used for measuring.

tape recording: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (磁带)录音； tape recording A tape recording is a recording of sounds that has been made on tape.
tape streamer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 磁带机(利用磁带备份硬盘的设备)； tape streamer A tape streamer is a piece of computer equipment that you use for copying data from a hard disk onto magnetic tape for security or storage.

tapeworm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (寄生于人、畜体内的)绦虫； A tapeworm is a long, flat parasite which lives in the stomach and intestines of animals or people.
tapioca: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (木薯粉制成的)西米； Tapioca is a food consisting of white grains, rather like rice, which come from the cassava plant.

tap water: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 自来水； tap water Tap water is the water that comes out of a tap in a building such as a house or a hotel.
tar: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 柏油;沥青； tar Tar is a thick black sticky substance that is used especially for making roads.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (烟草中的)焦油； Tar is one of the poisonous substances contained in tobacco.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 被当作一丘之貉;被当成一路货色； tar If some people in a group behave badly and if people then wrongly think that all of the group is equally bad, you can say that the whole group is tarred with the same brush .  /  See also: tarred ; �
taramasalata: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 希腊鱼子酱； Taramasalata is a pink creamy food made from the eggs of a fish such as cod or mullet.
tarantula: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 狼蛛;塔兰托毒蛛； A tarantula is a large hairy spider which has a poisonous bite.
tardy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 晚的;迟到的； tardy tardiness If you describe something or someone as tardy , you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 拖沓的;反应迟缓的； tardy tardiness If you describe someone or something as tardy , you are criticizing them because they are slow to act.
target: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 靶子;目标;对象； target A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 目标;目的； target A target is a result that you are trying to achieve.  /  [VERB 动词] 攻击;批评;以…为攻击目标； target To target a particular person or thing means to decide to attack or criticize them.  /  [VERB 动词] 瞄准;面向;尽力吸引； target If you target a particular group of people, you try to appeal to those people or affect them.

tariff: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (政府对进口商品征收的)关税； tariff A tariff is a tax that a government collects on goods coming into a country.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (公共服务的)收费，费用;(旅馆的)住宿费，服务费； tariff A tariff is the rate at which you are charged for public services such as gas and electricity, or for accommodation and services in a hotel.
tarmac: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (铺路面用的)柏油碎石； tarmac Tarmac is a material used for making road surfaces, consisting of crushed stones mixed with tar.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 柏油碎石地面;(尤指)停机坪； tarmac The tarmac is an area with a surface made of tarmac, especially the area from which planes take off at an airport.
tarn: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 山中小湖； A tarn is a small lake in an area of mountains.
tarnish: [VERB 动词] 玷污，败坏，损害(名誉或形象)； tarnish tarnished If you say that something tarnishes someone's reputation or image, you mean that it causes people to have a worse opinion of them than they would otherwise have had.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使有污迹;使失去光泽;使变暗淡； tarnish tarnished If a metal tarnishes or if something tarnishes it, it becomes stained and loses its brightness.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 锈斑;污点； tarnish Tarnish is a substance which forms of the surface of some metals and which stains them or causes them to lose their brightness.

tarp: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (防水)帆布，油布； A tarp is a sheet of heavy waterproof material that is used as a protective cover.
tarpaulin: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 防水帆布;油布； tarpaulin Tarpaulin is a fabric made of canvas or similar material coated with tar, wax, paint, or some other waterproof substance.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (一块)防水帆布，油布； A tarpaulin is a sheet of heavy waterproof material that is used as a protective cover.
tarragon: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 龙蒿(叶子用作调料)； Tarragon is a European herb with narrow leaves which are used to add flavour to food.
tarred: [ADJ 形容词] (道路、屋顶)铺了柏油的，涂了沥青的； tarred A tarred road or roof has a surface of tar.
tarry: [VERB 动词] 逗留;停留;徘徊； If you tarry somewhere, you stay there longer than you meant to and delay leaving.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 柏油含量高的;像柏油的； tarry If you describe something as tarry , you mean that it has a lot of tar in it or is like tar.
tart: [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤指甜心的)果馅饼； tart A tart is a shallow pastry case with a filling of food, especially sweet food.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (水果等)味道浓烈的，味儿冲的； tart If something such as fruit is tart , it has a sharp taste.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (言语)尖刻的，尖酸的，刻薄的； tart tartly A tart remark or way of speaking is sharp and unpleasant, often in a way that is rather cruel.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 淫妇;荡妇;妓女； tart If someone refers to a woman or girl as a tart , they are criticizing her because they think she is sexually immoral or dresses in a way that makes her look sexually immoral.
tartan: [N-VAR 可变名词] (苏格兰)花格图案，花格织物，格呢； tartan Tartan is a design for cloth traditionally associated with Scotland, and which has a number of distinctive types.
tartar: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 牙垢;牙石； Tartar is a hard yellowish substance that forms on your teeth and causes them to decay if it is not removed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 凶悍的人，脾气暴戾的人;(尤指)悍妇； tartar If you describe someone, especially a woman in a position of authority, as a tartar , you mean that they are fierce, bad-tempered, and strict.  /  See also: cream of tartar ; �

tart up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把(房间或大楼)装饰得俗丽； tart up If someone tarts up a room or building, they try to improve its appearance, often with the result that it looks vulgar.
tarty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (女人或其衣着)妖艳的，风骚的，花枝招展的； tarty tartiest If you describe a woman or her clothes as tarty , you are critical of her because she tries to make herself look sexually attractive in a vulgar way.
task: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 任务;工作； task A task is an activity or piece of work which you have to do, usually as part of a larger project.  /  [VERB 动词] 给…分配任务;派给…工作； task If you are tasked with doing a particular activity or piece of work, someone in authority asks you to do it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 批评;责备； task If you take someone to task , you criticize them or tell them off because of something bad or wrong that they have done.

tern: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 燕鸥； A tern is a small black and white seabird with long wings and a forked tail.
terrace: [N-COUNT; N-IN-NAMES 名称名词；名称名词] 排屋(指相互连接、式样相似的房屋)； terrace A terrace is a row of similar houses joined together by their side walls.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (房屋外的)草坪，平台； terrace A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 梯田;阶地； terrace Terraces are a series of flat areas built like steps on the side of a hill so that crops can be grown there.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (足球赛观众可站立的)阶梯看台； The terraces at a football ground are wide steps that people can stand on when they are watching a game.
terraced: [ADJ 形容词] (斜坡、山坡)梯田状的，阶梯形的； A terraced slope or side of a hill has flat areas like steps cut into it, where crops or other plants can be grown.
terraced house: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (一所)排屋； A terraced house or a terrace house is one of a row of similar houses joined together by their side walls.
terracing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 梯田;阶地； terracing Terracing is a sloping piece of land that has had flat areas like steps built on it, for example so that people can grow crops there.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (足球赛观众可站立的)阶梯看台； At a football stadium, terracing is an area of wide steps that people can stand on when they are watching the game.
terracotta: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 赤陶土；赤土； terracotta Terracotta is a brownish-red clay that has been baked and is used for making things such as flower pots, small statues, and tiles.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 赤褐色;棕红色； terracotta Terracotta is used to describe things that are brownish-red in colour.
terra firma: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 大地，陆地相对于空中或海中而言让人感到安全； terra firma If you describe the ground as terra firma , you mean that it feels safe in contrast to being in the air or at sea.
terrain: [N-VAR 可变名词] 地形;地势;地带； terrain Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.
terrapin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 水龟； A terrapin is a reptile which has a thick shell covering its body and which lives partly in water and partly on land.
terrestrial: [ADJ 形容词] (动植物)陆地的，陆生的，陆栖的； A terrestrial animal or plant lives on land or on the ground rather than in the sea, in trees, or in the air.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 地球的;地球上的； terrestrial Terrestrial means relating to the planet Earth rather than to some other part of the universe.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (电视频道)地面的(有别于卫星转播的)； Terrestrial television channels are transmitted using equipment situated at ground level, and not by satellite.
terrible: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 非常严重的;骇人的;糟糕的； terrible terribly A terrible experience or situation is very serious or very unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (感觉或看起来)病得很重的，心情很糟的； terrible If you feel terrible , you feel extremely ill or unhappy.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 质量极差的;很糟糕的； terrible If something is terrible , it is very bad or of very poor quality.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (用来加强语气)十足的，极度的，不折不扣的； terrible terribly You use terrible to emphasize the great extent or degree of something.
terrier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 犭更;小猎犬； See also: bull terrier ; pit bull terrier ; A terrier is a small breed of dog.
terrific: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 极好的;非常棒的;了不起的； terrific If you describe something or someone as terrific , you are very pleased with them or very impressed by them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 很多的;很大的;很强的； terrific terrifically Terrific means very great in amount, degree, or intensity.
terrify: [VERB 动词] 吓坏;使极度恐慌;使非常害怕； terrified If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.
terrifying: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 吓人的;令人害怕的； terrifying terrifyingly If something is terrifying , it makes you very frightened.
territorial: [ADJ 形容词] 领土的;领海的； territorial Territorial means concerned with the ownership of a particular area of land or water.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (英国的)国防义勇军士兵； In Britain, the Territorials are the members of the Territorial Army .  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (动物或其行为)地盘意识强的，占地为王的； territorial If you describe an animal or its behaviour as territorial , you mean that it has an area which it regards as its own, and which it defends when other animals try to enter it.
Territorial Army: [N-PROPER 专有名词] (业余时间接受军训的)英国国防义勇军； The Territorial Army is a British armed force whose members are not professional soldiers but train as soldiers in their spare time.
territorial waters: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (一国的)领海； territorial waters A country's territorial waters are the parts of the sea close to its coast which are recognized by international agreement to be under its control, especially with regard to fishing rights.
territory: [N-VAR 可变名词] 领土;领地； territory Territory is land which is controlled by a particular country or ruler.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 属地，地区，托管地(指被别国控制的国家或地区)； A territory is a country or region that is controlled by another country.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (知识)领域;(经验)范围； territory You can use territory to refer to an area of knowledge or experience.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (动物的)领地，地盘； territory An animal's territory is an area which it regards as its own and which it defends when other animals try to enter it.
terror: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恐惧;惊恐;恐慌； terror Terror is very great fear.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指有政治目的的)恐怖活动，恐怖主义； terror Terror is violence or the threat of violence, especially when it is used for political reasons.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 恐怖的事物； terror A terror is something that makes you very frightened.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 讨厌的小孩;淘气鬼;小捣蛋； terror If someone describes a child as a terror , they think that he or she is naughty and difficult to control.
terrorism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 恐怖主义； Terrorism is the use of violence, especially murder and bombing, in order to achieve political aims or to force a government to do something.
terrorist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 恐怖主义分子； terrorist A terrorist is a person who uses violence, especially murder and bombing, in order to achieve political aims.
terrorize: [VERB 动词] 使惊恐;恐吓;威胁； terrorize If someone terrorizes you, they keep you in a state of fear by making it seem likely that they will attack you.
terry: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 尤用于制作毛巾、婴儿尿布等的毛圈棉织物，毛巾布； terry Terry or terry cloth is a type of fabric which has a lot of very small loops covering both sides.
terse: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 声明、评论简短的,短促的,无礼的； terse tersely A terse statement or comment is brief and unfriendly.
tertiary: [ADJ 形容词] 第三的;第三位的;第三阶段的； tertiary Tertiary means third in order, third in importance, or at a third stage of development.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 高等教育； tertiary Tertiary education is education at university or college level.
tertiary sector: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 第三产业； tertiary sector The tertiary sector consists of industries which provide a service, such as transport and finance.
TESL: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 作为第二语言的英语教学； TESL is the teaching of English to people who live in an English-speaking country, but whose first language is not English.
TESOL: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 作为外语的英语教学； TESOL is the teaching of English to people whose first language is not English.
test: [VERB 动词] 检验;试验;测试； test When you test something, you try it, for example by touching it or using it for a short time, in order to find out what it is, what condition it is in, or how well it works.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 试验;测试;检验； test A test is a deliberate action or experiment to find out how well something works.  /  [VERB 动词] 对…进行测试;考核;考查； test If you test someone, you ask them questions or tell them to perform certain actions in order to find out how much they know about a subject or how well they are able to do something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 测试题;考试题;考卷； test A test is a series of questions that you must answer or actions that you must perform in order to show how much you know about a subject or how well you are able to do something.
testament: [N-VAR 可变名词] 证据;证明； testament If one thing is a testament to another, it shows that the other thing exists or is true.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 最新遗嘱;尤指临终遗嘱,临终遗言； Someone's last will and testament is the most recent will that they have made, especially the last will that they make before they die.  /  See also: New Testament ; Old Testament ; �
test bed: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (测试新机器的)试验台，试验床； A test bed is a piece of equipment used for testing new machines.
test case: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 可作为类似案件判决依据的判例案件； A test case is a legal case which becomes an example for deciding other similar cases.
tester: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 测试员;试验员； A tester is a person who has been asked to test a particular thing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 测试器;测试仪； tester A tester is a machine or device that you use to test whether another machine or device is working properly.
testicle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 睾丸； A man's testicles are the two sex glands between his legs that produce sperm.
testicular: [ADJ 形容词] 睾丸的； testicular Testicular means relating to or involving the testicles.
testify: [VERB 动词] (在法庭上)作证，证明； testify When someone testifies in a court of law, they give a statement of what they saw someone do or what they know of a situation, after having promised to tell the truth.  /  [VERB 动词] 证明;证实； testify If one thing testifies to another, it supports the belief that the second thing is true.
testimonial: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (通常由雇主出具的、证明某人品格和能力的)推荐信，证明书； testimonial A testimonial is a written statement about a person's character and abilities, often written by their employer.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (部分票款捐给某运动员或其家人的)纪念赛，义捐比赛； A testimonial is a sports match which is specially arranged so that part of the profit from the tickets sold can be given to a particular player or to a particular player's family.
testimony: [N-VAR 可变名词] (法庭上的)证词； testimony In a court of law, someone's testimony is a formal statement that they make about what they saw someone do or what they know of a situation, after having promised to tell the truth.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 证明;证据； testimony If you say that one thing is testimony to another, you mean that it shows clearly that the second thing has a particular quality.
testing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (问题、局势)难对付的，考验人的，棘手的； testing A testing problem or situation is very difficult to deal with and shows a lot about the character of the person who is dealing with it.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 检验;试验;检测； testing Testing is the activity of testing something or someone in order to find out information.
testis: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 睾丸； A man's testes are his testicles .
test match: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (板球或橄榄球的)国际锦标赛； In cricket and rugby, a test match is a one of a series of matches played between teams representing two countries.
testosterone: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 睾丸素;睾丸酮； Testosterone is a hormone found in men and male animals, which can also be produced artificially.
test pilot: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 试飞员； A test pilot is a pilot who flies aircraft of a new design in order to test their performance.
test run: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (机器、系统的)试运行，初步试验； test run If you give a machine or system a test run , you try it out to see if it will work properly when it is actually in use.
test tube: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 试管； A test tube is a small tube-shaped container made from glass.
test-tube baby: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 试管婴儿； A test-tube baby is a baby that develops from an egg which has been removed from the mother's body, fertilized, and then replaced in her womb in order that it can continue developing.
testy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 急躁的;没耐心的;易怒的； testy testily If you describe someone as testy , you mean that they easily become impatient or angry.
tetanus: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 破伤风； Tetanus is a serious painful disease caused by bacteria getting into wounds.
tetchy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坏脾气的;易怒的;暴躁的； tetchy If you say that someone is tetchy , you mean they are bad-tempered and likely to get angry suddenly without an obvious reason.
tether: [PHRASE 短语] 无计可施;山穷水尽;走投无路； tether If you say that you are at the end of your tether , you mean that you are so worried, tired, and unhappy because of your problems that you feel you cannot cope.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (拴动物的)拴绳，拴链； A tether is a rope or chain which is used to tie an animal to a post or fence so that it can only move around within a small area.  /  [VERB 动词] 将…拴到； tether If you tether an animal or object to something, you attach it there with a rope or chain so that it cannot move very far.
Teutonic: [ADJ 形容词] 典型德国人的;日耳曼人所独具的； Teutonic Teutonic means typical of or relating to German people.
Tex-Mex: [ADJ 形容词] (食物、音乐)兼具墨西哥和美国西南风味的； Tex-Mex You use Tex-Mex to describe things such as food or music that combine typical elements from Mexico and the south-western United States.
text: [N-SING 单数名词] (书籍的)正文，文字部分； text The text of a book is the main part of it, rather than the introduction, pictures, or notes.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 书面材料;文字材料； text Text is any written material.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (讲演、广播、录音的)文字稿，原稿； text The text of a speech, broadcast, or recording is the written version of it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指科学或学术方面的)文献，文本； text A text is a book or other piece of writing, especially one connected with science or learning.
textbook: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 课本;教材;教科书； textbook A textbook is a book containing facts about a particular subject that is used by people studying that subject.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (案件、例子)典型的，典范的； textbook If you say that something is a textbook case or example, you are emphasizing that it provides a clear example of a type of situation or event.
textile: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 织物;纺织品； textile Textiles are types of cloth or fabric, especially ones that have been woven.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 纺织业； textile Textiles are the industries concerned with the manufacture of cloth.
texting: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同 text messaging； Texting is the same as text messaging .
text message: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (手机的)短信，短信息，短消息； A text message is a written message that you send using a mobile phone.
text messaging: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 发送(手机)短信； Text messaging is sending written messages using a mobile phone.
textphone: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (专为有听力障碍的人设计的)文字电话，文本电话； A textphone is a telephone with a screen and a keyboard, designed for people with hearing problems.
textual: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指文学)文本的，原文的； textual Textual means relating to written texts, especially literary texts.
texture: [N-VAR 可变名词] 摸上去的质地，质感，纹理； texture The texture of something is the way that it feels when you touch it, for example how smooth or rough it is.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤指食品、土壤的)结构，构造； texture The texture of something, especially food or soil, is its structure, for example whether it is light with lots of holes, or very heavy and solid.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (音乐、文学作品的)神韵，谐和统一感； texture The texture of a piece of music or a work of literature is the impression that it makes on you as a result of the way that its different elements are combined.
textured: [ADJ 形容词] 质地粗糙的;有纹理的； textured (亦可用于构词) A textured surface is not smooth, but has a particular texture, for example, it feels rough.
-th: [SUFFIX 后缀] (加在以 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 或 13 结尾的数字后构成序数词表示)“第…”； You add -th to numbers written in figures and ending in 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, or 13 in order to form ordinal numbers.
Thai: [ADJ 形容词] 泰国的;泰国人的;泰语的;泰国文化的； Thai Thai means belonging or relating to Thailand, or to its people, language, or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 泰国人； A Thai is a citizen of Thailand, or a person of Thai origin.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 泰语； Thai is the language spoken in Thailand.
thalidomide: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 酞胺哌啶酮，反应停(原为孕妇用药，被发现会导致胎儿四肢畸形后停用)； Thalidomide is a drug which used to be given to pregnant women, before it was discovered that it resulted in babies being born with wrongly shaped arms and legs.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (由于母亲怀孕期间服用了反应停导致的)四肢畸形的； thalidomide Thalidomide is used to describe someone whose arms and legs are wrongly shaped because their mother took thalidomide when she was pregnant.
than: [PREP 介词] (用于形容词、副词的比较级之后，连接比较对象)比； than You use than after a comparative adjective or adverb in order to link two parts of a comparison.  /  [PREP 介词] (数目、数量、价值等)比…(多、少、重要或次要等)； than You use than when you are stating a number, quantity, or value approximately by saying that it is above or below another number, quantity, or value.  /  [CONJ-COORD 连词] 与其说，而不是(连接对比的对象，以表示优先考虑等)； than You use than in order to link two parts of a contrast, for example in order to state a preference.  /  + + + easier said than done » see: easy less than » see: less more than » see: more more often than not » see: often other than » see: other rather than » see: rather �
thank: [CONVENTION 惯用语] 谢谢您;谢谢;多谢； thank You use thank you or, in more informal English, thanks to express your gratitude when someone does something for you or gives you what you want.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 谢谢你，多谢(用于有礼貌地接受或拒绝)； thank You use thank you or, in more informal English, thanks to politely accept or refuse something that has just been offered to you.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 谢谢你，多谢(尤用于礼貌地感谢对方的回答或所说的令人开心的话)； thank You use thank you or, in more informal English, thanks to politely acknowledge what someone has said to you, especially when they have answered your question or said something nice to you.  /  [CONVENTION 惯用语] 谢谢，非常感谢(用于坚决回绝别人的帮助或表示不喜欢别人的举动)； thank You use thank you or thank you very much in order to say firmly that you do not want someone's help or to tell them that you do not like the way that they are behaving towards you.
thankful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 感激的;感谢的;欣慰的； thankful thankfully When you are thankful , you are very happy and relieved that something has happened.
thankfully: [ADV 副词] 幸运的是;幸亏;幸好； thankfully You use thankfully in order to express approval or happiness about a statement that you are making.
thankless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (工作、任务)吃力不讨好的，劳而无功的； thankless If you describe a job or task as thankless , you mean that it is hard work and brings very few rewards.
Thanksgiving: [N-VAR 可变名词] 感恩节(美国的公共假日，在 11 月的第四个星期四)； Thanksgiving In the United States, Thanksgiving or Thanksgiving Day is a public holiday on the fourth Thursday in November.
thankyou: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 谢意；酬谢； thankyou See also: thank ; If you refer to something as a thankyou for what someone has done for you, you mean that it is intended as a way of thanking them.
that: [PRON 代词] 那，那个(指代前面句子里提到的)； that You use that to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.  /  [DET 限定词] 那个人,那个(用来指代已经提到的人或物)； that You use that to refer to someone or something already mentioned.  /  [DET 限定词] 那，那个(指已经谈到过的特定时期)； that When you have been talking about a particular period of time, you use that to indicate that you are still referring to the same period.  /  [PRON 代词] (用于 that of, that which 等短语中引出有关上文提到的某事物的更多信息，而避免重复相关名词)； that You use that in expressions such as that of and that which to introduce more information about something already mentioned, instead of repeating the noun which refers to it.
thatch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 茅草屋顶;稻草屋顶;芦苇屋顶； thatch A thatch or a thatch roof is a roof made from straw or reeds.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (用来盖屋顶的)茅草,稻草，芦苇； Thatch is straw or reeds used to make a roof.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (尤指浓密蓬乱的)头发； thatch You can refer to someone's hair as their thatch of hair, especially when it is very thick and untidy.
thatched: [ADJ 形容词] (房屋或屋顶)用茅草(或稻草、芦苇)铺盖的； A thatched house or a house with a thatched roof has a roof made of straw or reeds.
thatcher: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 盖茅草(或稻草、芦苇)屋顶的人； A thatcher is a person whose job is making roofs from straw or reeds.
thatching: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (茅草、稻草、芦苇等)盖屋顶草料； Thatching is straw or reeds used to make a roof.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 盖草屋顶(的技术)； Thatching is the skill or activity of making roofs from straw or reeds.

thematic: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 主题的;专题的;主旨的； thematic thematically Thematic means concerned with the subject or theme of something, or with themes and topics in general.

thesis: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 命题;论点； thesis A thesis is an idea or theory that is expressed as a statement and is discussed in a logical way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 论文;学位论文； thesis A thesis is a long piece of writing based on your own ideas and research that you do as part of a university degree, especially a higher degree such as a PhD.
