thigh: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大腿;股； Your thighs are the top parts of your legs, between your knees and your hips.
thimble: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 顶针;针箍； A thimble is a small metal or plastic object which you use to protect your finger when you are sewing.
thin: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 窄的;细的； thin Something that is thin is much narrower than it is long.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (人、动物)瘦的； thin thinness A person or animal that is thin has no extra fat on their body .  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (纸、布等)薄的； thin thinly Something such as paper or cloth that is thin is flat and has only a very small distance between its two opposite surfaces.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (液体)稀的，淡的； thin Liquids that are thin are weak and watery.
thine: [PRON-POSS 所有格代词] 你的(yours 在古时、诗歌或宗教中的用语)； Thine is an old-fashioned, poetic, or religious word for 'yours' when you are talking to only one person.
thing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (不能、不必、不愿指明的)东西，事物，特征，事情； thing You can use thing to refer to any object, feature, or event when you cannot, need not, or do not want to refer to it more precisely.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 等等;…之类； thing Thing is used in lists and descriptions to give examples or to increase the range of what you are referring to.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (用于形容词后，与其一起表示该形容词的意思)； thing Thing is often used after an adjective, where it would also be possible just to use the adjective.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (用于强调)任何事情，每件事； thing Thing is often used instead of the pronouns 'anything,' or 'everything' in order to emphasize what you are saying.
thingummy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (指代不知其名或不愿用确切词汇或固有名称指称的人或物)那人，那东西，某某； thingummy You refer to something or someone as thingummy , thingummyjig or thingummybob when you do not know or cannot be bothered to use the proper word or name for them.
thingy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (用来指代不知其名或不愿用确切词汇或固有名称指称的人或物)那人，那东西，某某； thingy You refer to something or someone as thingy when you do not know or cannot be bothered to use the proper word or name for them.
think: [VERB 动词] 想;认为； think If you think that something is the case, you have the opinion that it is the case.  /  [VERB 动词] 感觉;觉得； think If you say that you think that something is true or will happen, you mean that you have the impression that it is true or will happen, although you are not certain of the facts.  /  [VERB 动词] 以某种方式考虑，思考； think If you think in a particular way, you have those general opinions or attitudes.  /  [VERB 动词] 想;考虑;思考； think When you think about ideas or problems, you make a mental effort to consider them.
think back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 回忆;回想； think back If you think back , you make an effort to remember things that happened to you in the past.
thinker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 思考者;(尤指)思想家； thinker A thinker is a person who spends a lot of time thinking deeply about important things, especially someone who is famous for thinking of new or interesting ideas.
thinking: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 思想;观点； thinking The general ideas or opinions of a person or group can be referred to as their thinking .  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 思想;思维;思考； thinking Thinking is the activity of using your brain by considering a problem or possibility or creating an idea.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 有头脑的;有见识的； thinking If you describe someone as a thinking man or woman, you mean that they are intelligent and take an interest in important events and issues, and you approve of this.  /  See also: wishful thinking ; to my way of thinking » see: way �
think out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 仔细思考;全面考虑； If you think something out , you consider all the aspects and details of it before doing anything or making a decision.
think over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 仔细考虑;认真思考； think over If you think something over , you consider it carefully before making a decision.
think piece: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (报纸、杂志上的)评论文章，严肃文章； A think piece is an article in a newspaper or magazine that discusses a particular subject in a serious and thoughtful way.
think-tank: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] (尤指政府的)智囊团，智库； think-tank A think-tank is a group of experts who are gathered together by an organization, especially by a government, in order to consider various problems and try and work out ways to solve them.
think through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 充分考虑,全盘考虑，想透(所有可能的影响或结果)； think through If you think a situation through , you consider it thoroughly, together with all its possible effects or consequences.
think up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 想出，想到(主意、计划)； If you think something up , for example an idea or plan, you invent it using mental effort.
thin-skinned: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脸皮薄的;敏感的;易生气的； thin-skinned If you say that someone is thin-skinned , you mean that they are easily upset by criticism or unpleasantness.
third: [ORD 序数词] 第三； third The third item in a series is the one that you count as number three.  /  [FRACTION 分数词] 三分之一； third A third is one of three equal parts of something.  /  [ADV 副词] 第三点； You say third when you want to make a third point or give a third reason for something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三等学位(英国大学颁发的最低级荣誉学位)； A third is the lowest honours degree that can be obtained from a British university.
third-class: [ADJ 形容词] (英国大学颁发的荣誉学位)三等的； A third-class degree is the lowest honours degree that can be obtained from a British university.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (旧时的车厢或舱位)三等的，票价最低的； third-class In the past, the third-class accommodation on a train or ship was the cheapest and least comfortable accommodation.
third-degree: [ADJ 形容词] (烧伤)三度的，严重的； third-degree Third-degree burns are very severe, destroying tissue under the skin.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 严厉的责问;狠狠的批评； If you say that someone has been given the third degree , you mean that they have been questioned or criticized extremely severely, sometimes with physical violence.
thirdly: [ADV 副词] 第三点； thirdly You use thirdly when you want to make a third point or give a third reason for something.
third party: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (商业协议中的)第三方，第三者;(法律案件中的)第三当事人； third party A third party is someone who is not one of the main people involved in a business agreement or legal case, but who is involved in it in a minor role.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (保险)第三方责任的； Third-party insurance is a type of insurance that pays money to people who are hurt or whose property is damaged as a result of something you have done.
third person: [N-SING 单数名词] (语法)第三人称； In grammar, a statement in the third person is a statement about another person or thing, and not directly about yourself or about the person you are talking to.
third-rate: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 三流的;低劣的； third-rate If you describe something as third-rate , you mean that it is of a very poor quality or standard.
Third Way: [N-SING 单数名词] 第三条道路；中间路线； Third Way The Third Way is used to refer to a set of political beliefs and principles that is neither extremely right-wing nor extremely left-wing.
Third World: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 第三世界;第三世界国家； Third World The countries of Africa, Asia, and South America are sometimes referred to all together as the Third World , especially those parts that are poor, do not have much power, and are not considered to be highly developed.
thirst: [N-VAR 可变名词] 渴;口渴； thirst Thirst is the feeling that you need to drink something.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 干渴;缺水； thirst Thirst is the condition of not having enough to drink.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 渴望;渴求； thirst A thirst for something is a very strong desire for that thing.  /  [VERB 动词] 渴望;渴求； thirst If you say that someone thirsts for something, you mean that they have a strong desire for it.
thirsty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 渴的;干渴的； thirsty thirstily If you are thirsty , you feel a need to drink something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 渴望的;渴求的； thirsty If you are thirsty for something, you have a strong desire for it.
thirteen: [NUM 数词] (数字) 13； Thirteen is the number 13.
thirteenth: [ORD 序数词] 第十三； The thirteenth item in a series is the one that you count as number thirteen.
thirtieth: [ORD 序数词] 第三十； The thirtieth item in a series is the one that you count as number thirty.
thirty: [NUM 数词] (数字) 30； Thirty is the number 30.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 三十多，三十几(指 30 至 39 之间的数字)； When you talk about the thirties , you are referring to numbers between 30 and 39.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 三十年代(指 1930 年至 1939 年)； The thirties is the decade between 1930 and 1939.
this: [DET 限定词] (指代先前提及的人或物)这，这个； this You use this to refer back to a particular person or thing that has been mentioned or implied.  /  [PRON 代词] (引出将要谈论的人或物)下面(这个)，以下； You use this to introduce someone or something that you are going to talk about.  /  [PRON 代词] 这一点(指前一句或几句话中提到的观点或情况)； this You use this to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.  /  [DET 限定词] (叙述时引出新出现的人或物)这个，一个； this In spoken English, people use this to introduce a person or thing into a story.
thistle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 蓟(叶片带刺、开紫色花的野生植物)； A thistle is a wild plant which has leaves with sharp points and purple flowers.
thither: [ADV 副词] 到那里;向那边； thither Thither means to the place that has already been mentioned.
thong: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 皮带;塑料带;橡胶带； A thong is a long thin strip of leather, plastic, or rubber.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 丁字裤； A thong is a narrow band of cloth that is worn between a person's legs to cover up his or her sexual organs, and that is held up by a piece of string around the waist.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 人字拖鞋； Thongs are open shoes which are held on your foot by a V-shaped strap that goes between your big toe and the toe next to it.
thoracic: [ADJ 形容词] 胸的;胸腔的;胸廓的； thoracic Thoracic means relating to or affecting your thorax.
thorax: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胸部;胸腔;胸廓； Your thorax is the part of your body between your neck and your waist.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (昆虫的)胸部，胸节； An insect's thorax is the central part of its body to which the legs and wings are attached.
thorn: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某些植物、树木上的)刺，棘刺； thorn Thorns are the sharp points on some plants and trees, for example on a rose bush.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 荆棘;带刺的树;带刺小灌木； thorn A thorn or a thorn bush or a thorn tree is a bush or tree which has a lot of thorns on it.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 肉中刺;长期困扰的问题； thorn If you describe someone or something as a thorn in your side or a thorn in your flesh , you mean that they are a continuous problem to you or annoy you.
thorny: [ADJ 形容词] (植物、树木)带刺的，多刺的； thorny A thorny plant or tree is covered with thorns.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (问题)棘手的，复杂难解的，令人头疼的； thorny If you describe a problem as thorny , you mean that it is very complicated and difficult to solve, and that people are often unwilling to discuss it.
thorough: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行为、活动)详细的，全面的，彻底的； thorough thoroughly thoroughness A thorough action or activity is one that is done very carefully and in a detailed way so that nothing is forgotten.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人仔细的，严谨的； thorough thoroughness Someone who is thorough is always very careful in their work, so that nothing is forgotten.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 完全的，绝对的(用来强调程度)； thorough thoroughly Thorough is used to emphasize the great degree or extent of something.
thoroughbred: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 纯种马； A thoroughbred is a horse that has parents that are of the same high quality breed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 良种赛马； thoroughbred A thoroughbred is a particular breed of racing horse.
thoroughfare: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大道;大街;通衢； thoroughfare A thoroughfare is a main road in a town or city which usually has shops along it and a lot of traffic.
thoroughgoing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 完全的;十足的； thoroughgoing You use thoroughgoing to emphasize that someone or something is fully or completely the type of person or thing specified.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 仔细的;彻底的； thoroughgoing If you describe a piece of work as thoroughgoing , you approve of it because it has been carefully and thoroughly put together.
those: [DET 限定词] (指代已经提及的人或物)那些； those You use those to refer to people or things which have already been mentioned.  /  [DET 限定词] 那些(尤用于指示或指向在时间、空间上离自己稍远的人或物)； those You use those when you are referring to people or things that are a distance away from you in position or time, especially when you indicate or point to them.  /  [DET 限定词] (用于提供更多的细节、信息)； those You use those to refer to someone or something when you are going to give details or information about them.  /  [PRON 代词] (用来对已经提及的事物作补充说明)； those You use those to introduce more information about something already mentioned, instead of repeating the noun which refers to it.
thou: [PRON-SING 单数型代词] 你，汝，尔(旧用词，现亦用于诗歌或宗教类语境，用作主语)； See also: holier-than-thou ; Thou is an old-fashioned, poetic, or religious word for 'you' when you are talking to only one person.
though: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 尽管;虽然； though You use though to introduce a statement in a subordinate clause which contrasts with the statement in the main clause.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 不过;可是;然而； though You use though to introduce a subordinate clause which gives some information that is relevant to the main clause and weakens the force of what it is saying.  /  [ADV 副词] 不过;但是； though You use though to indicate that the information in a clause contrasts with or modifies information given in a previous sentence or sentences.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不是吹牛;我不是自夸； though You can say though I say so myself or even though I say it myself when you are praising yourself or something you have done, but do not want to sound too proud.
thought: + + + Thought is the past tense and past participle of think .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 念头;想法;主意； thought A thought is an idea that you have in your mind.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 心思;思想； thought A person's thoughts are their mind, or all the ideas in their mind when they are concentrating on one particular thing.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (关于具体问题的)观点，看法； thought A person's thoughts are their opinions on a particular subject.
thoughtful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 沉思的;默想的;认真思考的； thoughtful thoughtfully If you are thoughtful , you are quiet and serious because you are thinking about something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 体贴入微的;考虑周到的； thoughtful thoughtfully thoughtfulness If you describe someone as thoughtful , you approve of them because they remember what other people want, need, or feel, and try not to upset them.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (书籍、电影、讲话等)严肃的，思想性强的； thoughtful thoughtfully If you describe something such as a book, film, or speech as thoughtful , you mean that it is serious and well thought out.
thoughtless: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不顾及他人的;欠考虑的； thoughtless thoughtlessly thoughtlessness If you describe someone as thoughtless , you are critical of them because they forget or ignore other people's wants, needs, or feelings.
thought-provoking: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (书籍、电影等)发人深省的，引人深思的； thought-provoking If something such as a book or a film is thought-provoking , it contains interesting ideas that make people think seriously.
thousand: [NUM 数词] (数字) 1,000； thousand A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000.  /  [QUANT 数量词] 数千;成千上万； thousand If you refer to thousands of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.  /  a thousand and one » see: one �
thousandth: [ORD 序数词] 第一千； thousandth 第一千(强调某事发生次数之多) The thousandth item in a series is the one that you count as number one thousand.  /  [FRACTION 分数词] 千分之一； thousandth A thousandth is one of a thousand equal parts of something.
thrall: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 控制;奴役;束缚； thrall If you say that someone is in thrall to a person or thing, you mean that they are completely in their power or are greatly influenced by them.
thrash: [VERB 动词] (在比赛、竞赛中)轻松击败，以大比分战胜； thrash If one player or team thrashes another in a game or contest, they defeat them easily or by a large score.  /  [VERB 动词] (作为惩罚)连续击打，接连殴打，痛打； thrash If you thrash someone, you hit them several times as a punishment.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 猛烈摆动;翻来覆去;剧烈扭动(四肢)； thrash If someone thrashes about , or thrashes their arms or legs about , they move in a wild or violent way, often hitting against something.  /  [VERB 动词] 连续击打;猛烈抽打； thrash If a person or thing thrashes something, or thrashes at something, they hit it continually in a violent or noisy way.
thrashing: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (运动员、运动队的)遭痛打，大败，惨败； thrashing If one player or team gives another one a thrashing , they defeat them easily or by a large score.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (作为惩罚的)连续击打，接连殴打，痛打； thrashing If someone gives someone else a thrashing , they hit them several times as a punishment.  /  See also: thrash ; �
thrash out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 经反复讨论制订出(计划、协议)； If people thrash out something such as a plan or an agreement, they decide on it after a great deal of discussion.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 讨论解决，商讨解决(问题、争端)； thrash out If people thrash out a problem or a dispute, they discuss it thoroughly until they reach an agreement.
thread: [N-VAR 可变名词] (尤指用于缝纫的)细线，细丝； thread Thread or a thread is a long very thin piece of a material such as cotton, nylon, or silk, especially one that is used in sewing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 主线;思路;脉络； thread The thread of an argument, a story, or a situation is an aspect of it that connects all the different parts together.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 线状物;一线； thread A thread of something such as liquid, light, or colour is a long thin line or piece of it.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 衣服； thread You can refer to clothes as threads .
threadbare: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服、地毯等)破旧的，磨薄的，陈旧的； threadbare Threadbare clothes, carpets, and other pieces of cloth look old, dull, and very thin, because they have been worn or used too much.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (活动、想法、论点)无力的，不充分的，陈旧乏味的； threadbare If you describe an activity, an idea, or an argument as threadbare , you mean that it is very weak, or inadequate, or old and no longer interesting.
threat: [N-VAR 可变名词] 构成威胁的人(或事物);祸根； threat A threat to a person or thing is a danger that something unpleasant might happen to them.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 威胁;恐吓； threat A threat is a statement by someone that they will do something unpleasant, especially if you do not do what they want.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 受到威胁； threat If a person or thing is under threat , there is a danger that something unpleasant might be done to them, or that they might cease to exist.
threaten: [VERB 动词] 威胁;恐吓； threaten If a person threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.  /  [VERB 动词] 危害到;威胁到； threaten If something or someone threatens a person or thing, they are likely to harm that person or thing.  /  [VERB 动词] (坏事)可能发生，将要发生； threaten If something unpleasant threatens to happen, it seems likely to happen.  /  See also: threatened ; threatening ; �
threatened: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 受到威胁的;感到危险的； threatened See also: threaten ; If you feel threatened , you feel as if someone is trying to harm you.
threatening: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行为)有威胁性的，危险的； threatening threateningly You can describe someone's behaviour as threatening when you think that they are trying to harm you.
three: [NUM 数词] (数字) 3； three Three is the number 3.
three-cornered: [ADJ 形容词] (争端、竞赛、比赛等)三角的，三人的，三方的； three-cornered If you describe something such as a disagreement, competition, or game as three-cornered , you mean that it involves three people, groups, or teams.
three-dimensional: [ADJ 形容词] 三维的(缩略形式为 3-D)； three-dimensional A three-dimensional object is solid rather than flat, because it can be measured in three different directions, usually the height, length, and width.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (照片、图像、电影)三维的，有立体感的(缩略形式为 3-D)； three-dimensional A three-dimensional picture, image, or film looks as though it is deep or solid rather than flat.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (虚构的人物)栩栩如生的，逼真的，鲜活的； three-dimensional If you describe fictional characters as three-dimensional you mean that they seem real and natural.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (艺术、设计)立体的(缩略形式为 3-D)； three-dimensional Three-dimensional art or design is produced by carving or shaping stone, wood, clay, or other materials.
three-fourths: [QUANT 数量词] 四分之三(美国英语)； three-fourths In American English, people sometimes use three-fourths to mean three-quarters .
three-line whip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (要求某政党议员参加议会并按照要求就某议题投票的)紧急指令； A three-line whip is a situation where the MPs in a political party are ordered to attend parliament and vote in a particular way on a particular issue.
three-piece: [ADJ 形容词] (衣服)三件套的(通常包括男式上衣、马甲和裤子)； A three-piece suit is a set of three pieces of matching clothing, usually a man's jacket, waistcoat, and trousers.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (沙发)三件套的； A three-piece suite is a sofa and two matching armchairs.
three-point turn: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三点转向(指司机先向前转向，再向后转向，然后向前开的转向方法)； When the driver of a vehicle does a three-point turn , he or she turns the vehicle by driving forwards in a curve, then backwards in a curve, and then forwards in a curve.
three-quarter: [ADJ 形容词] (正常尺寸、标准量度的)四分之三的； three-quarter You can use three-quarter to describe something which is three fourths of the usual size or three fourths of a standard measurement.
three-quarters: [QUANT 数量词] 四分之三； three-quarters Three-quarters is an amount that is three out of four equal parts of something.
three Rs: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (儿童必须掌握的) 三R 技能，读写算技能； three Rs When talking about children's education, the three Rs are the basic skills of reading, writing, and arithmetic.
threesome: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三人一组； A threesome is a group of three people.
three-wheeler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脚踏三轮车;三轮汽车； A three-wheeler is a bicycle or car with three wheels.
thresh: [VERB 动词] 给(玉米、小麦、水稻等)脱粒;打谷； thresh threshing When a cereal such as corn, wheat, or rice is threshed , it is beaten in order to separate the grains from the rest of the plant.
threshold: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 门槛;门口； threshold The threshold of a building or room is the floor in the doorway, or the doorway itself.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (某事发生或改变的)界限，阈，起始点； threshold A threshold is an amount, level, or limit on a scale.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 在…开端;将要经历;面临着； threshold If you are on the threshold of something exciting or new, you are about to experience it.
threw: + + + Threw is the past tense of throw .
thrice: [ADV 副词] 三次； thrice Something that happens thrice happens three times.  /  [ADV 副词] 三倍； thrice You can use thrice to indicate that something is three times the size, value, or intensity of something else.
thrift: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 节俭;节省;节约； thrift Thrift is the quality and practice of being careful with money and not wasting things.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 储蓄银行； A thrift or a thrift institution is a kind of savings bank.
thrift shop: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (为慈善机构募捐而出售旧货的)廉价旧货店； A thrift shop or thrift store is a shop that sells used goods cheaply and gives its profits to a charity.
thrifty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 节俭的;节省的;节约的； thrifty If you say that someone is thrifty , you are praising them for saving money, not buying unnecessary things, and not wasting things.
thrill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (突然而强烈的)激动，狂喜，恐惧； thrill If something gives you a thrill , it gives you a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使狂喜;使激动;使极度兴奋； thrill If something thrills you, or if you thrill at it, it gives you a feeling of great pleasure and excitement.  /  See also: thrilled ; thrilling ;  /  [PHRASE 短语] 惊险刺激； thrill If you refer to thrills and spills , you are referring to an experience which is exciting and full of surprises.
thrilled: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 欣喜若狂的;非常开心的； thrilled 兴奋不已;非常愉快 If someone is thrilled , they are extremely pleased about something.  /  See also: thrill ; �
thriller: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 惊险小说(或电影、戏剧)； thriller A thriller is a book, film, or play that tells an exciting fictional story about something such as criminal activities or spying.
thrilling: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 扣人心弦的;激动人心的;引人入胜的； thrilling thrillingly Something that is thrilling is very exciting and enjoyable.  /  See also: thrill ; �
thrive: [VERB 动词] 欣欣向荣;茁壮成长;兴旺发达； thrive If someone or something thrives , they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong.  /  [VERB 动词] (尤指在别人觉得困难的时候)以…为乐，可以出色应对； thrive If you say that someone thrives on a particular situation, you mean that they enjoy it or that they can deal with it very well, especially when other people find it unpleasant or difficult.
throat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 咽喉;喉咙;嗓子； throat Your throat is the back of your mouth and the top part of the tubes that go down into your stomach and your lungs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 喉部;颈前部； throat Your throat is the front part of your neck.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 清嗓子； throat If you clear your throat , you cough once in order to make it easier to speak or to attract people's attention.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 向…反复灌输;向…不断强调;迫使…接受； throat If you ram something down someone's throat or force it down their throat , you keep mentioning a situation or idea in order to make them accept it or believe it.
throaty: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (说话声或笑声)低沉的，沙哑的； A throaty voice or laugh is low and rather rough.
throb: [VERB 动词] (身体局部)抽动，阵痛； throb If part of your body throbs , you feel a series of strong and usually painful beats there.  /  [VERB 动词] 震动作响;有规律地颤动； throb If something throbs , it vibrates and makes a steady noise.
throes: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (尤指最后阶段的)困境,痛苦； throes If someone is experiencing something very unpleasant or emotionally painful, you can say that they are in the throes of it, especially when it is in its final stages.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 正忙于…;处于…困境之中； throes If you are in the throes of doing or experiencing something, especially something difficult, you are busy doing it or are deeply involved in it.  /  See also: death throes ; �
thrombosis: [N-VAR 可变名词] 血栓形成； thrombosis See also: coronary thrombosis ; deep vein thrombosis ; Thrombosis is the formation of a blood clot in a person's heart or in one of their blood vessels, which can cause death.
throne: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (君王的)宝座，御座； A throne is a decorative chair used by a king, queen, or emperor on important official occasions.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 王位;皇位； throne You can talk about the throne as a way of referring to the position of being king, queen, or emperor.
throng: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一大群人;人群； throng A throng is a large crowd of people.  /  [VERB 动词] (人群)涌向，蜂拥； throng When people throng somewhere, they go there in great numbers.  /  [VERB 动词] 挤满;群集； throng thronged If people throng a place, they are present there in great numbers.
throttle: [VERB 动词] 掐死;勒死;掐住…的脖子;使窒息； throttle To throttle someone means to kill or injure them by squeezing their throat or tightening something around it and preventing them from breathing.  /  [VERB 动词] 阻挡;阻碍;压制;扼杀； If you say that something or someone is throttling a process, institution, or group, you mean that they are restricting it severely or destroying it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (汽车、飞机的)节流阀，油门杆，油门踏板； throttle The throttle of a motor vehicle or aircraft is the device, lever, or pedal that controls the quantity of fuel entering the engine and is used to control the vehicle's speed.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 功率;马力； throttle Throttle is the power that is obtained by using a throttle.
throttle back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 减速;调节油门使减速； throttle back If you throttle back , or you throttle back the engine, when driving a motor vehicle or flying an aircraft, you make it go slower by reducing the quantity of fuel entering the engine.
through: In addition to the uses shown below, through is used in phrasal verbs such as 'see through', 'think through', and 'win through'.  /  [PREP 介词] 穿过,通过(洞、口子、管道等);从…的一端到另一端； through To move through something such as a hole, opening, or pipe means to move directly from one side or end of it to the other.  /  [PREP 介词] 切开;割断;凿穿； through To cut through something means to cut it in two pieces or to make a hole in it.  /  [PREP 介词] 穿过，通过(城市、地区、国家);遍及； through To go through a town, area, or country means to travel across it or in it.
throughout: [PREP 介词] 自始至终;从头到尾;贯穿； throughout If you say that something happens throughout a particular period of time, you mean that it happens during the whole of that period.  /  [PREP 介词] 遍及;遍布； throughout If you say that something happens or exists throughout a place, you mean that it happens or exists in all parts of that place.
throughput: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (组织、系统在一定时间内的)工作量，生产量，吞吐量； throughput The throughput of an organization or system is the amount of things it can do or deal with in a particular period of time.
throw: [VERB 动词] 扔;抛;投;掷； throw throwing When you throw an object that you are holding, you move your hand or arm quickly and let go of the object, so that it moves through the air.  /  [VERB 动词] 急伸，猛动(身体或某部位)； throw If you throw your body or part of your body into a particular position or place, you move it there suddenly and with a lot of force.  /  [VERB 动词] (随手)抛，丢，扔； throw If you throw something into a particular place or position, you put it there in a quick and careless way.  /  [VERB 动词] 摔;掼;抛； throw To throw someone into a particular place or position means to force them roughly into that place or position.
throw around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…挂在嘴边;念叨； If you say that someone throws around a word or name, you disapprove of the fact that they mention it frequently, often in an inappropriate way in order to impress someone.
throw aside: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 放弃，拒绝接受(生活方式、原则、思想)； If you throw aside a way of life, a principle, or an idea, you abandon it or reject it.
throw away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 扔掉，丢掉(废弃物)； throw away When you throw away or throw out something that you do not want, you get rid of it, for example by putting it in a rubbish container.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 错过，浪费(机会、优势或好处)； See also: throwaway ; If you throw away an opportunity, advantage, or benefit, you waste it, rather than using it sensibly.
throwaway: [ADJ 形容词] 一次性的;用完即弃的； throwaway 一次性产品 A throwaway product is intended to be used only for a short time, and then to be thrown away.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (讲话、动作)不经意的，随意的； throwaway If you say that someone makes a throwaway remark or gesture, you mean that they make it in a casual way, although it may be important, or have some serious or humorous effect.
throwback: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 复古;回归； throwback If you say that something is a throwback to a former time, you mean that it is like something that existed a long time ago.
throw back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 翻旧账;揭疮疤； If you throw something back at a person, you remind them of something bad they did in the past, in order to upset them.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 不得不动用，只好依靠(自己的能力或资源)； If someone is thrown back on their own powers or resources, they have to use them, because there is nothing else they can use.
throw down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 公然挑衅;大胆挑战； If you throw down a challenge to someone, you do something new or unexpected in a bold or forceful manner that will probably cause them to reply or react equally strongly.
throw-in: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (足球或橄榄球比赛中的)掷边线球，掷界外球； When there is a throw-in in a football or rugby match, the ball is thrown back onto the field after it has been kicked off it.
throw in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 无意中说;随口说； If you throw in a remark when having a conversation, you add it in a casual or unexpected way.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 免费赠送;额外奉送； throw in If a person who is selling something throws in something extra, they give you the extra thing and only ask you to pay for the first thing.
thrown: + + + Thrown is the past participle of throw .
throw off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 摆脱，抛掉(束缚，苦恼)； throw off If you throw off something that is restricting you or making you unhappy, you get rid of it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (向空中)释放，散发出； throw off If something throws off a substance, it produces it and releases it into the air.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 甩掉，摆脱(追赶者)； If you throw off people who are chasing you or trying to find you, you do something unexpected that makes them unable to catch you or find you.  /  See also: throw ; �
throw out: »see: throw away 1 ;  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (法官)不受理，不立案； throw out If a judge throws out a case, he or she rejects it and the accused person does not have to stand trial.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 撵走;赶走;开除;将…除名； If you throw someone out , you force them to leave a place or group.
throw together: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 仓促做成;快速张罗出； If you throw something together , for example a meal or a costume, you make it quickly and not very carefully.  /  [PHR-V-RECIP 相互动词短语] 使…相遇相识； If people are thrown together by a situation or event, it causes them to get to know each other, even though they may not want to.
throw up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 呕吐;呕出； When someone throws up , they vomit.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 激起，扬起，搅起，溅起(尘土、石子或水)； If something throws up dust, stones, or water, when it moves or hits the ground, it causes them to rise up into the air.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 匆匆搭建起来;匆忙建成； If you say that a building or structure is thrown up , you mean that it is built or made very quickly, usually so that it is not of very good quality.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 产生;突出;凸显； To throw up a particular person or thing means to produce them or cause them to become noticeable.
thrum: [VERB 动词] (机器、引擎)嗡嗡响，发出沉闷声； thrum When something such as a machine or engine thrums , it makes a low beating sound.
thrush: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鸫； A thrush is a fairly small bird with a brown back and a spotted breast.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 鹅口疮;真菌性口炎;念珠菌性阴道炎； Thrush is a medical condition caused by a fungus.
thrust: [VERB 动词] 猛推;猛塞;刺;戳； thrust If you thrust something or someone somewhere, you push or move them there quickly with a lot of force.  /  [VERB 动词] 挤;推;扎； thrust If you thrust your way somewhere, you move there, pushing between people or things which are in your way.  /  [VERB 动词] 露在外面;凸出来； thrust If something thrusts up or out of something else, it sticks up or sticks out in a noticeable way.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (车辆等的)推力，反压力，侧向压力； thrust Thrust is the power or force that is required to make a vehicle move in a particular direction.
thrust upon: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 迫使…接受;把…强加于;强人所难； thrust upon If something is thrust upon you, you are forced to have it, deal with it, or experience it.
thruway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 高速公路； A thruway is a wide road that is specially designed so that a lot of traffic can move along it very quickly.
thud: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (重物撞击软物时的)沉闷声，低沉声； thud A thud is a dull sound, such as that which a heavy object makes when it hits something soft.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出沉重的声音;砰砰作响； thud thudding If something thuds somewhere, it makes a dull sound, usually when it falls onto or hits something else.  /  [VERB 动词] (心脏)咚咚跳，怦怦跳； thud When your heart thuds , it beats strongly and rather quickly, for example because you are very frightened or very happy.
thug: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 恶棍;凶手;罪犯； thug You can refer to a violent person or criminal as a thug .
thuggery: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 罪行;粗暴行径； Thuggery is rough, violent behaviour.
thuggish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 凶狠的;粗野的;蛮横的； thuggish If you describe a person or their behaviour as thuggish , you mean they behave in a violent, rough, or threatening way.
thumb: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 大拇指； thumb Your thumb is the short thick part on the side of your hand next to your four fingers.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (手套的)拇指部分； The thumb of a glove is the part which a person's thumb fits into.  /  [VERB 动词] (站在路边，伸出手，拇指向上)请求搭便车，拦车； thumb If you thumb a lift or thumb a ride, you stand by the side of the road holding out your thumb until a driver stops and gives you a lift.  /  See also: well-thumbed ;
thumbnail: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拇指甲； Your thumbnail is the nail on your thumb.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 简要的;概括的;简略的； A thumbnail sketch or account is a very short description of an event, idea, or plan which gives only the main details.
thumbprint: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拇指纹； A thumbprint is a mark made by a person's thumb which shows the pattern of lines on its surface.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 痕迹； thumbprint If you say that something such as a project has someone's thumbprint on it, you mean that it has features that make it obvious that they have been involved with it.
thumbscrew: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拇指夹(旧时的一种刑具)； A thumbscrew is an object that was used in the past to torture people by crushing their thumbs.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 极大的压力； If someone puts the thumbscrews on you, they start to put you under extreme pressure in order to force you to do something.
thumbs down: [N-SING 单数名词] 否定;反对;拒绝； If you say that someone gives a plan, idea, or suggestion the thumbs-down , you are indicating that they do not approve of it and refuse to accept it.
thumbs-up: [N-SING 单数名词] 竖起大拇指(表示赞成或满意)； thumbs-up A thumbs-up or a thumbs-up sign is a sign that you make by raising your thumb to show that you agree with someone, that you are happy with an idea or situation, or that everything is all right.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 赞同;接受； If you give a plan, idea, or suggestion the thumbs-up , you indicate that you approve of it and are willing to accept it.
thumbtack: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 图钉； A thumbtack is a short pin with a broad flat top which is used for fastening papers or pictures to a board, wall, or other surface.
thumb through: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 匆匆翻阅，浏览(书籍、杂志)； If you thumb through something such as a book or magazine, you turn the pages quickly rather than reading each page carefully.
thump: [VERB 动词] (常指用拳头)猛击，重击，捶打； thump If you thump something, you hit it hard, usually with your fist.  /  [VERB 动词] (用拳头)打击，捶打； thump If you thump someone, you attack them and hit them with your fist.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 重重地摔出;沉闷地撞击； thump If you thump something somewhere or if it thumps there, it makes a loud, dull sound by hitting something else.  /  [VERB 动词] (心脏)怦怦跳，咚咚跳； thump When your heart thumps , it beats strongly and quickly, usually because you are afraid or excited.
thumping: [ADJ 形容词] 极大的;了不起的;严重的； thumping Thumping is used to emphasize that something is very great or severe.  /  See also: thump ; �
thunder: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 雷;雷声； thunder Thunder is the loud noise that you hear from the sky after a flash of lightning, especially during a storm.  /  [VERB 动词] 打雷； thunder When it thunders , a loud noise comes from the sky after a flash of lightning.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 雷鸣般的响声;轰隆声； thunder The thunder of something that is moving or making a sound is the loud deep noise it makes.  /  [VERB 动词] 轰隆隆地快速移动； thunder If something or someone thunders somewhere, they move there quickly and with a lot of noise.
thunderbolt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雷电；霹雳； A thunderbolt is a flash of lightning, accompanied by thunder, which strikes something such as a building or a tree.
thunderclap: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雷声;雷鸣； A thunderclap is a short loud noise that you hear in the sky just after you see a flash of lightning.
thundercloud: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雷雨云； A thundercloud is a large dark cloud that is likely to produce thunder and lightning.
thunderous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (声音)轰隆隆的，低沉的，低吼的； thunderous If you describe a noise as thunderous , you mean that it is very loud and deep.
thunderstorm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 雷暴;雷雨； A thunderstorm is a storm in which there is thunder and lightning and a lot of heavy rain.
thunderstruck: [ADJ 形容词] 极其惊讶的;震惊的； If you say that someone is thunderstruck , you mean that they are extremely surprised or shocked.

thyme: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 百里香(一种调料)； Thyme is a type of herb used in cooking.
thyroid: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 甲状腺； Your thyroid or your thyroid gland is a gland in your neck that produces chemicals which control the way your body grows and functions.
thyself: [PRON-REFL 反身代词] 你本人，你自己(yourself 在古时、诗歌或宗教中的用语)； thyself Thyself is an old-fashioned, poetic, or religious word for 'yourself' when you are talking to only one person.
tiara: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指上流社会妇女在正式场合佩戴的)冕状宝石头饰； A tiara is a metal band shaped like half a circle and decorated with jewels which a woman of very high social rank wears on her head at formal social occasions; also used of similar ornaments that girls or women wear on their heads.
tibia: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胫骨； Your tibia is the inner bone of the two bones in the lower part of your leg.
tic: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (面部或身体局部的)抽搐，痉挛； tic If someone has a tic , a part of their face or body keeps making a small uncontrollable movement, for example because they are tired or have a nervous illness.
tick: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 钩号(符号为√)； tick A tick is a written mark like a V: ✓.  /  [VERB 动词] 在纸上打钩； tick If you tick something that is written on a piece of paper, you put a tick next to it.  /  [VERB 动词] (钟表)嘀嗒作响，发出嘀嗒声； tick tick away 同 tick ticking When a clock or watch ticks , it makes a regular series of short sounds as it works.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (钟表的)嘀嗒声； tick The tick of a clock or watch is the series of short sounds it makes when it is working, or one of those sounds.
tick away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指等候时时间)嘀嘀嗒嗒地过去，一分一秒地过去； See also: tick ; or tick on If you say that the clock or time is ticking away , ticking by , or ticking on , you mean that time is passing, especially when there is something that needs to be done or when you are waiting for something to happen.
tick box: 打钩框； A tick box is a small square on a form, questionnaire, or test in which you put a tick to show that you agree with a statement.
ticker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 心;心脏； Your ticker is your heart.
ticker tape: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (印有信息的窄长条)纸带(在美国城市中，人们有时从高楼上抛下纸带以示庆祝或向某人表示敬意)； ticker tape Ticker tape consists of long narrow strips of paper on which information such as stock exchange prices is printed by a machine.
ticket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (剧院、运动场、表演等的)入场券，门票，票； ticket A ticket is a small, official piece of paper or card which shows that you have paid to enter a place such as a theatre or a sports ground, or shows that you have paid for a journey.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (交通)罚款通知单，违章通知单； ticket A ticket is an official piece of paper which orders you to pay a fine or to appear in court because you have committed a driving or parking offence.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兑奖券;彩票； ticket A ticket for a game of chance such as a raffle or a lottery is a piece of paper with a number on it.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (竞选时所代表的)政党;(竞选时所支持的)纲领，政见； ticket The particular ticket on which a person fights an election is the party they represent or the policies they support.
ticketing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 售票;出票； Ticketing is the act or activity of selling tickets.
ticking off: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 斥责;责骂； ticking off If you give someone a ticking off , you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.
tickle: [VERB 动词] 胳肢;使笑个不停； When you tickle someone, you move your fingers lightly over a sensitive part of their body, often in order to make them laugh.  /  [VERB 动词] 使发痒;使难受； tickle If something tickles you or tickles , it causes an irritating feeling by lightly touching a part of your body.  /  [VERB 动词] 使开心;使高兴； tickle tickled If a fact or a situation tickles you, it amuses you or gives you pleasure.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 非常开心； tickle If you are tickled pink , you are extremely pleased about something.
ticklish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (问题、情况、任务)艰难的，难处理的;棘手的； ticklish A ticklish problem, situation, or task is difficult and needs to be dealt with carefully.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 怕痒的;怕胳肢的； ticklish Someone who is ticklish is sensitive to being tickled, and laughs as soon as you tickle them.
tick off: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 在…上打钩； If you tick off items on a list, you write a tick or other mark next to them, in order to show that they have been dealt with.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 怒斥;责骂； See also: ticking off ; If you tick someone off , you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 惹恼;激怒； If you say that something ticks you off , you mean that it annoys you.
tick over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (引擎)空转，低速运转； If an engine is ticking over , it is running at a low speed or rate, for example when it is switched on but you are not actually using it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (人、系统、业务)慢吞吞地工作，进展缓慢； If a person, system, or business is ticking over , they are working steadily, but not producing very much or making much progress.
tidal: [ADJ 形容词] 潮汐的;受潮汐影响的； tidal Tidal means relating to or produced by tides.
tidal wave: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 海啸;潮波;异常高的潮位； tidal wave A tidal wave is a very large wave, often caused by an earthquake, that flows onto the land and destroys things.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (感情、事物或人出现的)高潮期； tidal wave If you describe a very large number of emotions, things, or people as a tidal wave , you mean that they all occur at the same time.
tiddler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小鱼； A tiddler is a very small fish of any kind.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小人物;小玩意儿； tiddler If you refer to a person or thing as a tiddler , you mean that they are very unimportant or small, especially when compared to other people or things of the same type.
tiddly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 微醉的； If someone is tiddly , they are slightly drunk.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 很小的； tiddly If you describe a thing as tiddly , you mean that it is very small.
tiddlywink: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 弹塑料片游戏； Tiddlywinks is a game in which the players try to make small round pieces of plastic jump into a container, by pressing their edges with a larger piece of plastic.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (弹塑料片游戏所用的)塑料圆片； Tiddlywinks are the small round piece of plastic used in the game of tiddlywinks.
tide: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 潮;潮水;潮汐； tide The tide is the regular change in the level of the sea on the shore.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (不断冲刷海岸的)潮水，潮汐； tide A tide is a current in the sea that is caused by the regular and continuous movement of large areas of water towards and away from the shore.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (观点等的)潮流，趋势； tide The tide of opinion, for example, is what the majority of people think at a particular time.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] (无法抗拒的)潮流，浪潮； tide People sometimes refer to events or forces that are difficult or impossible to control as the tide of history, for example.
tide over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (尤指通过借钱)帮助…渡过难关； tide over If you do something for someone to tide them over , you help them through a period when they are having difficulties, especially by lending them money.
tidings: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 消息； tidings You can use tidings to refer to news that someone tells you.
tidy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 整洁的;整齐的； tidy tidily tidiness Something that is tidy is neat and is arranged in an organized way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 整洁的;有条理的； tidy tidiness Someone who is tidy likes everything to be neat and arranged in an organized way.  /  [VERB 动词] 收拾，整理(房间、橱柜等)； When you tidy a place such as a room or cupboard, you make it neat by putting things in their proper places.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 一大笔钱； tidy A tidy amount of money is a large amount.
tidy away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 收拾;拾掇； When you tidy something away , you put it in something else so that it is not in the way.
tidy up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 收拾;整理； tidy up When you tidy up or tidy a place up , you put things back in their proper places so that everything is neat.
tie: [VERB 动词] 系；扣；捆；将…打成结； tie If you tie two things together or tie them, you fasten them together with a knot.  /  [VERB 动词] (用绳索)捆扎，固定，系牢； tie If you tie something or someone in a particular place or position, you put them there and fasten them using rope or string.  /  [VERB 动词] 用绳子或布捆扎； tie If you tie a piece of string or cloth around something or tie something with a piece of string or cloth, you put the piece of string or cloth around it and fasten the ends together.  /  [VERB 动词] 打(结或蝴蝶结)；将…打成(结或蝴蝶结)； tie If you tie a knot or bow in something or tie something in a knot or bow, you fasten the ends together.
tie-break: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (网球比赛中各胜6局后的)决胜局，抢七局； A tie-break is an extra game which is played in a tennis match when the score in a set is 6-6.
tie-breaker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (比赛或游戏中双方战平后的)决胜题，决胜局； A tie-breaker is an extra question or round that decides the winner of a competition or game when two or more people have the same score at the end.
tied: [ADJ 形容词] (农舍、房屋)出租的，供雇工租住的； tied A tied cottage or house belongs to a farmer or other employer and is rented to someone who works for him or her.  /  See also: tie ; �
tie down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 限制;束缚;牵制； A person or thing that ties you down restricts your freedom in some way.
tied up: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 忙得不可开交的;不得闲的;正在使用的； tied up If someone or something is tied up , they are busy or being used, with the result that they are not available for anything else.
tie-dye: [VERB 动词] 扎染(指将布料打结后用染料染色)； tie-dye If a piece of cloth or a garment is tie-dyed , it is tied in knots and then put into dye, so that some parts become more deeply coloured than others.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 扎染衣服;扎染布料； tie-dye A tie-dye is a garment or piece of cloth that has been tie-dyed.
tie in with: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] (想法或事实)与…一致，与…有关； tie in with If something such as an idea or fact ties in with or ties up with something else, it is consistent with it or connected with it.
tiepin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 领带别针； A tie-pin is a thin narrow object with a pin on it and is used to pin a person's tie to their shirt.
tie-pin: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 领带别针； A tie-pin is a thin narrow object with a pin on it and is used to pin a person's tie to their shirt.
tier: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一排;一行;一列； tier 亦可用于构词 A tier is a row or layer of something that has other layers above or below it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (组织或系统的)层，级； tier 亦可用于构词 A tier is a level in an organization or system.
tie up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (用线或绳)固定，扎牢，捆紧； When you tie something up , you fasten string or rope round it so that it is firm or secure.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 把…绑起来;捆绑； If someone ties another person up , they fasten ropes or chains around them so that they cannot move or escape.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 将(动物)拴牢;把…系牢； If you tie an animal up , you fasten it to a fixed object with a piece of rope so that it cannot run away.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 完满解答，妥善解决(问题等)； tie up If you tie up an issue or problem, you deal with it in a way that gives definite conclusions or answers.
tie-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (交通)阻塞； tie-up A tie-up or a traffic tie-up is a long line of vehicles that cannot move forward because there is too much traffic, or because the road is blocked by something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 经济关系;贸易往来； tie-up A tie-up between two organizations is a business connection that has been arranged between them.
tiff: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (亲密朋友、情侣之间的)小争吵，口角，拌嘴； A tiff is a small unimportant quarrel, especially between two close friends or between people in a romantic relationship.
tiger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 虎;老虎； See also: paper tiger ; A tiger is a large fierce animal belonging to the cat family.
tight: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (衣服或鞋)紧身的，紧贴的； tight tightly Tight clothes or shoes are rather small and fit closely to your body.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 牢牢地;紧紧地； tight tightly If you hold someone or something tight , you hold them firmly and securely.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (控制或规则)严格的，严厉的； tight tightly Tight controls or rules are very strict.  /  [ADV-GRADED 副词] 紧紧地;密不透风地;滴水不漏地； tight tightly Something that is shut tight is shut very firmly.
tighten: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 抓紧;攥紧； tighten If you tighten your grip on something, or if your grip tightens , you hold the thing more firmly or securely.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 绷紧，拉紧(绳、链)； tighten If you tighten a rope or chain, or if it tightens , it is stretched or pulled hard until it is straight.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] (对…)严加控制;使加强控制； tighten If a government or organization tightens its grip on a group of people or an activity, or if its grip tightens , it begins to have more control over it.  /  [VERB 动词] 拧紧，旋紧(螺钉、螺丝帽等)； tighten tighten up 同 tighten When you tighten a screw, nut, or other device, you turn it or move it so that it is more firmly in place or holds something more firmly.
tighten up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 加紧工作;加强管理;严格要求； tighten up See also: tighten 4 ; 6 ; If a group, team, or organization tightens up , they make an effort to control what they are doing more closely, in order to become more efficient and successful.
tight-fisted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 吝啬的;小气的;抠门的； tight-fisted If you describe someone as tight-fisted , you disapprove of them because they are unwilling to spend money.
tight-lipped: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 口风紧的;守口如瓶的； tight-lipped If you describe someone as tight-lipped , you mean that they are unwilling to give any information about something.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (尤指生气、不赞同时)紧闭双唇的； tight-lipped Someone who is tight-lipped has their lips pressed tightly together, especially because they are angry or disapproving.
tightrope: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (马戏团的表演用)绷索，钢丝； A tightrope is a tightly stretched piece of rope on which someone balances and performs tricks in a circus.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 走钢丝(比喻处境艰难，必须小心行事)； tightrope You can use tightrope in expressions such as walk a tightrope and live on a tightrope to indicate that someone is in a difficult situation and has to be very careful about what they say or do.
tights: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 紧身衣;紧身裤袜； tights Tights are a piece of clothing, usually worn by women and girls.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (通常指舞蹈演员、杂技演员或人们运动时穿的)紧身衣； Tights are a piece of tight clothing, usually worn by dancers, acrobats, or people in exercise classes, and covering the hips and each leg.
tigress: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 母虎； A tigress is a female tiger .
tilde: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鼻音化符号，腭化符号(西班牙语标在字母 n上，葡萄牙语标在字母 o 和 a 上)； A tilde is a symbol that is written over the letter 'n' in Spanish ñ and the letters 'o' õ and 'a' ã in Portuguese to indicate the way in which they should be pronounced.
tile: [N-VAR 可变名词] 瓷砖;墙砖;地砖； tile Tiles are flat, square pieces of baked clay, carpet, cork, or other substance, which are fixed as a covering onto a floor or wall.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 瓦片； tile Tiles are flat pieces of baked clay which are used for covering roofs.  /  [VERB 动词] 铺瓦于;贴地砖于； tile -tiled When someone tiles a surface such as a roof or floor, they cover it with tiles.  /  See also: tiling ;
tiling: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 瓦屋顶;地砖面;瓷砖面； tiling You can refer to a surface that is covered by tiles as tiling .  /  See also: tile ; �
till: [PREP 介词] (常于口语与非正式书面语中代替 until)； till In spoken English and informal written English, till is often used instead of until .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (商店等处的)现金出纳机，收银机； till In a shop or other place of business, a till is a counter or cash register where money is kept, and where customers pay for what they have bought.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (收银机中的)钱柜，放钱的抽屉； till A till is the drawer of a cash register, in which the money is kept.  /  [VERB 动词] 耕，犁地； till When people till land, they prepare the earth and work on it in order to grow crops.
tiller: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (船的)舵柄； The tiller of a boat is a handle that is fixed to the rudder.
tilt: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使倾斜;使歪斜； tilt If you tilt an object or if it tilts , it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.  /  [VERB 动词] (略微)倾侧(身体部位)，仰头，把头歪向一边； tilt If you tilt part of your body, usually your head, you move it slightly upwards or to one side.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 倾斜;倾侧;倾斜度； tilt The tilt of something is the fact that it tilts or slopes, or the angle at which it tilts or slopes.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使倾向于;使偏向于； tilt If a person or thing tilts towards a particular opinion or if something tilts them towards it, they change slightly so that they become more in agreement with that opinion or position.
tilting train: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 倾斜式列车在铁轨弯曲处会倾斜，比普通列车速度快； A tilting train is a type of train that can travel faster than ordinary trains because it tilts when the track curves.
timber: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 木材;原木;树木；林木； timber Timber is wood that is used for building houses and making furniture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (造船或建屋用的)栋木，大梁； timber The timbers of a ship or house are the large pieces of wood that have been used to build it.
timbered: [ADJ 形容词] 木制的;木结构的； See also: half-timbered ; A timbered building has a wooden frame or wooden beams showing on the outside.
timber yard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 木材场； A timber yard is a place where timber is stored and sold.
timbre: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 音色;音质;音品； timbre The timbre of someone's voice or of a musical instrument is the particular quality of sound that it has.
time: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 时间； time Time is what we measure in minutes, hours, days, and years.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 时刻;时候;钟点； time You use time to ask or talk about a specific point in the day, which can be stated in hours and minutes and is shown on clocks.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 规定时间； time See also: opening time ; The time when something happens is the point in the day when it happens or is supposed to happen.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (某一时区的)时间； time You use time to refer to the system of expressing time and counting hours that is used in a particular part of the world.

treasure: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 金银财宝； treasure Treasure is a collection of valuable old objects such as gold coins and jewels that has been hidden or lost.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 珍品，珍宝(尤指艺术品和文物)； treasure Treasures are valuable objects, especially works of art and items of historical value.  /  [VERB 动词] 珍藏;珍视;珍爱； treasure treasured If you treasure something that you have, you keep it or care for it carefully because it gives you great pleasure and you think it is very special.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 得力助手;好帮手； treasure If you say that someone is a treasure , you mean that they are very helpful and useful to you.
treasure chest: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 财宝箱； A treasure chest is a box containing treasure.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (为某物提供丰富来源的)百宝箱； treasure chest If you describe something as a treasure chest of a particular thing, you mean that it is very good source of that thing.
treasurer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 司库;财务主管;会计;出纳； The treasurer of a society or organization is the person who is in charge of its finances and keeps its accounts.
treasure trove: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (为某物提供丰富来源的)宝库； treasure trove If you describe something or someone as a treasure trove of a particular thing, you mean that they are a very good or rich source of that thing.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (有价值物品的)宝藏； treasure trove You can refer to a collection of valuable objects as a treasure trove .
treasury: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] (英、美等国的)财政部； In Britain, the United States, and some other countries, the Treasury is the government department that deals with the country's finances.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (城堡、教堂等的)宝库，珍藏室； The treasury in a building such as a castle or a church is a room where valuable objects are displayed or stored.
treat: [VERB 动词] 对待;看待;处理； treat If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave towards them or deal with them in that way.  /  [VERB 动词] 治疗;医治； treat When a doctor or nurse treats a patient or an illness, he or she tries to make the patient well again.  /  [VERB 动词] 处理;给…上保护层； treat If something is treated with a particular substance, the substance is put onto or into it in order to clean it, to protect it, or to give it special properties.  /  [VERB 动词] 请客;招待;款待； treat If you treat someone to something special which they will enjoy, you buy it or arrange it for them.
treatable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 能治疗的;可治愈的； treatable A treatable disease is one which can be cured or controlled, usually by the use of drugs.
treatise: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (专题)论文； A treatise is a long, formal piece of writing about a particular subject.
treatment: [N-VAR 可变名词] 治疗;疗法;疗程； treatment Treatment is medical attention given to a sick or injured person or animal.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 对待；待遇； treatment Your treatment of someone is the way you behave towards them or deal with them.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 处理;治理;护理； treatment Treatment of something involves putting a particular substance onto or into it, in order to clean it, to protect it, or to give it special properties.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 盛情款待;特别严厉的对待； treatment If you say that someone is given the full treatment , you mean either that they are treated extremely well or that they are treated extremely severely.
treaty: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (国家间的)条约，协定； treaty A treaty is a written agreement between countries in which they agree to do a particular thing or to help each other.

treetop: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 树梢； treetop The treetops are the top branches of the trees in a wood or forest.

trellis: [N-VAR 可变名词] (支撑攀缘植物的)棚，架； A trellis is a frame which supports climbing plants.
tremble: [VERB 动词] 颤抖;战栗;哆嗦； tremble If you tremble , you shake slightly because you are frightened or cold.  /  [VERB 动词] 颤动;摇动;摇晃； tremble If something trembles , it shakes slightly.  /  [VERB 动词] (通常因难过或紧张而声音)发颤，颤抖； tremble If your voice trembles , it sounds unsteady and uncertain, usually because you are upset or nervous.
tremendous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 巨大的;极大的;大量的； tremendous tremendously You use tremendous to emphasize how strong a feeling or quality is, or how large an amount is.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 精彩的;出色的;极好的； tremendous tremendously You can describe someone or something as tremendous when you think they are very good or very impressive.
tremolo: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 歌声或说话声中的颤音,震音； If someone's singing or speaking voice has a tremolo in it, it moves up and down instead of staying on the same note.
tremor: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻微地震;小震； A tremor is a small earthquake.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 波动;风波； tremor If an event causes a tremor in a group or organization, it threatens to make the group or organization less strong or stable.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (身体或声音不由自主的)震颤，颤抖； tremor A tremor is a shaking of your body or voice that you cannot control.

trench coat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (军大衣式带有口袋与腰带的)雨衣； A trench coat is a type of raincoat with pockets and a belt.
trend: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 趋势;倾向;动向； trend A trend is a change or development towards something new or different.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 规范;风尚;时尚； trend To set a trend means to do something that becomes accepted or fashionable, and that a lot of other people copy.
trend-setter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 开创新风尚的人(或机构);领导新潮流的人(或机构)； A trend-setter is a person or institution that starts a new fashion or trend.
trendsetter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 开创新风尚的人(或机构);领导新潮流的人(或机构)； A trend-setter is a person or institution that starts a new fashion or trend.
trendy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 时髦的;时尚的;现代的； trendy 时髦的人;时尚人士 If you say that something or someone is trendy , you mean that they are very fashionable and modern.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 赶时髦的;盲从的； 赶时髦的人;盲目追求时髦者 If you describe someone who follows new ideas as trendy , you disapprove of them because they are more interested in being fashionable than in thinking seriously about these ideas.

trespass: [VERB 动词] 擅自进入，非法侵入(他人土地)； trespass 擅自进入(或非法侵入)行为 trespasser If someone trespasses , they go onto someone else's land without their permission.  /  [VERB 动词] 干涉;妨碍；插手； trespass If you say that someone is trespassing on something, you mean that they are involving themselves in something that is not their concern.
tress: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (女子飘逸的)长发； A woman's tresses are her long flowing hair.
trestle: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (桌面等的)支架，搁凳； A trestle is a wooden or metal structure that is used, for example, as one of the supports for a table.

triad: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三合会(旧中国秘密组织)； The Triads were Chinese secret societies in old China.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三个一组;三件一套;三位一体； triad A triad is a group of three similar things.

trial: [N-VAR 可变名词] 审讯;审理;审判； trial A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 试验;试用； trial A trial is an experiment in which you test something by using it or doing it for a period of time to see how well it works.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (人员的)试用，试用期； trial If someone gives you a trial for a job, or if you are on trial , you do the job for a short period of time to see if you are suitable for it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 磨难;痛苦;麻烦； trial If you refer to the trials of a situation, you mean the unpleasant things that you experience in it.

triangular: [ADJ 形容词] 三角形的； triangular Something that is triangular is in the shape of a triangle.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 三角关系的;三人间的;三方面的； triangular You can describe a relationship or situation as triangular if it involves three people or things.
triathlete: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 参加三项全能比赛的运动员； A triathlete is someone who takes part in a triathlon .
triathlon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三项全能运动;铁人三项赛； A triathlon is an athletics competition in which each competitor takes part in three events; swimming, cycling, and running.
tribal: [ADJ 形容词] 部落的;部族的； tribal Tribal is used to describe things relating to or belonging to tribes and the way that they are organized.
tribalism: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 部落制度;部族制度； tribalism Tribalism is the state of existing as a tribe.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 集团意识;部落意识;宗族主义； tribalism You can use tribalism to refer to the loyalties that people feel towards particular social groups and to the way these loyalties affect their behaviour and their attitudes towards others.

tribesman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 部落男性成员； A tribesman is a man who belongs to a tribe.

trigger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (枪的)扳机； trigger The trigger of a gun is a small lever which you pull to fire it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (炸弹的)引爆器； trigger The trigger of a bomb is the device which causes it to explode.  /  [VERB 动词] 引爆;启动;触发； trigger To trigger a bomb or system means to cause it to work.  /  [VERB 动词] 引起;发动;促使； trigger trigger off 同 trigger If something triggers an event or situation, it causes it to begin to happen or exist.

trim: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 整齐的;美观整洁的； trim Something that is trim is neat, tidy, and attractive.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 苗条的;修长的； trim If you describe someone's figure as trim , you mean that it is attractive because there is no extra fat on their body.  /  [VERB 动词] 修剪;剪； trim If you trim something, for example someone's hair, you cut off small amounts of it in order to make it look neater and tidier.  /  [VERB 动词] 削减;缩减； trim If a government or other organization trims something such as a plan, policy, or amount, they reduce it slightly in extent or size.
trimaran: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三体帆船； A trimaran is a fast sailing boat similar to a catamaran, but with three hulls instead of two.
trim away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 修剪;剪掉;切除； trim away If you trim away or trim off parts of something, you cut them off, because they are not needed.
trimming: [N-VAR 可变名词] 装饰物;镶边； trimming The trimming on something such as a piece of clothing is the decoration, for example along its edges, that is in a different colour or material.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] (切取所需部分以后的)下脚料，剩余物； trimming Trimmings are pieces of something, usually food, which are left over after you have cut what you need.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 种种额外的东西;外加的种种配搭； trimming If you say that something comes with all the trimmings , you mean that it has many extra things added to it to make it more special.
Trinity: [N-PROPER 专有名词] (基督教圣父、圣子、圣灵的)三位一体； In the Christian religion, the Trinity or the Holy Trinity is the union of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit in one God.
trinket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 廉价首饰;小装饰物； trinket A trinket is a pretty piece of jewellery or small ornament that is inexpensive.
trio: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 三人组合;尤指三重唱;三个一组;三件一套； trio A trio is a group of three people together, especially musicians or singers, or a group of three things that have something in common.
trip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旅行;出行;旅游； trip See also: round trip ; A trip is a journey that you make to a particular place.  /  [VERB 动词] 绊倒;绊； trip trip up 同 trip If you trip when you are walking, you knock your foot against something and fall or nearly fall.  /  [VERB 动词] 使绊;将…绊倒; 使跌倒； trip trip up 同 trip If you trip someone who is walking or running, you put your foot or something else in front of them, so that they knock their own foot against it and fall or nearly fall.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (对权力等的)迷恋;(内疚、怀旧感等的)困扰； trip If you say that someone is, for example, on a power trip , a guilt trip , or a nostalgia trip , you mean that their behaviour is motivated by power, guilt, or nostalgia.
tripartite: [ADJ 形容词] 分为三部分的;涉及三方的； tripartite You can use tripartite to describe something that has three parts or that involves three groups of people.
tripe: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 可食用的猪肚，牛肚，百叶； Tripe is the stomach of a pig, cow, or ox which is eaten as food.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 蠢话；废话;无聊文字； tripe You refer to something that someone has said or written as tripe when you think that it is silly and worthless.
triple: [ADJ 形容词] 三个的;三方的;三部分的； triple Triple means consisting of three things or parts.  /  [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使变成三倍;使增至三倍； triple If something triples or if you triple it, it becomes three times as large in size or number.  /  [PREDET 前置限定词] 是…的三倍； triple If something is triple the amount or size of another thing, it is three times as large.
triple jump: [N-SING 单数名词] 三级跳远； The triple jump is an athletic event in which competitors have to jump as far as they can, and are allowed to touch the ground once with each foot in the course of the jump.
triplet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三胞胎中的一个； Triplets are three children born at the same time to the same mother.
tripod: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三脚架； A tripod is a stand with three legs that is used to support something such as a camera or a telescope.
tripper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 旅行者;度假者； tripper See also: day-tripper ; A tripper is a person who is on a trip or on holiday.
triptych: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三拼画;三拼浮雕； A triptych is a painting or a carving on three panels that are usually joined together by hinges.
trip up: [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 使犯错;使失误； trip up See also: trip 2 ; 3 ; If someone or something trips a person up , or if they trip up , they fail or make a mistake.
tripwire: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 陷阱、爆炸装置等的绊线，绊网； A tripwire is a wire stretched just above the ground, which sets off something such as a trap or an explosion if someone touches it.
trite: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 陈腐的;老一套的； trite If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite , you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.
triumph: [N-VAR 可变名词] 非凡的成功;杰出的成就； triumph A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (成功或获胜时的)极大的满足，狂喜，骄傲； triumph Triumph is a feeling of great satisfaction and pride resulting from a success or victory.  /  [VERB 动词] 成功;获胜;得胜； triumph If someone or something triumphs , they gain complete success, control, or victory, often after a long or difficult struggle.
triumphal: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 庆祝胜利(或成功)的;以示凯旋的； triumphal Triumphal is used to describe things that are done or made to celebrate a victory or great success.

triumphalist: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (政客或组织的行为)炫耀胜利(或成功)的，洋洋得意的，耀武扬威的； triumphalist Triumphalist behaviour is behaviour in which politicians or organizations celebrate a victory or a great success, especially when this is intended to upset the people they have defeated.
triumphant: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (成功或获胜后)欢欣鼓舞的，狂喜的； triumphant triumphantly Someone who is triumphant has gained a victory or succeeded in something and feels very happy about it.
triumvirate: [N-SING-COLL 单数集合名词] 三人工作组；尤指三人领导小组，三巨头； triumvirate A triumvirate is a group of three people who work together, especially when they are in charge of something.
trivia: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 琐事；花边消息； trivia Trivia is unimportant facts or details that are considered to be amusing rather than serious or useful.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (游戏或竞赛)益智问答的； trivia A trivia game or competition is one where the competitors are asked questions about interesting but unimportant facts in many subjects.
trivial: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 琐碎的;不重要的;微不足道的； trivial If you describe something as trivial , you think that it is unimportant and not serious.

trivialize: [VERB 动词] 贬低;轻视;使显得琐碎(或简单)； trivialize If you say that someone trivializes something important, you disapprove of them because they make it seem less important, serious, and complex than it is.
trod: + + + Trod is the past tense of tread .
trodden: + + + Trodden is the past participle of tread .
troglodyte: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 穴居人； A troglodyte is someone who lives in a cave.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 井底之蛙;见识短浅的人； troglodyte If you refer to someone as a troglodyte , you mean that they are unsophisticated and do not know very much about anything.
troika: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三人领导小组;三头政治;三国集团； troika Journalists sometimes refer to a group of three powerful politicians or states as a troika .

troll: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (斯堪的纳维亚神话中居于洞穴或山上、专门偷小孩的)丑陋怪物，山精，巨怪； In Scandinavian mythology, trolls are creatures who look like ugly people.  /  [VERB 动词] 闲逛;游荡； troll If you troll somewhere, you go there in a casual and unhurried way.  /  [VERB 动词] 随便浏览;随便翻翻； If you troll through papers or files, you look through them in a fairly casual way.
trolley: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (购物或装行李用的)手推车； trolley A trolley is an object with wheels that you use to transport heavy things such as shopping or luggage.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (运送食品饮料上桌的)小推车，台车； trolley A trolley is a small table on wheels which is used for serving drinks or food.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 担架车； trolley A trolley is a bed on wheels for moving patients in hospital.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 有轨电车； trolley A trolley or trolley car is an electric vehicle for carrying people which travels on rails in the streets of a town.
trolley bus: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无轨电车； A trolley bus is a bus that is driven by electric power taken from cables above the street.
trombone: [N-VAR 可变名词] 长号;伸缩长号； A trombone is a large musical instrument of the brass family.

trompe l'oeil: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 以非常逼真的手法按事物正常比例描绘的错视画法； trompe l'oeil Trompe l'oeil is a technique used in art in which objects are painted their normal size in a very realistic way, to make people think that the objects are solid and real.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 错视画； A trompe l'oeil is a trompe l'oeil painting.
troop: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 部队;军队;士兵； troop Troops are soldiers, especially when they are in a large organized group doing a particular task.  /  [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 骑兵队;装甲团； troop A troop is a group of soldiers within a cavalry or armoured regiment.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 童子军中队； troop A troop of boy scouts is a local group of them that meets regularly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一群;一队； troop A troop of people or animals is a group of them.
trooper: [N-COUNT; N-TITLE 可数名词；头衔名词] 骑兵;装甲团士兵； trooper A trooper is a soldier of low rank in the cavalry or in an armoured regiment in the army.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (美国)州警察； trooper In the United States, a trooper is a police officer in a state police force.  /  See also: storm trooper ; �
troopship: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 运兵舰;军队运输船； A troopship is a ship on which large numbers of soldiers are taken from one place to another.
trophy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (竞赛、赛跑等的)奖品，奖杯； A trophy is a prize, for example a silver cup, that is given to the winner of a competition or race.  /  [N-IN-NAMES 名称名词] (用于一些竞赛或赛跑的名称后)…杯，…奖； Trophy is used in the names of some competitions and races in which the winner receives a trophy.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 胜利纪念品;战利品； A trophy is something that you keep in order to show that you have done something very difficult.
tropical: [ADJ 形容词] 热带的;有热带特征的； tropical Tropical means belonging to or typical of the tropics.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 湿热的;典型热带气候的； Tropical weather is hot and damp weather that people believe to be typical of the tropics.

Tropic of Capricorn: 南回归线； The Tropic of Capricorn is an imaginary line around the Earth 23˚26′ south of the equator.
tropics: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 热带地区； The tropics are the parts of the world that lie between two lines of latitude, the tropic of Cancer, 23½˚ north of the equator, and the tropic of Capricorn, 23½˚ south of the equator.
trot: [VERB 动词] 快步走;小步跑； trot If you trot somewhere, you move fairly fast at a speed between walking and running, taking small quick steps.  /  [VERB 动词] (马等)小跑;骑马小跑； trot When an animal such as a horse trots , it moves fairly fast, taking quick small steps.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 接连地;持续地； trot If something happens several times on the trot , it happens that number of times without a break.  /  相关词组： trot out �

troubadour: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 行吟诗人，民谣歌手(12、13 世纪周游意大利及法国为贵族表演的诗人或歌手)； Troubadours were poets and singers who used to travel around and perform to noble families in Italy and France in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指歌词在音乐中至关重要的)流行歌手； People sometimes refer to popular singers as troubadours , especially when the words of their songs are an important part of their music.
trouble: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 麻烦;困难;问题； trouble You can refer to problems or difficulties as trouble .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 麻烦;问题;引起麻烦的事； trouble If you say that one aspect of a situation is the trouble , you mean that it is the aspect which is causing problems or making the situation unsatisfactory.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 苦恼;烦恼;忧虑； trouble Your troubles are the things that you are worried about.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 疾病;不适;疼痛； trouble If you have kidney trouble or back trouble , for example, there is something wrong with your kidneys or your back.

trouble-free: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 顺利的;没问题的;没困难的； trouble-free Something that is trouble-free does not cause any problems or difficulties.

troubleshooter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 公司或政府的处理重大问题的人，解决难题的人； A troubleshooter is a person whose job is to solve major problems or difficulties that occur in a company or government.

troublesome: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 令人烦恼的;令人头疼的;烦人的； troublesome You use troublesome to describe something or someone that causes annoying problems or difficulties.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (形势、问题等)麻烦的，困难的，棘手的； troublesome A troublesome situation or issue is full of complicated problems or difficulties.

trounce: [VERB 动词] 轻松战胜;大胜;击溃； trounce If you trounce someone in a competition or contest, you defeat them easily or by a large score.
troupe: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] (巡回演出的)演出团，歌舞团，戏班子； troupe A troupe is a group of actors, singers, or dancers who work together and often travel around together, performing in different places.
trouper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤指经验老到的演员，表演者； trouper You can refer to an actor or other performer as a trouper , especially when you want to suggest that they have a lot of experience and can deal with difficult situations in a professional way.
trouser: [VERB 动词] 捞取，得到(不义之财)； trouser If you say that someone trousers a sum of money, you mean that they receive it, usually when they do not deserve it or should not take it.
trousers: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 裤子； trousers -trousered Trousers are a piece of clothing that you wear over your body from the waist downwards, and that cover each leg separately.  /  to wear the trousers » see: wear �

trout: [N-VAR 可变名词] 鳟鱼； 鳟鱼肉 A trout is a fairly large fish that lives in rivers and streams.
trowel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (园艺用的)小铲子； A trowel is a small garden tool which you use for digging small holes or removing weeds.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 抹子;泥刀;瓦刀； A trowel is a small tool with a flat blade that you use for spreading things such as cement and plaster onto walls and other surfaces.

truce: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 停战(协定);休战(协定)； truce A truce is an agreement between two people or groups of people to stop fighting or quarrelling for a short time.
truck: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 卡车； truck A truck is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (铁路)运货车皮，敞篷货运火车； truck A truck is an open vehicle used for carrying goods on a railway.  /  [VERB 动词] 用卡车装运;用货车运送； truck When something or someone is trucked somewhere, they are driven there in a lorry.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 不愿参与;不与…来往;不掺和； truck If you say that you will have no truck with someone or something, you are refusing to be involved with them in any way.
