Ugandan: [ADJ 形容词] 乌干达的；乌干达人的；乌干达文化的； Ugandan Ugandan means belonging or relating to Uganda or to its people or culture.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 乌干达人； A Ugandan is a Ugandan citizen, or a person of Ugandan origin.
ugh: [EXCLAM 感叹语] 表示不快、厌恶、恐惧等呃，啊； Ugh is used in writing to represent the sound that people make if they think something is unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.
ugly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 丑陋的；难看的； ugly ugliness If you say that someone or something is ugly , you mean that they are very unattractive and unpleasant to look at.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 通常因涉及暴力、挑衅行为而令人厌恶的，邪恶的，恶性的； ugly ugliness If you refer to an event or situation as ugly , you mean that it is very unpleasant, usually because it involves violent or aggressive behaviour.  /  to rear its ugly head » see: head �
ugly duckling: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 丑小鸭尤指现在丑笨、但将来可能会变得美丽漂亮、事业有成的小孩； ugly duckling If you say that someone, especially a child, is an ugly duckling , you mean that they are unattractive or awkward now, but will probably develop into an attractive and successful person.
UHF: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 超高频； UHF UHF is a range of radio waves which allows a radio or television receiver to produce a good quality of sound.
uh huh: [CONVENTION 惯用语] 表示赞同、领悟、同意等嗯，呃，噢； Uh huh is used in writing to represent a sound that people make when they are agreeing with you, when they want to show that they understand what you are saying, or when they are answering 'yes' to a question.
UHT: [ADJ 形容词] 牛奶经超高温灭菌的； UHT is used to describe milk which has been treated at a very high temperature so that it can be kept for a long time if the container is not opened.
UK: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 联合王国[指大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国]; 英国； The UK is Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
ukulele: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 尤克莱利琴四弦小吉他； A ukulele is a small guitar with four strings.
ulcer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 溃疡； ulcer An ulcer is a sore area on the outside or inside of your body which is very painful and may bleed or produce an unpleasant poisonous substance.
ulcerated: [ADJ 形容词] 溃疡的；溃烂的； ulcerated If a part of someone's body is ulcerated , ulcers have developed on it.
ulterior: [ADJ 形容词] 动机等隐蔽的，隐秘的，隐藏的； ulterior If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.
ultimate: [ADJ 形容词] 最后的；最终的； ultimate You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 最根本的；最基础的；最原始的； ultimate You use ultimate to describe the original source or cause of something.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 最重要的；最强大的；至高的； ultimate You use ultimate to describe the most important or powerful thing of a particular kind.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 极端的；极度的；令人极其不快的； ultimate You use ultimate to describe the most extreme and unpleasant example of a particular thing.
ultimately: [ADV 副词] 最终；最后；终于； ultimately Ultimately means finally, after a long and often complicated series of events.  /  [ADV 副词] 根本上；归根结底； You use ultimately to indicate that what you are saying is the most important point in a discussion.
ultimatum: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 最后通牒； ultimatum An ultimatum is a warning to someone that unless they act in a particular way, action will be taken against them.
ultra-: [PREFIX 前缀] 置于形容词之前构成形容词，用以强调表示“超…的”，“极其…的”； ultra- Ultra- is added to adjectives to form other adjectives that emphasize that something or someone has a quality to an extreme degree.
ultramarine: [COLOUR 颜色词] 佛青色[的]; 湛蓝色的； ultramarine Ultramarine is used to describe things that are very bright blue in colour.
ultrasonic: [ADJ 形容词] 超声波的； Ultrasonic sounds have very high frequencies, which human beings cannot hear.
ultrasound: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 超声波； ultrasound Ultrasound is sound waves which travel at such a high frequency that they cannot be heard by humans.
ultraviolet: [ADJ 形容词] 紫外的；紫外线的； ultraviolet Ultraviolet light or radiation is what causes your skin to become darker in colour after you have been in sunlight.
ululate: [VERB 动词] 号叫；大呼小叫； ululate If someone ululates , they make quickly repeated loud sounds, often to express sorrow or happiness.
um: 表示犹豫不定、沉思等嗯，呃； um Um is used in writing to represent a sound that people make when they are hesitating, usually while deciding what they want to say next.
umber: [COLOUR 颜色词] 红棕色；赭色； umber Umber is used to describe things that are yellowish or reddish brown in colour.
umbilical cord: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 脐带； The umbilical cord is the tube that connects an unborn baby to its mother, through which it receives oxygen and food.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 停止对…的依赖；脱离…自立； umbilical cord If you say that one person, organization, or country has cut its umbilical cord with another, you mean that they have done something that makes them more independent.
umbrage: [PHRASE 短语] 愤懑；不快；生气； umbrage If you say that a person takes umbrage , you mean that they are upset or offended by something that someone says or does to them, often without much reason.
umbrella: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 伞；雨伞；阳伞； umbrella An umbrella is an object which you use to protect yourself from the rain or hot sun.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 综合团体；总称；统称； umbrella Umbrella is used to refer to a single group or description that includes a lot of different organizations or ideas.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 保护伞指保护某个国家或群体的体制或协议； umbrella Umbrella is used to refer to a system or agreement which protects a country or group of people.
umlaut: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 德语等语言中加于元音之上的变音符，曲音符号； An umlaut is a symbol that is written over vowels in German and some other languages to indicate the way in which they should be pronounced.
umpire: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 体育比赛或竞赛中的裁判，裁判员； umpire An umpire is a person whose job is to make sure that a sports match or contest is played fairly and that the rules are not broken.  /  [VERB 动词] 在…中担任裁判； umpire To umpire means to be the umpire in a sports match or contest.
umpteen: [DET 限定词] 无数的；大量的；许许多多的； umpteen Umpteen can be used to refer to an extremely large number of things or people.
umpteenth: [ORD 序数词] 第无数次的； umpteenth You use umpteenth to indicate that an occasion, thing, or person happens or comes after many others.
UN: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 同 United Nations； UN The UN is the same as the United Nations .
un-: [PREFIX 前缀] 置于形容词、副词、名词之前表示反义； Un- is added to the beginning of adjectives, adverbs, and nouns, in order to form words that have the opposite meaning.  /  [PREFIX 前缀] 置于动词之前表示相反的过程； Un- is added to the beginning of a verb that describes a process, in order to form another verb that describes the reverse of that process.  /  [PREFIX 前缀] 置于动词的过去分词之前构成形容词，表示动作尚未发生； Un- is added to the beginning of the past participle of a verb, in order to form an adjective that means that the process described by the verb has not happened.
unabashed: [ADJ 形容词] 不害臊的；不难为情的； unabashed If you describe someone as unabashed , you mean that they are not ashamed, embarrassed, or shy about something, especially when you think most people would be.
unabated: [ADJ 形容词] 未减弱的；未减少的；未衰退的； unabated If something continues unabated , it continues without any reduction in intensity or amount.
unable: [ADJ 形容词] 不能…的；无法…的； unable If you are unable to do something, it is impossible for you to do it, for example because you do not have the necessary skill or knowledge, or because you do not have enough time or money.
unabridged: [ADJ 形容词] 未删节的；未节略的；足本的；完整的； unabridged An unabridged piece of writing, for example a book or article, is complete and not shortened in any way.
unacceptable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 难以接受的；不能容忍的； unacceptable unacceptably If you describe something as unacceptable , you strongly disapprove of it or object to it and feel that it should not be allowed to continue.
unaccompanied: [ADJ 形容词] 无人陪伴的；独自的； unaccompanied If someone is unaccompanied , they are alone.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 行李、货物等单独运送的，不随主人同行的； Unaccompanied luggage or goods are being sent or transported separately from their owner.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 无伴奏的；清唱的；独奏的； unaccompanied An unaccompanied voice or instrument sings or plays alone, with no other instruments playing at the same time.
unaccountable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无法解释的；不可理解的；莫名其妙的； unaccountable unaccountably Something that is unaccountable does not seem to have any sensible explanation.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不负责任的；无须解释的； unaccountable If you describe a person or organization as unaccountable , you are critical of them because they are not responsible to anyone for their actions, or do not feel they have to explain their actions to anyone.
unaccounted for: [ADJ 形容词] 不知下落的；未予说明的； unaccounted for If people or things are unaccounted for , you do not know where they are or what has happened to them.
unaccustomed: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不习惯的；不熟悉的；不适应的； unaccustomed If you are unaccustomed to something, you do not know it very well or have not experienced it very often.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不寻常的；奇怪的； unaccustomed If you describe someone's behaviour or experiences as unaccustomed , you mean that they do not usually behave like this or have experiences of this kind.
unacknowledged: [ADJ 形容词] 被忽视的；未被注意的； unacknowledged If you describe something or someone as unacknowledged , you mean that people ignore their existence or presence, or are not aware of it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 未获认可的；未得到承认的； unacknowledged If you describe something or someone as unacknowledged , you mean that their existence or importance is not recognized officially or publicly.
unacquainted: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不熟悉…的；不知道…的； unacquainted If you are unacquainted with something, you do not know about it or do not have any experience of it.
unadorned: [ADJ 形容词] 无装饰的；简朴的； unadorned Something that is unadorned is plain, rather than having decoration on it.
unadulterated: [ADJ 形容词] 未掺杂的;纯的； unadulterated Something that is unadulterated is completely pure and has had nothing added to it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 常用于强调不好的品质十足的，纯粹的，地道的； unadulterated You can also use unadulterated to emphasize a particular quality, often a bad quality.
unaffected: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 未受影响的；未被改变的； unaffected If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不矫揉造作的；自然的；率真的； unaffected If you describe someone as unaffected , you mean that they are natural and genuine in their behaviour, and do not act as though they are more important than other people.
unafraid: [ADJ 形容词] 不害怕的；不畏惧的； unafraid If you are unafraid to do something, you are confident and not at all nervous about doing it.
unaided: [ADJ 形容词] 无外援的；独立的； unaided If you do something unaided , you do it without help from anyone or anything else.
unalloyed: [ADJ 形容词] 感情纯粹的，不掺杂的； unalloyed If you describe a feeling such as happiness or relief as unalloyed , you are emphasizing that it is a strong feeling and no other feeling is involved.
unaltered: [ADJ 形容词] 未改变的；照旧的； unaltered Something that remains unaltered has not changed or been changed.
unambiguous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不含糊的；清晰的；明确的； unambiguous unambiguously If you describe a message or comment as unambiguous , you mean that it is clear and cannot be understood wrongly.
unambitious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无雄心的；不求名利的； unambitious An unambitious person is not particularly interested in improving their position in life or in being successful, rich, or powerful.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 中规中矩的；平实的； unambitious An unambitious idea or plan is not very complicated, risky, or new, and is easy to carry out successfully.
unanimity: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 一致同意；全体一致； unanimity When there is unanimity among a group of people, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.
unanimous: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 所有人一致同意的，全体一致的，无异议的； unanimous unanimously When a group of people are unanimous , they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 投票、决定、协议等全体同意的，无异议的，一致通过的； unanimous A unanimous vote, decision, or agreement is one in which all the people involved agree.
unannounced: [ADJ 形容词] 未事先通知的；未提前说明的；未打招呼的； unannounced If someone arrives or does something unannounced , they do it unexpectedly and without anyone having being told about it beforehand.
unanswerable: [ADJ 形容词] 无法回答的；没有答案的； unanswerable If you describe a question as unanswerable , you mean that it has no possible answer or that a particular person cannot possibly answer it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 明摆着的；无可辩驳的； unanswerable If you describe a case or argument as unanswerable , you think that it is obviously true or correct and that nobody could disagree with it.
unanswered: [ADJ 形容词] 未予回答的；未得到回复的； unanswered Something such as a question or letter that is unanswered has not been answered.
unappealing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不诱人的；无吸引力的； unappealing If you describe someone or something as unappealing , you find them unpleasant and unattractive.
unappetizing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 引不起食欲的；倒胃口的； unappetizing If you describe food as unappetizing , you think it will be unpleasant to eat because of its appearance.
unapproachable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 难以接近的；不友好的； unapproachable If you describe someone as unapproachable , you mean that they seem to be difficult to talk to and not very friendly.
unarguable: [ADJ 形容词] 不容争论的；不容置疑的； unarguable unarguably If you describe a statement or opinion as unarguable , you think that it is obviously true or correct and that nobody could disagree with it.
unarmed: [ADJ 形容词] 未携带武器的；未武装的；徒手的； unarmed If a person or vehicle is unarmed , they are not carrying any weapons.
unashamed: [ADJ 形容词] 不害羞的；不难为情的；无羞耻心的； unashamed unashamedly If you describe someone's behaviour or attitude as unashamed , you mean that they are open and honest about things that other people might find embarrassing or shocking.
unasked: [ADJ 形容词] 未被提出的；未被问及的； unasked An unasked question is one that has not been asked, although people are wondering what the answer is.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 未被要求的；未受邀请的；主动的； unasked If someone says or does something unasked , they say or do it without being asked to do it.
unassailable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 坚不可摧的；无懈可击的； unassailable If you describe something or someone as unassailable , you mean that nothing can alter, destroy, or challenge them.
unassisted: [ADJ 形容词] 无人帮助的；独力的； unassisted If you do something unassisted , you do it on your own and no-one helps you.
unassuming: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 低调的；谦逊的；不招摇的； unassuming If you describe a person or their behaviour as unassuming , you approve of them because they are quiet and do not try to appear important.
unattached: [ADJ 形容词] 未婚的；没有女朋友或男朋友的； unattached Someone who is unattached is not married or does not have a girlfriend or boyfriend.
unattainable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无法实现的；难以得到的； unattainable If you say that something is unattainable , you mean that it cannot be achieved or is not available.
unattended: [ADJ 形容词] 无人照料的；无人看管的； unattended When people or things are left unattended , they are not being watched or looked after.
unattractive: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不漂亮的；难看的；不吸引人的； unattractive Unattractive people and things are unpleasant in appearance.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 无吸引力的；不受欢迎的； unattractive If you describe something as unattractive , you mean that people do not like it and do not want to be involved with it.
unauthorized: [ADJ 形容词] 未经授权的；未经许可的； unauthorized If something is unauthorized , it has been produced or is happening without official permission.
unavailable: [ADJ 形容词] 弄不到的；得不到的；不方便的； unavailable When things or people are unavailable , you cannot obtain them, meet them, or talk to them.
unavailing: [ADJ 形容词] 徒劳的；不成功的；无成果的； unavailing An unavailing attempt to do something does not succeed.
unavoidable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不可避免的；无法阻止的； unavoidable unavoidably If something is unavoidable , it cannot be avoided or prevented.
unaware: [ADJ 形容词] 不知道的；不晓得的；未注意到的； unaware If you are unaware of something, you do not know about it.
unawares: [PHRASE 短语] 冷不防地；出其不意地； unawares If something catches you unawares or takes you unawares , it happens when you are not expecting it.
unbalance: [VERB 动词] 使失衡；使紊乱；使失常； unbalance If something unbalances a relationship, system, or group, it disturbs or upsets it so that it is no longer successful or functioning properly.  /  [VERB 动词] 使失去平衡;使不稳;使倾侧； To unbalance something means to make it unsteady and likely to tip over.
unbalanced: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 情绪不稳的；精神失常的； unbalanced If you describe someone as unbalanced , you mean that they appear disturbed and upset or they seem to be slightly mad.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不公正的；偏颇的；片面的； unbalanced If you describe something such as a report or argument as unbalanced , you think that it is unfair or inaccurate because it emphasizes some things and ignores others.
unbearable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不堪忍受的；无法容忍的；难以承受的； unbearable unbearably If you describe something as unbearable , you mean that it is so unpleasant, painful, or upsetting that you feel unable to accept it or deal with it.
unbeatable: [ADJ 形容词] 无与伦比的；无可匹敌的； unbeatable If you describe something as unbeatable , you mean that it is the best thing of its kind.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 无法战胜的；无敌的； unbeatable In a game or competition, if you describe a person or team as unbeatable , you mean that they win so often, or perform so well that they are unlikely to be beaten by anyone.
unbeaten: [ADJ 形容词] 体育中保持不败的，未被打败过的； unbeaten In sport, if a person or their performance is unbeaten , nobody else has performed well enough to beat them.
unbecoming: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不好看的；不吸引人的； unbecoming If you describe things such as clothes as unbecoming , you mean that they look unattractive.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不得体的；不合宜的；不恰当的； unbecoming If you describe a person's behaviour or remarks as unbecoming , you mean that they are shocking and unsuitable for that person.
unbeknown: [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 在…不知情的情况下；瞒着…； unbeknown If something happens unbeknown to you or unbeknownst to you, you do not know about it.
unbelievable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不可思议的；难以置信的；极好的；非常棒的； unbelievable unbelievably If you say that something is unbelievable , you are emphasizing that it is very good, impressive, intense, or extreme.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 极其糟糕的；令人震惊的；令人无法相信的； unbelievable unbelievably You can use unbelievable to emphasize that you think something is very bad or shocking.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 不可信的；不像真实的； unbelievable unbelievably If an idea or statement is unbelievable , it seems so unlikely to be true that you cannot believe it.
unbeliever: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无宗教信仰者； People who do not believe in a particular religion are sometimes referred to as unbelievers .

ungodly: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不道德的；违背宗教教义的； ungodly If you describe someone or something as ungodly , you mean that they are morally bad or are opposed to religion.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 时间过早的； ungodly If you refer to a time as an ungodly hour, you are emphasizing that it is very early in the morning.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 过度的；不合理的； ungodly If you refer to the amount or volume of something as ungodly , you mean that it is excessive or unreasonable.

ungracious: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不礼貌的；不友好的； ungracious If you describe a person or their behaviour as ungracious , you mean that they are not polite or friendly in their speech or behaviour.

unhappy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不幸福的；不快乐的；愁苦的； unhappy unhappily unhappiness If you are unhappy , you are sad and depressed.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 不高兴的；不满意的； unhappy unhappiness If you are unhappy about something, you are not pleased about it or not satisfied with it.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 令人不满的；不可取的； unhappy An unhappy situation or choice is not satisfactory or desirable.

unheard: [ADJ 形容词] 没听到的；不被理睬的；被忽略的； unheard If you say that a person or their words go unheard , you are expressing criticism because someone refuses to pay attention to what is said or take it into consideration.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 不为人知的；前所未闻的； unheard If you describe spoken comments or pieces of music as unheard , you mean that most people are not familiar with them because they have not been expressed or performed in public.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 听不到的； unheard If someone's words or cries go unheard , nobody can hear them, or a particular person cannot hear them.
unheard of: [ADJ 形容词] 没发生过的； unheard of You can say that an event or situation is unheard of when it never happens.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 令人震惊的；前所未有的； unheard of You can say that an event or situation is unheard of when it happens for the first time and is very surprising or shocking.

unhelpful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 没有帮助的；无益的； unhelpful If you say that someone or something is unhelpful , you mean that they do not help you or improve a situation, and may even make things worse.
unheralded: [ADJ 形容词] 艺术家、运动员等被埋没的，怀才未遇的； unheralded If you describe an artist or sports player as unheralded , you mean that people have not recognized their talent or ability.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 出乎意料的；毫无先兆的； unheralded If you describe something that happens as unheralded , you mean that you did not expect it, because nobody mentioned it beforehand.
unhesitatingly: [ADV 副词] 果断地;毫不犹豫地； unhesitatingly If you say that someone does something unhesitatingly , you mean that they do it immediately and confidently, without any doubt or anxiety.

vulgar: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 粗俗的;庸俗的;俗气的;不雅的； vulgar vulgarity If you describe something as vulgar , you think it is in bad taste or of poor artistic quality.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 图画、姿势或言论下流的，猥亵的； vulgar vulgarity If you describe pictures, gestures, or remarks as vulgar , you dislike them because they refer to sex or parts of the body in a rude way that you find unpleasant.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 粗俗的;无礼的;粗鄙的;粗鲁的； vulgar vulgarity If you describe a person or their behaviour as vulgar , you mean that they lack taste or behave rudely.
vulnerable: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 脆弱的;易受伤害的； vulnerable vulnerability Someone who is vulnerable is weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易感染某种疾病的；易患病的； vulnerable vulnerability If a person, animal, or plant is vulnerable to a disease, they are more likely to get it than other people, animals, or plants.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 易受伤害的;易受影响的； vulnerable vulnerability Something that is vulnerable can be easily harmed or affected by something bad.
vulture: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 兀鹫;秃鹫； A vulture is a large bird which lives in hot countries and eats the flesh of dead animals.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 趁火打劫的人;乘人之危的人； vulture If you describe a person as a vulture , you disapprove of them because you think they are trying to gain from another person's troubles.
vulva: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女阴;外阴； The vulva is the outer part of a woman's sexual organs.
vying: + + + Vying is the present participle of vie .
W: [N-VAR 可变名词] 英语字母表的第23个字母； W is the twenty-third letter of the English alphabet.  /  [用于首字母为w的一些单词的缩写，如west和watt] ； W or w is an abbreviation for words beginning with w, such as 'west' or 'watt'.
wacko: [ADJ 形容词] 古怪的;乖僻的； wacko If you say that someone is wacko , you are saying in an unkind way that they are strange and eccentric.
wacky: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 古怪的;乖僻的;滑稽可笑的； wacky If you describe something or someone as wacky , you mean that they are eccentric, unusual, and often funny.
wad: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 卷;叠;捆； wad A wad of something such as paper or cloth is a tight bundle or ball of it.
wadding: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 软填料;填絮； Wadding is soft material which is put around things to protect them, for example in packing.
waddle: [VERB 动词] 蹒跚行走;摇摇晃晃地行走； waddle To waddle somewhere means to walk there with short, quick steps, swinging slightly from side to side.
wade: [VERB 动词] (艰难地)涉，蹚，跋涉； wade If you wade through something that makes it difficult to walk, usually water or mud, you walk through it.  /  [VERB 动词] 费力地阅读;艰难地处理； wade To wade through a lot of documents or pieces of information means to spend a lot of time and effort reading them or dealing with them.  /  相关词组： wade in �
wade in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (常指不计后果地)介入，干涉； wade in If someone wades in or wades into something, they get involved in a very determined and forceful way, often without thinking enough about the consequences of their actions.
wader: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 涉禽； A wader is a bird with long legs and a long neck, which lives near water and feeds on fish.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (涉水捕鱼时穿的)长筒靴； Waders are long rubber boots which cover all of the legs and are worn by fishermen when they are standing in water.
wadi: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (北非或阿拉伯仅雨季有水的)干涸河道，干河谷； A wadi is a river in North Africa or Arabia which is dry except in the rainy season.
wading pool: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (供孩子玩耍的)浅水池； A wading pool is a shallow artificial pool for children to play in.
wafer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 威化饼，薄脆饼(常与冰激凌同吃)； A wafer is a thin crisp biscuit which is usually eaten with ice cream.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (基督教圣餐仪式上牧师发放的)圣饼； A wafer is a circular, thin piece of special bread which the priest gives people to eat in the Christian service of Holy Communion.
wafer-thin: [ADJ 形容词] 极薄的;极扁薄的； wafer-thin Wafer-thin means extremely thin and flat.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 优势极微弱的； wafer-thin If you succeed by a wafer-thin margin, you succeed by a very small amount.
waffle: [VERB 动词] 胡扯;胡说;废话连篇； waffle waffle on 同 waffle If you say that someone waffles , you are critical of them because they talk or write a lot without actually making any clear or important points.  /  [VERB 动词] 犹豫不决;含糊其词； waffle waffling If someone waffles on an issue or question, they cannot decide what to do or what their opinion is about it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 华夫饼； A waffle is a kind of square cake made of batter with squares marked on it.
waft: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使飘荡;吹拂； waft If sounds or smells waft through the air, or if something such as a light wind wafts them, they move gently through the air.
wag: [VERB 动词] 摇动，摇摆(尾巴)； wag When a dog wags its tail, it repeatedly waves its tail from side to side.  /  [VERB 动词] (通常指由于厌恶而)左右摇晃(手指)； wag If you wag your finger, you shake it repeatedly and quickly from side to side, usually because you are annoyed with someone.  /  [VERB 动词] (常指因不高兴而)摇头； wag If you wag your head, you move it from side to side, often because you are unhappy about a situation.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 爱说笑的人；幽默的人； wag A wag is someone who makes jokes.
wage: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 工资;工钱； wage Someone's wages are the amount of money that is regularly paid to them for the work that they do.  /  [VERB 动词] 开展，发动(运动或战争)； wage If a person, group, or country wages a campaign or a war, they start it and continue it over a period of time.
waged: + + + Waged is the past tense and past participle of wage .  /  [ADJ 形容词] 人领工资的，带薪的;工作支付工资的； waged Waged workers receive money regularly for doing a job.
wage packet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 工资袋； wage packet People's wages can be referred to as their wage packet .
wager: [VERB 动词] 押(赌注);打赌； wager If you wager on the result of a horse race, football match, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not.  /  [VERB 动词] (表示很确定)打赌，保证； wager If you say that you will wager that something is the case, you mean you are confident that it is the case.
waggle: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使来回摇摆;使上下移动； waggle If you waggle something, or if something waggles , it moves up and down or from side to side with short quick movements.
wagon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 四轮运货马车； A wagon is a strong vehicle with four wheels, usually pulled by horses or oxen and used for carrying heavy loads.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (火车的)货车车厢，车皮； A wagon is a large container on wheels which is pulled by a train.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 停止喝酒;戒酒； wagon Someone who is on the wagon has stopped drinking alcohol.  /  See also: station wagon ; �
wagtail: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鹡鸰； A wagtail is a type of small bird which moves its tail quickly up and down as it walks.
wah-wah: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (铜管乐器开或闭所发出的) 哇音;(电子乐器，尤指电吉他的)哇音； wah-wah In music, wah-wah is used to describe the sound produced by covering and uncovering the open end of a brass instrument.
waif: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 极瘦弱的人；无家可归者;流浪儿； waif If you refer to a child or young woman as a waif , you mean that they are very thin and look as if they have nowhere to live.
wail: [VERB 动词] 哀号;悲鸣;恸哭； wail wailing If someone wails , they make long, loud, high-pitched cries which express sorrow or pain.  /  [VERB 动词] 哀诉;哀号着说； wail If you wail something, you say it in a loud, high-pitched voice that shows that you are unhappy or in pain.  /  [VERB 动词] (警报器等)尖叫，尖啸； wail wailing If something such as a siren or an alarm wails , it makes a long, loud, high-pitched sound.
waist: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 腰;腰部； waist -waisted Your waist is the middle part of your body where it narrows slightly above your hips.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (衣服的)腰部，腰身； -waisted waist The waist of a garment such as a dress, coat, or pair of trousers is the part of it which covers the middle part of your body.
waistband: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 裤腰;裙腰； A waistband is a narrow piece of material which is sewn on to a pair of trousers, a skirt, or other item of clothing at the waist in order to strengthen it.
waistcoat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 背心;马甲； A waistcoat is a sleeveless piece of clothing with buttons which people usually wear over a shirt.
waistline: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 腰围； waistline Your waistline is your waist measurement.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (衣服的)腰身； The waistline of a piece of clothing is the place where the upper and lower parts are sewn together, which is near to your waist when you wear it.
wait: [VERB 动词] 等待;等候； wait waiting When you wait for something or someone, you spend some time doing very little, because you cannot act until that thing happens or that person arrives.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 等待;等待的时间； wait A wait is a period of time in which you do very little, before something happens or before you can do something.  /  [VERB 动词] 准备妥当;可获得;可使用； wait If something is waiting for you, it is ready for you to use, have, or do.  /  [VERB 动词] 延缓;推迟;搁置； wait If you say that something can wait , you mean that it is not important or urgent and so you will deal with it or do it later.
wait around: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (长时间地)干等，空等； If you wait around or wait about , you stay in the same place, usually doing very little, because you cannot act before something happens or before someone arrives.
waiter: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 男侍者;男服务员； See also: dumb waiter ; A waiter is a man who works in a restaurant, serving people with food and drink.
wait in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 在家等候； wait in If you wait in , you deliberately stay at home and do not go out, for example because someone is coming to see you.
waiting game: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 拖延战术； If you play a waiting game , you deal with a situation by deliberately doing nothing, because you believe you will gain an advantage by acting later, or because you are waiting to see how other people are going to act.
waiting list: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 等候者名单； waiting list A waiting list is a list of people who have asked for something which cannot be given to them immediately, for example medical treatment, housing, or training, and who must therefore wait until it is available.
waiting room: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 等候室;候车室;候诊室； A waiting room is a room in a place such as a railway station or a clinic, where people can sit down while they wait.
wait on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 等待某事发生； wait on If you are waiting on something, you are waiting for it to happen, for example before you do or decide anything.
waitress: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 女侍者;女服务员； A waitress is a woman who works in a restaurant, serving people with food and drink.  /  [VERB 动词] 做女侍者;当女服务员； waitress waitressing A woman who waitresses works in a restaurant serving food and drink.
wait up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 等着不睡;熬夜等待；尤指等待夜归的人； wait up If you wait up , you deliberately do not go to bed, especially because you are expecting someone to return home late at night.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 走慢点;等一等； wait up If you ask someone to wait up , you are asking them to go more slowly or to stop and wait for you.
waive: [VERB 动词] 放弃合法权利等； waive If you waive your right to something, for example legal representation, you choose not to have it or do it.  /  [VERB 动词] 特定情况下不强求执行(规则等)； waive If someone waives a rule, they say that people do not have to obey it in a particular situation.
waiver: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 权利放弃,弃权;(规则或法律的)不强求执行； waiver A waiver is when a person, government, or organization agrees to give up a right or says that people do not have to obey a particular rule or law.
wake: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 醒;醒来;唤醒;弄醒； wake wake up 同 wake When you wake or when someone or something wakes you, you become conscious again after being asleep.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (航行中的船等留下的)伴流，尾流，航迹； wake The wake of a boat or other object moving in water is the track of waves that it makes behind it as it moves through the water.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (葬礼前后的)守夜，守灵； wake A wake is a gathering or social event that is held before or after someone's funeral.  /  [PREP-PHRASE 短语介词] 随着…而来;作为…的结果； wake If one thing follows in the wake of another, it happens after the other thing is over, often as a result of it.
wakeful: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 难以入睡的;失眠的;睡眠轻的； wakefulness wakeful Someone who is wakeful finds it difficult to get to sleep and wakes up very often when they should be sleeping.
waken: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 醒来;唤醒； waken waken up同waken When you waken , or when someone or something wakens you, you wake from sleep.
wake up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 激起;唤起； See also: wake ; If something such as an activity wakes you up , it makes you more alert and ready to do things after you have been lazy or inactive.
wake-up call: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (旅馆等提供的)叫醒电话，叫醒服务； A wake-up call is a telephone call that you can book through an operator or at a hotel to make sure that you wake up at a particular time.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 警钟;警示； wake-up call If you say that something is a wake-up call to a person or group of people, you mean that it will make them notice something and start to take action.
wake up to: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 觉察到;意识到； wake up to If you wake up to something, you become aware of it.
walk: [VERB 动词] 走;行走;走路； walk When you walk , you move forward by putting one foot in front of the other in a regular way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 漫步;散步； walk A walk is a journey that you make by walking, usually for pleasure.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 步行的距离(或路程)； walk A walk of a particular distance is the distance which a person has to walk to get somewhere.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 步行小径;(适宜散步的)小径，道路； walk A walk is a route suitable for walking along for pleasure.
walkabout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (国王、女王或其他要人为亲近民众在公共场所进行的)巡行； walkabout (国王、女王或其他要人为亲近民众在公共场所)巡行 A walkabout is a walk by a king, queen, or other important person through a public place in order to meet people in an informal way.
walk away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 脱身;一走了之； walk away If you walk away from a problem or a difficult situation, you do nothing about it or do not face any bad consequences from it.
walk away with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻松赢得;轻易获得； walk away with If you walk away with something such as a prize, you win it or get it very easily.
walker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指在乡间休闲或锻炼的)散步者，步行者； A walker is a person who walks, especially in the countryside for pleasure or in order to keep healthy.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (帮助婴儿、残疾人或病人走路的)助行架； walker A walker is a special kind of frame which is designed to help babies or disabled or ill people to walk.
walkie-talkie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无线电对话机;步话机； A walkie-talkie is a small portable radio which you can talk into and hear messages through so that you can communicate with someone far away.
walking: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (尤指在乡间以休闲或锻炼为目的的)散步，步行； walking Walking is the activity of taking walks for exercise or pleasure, especially in the country.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 表示强调活的…； walking You can use walking in expressions like a walking disaster or a walking dictionary in order to emphasize, for example, that someone causes a lot of disasters, or knows a lot of difficult words.
walking stick: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 手杖;拐杖； A walking stick is a long wooden stick which a person can lean on while walking.
walk in on: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 进屋撞见别人在做私密的事； If you walk in on someone, you enter the room that they are in while they are doing something private, and this creates an embarrassing situation.
walk into: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (不小心)遇上;(不慎)陷入； If you walk into an unpleasant situation, you become involved in it without expecting to, especially because you have been careless.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻易获得(工作)； walk into If you walk into a job, you manage to get it very easily.
Walkman: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 随身听； A Walkman is a small cassette player with light headphones which people carry around so that they can listen to music, for example while they are travelling.
walk off with: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 不经允许就拿走;偷走； If someone walks off with something that does not belong to them, they take it without permission.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 轻松赢得;轻易获得； If you walk off with something such as a prize, you win it or get it very easily.
walk of life: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 行业;职业;身份； The walk of life that you come from is the position that you have in society and the kind of job you have.
walk-on: [ADJ 形容词] 角色跑龙套的； walk-on A walk-on part in a play or film is a very small part which usually does not involve any speaking.
walkout: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 罢工； A walkout is a strike.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (会议上表示反对的)离席，退场； walkout If there is a walkout during a meeting, some or all of the people attending it leave in order to show their disapproval of something that has happened at the meeting.
walk out: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (通常为表示愤怒或厌烦而从会议、演出等)退席，退场； If you walk out of a meeting, a performance, or an unpleasant situation, you leave it suddenly, usually in order to show that you are angry or bored.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 突然离开，抛弃(家庭或伴侣);出走； If someone walks out on their family or their partner, they leave them suddenly and go to live somewhere else.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 罢工； If workers walk out , they stop doing their work for a period of time, usually in order to try to get better pay or conditions for themselves.
walk over: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 粗暴或苛刻地对待;欺负； walk over If someone walks over you, they treat you very badly.
walkover: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻易取得的胜利；一边倒的比赛； If you say that a competition or contest is a walkover , you mean that it is won very easily.
walk-up: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 无电梯的公寓大楼;无电梯直通的公寓； walk-up A walk-up is a tall apartment block which has no lift.
walkway: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (常高于地面的)人行道，通道； A walkway is a passage or path for people to walk along.
wall: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 墙;墙壁； wall -walled A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (石或砖砌成的)围墙，隔墙； wall A wall is a long narrow vertical structure made of stone or brick that surrounds or divides an area of land.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (中空物体的)壁，内壁； wall The wall of something that is hollow is its side.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 屏障;堆成墙的大量物品； wall A wall of something is a large amount of it forming a high vertical barrier.
wallaby: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 沙袋鼠(产于澳大利亚和新几内亚)； A wallaby is an animal similar to a small kangaroo.
wallcovering: [N-VAR 可变名词] (墙纸等)墙面覆料； A wallcovering is a material such as wallpaper that is used to decorate the walls on the inside of a building.
walled: [ADJ 形容词] 有围墙的;有城墙的； walled If an area of land or a city is walled , it is surrounded or enclosed by a wall.
wallet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 钱包;皮夹； A wallet is a small flat folded case, usually made of leather or plastic, in which you can keep banknotes and credit cards.
wallflower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 桂竹香； A wallflower is a plant that is grown in gardens and has sweet-smelling yellow, red, orange, or purple flowers.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 墙花(在社交场合因害羞而没有舞伴或不与人交谈的人) ； wallflower If you say that someone is a wallflower , you mean that they are shy and do not get involved in dancing or talking to people at social events.
wall in: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] (用墙或障碍)围住，封闭； If someone or something is walled in , they are surrounded or enclosed by a wall or barrier.

wastebasket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 wastepaper basket； A wastebasket is the same as a wastepaper basket .

wastepaper basket: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 废纸篓； A wastepaper basket is a container for rubbish, especially paper, which is usually placed on the floor in the corner of a room or next to a desk.

watchtower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 瞭望塔;岗楼； A watchtower is a high building which gives a person a good view of the area around the place that they are guarding.
watchword: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 口号;格言； watchword Someone's watchword is a word or phrase that sums up their attitude or approach to a particular subject or to things in general.

water butt: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (接雨水的)积水桶，盛水桶； A water butt is a large barrel for collecting rain as it flows off a roof.
water cannon: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (警察用于驱散人群的)高压水枪，水炮； A water cannon is a machine which shoots out a large, powerful stream of water.

water cooler: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤指办公室里的)饮水机； A water cooler is a machine that dispenses drinking water, especially in an office.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 办公室，工作场所(用于表述在办公地点的闲聊)； water cooler Water cooler is used in expressions that refer to the informal conversations that people have in their office or workplace.

whence: [QUEST 疑问词] 从何处;来自何方； whence Whence means from where.
whenever: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 无论什么时候;每当； whenever You use whenever to refer to any time or every time that something happens or is true.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 不知什么时候； whenever You use whenever to refer to a time that you do not know or are not sure about.
where: [QUEST 疑问词] 用于疑问句在哪里，从哪里，到哪里； where You use where to ask questions about the place something is in, or is coming from or going to.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (尤用于动词和形容词后引导从句，表示某物所在或某事发生的地点)那里，那儿； where You use where after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention the place in which something is situated or happens.  /  [QUEST 疑问词] (用于疑问句)在哪一地点,在哪一阶段，在哪方面； where You use where to ask questions about a situation, a stage in something, or an aspect of something.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (尤用于某些动词和形容词后，引导表示地点、某事物所处状态、阶段等的从句)在哪儿，从哪儿； where You use where after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention a situation, a stage in something, or an aspect of something.
whereabouts: [N-SING-COLL 单数集合名词] (人或物的)行踪，下落，所在之处； whereabouts If you refer to the whereabouts of a particular person or thing, you mean the place where that person or thing may be found.  /  [QUEST 疑问词] (用于疑问句)具体在哪里； You use whereabouts in questions when you are asking precisely where something is.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (尤用于某些动词和形容词后，引导表示具体处所的从句)具体在哪里； whereabouts You use whereabouts after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention precisely where something is situated or happens.
whereas: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (表示对比)但是，然而； whereas You use whereas to introduce a comment which contrasts with what is said in the main clause.
whereby: [PRON-REL 关系代词] 凭此;借以； whereby A system or action whereby something happens is one that makes that thing happen.
wherefores: [PHRASE 短语] 理由;原因； wherefores The whys and wherefores of something are the reasons for it.
wherein: [PRON-REL 关系代词] 在那里;在其中； wherein Wherein means in which place or thing.  /  [QUEST 疑问词] 在哪里;在哪方面； wherein Wherein means in which part or respect.
whereupon: [CONJ-COORD 连词] 于是;随之； whereupon You use whereupon to say that one thing happens immediately after another thing, and usually as a result of it.
wherever: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 无论哪里;在任何地方； wherever You use wherever to indicate that something happens or is true in any place or situation.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 不管在哪里； wherever You use wherever when you indicate that you do not know where a person or place is.  /  [QUEST 疑问词] (用在疑问句中作为where的强调形式，通常表示惊讶)究竟在哪里； You use wherever in questions as an emphatic form of 'where', usually when you are surprised about something.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 或别的什么地方； wherever You use or wherever to say that something might happen in a place other than the place you have mentioned, but that you are not able to say exactly where.
wherewithal: [N-SING 单数名词] (某一特定用途的)必要设备，必要手段;尤指所需资金； wherewithal If you have the wherewithal for something, you have the means, especially the money, that you need for it.
whet: [PHRASE 短语] 刺激(某人)对…的欲望;激发某人对…的兴趣； whet If someone or something whets your appetite for a particular thing, they increase your desire to have it or know about it, especially by giving you an idea of what it is like.
whether: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (表示选择或怀疑)是否，是不是； whether You use whether when you are talking about a choice or doubt between two or more alternatives.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 无论;不管； whether You use whether to say that something is true in any of the circumstances that you mention.
whetstone: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 磨刀石； A whetstone is a stone which is used for sharpening knives or other tools that have a blade.
whew: [EXCLAM 感叹语] (用于书面表示感到很热、宽慰或惊讶时发出的声音)哟，唷； Whew is used in writing to represent a sound that you make when you breathe out quickly, for example because you are very hot, very relieved, or very surprised.
whey: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 乳清； Whey is the watery part of sour milk that is separated from the thick part called curds, for example when you are making cheese.
which: [QUEST 疑问词] (用于疑问句中)哪个，哪些； You use which in questions when there are two or more possible answers or alternatives.  /  [DET 限定词] (用于指明在两个或多个答案或选项中所作出的选择)哪个，哪些； which You use which to refer to a choice between two or more possible answers or alternatives.  /  [PRON-REL 关系代词] (用于关系从句句首，具体说明所谈论的事物或提供关于它的更多信息)； which You use which at the beginning of a relative clause when specifying the thing that you are talking about or when giving more information about it.  /  [PRON-REL 关系代词] (用来回指前面句子表达的观点或状况)这，那； which You use which to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences, especially when you want to give your opinion about it.
whichever: [DET 限定词] 任何一种;不管哪种； whichever You use whichever in order to indicate that it does not matter which of the possible alternatives happens or is chosen.  /  [DET 限定词] (用来指明多个可能性中正确或特指的一个)…的那个； whichever You use whichever to specify which of a number of possibilities is the right one or the one you mean.
whiff: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一阵(气味)； whiff If there is a whiff of a particular smell, you smell it only slightly or only for a brief period of time, for example as you walk past someone or something.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 轻微的征兆;迹象； whiff A whiff of something bad or harmful is a slight sign of it.
Whig: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (18和19世纪致力于政治和社会改革的)辉格党成员； A Whig was a member of a British political party in the 18th and 19th centuries that was in favour of political and social changes.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 美国独立战争的支持者； In the American Revolution, a Whig was an American who supported the revolution against the British.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (美国19世纪的想要限制总统权力的)政党成员； A Whig was a member of an American political party in the 19th century that wanted to limit the powers of the President.
while: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (表示两件事同时发生)当…的时候，在…时； while If something happens while something else is happening, the two things are happening at the same time.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (表示某一件事是在另一件事发生过程中的某一时间点发生的)当…的时候，在…时； while If something happens while something else happens, the first thing happens at some point during the time that the second thing is happening.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 却;但是;然而； while You use while at the beginning of a clause to introduce information which contrasts with information in the main clause.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 虽然;尽管； You use while , before making a statement, in order to introduce information that partly conflicts with your statement.
while away: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 消磨，打发(时间)； If you while away the time in a particular way, you spend time in that way, because you are waiting for something else to happen, or because you have nothing else to do.
whilst: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] 同 while连词； Whilst means the same as the conjunction while .
whim: [N-VAR 可变名词] 一时的兴致;心血来潮;突发的奇想； whim A whim is a wish to do or have something which seems to have no serious reason or purpose behind it, and often occurs suddenly.
whimper: [VERB 动词] 抽泣;呜咽;啜泣； whimper If someone whimpers , they make quiet unhappy or frightened sounds, as if they are about to start crying.  /  [VERB 动词] 抽噎着说;哀诉； whimper If someone whimpers something, they say it in an unhappy or frightened way.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 雷声大，雨点小； whimper If you say that something happens not with a bang but a whimper , you mean that it is less effective or exciting than was expected or intended.
whimsical: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 怪异的;反复无常的;不切实际的； whimsical A whimsical person or idea is unusual, playful, and unpredictable, rather than serious and practical.
whimsy: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 奇思异想;不同寻常的行为； Whimsy is behaviour which is unusual, playful, and unpredictable, rather than having any serious reason or purpose behind it.
whine: [VERB 动词] 尖叫;哀号;悲鸣； whine If something or someone whines , they make a long, high-pitched noise, especially one which sounds sad or unpleasant.  /  [VERB 动词] 令人讨厌地抱怨;唠叨； whine If you say that someone is whining , you mean that they are complaining in an annoying way about something unimportant.
whinge: [VERB 动词] 发牢骚;絮絮叨叨地抱怨； whinge If you say that someone is whingeing , you mean that they are complaining in an annoying way about something unimportant.
whinger: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 发牢骚的人；抱怨的人； whinger If you call someone a whinger , you are critical of them because they complain about unimportant things all the time.
whinny: [VERB 动词] 马嘶鸣； whinny When a horse whinnies , it makes a series of high-pitched sounds, usually not very loudly.
whip: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 鞭子； A whip is a long thin piece of material such as leather or rope, fastened to a stiff handle.  /  [VERB 动词] 鞭打(人或动物)； whip whipping If someone whips a person or animal, they beat them or hit them with a whip or something like a whip.  /  [VERB 动词] (风等)猛烈地抽打； whip If something, for example the wind, whips something, it strikes it sharply.  /  [VERB 动词] (在外力作用下)猛然移动； whip If something flexible whips in a particular way, it moves sharply when it is affected by a force, for example by the wind.
whiplash: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (车祸等中造成的)颈部过度屈伸损伤； whiplash Whiplash is a neck injury caused by the head suddenly moving forwards and then back again, for example in a car accident.
whippersnapper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 自以为是的人;妄自尊大的人； whippersnapper If you refer to a young person as a whippersnapper , you disapprove of them because you think that they are behaving more confidently than they should.
whippet: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小灵狗(腿长，瘦小，可用于赛狗)； A whippet is a small thin dog with long legs.
whipping boy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 替人受过者;替罪羊； whipping boy If someone or something is a whipping boy for a particular situation, they get all the blame for it.
whipping cream: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (经快速搅打后会发硬的)搅打奶油； Whipping cream is cream that becomes stiff when it is stirred very fast.
whippoorwill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 三声夜鹰见于北美； A whippoorwill is a North American bird that is active at night and has a call that sounds like 'whip poor will'.
whip-round: [N-SING 单数名词] 凑钱;凑份子； When a group of people have a whip-round , money is collected from each person so that it can be used to buy something for all of them or for someone they all know.
whip up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 激起，煽动(仇恨等危险情感)； If someone whips up an emotion, especially a dangerous one such as hatred, or if they whip people up into an emotional state, they deliberately cause and encourage people to feel that emotion.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 风激起，吹起(尘土或水)； If a force such as the wind whips up dust or water, it makes it rise up.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 很快做好(尤指一顿饭)； whip up If you whip up something, especially a meal, you make it quickly.
whirl: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使回旋;使旋转； whirl If something or someone whirls around or if you whirl them around, they move around or turn around very quickly.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一连串;接连不断的活动； whirl You can refer to a lot of intense activity as a whirl of activity.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 混乱;躁动； whirl If a person or their mind is in a whirl , they are very confused or excited.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 试一试;尝试一下； whirl If you decide to give an activity a whirl , you do it even though it is something that you have never tried before.
whirlpool: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 漩涡； A whirlpool is a small area in a river or the sea where the water is moving quickly round and round, so that objects floating near it are pulled into its centre.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (很多不愉快或复杂事情构成的)漩涡； whirlpool You can describe a situation in which a lot of unpleasant or complicated things are happening, and from which it is very difficult to escape, as a whirlpool .  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 涡旋浴池； whirlpool A whirlpool bath or a whirlpool is a bath that is specially designed so that the water moves round and round.
whirlwind: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (陆地或海洋上的)旋风，旋流； A whirlwind is a tall column of air which spins round and round very fast and moves across the land or sea.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 一连串的突发事件； whirlwind You can describe a situation in which a lot of things happen very quickly and are very difficult for someone to control as a whirlwind .  /  [ADJ 形容词] 旋风般的;匆匆忙忙的;快速的； whirlwind A whirlwind event or action happens or is done much more quickly than normal.
whirr: [VERB 动词] (机器、昆虫翅膀等)发出呼呼声，嗡嗡作响； whirr whirring When something such as a machine or an insect's wing whirrs , it makes a series of low sounds so quickly that they seem like one continuous sound.
whisk: [VERB 动词] 迅速送走;匆匆带走； whisk If you whisk someone or something somewhere, you take them or move them there quickly.  /  [VERB 动词] 搅拌，搅打(鸡蛋、奶油等)； whisk If you whisk something such as eggs or cream, you stir it very fast, often with an electric device, so that it becomes full of small bubbles.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 搅拌器;打蛋器； whisk A whisk is a kitchen tool used for whisking eggs or cream.
whisker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (猫、鼠等动物的)胡须； The whiskers of an animal such as a cat or a mouse are the long stiff hairs that grow near its mouth.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 连鬓胡子;络腮胡子； whisker You can refer to the hair on a man's face, especially on the sides of his face, as his whiskers .  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 微小的数量；一丝；一点儿； whisker You can use whisker in expressions such as by a whisker or within a whisker of to indicate that something happened or is true, but only by a very small amount or degree.
whiskery: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 胡须多的； whiskery If you describe someone as whiskery , you mean that they have lots of stiff little hairs on their face.
whiskey: [N-MASS 物质名词] (产于爱尔兰或美国的)威士忌酒； whiskey 一杯威士忌 Whiskey is whisky that is made in Ireland or the United States.
whisky: [N-MASS 物质名词] (尤指产于苏格兰、由大麦或黑麦酿制的)威士忌酒； whisky 一杯威士忌 Whisky is a strong alcoholic drink made, especially in Scotland, from grain such as barley or rye.
whisper: [VERB 动词] 低声说;悄悄说;耳语； whisper When you whisper , you say something very quietly, using your breath rather than your throat, so that only one person can hear you.  /  [VERB 动词] 私下谈论；谣传； whisper If people whisper about a piece of information, they talk about it, although it might not be true or accurate, or might be a secret.  /  [VERB 动词] 发出低沉而轻微的声音；沙沙或飒飒作响； whisper If something whispers , it makes a low quiet sound which can only just be heard.
whist: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 惠斯特牌两人一组玩的扑克牌游戏； Whist is a card game in which people play in pairs against each other.
whistle: [VERB 动词] 吹口哨；用口哨吹出(曲调)； whistle When you whistle or when you whistle a tune, you make a series of musical notes by forcing your breath out between your lips, or your teeth.  /  [VERB 动词] (吃惊、唤狗、赞叹等时)发出口哨声； whistle See also: wolf-whistle ; When someone whistles , they make a sound by forcing their breath out between their lips or their teeth.  /  [VERB 动词] (火车)鸣汽笛；(水开时水壶)发出尖啸声； whistle whistling If something such as a train or a kettle whistles , it makes a loud, high sound.  /  [VERB 动词] (风、子弹等)呼啸而过； whistle If something such as the wind or a bullet whistles somewhere, it moves there, making a loud, high sound.
whistle-blower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 告发者;检举者； whistle-blower A whistle-blower is someone who finds out that the organization they are working for is doing something immoral or illegal and tells the authorities or the public about it.
whistleblower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 告发者;检举者； A whistle-blower is someone who finds out that the organization they are working for is doing something immoral or illegal and tells the authorities or the public about it.
whistle-blowing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (向当局或公众)检举，告发； whistle-blowing Whistle-blowing is the act of telling the authorities or the public that the organization you are working for is doing something immoral or illegal.
whistleblowing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] (向当局或公众)检举，告发； Whistle-blowing is the act of telling the authorities or the public that the organization you are working for is doing something immoral or illegal.
whistle-stop: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指政界人士在很多地方)短暂停留的； whistle-stop If someone, especially a politician, goes on a whistle-stop tour, they visit a lot of different places in a short time.
whit: [PHRASE 短语] 一点也不;完全不； whit You say not a whit or not one whit to emphasize that something is not the case at all.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 同 Whitsun； Whit means the same as Whitsun .
white: [COLOUR 颜色词] 白色;白； white whiteness Something that is white is the colour of snow or milk.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 白种人的;白肤色的； white 白种人 A white person has a pale skin and belongs to a race which is of European origin.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (因情绪变化或生病等)脸色苍白的； white (因惊吓或生病而)脸色苍白的 If someone goes white , the skin on their face becomes very pale, for example because of fear, shock, anger, or illness.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (葡萄酒)白的，淡黄色的； white 白葡萄酒 White wine is pale yellow in colour.
whiteboard: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 白色书写板； A whiteboard is a shiny white board on which people draw or write using special pens.
white Christmas: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (下雪的)白色圣诞节； A white Christmas is a Christmas when it snows.
white-collar: [ADJ 形容词] 白领的;文职的;脑力劳动的； White-collar workers work in offices rather than doing physical work such as making things in factories or building things.  /  [ADJ 形容词] (犯罪)白领的(指非法窃取公司、政府钱财等)； White-collar crime is committed by people who work in offices, and involves stealing money secretly from companies or the government, or getting money in an illegal way.
white elephant: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 昂贵而无用的东西;华而不实的东西； white elephant If you describe something as a white elephant , you mean that it is a waste of money because it is completely useless.
white goods: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 白色家电(指冰箱、洗衣机等)； People in business sometimes refer to fridges, washing machines, and other large pieces of electrical household equipment as white goods .
white-haired: [ADJ 形容词] (老者)白发苍苍的； Someone who is white-haired has white hair, usually because they are old.
Whitehall: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 怀特霍尔(伦敦一街名，许多政府机关所在地)；白厅(指英国政府)； Whitehall Whitehall is the name of a street in London in which there are many government offices.
white-hot: [ADJ 形容词] 白热的;炽热的； white-hot If something is white-hot , it is extremely hot.
White House: [N-PROPER 专有名词] 白宫(位于华盛顿特区的美国总统府邸，也指美国总统及其官员);； White House The White House is the official home in Washington DC of the President of the United States.
white knight: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (成功阻止公司被恶意收购或陷入财务困难的)白衣骑士，白武士，救星； A white knight is a person or an organization that rescues a company from difficulties such as financial problems or an unwelcome takeover bid.
white-knuckle: [ADJ 形容词] 乘坐游乐装置令人兴奋又紧张的； white-knuckle In a fairground, a white-knuckle ride is any large machine that people ride on which is very exciting but also frightening.  /  [ADJ 形容词] 经历等惊险刺激的； white-knuckle A white-knuckle experience is something that you find very exciting but also very frightening.
white lie: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 善意的谎言； If you refer to an untrue statement as a white lie , you mean that it is made to avoid hurting someone's feelings or to avoid trouble, and not for an evil purpose.
white meat: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 白肉如鸡肉等； White meat is meat such as chicken and pork, which is pale in colour after it has been cooked.
whiten: [V-ERG 及物/不及物动词] 使变白； whiten When something whitens or when you whiten it, it becomes whiter or paler in colour.
white noise: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 白噪音(尤指持续而无规律的杂音)； white noise White noise is sound, especially of a loud, continuous, or unpleasant kind, that seems to have no pattern or rhythm.
White Pages: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 白页电话号码查询手册中的一般用户部分，姓名和电话号码按字母顺序排列； White Pages is used to refer to the section of a telephone directory which lists names and telephone numbers in alphabetical order.
White Paper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 白皮书； In Britain, Australia, Canada, and some other countries, a White Paper is an official report which describes the policy of the Government on a particular subject.
white pepper: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 白胡椒； White pepper is pepper which has been made from the dried insides of the fruits of the pepper plant.
white sauce: [N-MASS 物质名词] 白沙司(用牛奶、面粉、黄油等制成的调味汁)； White sauce is a thick white sauce made from milk, flour, and butter.
white spirit: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 石油溶剂液； White spirit is a colourless liquid that is made from petrol and is used, for example, to make paint thinner or to clean surfaces.

whom: [QUEST 疑问词] (用于疑问句，询问人的姓名或身份)谁； whom You use whom in questions when you ask about the name or identity of a person or group of people.  /  [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] (尤用于某些动词和形容词后，引导谈论某人或某一群人的姓名或身份的从句)谁； whom You use whom after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause where you talk about the name or identity of a person or a group of people.  /  [PRON-REL 关系代词] (用于进行限定说明或提供更多信息的关系从句的句首)；  whom You use whom at the beginning of a relative clause when specifying the person or group of people you are talking about or when giving more information about them.
whomever: [CONJ-SUBORD 连词] [用作动词或介词的宾语时，whoever 的正式形式] ； Whomever is a formal word for whoever when it is the object of a verb or preposition.

wild child: [N-SING 单数名词] 新闻用语疯丫头，野丫头； Journalists sometimes use wild child to refer to a teenage girl who enjoys herself in an uncontrolled way, for example by going to a lot of parties.
wildebeest: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 牛羚，角马(一种大型非洲羚羊)； A wildebeest is a large African antelope which has a hairy tail, short curved horns, and long hair under its neck.

wildfire: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 野火； wildfire A wildfire is a fire that starts, usually by itself, in a wild area such as a forest, and spreads rapidly, causing great damage.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (消息或谣言等)迅速传播； wildfire If something, especially news or a rumour, spreads like wildfire , it spreads extremely quickly.
wild flower: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 野花； Wild flowers are flowers which grow naturally in the countryside, rather than being grown by people in gardens.
wildfowl: [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 野禽； Wildfowl are birds such as ducks, swans, and geese that live close to lakes or rivers.

wilful: [ADJ 形容词] 故意的，有意的，成心的(尤指意在造成伤害)； wilful wilfully If you describe actions or attitudes as wilful , you are critical of them because they are done or expressed deliberately, especially with the intention of causing someone harm.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 任性的;一意孤行的； wilful wilfulness If you describe someone as wilful , you mean that they are determined to do what they want to do, even if it is not sensible.
will: Will is a modal verb.  /  [MODAL 情态动词] 将;将会;将要； will You use will to indicate that you hope, think, or have evidence that something is going to happen or be the case in the future.  /  [MODAL 情态动词] (表示将来的正式安排)； will You use will in order to make statements about official arrangements in the future.  /  [MODAL 情态动词] (表示承诺或威胁)会，要； will You use will in order to make promises and threats about what is going to happen or be the case in the future.
willing: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 乐意的;愿意的； willing willingness If someone is willing to do something, they are fairly happy about doing it and will do it if they are asked or required to do it.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 自愿的;愿意的;积极肯干的； willing willingly willingness Willing is used to describe someone who does something fairly enthusiastically and because they want to do it rather than because they are forced to do it.  /  God willing » see: god �

willpower: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 意志力;毅力； willpower Willpower is a very strong determination to do something.
willy: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 小鸡鸡； A boy's or man's willy is his penis.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 使紧张;使害怕； If someone or something gives you the willies , they make you feel nervous or frightened.
willy-nilly: [ADV 副词] 不管喜欢不喜欢;无可奈何地； willy-nilly If something happens to you willy-nilly , it happens whether you like it or not.  /  [ADV 副词] 随意地;胡乱地； willy-nilly If someone does something willy-nilly , they do it in a careless and disorganized way, without planning it in advance.

wily: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 诡计多端的;狡诈的;狡猾的； wily If you describe someone or their behaviour as wily , you mean that they are clever at achieving what they want, especially by tricking people.
wimp: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 软蛋;窝囊废； If you call someone a wimp , you disapprove of them because they lack confidence or determination, or because they are often afraid of things.
wimpish: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 同 wimpy； Wimpish means the same as wimpy .

win: [VERB 动词] 赢；赢得； win If you win something such as a competition, battle, or argument, you defeat those people you are competing or fighting against, or you do better than everyone else involved.  /  [VERB 动词] 使…赢得;使…获得； win If something wins you something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, it causes you to defeat the people competing with you or fighting you, or to do better than everyone else involved.  /  [VERB 动词] 赢得，获得(奖项或奖牌)； win If you win something such as a prize or medal, you get it because you have defeated everyone else in something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, or have done very well in it.  /  [VERB 动词] 获得，赢得(想要或需要之物)； win If you win something that you want or need, you succeed in getting it.
win back: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 尤指经过千辛万苦赢回，夺回； win back If you win back something that you have lost, you get it again, especially as a result of a great effort.
wince: [VERB 动词] (因疼痛或因看到、听到或记起不快之事而)皱起脸，皱眉蹙额； wince If you wince , the muscles of your face tighten suddenly because you have felt a pain or because you have just seen, heard, or remembered something unpleasant.
winch: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绞车;卷扬机； A winch is a machine which is used to lift heavy objects or people who need to be rescued.  /  [VERB 动词] 用绞车吊起； winch If you winch an object or person somewhere, you lift or lower them using a winch.
wind: [N-VAR 可变名词] 风； wind A wind is a current of air that is moving across the earth's surface.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (影响事件的)趋势或因素常作新闻用语； wind Journalists often refer to a trend or factor that influences events as a wind of a particular kind.  /  [VERB 动词] 使气急;使呼吸困难； wind If you are winded by something such as a blow, the air is suddenly knocked out of your lungs so that you have difficulty breathing for a short time.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 胃肠中的气； Wind is the air that you sometimes swallow with food or drink, or gas that is produced in your intestines, which causes an uncomfortable feeling.
windbag: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 话篓子;唠叨鬼； If you call someone a windbag , you are saying in a fairly rude way that you think they talk a great deal in a boring way.
windblown: [ADJ 形容词] 被风吹动的;随风飘动的； You can use wind-blown to indicate that something has been blown from one place to another by the wind.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (头发等)被风吹乱的； windblown If something such as someone's hair is wind-blown , it is untidy because it has been blown about by the wind.
wind-blown: [ADJ 形容词] 被风吹动的;随风飘动的； wind-blown You can use wind-blown to indicate that something has been blown from one place to another by the wind.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (头发等)被风吹乱的； If something such as someone's hair is wind-blown , it is untidy because it has been blown about by the wind.
windbreak: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 风障;防风林;挡风篱； A windbreak is something such as a line of trees or a fence which gives protection against the wind.
Windbreaker: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 防风夹克;风衣； A Windbreaker is a warm casual jacket.
wind down: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 摇下(车窗等)； wind down When you wind down something such as the window of a car, you make it move downwards by turning a handle.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 放松;松弛； wind down If you wind down , you relax after doing something that has made you feel tired or tense.  /  [PHRASAL VERB-ERG ] 逐渐减小(工作规模);使逐步停止;使逐渐关闭； wind down If someone winds down a business or activity, they gradually reduce the amount of work that is done or the number of people that are involved, usually before closing or stopping it completely.
windfall: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 意外之财;横财； A windfall is a sum of money that you receive unexpectedly or by luck, for example if you win a lottery.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 被风吹落的果子尤指苹果； A windfall is a fruit, especially an apple, that has fallen from a tree.
wind farm: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 风力发电场； A wind farm is a place where windmills are used to convert the power of the wind into electricity.
wind instrument: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 管乐器； A wind instrument is a musical instrument that you blow into in order to produce sounds, such as a flute, a clarinet, or a recorder.
windlass: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 绞盘;卷扬机;辘轳； A windlass is a mechanical device for lifting heavy objects, which uses a motor to pull a rope or chain around a cylinder.
windless: [ADJ 形容词] 无风的;不起风的； If the air is windless , or if it is a windless day, it is very calm and still.
windmill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 风车磨坊；风力发电的风车； A windmill is a building with long pieces of wood on the outside which turn around as the wind blows and provide energy for a machine that crushes grain.
window: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗;窗户； window A window is a space in the wall of a building or in the side of a vehicle, which has glass in it so that light can come in and you can see out.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (商店的)玻璃橱窗，陈列窗； window A window is a large piece of glass along the front of a shop, behind which some of the goods that the shop sells are displayed.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] (银行、邮局、火车站、博物馆等处柜台的)窗口； window A window is a glass-covered opening above a counter, for example in a bank, post office, railway station, or museum, which the person serving you sits behind.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗口;视窗； On a computer screen, a window is one of the work areas that the screen can be divided into.
window box: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗台花槽;窗栏花箱； A window box is a long narrow container on a shelf at the bottom of a window and is used for growing plants.
window-dressing: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 窗饰艺术；尤指橱窗装饰艺术;橱窗布置； Window-dressing is the skill of arranging objects attractively in a window, especially a shop window, or the way in which they are arranged.  /  [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 粉饰门面;弄虚作假； If you refer to something as window-dressing , you are critical of it because it is done in order to create a good impression and to prevent people from realizing the real or more unpleasant nature of someone's activities.
window frame: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗框； A window frame is a frame around the edges of a window, which glass is fixed into.
windowpane: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗玻璃； A windowpane is a piece of glass in the window of a building.
window seat: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 房间内窗下的靠窗的座位,窗座； A window seat is a seat which is fixed to the wall underneath a window in a room.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 火车、巴士或飞机上的靠窗的座位； On a train, bus, or aeroplane, a window seat is a seat next to a window.
window shade: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗帘；卷帘； A window shade is a piece of stiff cloth or heavy paper that you can pull down over a window as a covering.
window shopping: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 无意购物的浏览商店橱窗； If you do some window shopping , you spend time looking at the goods in the windows of shops without intending to buy anything.
windowsill: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 窗台；窗沿； A windowsill is a shelf along the bottom of a window, either inside or outside a building.
windpipe: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 气管； Your windpipe is the tube in your body that carries air into your lungs when you breathe.
windscreen: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (汽车等的)风挡，挡风玻璃； The windscreen of a car or other vehicle is the glass window at the front through which the driver looks.
windscreen wiper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (挡风玻璃)刮雨器，雨刷； A windscreen wiper is a device that wipes rain from a vehicle's windscreen.
windshield: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (汽车等的)风挡，挡风玻璃； The windshield of a car or other vehicle is the glass window at the front through which the driver looks.
windshield wiper: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 同 windscreen wiper； A windshield wiper is the same as a windscreen wiper .
windsurfer: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 帆板； A windsurfer is a long narrow board with a sail attached to it.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 帆板运动员； A windsurfer is a person who rides on a windsurfer.

wind tunnel: [N-COUNT 可数名词] (尤用于测试新汽车、新飞机等的)风洞； A wind tunnel is a room or passage through which air can be made to flow at controlled speeds.
wind up: [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 完成;停止； wind up When you wind up an activity, you finish it or stop doing it.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 关停，关闭(企业或其他组织)； wind up When someone winds up a business or other organization, they stop running it and close it down completely.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 最终沦落到；最终落得；(以…)告终； wind up If you wind up in a particular place, situation, or state, you are in it at the end of a series of actions, events, or experiences, even though you did not originally intend to be.  /  [PHRASAL VERB 短语动词] 摇上(车窗等)； When you wind up something such as the window of a car, you make it move upwards by turning a handle.
wind-up: [ADJ 形容词] (机械装置)装有发条的，用手柄操作的； wind-up A wind-up device is a mechanical device with a handle or key that you turn several times before you use it in order to make it work.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 故意惹人生气的玩笑;故意戏弄人的把戏； wind-up A wind-up is a joke or trick in which someone deliberately tells you something untrue in order to annoy you.
windward: [ADJ 形容词] (尤指船侧)迎风的，向风的，顶风的； windward Windward is used to describe the side of something, especially a ship, which is facing the wind.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (船等)顶风，迎风； If a ship sails to windward , it sails towards the place from which the wind is blowing.
windy: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 多风的;大风的； windy If it is windy , the wind is blowing a lot.
wine: [N-MASS 物质名词] 葡萄酒;果蔬酒； wine Wine is an alcoholic drink which is made from grapes.  /  [COLOUR 颜色词] 深红色;紫红色;酒红色； wine Wine is used to describe things that are very dark red in colour.  /  [PHR-ERG ] 大吃大喝；盛宴款待； wine If you wine and dine , or if someone wines and dines you, you go out, for example to expensive restaurants, and spend a lot of money.

winery: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 葡萄酒厂;酿酒厂； A winery is a place where wine is made.

winged: [ADJ 形容词] (昆虫等)有翼的，带翅的； winged A winged insect or other creature has wings.

wire wool: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 常用来清洁木质及金属物质的钢丝球；钢丝绒； Wire wool consists of very thin pieces of wire twisted together, often in the form of small pads.

wisdom: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 智慧;才智； wisdom Wisdom is the ability to use your experience and knowledge in order to make sensible decisions or judgments.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] (社会或文化长期积累的)知识，学问； wisdom Wisdom is the store of knowledge that a society or culture has collected over a long period of time.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 明智； wisdom If you talk about the wisdom of a particular decision or action, you are talking about how sensible it is.  /  [N-VAR 可变名词] 一般观点;普遍看法； wisdom 传统观念;一般看法 You can use wisdom to refer to ideas that are accepted by a large number of people.
wisdom tooth: [N-COUNT 可数名词] 智齿;智牙； Your wisdom teeth are the four large teeth at the back of your mouth which usually grow much later than your other teeth.
wise: [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] 人充满智慧的，英明的，睿智的； wise wisely A wise person is able to use their experience and knowledge in order to make sensible decisions and judgments.  /  [ADJ-GRADED 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词] (行动或决定)明智的，高明的； wise wisely A wise action or decision is sensible.  /  [PHRASE 短语] (做…)是明智的；最好做…； wise If someone says to you that it would be wise to do something, they are advising you to do it, because it is the most sensible and reasonable action or decision in a particular situation.  /  [PHRASE 短语] 明白，察觉(尤指他人试图保密之事)； wise If you get wise to something, you find out about it, especially when someone has been trying to keep it secret.

wit: [N-UNCOUNT 不可数名词] 说话的风趣，机智，巧妙； wit Wit is the ability to use words or ideas in an amusing, clever, and imaginative way.  /  [N-COUNT 可数名词] 风趣的人;机智的人； wit If you describe someone as a wit , you mean that they have the ability to use words or ideas in an amusing, clever, and imaginative way.  /  [N-SING 单数名词] 头脑；智慧； wit If you say that someone has the wit to do something, you mean that they have the intelligence and understanding to make the right decision or take the right action in a particular situation.  /  [N-PLURAL 复数名词] 机智； wit You can refer to your ability to think quickly and cleverly in a difficult situation as your wits .

working party: [N-COUNT-COLL 可数集合名词] 专题调查委员会;特别工作组； working party A working party is a committee which is formed to investigate a particular situation or problem and to produce a report containing its opinions and suggestions.

worsted: [N-MASS 物质名词] 精纺毛料； Worsted is a kind of woollen cloth.
